(Acts iv. 12): "Nor is there salvation in anyone else; for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved." See also John xvii. 1, 3; 1 Cor. iii. 11; 1 Tim. ii. 5; Gal. i. 6–9. But natural reason does not attain this knowledge by itself.

units.la: 3. Quia necessarium est Fœdus Evangelicum, & vera ratio justitiæ secundùm istud consequendæ, Rom. x, 3. "Ignorantes Dei justitiam, & propriam justitiam statuere, justitiæ Dei non fuerunt subjecti, Gal. ii, 21. "Non irritam facio gratiam Dei: nam si per Legem est justitia, Christus sine causa mortuus est. Vide etiam Gal. v, 4. Hebr. viii, 7-.
units.tr: Third, because the Gospel covenant is necessary, and the true way of obtaining righteousness according to it (Rom. x. 3): "Being ignorant of God's righteousness, and seeking to establish their own righteousness, they did not submit to the righteousness of God." (Gal. ii. 21): "I do not set aside the grace of God; for if righteousness comes through the Law, Christ died in vain." See also Gal. v. 4; Heb. viii. 7 ff.

units.la: 4. Omnium eorum, qui Revelatione supernaturali destituuntur, miserrima est conditio. Act. xiv, 16. "Deus præteritis ætatibus sivit omnes Gentes suis ipsarum viis incedere. Eph. ii, 12. "Vos, (inquam) illo tempore fuisse absque Christo, abalienatos à civili statu Israëlis, & extraneos quod ad pactorum promissiones attinet, spem non habentes, & absque Deo in mundo. Adde Eph. iv, 17, 18.
units.tr: 4. Of all those who are deprived of supernatural Revelation, the condition is most wretched. Acts 14:16: "God, in past ages, suffered all the nations to walk in their own ways." Ephesians 2:12: "You, I say, were at that time without Christ, alienated from the civil state of Israel, and strangers as regards the promises of the covenants, having no hope, and without God in the world." Add Ephesians 4:17, 18.

units.la: XXIV. Obj. 1. Act. x, 34, 35. "Deus non respicit ad personas
units.tr: XXIV. Objection 1. Acts 10:34, 35. "God does not regard the person,

units.la: ,,personam, sed in quâvis gente acceptus ei est quivis, qui ;; eum timet, & operum dat justitiæ. Hæc autem secundùm Conscientiam naturalem, & lumen Rationis præstari possunt. Resp. Negamus, verum Dei timorem, (filialem,) verumque studium ac praxin justitiæ, in ullo homine reperiri, absque gratiâ & revelatione supernaturali. Vide Rom. xiv, 23. Tit. i, 15.
units.tr: "...God does not regard the person, but in every nation whoever fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him." These things can be achieved according to natural conscience and the light of reason. Answer: We deny that true fear of God (filial fear), and true zeal and practice of righteousness, can be found in any man without grace and supernatural revelation. See Rom. xiv, 23. Tit. i, 15.

units.la: Obj. 2. Cornelius, Centurio ex legione Italicâ, & ipse alienigena, Christum adhùc ignorans, dicitur ibid. vers. 2. & 4. pius fuisse ac timens Deum, cum totâ domo suâ: quodque preces ejus, & eleemosynæ, ascenderint in memoriam in Dei conspectu. Ergò ex Religione naturali, &c. Resp. Interim idem Cornelius etiàm dicitur vers. 22, testimonio ornatus totius gentis Judæorum: undè facile est colligere, eum minimè alienum fuisse à cognitione & expectatione Messiæ. Quin & Petrus testatur vers. 37, 38. eum non prorsus ignorasse Jesum Nazarenum. Ex quibus patet, eum tunc non habuisse solùm Religionem aliquam naturalem ; sed & supernaturalem: sicut extraordinaria revelatio per Angelum ei quoque accidit. vers. 4; 30, 31. & deinceps ex Petro amplius didicit Religionem Christianam, secundùm œconomiam N. T. vers. 39–43.
units.tr: Objection 2. Cornelius, a centurion of the Italian legion and himself a foreigner, still ignorant of Christ, is said in the same passage (vv. 2 and 4) to have been pious and fearing God along with his whole household, and that his prayers and alms had come up as a memorial before God. Therefore from natural religion, etc. Answer: The same Cornelius is also said (v. 22) to have been commended by the testimony of the whole nation of the Jews; from which it is easy to gather that he was by no means a stranger to the knowledge and expectation of the Messiah. Indeed Peter testifies (vv. 37, 38) that he had not wholly been ignorant of Jesus of Nazareth. From these things it is clear that at that time he had not only some natural religion but also a supernatural one; just as an extraordinary revelation through an angel also came to him (vv. 4, 30, 31). And afterwards, from Peter, he learned more fully the Christian religion, according to the economy of the New Testament (vv. 39–43).

units.la: XXXV. Ex Theologia naturali corruptâ, admixtis interim & adulteratis quibusdam Theologiæ supernaturalis reliquiis, quæ ex familiis Patriarcharum promanaverant, accedentibus etiàm traditionibus & institutis Diabolicis, orta est Pseudo-theologia Gentium. Hæc autem versabatur partim circa Deos; ut μυθικὴ, fabulosa, Poëtarum; φυσικὴ, naturalis, Philosophorum; & πολιτικὴ, civilis, sacerdotum: partim circa Dæmonas; malis cooperando, aut eos averruncando, bonos sacrificiis invitando: quò pertinent μαγία, γοητεία, τελετὴ, &c.
units.tr: XXXV. Out of corrupted natural theology, with certain remnants of supernatural theology, which had flowed down from the families of the patriarchs, mixed in and adulterated from time to time, and with traditions and Diabolical institutions also added, there arose the pseudo-theology of the Gentiles. This was concerned partly with the gods: the mythical [μυθικὴ], that is fabulous, of the poets; the natural [φυσικὴ] of the philosophers; and the civil [πολιτικὴ] of the priests. Partly it was concerned with demons: by cooperating with evil ones, or by warding them off, and by inviting the good ones with sacrifices; to this belong magic [μαγία], sorcery [γοητεία], rites [τελετὴ], etc.

units.la: XXVI. Theologia supernaturalis est, quæ sphæram naturæ
units.tr: XXVI. Supernatural theology is that which, going beyond the sphere of nature,

units.la: naturæ excedens, ex Verbo Dei hauritur; & ad salutarem ipsius communionem, juxta Fœdus Euangelicum obtinendum pertingit. Inservit ei sua Revelatio, tùm extraordinaria, tùm ordinaria.
units.tr: is drawn from the Word of God, and attains to the saving communion with him, obtained according to the Gospel covenant. Its revelation serves it, both extraordinary and ordinary.

units.la: XXVII. Extraordinaria per peculiarem inspiratio- nem, aut manifestationem, obtigit extra ordinem san- ctis potissimùm Dei hominibus.
units.tr: XXVII. Extraordinary revelation came, through a special inspiration or manifestation, outside the ordinary course, chiefly to the holy men of God.

units.la: Sic David, 2 Sam. XXIII, 2. „Spiritus Jehovæ locutus est per me, & sermo ejus (factus est) per linguam meam. 2 Petr, 1, 21. „Acti à Spiritu Sancto locuti sunt sancti Dei homines.
units.tr: So David (2 Sam. xxiii. 2): „The Spirit of Jehovah spoke through me, and his word was through my tongue." (2 Pet. i. 21): „Moved by the Holy Spirit, holy men of God spoke."

units.la: 2 Tim. III, 16. „Tota Scriptura Divinitus (est) inspirata. Undè etiam tales homines dicuntur Θεόπνευστοι. Hùc quoque pertinent Alloquia Divina: Num. XII, 8. Gen. XII, 1, 2, 3, 7. XV, 1, – XVII, 1, – 22. Jerem. 1, 4, – Ezech. VI, 1, 2. Raptùs, sive Ecstases; Act. XXII, 17. 2 Cor. XII. 2, 3, 4. Apoc. 1, 10. Visiones; Exod. III, 2. Jes. VI. Ezech. I. Am. VII, VIII. IX. Zach. 1, 8, –. II, – VI. His accedunt Apparitiones Angelorum; Dan. IX, 21, 22. Luc. II, 1, 13, – 20; 26, – 38. II, 8, – 14. Matth. XXVIII, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7. Act. I, 10, 11. Ac tandem Insomnia; Gen. XXXVII, 5, – 10. Matth. 1, 20, 21. II, 19, 20; 22.
units.tr: (2 Tim. iii. 16): „All Scripture is divinely inspired." Hence such men are called God-breathed [Θεόπνευστοι]. To this belong also the divine addresses: Num. xii. 8; Gen. xii. 1, 2, 3, 7; xv. 1; xvii. 1, 22; Jer. i. 4; Ezek. vi. 1, 2. Rapture, or ecstasies: Acts xxii. 17; 2 Cor. xii. 2, 3, 4; Rev. i. 10. Visions: Exod. iii. 2; Isa. vi; Ezek. i; Amos vii, viii, ix; Zech. i. 8; ii; vi. To these are added the appearances of angels: Dan. ix. 21, 22; Luke i. 11, 13, 20, 26, 38; ii. 8, 14; Matt. xxviii. 2, 3, 5, 6, 7; Acts i. 10, 11. And finally dreams: Gen. xxxvii. 5, 10; Matt. i. 20, 21; ii. 19, 20, 22.

units.la: Sed à recensitis speciebus Revelationis extraordinariæ, distinguendæ sunt Revelationes, suggestiones, increpationes, convictiones, similibusferè modis factæ hominibus quibusdam irregenitis & à salutari Dei communione alienis; quales Θεήλατοι quandoque appellantur: Num. XXII, 9, – 12; 20; 31, – 35. XXIII, 4, – 10; 16. – 24; XXIV, 2, – 9. Job. XI, 49 – 52. Confer Gen. XLI, 1, – 32. Dan. II, 1; 27, – 45; IV, 4, – 27. V, 5, – 28. Matth. XXVIII, 2, 3, 4. Longissimè autem distant Illusiones Diabolicæ, nec non vana deliria, & fallacia figmenta Pseudo-Enthusiastarum, aliorumque Fanaticorum.
units.tr: But from the species of extraordinary revelation just listed must be distinguished the revelations, suggestions, rebukes and convictions, made in much the same ways to certain men who are unregenerate and alienated from the saving communion of God; which are sometimes called God-sent [Θεήλατοι]: Num. xxii. 9–12, 20, 31–35; xxiii. 4–10, 16–24; xxiv. 2–9; Job xi. 49–52. Compare Gen. xli. 1–32; Dan. ii. 1, 27–45; iv. 4–27; v. 5–28; Matt. xxvii. 19 (sic). But the diabolical illusions, as well as the vain delusions and false fictions of the Pseudo-Enthusiasts, and of other Fanatics, are very far removed from these.

units.la: XXVIII. Extraordinarias illas revelationes potissimum
units.tr: XXVIII. Those extraordinary revelations, chiefly

units.la: mùm dedit Deus, 1. in Ecclesiâ ex lapsu per Christum salvandorum primùm fundandâ: aut singulari modo stabiliendâ: Gen. III, 15. XII, 1, 2, 3. XVII, 1, -16.
units.tr: God gave them chiefly (1) in the Church, which was first to be founded after the fall for those to be saved through Christ, or to be established in a singular manner: Gen. III, 15. XII, 1, 2, 3. XVII, 1, -16.

units.la: 2. Ubi valdè corrupta esset, reformandâ; Exod. III, 6, -17. cum Ezech. XX, 6, -9. 1 Reg. XVIII, 21, -40.
units.tr: (2) where it was greatly corrupted, to be reformed: Exod. III, 6, -17, with Ezek. XX, 6, -9. 1 Kings XVIII, 21, -40.

units.la: 3. Ac porrò ab œconomiâ V. T. ad œconomiam N. T. traducendâ: Matth. III, 1, 2, 3. X, 1, -8. XXVIII, 19, 20. Eph. IV, 11, 12, 13. 1 Cor. XII, 7, 8, 28, 29.
units.tr: (3) and further, to be carried over from the economy of the Old Testament to the economy of the New: Matth. III, 1, 2, 3. X, 1, -8. XXVIII, 19, 20. Eph. IV, 11, 12, 13. 1 Cor. XII, 7, 8, 28, 29.

units.la: 4. Vel etiàm ubi voluit singularia judicia exercere, deque iis homines præmonere: Am. III, 7. Gen. VI, 6, 7, 17, 18. XVIII, 17, -20. Joh. I, 2. II, 1, -4.
units.tr: (4) or even where he willed to execute singular judgments and to forewarn men of them: Amos III, 7. Gen. VI, 6, 7, 17, 18. XVIII, 17, -20. John I, 2. II, 1, -4.

units.la: Eademque opera, per sanctos illos Ministros Θεόπνευστος, Ecclesiæ datus & scripto consignatus est perpetuus deinceps futurus Canon Theologiæ ordinariæ: Deut. XXXI, 9, 24, 26. Joh. V, 39. XX, 31. Rom. IV, 23, 24. XV, 4. 1 Cor. X, 11. 2 Tim. III. 15, 16, 17. 1 Petr. I, 10, 11, 12. 2. I, 19, 20, 21. Apoc. I, 3. XXII, 18, 19.
units.tr: By the same work, through those holy ministers, God-breathed [Θεόπνευστος] Scripture was given to the Church and committed to writing, to be from then on the perpetual canon of ordinary theology: Deut. XXXI, 9, 24, 26. John V, 39. XX, 31. Rom. IV, 23, 24. XV, 4. 1 Cor. X, 11. 2 Tim. III, 15, 16, 17. 1 Pet. I, 10, 11, 12. 2 Pet. I, 19, 20, 21. Rev. I, 3. XXII, 18, 19.

units.la: XXIX. Ordinaria revelatio fit per Verbum Dei foris propositum, & per Spiritum Sanctum intus nos aptos facientem, atque hyperphysicè moventem, ad intelligendam veritatem illam, ad agnoscendam ejus Divinitatem, quin imò ad mentem, voluntatem, omnemque vitam nostram ei subjiciendam & conformandam: Jes. LIX, 21. Spiritum meum, qui est super te; & verba mea, quæ posui in ore tuo, non recedent de ore tuo, & de ore seminis tui, & de ore seminis seminis tui, dixit Jehovah, ex hoc tempore & usque in sæculum. 2 Cor. III, 5, 6. Quòd idonei sumus, (id) ex Deo est: Qui etiàm fecit ut idonei essemus Ministri novi pacti; non litteræ, sed Spiritus. Videt etiàm 1 Cor. II, 6. 1 Thess. II, 13. Act. XVI, 14. XXX. Hinc innotescit Theologiæ nostræ causa constitutionis instrumentalis; videl. Verbum Dei quod ipso volente, in hunc finem scriptum consignatum & obsi-
units.tr: XXIX. Ordinary revelation comes about through the Word of God set forth outwardly, and through the Holy Spirit, who within us makes us fit and moves us beyond nature, to understand that truth, to acknowledge its divinity, and indeed to subject and conform our mind, will and whole life to it: Isa. LIX, 21. "My Spirit that is upon you, and my words that I have put in your mouth, shall not depart out of your mouth, nor out of the mouth of your seed, nor out of the mouth of your seed's seed, saith the LORD, from henceforth and for ever." 2 Cor. III, 5, 6. "Our sufficiency is of God; who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit." See also 1 Cor. II, 6. 1 Thess. II, 13. Acts XVI, 14. XXX. From this it becomes known that the instrumental cause of the constitution of our theology is the Word of God, which, by his will, was written and sealed for this purpose

units.la: obsignatum est, ne sapiamus supra id quod scriptum est, 1 Cor, iv, 6.
units.tr: sealed, that we not be wise above what is written, 1 Cor. IV, 6.

units.la: XXXI. Objectum ejus primarium ac denominationis, est ipse Deus Opt. Max. Vide Matth. xix. 17. 1 Tim.vi. 15, 16. & confer sup. th. 2.
units.tr: XXXI. Its primary and denominating object is God himself, the best and greatest. See Matth. XIX, 17. 1 Tim. VI, 15, 16, and compare above, th. 2.

units.la: Subordinatur illi Religio: Vinculum istud pietatis, quo obstricti sumus & religati Deo. Hæc verò piam Dei ac veritatis Divinæ agnitionem complectitur, & cultum Ejusdem sincerum. Tit. i. 1. Agnitionem veritatis, quæ est secundum pietatem. Vide Joh. xvii. 17. Jac. i. 27.
units.tr: Religion is subordinate to it: that bond of piety by which we are bound and tied to God. This in turn embraces the pious acknowledgment of God and of divine truth, and sincere worship of him. Titus I, 1: "the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness." See John XVII, 17. James I, 27.

units.la: XXXII. Agnoscendus est Deus, qualem Se nobis Verbo suo revelavit. Omnis autem Divina revelatio, ubi nobis innotuit, nos illicò ad assensum obligat necessitate præcepti. Act. xxiv, 14. Ut qui credam omnibus, quæ in Lege & in Prophetis scripta sunt. At si necessitatem medii spectemus, ad salutem juxta Fœdus Euangelicum consequendam, fundamentum fundamentorum est Jesus Christus: 1 Cor, iii. 11. Quod ipsum tamen plura involvit.
units.tr: XXXII. God is to be acknowledged as he has revealed himself to us in his Word. Every divine revelation, once it has become known to us, binds us immediately to assent by the necessity of a precept: Acts XXIV, 14: "that I believe all things which are written in the law and in the prophets." But if we consider the necessity of the means for obtaining salvation under the Gospel covenant, the foundation of foundations is Jesus Christ: 1 Cor. III, 11. Yet this itself involves several things.

units.la: Infantibus statim proponuntur Elementa doctrinæ Christianæ; Decalogus, Symbolum fidei, Oratio Dominica, Institutio Sacramentorum, & Ordinis ac Disciplinæ Ecclesiasticæ. Hebr. vi, 1, 2. Omisso qui in Christo rudes inchoat sermone, ad perfectionem feramur: non jacientes rursum fundamentum resipiscentiæ ab operibus mortuis, & fidei in Deum, Baptismatum doctrinæ, ac manuum impositionis, & resurrectionis, & judicii æterni.
units.tr: Infants are at once set before the elements of Christian doctrine: the Decalogue, the Creed, the Lord's Prayer, the teaching of the sacraments, and of the order and discipline of the Church. Heb. VI, 1, 2: "Leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God, of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment."

units.la: Proficientibus plures articuli traduntur: qui in Catholicos & Theologicos dispesci solent; illi ad fidem catholicè salutarem pertinent; hi ad accuratiorem scientiam Theologicam fundamento superstruuntur.
units.tr: For those making progress more articles are handed on, which are usually divided into Catholic and theological; the former pertain to the faith that is catholically saving; the latter are built upon this foundation for a more exact theological knowledge.

units.la: 1 Cor. iii, 12, 13. Quodsi quis super ædificat super fundamentum hoc, aurum, argentum, lapides pretiosos, ligna, fœnum, stipulam: Cujusque opus manifestum fiet: &c. 1 Tim. I, 13. Expressam formam teneto sanorum sermonum, quos à me audisti, cum fide & charitate quæ (est) in Christo Jesu. Adde 2 Tim. II, 2. III. 14.
units.tr: 1 Cor. III, 12, 13: "Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; every man's work shall be made manifest," etc. 1 Tim. I, 13: "Hold fast the form of sound words, which thou hast heard of me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus." Add 2 Tim. II, 2; III, 14.

units.la: XXXIII. Deus agnitus colendus est devotâ mente, atque omnibus viribus nostris.
units.tr: XXXIII. God, once acknowledged, is to be worshipped with a devout mind and with all our strength.

units.la: Hoc enim postulat 1. Natura Dei sanctissima.
units.tr: For this is required, (1) by the most holy nature of God.

units.la: 2. Mandata nobis præscripta, & serio commendata.
units.tr: (2) by the commands prescribed to us and seriously commended.

units.la: 3. Beneficia in nos collata; tum naturæ, tum gratiæ.
units.tr: (3) by the benefits conferred upon us, both of nature and of grace.

units.la: 4. Nostra à Deo dependentia, ut realis, itâ quoque moralis.
units.tr: (4) by our dependence on God, as real, so also moral.

units.la: 1 Joh. III, 3. Quisquis habet hanc spem in eo (sitam,) purum se conservat, sicut & ille purus est. Deut. VI, 5. Diliges ergo Iehovam Deum tuum toto corde tuo, & tota anima tua, & tota fortitudine tua. Psal. cxvi, 12. Quid reddam Iehovæ (pro) omnibus beneficiis ejus (quæ contulit) in me? Act. XVII, 27, 28. Ut quaerarent Dominum, - In ipso enim vivimus, movemur, & sumus. Adde Joh. XIII, 17. Tit. II, 11, 14. 1 Joh. I, 5. 6, 7.
units.tr: 1 John III, 3: "Every man that hath this hope in him purifieth himself, even as he is pure." Deut. VI, 5: "Thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might." Ps. CXVI, 12: "What shall I render unto the LORD for all his benefits toward me?" Acts XVII, 27, 28: "That they should seek the Lord... for in him we live, and move, and have our being." Add John XIII, 17. Titus II, 11, 14. 1 John I, 5, 6, 7.

units.la: XXXIV. Ex dictis patet, primo, gravissimè errare Socinianos, dum Religionem duabus hisce partibus comprehendunt; Præceptis Divinis, & Promissis: atque item Remonstrantes, hisce tribus eam circumscribentes; Fide Divinorum promissorum, Obedientia Divinorum præceptorum, & debitâ Scripturis Reverentia. Neque enim Fides restringenda est ad Promissa Dei sola; sed ad omnes veritates, ab Ipso revelatas extendenda. Deinde, non merè speculativam esse Theologiam nostram; (quod calumniantur Remonstrantes;) sed maximè practicam. Sic enim contemplamur Deum, & opera Ipsius, ac sermones veraces: ut omnis illa contemplatio perpetuam praxin requirat, & efficaciter promoveat. Sic contemplamur summum verum, ut simul agnoscamus ac diligamus summum bonum, ac devotè obedianus sanctissimo isti Domino. Matth. v. 8. Mundi corde, - videbunt Deum.
units.tr: XXXIV. From what has been said it is plain, first, that the Socinians err very gravely when they comprise religion in these two parts, divine precepts and promises; and likewise the Remonstrants, who circumscribe it by these three: faith in the divine promises, obedience to the divine precepts, and due reverence for the Scriptures. For faith is not to be restricted to God's promises alone, but must be extended to all the truths revealed by him. Next, our theology is not merely speculative (which the Remonstrants falsely charge), but chiefly practical. For we contemplate God, his works and his true words in such a way that all such contemplation requires and effectively promotes a constant practice. We contemplate the highest truth in such a way that at the same time we acknowledge and love the highest good, and devoutly obey that most holy Lord. Matth. V, 8: "Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God."

units.la: XXXV. Objectum secundarium, sive directionis Theologiae nostrae, est totus Homo 1 Thess. v. 23. "Ipse autem Deus pacis Sanctificet vos totos: & integer "vester spiritus, & anima, & corpus, inculpate in ad-"ventum Domini nostri Jesu Christi servetur.
units.tr: XXXV. The secondary object, or the object of direction, of our theology is the whole man. 1 Thess. V, 23: "And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ."

units.la: In Anima scil. Intellectus theoreticus veritate Divina informandus; practicus notitia eorum, quae ad officia nostra coram Deo pertinent: voluntas in Deum rite dirigenda, & ad ea quae Deus vult; ab oppositis vero avertenda: tum facultates reliquae, & affectus, ipsaque Corporis membra, & consequenter omnes actiones nostrae, ad sanctum obsequium formanda. Vide 1 Cor. vi. 20. Eph. 1, 18. Prov. xxiii. 26. Luc. x, 27. Rom. vi. 13. 1 Cor. x. 31.
units.tr: That is, in the soul: the theoretical intellect is to be informed by divine truth; the practical by knowledge of those things which pertain to our duties before God; the will is to be rightly directed towards God and towards what God wills, and turned away from the opposite; then the remaining faculties and affections, and the very members of the body, and consequently all our actions, are to be shaped to holy obedience. See 1 Cor. VI, 20. Eph. I, 18. Prov. XXIII, 26. Luke X, 27. Rom. VI, 13. 1 Cor. X, 31.

units.la: XXXVI.
units.tr: XXXVI.

units.la: Consequenter etiam Subjectum quo, est primo Intellectus, tum theoreticus, tum practicus; ac porro Voluntas, & reliquae facultates.
units.tr: Consequently, the subject by which is first the intellect, both theoretical and practical; then the will and the remaining faculties.

units.la: Sed Subjectum quod, primario & proprie constituunt Electi efficaciter vocati - Matth. xi, 25, 26. "Gloriam tibi tribuo, Pater; Domine coeli & terrae, quod haec "occultaveris sapientibus & intelligentibus; & ea de-"texeris infantibus. Etiam Pater, quia ita libuit apud Te. xiii. 11. "Vobis datum est nosse mysteria Regni coelorum, illis autem non est datum. Tit. I, 1. "Secundum fidem electorum Dei.
units.tr: But the subject which, primarily and properly, is constituted by the elect who are effectually called: Matt. xi. 25, 26. "I give thanks to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to infants. Yes, Father, for so it pleased you." Matt. xiii. 11. "To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given." Tit. i. 1. "According to the faith of God's elect."

units.la: Secundario tamen, & per similitudinem quandam, aliqui reprobi gratiae solum illuminantis & refrenantis participes facti. Vide Hebr. vi. 4, 5, 6. 1 Tim. 1, 19. Matth. xiii, 20, 21.
units.tr: Secondarily, however, and by a certain likeness, some reprobate have become partakers of grace only in its illuminating and restraining aspect. See Heb. vi. 4, 5, 6. 1 Tim. i. 19. Matt. xiii. 20, 21.

units.la: XXXVII.
units.tr: XXXVII.

units.la: Finis primarius ac summus, quem in hoc studio singulos serio intendere oportet, est ipsius Dei gloria 1 Petr. II, 9. Ut virtutes praedicetis illius, qui vos vocavit e tenebris in admirabilem lucem suam. Confer Prov. xvi, 4. Rom. xi, 36. 1 Cor. x, 31.
units.tr: The primary and highest end, which each person ought seriously to aim at in this study, is the glory of God himself. 1 Pet. ii. 9. "That you may proclaim the virtues of him who called you out of darkness into his marvellous light." Compare Prov. xvi. 4. Rom. xi. 36. 1 Cor. x. 31.

units.la: Subordinatur illi Beatitudo nostra, & gloria aeterna. Psal. i, 1, 2. "Beatus vir, qui in Lege Jehovae voluntas "tas ejus, & in lege ejus meditatur die ac noćte. 1 Sam. "11. 30. " Dicit Jehovah; -Honorantes me honorabo. "Adde Ioh. v, 39. xx, 31. Rom. 1, 16. 2 Tim. iii, 15. Sed in reprobis eventus per accidens est, eorum convictio, & gravior condemnatio. Luc. xii, 47. "Ille "autem servus, qui novit voluntatem Domini sui, neque "se comparavit, neque se gessit ex ejus voluntate, cædetur multis (plagis.) Adde Ezech. ii, 5, 7. iii. 27. 2 Cor. ii, 15, 16. Luc. ii, 34.
units.tr: Our blessedness and eternal glory are subordinate to this. Ps. i. 1, 2. "Blessed is the man who in the law of Jehovah meditates day and night." 1 Sam. ii. 30. "Jehovah says: Those who honour me I will honour." Add John v. 39; xx. 31. Rom. i. 16. 2 Tim. iii. 15. But in the reprobate it is an incidental outcome: their conviction and heavier condemnation. Luke xii. 47. "But that servant who knew the will of his lord, and neither prepared himself nor acted according to his will, will be beaten with many blows." Add Ezek. ii. 5, 7; iii. 27. 2 Cor. ii. 15, 16. Luke ii. 34.

units.la: XXXVIII. Beatitudo ista in hac vita inchoatur; in altera consummabitur.
units.tr: XXXVIII. This blessedness begins in this life and will be consummated in the next.

units.la: Caput rei est Communio nostra cum Deo. 1 Joh. 1, 3, 4. "Quod vidimus & audivimus, id annunciamus "vobis; ut & vos communionem habeatis nobiscum: & "communio nostra sit cum Patre, & cum Filio ejus Jesu "Christo. Et hoc scribimus vobis, ut gaudium vestrum "sit plenum. Psal. xxxiii. 12. Beata gens, cujus Jehovah "est Deus: populus, quem elegit in hæreditatem sibi.
units.tr: The heart of the matter is our communion with God. 1 John i. 3, 4. "What we have seen and heard we announce to you, so that you may have communion with us; and our communion is with the Father, and with his Son Jesus Christ. And we write this to you, so that your joy may be full. Ps. xxxiii. 12. Blessed is the nation whose God is Jehovah, the people whom he chose as his inheritance."

units.la: Hoc bonum propterea 1. Deus promisit: Gen. xv, 1. xvii, 7.
units.tr: For this reason, this good was promised by God first: Gen. xv. 1; xvii. 7.

units.la: 2. Christus suo merito nobis acquisivit: 1 Petr. iii, 18. Eph. ii, 12, 13, 16, 19.
units.tr: Second, Christ acquired it for us by his merit: 1 Pet. iii. 18. Eph. ii. 12, 13, 16, 19.

units.la: 3. Atque intercessione sua applicari petit: Joh. xvii, 11, 21, 22, 23. cum Hebr. vii, 25.
units.tr: Third, by his intercession he seeks that it be applied: John xvii. 11, 21, 22, 23, with Heb. vii. 25.

units.la: 4. Fideles autem cum summa oblectatione illud percipiunt: Psal. iv, 7, 8. xxxiii, 21, 22. xxxvi, 8, 9, 10. lxxiii, 25, 26.
units.tr: Fourth, the faithful receive it with the greatest delight: Ps. iv. 7, 8; xxxiii. 21, 22; xxxvi. 8, 9, 10; lxxiii. 25, 26.

units.la: XXXIX. Hinc ergo scaturiunt omnia ζωῆς τῆς ζωῆς, καὶ τῆς εὐδαιμονίας, requisita. 2 Petr. I, 3, 4. "Prout Divina vis ipsius omnia nobis donavit, "quæ ad vitam & pietatem (pertinent):-ut per hæc efficeremini Divinæ consortes naturæ. Adde Joh. I, 16. Col. II, 9, 10. Psal. xxxiii. Eph. i, 3. Rom. viii, 31, 32. Matth. vi, 25-33.
units.tr: XXXIX. From this flow all the requisites of life and of blessedness [ζωῆς τῆς ζωῆς, καὶ τῆς εὐδαιμονίας]. 2 Pet. i. 3, 4. "Since his divine power has given us all things that pertain to life and godliness, so that through these you might become partakers of the divine nature." Add John i. 16. Col. ii. 9, 10. Ps. xxxiii. Eph. i. 3. Rom. viii. 31, 32. Matt. vi. 25-33.

units.la: Ita scit. 1. sanctam & gloriosam Dei imaginem habemus bemus nobis restitutam: Col. iii,10. Eph. iv,24. Rom. vi,11,13.
units.tr: Thus we know: 1. we have the holy and glorious image of God restored to us: Col. iii. 10. Eph. iv. 24. Rom. vi. 11, 13.

units.la: Et 2. pacem illam Dei, quae omnem mentem exsuperat: Phil. iv,7.
units.tr: And 2. that peace of God which surpasses every mind: Phil. iv. 7.

units.la: 3. Spe servati fumus: Rom. viii,24. sed certissimâ, quae minime confundit expectantem: Rom. v,3,4.
units.tr: 3. We are saved by hope: Rom. viii. 24, but a most certain hope, which does not disappoint the one who waits: Rom. v. 3, 4.

units.la: Et 4. gaudium percipimus gloriosum, ineffabile, perpetuum: 1 Petr. i,8,9. 1 Thess. v,16. In ipsis etiam adversis: Jac. i,2. Rom. v,3,4,5. viii,17,18,28,35.
units.tr: And 4. we receive a glorious, inexpressible, perpetual joy: 1 Pet. i. 8, 9. 1 Thess. v. 16. Even in adversities: James i. 2. Rom. v. 3, 4, 5; viii. 17, 18, 28, 35.

units.la: XL. Adcoque Θεολογία nostraverè etiàm est Θεοζωία, καὶ Θεypгία: ut Deo & Christo vivamus que operemur.
units.tr: XL. And so our theology is truly also theozoia [Θεοζωία] and theopragia [Θεοπραγία]: that we may live and act for God and Christ.

units.la: Rom. vi,11. "Colligite, vos-vivere Deo, per Christum Jesum Dominum nostrum. xiv, 7,8,9. "Domino vivimus; &c. Gal. ii,19,20. "Ut Deo viverem. - Vivit in me Christus; &c.
units.tr: Rom. vi. 11. "Reckon yourselves to be alive to God, through Christ Jesus our Lord." xiv. 7, 8, 9. "We live to the Lord," etc. Gal. ii. 19, 20. "That I might live to God... Christ lives in me," etc.

units.la: Scil. 1. Ipso intùs in nobis agente, & nos agere faciente: Joh. xv,4,5. 2 Cor. iv,10. xiii,5. Gal. ii,20. Phil. ii,13.
units.tr: Namely: 1. with him acting within us and making us act: John xv. 4, 5. 2 Cor. iv. 10; xiii. 5. Gal. ii. 20. Phil. ii. 13.

units.la: 2. Per fidem ipsius: Gal. ii,20. Eph. iii,17.
units.tr: 2. Through his faith: Gal. ii. 20. Eph. iii. 17.

units.la: 3. Secundùm voluntatem ipsius: 1 Petr. iv,2,6. Rom. xii,1,2.
units.tr: 3. According to his will: 1 Pet. iv. 2, 6. Rom. xii. 1, 2.

units.la: Ac tandem 4. in gloriam ipsius. 1 Cor. x,31. Phil. i,20. Col. iii,17.
units.tr: And finally, 4. to his glory: 1 Cor. x. 31. Phil. i. 20. Col. iii. 17.

units.la: Atque ista vita, essentialiter eadem, est aeterna; quae nunc modò habemus: Joh. iii,36. v,24. xvii,3. & quidem in nobis manentem: 1 Joh. iii,15. per Spiritum vivificantem, qui in nobis est; Joh. vi,63. 2 Cor. iii,6. Rom. viii,11. idemque est Spiritus adoptionis, & arrhabo futurae haereditatis nostrae coelestis: Rom. viii,15,16,17. 2 Cor. i,21,22. Eph. i,13,14. iv,30.
units.tr: And this life, essentially the same as the one we now have, is eternal: John iii. 36; v. 24; xvii. 3. And indeed it remains in us: 1 John iii. 15. It is through the Spirit who quickens, who is in us: John vi. 63. 2 Cor. iii. 6. Rom. viii. 11. It is also the same Spirit of adoption and the pledge of our future heavenly inheritance: Rom. viii. 15, 16, 17. 2 Cor. i. 21, 22. Eph. i. 13, 14; iv. 30.

units.la: XLI. Perficietur ista Beatitudo primùm in animâ separata; ac tandem absolutissimè consummabitur in personâ integra, quin & universa Ecclesiâ electorum, novissimo die, in beata resurrectione. Ea excludet omnem dolorem ac miseriam: Apoc. xxi, 3, 4. omnemque imperfectionem abolebit: 1 Cor. xiii, 9, -12. Afferet autem bona, quæ oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in mentem hominis venerunt: 1 Cor. ii, 9. dùm ipse Deus erit omnia in omnibus: 1 Cor. xv, 28. Quæ quidem plenius exponenda venient suo loco, in cap. de Glorificatione.
units.tr: XLI. This blessedness will be perfected first in the separated soul, and finally will be most fully consummated in the whole person, and indeed in the whole Church of the elect, on the last day, in the blessed resurrection. It will exclude all grief and misery: Rev. xxi. 3, 4. It will abolish every imperfection: 1 Cor. xiii. 9-12. It will bring the good things which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor which have entered the human mind: 1 Cor. ii. 9, when God himself will be all in all: 1 Cor. xv. 28. These things will be explained more fully in their place, in the chapter on Glorification.

units.la: Sed veram ac solidam Beatitudinem, ipsumque Summum bonum, in natura temerè quæsiverunt, & promiserunt, Philosophi Gentiles.
units.tr: But the true and solid blessedness, and the highest good itself, the Gentile philosophers rashly sought and promised from nature alone.

units.la: XLII. Media Theologiæ sic feliciter consequendę sunt, 1. potissimum SS. Literæ, Rom. xv, 4. Nam quæ ante scripta sunt, ad nos docendos ante scripta sunt, &c. Adde 2 Tim. iii, 15, 16, 17. Ioh. xx, 31.
units.tr: XLII. The means by which theology is happily attained are: 1. above all the Holy Scriptures. Rom. xv. 4. "For whatever was written before was written for our instruction," etc. Add 2 Tim. iii. 15, 16, 17. John xx. 31.

units.la: 2. Ut rectè iis utamur, adsit humilis Dei reverentia, & pia Precatio. Psal. cxi, 10. "Principium sapientiæ, timor Iehovæ. Adde Prov. i, 7. ix, 10. Iob. xxviii, 28. Psal. xxv, 9, 12. Spiritus autem humiliationis & gratiæ, idem est precum: Zach. xii, 10. Hic ergo docet nos precari, atque ita quærere; & sic porrò facit ut inveniamus: Iac. i, 5. "Quodsi cui vestrum deest sapientia, petito a Deo, qui dat (eam) omnibus benignè, &c. Adde Matth. vii, 7. Psalm. xxv, 4, 5. cxix, 12, 18, 26, 27. &c.
units.tr: 2. That we may use them rightly, let there be humble reverence for God and pious prayer. Ps. cxi. 10. "The fear of Jehovah is the beginning of wisdom." Add Prov. i. 7; ix. 10. Job xxviii. 28. Ps. xxv. 9, 12. The Spirit of humiliation and grace is also the Spirit of prayer: Zech. xii. 10. He therefore teaches us to pray, and so to seek; and thus in turn he makes us find: James i. 5. "But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives to all generously," etc. Add Matt. vii. 7. Ps. xxv. 4, 5; cxix. 12, 18, 26, 27, etc.

units.la: 3. Adhibeatur sedula Meditatio, atque indefessum Studium rerum Divinarum.
units.tr: 3. Let there be diligent meditation and tireless study of divine things.

units.la: Hùc pertinet primariò pia ac frequens Lectio S. Scripturæ; & secundariò etiam scriptorum Ecclesiasticorum. 1 Tim. iv, 13. "Intentus esto lectioni. Adde 2 Tim. iii, 14, 15, 17. iv, 13.
units.tr: To this belongs chiefly pious and frequent reading of Holy Scripture, and secondarily also of ecclesiastical writers. 1 Tim. iv. 13. "Be attentive to reading." Add 2 Tim. iii. 14, 15, 17; iv. 13.

units.la: Accedat avida atque obediens auditio explicationum & applicationum: Rom. x, 17. Eph. iv, 11. 1 Thess. v, 12, 13.
units.tr: Let there be added eager and obedient hearing of explanations and applications: Rom. x. 17. Eph. iv. 11. 1 Thess. v. 12, 13.

units.la: Nec non sancta scrutatio, ac prudens discretio: Ioh. v, 39. Act. xvii, 11. Phil. i, 10. 1 Thess. v, 21. 1 Joh. iv, 1.
units.tr: Nor the holy searching, and prudent discernment: John v. 39. Acts xvii. 11. Phil. i. 10. 1 Thess. v. 21. 1 John iv. 1.

units.la: Ac porrò diligens ruminatio; Luc. ii, 19. Itémque modesta cum aliis collatio: Col. iii, 16.
units.tr: Further, diligent pondering: Luke ii. 19. Likewise modest comparison with others: Col. iii. 16.

units.la: 1 Thess. v, 11.
units.tr: 1 Thess. v. 11.

units.la: Tandem perpetua applicatio ad praxin: Tit. II, 11, 12. 2 Tim. iii, 16. Joh. xvii, 17. xiii, 17.
units.tr: Finally, constant application to practice: Titus ii. 11, 12. 2 Tim. iii. 16. John xvii. 17. xiii. 17.

units.la: Istis autem ancillantur Studia Linguarum, Hebraeae potissimum & Graecae; ac porrò Artium, Grammatica, Rhetoricae, & Logicae: quin & Philosophiae sobriae: nec non Historiarum, Geographiae, & Chronologiae.
units.tr: These are served by the studies of languages, Hebrew and Greek above all; then by the arts, grammar, rhetoric and logic; and indeed by sober philosophy; and likewise by history, geography and chronology.

units.la: 4. Necessario etiam est Militia spiritualis: 1 Tim. vi, 12. „ Decerta praeclarum illud certamen fidei.
units.tr: 4. Spiritual warfare is also necessary: 1 Tim. 6:12, "Fight the good fight of faith."

units.la: Hic autem strenuè resistendum est hostibus nostris spiritualibus, eorumque tentationibus, contra Dei veritatem, justitiam, & sanctitatem; aut Verbi Divini sinceritatem: Psal. lxxiii, 2, 3, 13, 14, 16, 17.
units.tr: Here we must vigorously resist our spiritual enemies and their temptations against the truth, justice and holiness of God, or the sincerity of the Divine Word: Ps. 73:2, 3, 13, 14, 16, 17.

units.la: Itemque ad superbiam; 1 Cor. viii, 1. 1 Petr. v, 5, 6, aut disputationes curiosas, & contentiones acres; 1 Tim. i, 4. iv, 7. vi, 20, 21. 2 Tim. ii, 16, 23, 24, 25. Tit. i, 14. iii, 9.
units.tr: Likewise against pride: 1 Cor. 8:1; 1 Pet. 5:5, 6; or against curious disputations and sharp contentions: 1 Tim. 1:4; 4:7; 6:20, 21; 2 Tim. 2:16, 23, 24, 25; Tit. 1:14; 3:9.

units.la: Nec non ad remissionem, otium, aut profanitatem; Rom. xii, 11. Phil. iii, 14, -18. 1 Tim. vi, 5.
units.tr: Nor against slackness, idleness or profanity: Rom. 12:11; Phil. 3:14–18; 1 Tim. 6:5.

units.la: Per omnia nitendum est Christo, ejusque robore; tenenda spiritualis armatura; & perseverandum in officiis nostris: Phil. iv, 13. 2 Tim. ii, 1, 19. 1 Thess. v, 24. Eph. vi, 10, -18. 1 Petr. v, 8. 1 Tim. iv, 13, 15, 16. vi, 11, 12.
units.tr: In all things we must strive towards Christ and rely on his strength; we must hold fast the spiritual armour and persevere in our duties: Phil. 4:13; 2 Tim. 2:1, 19; 1 Thess. 5:24; Eph. 6:10–18; 1 Pet. 5:8; 1 Tim. 4:13, 15, 16; 6:11, 12.

units.la: XLIII. Theologiae supernaturali repugnant potissimum Infidelitas Judaeorum & Muhammedistarum; Apostasia Pontificiorum, nominatim in ipsorum Theologia Scholastica; Haeresies Socinianorum, Libertinorum, Anabaptistarum, Remonstrantium, &c. Itemque omnis impietas, profanitas, &c. contra supernaturalem Dei revelationem.
units.tr: XLIII. Supernatural theology is chiefly opposed by the unbelief of the Jews and Muhammadans; the apostasy of the Papists, especially in their Scholastic theology; the heresies of the Socinians, Libertines, Anabaptists, Remonstrants, etc. Likewise every impiety and profanity, etc., against the supernatural revelation of God.

units.la: XLIV. Distributio Theologiae nostrae desumenda est ex objecto subordinato; Religione: Sic autem duae ejus partes occurrunt: prior, de Fide; sive rectâ Agnitione rerum credendarum, aut veritatum Divinitus nitus nobis revelatarum: posterior, de Charitate; seu piâ Observantiâ eorum, quæ Deus nobis facienda præscripsit. Utramque tradit Theologia docens; earumque exercitio occupatur Theologia utens, seu ipsa Religio Act. xxiv, 14, 15, 16. „Ut qui credam omnibus, „quæ in Lege & in Prophetis scripta sunt. - Interea vero „ipse (me) exerceo, ad conscientiam omni tempore habendam sine offensa apud Deum, & apud homines. Ad de 1 Tim. 1, 19. 2 Tim. 1, 13. Tit. iii, 8.
units.tr: XLIV. The division of our theology is to be drawn from its subordinate object, religion. Thus two parts present themselves: the first, concerning faith, or the correct knowledge of the things to be believed, or of the truths revealed to us by God; the second, concerning charity, or the devout observance of those things which God has prescribed for us to do. Teaching theology delivers both, and using theology, or religion itself, is occupied with their exercise: Acts 24:14–16, "that I believe all things which are written in the Law and in the Prophets. And in this I exercise myself, to have always a conscience without offence before God and before men." Add 1 Tim. 1:19; 2 Tim. 1:13; Tit. 3:8.

units.la: XLV. Praxis denique hæc esto: 1. Theologiam ipsius Dei piè admiremur, & celebremus! Rom. xi, 33, 34.
units.tr: XLV. Finally, the practice of this shall be as follows: 1. Let us piously admire and celebrate the theology of God himself! Rom. 11:33, 34.

units.la: 2. Theologiam unionis in Christo Mediatore & Capite nostro itâ consideremus, ut per communionem nostram cum ipso, ex illâ plenitudine, nos etiam pro nostro modulo repleamur! Joh. iii, 34. 1, 16. Col. ii, 3, 9, 10.
units.tr: 2. Let us so consider the theology of union in Christ, our Mediator and Head, that through our communion with him we may also, according to our measure, be filled from that fullness! John 3:34; 1:16; Col. 2:3, 9, 10.

units.la: 3. Ad Theologiam visionis, in hoc mortali corpore degentes, à Domino peregrinantes, & fide interim ambulantes, aspiremus serio! 2 Cor. v, 1, 6, 7. 1 Joh. iii, 2. Matth. v, 8. cum xviii, 10. Phil. i, 23.
units.tr: 3. While we dwell in this mortal body, are away from the Lord, and walk meanwhile by faith, let us earnestly aspire to the theology of vision! 2 Cor. 5:1, 6, 7; 1 John 3:2; Matt. 5:8, with 18:10; Phil. 1:23.

units.la: 4: Theologiam naturalem sic excolamus, ut ipsa supernaturali, sed verè salutari, ex gratiâ Dei in Christo, perficiatur & sanctificetur! Rom. i, 19, 20. Act. xvii, 26, 27, 28. cum Tit. i, 15, ii, 11, 12-14.
units.tr: 4. Let us so cultivate natural theology that it may be perfected and sanctified by supernatural, yet truly saving, grace from God in Christ! Rom. 1:19, 20; Acts 17:26–28, with Tit. 1:15; 2:11–14.

units.la: 5. Theologiæ nostræ Finem gloriosissimum sic intueamur serio, & Media ejus propria ac necessaria sic adhibeamus religiosè, ut certò illum consequamur: neque unquàm reprobi, & qui incassum laboraverimus, deprehendamur! Hebr. xi, 1, 13, 14, 16, 26. Phil. iii, 8, 13-16. 1 Cor. ix, 23, 27.
units.tr: 5. Let us earnestly keep in view the most glorious end of our theology, and religiously apply its proper and necessary means, so that we surely attain it and are never found reprobate or to have laboured in vain! Heb. 11:1, 13, 14, 16, 26; Phil. 3:8, 13–16; 1 Cor. 9:23, 27.

units.la: CAPVT.
units.tr: CHAPTER.

units.la: CAPUT II. DE FIDE.
units.tr: CHAPTER II. CONCERNING FAITH.

units.la: Quid vox alias notet; & quid hoc loco. Quaeruplex Fides. 1. Fides Divina. Non potest ei iubesse falsum, 2. Objectiones solvuntur. 3. Veritas testimonio Divino confirmata, quibus modis. Requisita ad Fidem constituendam. 4. Necessitas Notitia probatur. 5. Sententia Pontificiorum. Objectio solvitur. 6. Fides implicita, seu Carbonaria. 7. Assensus omninò necessarius; exclusâ Dubitatione. 8. Objectum Fidei Divinae in universum. Fides merè historica. Fides in ra-culorum, activa, & passiva. 9. Fides Evangelica. Temporaria. 10. Fides salvifica. Ejus fundamentum. Justificans. 11. Specialis applicatio probatur contra Pontificios. 12. Objectiones solvuntur. 13. Definitur Fides salvifica. Est virtus habitualiter. 14. Quomodò se habeat ad historicam, & temporariam; itemque miraculorum. 15. Subjectum quod. 16. Subjectum quo; Intellectus. Objectiones solvuntur. 17. Ejus origo. 18. Efficacia verbi. 19. Analysis fidei. 20. Methodus. 21. Fructus. 22. Efficacia ad praxin pietatis promovendam. 23. Solvitur dubium, An rectè dicatur virtus, aut actus obedientialis; cum objectionibus. 24. Usus practici hujus doctrinae, 25.
units.tr: What the word fides means elsewhere, and what it means here. Faith is of two kinds. 1. Divine faith. It cannot be commanded to falsehood. 2. Objections are answered. 3. Truth confirmed by divine testimony, and in what ways. The requisites for establishing faith. 4. The necessity of knowledge is proved. 5. The opinion of the Papists. An objection is answered. 6. Implicit faith, or collier's faith. 7. Assent altogether necessary, with doubt excluded. 8. The object of divine faith in general. Merely historical faith. Faith in miracles, active and passive. 9. Evangelical faith. Temporary faith. 10. Saving faith. Its foundation. Justifying faith. 11. Specific application is proved against the Papists. 12. Objections are answered. 13. Saving faith is defined. It is a virtue, as a habit. 14. How it stands in relation to historical and temporary faith, and likewise to faith in miracles. 15. The subject which. 16. The subject by which: the intellect. Objections are answered. 17. Its origin. 18. The efficacy of the Word. 19. Analysis of faith. 20. Method. 21. Fruit. 22. Its efficacy for promoting the practice of piety. 23. The doubt is resolved: whether it is rightly called a virtue or an obedient act; with objections. 24. Practical uses of this doctrine. 25.

units.la: I. Ides alias notat, dictorum conventorumque veritatem & constantiam. Ita dicimus, Fidem alicui servare, aut praestare; &c. Sed hoc loco est Actus credendi; sive, Actus mentis testimonio alterius assensum praebentis; quemadmodum dicitur, Fidem alicui habere, vel adhibere. Spectatur hic Veritas in testimonio, sive in dictis alterius; & qui de ea persuasus est, assensum illi praebet, sive credit. Graece πίστις nuncupatur; unde πιστεύω, credo; ex praeterito passivo πέπεισμαι, persuasus est. Hebraice אמן; sed אמת; & אמונה, veritatem designant. Verum pro duplici Testimonio, vel Divino, vel Humano; Fides etiam vel Divina spectari potest, vel Humana: quarum prior nunc nostrae considerationis est.
units.tr: Faith (fides) elsewhere means the truthfulness and constancy of words and agreements, as when we say to keep faith with someone or to show it. Here, however, it is the act of believing, that is, the act of the mind giving assent on the testimony of another, just as we say to have faith in someone or to place faith in him. What is looked at here is the truth in the testimony, that is, in the words of another; and whoever is persuaded of it gives assent to him, or believes. In Greek it is called [πίστις], whence [πιστεύω], I believe, and from the passive perfect [πέπεισμαι], he is persuaded. In Hebrew it is [אמן]; but [אמת] and [אמונה] signify truth. Now, since testimony is twofold, either divine or human, faith too can be regarded either as divine or as human; of these, the former is the subject of our consideration now.

units.la: II. Fides Divina sequitur testimonium Divinum; & propter hujus primam & absolute perfectissimam veritatem, certissima est & absolute infallibilis. Sed aliter se habet fides humana. Rom. iii, 4. "Imo esto Deus verax; omnis autem homo mendax."
units.tr: II. Divine faith follows divine testimony; and because of the first and absolutely most perfect truth of this testimony, it is most certain and absolutely infallible. But human faith is otherwise. Rom. 3:4: "Yea, let God be true, but every man a liar."

units.la: Hinc fidei Divinae objective non potest subesse falsum: cum proprium ejus objectum sit testimonium Divinum, quod necessario verum est; quandoquidem fieri non potest, ut Deus mentiatur; vel aliquod falsum suo testimonio afferat, & sic credendum proponat. Num. xxiii, 19. "Non est homo Deus, ut mentiatur, &c." Tit. i, 2. "Deus ille mentiri nescius. Hebr. vi, 18. Per duas res immutabiles, in quibus fieri non potest, ut mentitus sit Deus, &c. Adde 1 Sam. xv, 29. 2 Tim. ii, 13. Job. iii, 33. 1 Joh. v, 9, 10.
units.tr: Hence falsehood cannot underlie divine faith objectively, since its proper object is divine testimony, which is necessarily true; for it cannot happen that God should lie, or set forth anything false by his testimony and so propose it to be believed. Num. 23:19: "God is not a man, that he should lie, etc." Titus 1:2: "God, who cannot lie." Heb. 6:18: "By two immutable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, etc." Add 1 Sam. 15:29; 2 Tim. 2:13; John 3:33; 1 John 5:9, 10.

units.la: III. Obj. 1. Adam lapsus, fide Divina credere debuit, se cum omnibus posteris suis aeternum fuisse condemnandum: hoc tamen falsum fuisse patet ex eventu. Ergo, &c. Resp. Credera solum debuit, se cum posteris reum condemnationis, juxta sanctionem, Gen. II. 17. adeoque condemnandum fuisse, nisi sufficiens remedium intervenisset: sed hoc remedium excludere non debuit, aut potuit, fide Divinâ.
units.tr: III. Objection 1. Adam, having fallen, ought to have believed by divine faith that he, together with all his posterity, would be condemned to eternity; yet this was plainly false, as the outcome shows. Therefore, etc. Answer. He ought only to have believed that he, together with his posterity, was liable to condemnation under the sanction of Gen. 2:17, and so would be condemned unless a sufficient remedy intervened; but he ought not, and could not, by divine faith exclude this remedy.

units.la: Obj. 2. Abraham similiter credere debuit, Gen. XXII. filium suum Isaacum per immolationem fuisse moriturum: &c. Resp. Imò tantùm, se obligatum ad peragendam istam immolationem: sed quid de eâ futurum esset, ex eventu, vel aliâ Dei revelatione, discere debuit.
units.tr: Objection 2. Abraham similarly ought to have believed, Gen. 22, that his son Isaac would die by being sacrificed; etc. Answer. Rather, he ought only to have believed that he was bound to carry out that sacrifice; but what would become of it he had to learn from the outcome, or from some other revelation of God.

units.la: Obj. 3. Moses & Aharon credere debuerunt, aquas ad alloquium suum profiliturlas fuisse ex petrâ; Num. XX, 8, & seqq. id enim Deus promiserat: neque tamen factum est: ergò, &c. Resp. Miraculum reipsâ secutum non est ad istud signum; quoniam signum istud non praecesslt; sed ab illis malè ac diffidenter neglectum fuit. Idem tamen effectus, ad aliud signum, ab illis interim adhibitum, secutus est; juxta promissionem Dei generalem, & decretum effectivum, quod eventu manifestatum est.
units.tr: Objection 3. Moses and Aaron ought to have believed that waters would gush out of the rock at their word, Num. 20:8 and following, for God had promised this; yet it did not happen; therefore, etc. Answer. The miracle did not in fact follow upon that sign, since that sign did not precede it; rather, they neglected it badly and distrustfully. Nevertheless the same effect followed upon another sign, which they used in the meantime, in accordance with God's general promise and his effective decree, which was made manifest by the outcome.

units.la: Obj. 4. Ezechias credere debuit, se brevi post alloquium Jesaiae moriturum; Jes. XXXVIII. quod tamen verum non fuisse, docuit eventus: ergò, &c. Resp. Imò credere debuit, morbum istum ratione gravitatis suae, & virium ipsius, fuisse lethalem; atque adeo ejus exitum futurum ad mortem; nisi per singularem praxin resipiscentiae, humilemque ac fidelem deprecationem, extraordinariam sanationem consequeretur. Hoc autem factum est, quemadmodum Deus solet in comminationibus saepius tacitam conditionem intelligere: Jerem. XVIII, 7, 8.
units.tr: Objection 4. Hezekiah ought to have believed that he would die shortly after Isaiah's address, Isa. 38; yet the outcome showed this was not true; therefore, etc. Answer. Rather, he ought to have believed that this sickness, by reason of its severity and his own strength, was deadly, and so its end would be death; unless, through a singular exercise of repentance and a humble and faithful prayer, he obtained an extraordinary healing. This in fact happened, just as God is accustomed in his threats to understand a tacit condition more than once: Jer. 18:7, 8.

units.la: Obj. 5. Discipuli credere debuerunt, Matth. XVII, 20. Diabolum istum ipsorum operâ fuisse ejiciendum; quod tamen factum non est. Resp. Factum non est; quia Discipuli non adhibuerunt media necessaria, jejunium, preces, & mandatum cum fiduciâ conjunctum, ut exi-
units.tr: Objection 5. The disciples ought to have believed, Matt. 17:20, that the devil would be cast out by their work; yet this did not happen. Answer. It did not happen because the disciples did not employ the necessary means: fasting, prayers, and the command joined with confidence, so that

units.la: Note: the lower-left printed text is faint; no further footnotes are legible. ret Diabolus. Credere autem solummodo debuerunt, rem succesturam fuisse, si media rite adhibuissent; quod verum erat.
units.tr: Note: the lower-left printed text is faint; no further footnotes are legible. ...the devil might be driven out. They ought only to have believed that the thing would succeed if they had used the means rightly; and this was true.

units.la: Obj. 6. Reprobi, Euangelium audientes, tenentur credere, Christum pro ipsis etiam mortuum: quod interim verum non est. Resp. Tenentur credere quod Euangelio proponitur; & sicut proponitur: sed non absolute, aut immediatè, Christum pro ipsis etiam esse mortuum. Ad specialem ejusmodi applicationem procedendum est methodo, quam Euangelium praescribit: positis ponendis, &c.
units.tr: Objection 6. The reprobate, hearing the Gospel, are bound to believe that Christ died also for them; yet this is in fact not true. Answer. They are bound to believe what is proposed in the Gospel, and as it is proposed; but not absolutely or immediately that Christ died also for them. For such a special application one must proceed by the method which the Gospel prescribes: the things to be placed first being placed first, etc.

units.la: IV. Hic igitur occurrit veritas testimonio Divino propósita & confirmata, sive ab ipso Deo immediatè: sive mediatè per Angelos, aut Homines Θεοπνεύστως; sive ex iis etiam per alios: sic tamen, ut ad externa media, accedat interna & immediata Spiritus Sancti illuminatio & obsignatio. 1 Thess. 11, 13. Gratias agimus Deo sine intermissione, quòd acceptum de Deo sermonem, quem audistis ex nobis, exceperitis, non ut sermonem hominum, sed (sicut est verè) ut Dei sermonem: qui etiam agit in vobis, qui creditis, 2 Cor. 1, 21, 22. Qui nos confirmat vobiscum in Christum, & qui unxit nos, Deus (est.) Qui etiam obsignavit nos, indiditque arrhaabonem Spiritus cordibus nostris.
units.tr: IV. Here, then, truth set forth and confirmed by divine testimony meets us, whether immediately by God himself, or mediately through angels, or through men inspired by God (Θεοπνεύστως); or even through others from among these; yet in such a way that to the outward means there is added the inward and immediate illumination and sealing of the Holy Spirit. 1 Thess. 2:13: "We thank God without ceasing, that when you received from us the word of God's message, you accepted it not as the word of men, but (as it truly is) as the word of God, who also works in you who believe." 2 Cor. 1:21, 22: "Now he who establishes us with you in Christ, and who has anointed us, is God; who has also sealed us and given us the guarantee of the Spirit in our hearts."

units.la: Sic ad hanc Fidem constituendam prorsus requiritur, tùm Notitia veritatis Divinæ, tùm plenus animi Assensus & acquiescentia in istâ veritate, quia & quatenùs Divina est.
units.tr: Thus, to establish this faith there is absolutely required both knowledge of the divine truth and full assent of the mind and acquiescence in this truth, because and insofar as it is divine.

units.la: V. Notitiam ad Fidem omnino requiri, atque in ejus conceptu involvi, probatur: 1. quia Fides diserte appellatur Cognitio, aut Scientia, per synechdochen; Jes. LIII, 11. Scientiâ sui justificabit justus Servus meus multos. Joh. XVII, 3. Vide sup. cap. 1. th. 2. cum Hab. II, 4. Justus autem fide sua vivet.
units.tr: V. That knowledge is wholly required for faith, and is involved in its concept, is proved: 1. because faith is expressly called knowledge or science, by synecdoche; Isa. 53:11: "By his knowledge shall my righteous Servant justify many." John 17:3; see above, chapter 1, thesis 2; with Hab. 2:4: "But the just shall live by his faith."

units.la: Objecta fidei dicuntur etiam cognosci aut sciri: Joh. „Novi Redemtorem meum esse viven„tem. 2 Cor. v, 1, 2. „Scimus enim nos, si terrestris „hujus domûs tabernaculum dissolutum fuerit, ædifi„cium ex Deo habituros. Adde Eph. i, 17, 18, 19.
units.tr: The objects of faith are also said to be known or understood: Job 19:25: "I know that my Redeemer lives." 2 Cor. 5:1, 2: "For we know that if the earthly house of this tabernacle is dissolved, we have a building from God." Add Eph. 1:17, 18, 19.

units.la: 2. Cùm Fide conjungitur Notitia, tanquàm prorsùs necessaria ad eam constituendam: Joh. vi, 69. „Cre„didimus & scimus, te esse Christum illum, Filium Dei „viventis. 2 Tim. i, 12. Novi cui crediderim. iii, 15. „Quæ (SS. Literæ) te possunt sapientem reddere ad sa„lutem, per fidem, quæ est in Christo Jesû.
units.tr: 2. Knowledge is joined with faith as absolutely necessary for establishing it: John 6:69: "We have believed and know that you are that Christ, the Son of the living God." 2 Tim. 1:12: "I know whom I have believed." 2 Tim. 3:15: "The sacred writings can make you wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus."

units.la: 3. Ex ejus origine, aut modo productionis: Rom. x, 17. „Ergò fides ex auditû (est); auditus autem per „Verbum Dei. Veritas Verbo Dei proposita, auditû percipi debet; atque ità cognosci; ut Fides homini in generetur. Unde etiàm monet Apostolus, Col. iii, 16. „Sermo Christi inhabitet in vobis copiosè cum omni „sapientiâ.
units.tr: 3. From its origin, or its mode of production: Rom. x, 17. "Therefore faith comes from hearing; and hearing comes through the Word of God." The truth proposed in the Word of God must be perceived by hearing, and so known, so that faith is generated in a person. Hence the Apostle also urges, Col. iii, 16: "Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly with all wisdom."

units.la: 4. Ex requisito consequente: Rom. x, 9, 10. „Si pro„fessus fueris ore tuo Dominum Jesum, & crediderìs in„ corde tuo, quòd Deus eum suscitavit ex mortuis, ser„vaberis. Nam corde creditur ad justitiam; fit autem „ore professio ad salutem. 1 Petr. iii, 15. „(Estote) verò „semper parati ad respondendum (ἕτοιμοι ἀπολογίαν) „cum lenitate & timore, cuivis petenti à vobis rationem „ejus quæ in vobis est spei. Matth. xii, 32. — Quisquis „igitur agnoscet Me coram hominibus; agnoscam & Ego eum coram Patre Meo, qui est in cœlis. At verò Confessio illa, sive Agnitio coram hominibus, Notitiam omninò prærequirit, tanquàm Fide comprehensam.
units.tr: 4. From its consequent requirement: Rom. x, 9, 10. "If you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus, and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. For with the heart one believes unto righteousness, but confession is made with the mouth unto salvation." 1 Pet. iii, 15: "But always be ready to give an answer [ἕτοιμοι ἀπολογίαν] with gentleness and fear to anyone who asks you for a reason for the hope that is in you. Matth. xii, 32: "Whoever therefore acknowledges me before men, I will acknowledge him also before my Father who is in heaven." But that confession, or acknowledgment before men, presupposes knowledge, as something grasped by faith.

units.la: VI. Errant ergò Pontificii, dùm afferunt, Fidem tantùm esse viam & gradum ad Notitiam; imò meliùsper Ignorantiam describi, quàm per Notitiam.
units.tr: VI. The Papists therefore err when they assert that faith is only a way and step to knowledge; indeed, it is better described through ignorance than through knowledge.

units.la: Obj.-Jef. v 11, 9. Nisi crediderìtis, non intelligetis. Ergo Fides tantum est conditio præquisita, & gradus ad Intelligentiam. Resp. 1. Vitiosa est Vulgata Versio Latina in membro posteriori. Textus Hebraicus habet; non confirmabimini; sive, non eritis stabiles. 2. Fides unius veritatis potest esse via & gradus ad cognoscendam aliam veritatem, quae virtualiter in priori continetur. Unde tamen non sequitur, Fidem esse tantum viam, &c. aut non statim involvere Notitiam illius veritatis, quae actu creditur.
units.tr: Objection: Isa. vii, 9: "Unless you believe, you will not understand." Therefore faith is only a prerequisite condition and a step to understanding. Reply: (1) The Vulgate Latin version is faulty in the latter clause. The Hebrew text has "you will not be confirmed," or "you will not be stable." (2) The faith of one truth can be a way and step to knowing another truth, which is virtually contained in the former. Yet it does not follow from this that faith is only a way, etc., or that it does not at once involve knowledge of the truth that is actually believed.

units.la: VII. Iidem mirum in modum praedicant Fidem implicitam, quam etiam Carbonariam appellant; ut quis simpliciter credat, quod Ecclesia credit. Sed qui ignorat quid credat Ecclesia, non magis vere istud dicere potest; quàm caecus, se ea videre quae alii vident.
units.tr: VII. The same people strangely preach an implicit faith, which they also call charcoal-burners' faith: namely, that someone simply believes what the Church believes. But one who does not know what the Church believes cannot say this truly any more than a blind man can say that he sees what others see.

units.la: Obj. Atqui admittenda est Fides implicita: scil. ut credas vera esse, quaecunque Verbo Dei comprehensa sunt; quamvis omnium & singulorum explicitam Notitiam atque Intelligentiam non habeas.
units.tr: Objection: Yet implicit faith must be admitted: namely, that you believe whatever is contained in the Word of God is true, even though you do not have explicit knowledge and understanding of all and each of its parts.

units.la: Resp. Fides illic implicita est, quousque Notitia implicita: sed non simpliciter & tantum implicita; non certè circa ipsa principia, & articulos potissimum fundamentales Religionis Christianae.
units.tr: Reply: Faith is implicit there only so far as the knowledge is implicit; but it is not simply and merely implicit, certainly not with regard to the principles themselves, and especially the fundamental articles of the Christian religion.

units.la: VIII. At non sufficit qualiscunque Notitia: haec enim in profanis irrisoribus, Fidem minimè habentibus, frequenter reperitur: 2 Petr. iii, 3, 4. Assensus omnino necessarius est; seu veritatis, quae in Verbo illo inest, pia Agnitio. Hinc Joh. iii, 33. Qui recipit ejus testimonium, is obsignavit Deum veracem esse. 1 Joh. v, 9, 10. Si testimonium hominum accipimus, testimonium Dei majus est: nam hoc est testimonium Dei, quod testificatus est de Filio suo. Qui credit in Filium Dei, habet testimonium in seipso; qui non credit, Deo, mendacem eum facit; quia non credidit testimonio, quod testificatus est Deus de Filio suo.
units.tr: VIII. But no kind of knowledge is enough: for this is often found in profane scoffers who have no faith: 2 Pet. iii, 3, 4. Assent is entirely necessary, that is, a pious acknowledgment of the truth contained in that Word. Hence John iii, 33: "He who receives his testimony has certified that God is true." 1 John v, 9, 10: "If we receive the testimony of men, the testimony of God is greater; for this is the testimony of God, which he has testified concerning his Son. He who believes in the Son of God has the testimony in himself; he who does not believe God makes him a liar, because he has not believed the testimony that God has testified concerning his Son."

units.la: Quin imo sicut objective hic nobis proponitur Veritas Divina, absolutè summa & infallibilis; ita subjectivè Assensus debet esse firmissimus, omnem Dubitationem nem excludens: Rom. iv, 18, - 21. „(Abrahamus) „contra spem sub spe credidit, - Ac minime infirmus fide, „non addubitavit incredulitate: sed corroboratus fuit fide, „tributâ gloriâ Deo. Ac plenè certioratus est, cum) „quod promiserat, posse etiàm efficere, Jac. i, 6, Po„stulet cum fide, nihil ambigens.
units.tr: Indeed, just as the divine truth is set before us objectively as absolutely supreme and infallible, so the assent subjectively ought to be most firm, excluding all doubt: Rom. iv, 18–21: "(Abraham) against hope believed in hope... And not weak in faith, he did not waver in unbelief, but was strengthened in faith, giving glory to God. And he was fully assured that what he had promised he was also able to do." Jas. i, 6: "Let him ask in faith, doubting nothing."

units.la: Quod æquè de rebus futuris accipiendum, acsi jàm „præsentes essent: summam enim certitudinem nobis „præstat Verbum Dei. Hebr. xi, 1. „Est autem fides, „illud quo subsistunt quæ sperantur, & qua demonstrat „quæ non cernuntur. Rom. viii, 25. „Si verò quod non „videmus, speramus, (nempè) per tolerantiam expe„ctamus. 38. „Nam mihi persuasum est, &c.
units.tr: This must equally be understood of future things, as if they were already present; for the Word of God gives us the highest certainty. Heb. xi, 1: "Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen." Rom. viii, 25: "But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with patience." Verse 38: "For I am persuaded, etc."

units.la: IX. Objectum Fidei Divinæ in universum est omne Verum Auctoritate Divinâ propositum & confirmatum. Act. xxiv, 14. Vide sup. cap. i. th. 32.
units.tr: IX. The object of divine faith in general is every truth proposed and confirmed by divine authority. Acts xxiv, 14. See above, chap. i, th. 32.

units.la: At siquis generatim solummodo credat, absque speciali applicatione, & spirituali fiduciâ, per gratiam duntaxat illuminantem & persuadentem; hæc Fides merè historica est: de quâ Jac. ii, 19. Vide sup. cap. i. th. 10. Confer Act. xxvi, 27, 28.
units.tr: But if someone believes only in general, without special application and spiritual trust, and only through grace that illuminates and persuades, this faith is merely historical: concerning which James ii, 19. See above, chap. i, th. 10. Compare Acts xxvi, 27, 28.

units.la: Si effectus aliquis miraculosus spectetur, Fides miraculorum dicitur.
units.tr: If some miraculous effect is considered, it is called the faith of miracles.

units.la: Hæc verò activa est in eo, qui miraculi patrandi causa instrumentalis moralis existit: Matth. xvii, 20. „Si habeatis fidem, quantulum est granum sinapis, „dicetis monti huic, Transgreditor hinc illuc; & transgre„dietur: & nihil impossibile erit vobis. Adde 1 Cor. xiii, „2. Marc. xvi, 17, 18. Matth. vii, 22, 23.
units.tr: This is active in one who is the moral instrumental cause of performing a miracle: Matth. xvii, 20: "If you have faith as small as a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there,' and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you." Add 1 Cor. xiii, 2; Mark xvi, 17, 18; Matth. vii, 22, 23.

units.la: Passiva est in eo, qui effectum miraculosum recipitMatth. ix, 29. Tunc tetigit oculos eorum, dicens:„Secundùm fidem vestram fiat vobis. Adde Actor; xiv, 9, 10.
units.tr: It is passive in one who receives the miraculous effect: Matth. ix, 29: "Then he touched their eyes, saying, 'According to your faith be it done to you.'" Add Acts xiv, 9, 10.

units.la: X. Speciatim tamen hic ea consideranda veniunt, quæ ad Fœdus Euangelicum pertinent, ad reconciliationem noltrî cum Deo, & salutem per Christum ; quæ est Fides Euangelica.
units.tr: X. Specifically, however, those things come into consideration here which pertain to the Gospel covenant, to the reconciliation of us with God, and to salvation through Christ; this is evangelical faith.

units.la: Si hæc solido fundamento & viva radice destituatur, atque interim gaudium aliquod temporarium ex percepta rei bonitate ac novitate adferat, Fides temporaria vocatur. Matth. xiii, 20, 21. „Qui vero in „petrosa semen excepit, is est, qui sermonem audit, „& eum statim cum gaudio accipit. Non habet autem „radicem in se, sed temporarius est: ortâque affliction̈e, „vel persecutione, propter sermonem, statim offenditur. Adde Hebr. vi, 4, 5. Actor. viii, 13, 21.
units.tr: If this lacks a solid foundation and a living root, yet meanwhile brings some temporary joy from the perceived goodness and novelty of the thing, it is called temporary faith. Matth. xiii, 20, 21: "But he who received the seed on stony ground is he who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy. He has no root in himself, but is temporary; and when affliction or persecution arises because of the word, he immediately falls away." Add Heb. vi, 4, 5; Acts viii, 13, 21.

units.la: XI. At si pertendat ad veram unionem & communionem cum Christo, auctore vitæ spiritualis & salutis æternæ, adeòque actus spiritualiter vitales & salutares producat, Fides salvifica nuncupatur. Marc. xvi, 16. „Qui crediderit, servabitur. Eph. ii, 8. Gratia „enim illa estis servati per fidem. Adde Joh. iii, 18, 36. Rom. x, 9, 10, 11.
units.tr: XI. But if it reaches to true union and communion with Christ, the author of spiritual life and eternal salvation, and so produces spiritually vital and saving acts, it is called saving faith. Mark xvi, 16: "Whoever believes will be saved." Eph. ii, 8: "For by grace you have been saved through faith." Add John iii, 18, 36; Rom. x, 9, 10, 11.

units.la: Hæc nititur duplici testimonio Dei, exteriori, in libro Scripturæ & prædicatione Euangelii: Rom. x, 17. Vide sup. cap. 5. & interiori, in libro conscientiæ nostræ; ubi Spiritus Sanctus vitam spiritualem operatur, atque istam gratiam salutarem spiritui nostro attestatur. Eph. ii, 5. „Etiàm nos, cùm in offensis mortui esse- „mus, unà vivificavit cum Christo; (cujus) gratiâ estis „servati. 10, „Nam ipsius sumus opus, conditi in Chri„sto Jesu ad opera bona. I, 13, 14. „In quo etiàm si- „de (ipsi) habitâ obsignati estis per Spiritum illum pro„missionis Sanctum: Qui est arrhabo hæreditatis nostræ, „&c. Adde Rom. viii, 2, 9, 14, 15, 16. 1 Cor. 11, 12. 2, 1, 22. Eph. iv, 30.
units.tr: This rests on a twofold testimony of God: an external one, in the book of Scripture and the preaching of the Gospel, Rom. x, 17 (see above, chap. 5); and an internal one, in the book of our conscience, where the Holy Spirit works spiritual life and attests this saving grace to our spirit. Eph. ii, 5: "Even when we were dead in trespasses, he made us alive together with Christ (by whose grace you have been saved)." Verse 10: "For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works." i, 13, 14: "In whom you also, having believed, were sealed by the Holy Spirit of promise, who is the guarantee of our inheritance," etc. Add Rom. viii, 2, 9, 14, 15, 16; 1 Cor. ii, 12; 2 Cor. i, 22; Eph. iv, 30.

units.la: Eadem quoque Fides justificans appellatur; quatenùs videl. credimus, in Christum nobis à Deo factum justitiam: 1 Cor. 1, 30. & sic justificationem accipimus: Rom. 1, 17. „Justitia Dei per illud (Euang. lium) „revelegitur ex fide in fidem, sicut scriptum est; (Hab. ii, 4.) „Justus vero ex fide vivet. Adde Cap. III, 21, 22, 24–28. IV, 5; 22, 25. V, 1, 11, 18, 19. X, 3, 4, 10.
units.tr: The same faith is also called justifying faith, insofar as we believe that Christ has been made righteousness for us by God: 1 Cor. i, 30; and thus we receive justification. Rom. i, 17: "For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith, as it is written, 'The righteous shall live by faith.'" (Hab. ii, 4.) Add ch. iii, 21, 22, 24–28; iv, 5; 22, 25; v, 1, 11, 18, 19; x, 3, 4, 10.

units.la: XII. Inest igitur in fide salvifica speciali Applicatio bonorum Evangelicorum.
units.tr: XII. Therefore saving faith contains a special application of the Gospel blessings.

units.la: Probatur hoc contra Pontificios; 1. ex professione fidelium: Gal. II, 20. „Vivo „per fidem illam Filii Dei, qui dilexit me, & tradidit semet „ipsum pro me. Psal. XXIII, 1, – „Jehovah pastor meus „(est): non deficiam. In tuguriis germinis accubare sa-„cit me, &c. Etiamsi ambulavero per vallem umbrae mortis, non timebo malum; quoniam Tu mecum es: &c. Adde Job. XIX, 25; Phil. I, 21, 23. Rom. VIII, 33, – 39. X, 9, 10. 2 Cor. V, 1, 2, 6. cum 2 Cor. IV, 13. „Quoniam „habemus eundem Spiritum fidei, secundum illud quod „scriptum est, (Psal. CXVI, 10.) Credidi, & ideo lo„cutus sum, nos quoque credimus, quamobrem etiam „loquimur. 2 Petr. I, 1. – „aeque pretiosam fidem nobiscum „sortitis. Ac porro verf. 3. 4. „Prout Divina vis ip„sius omnia nobis donavit, quae ad vitam & pietatem „(pertinent), per agnitionem illius qui vocavit nos ad „gloriam ac virtutem: Ex eo quod maxima illa nobis „ac pretiosa promissa donavit, &c.
units.tr: This is proved against the Papists. (1) From the profession of believers: Gal. 2:20, "I live by that faith of the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me." Ps. 23:1, "The LORD is my shepherd (he is): I shall not want. He makes me lie down in pastures of green, etc. Even if I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me," etc. Add Job 19:25; Phil. 1:21, 23; Rom. 8:33–39; 10:9, 10; and 2 Cor. 5:1, 2, 6 with 2 Cor. 4:13: "Since we have the same spirit of faith, according to what is written (Ps. 116:10), I believed, and therefore I spoke, we also believe, and therefore we also speak." 2 Pet. 1:1, "who have obtained a faith as precious as ours." And again verses 3 and 4: "As his divine power has given us all things that pertain to life and godliness, through the knowledge of him who called us to glory and virtue; by which he has given us his very great and precious promises," etc.

units.la: 2. Ex Spiritu illo fidei: 2 Cor. IV, 13. qui singulos vere Christianos ducit: Rom. VIII, 9, 14. & docet ea, quae Deus nobis gratificatus est: 1 Cor. II, 12. idemque est Spiritus adoptionis; testificans spiritui nostro, nos esse filios & haeredes Dei, cohaeredes autem Christi: Rom. VIII, 15, 16, 17. estque arrhabo haereditatis nostrae coelestis, 2 Cor. I, 21, 22. Eph. I, 13, 14. IV, 30.
units.tr: (2) From that Spirit of faith: 2 Cor. 4:13, who leads all true Christians individually (Rom. 8:9, 14), and teaches those things which God has freely given us (1 Cor. 2:12). He is also the Spirit of adoption, bearing witness to our spirit that we are children and heirs of God, and fellow-heirs with Christ (Rom. 8:15–17), and he is the pledge of our heavenly inheritance (2 Cor. 1:21, 22; Eph. 1:13, 14; 4:30).

units.la: Quo etiam 3. pertinet Calculus albus; & novum Nomen calculo isti inscriptum, quod ille solus novit, qui ipsum accipit; & Manna occultum: Apoc. II, 17.
units.tr: To this also belongs (3) the white stone, and the new name written on it, which no one knows except the one who receives it, and the hidden manna (Rev. 2:17).

units.la: 4. Ex effectis: animi scil. fiducia, & libertate apud Deum, orta ex fide: Eph. III, 12. Hebr. IV, 16. spei robore: Hebr. XI, 1. & gloriatione, in ipsis etiam adversis, Rom. V, 2, 3.
units.tr: (4) From its effects: namely, confidence of mind and freedom before God, arising from faith (Eph. 3:12; Heb. 4:16), the strength of hope (Heb. 11:1), and boasting even in adversities (Rom. 5:2, 3).

units.la: XIII. Obj. 1. Objecta credenda passim terminis generalibus proponuntur: ergo, &c. Resp. Sed alibi quoque docetur specialis applicatio, ejusque modus ac methodus.
units.tr: XIII. Objection 1. The objects to be believed are everywhere proposed in general terms; therefore, etc. Answer: But elsewhere too the special application is taught, together with its mode and method.

units.la: Obj. 2. Specialis ista applicatio carnalem securitatem inducit: &c. Resp. Neg. Imo ad pietatem promovendam validissima est: quo enim magis cognoscimus singularem Dei & Christi erga nos charitatem, eo magis obligamur ad gratitudinem, novam obedientiam, reverentiam, ac dilectionem vicissim praestandam. 1 Joh. III, 1, 2, 3. IV, 19. 2 Cor. V, 14, 15.
units.tr: Objection 2. This special application induces carnal security; etc. Answer: Denied. Indeed it is most powerful for promoting piety. For the more we know God's and Christ's singular love towards us, the more we are bound in turn to render gratitude, new obedience, reverence and love (1 John 3:1, 2, 3; 4:19; 2 Cor. 5:14, 15).

units.la: XIV. Ex superioribus conficitur definitio
units.tr: XIV. From the above, the definition is drawn up.

units.la: Fides salvifica est virtus Theologica, qua Divinam veritatem eorum, quae Deus Verbo suo revelavit, agnoscimus, & bona Euangelica speciatim ac fiducialiter nobis applicamus, per Spiritum Sanctum.
units.tr: Saving faith is a theological virtue by which, through the Holy Spirit, we acknowledge the divine truth of those things which God has revealed in his Word, and apply the Gospel blessings to ourselves specially and with trust.

units.la: Virtutem dicimus habitualiter: quia in subjecto permanet, & actus, tum elicti, tum imperati ex ea producuntur. 2 Tim. I, 5.
units.tr: We say "virtue" in the habitual sense, because it remains in the subject, and acts, both elicited and commanded, are produced from it (2 Tim. 1:5).

units.la: Memoria repetens eam, quae sinte est, non simulatam fidem, quae habitavit prius in avia tua Loide, & matre tua Eunica, persuasus sum autem, quod in te quoque. Luc. XXII, 32. Ego deprecatus sum pro te, ne deficiat fides tua. Eph. III. 12. In quo habemus loquendi libertatem, & aditum cum fiducia, per fidem ipsius. 17. Ut inhabitet Christus per fidem in cordibus vestris. Galat. V, 6. Fides per charitatem operans.
units.tr: Calling to mind the unfeigned faith that dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am persuaded that it is in you also (2 Tim. 1:5). Luke 22:32, I have prayed for you that your faith may not fail. Eph. 3:12, In whom we have boldness of speech and access with confidence through his faith. 3:17, That Christ may dwell by faith in your hearts. Gal. 5:6, Faith working through love.

units.la: XV. Fides salvifica
units.tr: XV. Saving faith

units.la: eminenter in se continet id quod in mere historica & temporaria inest: illa enim vera ac solida virtus Theologica est, ad vitam spiritualem pertinens; unde ejus expertes, dicuntur alienati a vita Dei, Eph. IV, 18. haec, quasi umbrae, aliqualem ejus similitudinem mentiuntur; atque in multis, vita spirituali destitutis, exsistunt.
units.tr: eminently contains within itself what is found in merely historical and temporary faith. For the former is a true and solid theological virtue, pertaining to spiritual life; whence those who lack it are said to be alienated from the life of God (Eph. 4:18). The latter, like shadows, feign some likeness of it, and exist in many who lack spiritual life.

units.la: Consequenter, quae th. 9, 10, & 11. praepositia est distinctio, potius est vocis ambiguae in sua significata: quam generis in suas species: perperam vero criminantur.
units.tr: Consequently, the distinction proposed in theses 9, 10 and 11 is rather a distinction of an ambiguous word in its meanings than of a genus into its species; and they wrongly accuse us of error.

units.la: Quae th. 9. 10. & 11. nàntur Pontificii, plures à nobis Fidei species constitui. Graviter item errant Remonstrantes; ubi fidem salvificam à temporariâ non essentialiter, sed solâ duratione, distinguunt.
units.tr: The Papists object, as in theses 9, 10 and 11, that we establish several species of faith. The Remonstrants also err gravely, where they distinguish saving faith from temporary faith not essentially but only by duration.

units.la: Similiter Fides miraculorum, ubi cum salvificâ in eodem singulari subjecto existit, non differt ab eâ realiter; sed tantùm respectû quodam ad objecta & effecta. Cæteroquin Fides miraculorum etiam potest esse solùm historica & temporaria; cum adjuncto modo extensionis ad effecta miraculosa.
units.tr: Likewise, faith of miracles, where it exists in the same individual subject as saving faith, does not differ from it really, but only with a certain respect to objects and effects. Otherwise, faith of miracles can also be merely historical and temporary, with the added mode of extension to miraculous effects.

units.la: XVI. Fidei salvificæ subjectum quod sunt Homines electi efficaciter vocati.
