Similarly, it is indicated and taught what and what kind of authority Holy Scripture has, and it is urged that faith be given to it; here alone appears the external cause ministerially helping the knowledge of this authority.

units.la: XVIII. Principalior est ipsa S. Scriptura, Verbum infallibile ipsius Dei Opt. Max. veritas αὐτόπιστον, lux propriis suis radiis fulgens; suæ Divinitatis & auctoritatis characteres clarissimos in se habens, & de se ostendens, ut certo agnoscantur à subjectis capacibus.
units.tr: XVIII. The more principal is Holy Scripture itself, the infallible Word of God the Best and Greatest, truth αὐτόπιστον [self-credible], a light shining with its own rays, having and displaying in itself the most clear marks of its divinity and authority, so that they may be recognised with certainty by those who are capable.

units.la: Huc pertinent 1. Materia, & Forma S. Scripturæ: Doctrina vera, sublimis ac sancta; & stylus simplex, sed majestatem Divinam interim referens; Deut. 1v, 6, 7. Vide sup. th. 4.
units.tr: To this belong, first, the matter and form of Holy Scripture: a true, sublime, and holy doctrine, and a simple style which nevertheless at the same time reflects divine majesty. Deut. iv, 6, 7. See above, th. 4.

units.la: 2. Speciatim Prophetiæ tam multæ, ac variæ, quibus verif &c. xxxix, 34, - 38. xlr, 1, 1⟩-6; 7. Pfal. CVI, 3 3.
units.tr: Second, especially its prophecies, so many and so various, by which the truth... Ezek. xxxix, 34-38. xli, 1, 1-6; 7. Ps. cvi, 3, 3.

units.la: 3. Factis similiter improbatis, aut saltem nullo modo approbatis.
units.tr: Third, the deeds likewise condemned, or at least in no way approved.

units.la: 4. Quin & operibus, vires humanas absolutè excedentibus: quæ sic ad imitationem non sunt proposita. Cujusmodi sunt Opera creationis, Miracula, &c.
units.tr: Fourth, and also works which absolutely exceed human powers, and which are therefore not set before us for imitation. Such are the works of creation, miracles, and so on.

units.la: XXI. Observatâ hâc distinctione facilè intelligitur, quomodo Auctoritas Divina conveniat totiS.Scripturæ, & singulis ejus partibus, ac particulis: 2 Tim. iii, 16, 2 Petr. 1, 19, 20, 21. Rom. xv, 4. 1 Cor. vii, 25, 40. Luc. 1, 41, 42, 67, 68. Act. vi, 8, 10. Quod contra Gentiles & Muhammedanos asserimus ac defendimus: & de libris N. T. non minùs, quàm V. T. contra Judæos.
units.tr: XXI. Having observed this distinction, it is easily understood how the divine authority belongs to all of Holy Scripture, and to its individual parts and particles: 2 Tim. iii, 16; 2 Pet. i, 19, 20, 21; Rom. xv, 4; 1 Cor. vii, 25, 40; Luke i, 41, 42, 67, 68; Acts vi, 8, 10. This we assert and defend against the Gentiles and Muhammadans, and regarding the books of the New Testament no less than the Old, against the Jews.

units.la: Alia tamen est ratio Titulorum præfixorum ipsi Contextui sacro, Subscriptionum ad finem alicubi adjectarum, Distributionis in Capita, Supputationis Versuum, & si quæ sunt illis similia.
units.tr: There is, however, a different reason for the titles prefixed to the sacred text itself, the subscriptions added at the end in some places, the division into chapters, the numbering of verses, and whatever is similar to these.

units.la: XXII. Quoniàm verò SS. Scriptores immediatè & efficaciter inter scribendum ubique acti fuerunt à Spiritu Sancto; 1. nusquàm ipsi de facto erra runt, neque errare potuerunt.
units.tr: XXII. But since the holy writers were immediately and effectively moved by the Holy Spirit everywhere in writing, first, they never in fact erred, nor could they err.

units.la: 2. Nulla usquam occurrit vera dissensio, aut repugnantia: ubi verò species aliqua contrarietatis occurrit, spectandæ sunt regulæ oppositionis, & sic instituenda conciliatio; vel agnoscenda nostra ignorantia.
units.tr: Second, no true dissent or contradiction occurs anywhere; where, however, some appearance of contrariety occurs, the rules of opposition must be considered, and reconciliation thus undertaken, or else our ignorance acknowledged.

units.la: 3. S. Scriptura ubique loquitur secundùm accuratam rerum veritatem, sive proprie id fiat, sive tropicè, nusquàm secundùm erroneam hominum opinionem; sàm in naturalibus, & moralibus, quàm in supernaturalibus. Pfal. xii, 7. Eloquia Jehovæ, eloquia munda, argentum excoctum in fornace terrea, defecatum septies. xix, 8, 9. Lex Jehovæ perfecta, convertens animam: testimonium Iehovæ fidele, sapientem efficiens parvulum. Præcepta Iehovæ recta, lætificantia corcor: præceptum Iehovæ purum, illuminans oculos. Confer sup. th. 4. & cap. 2. th. 2.
units.tr: 3. Holy Scripture speaks everywhere according to the accurate truth of things, whether it does so properly or figuratively, and never according to the erroneous opinion of men. This holds as much for natural and moral matters as for supernatural ones. Ps. 12:7: The words of Jehovah are pure words, silver refined in an earthen furnace, purified seven times. 19:8, 9: The law of Jehovah is perfect, converting the soul; the testimony of Jehovah is sure, making wise the simple. The precepts of Jehovah are right, rejoicing the heart; the commandment of Jehovah is pure, enlightening the eyes. See above, thesis 4, and chapter 2, thesis 2.

units.la: XXIII. Quæ hactenus de Auctoritate S. Scripturæ dicta sunt, non solum sic accipi debent de Autographis, verum etiam de Apographis fideliter factis: prout Deus plurium codicum descriptionem, eorumque familiarem usum, diserte mandavit; Deut. xvii, 18, 19. cum Iof. 1, 8. Psal. 1, 2. Iob. v, 39. xx, 31. Act. xvii, 11. Rom. iv, 23, 24. xv, 4. 1 Cor. x, 11. Col. iii, 16. 1 Tim. iv, 13. 2, iii, 14, 17.
units.tr: XXIII. What has so far been said about the authority of Holy Scripture must be understood not only of the autographs, but also of copies faithfully made. God plainly commanded that many copies be written and that they be used constantly: Deut. 17:18, 19, with Josh. 1:8; Ps. 1:2; Job 5:39; 20:31; Acts 17:11; Rom. 4:23, 24; 15:4; 1 Cor. 10:11; Col. 3:16; 1 Tim. 4:13; 2 Tim. 3:14, 17.

units.la: Eadem interim Veritas, Divinitas, & Auctoritas in Apographis etiam cognoscitur, 1. Exemplarium consensu.
units.tr: Meanwhile the same truth, divinity and authority are also recognised in the copies, (1) from the agreement of the copies;

units.la: 2. Per characteres Divinitatis istic similiter conspicuos.
units.tr: (2) through the marks of divinity that shine out equally in them;

units.la: 3. Accedit Ecclesiæ testimonium.
units.tr: (3) the testimony of the Church is added;

units.la: Et 4. potissimum, efficax Spiritûs Sancti persuasio, Fidem Divinam in nobis producens; quam ne quidem accuratissima manuum cognitio facere posset, aut qualiscunque hominum traditio & attestatio de Autographis, si ea superessent.
units.tr: and (4) chiefly, the effective persuasion of the Holy Spirit producing divine faith in us. Even the most accurate knowledge of languages could not produce this, nor any kind of human tradition and attestation about the autographs, if these still survived.

units.la: XXIV. Verùm Autographa interire Deus sivit: tùm quòd veris Apographis Ecclesiæ satis prospectum sit: tùm etiàm, ne cæteroquin una Ecclesia videretur ab alià dependere; aut reliquis imposita necessitas recurrendi perpetuò ad illam, ubi Autographa exstarent.
units.tr: XXIV. God, however, allowed the autographs to perish: partly because the Church has been sufficiently provided with true copies, and partly so that one Church should not appear to depend on another, or so that the rest would not be under the necessity of constantly resorting to that Church where the autographs were kept.

units.la: Obj. Atqui passim in Codicibus σφάλματα quædam irrepserunt, per Librariorum incuriam, vel inscitiam. Resp. Codices satis multos voluit Deus in Ecclesiâ suâ exstare; ut ubi dubium suboriretur, alii Codices consuli possent, atque itâ scrupulus eximi. Sic interim per infirma operatur Deus, & potentiam suam demonstrat; atque hunc thesaurum in testaceis vasculis haberi voluit:
units.tr: Objection. Yet certain errors (σφάλματα) have crept into the manuscripts here and there, through the carelessness or ignorance of the copyists. Answer. God willed that a good number of manuscripts should exist in his Church, so that where a doubt arose, other manuscripts could be consulted, and the difficulty removed in this way. Thus God works through weak means meanwhile and demonstrates his power, and he willed that this treasure be kept in earthen vessels:

units.la: 2 Cor. xii, 9. iv, 7.

XXV. Sed nullis planè Versionibus formalis ista ἀνθρώπινα competit: nec speciatim Vulgatæ Latinæ; quam Concilium Tridentinum decrevit pro authentica habendam. Nam 1. est opus humano studio, non autem à viris Θεοπνεύστοις, concinnatum.
units.tr: XXV. But this formal quality of being human (ἀνθρώπινα) belongs to no versions whatever, and in particular not to the Latin Vulgate, which the Council of Trent decreed should be held authentic. For (1) it is a work produced by human diligence, and not by men inspired by God (Θεοπνεύστοις).

units.la: 2. Ex variis auctoribus conflatum est.
units.tr: (2) It was compiled from various authors.

units.la: 3. Saepius interpolatum & correctum, etiam postquam Concilium Tridentinum esset habitum, ac de eâ decretum condidisset; jussu Papæ Sixti V. ac deinde iterum jussu Clementis VIII.
units.tr: (3) It was often interpolated and corrected, even after the Council of Trent had been held and had issued its decree about it, by order of Pope Sixtus V, and then again by order of Clement VIII.

units.la: 4. Interim fatentur auctores, alia, quæ mutanda videbantur, consulto immutata relicta esse, ad offensionem populorum vitandam, &c. Errores etiam satis multi ac manifesti sunt.
units.tr: (4) Meanwhile the authors themselves admit that other things, which seemed to need changing, were deliberately left unchanged, in order to avoid offence to the peoples, and so on. Errors, moreover, are quite numerous and manifest.

units.la: Similiter existimandum de Versione Græca, quæ appellatur LXX. Interpretum: cujus etiam auctores 1. non fuerunt Θεοπνεῦστοι.
units.tr: The same must be judged of the Greek version called that of the Seventy Interpreters (LXX). Its authors (1) were not God-breathed (Θεόπνευστοι).

units.la: 2. Quot, & quales fuerint isti Interpretes; & an integra Biblia V. T. per eos translata, incertum est.
units.tr: (2) Who and how many those interpreters were, and whether the whole of the Old Testament was translated by them, is uncertain.

units.la: 3. Translationem illam adhuc puram exstare, non est certum; imo nec probabile.
units.tr: (3) That this translation survives today in its purity is not certain; indeed, it is not even probable.

units.la: 4. Quæ isto nomine commendatur, plurimum discrepat ab Editione Hebraica, verè authentica.
units.tr: (4) The version that is commended under that name differs widely from the Hebrew edition, which is truly authentic.

units.la: XXVI. Diximus th. 13. faciendas etiam esse SS. Bibliorum Translationes in alias linguas; sicut autem in Ministris Christi, ac Dispensatoribus mysteriorum Dei, omnino requiritur, ut fidi reperiantur; 1 Cor. iv, 1, 2. ita in transferendis SS. Bibliis singularis cura & fides adhibenda est, ut originalis veritas quam optime exprimatur; vocesque & phrases singulæ, pro ratione linguarum ac idiotismorum, exhibeantur quam proximè & efficacissimè.
units.tr: XXVI. We said in thesis 13 that translations of the Holy Bible into other languages must also be made. Just as faithfulness is absolutely required of ministers of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God (1 Cor. 4:1, 2), so in translating the Holy Bible a unique care and fidelity must be applied, so that the original truth is expressed as well as possible, and that each word and phrase is rendered as closely and as effectively as possible, according to the nature of the languages and idioms.

units.la: In Bibliis autem fideliter translatis, agnoscenda est eadem Divina & Canonica Auctoritas materialiter, secundum rem contentam, ejusque methodicam dispositionem, & realem expressionem; sed mutato idiomate.
units.tr: In Bibliès faithfully translated, the same Divine and Canonical Authority must be recognised materially, according to the content, its methodical arrangement and its real expression, but with the idiom changed.

units.la: Obj. Interpretes omnes fallibiles sunt. Resp. Attamen suppositâ fidelitate, & reali convenientiâ cum originalibus, non fefellerunt, nec falsi fuerunt actû Interpretes.
units.tr: Objection. All translators are fallible. Answer. Nevertheless, given faithfulness and real agreement with the originals, the translators did not deceive, nor were they actually false.

units.la: XXVII. Translationum sinceritas, saltem in rebus principalibus, ad fidem & mores potissimùm necessariis, earumque Divinâ tractatione; atque adeò Canonica earum Authoritas secundum illud materiale, cognoscitur 1. ex collatione plurium Translationum.
units.tr: XXVII. The sincerity of translations, at least in the principal matters that are chiefly necessary for faith and morals, and their divine handling, and thus their canonical authority with respect to that material content, are recognised (1) by comparing several translations.

units.la: 2. Ex testimonio aliorum, sive fidelium, sive etiam infidelium, qui Linguas originales intelligunt.
units.tr: (2) From the testimony of others, whether faithful or even unfaithful, who understand the original languages.

units.la: 3. Per characteres Divinitatis, qui etiam in Translationibus exprimuntur.
units.tr: (3) Through the marks of divinity, which are also expressed in translations.

units.la: 4. Accedit insuper Spiritûs Sancti attestatio, & persuasio interna, in cordibus nostris: quâ quidem luce subjectivè collustrati singuli, vident lucem illam objectivè, eamque pie agnoscunt; & sic fide Divinâ credunt, hoc revera esse Verbum Dei.
units.tr: (4) Moreover, there is added the attestation of the Holy Spirit and his inward persuasion in our hearts. Illuminated by this light subjectively, each believer sees that light objectively and piously acknowledges it, and so believes with divine faith that this is truly the Word of God.

units.la: XXVIII. Perfectio, vel sufficientia S. Scripturæ est, quâ Systema Biblicum omnia fidei & vitæ Christianæ dogmata, ad salutem consequendam necessaria plenè complectitur.
units.tr: XXVIII. The perfection, or sufficiency, of Holy Scripture is that by which the biblical system fully embraces all the doctrines of faith and Christian life that are necessary for obtaining salvation.

units.la: Hæc autem spectatur, tùm, integralis, tùm essentialis.
units.tr: This is viewed both as integral and as essential.

units.la: Integralis perfectio dicitur respectû partium integrantium; ut Systema S. Scripturæ etiam nunc omnes libros & omnes singulorum librorum partes, ac particulas comprehendat, prout Deus Ecclesiæ suæ dedit in canonem fidei ac morum.
units.tr: Integral perfection is so called with respect to the parts that make up the whole: the system of Holy Scripture, as God has given it to his Church as the canon of faith and morals, still comprehends all the books and all the parts and particles of each book.

units.la: Asserimus ergo, S. Scripturam non esse in universum corruptam, aut depravatam; multis ex eâ sublatis, aliisque perperam insertis; contra Muhammedanos, qui isto prætextû Alkoranum suum commendare solent.
units.tr: We therefore assert that Holy Scripture has not been corrupted or depraved in general, with many things taken away from it and others wrongly inserted. This is against the Muslims, who commonly use this pretext to commend their Qur'an.

units.la: Neque ullos libros intercidisse, nec pluribus locis immutatam ac depravatam esse S. Scripturam; contra Pontificios, Socinianos, & incautos quosdam Criticos-
units.tr: Nor have any books perished, nor has Holy Scripture been altered and corrupted in many places. This is against the Papists, the Socinians, and certain incautious critics.

units.la: Huc pertinent 1. diserta quaedam Testimonia: Psal. xii,7; xix,8,9. Vide sup. th. 22. Adde Psal. xviii, 31. xciii, 5. cxix, 140. Prov. xxx, 5. Item Matth. v,18. „Amen quippe dico vobis; Ufquedum Praeterierit coelum & terra, ἰῶτα unum, aut unus apex ne„quaquam praeterierit ex Lege, ufquedum omnia facta „tuerint. 1 Petri ii,2. „Ut modo geniti infantes, „lac illud sermonis sincerum expetite. 2, 19. Habemus „firmissimum sermonem Propheticum: quem bene facitis „quod attendatis, &c.
units.tr: To this belong (1) certain clear testimonies: Ps. 12:7; 19:8, 9; see above, thesis 22. Add Ps. 18:31; 93:5; 119:140; Prov. 30:5. Likewise Matt. 5:18: "Truly I say to you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota [ἰῶτα] or one stroke will pass from the Law, until all things have been done." 1 Pet. 2:2: "As newborn infants, desire the pure milk of the word." 2:19: "We have the most sure prophetic word, which you do well to heed," etc.

units.la: 2. Argumentamur à Fine; cujus gratia SS. Literae exaratae sunt; quippe requirit, ut integrae exstent usque ad finem mundi: Deuter. xxxi, 26, 27. „Capite „librum istum Legis,& ponite eum in latere Arcae foederis Iehovae Dei vestri; sitque ibi contra te in te„stem. -- Ecce adhuc me vivente vobiscum hodie, re„belles estis Iehovae; & quanto magis posteaquam mor„tuus fuero? Jef. viii,20. Vide sup. cap. 1. th. 6. Luc. xvi, 29. „Habent Mosen & Prophetas; audiant eos: Rom. iv, 23, 24. „Non scriptum est autem propter eum (Abrahamum) solum, quod (hoc) imputatum fuerit ei: Sed etiam propter nos, quibus futurum est ut imputetur, &c. 1 Cor. x, 11. „Haec autem typice evenerunt eis (sub V. T.); scripta vero sunt ad nostri admonitionem, in quos fines saeculorum devenerunt. Job. xx, 31. Rom. xv, 4. Tim. iii, 16, 17. Vide sup. th. 4.
units.tr: (2) We argue from the end for which the Holy Scriptures were written. Clearly they must remain whole until the end of the world: Deut. 31:26, 27: "Take this book of the Law and put it beside the ark of the covenant of Jehovah your God, that it may be there as a witness against you. … Behold, while I am still alive with you today, you have been rebellious against Jehovah; how much more after I am dead?" Isa. 8:20; see above, chapter 1, thesis 6. Luke 16:29: "They have Moses and the Prophets; let them hear them." Rom. 4:23, 24: "Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him; but also for our sake, to whom it is to be imputed," etc. 1 Cor. 10:11: "These things happened to them as types (under the Old Testament); but they were written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the ages have come." John 20:31; Rom. 15:4; 2 Tim. 3:16, 17. See above, thesis 4.

units.la: 3. A Providentia Dei speciali conservatrice: hanc enim non minus saltem circa S. Scripturam versari necesse est, quam circa Naturam. Quemadmodum igitur in Natura omnes creaturarum species perpetuo conservantur; etiam omnes & singulas S. Scripturae partes conservari, statuendum est: quia maxime versatur circa fideles, & quidem in ordine ad salutem ipsorum aeternam, & circa media ad eam promovendam necessaria. Jef. xlix,15,16. Matth. x, 29, 30, 31. 1 Petr. i,5. 1. f. cum Ief. lix, 21. Vide fup. Cap. i. th. 29.
units.tr: (3) From the special conserving providence of God. For this providence must be exercised over Holy Scripture no less than over nature. Just as in nature all the species of creatures are perpetually preserved, so it must be held that all the parts and single portions of Holy Scripture are preserved, because this providence is chiefly concerned with the faithful, and indeed with their eternal salvation, and with the means necessary to promote it. Isa. 49:15, 16; Matt. 10:29, 30, 31; 1 Pet. 1:5; 1 Cor. 1:5; with Isa. 59:21. See above, chapter 1, thesis 29.

units.la: 4. A Curâ & fidelitate Ecclesiae, cui S. Scriptura commissa est,& quae Providentiae isti Divinae subordinatur. Psal. CXLVII, 19, 20. Rom. iii, 2. 1 Tim. iii, 15. Vide sup. th. 4 & 16. cum Matth. xxviii, 20. „Ecce, Ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem saeculi.
units.tr: 4. From the care and faithfulness of the Church, to which Holy Scripture has been committed, and which is subordinate to this divine providence. Ps. 147:19, 20. Rom. 3:2. 1 Tim. 3:15. See above, theses 4 and 16, with Matt. 28:20: "Lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the world."

units.la: XXIX. Obj. 1. Numer. xxi. 14. allegatur Liber Bellorum Domini, Iof. x.13. Liber recti; & 1 Reg. xiv. 19. Chronica Regum Israelis.
units.tr: XXIX. Objection 1. Numbers 21:14 cites the Book of the Wars of the Lord, Joshua 10:13, the Book of the Upright, and 1 Kings 14:19, the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

units.la: Verùm isti libri in Canone sacro nunc non comparent: ergo. Resp. Isti libri non sunt, neque olim fuerunt, Canonici: unde nihil necesse fuit, eos semper conservari. At veritatem aliquam, quam Deus in Ecclesia omninò exstare voluit, ex illis allegavit,& comprobavit in libris verè Canonicis: Confer allegata ex Arato, Menandro,& Epimenide; Act. xvii, 28. 1 Cor. xv. 33. Tit. i. 12.
units.tr: But these books do not now appear in the sacred canon; therefore... Answer: These books are not, and never were, canonical. So there was no need for them always to be preserved. But God wished some truth to exist in the Church, and he drew it from those books and confirmed it in books that are truly canonical. Compare the passages cited from Aratus, Menander and Epimenides: Acts 17:28; 1 Cor. 15:33; Titus 1:12.

units.la: Obj. 2. Atqui etiam allegantur scripta Nathanis, Gadi, &c. 1 Chron. xxix. 29. 2. ix, 29. Resp. Ista scripta vel exstant sub aliis titulis; in libris scil. Samuëlis, & Regum; vel Canonicae non fuerunt.
units.tr: Objection 2. Yet the writings of Nathan, Gad, and so on are also cited: 1 Chron. 29:29; 2 Chron. 9:29. Answer: Those writings either exist under other titles, namely in the books of Samuel and Kings, or they were not canonical.

units.la: Obj. 3. Paulus etiam commemorat epistolam suam ad Laodicenses; Col. iv. 16. Resp. Apostolus 1. non dicit epistolam illam à se scriptam; 2. nec ad Laodicenses; 3. neque eam esse Canonicam. Sed epistolam aliquam scriptam Laodicea commendat, ut legatur à Colossensibus. 4. Si quae Epistola à Paulo istic scripta intelligi deberet, cogitari posset de priori ad Timotheum, juxta ejus subscriptionem.
units.tr: Objection 3. Paul also mentions his letter to the Laodiceans, Col. 4:16. Answer: The Apostle (1) does not say that this letter was written by him; (2) nor that it was written to the Laodiceans; (3) nor that it is canonical. He only commends some letter written at Laodicea, to be read by the Colossians. (4) If any letter written there by Paul were meant, one could think of the first to Timothy, according to its subscription.

units.la: XXX. Perfectio essentialis dicitur ratione doctrinae salutaris, istis libris comprehensae, & per singulas partes diffusae, multisque vicibus ac modis repetitae, sic tamen ut ratione substantiae indè ab initio Foederis gratiae semper fuerit eadem. Heb. xiii, 8. Act. x. 43. xv, 11. v. 12, 2 Cor. iii. 11. 1 Tim. ii, 5, 6. Joh. xiv, 6. 1.16. Col. i, 19, 20.
units.tr: XXX. The essential perfection is spoken of with regard to the saving doctrine comprehended in these books, and spread through each of their parts and repeated many times and in many ways, yet so that, as regards its substance, it has always been the same from the beginning of the covenant of grace. Heb. 13:8; Acts 10:43; 15:11; Rom. 5:12; 2 Cor. 3:11; 1 Tim. 2:5, 6; John 14:6; 1:16; Col. 1:19, 20.

units.la: Sic autem Systema S. Sripturæ indè ab initio fui continuit, & nunc etiam clarius continet omnia, quæ hominibus ad salutem consequendam necessaria sunt.
units.tr: Thus the system of Holy Scripture has contained from the beginning, and now contains more clearly, all things that are necessary for men to attain salvation.

units.la: S. Literis interim comprehensa intelligimus, non solum eā, quæ formaliter, αὐτολεξεὶ & ἐξ ἐνητὸν expressa sunt; sed etiàm, quæ virtualiter, καὶ' Ἀξιόνοιαν, καὶ' ισοδυναμίαν, aut καὶα συναγολλήσιν, continentur.
units.tr: By things comprehended in the Holy Writings we understand not only those things that are expressed formally, word for word (αὐτολεξεί) and in so many words [ἐξ ἑνὸς], but also those that are contained virtually, by sense [κατὰ διάνοιαν], by equivalence [κατὰ ἰσοδυναμίαν], or by inference [κατὰ συναγωγήν].

units.la: Neque spectamus, quæcunque in Ecclesiâ unquàm Divinitùs dicta aut facta sunt; sed quæ hominibus ad salutem consequendam necessaria, tùm in credendis tùm etiàm in agendis. Joh. xx, 30, 31. „Multa vero „etiàm alia signa edidit Jesus in Discipulorum suorum „conspectu, quæ non sunt scripta in hoc libro: Hæc au„tem scripta sunt, ut credatis, &c.
units.tr: Nor do we consider whatever was ever said or done in the Church by divine direction, but what is necessary for men to attain salvation, both in what is to be believed and in what is to be done. John 20:30, 31: "Jesus did many other signs in the sight of his disciples, which are not written in this book. But these are written that you may believe, etc."

units.la: XXXI. Sententia ista orthodoxa probatur; 1. illu-
units.tr: XXXI. This orthodox view is proved: 1. by that famous testimony

units.la: stri illo testimonio, 2 Tim. iii, 14, 17. „At tu manet- „to in iis, quæ didicisti, & quæ tibi concredita sunt: sciens „à quo didiceris: Teque à puero sacras literas novisse; „quæ te possunt sapientem reddere ad salutem, per fidem, „quæ est in Christo. Tota Scriptura Divinitus (est) in„spirata, &c. Vide sup: th. 4. Apostolus Euangelistam à falsis doctrinis dehortatur, docetque, in quibus post excessum suum ei perseverandum esset: ità scil. ut eum revocet ad SS. Literas. De iis autem asserit (α.) posse sapientem reddere ad salutem, &c. Sapientia habitum perfectum notat: hæc vero in fide Christi ad salutem, SS. Literis, tanquàm unico principio doctrinali, tribuitur. (β.) Docet, Totam S. Scripturam esse Divinitus inspiratam: ab Auctore scil. Auctoritatem & Perfectionem arcessens; juxta Iac. i, 17. Verùm insuper (γ.) pet partes hanc exequitur; utilis ad doctrinam, &c. Sic enim ejus usum demonstrat, non in uno tantùm, sed in omni genere ad salutem necessario; sive veritas fuerit docenda, sive falsitas redarguenda, sive mali mores corrigendi, sive disciplina justitiæ inculcanda. Quin etiàm (*.) totum negotium conficit, & planè hanc litem terminat; concludens: ut Vir Dei (h. e. Doctor Ecclesiæ ex ordinatione Dei; ꝥ Reg. xvii, 24. 1 Tim. vi, 11.) perfectus fit, in omnibus videl. istis partibus; & breviter ad omne opus bonum perfectè instructus. Ex persectione effectûs patet perfectio causæ.
units.tr: of 2 Timothy 3:14-17: "But you continue in the things you have learned and have been entrusted with, knowing from whom you have learned them, and that from a child you have known the holy Scriptures, which are able to make you wise unto salvation through the faith that is in Christ. All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, etc." See above, thesis 4. The Apostle dissuades Timothy from false doctrines and teaches what he must persist in after his own departure, namely that he should recall him to the Holy Scriptures. Of these he asserts (a) that they are able to make one wise unto salvation, etc. Wisdom denotes a perfect habit, and this is ascribed to the Holy Writings, as the single doctrinal principle, in the faith of Christ, for salvation. (b) He teaches that all Holy Scripture is divinely inspired, deriving its authority and perfection from the Author, in accordance with James 1:17. Moreover (c) he carries this out part by part: useful for teaching, etc. For in this way he shows its use not in one kind only but in every kind necessary for salvation, whether truth is to be taught, falsehood refuted, evil morals corrected, or the discipline of righteousness inculcated. Indeed (d) he completes the whole business and finally settles the dispute, concluding that the man of God (that is, a teacher of the Church by appointment of God; 1 Kings 17:24; 1 Tim. 6:11) may be perfect, that is, in all these parts; and in brief thoroughly furnished unto every good work. From the perfection of the effect the perfection of the cause is evident.

units.la: 2. Locis quibusdam V. T. Exod. xxiv, 3, 4. „Venit ergo Moseh, & narravit populo omnia Verba Iehovæ, omniaque judicia: & respondit totus populus voce unâ, ac dixerunt; Omnia Verba, quæ locutus est „Jehovah, faciemus. Et scripsit Moseh omnia verba Iehovæ. Moses, quæ à Deo audivit, omnia populo narravit; eademque omnia scripto consignavit: ne ea oblivioni traderentur, imò ut etiàm posterorum usibus servirent; cum quibus Deus idem fœdus pepigit. Exod. xxiv, 27. Deut. xxix, 14, 15. xxxi, 9, 21.
units.tr: 2. From certain places of the Old Testament: Exodus 24:3, 4: "Moses came and told the people all the words of Jehovah and all the judgments. And all the people answered with one voice and said, All the words which Jehovah has spoken we will do. And Moses wrote all the words of Jehovah." Moses told the people all that he heard from God, and he recorded all of it in writing, so that it would not be lost to forgetfulness, but might also serve the use of posterity, with whom God made the same covenant. Exodus 24:27; Deut. 29:14, 15; 31:9, 21.

units.la: Iterùm Deut. xxxi, 24, -27. „Cùm autem finem fecisset Moseh scribendi verba Legis istius in libro, donec ea complerentur: Præcepit Moseh Levitis portantibus arcam fœderis Jehovæ dicendo; Capite librum istum, &c. Vide sup. th. 28. Legis ergò scripturam absolvit Moses; omnesque ejus partes complevit: & pro posteris exemplar illud, tanquàm depositum ac testimonium, diligentissimè conservandum mandavit. Ita quidem ut nemini quicquam addere, vel detrahere liceret; sed præscriptum illud accuratissimè omnes sequi deberent, non recedendo dextrorsùm vel sinistrorsùm; Deut. iv, 1, 2. v, 38, 39. xii, 32. Iof.1,7. xxiii, 6. Prov. xxx, 5, 6.
units.tr: Again, Deut. 31:24-27: "When Moses had finished writing the words of this law in a book, until they were completed, Moses commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, saying: Take this book, etc." See above, thesis 28. Moses therefore finished the writing of the Law and completed all its parts, and for posterity he commanded that this copy, as a deposit and testimony, be most diligently preserved. So that no one might add anything or take away, but all should follow that prescription most exactly, not turning aside to the right hand or to the left: Deut. 4:1, 2; 5:38, 39; 12:32; Josh. 1:7; 23:6; Prov. 30:5, 6.

units.la: Insigne etiam est testimonium Psal. xix, 8, 9. Vide sup. th. 22. Ubi diserte perfectio laudatur, & quidem ad convertendam animam, sapientiam efficiendam, cor lætificandum, &c.
units.tr: The testimony of Psalm 19:8, 9 is also remarkable. See above, thesis 22. There perfection is plainly praised, and that for converting the soul, making wise, rejoicing the heart, etc.

units.la: 3. Similia sunt testimonia N. T. Luc. xvi, 29. ubi de evitandâ condemnatione: Habent Mosen & Prophetas; 23, 24. xv, 4. 1 Cor. x, 11. At vero non Hebraicam sed Græcam, istius Euangelii editionem Deus confervavit: & quidem talem, ubi non solùm voces quædam, sed etiàm sententiæ Hebraicæ, aut Syriacæ, formaliter citantur, ac porrò in Græcum sermonem transferuntur: Matth. 1, 23. xxvii, 46. quæ sic Hebraicè conscribi non potuerunt.
units.tr: 3. Similar are the testimonies of the New Testament: Luke 16:29, where, concerning the avoiding of condemnation, it says: "They have Moses and the Prophets"; see also 23, 24; Luke 4:4; 1 Cor. 10:11. But God has preserved not the Hebrew but the Greek edition of this Gospel, and indeed such an edition in which not only certain words but even Hebrew or Syriac sentences are formally cited and then translated into Greek: Matt. 1:23; 27:46, which could not have been written in Hebrew in this way.

units.la: Similiter neque admittimus, Euangelium Marci Latinè, vel Epistolam ad Hebræos Hebraicè primùm exaratam fuisse.
units.tr: Likewise we do not admit that the Gospel of Mark was first written in Latin, or the Epistle to the Hebrews first written in Hebrew.

units.la: XIII. Editio secundaria
units.tr: XIII. Secondary edition

units.la: XIII. Editio secundaria est, quâ SS. Literæ, ex Linguis originalibus, in aliam qualemcunque translatæ, sic exhibentur, ut ab harum ignaris ad instructionem ac demonstrationem Theologicam intelligi & usurpari possint.
units.tr: XIII. A secondary edition is one in which the Holy Scriptures, translated from the original languages into some other language, are presented in such a way that those who are ignorant of the originals can understand them and use them for theological instruction and proof.

units.la: Istiusmodi Translationes non solùm ad Ecclesiæ ædificationem utiliter institui posse, sed etiàm ex voluntate Dei sub hac œconomia necessario institui debere, probatur contra Pontificios Scripturarum lucifugas; 14 Quia Deus omnino vult, ut Verbum suum scriptum familiariter legatur atque intelligatur ab omnibus, qui ad communionem istius Fœderis vocantur: patet hoc ex ipsis Editionibus primariis. At vero gentes quaurumvis Linguarum sub hac œconomia vocatæ sunt, atque amplius vocandæ: Matth. xxviii, 19. Profecti docete omnes gentes, &c. Confer Rom. iii, 29. Eph. ii, 19, 20. Phil. ii, ii. Apoc. v, 8.
units.tr: That translations of this kind can be usefully made for the building up of the Church, and that under this dispensation they ought to be made by the will of God, is proved against the Papists, the enemies of Scripture. (1) God wills absolutely that his written Word be read and understood familiarly by all who are called into the fellowship of this covenant; this is evident from the primary editions themselves. But people of every language have been called under this dispensation, and are yet to be called: Matt. 28:19, "Go and teach all nations," etc. Compare Rom. 3:29; Eph. 2:19, 20; Phil. 2:11; Rev. 5:8.

units.la: 2. Christus Apostolos non dimisit ad Euangelium omnibus gentibus prædicandum, nisi priùs omnium Linguarum notitiâ instructos; ut unusquisque audiret eos sua propria lingua loquentes, & magnifica Dei facta prædicantes: Actor. 1, 4, 8. ii, 4, 6, 8, 11. Quali dono variarum linguarum tunc etiàm plures fuerunt instructi; additoinsuper in quibusdam aliis dono interpretationis verbalis: 1 Cor. xiv, 6, 13, 27, 28. unde conficitur, in quolibet cœtu etiàm Scripta Prophetica & Apostolica alleganda, explicanda, & applicanda esse linguâ istic notâ.
units.tr: 2. Christ did not send out the apostles to preach the gospel to all nations unless they had first been instructed in the knowledge of all languages, so that each one might hear them speaking in his own tongue and proclaiming the mighty works of God: Acts 1:4, 8; 2:4, 6, 8, 11. By this gift of many tongues many were then also instructed; and in some the gift of verbal interpretation was added: 1 Cor. 14:6, 13, 27, 28. From this it follows that in every assembly the prophetic and apostolic Scriptures are to be cited, explained and applied in the language known there.

units.la: 3. Idem evincunt præcepta & exhortationes de Verbo Dei legendo, meditando, & aliis inculcando: Deut. vi, 6, -9. xvii, 18, 19. xxxi, 11, 12, 13. Psal. i, 2. xix, 9, -12. cxix, 1, &c. Jes. viii, 20. Luc. xvi, 29. Job. v, 39. xx, 31. Act. xvii, 11. Rom. iv, 23, 24. xv, 4. 1 Cor. x, 11. 2 Tim. iii, 14, -17. 2 Petr. i, 19. 1 Joh. i, 4. Judæ, 3. Apoc. i, 3. xxii, 18, 19. Ista enim fieri non possunt ab hominibus linguarum originalium ignaris, nisi per translationem.
units.tr: 3. The same is shown by the precepts and exhortations to read, meditate on and teach the Word of God to others: Deut. 6:6–9; 17:18, 19; 31:11–13; Ps. 1:2; 19:9–12; 119:1, etc.; Isa. 8:20; Luke 16:29; John 5:39; 20:31; Acts 17:11; Rom. 4:23, 24; 15:4; 1 Cor. 10:11; 2 Tim. 3:14–17; 2 Pet. 1:19; 1 John 1:4; Jude 3; Rev. 1:3; 22:18, 19. For these things cannot be done by men ignorant of the original languages, except through translation.

units.la: 4. Ex praxi, eventu, & salutari successu istius negotii, olim atque etiamnum.
units.tr: 4. From the practice, the outcome and the saving success of this undertaking, both formerly and still today.

units.la: XIV. Succedunt Attributa; & quidem potissi- mùm Auctoritas, Perfectio, Perspicuitas, & Necessitas.
units.tr: XIV. The attributes follow; and chiefly these: authority, perfection, perspicuity and necessity.

units.la: Auctoritas S. Scripturæ, elt Divina ejus potestas, ad fidem & observantiam Deo debitam nos obligans.
units.tr: The authority of Holy Scripture is its divine power, binding us to the faith and obedience owed to God.

units.la: Quoniàm Auctor ejus est ipse Deus Opt. Max. ut ostensum th. 4. indè manifesta est ejus in se Divinitas; atque in ordine ad homines, quibus tradita est, Auctoritas, & quidem Divina; ut ei fides haberi debeat, tanquàm verè Verbo Dei; & obedientia religiosa præstari debeat, juxta voluntatem mandati Divini istic expressam. Vide 1 Thess. ii, 13. 1 Joh. v, 9, 10.
units.tr: Since its author is God himself, the best and greatest, as shown in thesis 4, its divinity is thereby plain in itself; and in relation to the men to whom it has been delivered, it has authority, and indeed divine authority: so that it ought to be believed as truly the Word of God, and religious obedience ought to be rendered to it according to the will of the divine command expressed there. See 1 Thess. 2:13; 1 John 5:9, 10.

units.la: XV. Manifestum est, omnis testimonii, mandati, legis, diplomatis, &c. Auctoritatem, ab Auctore suo proprie pendere, & arcessendam esse: atque adeo Auctoritatem S. Scripturæ, ab Auctore Deo.
units.tr: XV. It is clear that the authority of every testimony, command, law, charter, etc., depends properly on its author and must be sought from him; and therefore the authority of Holy Scripture is derived from its author, God.

units.la: Absurdè vero & impiè Pontificii Auctoritatem S. Scripturæ, in ordine ad nos, suspendunt ab Ecclesiâ, & quidem Romanâ, ejusque Pontifice.
units.tr: But the Papists absurdly and impiously make the authority of Holy Scripture, in relation to us, depend on the Church, and indeed the Roman Church, and on its Pope.

units.la: Nam 1. omnis Auctoritas est relativa; & in ordine ad alios, qui eâ obligantur: si ergo S. Scriptura, tanquam ipsius Dei Verbum scriptum, ab ipso Deo Auctoritatem in se habet, necessariò eandem sic habere debet in ordine ad homines, quibus S. Scriptura ptura data est in normam fidei ac morum.
units.tr: For (1) all authority is relative, and is related to others who are bound by it. If therefore Holy Scripture, as the written Word of God himself, has authority in itself from God himself, it must necessarily have the same authority in relation to the men to whom Holy Scripture has been given as the rule of faith and conduct.

units.la: 2. Christus, tanquam αὐτόπιστος, negat, se testimonium ab homine accipere; cum de se aliud majus habeat; idem ergo tenendum de Deo, aut Christo, loquente in Verbo suo scripto. Ioh. v, 34, 36. cum 1 Ioh. v, 9. Tit. 1, 1. 2 Tim. ii, 13. Hebr. vi, 13, 18.
units.tr: (2) Christ, as [αὐτόπιστος] self-attesting, denies that he receives testimony from man, since he has something greater concerning himself; the same must be held concerning God, or Christ, speaking in his written Word. John 5:34, 36, compared with 1 John 5:9; Titus 1:2; 2 Tim. 2:13; Heb. 6:13, 18.

units.la: 3. Vera Ecclesia exstructa est super fundamento Apostolorum & Prophetarum: Eph. ii, 20. & sanctificata in veritate Dei, quae est Verbum ipsius: Ioh. xvii, 17. Ipsa igitur in fide sua nititur Verbo Dei, per Prophetas & Apostolos exhibito; atque in obedientia sua similiter conformatur ad illam normam: non vero contra Verbum Dei scriptum, ejusque Auctoritas obligatoria, nititur Ecclesia, tanquam fundamento.
units.tr: (3) The true Church is built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Eph. 2:20, and is sanctified in the truth of God, which is his Word, John 17:17. Therefore the Church itself, in its faith, rests on the Word of God delivered through the prophets and apostles, and in its obedience is likewise conformed to that rule; the Church does not rest, as on a foundation, against the written Word of God, nor on its binding authority.

units.la: 4. Absurde, & non sine crimine laesae majestatis, subditi arrogarent sibi dignitatem, ex qua penderet potestas obligatoria Legis a Principe latae, in ordine ad hos vel illos. Similiter autem hic agunt Adversarii.
units.tr: (4) It would be absurd, and not without the crime of treason, for subjects to claim for themselves a dignity on which the binding power of a law enacted by the prince would depend, in relation to this or that person. Yet this is what the adversaries do here.

units.la: XVI. Obj. 1. Ecclesia est columna & stabilimentum veritatis; 1 Tim. iii, 15. Ergo. Resp. 1. Ita scil. ut 1. Ecclesia, tanquam columna, erecta & stabilita sit super illo fundamento, Verbo Dei; sic coagmentata & confirmata in veritate, pallive: non vero contra ut Verbum Dei scriptum nitatur Ecclesia; sicut tectum aliquod columna ipsum sustentante, architectonice. 2. Ut veritatem Verbi Divini aliis exhibeat, indicet, & suo modo attestetur: cujusmodi columnarum quarundam usus politicus est. 3. Nihil ibi speciatim de Ecclesia Romana.
units.tr: XVI. Objection 1. The Church is the pillar and ground of the truth, 1 Tim. 3:15. Therefore... Answer 1. Only in the sense that (1) the Church, as a pillar, is erected and established upon that foundation, the Word of God, and is so joined together and confirmed in the truth, and not that the Church rests against the written Word of God, as a roof rests architecturally on a pillar that supports it. (2) It exhibits, points out and in its own way attests the truth of the divine Word to others, as is the political use of certain pillars. (3) Nothing there is said specifically about the Roman Church.

units.la: Obj. 2. Augustinus alibi; Non crederem S. Scripturae, nisi me auctoritas Ecclesiae Catholicae moveret. Resp. Non quicquid Augustinus dixit, aut credidit, verum est; neque ab ipsis Pontificiis, ut tale, admittitur: ex, gr. de Eucharistia danda infantibus. 2. Augustinus isto dicto offendit, qua methodo ipse perductus fuerit ad DiviDivinitatem S. Scripturæ agnoscendam; interveniente scilicet ministeriali testimonio Ecclesiæ, aut Antecessorum ejus.
units.tr: Objection 2. Augustine elsewhere: I would not believe Scripture, unless the authority of the Catholic Church moved me. Answer 1. Not everything Augustine said or believed is true, nor is it accepted as such even by the Papists themselves; for example, concerning the giving of the Eucharist to infants. 2. Augustine, in this saying, refers to the method by which he himself was led to acknowledge the divinity of Holy Scripture; namely, by the intervention of the ministerial testimony of the Church, or of its predecessors.

units.la: XVII. Si quæratur, quomodò aliis innotescat Auctoritas S. Scripturæ? Hîc etiam Ecclesiæ sunt suæ partes; Antecessorum scil. Ecclesiasticorum, quin & singulorum fidelium, suo modo. De luce quippè testatur, ut alii quoque credant; non tamen sunt ipsa lux, aut lucis causa, vel ἀξιοπιστίας in eâ; sed luce illâ collustrati, testimonium ei apud alios perhibent. Vide Joh. 1, 7, 8. Confer exemplum Samaritanorum, & mulieris de Christo apud illos testantis; Joh. 1v, 28, 29, 30, 39. -42. Apparitor, vel etiam quivis ex plebe, advenæ alicui, aliive ignaro, indicium facere potest, dicens; Iste est Consul civitatis; ille Prætor; Hoc Diploma Senatus urbani, &c. Verùm istâ ratione nequaquam confert in Consulem, Prætorem, &c. talem dignitatem aut potestatem, &c. Non est causa rei constitutiva, vel effectiva; sed medium ejus cognoscendæ, quæ ante & citra istam cognitionem etiam verè talis est. Similiter indicatur, docetur, quòd sit, & qualis sit Auctoritas S.Scripturæ; ac suadetur, ut ei fides habeatur: ubi sic solùm occurrit externa ministerialiter adjuvans causa Auctoritatis istius cognoscendæ.
units.tr: XVII. If it is asked how the authority of Holy Scripture becomes known to others, here too the Church has its part: that is, of its ecclesiastical predecessors, and indeed of individual faithful in their own way. For they bear witness to the light, so that others also may believe; yet they are not the light itself, nor the cause of the light, nor of its [ἀξιοπιστίας] credibility; but illumined by that light they bear testimony to it before others. See John 1:7, 8. Compare the example of the Samaritans, and of the woman who testified about Christ to them, John 4:28–30, 39–42. A court officer, or even any ordinary person, can point out to a stranger or someone ignorant of such things, saying: "This man is the consul of the city; that one is the praetor; this is a decree of the city senate," and so on. Yet by this reasoning he does not in any way confer on the consul, the praetor, etc., such dignity or power. He is not the constitutive or effective cause of the thing, but the means of coming to know it, which is truly such even before and apart from that knowledge. Similarly it is pointed out and taught that the authority of Holy Scripture exists and what sort it is, and it is urged that faith be given to it; here there occurs only an external cause, helping ministerially, of coming to know that authority.

units.la: XVIII. Principalior est ipsa S. Scriptura, Verbum infallibile ipsius Dei Opt. Max. veritas αυτόπιϛ, lux propriis suis radiis fulgens; suæ Divinitatis & auctoritatis characteres clarissimos in se habens, & de se ostendens, ut certo agnoscantur à subjectis capacibus.
units.tr: XVIII. The principal witness is Holy Scripture itself, the infallible Word of God, the best and greatest, the truth [αὐτόπιστος] self-attesting, a light shining with its own rays, having in itself, and showing from itself, the clearest marks of its divinity and authority, so that they may be known with certainty by those who are capable.

units.la: Huc pertinent 1. Materia, & Forma S. Scripturæ; Doctrina vera, sublimis ac sancta; & stylus simplex, sed majestatem Divinam interim referens; Deut. 1v, 6, 7. Vide sup. th. 4.
units.tr: To this pertain (1) the matter and the form of Holy Scripture: a true, lofty and holy doctrine; and a simple style, yet at the same time expressing the divine majesty. Deut. 4:6, 7. See above, thesis 4.

units.la: 2. Speciatim Prophetiæ tam multæ, ac variæ, quibus verissimè prædicta, quæ diu post, etiam ultra annorum aliquot centurias erant implenda, & suo tempore certissime impleta sunt. Ief. xli, 21, 22, 23. „Appropinquare facite litem vestram, dicit Jehovah: accedere facite fortia vestra, dicit Rex Jaacob. Accedere faciant, & annuciént nobis quæ eventura sint: - aut quæ futura sunt, narrate nobis. Annunciate, quæ ventura sunt in posterum: & cognoscemus, quòd Dii estis.
units.tr: (2) Especially the prophecies, so many and so varied, by which things were most truly foretold which were to be fulfilled long afterwards, even more than some centuries later, and which were most certainly fulfilled at their appointed time. Isa. 41:21–23: "Bring forward your cause, says the LORD; bring forth your strong reasons, says the King of Jacob. Let them bring them forth, and declare to us what shall happen; or declare the former things, what they are, that we may consider them. Declare the things that are to come hereafter, that we may know that you are gods."

units.la: 3. Adjuncta Amanuensium sinceritas: quâ factum est ut gloriæ Divinæ ; ac salutari Ecclesiæ instructioni unice intenti, & quæ Dominus mandabat conscribentes, non minus exposuerint proprios suos defectus, infirmitates, peccata; quam virtutes ac bona opera. Quin & Miracula, quibus plurimi eorum Verbum Domini confirmârunt.
units.tr: 3. The sincerity of the writers: because they were intent solely on God's glory and the salutary instruction of the Church, and wrote down what the Lord commanded, they set out their own failings, infirmities and sins no less than their virtues and good works. Indeed, there are also miracles by which many of them confirmed the Word of the Lord.

units.la: 4. Effecta tum in fidelibus per S. Scripturam ad Religionem adductis ; ubi spectanda eorum conversio, pietas, zelus, confessiones, martyria, &c. tum in hostibus Ecclesiæ, per eandem terrore sæpius perculsis, confusis, &c.
units.tr: 4. The effects produced by Scripture in the faithful who have been brought to religion, where one should observe their conversion, piety, zeal, confessions, martyrdoms, etc.; and in the enemies of the Church, who have often been struck with terror and confounded by it, etc.

units.la: XIX. Sed causa interior, hyperphysica efficacia hominem idoneum reddens ad percipiendos & agnoscendos istos characteres Divinitatis, simulq; ad auscultandum instructionibus & suasionibus Ecclesiasticis, difficillis mentis humanæ tenebris, sublatâ naturali voluntatis perversitate, &c. imo intime & efficacissime persuadens, est Spiritus Sanctus. 1 Cor. 11, 12. „Nos vero non spiritum mundi accepimus ; sed Spiritum, qui „(est) ex Deo: ut sciamus quæ Deus est nobis gratificatus „1 Joh. 1 1, 27. „Eadem unctio docet vos de omnibus. Docet ergo maxime & primo de Principio Religionis Christianæ. Vide etiam Psal. cxix, 18. Prov. 1, 23, Ief. lix, 21. Matth. xvi, 17. Luc. xxiv, 45. Joh. vi, 45. Act. xvi, 14. 2 Cor. iii, 5. iv, 13, 16. Eph. 1, 17, 20. 1 Thess. ii, 13.
units.tr: XIX. But the inner cause, a hyperphysical efficacy that makes a person fit to perceive and recognise these marks of divinity, and at the same time to listen to ecclesiastical instruction and persuasion, the darkness of the human mind being removed and the natural perversity of the will overcome, etc., and which inwardly and most effectively persuades, is the Holy Spirit. 1 Cor. 2:12: "But we have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit which is from God, that we may know the things that have been freely given to us by God." 1 John 2:27: "The same anointing teaches you about all things." It therefore teaches chiefly and first about the principle of the Christian religion. See also Ps. 119:18; Prov. 1:23; Isa. 59:21; Matt. 16:17; Luke 24:45; John 6:45; Acts 16:14; 2 Cor. 3:5; 4:13, 16; Eph. 1:17, 20; 1 Thess. 2:13.

units.la: Quoniam vero docemus, istam Spiritus Sancti doctrinam, strinam, attestationem, & confirmationem, cum usu S. Scripturæ conjunctam esse; satis patet, adversus Pontificiorum calumniam, nos procul abesse ab Enthusiasmis fanaticorum, præter, & sæpe contra verißimum & constantißimum Dei Verbum. Quin & ipsorum Adversariorum spiritus, in negotio Pontificis Romani, Traditionum non scriptarum, &c. spiritui illi Enthusiastico proximus est.
units.tr: Since we teach that this teaching, inspiration, attestation and confirmation of the Holy Spirit is joined with the use of Holy Scripture, it is sufficiently clear, against the calumny of the Papists, that we are far from the enthusiasms of the fanatics, which are apart from, and often against, the most true and constant Word of God. Indeed, the spirit of the adversaries themselves, in the matter of the Roman Pontiff, of unwritten traditions, etc., is close to that enthusiastic spirit.

units.la: XX. Tenenda interim distinctio inter αυθεντίαν normæ, & historiæ tantum.
units.tr: XX. Meanwhile the distinction between the authority of the norm and the authority of history alone must be maintained.

units.la: Αυθεντία normæ nos obligat ad fidem habendam omnibus eo modo ac fine dictis, vitamque instituendam juxta istud præscriptum; itemque ad imitationem talium factorum.
units.tr: The authority of the norm [αὐθεντία] obliges us to give belief to all things in the manner and for the purpose stated, and to order our life according to that prescription; likewise to the imitation of such deeds.

units.la: Hæc autem competit 1. dictis ipsius Dei absolute omnibus.
units.tr: This belongs, first, to the words of God himself, absolutely, all of them.

units.la: 2. Dictis bonorum Angelorum, & Hominum Θεοπνευστως loquentium.
units.tr: Second, to the words of good angels and of men speaking as God-breathed [θεοπνεύστως].

units.la: 3. Dictis etiam aliorum, Θεοπνευστως laudatis, vel approbatis; sive istic directè; (vide Job. 1,33. Act. xvii, 38. 1 Cor. xv,33. Tit. 1,13,13.) sive alibi per similes sententias Θεοπνευστως.
units.tr: Third, also to the words of others that are praised or approved as God-breathed; whether directly there (see Job 1:33; Acts 17:38; 1 Cor. 15:33; Titus 1:12, 13), or elsewhere through similar sayings that are God-breathed.

units.la: 4. Actionibus similiter laudatis, vel approbatis, & ad imitationem propositis.
units.tr: Fourth, to actions likewise praised or approved and set forth for imitation.

units.la: Αυθεντία historiæ tantum, nos obligat ad credendum fide Divinâ sic omnino facta vel dicta esse, quæ ita materialiter commemorantur in sacro illo systemate; non autem ad imitationem illorum factorum; neque ut credamus, ista recte atque ex vero dicta esse.
units.tr: The authority of history alone obliges us to believe with divine faith that those things were indeed done or said exactly as they are recorded materially in that sacred system; but not to imitate those deeds, nor to believe that those things were rightly and truly said.

units.la: Ea convenit, 1. Dictis Diaboli, & Hominum infidelium, ex sese loquentium; qualia in SS. Literis aliquoties commemorantur.
units.tr: This applies, first, to the words of the devil and of unbelieving men, speaking on their own; such as are recorded several times in the Holy Scriptures.

units.la: 3. Dictis etiam fidelium, non loquentium Θεοπνευστως; atque adeo vel aperte improbatis, vel saltem prorisus non approbatis. Vide Job. xxxvi ii, 1,2, &c. &c. XXXIX, 34, -38. XLI, 1, 13-6; 7. Psal. CVI, 33.
units.tr: Second, to the words of the faithful who were not speaking as God-breathed; and so either openly disapproved or at least not approved at all. See Job 38:1, 2, etc.; 39:34–38; 41:1, 13–16 [41:7]; Ps. 106:33.

units.la: 3. Factis similiter improbatis, aut saltem nullo modo approbatis.
units.tr: Third, to deeds likewise disapproved, or at least in no way approved.

units.la: 4. Quin & operibus, vires humanas absolutè excedentibus: quæ sic ad imitationem non sunt proposita. Cujusmodi sunt Opera creationis, Miracula, &c.
units.tr: Fourth, also to works that absolutely exceed human powers, which are therefore not set forth for imitation. Such are the works of creation, miracles, etc.

units.la: XXI. Observatâ hâc distinctione facilè intelligitur, quomodo Auctoritas Divina conveniat totiS. Scripturæ, & singulis ejus partibus, ac particulis: 2 Tim. III, 16, 2 Petr. I, 19, 20, 21. Rom. XV, 4. 1 Cor. VII, 25, 40. Luc. I, 41, 42, 67, 68. Act. VI, 8, 10. Quod contra Gentiles & Muhammedanos asserimus ac defendimus: & de libris N. T. non minus, quàm V. T. contra Judæos.
units.tr: XXI. Once this distinction is observed, it is easily understood how divine authority belongs to the whole of Holy Scripture, and to each of its parts and particles: 2 Tim. 3:16; 2 Pet. 1:19, 20, 21; Rom. 15:4; 1 Cor. 7:25, 40; Luke 1:41, 42, 67, 68; Acts 6:8, 10. This we assert and defend against the Gentiles and Muhammadans, and in regard to the books of the New Testament no less than the Old, against the Jews.

units.la: Alia tamen est ratio Titulorum præfixorum ipsi Contextui sacro, Subscriptionum ad finem alicubi adjectarum, Distributionis in Capita, Supputationis Versuum, & si quæ sunt illis similia.
units.tr: The case is otherwise, however, with the titles prefixed to the sacred text itself, the subscriptions added at the end in some places, the division into chapters, the numbering of verses, and whatever is similar to these.

units.la: XXII. Quoniam verò SS. Scriptores immediatè & efficaciter inter scribendum ubique acti fuerunt à Spiritu Sancto; 1. nusquam ipsi de facto erra runt, neque errare potuerunt.
units.tr: XXII. Since, however, the sacred writers were everywhere moved immediately and effectively by the Holy Spirit in writing: 1. they never erred in fact, nor could they have erred.

units.la: 2. Nulla uspiam occurrit vera dissensio, aut repugnantia: ubi verò species aliqua contrarietatis occurrit, spectandæ sunt regulæ oppositionis, & sic instituenda conciliatio; vel agnoscenda nostra ignorantia.
units.tr: 2. No true dissension or contradiction occurs anywhere; where some appearance of contrariety does occur, the rules of opposition must be considered and reconciliation accomplished in this way, or else our ignorance must be acknowledged.

units.la: 3. S. Scriptura ubique loquitur secundùm accuratam rerum veritatem, sive proprie id fiat, sive tropicè, nusquam secundùm erroneam hominum opinionem; tam in naturalibus, & moralibus, quàm in supernaturalibus. Psal. XII, 7. „Eloquia Jehovæ, eloquia munda; „argentum excoctum in fornace terrea, defecatum septies. XIX, 8, 9. „Lex Jehovæ perfecta, convertens „animam: testimonium Iehovæ fidele, sapientem efficiens parvulum. Præcepta Iehovæ recta, lætificantia cor-
units.tr: 3. Holy Scripture everywhere speaks according to the exact truth of things, whether this is done properly or figuratively, and never according to the erroneous opinion of men; both in natural and moral matters, and in supernatural ones. Ps. 12:7: "The words of the LORD are pure words, silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times." 19:8, 9: "The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul; the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple. The precepts of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart."

units.la: CAP. III. De Sacra Scriptura.
units.tr: CHAPTER III. On Holy Scripture.

units.la: cor: præceptum Iehovæ purum, illuminans oculos. Confer sup. th. 4. & cap. 2. th. 2.
units.tr: heart: the commandment of Jehovah is pure, enlightening the eyes. Compare above, thesis 4, and chapter 2, thesis 2.

units.la: XXIII. Quæ hactenus de Auctoritate S. Scripturæ dicta sunt, non solum sic accipi debent de Autographis, verum etiam de Apographis fideliter factis: prout Deus plurium codicum descriptionem, eorumque familiarem usum, diserte mandavit; Deut. xvii, 18, 19. cum Josh. i, 8. Psal. i, 2. Joh. v, 39. xx, 31. Act. xvii, 11. Rom. iv, 23, 24. xv, 4. 1 Cor. x, 11. Col. iii, 16. 1 Tim. iv, 13. 2, 3, 14–17.
units.tr: XXIII. What has so far been said about the authority of Holy Scripture must be understood not only of the autographs but also of faithfully made copies (apographs), just as God expressly commanded that many copies be written and that they be used constantly; Deut. xvii, 18, 19, with Josh. i, 8; Ps. i, 2; John v, 39; xx, 31; Acts xvii, 11; Rom. iv, 23, 24; xv, 4; 1 Cor. x, 11; Col. iii, 16; 1 Tim. iv, 13; 2, 3, 14–17.

units.la: Eadem interim Veritas, Divinitas, & Auctoritas in Apographis etiam cognoscitur, 1. Exemplarium consensu.
units.tr: The same truth, divinity and authority are recognised also in the copies, (1) from the agreement of the copies;

units.la: 2. Per characteres Divinitatis ibi similiter conspicuos.
units.tr: (2) through the marks of divinity conspicuous in them likewise;

units.la: 3. Accedit Ecclesiæ testimonium.
units.tr: (3) to which is added the testimony of the Church;

units.la: Et 4. potissimum, efficax Spiritus Sancti persuasio, Fidem Divinam in nobis producens; quam ne quidem accuratissima manuum cognitio facere posset, aut qualiscunque hominum traditio & attestatio de Autographis, si ea superessent.
units.tr: and (4) chiefly, the effective persuasion of the Holy Spirit, producing divine faith in us, which not even the most accurate knowledge of handwriting could produce, nor any human tradition or attestation concerning the autographs, if these had survived.

units.la: XXIV. Verùm Autographa interire Deus sivit: tum quòd veris Apographis Ecclesiæ satis prospectum sit: tum etiam, ne caeteroquin una Ecclesia videretur ab alia dependere; aut reliquis imposita necessitas recurrendi perpetuò ad illam, ubi Autographa exstarent.
units.tr: XXIV. But God allowed the autographs to perish: partly because the Church has been sufficiently provided with true copies; and partly so that otherwise one church would seem to depend on another, or the rest would be under the necessity of constantly having recourse to that one where the autographs were extant.

units.la: Obj. Atqui passim in Codicibus σφάλματα quædam irrepserunt, per Librariorum incuriam, vel infscitiam. Resp. Codices satis multos voluit Deus in Ecclesiâ suâ exstare; ut ubi dubium suboriretur, alii Codices consuli possent, atque itâ scrupulus eximi. Sic interim per infirma operatur Deus, & potentiam suam demonstrat; atque hunc thesaurum in testaceis vasculis haberi voluit:
units.tr: Objection: Yet various errors [σφάλματα] have crept into the copies here and there through the carelessness or ignorance of scribes. Reply: God willed that copies should exist in his Church in sufficient number, so that where a doubt arose other copies could be consulted and the scruple thus removed. In this way God works meanwhile through weak things and shows his power, and he willed that this treasure be kept in earthen vessels:

units.la: 2 Cor. xii, 9. iv, 7.
units.tr: 2 Cor. xii, 9; iv, 7.

units.la: XXV. Sed nullis planè Versionibus formalis ista αὐἀυϑεντία competit: nec speciatim Vulgatæ Latinæ; quam Concilium Tridentinum decrevit pro authenticâ habendam. Nam 1. est opus humano studio, non autem à viris Θεοπνεύστοις, concinnatum.
units.tr: XXV. But this formal authority [αὐθεντία] belongs in no way to any versions, and specifically not to the Latin Vulgate, which the Council of Trent decreed should be held authentic. For (1) it is a work put together by human diligence, not by men inspired by God [θεοπνεύστοις].

units.la: 2. Ex variis auctoribus conflatum est.
units.tr: (2) It has been compiled from various authors.

units.la: 3. Saepius interpolatum & correctum, etiam postquam Concilium Tridentinum effet habitum, ac de eâ decretum condidisset; jussu Papæ Sixti V. ac deinde iterum jussu Clementis VIII.
units.tr: (3) It has been often interpolated and corrected, even after the Council of Trent had been held and had issued its decree concerning it, by order of Pope Sixtus V, and then again by order of Clement VIII.

units.la: 4. Interim fatentur auctores, alia, quæ mutanda videbantur, consulto immutata relicta esse, ad offensionem populorum vitandam, &c. Errores etiam satis multi ac manifesti sunt.
units.tr: (4) Meanwhile the authors themselves admit that other things, which seemed to need changing, were deliberately left unchanged, to avoid offending the peoples, and so on. Quite a few manifest errors are also present.

units.la: Similiter existimandum de Versione Græcâ, quæ appellatur LXX. Interpretum: cujus etiam auctores 1. non fuerunt Θεοπνεύστοι.
units.tr: The same must be judged of the Greek version called that of the Seventy, the Septuagint, whose authors also (1) were not inspired by God.

units.la: 2. Quot, & quales fuerint isti Interpretes; & an integra Biblia V. T. per eos translata, incertum est.
units.tr: (2) How many and what sort of interpreters they were, and whether the whole Old Testament was translated by them, is uncertain.

units.la: 3. Translationem illam adhuc puram exstare, non est certum; imò nec probabile.
units.tr: (3) That this translation still survives in its purity is not certain; indeed it is not even probable.

units.la: 4. Quæ isto nomine commendatur, plurimum discrepat ab Editione Hebraïca, verè authentica.
units.tr: (4) The version commended under that name differs considerably from the Hebrew edition, which is truly authentic.

units.la: XXVI. Diximus th. 15. faciendas etiam esse SS. Bibliorum Translationes in alias linguas; sicut autem in Ministris Christi, ac Dispensatoribus mysteriorum Dei, omnino requiritur, ut fidi reperiantur; 1 Cor. iv, 1, 2. ita in transferendis SS. Bibliis singularis cura & fides adhibenda est, ut originalis veritas quam optime exprimatur; vocesque & phrases singulæ, pro ratione linguarum ac idiotismorum, exhibeantur quam proximè & efficacissimè.
units.tr: XXVI. We said in thesis 15 that translations of the Holy Bible into other languages must also be made. But just as in the ministers of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God it is absolutely required that they be found faithful (1 Cor. iv, 1, 2), so in translating the Holy Scriptures a singular care and fidelity must be applied, so that the original truth is expressed as well as possible, and each word and phrase is rendered as closely and effectively as possible, according to the nature of the languages and their idioms.

units.la: In Bibliis autem fideliter translatis, agnoscenda est eadem Divina & Canonica Authoritas materialiter, secundum rem contentam, ejusque methodicam dispositionem, & realem expressionem; sed mutato idiomate.
units.tr: In Bibles faithfully translated, however, the same divine and canonical authority must be acknowledged materially, that is, according to the content, its methodical arrangement and real expression, but with the idiom changed.

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III.

units.la: Obj. Interpretes omnes fallibiles sunt. Resp. Attamen suppositâ fidelitate, & reali convenientiâ cum originalibus, non fefellerunt, nec falsi fuerunt actû Interpretes.
units.tr: Objection. All translators are fallible. Answer. Nevertheless, granting faithfulness and real agreement with the originals, the translators did not deceive, nor were they in fact false.

units.la: XXVII. Translationum sinceritas, saltem in rebus principalibus, ad fidem & mores potissimum necessariis, earumque Divinâ tractatione; atque adeò Canonica earum Authoritas secundum illud materiale, cognoscitur 1. ex collatione plurium Translationum.
units.tr: XXVII. The sincerity of translations, at least in principal matters, those chiefly necessary for faith and morals, and their divine handling; and so their canonical authority, in that material respect, is recognised: 1. from the comparison of several translations.

units.la: 2. Ex testimonio aliorum, sive fidelium, sive etiam infidelium, qui Linguas originales intelligunt.
units.tr: 2. From the testimony of others, whether faithful or even unfaithful, who understand the original languages.

units.la: 3. Per characteres Divinitatis, qui etiam in Translationibus exprimuntur.
units.tr: 3. Through the marks of divinity, which are also expressed in translations.

units.la: 4. Accedit insuper Spiritûs Sancti attestatio, & perfuafio interna, in cordibus nostris: quâ quidem luce subjectivè collustrati singuli, vident lucem illam objectivè, eamque pie agnoscunt; & sic fide Divinâ credunt, hoc revera esse Verbum Dei.
units.tr: 4. In addition there is the attestation of the Holy Spirit and his inward persuasion in our hearts. By this light, individuals illumined subjectively see that light objectively and piously acknowledge it; and so with divine faith they believe that this really is the Word of God.

units.la: XXVIII. Perfectio, vel sufficientia S. Scripturæ est, quâ Systema Biblicum omnia fidei & vitæ Christianæ dogmata, ad salutem consequendam necessaria plenè complectitur.'
units.tr: XXVIII. The perfection, or sufficiency, of Holy Scripture is that by which the biblical system fully embraces all the doctrines of faith and Christian life necessary for obtaining salvation.

units.la: Hæc autem spectatur, tùm, integralis, tùm essentialis.
units.tr: This is considered both integrally and essentially.

units.la: Integralis perfectio dicitur respectû partium integrantium; ut Systema S. Scripturæ etiam nunc omnes libros & omnes singulorum librorum partes, ac particulas comprehendat, prout Deus Ecclesiæ suæ dedit in canonem fidei ac morum.
units.tr: Integral perfection is spoken of with respect to the parts that make up the whole, so that the system of Holy Scripture now comprehends all the books, and all the parts and particles of each book, just as God has given them to his Church as the canon of faith and morals.

units.la: Asserimus ergò, S. Scripturam non esse in universum corruptam, aut depravatam; multis ex eâ sublatis, aliisque perperam insertis; contra Muhammedanos, qui isto prætextû Alkoranum suum commendare solent.
units.tr: We assert, therefore, that Holy Scripture has not been corrupted or depraved as a whole, with many things removed from it and others wrongly inserted; this is against the Muhammadans, who customarily commend their Alcoran on this pretext.

units.la: Neque ullos libros intercidisse, nec pluribus locis immutatam ac depravatam esse S. Scripturam; contra
units.tr: Nor have any books been lost, nor has Holy Scripture been changed and depraved in many places; against

units.la: CAP. III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III.

units.la: Pontificios, Socinianos, & incautos quosdam Criticos.
units.tr: Against the Papists, the Socinians, and certain incautious critics.

units.la: Huc pertinent 1. diserta quaedam Testimonia: Psal. XII, 7. XIX, 8, 9. Vide sup. th. 22. Adde Psal. XVIII, 31. XCIII, 5. CXIX, 140. Prov. XXX, 5. Item Matth. V, 18. „Amen quippe dico vobis; Ufquedum Praeterierit coelum & terra, ἰῶτα unum, aut unus apex ne„quaquam praeterierit ex Lege, ufquedum omnia facta „fuerint. 1 Petri II, 2. „Ut modo geniti infantes, „lac illud sermonis sincerum expetite. 2, 19. Habemus „firmissimum sermonem Propheticum: quem bene facitis „quod attendatis, &c.
units.tr: To this belong, first, certain plain testimonies: Ps. 12:7; 19:8, 9. See above, th. 22. Add Ps. 18:31; 93:5; 119:140; Prov. 30:5. Likewise Matt. 5:18: "For truly I say to you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota [ἰῶτα] or one stroke [ἀπex] shall by no means pass away from the Law, until all things have come to pass." 1 Pet. 2:2: "As newborn infants, desire the pure milk of the word." 2:19: "We have a most sure prophetic word, to which you do well to give heed," etc.

units.la: 2. Argumentamur à Fine; cujus gratiâ SS. Literae exaratae sunt; quippe requirit, ut integrae exstent usque ad finem mundi: Deuter. XXXI, 26, 27. „Capite „librum istum Legis, & ponite eum in latere Arcae foederis Iehovae Dei vestri; sitque ibi contra te in te„stem. -- Ecce adhuc me vivente vobiscum hodie, rebelles estis Iehovae; & quanto magis post mortem vestram? Jef. VIII, 20. Vide sup. cap. 1. th. 6. Luc. XVI, 29. „Habent Mosen & Prophetas; audiant eos: Rom. IV, 23, 24. „Non scriptum est autem propter eum (Abrahamum) solum, quod (hoc) imputatum fuerit ei: Sed etiam propter nos, quibus futurum est ut imputetur, &c. 1 Cor. X, 11. „Haec autem typice evenerunt eis (sub V. T.); scripta vero sunt ad nostri admonitionem, in quos fines saeculorum devenerunt. Job. XX, 31. Rom. XV, 4. Tim. III, 16, 17. Vide sup. th. 4.
units.tr: Second, we argue from the end, for the sake of which the Holy Scriptures were written. Indeed, it requires that they remain whole until the end of the world. Deut. 31:26, 27: "Take this book of the Law and put it beside the ark of the covenant of Jehovah your God, that it may be there as a witness against you. ... Behold, while I am still living with you today, you are rebels against Jehovah; how much more after my death?" Jer. 8:20; see above, ch. 1, th. 6. Luke 16:29: "They have Moses and the Prophets; let them hear them." Rom. 4:23, 24: "Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed to him; but also for our sake, to whom it is going to be imputed," etc. 1 Cor. 10:11: "Now these things happened to them as types (under the Old Testament); but they were written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the ages have come." John 20:31; Rom. 15:4; 2 Tim. 3:16, 17; see above, th. 4.

units.la: 3. A Providentia Dei speciali conservatrice: hanc enim non minus saltem circa S. Scripturam versari necesse est, quam circa Naturam. Quemadmodum igitur in Natura omnes creaturarum species perpetuo conservantur; etiam omnes & singulas S. Scripturae partes conservari, statuendum est: quia maxime versatur circa fideles, & quidem in ordine ad salutem ipsorum aeternam, & circa media ad eam promovendam necessaria. Jef. XLIX, 15, 16. Matth. X, 29, 30, 31. 1 Petr. 1. 5. cum Isf. lix, 21. Vide sup. Cap. 1. th. 29.
units.tr: Third, from the special preserving providence of God. For this must be concerned with Holy Scripture no less at least than with Nature. Just as in Nature all the species of creatures are perpetually preserved, so it must be held that all and each of the parts of Holy Scripture are preserved, because it is chiefly concerned with the faithful, and indeed with their eternal salvation, and with the means necessary to promote it. Isa. 49:15, 16; Matt. 10:29, 30, 31; 1 Pet. 1:5, compared with Isa. 59:21. See above, ch. 1, th. 29.

units.la: 4. A Curâ & fidelitate Ecclesiae, cui S. Scriptura committa est,& quae Providentiae isti Divinae subordinatur. Psal. CXLVII, 19, 20. Rom. iii, 2. 1 Tim. iii, 15. Vide sup. th. 4 & 16. cum Matth. xxviii, 20. "Ecce, Ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem saeculi.
units.tr: Fourth, from the care and faithfulness of the Church, to which Holy Scripture has been committed, and which is subordinate to this divine providence. Ps. 147:19, 20; Rom. 3:2; 1 Tim. 3:15; see above, th. 4 and 16, compared with Matt. 28:20: "Behold, I am with you all the days, even to the end of the age."

units.la: XXIX. Obj. 1. Numer. xxi. 14. allegatur Liber Bellorum Domini, Jof. x.13. Liber recti; & 1 Reg. xiv. 19. Chronica Regum Israelis.
units.tr: XXIX. Objection 1. Num. 21:14 cites the Book of the Wars of the Lord; Josh. 10:13, the Book of the Upright; and 1 Kings 14:19, the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

units.la: Verum isti libri in Canone sacro nunc non comparent: ergo. Resp. Isti libri non sunt, neque olim fuerunt, Canonici: unde nihil necesse fuit, eos semper conservari. At veritatem aliquam, quam Deus in Ecclesia omnino exstare voluit, ex illis allegavit, & comprobavit in libris verè Canonicis: Confer allegata ex Arato, Menandro, & Epimenide; Act. xvii, 28. 1 Cor. xv. 33. Tit. i. 12.
units.tr: But these books do not now appear in the sacred canon; therefore... Answer: these books are not, and never were, canonical; hence there was no need for them always to be preserved. Yet from them he cited some truth, which God willed to exist in the Church, and he confirmed it in books that are truly canonical. Compare the passages cited from Aratus, Menander and Epimenides: Acts 17:28; 1 Cor. 15:33; Titus 1:12.

units.la: Obj. 2. Atqui etiam allegantur scripta Nathanis, Gadi, &c. 1 Chron. xxix. 29. 2. ix, 29. Resp. Ista scripta vel exstant sub aliis titulis; in libris scil. Samuelis, & Regum; vel Canonicae non fuerunt.
units.tr: Objection 2. Yet the writings of Nathan, Gad, etc. are also cited: 1 Chron. 29:29; 2 Chron. 9:29. Answer: those writings either exist under other titles, namely in the books of Samuel and Kings, or they were not canonical.

units.la: Obj. 3. Paulus etiam commemorat epistolam suam ad Laodicenses; Col. iv. 16. Resp. Apostolus 1. non dicit epistolam illam à se scriptam; 2. nec ad Laodicenses; 3. neque eam esse Canonicam. Sed epistolam aliquam scriptam Laodicea commendat, ut legatur à Colossensibus. 4. Si quae Epistola à Paulo istic scripta intelligi deberet, cogitari posset de priori ad Timotheum, juxta ejus subscriptionem.
units.tr: Objection 3. Paul also mentions his epistle to the Laodiceans: Col. 4:16. Answer: the Apostle (1) does not say that this epistle was written by himself; (2) nor to the Laodiceans; (3) nor that it is canonical. But he commends some epistle written at Laodicea, to be read by the Colossians. (4) If an epistle written there by Paul is to be understood, one could think of the former one to Timothy, according to its subscription.

units.la: XXX. Perfectio essentialis dicitur ratione doctrinae salutaris, istis libris comprehensae, & per singulas partes diffusae, multisque vicibus ac modis repetitae, sic tamen ut ratione substantiae indè ab initio Foederis gratiae semper fuerit eadem. Heb. xiii, 8. Act. x. 43. xv, 11. v. 12, 2 Cor. iii. 11. 1 Tim. ii, 5, 6. Joh. xiv, 6. i. 16. Col. i, 19, 20.
units.tr: XXX. Essential perfection is said with respect to the doctrine of salvation, contained in these books and spread through their individual parts, and repeated many times and in many ways; yet so that, as to its substance, it has always been the same from the beginning of the covenant of grace. Heb. 13:8; Acts 10:43; 15:11; Rom. 5:12; 2 Cor. 3:11; 1 Tim. 2:5, 6; John 14:6; 1:16; Col. 1:19, 20.

units.la: Sic autem Systema S. Sripturæ indè ab initio fui continuit, & nunc etiam clarius continet omnia, quæ hominibus ad salutem consequendam necessaria sunt.
units.tr: Thus the system of Holy Scripture has contained from the beginning, and now contains even more clearly, all the things that are necessary for men to attain salvation.

units.la: S. Literis interim comprehensa intelligimus, non solum eâ, quæ formaliter, αὐτολεξεὶ & κατ' ἔνητον expressa sunt; sed etiàm, quæ virtualiter, καθ' ἀλλοιαν, καθ' ισοδυναμίαν, aut καθα συνα—χολουθησιν, continentur.
units.tr: By the things comprehended in the Sacred Writings we understand not only those that are expressed formally, word for word [αὐτολεξεί] and according to sense [κατ' ἔννοιαν]; but also those that are contained virtually, in another manner [καθ' ἄλλον τρόπον], by equivalence [καθ' ἰσοδυναμίαν], or by consequence [κατὰ συνακολούθησιν].

units.la: Neque spectamus, quæcunque in Ecclesiâ unquàm Divinitùs dicta aut facta sunt; sed quæ hominibus ad salutem consequendam necessaria, tùm in credendis tùm etiàm in agendis. Joh. xx, 30, 31. Multa vero etiàm alia signa edidit Jesus in Discipulorum suorum conspectu, quæ non sunt scripta in hoc libro: Hæc autem scripta sunt, ut credatis, &c.
units.tr: Nor do we look at whatever things were ever spoken or done by divine direction in the Church, but at those necessary for men to attain salvation, both in what is to be believed and in what is to be done. John 20:30, 31: "Jesus indeed did many other signs in the sight of his disciples, which are not written in this book; but these things are written, that you may believe," etc.

units.la: XXXI. Sententia ista orthodoxa probatur;
units.tr: XXXI. This orthodox view is proved:

units.la: 1. illustri illo testimonio, 2 Tim. iii, 14, 17. At tu mane-to in iis, quæ didicisti, & quæ tibi concredita sunt: sciens à quo didiceris: Teque à puero sacras literas novisse, quæ te possunt sapientem reddere ad salutem, per fidem, quæ est in Christo. Tota Scriptura Divinitus (est) inspirata, &c. Vide sup.: th. 4. Apostolus Euangelistam à falsis doctrinis dehortatur, docetque, in quibus post excessum suum ei perseverandum esset: itaque scil. ut eum revocet ad SS. Literas. De iis autem asserit (α.) posse sapientem reddere ad salutem, &c. Sapientia habitum perfectum notat: hæc vero in fide Christi ad salutem, SS. Literis, tanquàm unico principio doctrinali, tribuitur. (β.) Docet, Totam S. Scripturam esse Divinitus inspiratam: ab Auctore scil. Auctoritatem & Perfectionem arcessens; juxta Iac. i, 17. Verùm insupet (γ.) per partes hanc exequitur, utilis ad doctrinam, &c. Sic enim ejus usum demonstrat, non in uno tantùm, sed in omni genere ad salutem necessario; five veritas fuerit docenda, five falsitas redarguenda, five mali mores corrigendi, sive disciplina justitiae inculcanda. Quin etiam (s.) totum negotium conficit, & plane hanc litem terminat; concludens: ut Vir Dei (h. e. Doctor Ecclesiae ex ordinatione Dei; r Reg. xvii, 24. 1 Tim. vi, 11.) perfectus fit, in omnibus videl. istis partibus; & breviter ad omne opus bonum perfecte instructus. Ex persectione effectus patet perfectio causae.
