Ad Imagines creaturarum quod attinet non omnem earum formationem aut confectionem omnino illicitam vel prohibitam dicimus: nec absolutè vetitas artes ἰχαςικὰς; quibus rerum corporearum externa aspectabilis forma exprimitur & repræsentatur, vel operationes & effecta quædam aliarum etiam rerum symbolicè adumbrantur: Deus enim quosdam istis quoque artibus instruxisse dicitur, Exod. xxxi, 2, -6. xxxv, 30, -35. Atque in Tabernaculo, ac deinde etiam in Templo, ex praescripto ipsius Dei confectae fuerunt quaedam imagines Cherubinorum, palmarum, florum, &c. Sed illicitas & prohibitas dicimus imagines creaturarum, eo fine & modo, ut in iis, aut per eas, ipsum cultus religiosi objectum utcunque repraesentaretur, & sic ad eas cultus religiosus praestaretur. Hoc autem patet, ex verbis praecepti; Non facies tibi sculptile, neque ullam similitudinem, &c. Non incurvabis te eis, neque coles ea; Exod. xx, 4, 5.
units.tr: LIX. As for the images of creatures, we do not say that every formation or making of them is wholly unlawful or forbidden, nor are the arts of representation [ἰχαςικὰς] absolutely prohibited, by which the outward visible form of bodily things is expressed and portrayed, or certain operations and effects of other things are symbolically shadowed forth. For God is said to have endowed some with these very arts, Exod. 31:2–6; 35:30–35. Indeed, in the Tabernacle, and afterwards in the Temple, certain images of cherubim, palm trees, flowers, and so on were made according to the prescription of God himself. But we call the images of creatures unlawful and forbidden when they are made and used with the aim and in the manner that the object of religious worship is in some way represented in them or through them, and so religious worship is given to them. This is clear from the words of the precept: You shall not make for yourself a graven image, or any likeness, etc. You shall not bow down to them, nor serve them; Exod. 20:4, 5.

units.la: 2. Simile est interdictum, Deut. iv, 16, 17, 18. Ne forte corrumpatis vias vestras, &c.
units.tr: 2. Similar is the prohibition, Deut. 4:16, 17, 18: Lest perhaps you corrupt your ways, etc.

units.la: Atque iterum 3. Levit. xxvi, 1. Non facietis vobis idola, & sculptile, & statuam non erigetis vobis, neque lapidem pictum ponetis in terra vestra, ut incurvetis vos ei: Ego enim Iehovah Deus vester.
units.tr: And again, 3. Lev. 26:1: You shall not make idols for yourselves, nor set up a graven image or a standing stone for yourselves, nor shall you place a figured stone in your land, to bow down to it; for I am Jehovah your God.

units.la: Obj. Imagines Cherubinorum, aliaeque, fuerunt in Tabernaculo, & in Templo V. T. Ergo. Resp. Illae imagines ipsum objectum cultus religiosi nullo modo repraesentárunt; neque in iis & per eas Deo, aut sanctis quibusdam creaturis, cultus religiosus deferri debuit; imo nec secundum Dei praescriptum potuit. Sed pro ratione cultus istius oeconomici, pluriumque institutorum cerimonialium, per eas symbolice aliquid adumbratum fuit, ad Angelorum functiones, & ad majestatis ac gloriae Divinae indicium qualecunque, spectans: quod ipsum etiam in N. T. locum habere non debet, ubi cultum oportet esse magis spiritualem, sublatis omnibus istiusmodi typis ac symbolis.
units.tr: Objection: There were images of cherubim, and others, in the Tabernacle and in the Temple of the Old Testament. Therefore... Answer: Those images in no way represented the object of religious worship itself; nor was religious worship to be offered in them or through them to God or to certain holy creatures; indeed, it could not be so according to God's prescription. Rather, in keeping with the character of that economic worship and of the many ceremonial institutions, something was symbolically shadowed forth by them, relating to the functions of angels and to whatever indication of the divine majesty and glory there was. This itself ought not to hold a place even in the New Testament, where worship ought to be more spiritual, with all such types and symbols taken away.

units.la: IX. Prorsus igitur illicitus censeri debet talis imaginum usus, ut quis se coram iis prosterneret, eas amplexaretur, deosculaaretur, &c. quamvis ea mente ut non in ipsis, sed in earum exemplari vel archetypo, universus cultus religiosus terminaretur. Obstant enim 1. posteriora illa verba secundi praecepti, Non incurvabis te eis, neque coles ea; Exod. xx, 5. 2. Quoniam earum confectio in illum usum prohibita est; (ut modo probatum;) multo magis ipse talis earum usus censeri debet prohibitus.
units.tr: IX. Therefore such a use of images must be judged wholly unlawful, that a person should prostrate himself before them, embrace them, kiss them, etc., even though with the intention that the whole of religious worship terminates not in them but in their exemplar or archetype. For, first, the latter words of the second commandment stand in the way: You shall not bow down to them, nor serve them; Exod. 20:5. Second, since the making of them for that use has been forbidden (as has just been proved), such use of them itself must much more be judged forbidden.

units.la: 3. Deus omnem cultus religiosi communicationem ad aliud quodcunque objectum, præter se, districte prohibuit; utpote nolens gloriam suam alteri dari zelotes, & ignis consumens, Jef.xlii, 8. xlviii, 11. Exod. xx, 5, Deut. v, 9-iv,24.
units.tr: 3. God strictly forbade any communication of religious worship to any object whatever besides himself, since he is unwilling to give his glory to another, a jealous God and a consuming fire: Isa. 42:8; 48:11; Exod. 20:5; Deut. 5:9; 4:24.

units.la: 4. Magis etiam nunc sub N. T. talis usus adversatur cultui spirituali, qualem sub hac œconomiâ esse oportet.
units.tr: 4. Moreover, under the New Testament such a use is even more opposed to the spiritual worship that ought to exist under this dispensation.

units.la: Exc. Ex hominum socordia oritur necessitas devotionis per ejusmodi adminicula excitandæ & promovendæ. Resp. Sed nos non decet arbitratu proprio adminicula ištiusmodi fingere; nedum à Deo diserte prohibita: quin & ipse Deus objecta & adminicula satis multa ac varia nobis suppeditavit, quæ occasionem præbent majestatem ipsius meditandi & prædicandi, quæque nos ad ipsius cultum & honorem debent incitare: minus autem veniendum ad ea, quæ ulterioris etiam idololatriæ proclivem occasionem præbere possunt & solent.
units.tr: Objection. From the sloth of men there arises the need to stir up and promote devotion by such aids. Answer. But it is not fitting for us to devise such aids by our own judgment, much less those expressly forbidden by God. Indeed, God himself has supplied us with many and varied objects and aids, which provide occasion for meditating upon and proclaiming his majesty, and which ought to stir us up to his worship and honour. We should, however, avoid those things which can and commonly do provide a ready occasion for further idolatry.

units.la: Multo etiam magis censeri debet illicita confectio & usus imaginum in ordine ad falsa numina, aut qualiacunque objecta cultus religiosi præter unum verum Deum; quatenus videlicet istæ imagines adminicula forent, aut symbola, talis cultus idololatrici: quoniam enim omnis ejusmodi cultus illicitus est, adminicula ad ipsum proprie ordinata non possunt esse licita. Et quemadmodum ipse ille cultus primò Decalogi præcepto adversatur, sic talis imaginum confectio & usus ad illum cultum, secundo præcepto repugnat. Hoc autem ad imagines humanæ naturæ Christi, & Sanctorum, in Papatu quoque applicatum volumus.
units.tr: Much more must the making and use of images be judged unlawful with reference to false deities, or to any objects of religious worship other than the one true God; inasmuch as such images would be aids or symbols of that idolatrous worship. For since all such worship is unlawful, the aids properly directed to it cannot be lawful. And just as that worship itself opposes the first precept of the Decalogue, so such making and use of images for that worship opposes the second precept. We wish this to be applied also, in Popery, to images of the human nature of Christ and of the saints.

units.la: LXI. Sed neque imagines Christi, & Sanctorum, in templis aut oratoriis Christianorum habéri debent dum, quod Christus secundum praeceptum auxerit additio mandato de cavendis idolis, eorumque locis, ut & idolothytis. Nam 1. de idolis fugiendis satis aperta & emphatica est prohibitio. Exod xxi 1,13. In omnibus, quae dixi vobis, cauti eritis. Neque nomen Deorum aliorum memorabitis: non audietur in ore tuo. Imo & ratio huic secundo praecepto adjecta; Ego enim Iehovah Deus tuus, zelotes, &c. Atque item exemplum, Psal.xvi,4. Nec non promissio. Hos. 2,17.
units.tr: LXI. Nor should images of Christ and of the saints be kept in the temples or oratories of Christians, since Christ, in accordance with the precept, added to the command concerning the avoidance of idols and their places, also that of idol-offerings. For, first, the prohibition concerning the flight from idols is quite plain and emphatic: Exod. 23:13: In all that I have said to you, you shall be careful. Nor shall you make mention of the names of other gods; let it not be heard in your mouth. Indeed, the reason is also added to this second precept: For I, Jehovah your God, am a jealous God, etc. Likewise the example, Ps. 16:4, and the promise, Hos. 2:17.

units.la: Similiter etiam 2. de instrumentis & locis cultui idolorum appropriatis; ut ea confringantur, vel etiam diruantur, ad tollendum occasionem seductionis, & in detestationem idololatriae: Deut.vii, 25,26.xii,2,3. Confer factum Patriarchę Jacobi & familiarium ejus, Gen.xxxv,2,4. Atque item exemplum Regis Hiskijahu, 2 Reg.xviii,4.
units.tr: Similarly also, second, concerning the instruments and places appropriated to the worship of idols: that they should be broken in pieces, or even demolished, to remove the occasion of seduction and in detestation of idolatry: Deut. 7:25, 26; 12:2, 3. Compare the deed of the patriarch Jacob and his household, Gen. 35:2, 4. Likewise the example of King Hezekiah, 2 Kings 18:4.

units.la: Quantum vero attinet 3. ad Idolothyta, quatenus subesset conscientia idoli, aut participatio aliqua idololatriae, sic ea etiam sub V.T. fuisse prohibita & illicita, satis patet ex historia, Num. xxv,1,2,3. Coepit populus fornicari cum filiabus Moab. Et vocaverunt populum ad sacrificia Deorum suorum: comedit que populus. Unde etiam Apostolus argumentum petit, 1 Cor. x,7,8. Ne igitur idololatrae fiatis, sicut quidam eorum, &c. Adde exemplum Davidis, Psal.xvi,4.
units.tr: As far as concerns, third, idol-offerings, in so far as there was an awareness of the idol, or some participation in idolatry, that these also were forbidden and unlawful under the Old Testament is sufficiently clear from history, Num. 25:1, 2, 3: The people began to commit fornication with the daughters of Moab. And they invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate. Whence the Apostle also draws his argument, 1 Cor. 10:7, 8: Therefore do not become idolaters, as some of them did, etc. Add the example of David, Ps. 16:4.

units.la: Obj. In N.T. dicitur, 1 Joh. v,21. Filioli, cavete ab idolis. itemque 1 Cor. x,14. Dilecti mei, fugite ab idololatria. Et idolothyta, quamvis in se non illicita manducari, prohibentur tamen 1 Cor. viii, & x. Resp. Scil. quando & quatenus in iis foret participatio aliqua idololatriae, aut metus seductionis ad eam. Verum ista non sunt nova praecepta; sed antiqua, sub N.T. repetita, & ad praesentes occasiones applicata.
units.tr: Objection: In the New Testament it is said, 1 John 5:21: Little children, beware of idols; and likewise, 1 Cor. 10:14: My beloved, flee from idolatry. And idol-offerings, although in themselves lawful to eat, are nevertheless forbidden in 1 Cor. 8 and 10. Answer: Namely, when and in so far as there would be some participation in idolatry in them, or fear of seduction to it. But these are not new precepts; they are ancient ones, repeated under the New Testament and applied to present occasions.

units.la: Inst. Novo Test. proprium est, quod dicitur 1 Cor. 8,10,11. Etenim si quis viderit te, illa cognitione praeditum, in idolio accumbere, nonne conscientia ipsius quia infirmus firmus est, instruetur ad edendum ea quæ sunt idolis mactata ? Et tuâ istâ cognitione frater ille infirmus, propter quem Christus est mortuus, peribit ? Resp. Ista ratio à dilectione proximo debitâ, atque itâ ex posteriore Legis tabulâ, defumta est, sed novum additamentum ad secundum Decalogi præceptum nullo modo constituit; aut probat: ut neque mortis Christi mentio in præterito tempore.
units.tr: Instance: What is proper to the New Testament is what is said in 1 Cor. 8:10, 11: For if someone sees you, who have this knowledge, reclining in an idol's temple, will not his conscience, since he is weak, be emboldened to eat the things sacrificed to idols? And through your knowledge that weak brother, for whom Christ died, will perish? Answer: This reasoning is drawn from the love owed to one's neighbour, and so from the second table of the Law; but it in no way constitutes or proves a new addition to the second precept of the Decalogue, just as the mention of Christ's death in the past tense does not.

units.la: LXIV. Sed & contra Pantificios tenendum, Secundum illud præceptum à primo verè distinctum esse:
units.tr: LXIV. But against the Papists it must also be maintained that the second commandment is truly distinct from the first,

units.la: çum in primo prohibeantur falsa objecta terminantia cultus religiosi; & vel objecti agnitio & cultus conveniens præcipiatur: in secundo vero prohibeantur modi, ac media, absurdè ab hominibus excogitata, confecta, & adhibita ad cultum Dei; simulque præcipiatur modus Deum colendi ab ipso institutus. Consequenter, secundum istud præceptum nullo modo omittendum est, tanquam supervacaneum: quod frequenter faciunt Adversarii, ad occultandam enormem illam idololatriæ suæ speciem: neque pro appendicè solùm, aut declaratione primi præcepti, habendum.
units.tr: since the first forbids false objects that set the limits of religious worship, and commands the recognition of the proper object and fitting worship; whereas the second forbids the modes and means, absurdly devised, made and used by men in the worship of God, and at the same time commands the manner of worshipping God that he himself has instituted. Consequently this second commandment must by no means be omitted as superfluous, as the adversaries often do in order to hide the monstrous form of their idolatry, nor is it to be regarded merely as an appendix to, or explanation of, the first commandment.

units.la: XLV. Socinianí tertio præcepto duo per Christum pro N. T. adjecta statuunt; 1. ne leviter vel temere juremus. 2. quod etiam per nomen ipsius Christi jurare liceat. Sed quantum attinet ad prius; 1. Adversarii prorsus non possunt probare, sub V. T. juramenta temeraria, quâvis de causâ, & in vitâ quotidianâ, fuisse licita: neque enim id colligi potest ex reprehensione & correctione Christi, Matth. v, 33, -37. quæ solum adversus praxin & perversa glossemata Pharisæorum & Scribarum institutæ sunt.
units.tr: XLV. The Socinians hold that two things were added by Christ to the third commandment under the New Testament: (1) that we must not swear lightly or rashly; (2) that it is lawful to swear even by the name of Christ himself. But as far as the former is concerned: (1) the adversaries cannot at all prove that under the Old Testament rash oaths, for whatever cause and in everyday life, were lawful. For this cannot be inferred from the rebuke and correction of Christ, Matt. 5:33-37, which were directed solely against the practice and perverse glosses of the Pharisees and Scribes.

units.la: 2. Diserte in tertio præcepto prohibetur omnis usurpatio nominis Divini vana aut temeraria: at certe juramentum temerarium, est temeraria nominis Divini usurpatio.
units.tr: (2) The third commandment expressly forbids every vain or rash use of the divine name. But a rash oath is certainly a rash use of the divine name.

units.la: 3. Scopus præcepti procul dubio est, prohibere omnem tatem evecto ; ex auctoritate politica, juxta officium gratitudinis erga Deum, & commemorationis beneficiorum ejus: si non Spiritu prophetico ; atque ita ab universo populo libenter recepti. Consequenter ex illis non possunt colligi jejunia ordinaria & perpetua, sub N. T. lege Ecclesiastica, aut à Papâ Romano, omnibus gentibus obtrudenda, vel obtrusa.
units.tr: (3) The purpose of the commandment is without doubt to forbid every fast not proclaimed by political authority, which is undertaken as a duty of gratitude towards God and as a remembrance of his benefits, unless it is prompted by the prophetic Spirit, and thus willingly received by the whole people. Consequently, ordinary and perpetual fasts under the ecclesiastical law of the New Testament cannot be inferred from these, nor can they be imposed, or have been imposed, on all nations by the Roman Pope.

units.la: Obj. 3. Jejunia quaedam à Judaeis celebrata fuerunt sub captivitate Babylonica. Ergo. Resp. sed illi dies deinde, sublata ista causâ, fuerunt conversi in festivos, edicente ipso Deo, Zach. viii: 19. Unde nullo pacto colligi possunt stata jejunia in perpetuum observanda, & quidem sub N. T.
units.tr: Objection 3. Certain fasts were observed by the Jews during the Babylonian captivity. Therefore... Answer: but those days afterwards, that cause having been removed, were turned into festivals, God himself so commanding, Zech. 8:19. Hence fixed fasts to be observed in perpetuity cannot in any way be inferred, and certainly not under the New Testament.

units.la: Obj. 4. Christus praedixit, & docuit habenda ejusmodi jejunia; Matth. ix. 15. Ergo. Resp. Istic praedicitur quidem fore, ut Christiani urgente necessitate jejunent: sed nihil inde sequitur pro ordinariis & perpetuis jejuniis, & quidem Papisticè servandis.
units.tr: Objection 4. Christ foretold and taught that such fasts should be held, Matt. 9:15. Therefore... Answer: There it is indeed foretold that Christians will fast under pressing necessity, but nothing follows from this for ordinary and perpetual fasts, and certainly not for fasts to be kept in the Papist manner.

units.la: I. Vitiatur etiam precatio per inanem eorundem verborum repetitionem; quasi ea, propter iterationem istiusmodi ac prolixitatem, futura esset efficacior, Deoque grata, & exaudienda. Per istam βατταλογίαν καὶ πολυλογίαν non posse gratiam impetrari, 1. satis declaravit Deus sub V. T. Jef. 1, 15.
units.tr: I. Prayer is also corrupted by the empty repetition of the same words, as if by such repetition and wordiness it would be more effective, pleasing to God, and sure to be heard. (1) God has sufficiently declared under the Old Testament, Isa. 1:15, that grace cannot be obtained through such vain repetition and much speaking [βατταλογία καὶ πολυλογία].

units.la: 2. Et Christus in N.T. Matth. vi, 7.
units.tr: (2) Christ also in the New Testament, Matt. 6:7.

units.la: 3. Tales homines faciunt sè similes Gentilibus, verâ Dei cognitione ac fide destitutis: Matth. vi, 7, 8.
units.tr: (3) Such people make themselves like the Gentiles, who lack the true knowledge of God and faith, Matt. 6:7, 8.

units.la: 4. Accedit ratio: frustra scil. adhibentur frequentes illae repetitiones, & diuturni clamores sine mente; quia Deus satis novit quibus egeamus, & paratus est necessaria dare omnibus serio petentibus secundum voluntatem ipsius; Matth. vi, 8. Joh. xvi: 26, 27. 1 Joh. v, 14, 15.
units.tr: (4) There is also this reason: those frequent repetitions and long cries without understanding are in vain, since God knows well what we need, and is ready to give all necessary things to all who ask earnestly, according to his will, Matt. 6:8; John 16:26, 27; 1 John 5:14, 15.

units.la: Rejicienda igitur Pontificiorum Rosaria, aut Sphaerulae precatoriae, per quas ad numerum recitantur orationes, atque inde major earum praesumitur efficacia. Itemque boatû Monachorum in templis; cum quibus conferendi clamores Baalitarum, 1 Reg. xviii, 26, 27, 28.
units.tr: Therefore the rosaries of the Papists, or prayer beads, by which prayers are counted off by number, and from which greater efficacy is presumed, are to be rejected. Likewise the bawling of monks in the temples, with which the cries of the Baalites may be compared, 1 Kings 18:26, 27, 28.

units.la: LI. Sequitur Votum, Religiosa pollicitatio rei alicujus Deo gratæ, in ejus gloriam præstandæ; vel etiàm rei ingratæ, similiter omittendæ.
units.tr: LI. There follows the Vow: a religious promise of something pleasing to God, to be performed for his glory, or likewise of something displeasing to be omitted.

units.la: Hunc actum religionis soli Deo deferendum, satis evidenter docent SS. Literæ: Pf. lxxvi, 12. Vovete, & reddite Jehovæ Deo vestro. Vide etiam Num. xxx, 2, 3, Deut. xxiii; 21, 23. Psal. l, 14, cxvi, 14. Isef. xix; 21.
units.tr: That this act of religion is to be offered to God alone, the Holy Scriptures teach quite plainly: Ps. 76:12, "Vow, and pay to Jehovah your God." See also Num. 30:2, 3; Deut. 23:21, 23; Ps. 50:14; 116:14; Isa. 19:21.

units.la: 2. Accedunt exempla Sanctorum; utpote Jacobi, Gen. xxviii, 20, 21, 22.
units.tr: (2) Add the examples of the saints, such as Jacob's, Gen. 28:20, 21, 22.

units.la: 3. Quia in voto inest religiosa invocatio, quæ soli Deo debetur.
units.tr: (3) Because a vow contains a religious invocation, which is owed to God alone.

units.la: 4. Quia vovendum est ei soli, à quo omnia bona nos oportet expectare, cui pro beneficiis acceptis debemus gratias agere, cui intimè animum nostrum cognoscit, de-ue omnibus nostris judicare poterit; ut cuique ad rem ipsam attendenti satis manifestum est; hæc autem omnia soli Deo convenient.
units.tr: (4) Because one ought to vow to him alone, from whom we must expect all good things, to whom we owe thanks for the benefits received, who knows our heart inwardly and can judge all our affairs. As is plain enough to anyone who attends to the matter, all these things belong to God alone.

units.la: LII. Vota fieri debent de faciendis iis, quæ Deo placent; aut omittendis, quæ displicent. Deo autem placere intelliguntur, tùm quæ ipsè præcepit in specie; tùm etiàm talis usus rerum aliàs indifferentium, qualis ratione circumstantium ad gloriam Dei, nostramque & aliorum ædificationem faciem, conducit. Vide Gen. xxviii, 2, 22. Quis sub V. T. deberet esse votum Nazaræatus; ipse Deus c præscripsit Num. vi, 1, 21. De aliis item votis, quid, & quomodo sibi placeret, exposuit Levit. xxvii, 2, -14. atque alibi: imo & speciali nonnulla, quæ displicerent, indicavit, Levit. xxii, 23. Deut. xxiii, 18. Quemadmodum vero in universo cultu Divino improbanda est ἐθελοθρησκεία, sic etiàm in Votis. Vide Deut. xii, 8. Isef. xxix, 13. Matth. xv, 9. Col. 2, 23.
units.tr: LII. Vows ought to be made about doing what pleases God, or omitting what displeases him. Now things are understood to please God both when he himself has prescribed them in particular, and also when such use of things otherwise indifferent is suited to the glory of God and to our and others' edification, given the circumstances. See Gen. 28:2, 22. What the vow of the Nazarite under the Old Testament ought to be, God himself prescribed, Num. 6:1, 21. Concerning other vows likewise, he set out what and how he would be pleased, Lev. 27:2-14, and elsewhere; indeed he also pointed out some specific things that displeased him, Lev. 22:23; Deut. 23:18. But just as self-chosen worship [ἐθελοθρησκεία] is to be condemned in the whole of divine worship, so also in vows. See Deut. 12:8; Isa. 29:13; Matt. 15:9; Col. 2:23.

units.la: Hujusmodi sunt Vota Papistica de suscipiendâ peregrinatione religionis ergo, de processione sacra, &c. & speciatim Monastica, & perpetuo coelibatu, spontanea paupertate, & caeca obedientia erga superiores suos ac regulas Monasticas. Sed 1. S. Scriptura vitam illam Monasticam nec mandat, nec docet.
units.tr: Of this kind are the Papist vows: to undertake a pilgrimage for the sake of religion, to join a sacred procession, and so on; and especially the monastic vows of perpetual celibacy, voluntary poverty, and blind obedience to their superiors and the monastic rules. But (1) Holy Scripture neither commands nor teaches that monastic life.

units.la: 2. Opinionem de Satisfactionibus ac Meritis propriis, & Perfectione etiam supererogatoria, qui Monachorum Papalium scopus est, Euangelium refellit validissime; dum in solo Christo justitiam quaerendam, ac fide apprehendendam, proponit.
units.tr: (2) The gospel most strongly refutes the opinion about one's own satisfactions and merits, and even about supererogatory perfection, which is the aim of the Papal monks, since it sets forth that righteousness is to be sought in Christ alone and apprehended by faith.

units.la: 3. Neque Consilia Divina a Praeceptis differunt realiter. Vide sup. cap. 8. th. 32.
units.tr: (3) Nor do the divine counsels really differ from the precepts. See above, chap. 8, th. 32.

units.la: 4. In specie: a. Paupertatem nusquam ut bonum morale, pluribus vero locis malum triste, proponit S. Pagina: Prov. VI, 11. XXX. 8, 9. Act. XX, 35. 2 Cor. VIII, 9. Hoc autem nemo sibi ultro debet arcessere, sed Divinitus immissum patienter ac sapienter ferre:
units.tr: (4) In particular: a. Holy Scripture nowhere proposes poverty as a moral good, but in many places as a sad evil: Prov. 6:11; 30:8, 9; Acts 20:35; 2 Cor. 8:9. No one ought to seek it for himself of his own accord, but to bear patiently and wisely what is sent by God:

units.la: 2 Cor. XI, 26, 27. Phil. IV. 11, 12. Confer Math. XIX, 20, &c.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 11:26, 27; Phil. 4:11, 12. Compare Matt. 19:20, etc.

units.la: β. Coelibatum non nisi donum continentiae habentibus, ac pro ratione temporum, & respectu necessitatis, commendat: 1 Cor. VII, 7, 9, 26, 28, 32, 37. Luc. 23, 28, 29. Hebr. 13, 4. 1 Tim. 4, 1, 2, 3, III, 2, 4, 5.
units.tr: β. It commends celibacy only to those who have the gift of continence, and according to the circumstances of the times and the needs of the moment: 1 Cor. 7:7, 9, 26, 28, 32, 37; Luke 23:28, 29; Heb. 13:4; 1 Tim. 4:1, 2, 3; 3:2, 4, 5.

units.la: γ. Et probationem eorum, quae per homines praecipiuntur, ac de iis judicium decretionis, requirit, Deoque semper magis obediendum, quam hominibus, inculcat: 1 Thess. V, 21.
units.tr: γ. It requires the testing of what is commanded by men, and a judgment about it, and constantly impresses that God must be obeyed rather than men: 1 Thess. 5:21.

units.la: 1 Joh. IV, 1. 1 Cor. X, 15. Act. IV, 19, V. 29.

LIII. Socinians existimant, Christum in N. T. auxisse decem illa praecepta, ac perfectiora reddidisse: speciatim autem primo adjecisse, 1. praeceptum generale, de precibus Deo faciendis: 2. formulam orationis Dominicae; & 3. praeceptum de adorando etiam Christo.
units.tr: LIII. The Socinians think that Christ in the New Testament enlarged those ten commandments and made them more perfect; specifically, that he added to the first commandment (1) a general precept about making prayers to God, (2) the form of the Lord's Prayer, and (3) a precept about adoring Christ also.

units.la: Verum primo sub V. T. fuit eadem obligatio ad preces Deo faciendas super omni necessitate, juxta voluntatem ipsius tunc quoque revelatam : sic enim
units.tr: But first, under the Old Testament there was the same obligation to make prayers to God in every necessity, according to his will, which was then also revealed. For thus:

units.la: 1. Ipse Deus, Ps.L,15. Invocante in die angustiæ: eruam te;& honorificabis me. xci,15. Invocabit me;& exaudiam eum, &c. Adde, xcv, 6. Jes. LV, 6. Imo etiam, Deut. vi,13. Jehovam Deum tuum timebis, & ipsum colES; quam sententiam Servator exprellit hoc modo, Matth. iv, 10. Dominum Deum tuum adorabis,& illum solum coles.
units.tr: (1) God himself says, Ps. 50:15: "Call upon me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you shall honour me." Ps. 91:15: "He shall call upon me, and I will hear him," etc. Add Ps. 95:6; Isa. 55:6. Indeed also Deut. 6:13: "You shall fear Jehovah your God and serve him," which sentence the Saviour expressed thus, Matt. 4:10: "You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve him alone."

units.la: 2. Universa doctrina de sacrificiis Deo offerendis, hanc veritatem innuit etiam satis aperte: quis enim dubitat, preces sacrificiis adjungi debuisse, atque istas suffitu sacro propterea fuisse adumbratas? Vide Iob xliii, 8, 9, 10. Psal. cxli, 2. Confer Luc. I, 10. Act. iii, 1.
units.tr: 2. The whole doctrine of sacrifices offered to God also hints at this truth quite plainly. For who doubts that prayers ought to have been joined to the sacrifices, and that the sacred incense was foreshadowed on this account? See Job 43:8, 9, 10; Ps. 141:2. Compare Luke 1:10; Acts 3:1.

units.la: 3. Accedit praxis fidelium; utpote Danielis, etiam contra gravissimam Regis prohibitionem; vi, 11, 12. Adeo ut istius exercitii omissio habita fuerit pro notâ summæ impietatis; Psal. xiv, 4.
units.tr: 3. Add the practice of the faithful, as of Daniel, who did this even against the most severe prohibition of the King: Dan. 6:11, 12. So much so that the omission of this exercise was regarded as a mark of the greatest impiety: Ps. 14:4.

units.la: 4. Imo etiam Gentiles hoc officium agnoverunt utcunque, & alii idololatræ, ac superstitiosi; qui preces quoque usurpârunt, secundum conscientiam voluntatis Divinæ: quanto autem magis hoc de populo Dei, & fœderatis fidelibus, agnoscendum est?
units.tr: 4. Indeed the Gentiles too acknowledged this duty to some extent, and other idolaters and superstitious people, who also used prayers, according to their conscience of the divine will. How much more must this be acknowledged of the people of God and the faithful in covenant!

units.la: LIV. Secundo, Formula orationis Dominicæ non constituit novum aliquod præceptum; sed est medium à Christo propositum, quo nos in praxi precum (quam à nobis postulat primum Decalogi præceptum) juvaremur ac dirigeremur.
units.tr: LIV. Secondly, the formula of the Lord's Prayer does not establish some new precept. It is a means proposed by Christ by which we are helped and directed in the practice of prayer, which the first commandment of the Decalogue requires of us.

units.la: 2. Singulæ etiam particulæ istius orationis satis aperte fuerunt comprehensæ ac propositæ scriptis V. T. Exordium quidem in locis, Ief. lxiii, 16. Tu enim Pater noster es, &c. Mal. I. 6. Quod si Pater ego sum, ubi est honor mei? Ief. lxvi, 1. Sic dixit Iehovah, Cœlum est solium meum, &c.
units.tr: 2. The individual parts of that prayer were also quite plainly comprehended and set forth in the writings of the Old Testament. The opening appears in passages such as Isa. 63:16, For you are our Father, etc. Mal. 1:6, But if I am a Father, where is my honour? Isa. 66:1, Thus says Jehovah: Heaven is my throne, etc.

units.la: Petitio prima similiter, Psal. viii, 2. Iehovah Domine noster, quam grande est nomen tuum in universa terra: qui posuisti gloriam tuam super cœlos! Adde, cxv, 1.
units.tr: The first petition likewise: Ps. 8:2, Jehovah our Lord, how glorious is your name in all the earth, you who have set your glory above the heavens! Add Ps. 115:1.

units.la: Secunda ; Psal. II, 6. Ego constitui Regem meum super Tzionem montem sanctum meum. Adde, lxxii, 1. 7. 11, 20. lxxiv, 2.
units.tr: The second: Ps. 2:6, I have set my king upon Zion, my holy mountain. Add Ps. 72:1, 7, 11, 20; 74:2.

units.la: Tertia ; Psal. cxliii, 10. Doce me facere voluntatem Tuam ; quia Tu es Deus meus : Spiritus Tuus bonus deducat me in terram rectam. xxv, 4, 5.
units.tr: The third: Ps. 143:10, Teach me to do your will, for you are my God; let your good Spirit lead me into the land of uprightness. Ps. 25:4, 5.

units.la: Quarta ; Prov. xxx, 8. Aletne cibo qui convenit mihi, Gen. xxviii, 20, 21.
units.tr: The fourth: Prov. 30:8, Feed me with the food that is convenient for me; Gen. 28:20, 21.

units.la: Quinta ; Psal. xxv, 11. Propter nomen tuum Iehovah, parce iniquitati meæ : quoniam multa est. 11, 3, 4.
units.tr: The fifth: Ps. 25:11, For your name's sake, Jehovah, pardon my iniquity, for it is great. Ps. 11:3, 4.

units.la: Sexta item; Ps. xix, 14. Etiam à superbis prohibe servum Tuum, ne dominentur mihi : tunc perfectus ero, & mundus ero à prævaricatione magna. cxix, 36, 37.
units.tr: The sixth likewise: Ps. 19:14, Keep back your servant also from the proud, that they may not rule over me; then I shall be perfect, and I shall be clean from great transgression. Ps. 119:36, 37.

units.la: Ac tandem Conclusio ; 1 Chron. xxix, 11. Tibi, ô Iehovah, est magnificentia, & potentia, & gloria, & decor : cuncta enim, quæ in cœlo sunt & in terra ; tua sunt. Tuum est, ô Jehovah regnum, & exaltatio super omnes qui sunt in caput. Psal. xli, 14. Benedictus Jehovah Deus Israëlis sæculo, & usque in sæculum. Amen & Amen.
units.tr: And finally the conclusion: 1 Chron. 29:11, To you, O Jehovah, belong magnificence, and power, and glory, and majesty; for all that is in heaven and in earth is yours. Yours, O Jehovah, is the kingdom, and you are exalted above all as head. Ps. 41:14, Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Israel, from age to age. Amen and Amen.

units.la: LV. Neque tertio illud de adorando Christo censeri debet per ipsum primo Decalogi præcepto adjectum sub N. T. cum 1. ipse sit idem æternus & verus Deus cum Patre ac Spiritu Sancto, eâdemque religione semper colendus.
units.tr: LV. Nor, thirdly, should that precept about adoring Christ, added under the New Testament to the first commandment of the Decalogue, be judged to be of no account. For 1. he is the same eternal and true God with the Father and the Holy Spirit, and is always to be worshipped with the same worship.

units.la: 2. Propterea etiam scriptum est, Psal. 2, 12. Osculamini Filium, ne forte irascatur. - Beati omnes qui sperant in eo. Et xcvii, 7. Incurvate vos Ei, omnes Dii, cum Hebr. 1, 6. Pursum autem, cum inducit Primogenitum in orbem terrarum, dicit ; Et adorent Eum omnes Angeli Dei. Sic adorationem Filii ex illo V. T. loco allegavit Apostolus. Adde Gen. xlviii, 16.
units.tr: 2. For this reason it is also written: Ps. 2:12, Kiss the Son, lest he be angry. Blessed are all who put their trust in him. And Ps. 97:7, Bow down before him, all you gods. Compare Heb. 1:6, where the Apostle, when he brings the Firstborn into the world, says: And let all the angels of God worship him. Thus the Apostle cited the worship of the Son from that Old Testament passage. Add Gen. 48:16.

units.la: 3. In N. T. perstringitur idololatria Gentilium tali argumento. Rom. 1, 25. quod venerati sint & coluerint res conditas, præterito Creatore, qui est benedictus in sæcula. Ac similiter, Gal. iv, 8. Imo tum quidem ignorantes Deum, serviebatis iis, qui natura non sunt Dii. At si tunc obtinuisset sententia Socinistica, quam proclive fuisset Gentilibus regerere; Quid in eo absurdi; cum etiam vos Christiani veneremini & colatis Christum, ex novo quodam ipsius præcepto, qui tamen res condita est, non Deus natura, nec olim adoratus, aut adorari jussus?
units.tr: 3. In the New Testament the idolatry of the Gentiles is condemned by such an argument: Rom. 1:25, because they venerated and worshipped created things, passing over the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Likewise Gal. 4:8: Indeed, at that time, not knowing God, you served those who by nature are not gods. But if the Socinian opinion had prevailed then, how easily the Gentiles could have retorted: What is absurd in that, since you Christians too venerate and worship Christ by some new precept of his, who nevertheless is a created thing, not God by nature, nor was he formerly worshipped or commanded to be worshipped?

units.la: LVI. Imagines in secundo Decalogi præcepto spectantur ut media, quibus homines sibi Deum externè conan- tur repræsentare, & mentem in ipsum dirigere.
units.tr: LVI. Images in the second commandment of the Decalogue are regarded as means by which people outwardly try to represent God to themselves and to direct their minds towards him.

units.la: Quæritur autem, An liceat in talem usum conficere imagines ipsius Dei; & porrò confectas ejusmodi imagines sic retinere & usurpare? Nos negativam tenemus adversùs Pontificios, quorum contraria est sententia ac praxis; dùm variis modis Deum, & S. Trinitatem pingunt, & fingunt; potissimùm verò Deum Patrem in formâ hominis senis, triplici coronâ, ac deinceps reliquo Papali amictû vestiti; Filium in forma viri juvenis, aut agni vexilliferi; Spiritum Sanctum verò in formâ columbæ.
units.tr: The question is whether it is lawful to make images of God himself for such a use, and further, whether images so made may be kept and used in this way. We hold the negative against the Papists, whose opinion and practice are contrary, since they paint and fashion God and the Holy Trinity in various ways: above all God the Father in the form of an old man, with a triple crown and the rest of the papal vesture; the Son in the form of a young man, or of a lamb bearing a banner; and the Holy Spirit in the form of a dove.

units.la: Opponimus hæc Argumenta; 1. Ista imaginum & simulachrorum ipsius Dei ac personarum Divinarum formatio prorsùs adversatur naturæ Divinæ spirituali, simplicissimæ, & infinitæ; in quâ non est visibilitas, nec lineamenta, eorumve ductus ac terminatio, aut extensio ulla, nec ulli limites; adeò ut prorsùs fit ineffigiabilis. Consequenter per istiusmodi imagines non verè repræsentatur verus Deus; sed falsum & fallax Deitatis signum absurdè exhibetur. Hinc Jerem. x, 14, 15. Mendacium est conflatile ejus; -Vanitas sunt, &c. Hab. 2, 18. Conflatile, & quod docet mendacium
units.tr: We oppose these arguments. 1. The making of such images and likenesses of God and of the divine persons is utterly contrary to the spiritual, most simple and infinite divine nature, in which there is no visibility, no features or outline or their delineation and extent, nor any limits. So it is altogether incapable of being portrayed. Consequently through such images the true God is not truly represented, but a false and deceptive sign of deity is absurdly exhibited. Hence Jer. 10:14, 15: His molten image is a lie... they are vanity, etc. Hab. 2:18: A molten image, which teaches lies.

units.la: 2. Reprehenditur istiusmodi simulachrorum effigatio, tanquam absurda, & in Deum injuria: Jes. xl, 18. Cui igitur assimilabitis Deum? Et quam similitudinem disponetis ei? Et de ipsis Gentilibus; Rom. I, 22, 23, 25. Cum se dicerent sapientes, stulti facti sunt. Mutarunt enim gloriam incorruptibilis Dei in simulachrum imaginis corruptibilis hominis, & volucrum & quadrupedum &c.
units.tr: 2. The fashioning of such likenesses is rebuked as absurd and an injury to God: Isa. 40:18: To whom then will you liken God? And what likeness will you set up for him? And concerning the Gentiles themselves, Rom. 1:22, 23, 25: Claiming to be wise, they became fools. For they exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for an image of corruptible man, and of birds and four-footed beasts, etc.

units.la: 3. Prohibetur severissimè, ipsis verbis secundi praecepti, Exod. xx,4,5. Deut. v,8,9. Non facies tibi sculptile, neque ullam similitudinem eorum quae sunt in coelo sursum, &c. Itemque Deut.iv,15,16. Cavete ergò diligenter animabus vestris: Ne forte corrumpatis vias vestras, & faciatis vobis sculptile, aut imaginem ullius simulachri, &c.23. 24. Cavete vobis, ne forte oblivisci amini pacti Jehovæ Dei vestri, & faciatis vobis sculptile, aut imaginem cujuscunque rei; Nam Jehovah Deus tuus ignis consumens est, Deus zelotes.
units.tr: 3. It is most strictly forbidden, in the very words of the second commandment: Exod. 20:4, 5; Deut. 5:8, 9: You shall not make for yourself a graven image, or any likeness of what is in heaven above, etc. Likewise Deut. 4:15, 16: Take good heed therefore to your souls, lest you corrupt your ways and make for yourselves a graven image, or the image of any likeness, etc. Deut. 4:23, 24: Take heed to yourselves, lest you forget the covenant of Jehovah your God and make for yourselves a graven image or the image of anything; for Jehovah your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.

units.la: LVII. Obj. 1.
units.tr: LVII. Objection 1.

units.la: Homo à Deo conditus est ad ipsius imaginem: ergò rectè conficitur imago Dei ad similitudinem hominis. Resp. Nego consequentiam: nam 1. imago ista proprie constitit in dotibus ac perfectionibus spiritualibus; quae imagine corporeâ exprimi non possunt. 2. Retorqueo argumentum: cum enim tot homines exstant in mundo, ac tot hominum imagines, jam frustra impenduntur tanti labores & sumtus conficiendis peculiaribus imaginibus Dei.
units.tr: Man was created by God in his own image; therefore an image of God is rightly made in the likeness of a man. Answer: I deny the consequence. For (1) that image properly consists in spiritual gifts and perfections, which cannot be expressed by a bodily image. (2) I turn the argument back: since there are so many men in the world, and so many images of men, labour and expense are already being wasted in making special images of God.

units.la: Obj. 2. Deus aliquoties visibili aliquo signo se conspiciendum præbuit: ergo. Resp. Deus quidem interdum aliquo symbolo præsentiam suam extraordinariam, respectu extraordinariæ alicujus operationis ac revelationis, demonstravit: utpote in rubo ardente, specie columbæ, &c. non vero essentiam suam tali imagine repræsentavit, aut repræsentandam docuit: sed contrarium ipse docuit, Deut. iv,15,16 & alibi.
units.tr: Objection 2. God has on several occasions presented himself to be seen under some visible sign; therefore... Answer: God indeed at times showed his extraordinary presence by some symbol, with respect to some extraordinary operation or revelation: as in the burning bush, in the form of a dove, and so on. But he did not represent his essence by such an image, nor did he teach that it should be represented. Rather, he taught the contrary, Deut. 4:15,16, and elsewhere.

units.la: Obj.3. Virtutes & vitia, aliaque ejusmodi, quin & Angeli, imagine exhiberi possunt: ergo. Resp. Imo eorum operationes solum signo hieroglyphico utcunque repræsentantur; verum ipsæ essentiæ sic non exprimuntur. Quicquid autem in Deo est, per ipsius simplicitatem est ipse Deus: atque id, quo Deus est, & à creaturis distinctus, tale est, ut nullo simulachro possit exprimi.
units.tr: Objection 3. Virtues and vices, and other things of this kind, and even angels, can be exhibited by an image; therefore... Answer: Rather, their operations are represented only by some hieroglyphic sign, however it may be done; but the essences themselves are not expressed in this way. Whatever is in God is, through his simplicity, God himself; and that by which God is God and is distinct from creatures is such that it cannot be expressed by any likeness.

units.la: Obj.4. In meditationibus de Deo, & orationibus ad ipsum, Deum nobis repræsentamus imagine mentali: ergo. Resp. Non est necessum, imo nec licitum, Deum concipi ut corporeum, vel aliter finitum, atq; ita simulachrum aliquod Dei in mente nostrâ confici: is enim non foret verus conceptus veri Dei; sed conceptus alicujus creaturæ, loco veri Dei; atque adeò conceptus idololatricus. Neque tamen omnino nihil concipimus, qui foret conceptus atheisticus. Sed formamus de Deo conceptus plures inadæquatos, quemadmodum apprehensivè, non comprehensivè, ipsum cognoscimus. Sic ergo concipimus veram substantiam spiritualem, suâ perfectione omnes creaturas prorsus & infinitè transcendentem.
units.tr: Objection 4. In meditations on God and in prayers to him, we represent God to ourselves by a mental image; therefore... Answer. It is neither necessary nor even lawful to conceive God as corporeal or otherwise finite, and so to form some likeness of God in our minds. For that would not be a true concept of the true God, but the concept of some creature in place of the true God, and therefore an idolatrous concept. Yet we do not conceive nothing at all, which would be an atheistic concept. Rather, we form several inadequate concepts of God, just as we know him apprehensively, not comprehensively. Thus we conceive a true spiritual substance, which by its perfection utterly and infinitely transcends all creatures.

units.la: LVIII. Sed neque confectæ ejusmodi imagines sic usurpari debent, nec asservari in talem usum: ita enim 1. continuatur atque augetur peccatum in prima earum confectione inchoatum.
units.tr: LVIII. But images of this kind, once made, ought not to be used in this way, nor kept for such use. For thus (1) the sin begun in their first making is continued and increased.

units.la: 2. Istâ usurpatione peccatur formaliter adversus ἐμφατικώταλα hujus Præcepti verba; Non incurvabis te eis, neque coles ea; Exod. xx, 5.
units.tr: (2) By such use one sins formally against the most emphatic [ἐμφατικώτατα] words of this precept: "You shall not bow down to them, nor serve them," Exod. 20:5.

units.la: 3. In detestationem idololatriæ, Deus instrumenta ejus propria destrui mandavit aliquoties: inter alia Deut. vii, 25, 26.
units.tr: (3) In detestation of idolatry, God commanded its proper instruments to be destroyed several times, among them Deut. 7:25,26.

units.la: Atque ita 4. cum laude refertur de Rege Hizkijahu, 2 Reg. xviii, 4. Ipse sustulit excelsa, & contrivit statuas, & succidit lucum: confregitque serpentem æreum, quem fecerat Mose; quia usque ad dies illos filii Israëlis sufficebant ei: & vocavit eum Nehushtan.
units.tr: And so (4) King Hezekiah is praised for it, 2 Kings 18:4. He himself removed the high places, broke the statues, and cut down the grove; he also broke in pieces the bronze serpent which Moses had made, for until those days the children of Israel had offered incense to it; and he called it Nehushtan.

units.la: LIX. Ad Imagines creaturarum quod attinet non omnem earum formationem aut confectionem omnino illicitam vel prohibitam dicimus: nec absolutè vetitas artes εἰκαστικὰς; quibus rerum corporearum externa aspectabilis forma exprimitur & repræsentatur, vel operationes & effecta quædam aliarum etiam rerum symbolicè adumbrantur: Deus enim quosdam istis quoque artibus instruxisse dicitur, Exod. xxxi, 2,-6. xxxv, 30,-35. Atque in Tabernaculo, ac deinde etiam in Templo, ex praescripto ipsius Dei confectę fuerunt quaedam imagines Cherubinorum, palmarum, florum, &c. Sed illicitas & prohibitas dicimus imagines creaturarum, eo fine & modo, ut in iis, aut per eas, ipsum cultus religiosi objectum utcunque repraesentaretur, & sic ad eas cultus religiosus praestaretur. Hoc autem patet, 1. ex verbis praecepti; Non facies tibi sculptile, neque ullam similitudinem, &c. Non incurvabis te eis, neque coles ea; Exod. xx, 4, 5.
units.tr: LIX. As for images of created things, we do not say that every formation or making of them is wholly unlawful or forbidden, nor are the artistic arts (εἰκαστικάς) absolutely banned, by which the external visible form of bodily things is expressed and represented, or certain operations and effects of other things are symbolically shadowed forth. For God is said to have endowed some with these arts, Exod. 31:2–6; 35:30–35. And in the Tabernacle, and afterwards in the Temple, certain images of cherubim, palms, flowers, and so on were made according to God's own prescription. But we call illicit and forbidden those images of created things which are made with the aim and in the manner that the object of religious worship is in some way represented in them or through them, and so religious worship is rendered to them. This is evident (1) from the words of the precept: "You shall not make for yourself a graven image, nor any likeness," and so on. "You shall not bow down to them, nor serve them," Exod. 20:4,5.

units.la: 2. Simile est interdictum, Deut. iv, 16, 17, 18. Ne forte corrumpatis vias vestras, &c.
units.tr: (2) Similar is the prohibition in Deut. 4:16,17,18: "Lest perhaps you corrupt your ways," and so on.

units.la: Atque iterum 3. Levit. xxvi, 1. Non facietis vobis idola, & sculptile, & statuam non erigetis vobis; neque lapidem pictum ponetis in terra vestra, ut incurvetis vos ei: Ego enim Iehovah Deus vester.
units.tr: And again (3) Lev. 26:1: "You shall not make idols for yourselves, nor set up a graven image or statue for yourselves, nor shall you place a painted stone in your land to bow down before it; for I am the LORD your God."

units.la: Obj. Imagines Cherubinorum, aliaeque, fuerunt in Tabernaculo, & in Templo V. T. Ergo. Resp. Illae imagines ipsum objectum cultus religiosi nullo modo repraesentarunt; neque in iis & per eas Deo, aut sanctis quibusdam creaturis, cultus religiosus deferri debuit; imo nec secundum Dei praescriptum potuit. Sed pro ratione cultus istius oeconomici, pluriumque institutorum cerimonialium, per eas symbolice aliquid adumbratum fuit, ad Angelorum functiones, & ad majestatis ac gloriae Divinae indicium qualecunque, spectans: quod ipsum etiam in N. T. locum habere non debet, ubi cultum oportet esse magis spiritualem, sublatis omnibus istiusmodi typis ac symbolis.
units.tr: Objection: Images of cherubim and others were in the Tabernacle and in the Temple of the Old Testament; therefore... Answer: Those images in no way represented the object of religious worship, nor could religious worship be offered in them and through them to God or to certain holy creatures; indeed, according to God's prescription it could not be. But in keeping with the plan of that economic worship and of the many ceremonial institutions, something was symbolically shadowed forth by them, looking to the functions of angels and to whatever indication there was of divine majesty and glory. This ought not to have a place even in the New Testament, where worship should be more spiritual, with all such types and symbols removed.

units.la: IX. Prorsus igitur illicitus censeri debet talis imaginum usus, ut quis se coram iis prosterneret, eas amplexaretur, deosculade-retur, &c. quamvis eâ mente ut non in ipsis, sed in earum exemplari vel archetypo, universus cultus religiosus terminaretur. Obstant enim 1. posteriora illa verba secundi praecepti, Non incurvabis te eis, neque coles ea; Exod. xx, 5.
units.tr: IX. Therefore such a use of images must be judged wholly unlawful, that someone should prostrate himself before them, embrace them, kiss them, and so on, even though with the intention that the whole religious worship terminates not in them but in their exemplar or archetype. For (1) the latter words of the second precept oppose it: "You shall not bow down to them, nor serve them," Exod. 20:5.

units.la: 2. Quoniam earum confectio in ilum usum prohibita est; (ut modo probatum;) multo magis ipse talis earum usus censeri debet prohibitus.
units.tr: (2) Since their making for that use is forbidden (as has just been proved), such use itself must be judged much more forbidden.

units.la: 3. Deus omnem cultus religiosi communicationem ad aliud qualecunque objectum, præter se, districte prohibuit; utpote nolens gloriam suam alteri dari zelotes, & ignis consumens, Jef.xliii, 8. xlviii, 11. Exod. xx, 5, Deut. v, 9-iv,24.
units.tr: (3) God strictly forbade every communication of religious worship to any object whatever besides himself, being unwilling to give his glory to another, a jealous God and a consuming fire: Isa. 43:8; 48:11; Exod. 20:5; Deut. 5:9; 4:24.

units.la: 4. Magis etiam nunc sub N. T. talis usus adversatur cultui spirituali, qualem sub hac œconomia esse oportet.
units.tr: (4) Such use is even now, under the New Testament, more opposed to spiritual worship, such as ought to exist under this economy.

units.la: Exc. Ex hominum socordia oritur necessitas devotionis per ejusmodi adminicula excitandæ & promovendæ. Resp. Sed nos non decet arbitratu proprio adminicula istiusmodi fingere; nedum à Deo diserte prohibita: quin & ipse Deus objecta & adminicula satis multa ac varia nobis suppeditavit, quæ occasionem præbent majestatem ipsius meditandi & prædicandi, quæque nos ad ipsius cultum & honorem debent incitare: minus autem veniendum ad ea, quæ ulterioris etiam idololatriæ proclivem occasionem præbere possunt & solent.
units.tr: Objection: From men's sloth arises the need to arouse and promote devotion by such aids. Answer: But it does not befit us to invent such aids at our own discretion, much less when they are expressly forbidden by God. Indeed, God himself has supplied us with many and varied objects and aids which give occasion for meditating on and proclaiming his majesty, and which ought to stir us to his worship and honour. We should go less to those things which can and do readily offer occasion for further idolatry.

units.la: Multo etiam magis censeri debet illicita confectio & usus imaginum in ordine ad falsa numina, aut quaeliacunque objecta cultus religiosi præter unum verum Deum; quatenus videlicet istæ imagines adminicula forent, aut symbola, talis cultus idololatrici: quoniam enim omnis ejusmodi cultus illicitus est; adminicula ad ipsum proprie ordinata non possunt esse licita. Et quemadmodum ipse ille cultus primo Decalogi præcepto adversatur; sic talis imaginum confectio & usus ad illum cultum; secundo præcepto repugnat. Hoc autem ad imagines humanæ naturæ Christi; & Sanctorum, in Papatu quoque applicatum volumus.
units.tr: Much more must the making and use of images be judged unlawful in relation to false gods, or any objects of religious worship besides the one true God, insofar as those images would be aids or symbols of such idolatrous worship. For since all such worship is unlawful, aids properly ordained to it cannot be lawful. Just as that worship itself opposes the first precept of the Decalogue, so such making and use of images for that worship conflicts with the second precept. We wish this also to be applied to images of the human nature of Christ and of the saints, as it is applied in Popery too.

units.la: LXI. Sed neque imagines Christi; & Sanctorum; in templis aut oratoriis Christianorum habere debent pro libris Laicorum, quos vocant Pontificii: Deus enim 1. non ista media ad eorum instructionem ordinavit, sed Verbi sui lectionem & praedicationem, cum annexâ Sacramentorum administratione: Isef. VIII, 19,20. Luc. XVI, 29. 2 Petr. 1,19. Matth. XXVIII, 19, 20. 1 Cor. XI, 24,25,26. Rom. X, 8, 17. 1 Cor. 2, 1, 2. 2, V, 19. Gal. III, 1, 2.
units.tr: LXI. Nor should images of Christ and of the saints in the temples or oratories of Christians be held to be books for the laity, as the Papists call them. For God (1) did not ordain these means for their instruction, but the reading and preaching of his Word, with the administration of the sacraments joined to it: Isa. 8:19,20; Luke 16:29; 2 Pet. 1:19; Matt. 28:19,20; 1 Cor. 11:24–26; Rom. 10:8,17; 1 Cor. 2:1,2; 2 Cor. 5:19; Gal. 3:1,2.

units.la: 2: Nec idonea sunt, ignorantes docere veritatem Divinam ac salutarem: Psal. CXV, 4,5. Simulacra eorum sunt argentum & aurum, opus manuum hominum. Os est eis; & non loquuntur. Solo autem aspectû quis discernet Christum pictum, vel fictum, à Cajapha, aut Pilato: Petrum, à Judâ? &c.
units.tr: (2) Nor are they fit to teach the divine and saving truth, since they are ignorant: Ps. 115:4,5. "Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands. They have a mouth, but they do not speak." Moreover, by sight alone who could tell Christ painted or feigned from Caiaphas or Pilate, or Peter from Judas? And so on.

units.la: 3. Pontificiorum imagines, mendacia, vanitatem & superstitiones docere aut confirmare magis apta sunt. Jerem. X, 8, 14. Hab. 2, 18. Zach. X, 2. Facile ista apparent in Maria instar reginae vestibus pretiosissimis ac diademate amicta & exornata, in Petro externis clavibus instructo, in Paulo gladium gerente, &c. Ac potissimum in Divis chimaericis.
units.tr: 3. The images of the Papists are better suited to teaching or confirming lies, vanity and superstitions. Jerem. 10.8, 14; Hab. 2.18; Zach. 10.2. These things are plain in Mary, decked and adorned like a queen in the most precious garments and a diadem; in Peter, furnished with external keys; in Paul, carrying a sword; and so on. Above all, they are plain in the chimerical saints.

units.la: 4. Gravissimum est periculum, ne homines ab usû historico ulterius procedant, ac tandem ad idololatriam prolabantur; ut in Papatu factum.
units.tr: 4. There is a very grave danger that men will go further from the historical use of images and at last slip into idolatry, as has happened in the Papacy.

units.la: Propterea ne quidem approbamus usum historicum, & ornatum templorum per imagines, quem Lutherani praetendunt, & cujus gratiâ imagines conservari volunt: cum ornatus etiam talis simplicitati & spiritualitati oeconomiae N.T non conveniat; atque adeo Christiani in Ecclesia primitivâ eum nec habuerint, nec quaesiverint.
units.tr: For this reason we do not approve even the historical use of images, nor the adornment of churches with them, which the Lutherans put forward and for whose sake they wish images to be kept. Such ornamentation does not agree with the simplicity and spirituality of the economy of the New Testament, and so the Christians of the primitive Church neither had it nor sought it.

units.la: LXII. Succedit ἐθελοθρησκεία in ordine ad Deum; cultus scil. voluntarius, quem homo arbitratû proprio constituit, vel assumit & praestat, absque ipsius Dei mandato aut placito. De illa satis diserte, 1. Col. 2, 21. 23. Quae omnia sunt comparata ipso usu ad corruptionem, praescripta exprecceptis & doctrinis hominum: Quae rationem nem quidem habent sapientiæ in cultu voluntario, & submissione animi, & in eo quod corpori non parcant, nec tamen ullius sunt pretii, cum ad ea spectent quibus farcitur caro. Deut.22, 8. Non facietis juxta omnia quæ nos facimus hic hodie singuli quicquid rectum est in oculis suis. Confer 1Sam. 13,13.& 15,15,22. Sic Matth.15,9. ex Jef.29,13. Frustra Me colunt, docentes doctrinas quæ sunt præcepta hominum.
units.tr: LXII. There follows ἐθελοθρησκεία [ethelothrēskeia] in relation to God, that is, voluntary worship, which a man institutes, adopts and performs at his own discretion, without God's own command or approval. Concerning this, quite plainly, Col. 2.21, 23: All these things are destined to be consumed by use, prescribed by the precepts and doctrines of men, which indeed have no reason of wisdom in voluntary worship and submission of mind, and in not sparing the body, yet are of no value, since they pertain to the satisfying of the flesh. Deut. 12.8: You shall not do according to all the things that we do here today, each one whatever is right in his own eyes. Compare 1 Sam. 13.13 and 15.15, 22. So Matt. 15.9, from Isa. 29.13: In vain they worship me, teaching as doctrines the precepts of men.

units.la: 2. Contra vero, postulat Deus, ut sua præcepta quam accuratissimè observentur, omissis moribus, & patrum institutis, & qualicunque hominum arbitrio proprio. Ezech.xx, 18,19. In præceptis patrum vestrorum ne incedatis, & judicia eorum ne custodiatis. - Ego Jehovah Deus vester: in præceptis Meis ambulate, & judicia Mea custodite, & facite ea. Lev.18,3,4.Deut.12,32. Prov.30.6.
units.tr: 2. On the contrary, God requires that his own precepts be observed as exactly as possible, setting aside customs, the institutions of the fathers, and any arbitrary judgment of men. Ezek. 20.18, 19: Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers, nor keep their judgments. I am Jehovah your God: walk in my statutes, and keep my judgments, and do them. Lev. 18.3, 4; Deut. 12.32; Prov. 30.6.

units.la: 3. Ipsius Dei ὑπῳχὴ, nostræque ab eo dependentiæ, ac debitæ subjectioni, consentaneum omnino est, ut ipse præscribat, quem & qualem sibi cultum à nobis præstari velit.
units.tr: 3. Since God is sovereign and we depend on him and owe him subjection, it is altogether fitting that he himself prescribe what worship, and of what kind, he wishes to be rendered by us.

units.la: 4. Mens hominis, ubi deserit normam à Deo præscriptam, vel eâ destituitur, malè judicat de officio suo, & non potest non exorbitare. Prov.14, 12,xvi,25. Est via recta coram viro, & novissimum ejus Viæ mortis. Joh.16.2. Imo veniet tempus, cum quisquis trucidabit vos, putabit se cultum præstare Deo.
units.tr: 4. The mind of man, when it forsakes the norm prescribed by God, or is destitute of it, judges wrongly about its duty and cannot but go astray. Prov. 14.12; 16.25: There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death. John 16.2: Indeed the time will come when whoever kills you will think he is offering service to God.

units.la: Hoc igitur nomine rejicienda sunt plurima, quæ apud Pontificios, aliosque superstitiosos, magnam sanctitatis & devotionis laudem habere solent, & traditionum, vel institutorum Ecclesiasticorum, nomine commendari. Cujusmodi sunt vita monastica, horæ canonicæ, litaniæ, peregrinationes & processiones religiosæ, flagellationes spontaneæ, nudipedalia, discrimina ciborum, templorum dedicationes & sumtuosa ornamenta, &c. quibus omnibus recte applicantur, ista Ief.1,12. Quis quæsivit hoc de manu vestra? Ierem.xix,5. Quod non præcepi, nec locutus sum, nec ascendit super cor Meum.
units.tr: On this ground many things are to be rejected which among the Papists and other superstitious people usually have a great reputation for holiness and devotion, and are commended under the name of traditions or ecclesiastical institutions. Of this kind are monastic life, the canonical hours, litanies, religious pilgrimages and processions, voluntary flagellations, going barefoot, distinctions of foods, dedications of churches, sumptuous ornaments, etc. To all of these those words apply rightly: Isa. 1.12, "Who has required this at your hand?" Jer. 19.5, "Which I did not command, nor speak, nor did it come into my heart."

units.la: LXIII. Cum Socinianis hic etiam non est putan-dum, dum, quod Christus secundum præceptum auxerit addito mandato de cavendis idolis, eorumque locis, ut & idolothytis. Nam 1. de idolis fugiendis satis aperta & emphatica est prohibitio. Exod xxi 1,13. In omnibus, quæ dixi vobis, cauti eritis. Neque nomen Deorum aliorum memorabitis: non audietur in ore tuo. Imò & ratio huic secundo præcepto adjecta; Ego enim Iehovah Deus tuus, zelotes, &c. Atque item exemplum, Psal. xvi, 4. Nec non promissio. Hos. 2,17.
units.tr: LXIII. Nor are we to agree here with the Socinians, who hold that Christ, in addition to the precept, added a command about avoiding idols and their places, and also idol-offerings. For first, the prohibition of fleeing from idols is quite plain and emphatic. Exod. 23.13: In all things which I have said to you, you shall be cautious. Neither shall you make mention of the names of other gods; let it not be heard in your mouth. Indeed the reason is added to this second precept: For I, Jehovah your God, am a jealous God, and so on. Likewise there is the example, Psalm 16.4, and also the promise, Hos. 2.17.

units.la: Similiter etiàm 2. de instrumentis & locis cultui idolorum appropriatis; ut ea confringantur, vel etiam diruantur, ad tollendam occasionem seductionis, & in detestationem idololatriæ: Deut. vii, 25,26. xii,2,3. Confer factum Patriarchę Jacobi & familiarium ejus, Gen. xxxv,2,4. Atque item exemplum Regis Hiskijahu, 2 Reg. xviii, 4.
units.tr: Likewise, secondly, concerning the instruments and places appropriated to the worship of idols, that they are to be broken or even destroyed, to remove the occasion of seduction and in detestation of idolatry: Deut. 7.25, 26; 12.2, 3. Compare the deed of the patriarch Jacob and his household, Gen. 35.2, 4. Likewise the example of King Hezekiah, 2 Kings 18.4.

units.la: Quantum vero attinet 3. ad Idolothyta, quatenus subesset conscientia idoli, aut participatio aliqua idololatriæ, sic ea etiam sub V.T. fuisse prohibita & illicita, satis patet ex historia, Num. xxv, 1,2,3. Cœpit populus fornicari cum filiabus Moab. Et vocaverunt populum ad sacrificia Deorum suorum: comeditque populus. Unde etiam Apostolus argumentum petit, 1 Cor. x,7,8. Nec igitur idololatræ fratres, sicut quidam eorum, &c. Adde exemplum Davidis, Psal. xvi, 4.
units.tr: As far as concerns, thirdly, idol-offerings, insofar as a consciousness of the idol or some participation in idolatry was involved, that these also were forbidden and unlawful under the Old Testament too is clear enough from history: Num. 25.1, 2, 3: The people began to commit fornication with the daughters of Moab. And they invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate. Hence the Apostle also draws his argument, 1 Cor. 10.7, 8: Neither be idolaters, as some of them were, and so on. Add the example of David, Psalm 16.4.

units.la: Obj. In N.T. dicitur, 1 Joh. v, 21. Filioli, cavete ab idolis. itemque 1 Cor. x, 14. Dilecti mei, fugite ab idolatria. Et idolothyta, quamvis in se non illicita manducari, prohibentur tamen 1 Cor. viii, & x. Resp. Scil. quando & quatenus in iis foret participatio aliqua idololatriæ, aut saltem seductionis ad eam. Verum ista non sunt nova præcepta; sed antiqua, sub N.T. repetita, & ad præsentes occasiones applicata.
units.tr: Objection: In the New Testament it is said, 1 John 5.21: Little children, beware of idols; and likewise 1 Cor. 10.14: My beloved, flee from idolatry. And idol-offerings, although lawful to eat in themselves, are nevertheless forbidden, 1 Cor. 8 and 10. Answer: namely, when and insofar as there would be in them some participation in idolatry, or at least some seduction toward it. But these are not new precepts; they are ancient ones, repeated under the New Testament and applied to present occasions.

units.la: Inst. Novo Test. proprium est, quod dicitur 1 Cor. 8,10,11. Etenim si quis viderit te, illâ cognitione prædictum, in idolio accumbere, nonne conscientia ipsius quiinfirmus est, instruetur ad edendum ea quæ sunt idolis mactata ? Et tuâ ijstâ cognitione frater ille infirmus, propterquem Christus est mortuus, peribit ? Resp. Ista ratio à dilectione proximo debitâ, atque itâ ex posteriore Legis tabulâ, defuncta est, sed novum additamentum adsecundum Decalogi præceptum nullo modo constituit; aut probat: ut neque mortis Christi mentio in præterito tempore.
units.tr: Instance: What is peculiar to the New Testament is what is said in 1 Cor. 8.10, 11: For if someone sees you, who have this knowledge, reclining at table in an idol's temple, will not the conscience of him who is weak be emboldened to eat things sacrificed to idols? And through your knowledge that weak brother, for whom Christ died, will perish? Answer: That reasoning is derived from the love owed to a neighbour, and so from the second table of the Law. But it in no way establishes a new addition to the second precept of the Decalogue, nor does it prove one; nor does the mention of Christ's death in the past tense.

units.la: LXIV. Sed & contra Pantificios tenendum, Secundum illud præceptum à primo verè distinctum esse: cum in primo prohibeantur falsa obječta terminantiacultus religiosi; & vel objecti agnitio & cultus conveniens præcipiatur: in secundo vero prohibeanturmodi, ac media, absurdè ab hominibus excogitata, confecta, & adhibita ad cultum Dei; simulque præcipiatur modus Deum colendi ab ipso institutus. Consequenter, secundum istud præceptum nullo modo omittendum est, tanquam supervacaneum: quod frequenter faciunt Adversarii, ad occultandam enormem illam idololatriæ suæ speciem: neque pro appendicè solùm, aut declaratione primi præcepti,habendum.
units.tr: LXIV. But against the Papists it must also be maintained that the second precept is truly distinct from the first. In the first, false objects of religious worship are forbidden, and the recognition of the proper object and fitting worship are commanded. In the second, the modes and means absurdly devised, made and employed by men in the worship of God are forbidden, and at the same time the mode of worshipping God instituted by himself is commanded. Consequently this second precept must in no way be omitted as superfluous, as the adversaries often do to conceal that enormous form of their idolatry; nor is it to be regarded merely as an appendix or explanation of the first precept.

units.la: XLV. Sociniani tertio præcepto duo per Christumpro N. T. adjecta statuunt; 1. ne leviter vel temerèjuremus. 2. quod etiam per nomen ipsius Christi jurareliceat. Sed quantum attinet ad prius; 1. Adversariiprorsus non possunt probare, sub V. T. juramentatemeraria, quàvis de causâ, & in vitâ quotidianâ, fuisse licita: neque enim id colligi potest ex reprehensione & correctione Christi, Matth. v, 33,-37. quæ solum adversus praxin & perversa glossemataPharisæorum & Scribarum institutæ sunt.
units.tr: XLV. The Socinians hold that two things were added by Christ for the New Testament to the third precept: (1) that we should not swear lightly or rashly; (2) that we should also abstain from swearing by the name of Christ himself. But as far as the former is concerned: first, the adversaries can by no means prove that rash swearing, for whatever cause and in daily life, was lawful under the Old Testament. For this cannot be gathered from the reproof and correction of Christ, Matt. 5.33-37, which were directed only against the practice and perverse glosses of the Pharisees and Scribes.

units.la: 2. Diserte in tertio præcepto prohibetur omnis usurpatio nominis Divini vana aut temeraria: at certe juramentum temerarium, est temeraria nominis Diviniųsurpatio.
units.tr: Second, the third precept expressly forbids every vain or rash use of the divine name; but a rash oath is certainly a rash use of the divine name.

units.la: 3. Scopus præcepti procul dubio est, prohibereomnem omnem profanationem nominis Divini; sed ea manifeste inest in juramento temerario.
units.tr: Third, the aim of the precept is undoubtedly to forbid every profanation of the divine name; but this is manifestly present in a rash oath.

units.la: 4. Rationes, cur Socciniani existimant juramenta temeraria nunc sub N.T. esse prohibita & illicita, tales sunt, ut non debeant Novo Test. peculiares censeri; sed & Veteri communes: nimirum ut nomen Dei in summâ semper veneratione sit, & ne per malam ac levem jurandi consuetudinem homines ad periuria prolabantur.
units.tr: Fourth, the reasons why the Socinians think that rash oaths are now forbidden and unlawful under the New Testament are such that they ought not to be counted peculiar to the New Testament but common to the Old as well: namely, that the name of God should always be held in highest reverence, and that men should not fall into perjury through a bad and careless habit of swearing.

units.la: LXVI. Assinis est error Anabaptistarum, qui omnem juramenti usum sub N. T. illicitum & prohibitum putant, cum sub V. T. fuerit permissus & licitus. Nos autem hæc Argumenta opponimus; 1. Juramentum, ubi recte usurpatur, in causa verâ, & satis gravi, cum sincerâ & humili reverentia Dei, ad ipsius gloriam, ac proximorum nostrorum bonum, moralis cultus pars est: atque ita ab ipso Deo præscribitur, Deut. vi, 13. Jehovam Deum tuum timebis, & ipsum colės: ac per nomen ejus jurabis. Similiter x, 20. Confer Matth. iv, 10. Iterum Jer. iv. 2. Et jurabis, vivit Jehovah, in veritate, in judicio, & in justitiâ: & benedicent sese in eo Gentes, & in eo gloriabuntur. Ista ratione ipsi Gentiles ad reverentiam & cultum veri Dei debuerunt adduci; cujus rei complementum pertinet ad N. T. Specialis casus expressus est Exod. xxii, 10, 11. Adde exempla Abrahami, Gen. xxi, 23, 24, 31. Isaaci: xxvi, 31. Jacobi, xxxi, 53. Davidis, 1 Sam. xx, 17, 42. Primariorum Sacerdotum, Levitarum, universi Israëlis, præeunte Ezrâ; Ezr. x, 5.
units.tr: LXVI. The error of the Anabaptists is baseless, for they think every use of an oath is unlawful and forbidden under the New Testament, although it was permitted and lawful under the Old. We, however, set against them these arguments. 1. An oath, when rightly used, in a true and sufficiently serious cause, with sincere and humble reverence for God, for his glory and for the good of our neighbours, is part of moral worship. God himself prescribes it: Deut. vi, 13. Thou shalt fear Jehovah thy God, and serve him, and shalt swear by his name. Similarly x, 20. Compare Matt. iv, 10. Again Jer. iv, 2. And thou shalt swear, As Jehovah lives, in truth, in judgment, and in righteousness: and the nations shall bless themselves in him, and in him shall they glory. In this way the Gentiles themselves were to be brought to the reverence and worship of the true God, and the fulfilment of this belongs to the New Testament. A specific case is expressly stated in Exod. xxii, 10, 11. Add the examples of Abraham, Gen. xxi, 23, 24, 31; of Isaac, xxvi, 31; of Jacob, xxxi, 53; of David, 1 Sam. xx, 17, 42; of the chief priests, the Levites and all Israel, led by Ezra, Ezra x, 5.

units.la: 2. In V. T. extant illustres prophetiæ de juramentis sub N. T. faciendis, & ad religionem ejus spectaturis; Ief. xlv, 23. Per Me juravi, egressum est de ore Meo in justitia verbum, & non revertetur; quod Mihi curvabitur omne genu, per Me jurabit omnis lingua. Item cap. xix, 18. lxv, 16.
units.tr: 2. Under the Old Testament there are illustrious prophecies about oaths to be taken under the New Testament, which will concern its religion: Isa. xlv, 23. By myself have I sworn; the word has gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return: that to me every knee shall bow, by me every tongue shall swear. Likewise chap. xix, 18; lxv, 16.

units.la: 3. Usus legitimi juramenti docetur etiam in N.T. Hebr. Hebr. vi, 16, 17. Homines quidem per eum jurant qui sit major; atque iisdem omnis controversiæ finis est jusjurandum ad confirmationem adhibitum. Quâ in re Deus volens ex abundanti hæredibus promissionis ostendere immutabilitatem consilii sui, fidejussit jurejurando.
units.tr: 3. The lawful use of an oath is also taught in the New Testament: Heb. vi, 16, 17. Men indeed swear by one greater than themselves, and for them an oath for confirmation is the end of every dispute. In this matter God, wishing more abundantly to show to the heirs of the promise the immutability of his purpose, confirmed it with an oath.

units.la: Accedunt 4. irrefragabilia quædam exempla N. T. 2 Cor. 1, 23. Ego vero testem Deum invoco in meam animam. Similiter fere Rom. 1, 9. IX, 1. 2 Cor. XI, 31. Gal. 1, 20. Phil. 1 8. 1 Thess. II, 5. Adde exemplum Angeli, qui Apoc. X, 5, 6. sustulit manum suam ad cœlum: Et juravit per Eum qui vivit in sæcula sæculorum, qui creavit cœlum & ea quæ sunt in eo, &c. Ex quibus omnibus luce meridianâ clarius est, usum aliquem juramenti licitum & utilem, imo etiam pro ratione circumstantiarum necessarium, esse in N. T.
units.tr: To these come 4. certain unanswerable examples from the New Testament: 2 Cor. 1, 23. But I call God as witness upon my soul. Similarly, nearly every passage: Rom. 1, 9; IX, 1; 2 Cor. XI, 31; Gal. 1, 20; Phil. 1, 8; 1 Thess. II, 5. Add the example of the angel who, in Rev. X, 5, 6, lifted up his hand to heaven. And swore by him who lives for ever and ever, who created heaven and the things that are in it, etc. From all these things it is clearer than the noonday light that some lawful and useful use of an oath, indeed even one necessary according to the circumstances, exists under the New Testament.

units.la: Obj. Matth. v, 34,-37. & Jac. v, 12. Resp. illa accipi debent de juramentis temerariis; & speciatim istiusmodi, qualia Pharisæi & Scribæ sine scrupulo adhiberi posse existimabant; utpote per cœlum, per terram, per Hierosolymam, per caput suum, & id genus alia. Hunc eorum errorem Christus quoque detegit, & refutat Matth. xxiii, 16,-22. Tales propterea formulæ recensentur; at non Per Deum, Vivit Iehovah, aut similes. Atque ita verbum jurandi de juramento temerè, vel aliter, malè adhibito, usurpatur Eccl. ix, 2, Eventus unus est justo & impio:-sicut bonus, sic qui peccat: & is qui jurat, est sicut is qui juramentum timet. In communi & familiari conversatione igitur à juramentis abstinendum; nec facilè ultra simplicem affirmationem vel negationem progrediendum: Verum ubi rei gravitas, hominum negligentia, vel alia necessitas, quid amplius postulat, ulterius etiam licitè procedi, docet exemplum ipsius Christi, qui toties usurpavit, vel etiam ingeminavit, particulam Amen: & à Pontifice adjuratus per Deum viventem, respondere non dubitavit, Matth. xxvi, 63, 64. & alia plurima à nobis allegata.
units.tr: Obj. Matt. v, 34–37, and Jas. v, 12. Reply: those passages must be understood of rash oaths, and specifically of such oaths as the Pharisees and scribes thought could be used without scruple, namely by heaven, by earth, by Jerusalem, by one's own head, and others of that kind. Christ too uncovers and refutes this error of theirs, Matt. xxiii, 16–22. Such formulas are therefore listed; but not By God, As Jehovah lives, or similar ones. And so the word to swear is used of rash oaths, or of oaths otherwise wrongly made, in Eccl. ix, 2: One event comes to the righteous and the wicked: ...as the good, so the sinner; and he who swears is as he who fears an oath. In common and familiar conversation, therefore, one must abstain from oaths, and not readily go beyond a plain affirmation or negation. But where the gravity of the matter, the carelessness of men, or some other necessity asks for more, the example of Christ himself teaches that one may proceed further lawfully. He so often used, or even repeated, the particle Amen; and when the High Priest adjured him by the living God, he did not hesitate to answer, Matt. xxvi, 63, 64, and in many other passages we have cited.

units.la: LXVII. Ad alterum hujus præcepti augmentum quod attinet, non minus etiam hic errant Socinistæ: nam 1. Christus, aut Filius Dei, sub V. T. quoque agnoscendus fuit pro vero Deo; atque adeo per ipsum tunc pariter jurare licuit: imo, cum per Jehovam juratum est, hic minime fuit exclusus.
units.tr: LXVII. As for the second addition to this precept, the Socinians are no less mistaken here. For 1. Christ, or the Son of God, was to be acknowledged as the true God even under the Old Testament; and so it was then equally lawful to swear by him. Indeed, since swearing was done by Jehovah, he was in no way excluded here.

units.la: 2. Adoratio Christi non est Novo Test. propria, nec à Veteri excludenda; sed ejus species est juramentum.
units.tr: 2. The worship of Christ is not peculiar to the New Testament, nor is it to be excluded from the Old; and swearing is a kind of it.

units.la: 3. Speciatim Ječ. xlv, 23. Per me juravi, &c. quod Israëlitæ in isto negotio fecerunt sub V.T. idem Gentiles, per N. T. quoque vocandi, facturi erant similiter. Sed ad Christum, aut Filium Dei, applicandum esse istum locum, patet per ejus collationem cum Phil. II, 10, 11. Ut ad nomen Jesu omne genu se flestat. Per ipsum igitur sub V. T. etiam licitum fuit jurare.
units.tr: 3. Especially Isa. xlv, 23, By myself have I sworn, etc., which the Israelites did in that matter under the Old Testament, and the same Gentiles, who were also to be called under the New Testament, were likewise going to do. But that this place must be applied to Christ, or the Son of God, is evident from its comparison with Phil. II, 10, 11, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow. Therefore it was also lawful under the Old Testament to swear by him.

units.la: 4. Addimus ad hominem; quoniam frequenter verba formaliter expressa à nobis postulant Adversarii; minus recte, convenienter suæ propriæ methodo, dicere possunt, tertium præceptum hoc à Christo esse auctum, quod sub N.
