And whoever speaks against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, neither in this age nor in the age to come." Compare Mark 3:29: He has no forgiveness forever, but is liable to eternal judgement.

units.la: Item Hebr. 6. 4, 5, 6. „Fieri non potest, ut qui semel „fuerint illuminati, gustaverintque bonum Dei Ver„bum, ac virtutes futuri sæculi; Si prolabantur, denuò „renoventur ad refipiscentiam; ut qui rursum cruci„figant sibi Filium Dei, & ignominiæ exponant. x, „26, -29. „Si ultro peccaverimus post acceptam cogni„tionem veritatis, non adhuc pro peccatis reliqua est „hostia: Sed horrenda quædam expectatio judicii, „&c. Quanto (putatis) acerbiore supplicio dignus „censebitur, qui Filium Dei conculaverit, & sangui„nem Fœderis, per quem fuerat sanctificatus. prosanum duxerit, & Spiritum gratiæ contumeliâ affecerit? „Ac tandem 1 Joh. 5. 16. „Si quis viderit fratrem suum „peccare peccato, quod non est ad mortem, petet, „& dabit ei vitam: peccantibus dico non ad mortem. „Est peccatum ad mortem: non pro illo dico ut roget.
units.tr: Likewise Heb. 6:4, 5, 6: "It is impossible that those who have once been enlightened, and have tasted the good Word of God and the powers of the age to come, if they fall away, should be renewed again to repentance, since they crucify again the Son of God for themselves and expose him to disgrace." Heb. 10:26-29: "If we sin willingly after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins, but a certain dreadful expectation of judgement, etc. How much (do you think) will he be judged worthy of heavier punishment, who has trampled the Son of God, and has regarded the blood of the covenant, by which he was sanctified, as unholy, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?" And finally 1 John 5:16: "If anyone sees his brother sinning a sin that is not unto death, he shall ask, and God will give him life: I say to those who sin not unto death. There is a sin unto death; I do not say that one should pray for that."

units.la: XLV. Peccatum illud in Spiritum Sanctum, ut patet ex allegatis, præsupponit non solum qualemcunque auditionem & admissionem veritatis Euangelicæ; sed internam illuminationem & persuasionem per Spiritum Sanctum, quod ista doctrina sit veré salutaris. Formaliter autem consistit non in veritatis istius sic agnitæ qualicunque desertione, vel abnegatione; sed malitiosa ejus rejectione, odio, & blasphemia. Consequenter etiam infert finalem impœnitentiam, & impossibilem renovationem eorum, qui sic peccaverint; atque adeo certam eorum condemnationem; scil. juxta istiusmodi decretum, talem Dei ac Christi in opere redemtionis intentionem, & talem voluntatis Divinæ revelationem.
units.tr: XLV. That sin against the Holy Spirit, as is clear from the passages cited, presupposes not merely some kind of hearing and admission of the Evangelical truth, but an inward illumination and persuasion by the Holy Spirit that this doctrine is truly saving. Formally, however, it consists not in any kind of desertion or denial of this truth so recognised, but in its malicious rejection, hatred and blasphemy. Consequently it also brings final impenitence and the impossible renewal of those who have so sinned, and thus their certain condemnation; namely, according to such a decree, such an intention of God and Christ in the work of redemption, and such a revelation of the Divine will.

units.la: Citra extraordinariam revelationem, ac tale donum discretionis, difficillimum est judicium, quod hic vel ille commisisset istud peccatum; quia absolute non scimus interiora animi ejus.
units.tr: Apart from an extraordinary revelation and such a gift of discernment, a judgement that this or that person had committed that sin is most difficult, because we do not absolutely know the inward thoughts of his mind.

units.la: Pontificii plures illius peccati species statuunt perperam; utpote desperationem de gratia Dei, jactationem gratiæ sine bonis operibus, invidiam de donis gratiæ in alios collatis, pertinaciam, &c. atque adeo peccatum illud etiam remitti posse; sed ægrè admodum: contra doctrinam ex SS. Literis modo propositam.
units.tr: The Papists wrongly set up several species of that sin, such as despair of the grace of God, boasting of grace without good works, envy of the gifts of grace bestowed on others, obstinacy, etc.; and thus they hold that even that sin can be forgiven, but with great difficulty: this is contrary to the doctrine just set out from the Holy Scriptures.

units.la: XLVI. Ratione adjunctorum, dicuntur peccata manifesta; quæ sic committuntur, ut multi sint eorum conscii. Jef. 3. 9. Peccatum suum sicut Sodom enunciant; non celant. Gal. 5, 19. Manifesta sunt opera carnis: quæ sunt adulterium, fcortatio, &c.
units.tr: XLVI. By reason of circumstances, sins are called manifest, which are committed in such a way that many are aware of them. Jer. 3:9 (?): They declare their sin like Sodom; they do not conceal it. Gal. 5:19: The works of the flesh are manifest, which are adultery, fornication, etc.

units.la: Alia vero sunt occulta; quæ clam patrantur, ut præter peccantem nulli, aut saltem paucissimi eorum sint conscii: imo etiam frequenter ipse peccator ea ignorat, per inadvertentiam, vel per oblivionem.
units.tr: Others, however, are hidden, which are carried out secretly, so that no one except the sinner, or at least very few, are aware of them; indeed, often the sinner himself is ignorant of them, through inadvertence or forgetfulness.

units.la: 2 Sam 12. 12. Tu fecisti clam. Eph. 5. 12. Quæ occulte fiunt ab iis, turpe est vel dicere. Psal. 19. 13. Errores quis intelligat? ab occultis absolve me!
units.tr: 2 Sam. 12:12: You did it secretly. Eph. 5:12: It is shameful even to speak of those things that are done in secret by them. Ps. 19:12: Who can understand his errors? Cleanse me from hidden faults!

units.la: XLVII. Ratione graduum peccata alia aliis graviora sunt. Ezech. 5. 6. „Mutavit jura Mea in improbitatem plus, quam Gentes ipsæ; & statuta Mea plus, quam regiones quæ circumstant eam. viij. 15. Adhuc visurus es abominationes majores istis. Job. 19. 11. „Qui Me tradidit tibi, majus peccatum habet.
units.tr: XLVII. By reason of degrees, some sins are graver than others. Ezek. 5:6: "She has changed my judgements into wickedness more than the nations themselves, and my statutes more than the regions that surround her." Ezek. 8:15: You will see still greater abominations than these. John 19:11: He who delivered me to you has the greater sin.

units.la: Oritur autem ista differentia 1. ab objecto: nam cæteris paribus, gravius est peccatum, quod directe committitur adversus Deum, quam quod contra homines; lædere Principem, quam plebejum; parentem, quam peregrinum, vel ignotum, &c. Vide Exod. 22. 28. Mal. 1, 6. Levit. 18. 7. &c.
units.tr: This difference arises (1) from the object: for other things being equal, a sin committed directly against God is graver than one against men; to injure a prince is worse than to injure a commoner; a parent more than a stranger or an unknown person, etc. See Exod. 22:28; Mal. 1:6; Lev. 18:7, etc.

units.la: 2. A conditione peccantis, & gratiâ ei præstitâ: Hos. 4. 14. Si scortaris tu Israël, ne reatum obeat Jehudah. Luc. 12. 47. 48. Ille servus, qui novit voluntatem Domini sui, &c. Joh. 15. 22. Hebr. 10. 26.
units.tr: 2. From the condition of the sinner and the grace given to him: Hos. 4. 14. If you play the harlot, O Israel, let not Judah incur guilt. Luke 12. 47, 48. That servant who knew the will of his lord, etc. John 15. 22. Heb. 10. 26.

units.la: 3. A genere & natura rei: Matth. 5. 22. Quicunque irascitur fratri suo temere, -- : quicunque vero dixerit fratri suo, Raca, &c.
units.tr: 3. From the kind and nature of the thing: Matt. 5. 22. Whoever is angry with his brother without cause; but whoever says to his brother, Raca, etc.
4. From

units.la: 4. A principio, & modo agendi; ex ignorantia, infirmitate, vel etiam malitia. Vide sup. th. 41.
units.tr: 4. From the beginning and the manner of acting: whether from ignorance, weakness, or even malice. See above, th. 41.

units.la: 5. Ab intensione vel remissione actus: Prov. 1, 16. Pedibus suis ad malum concurrunt; & festinant ad effundendum sanguinem. Phil. 3. 6.
units.tr: 5. From the intensity or the slackness of the act: Prov. 1. 16. Their feet run to evil, and they hasten to shed blood. Phil. 3. 6.

units.la: 6. A circumstantiis loci, temporis, & personarum praesentium: Jes. 26. 10. In terra aequissima inique agit. 1 Cor XI, 10, 22.
units.tr: 6. From the circumstances of place, time, and the persons present: Isa. 26. 10. In the land of uprightness he deals unjustly. 1 Cor. 11. 10, 22.

units.la: Nullum interim peccatum absolute leve putandum est; propter repugnantiam adversus infinitam & sanctissimam Dei Majestatem, ac Legem Ipsius.
units.tr: Yet no sin should be considered absolutely slight, on account of its opposition to the infinite and most holy Majesty of God, and to His Law.

units.la: XLVIII. Admodum fertile est malum peccati;
units.tr: XLVIII. The evil of sin is exceedingly fruitful;

units.la: Matth. 7. 17. Gen. 6. 5. viij. 21. Psal. 19. 13. Unde etiam fit, ut peccantes in idem specie peccatum prolabantur saepius. Petrus ter abnegavit Dominum; Matth. 26. 70, 72, 74, 75. Et Abraham denuo uxorem suam; Gen. 12. 13, 18, 19. XX. 2, 5, 13. Ubi autem hoc contingit, postquam de priori suo actu admoniti sunt peccantes, & resipuerunt, recidiva spiritualis appellatur; quae gravior est, & maximopere vitanda. Tristissimus vero est eorum casus, qui se rursum totos peccatis prioribus mancipant. Prov. 26. 11. Ut canis redit ad vomitum suum, ita stolidus iterat stultitiam suam. 2 Petr. 2. 21, 22. Melius enim fuisset eis, non cognovisse viam justitiae, &c. Judae, 12. Arbores bis emortuae.
units.tr: Matt. 7. 17. Gen. 6. 5; 8. 21. Ps. 19. 13. Hence it also happens that those who sin in the same kind of sin fall into it again and again. Peter denied the Lord three times (Matt. 26. 70, 72, 74, 75), and Abraham again (Gen. 12. 13, 18, 19; 20. 2, 5, 13) passed off his wife as his sister. When this happens after sinners have been warned about their earlier act and have repented, it is called spiritual relapse, which is more serious and must be avoided above all. Most wretched, however, is the case of those who again give themselves wholly over to their former sins. Prov. 26. 11. As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly. 2 Pet. 2. 21, 22. It would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, etc. Jude 12. Trees twice dead.

units.la: XLIX. Iterando peccata, acquiritur consuetudo & habitus quidam peccandi: Jerem. 13, 23. Unde originalis corruptio incrementum capit; nisi per gratiam supprimatur, mortificetur, &c.
units.tr: XLIX. By repeating sins, a custom and a certain habit of sinning is acquired: Jer. 13. 23. Hence original corruption grows, unless it is restrained, mortified, etc., by grace.

units.la: Hinc peccatum habituale dispescitur in regnans, & non regnans. Rom. 6. 12, 13, 14, 16. ,,Ne regnato igitur peccatum in mortali vestro corpore; ut auscultetis ei in cupiditatibus corporis. -- Peccatum enim vobis non dominabitur: non enim estis sub Lege, sed sub Gratia, &c.
units.tr: Hence habitual sin is divided into reigning and non-reigning. Rom. 6. 12, 13, 14, 16. "Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, so that you obey it in its bodily lusts. ... For sin shall not have dominion over you, for you are not under the Law but under Grace," etc.

units.la: Peccatum igitur absolute regnans est, cui peccator omnino servit; dum extra Christi communionem, & Spiritus sanctificantis gratiam constitutus, per eam non emancipatus est. Joh. 8. 36. Si vos Filius in libertatem vindicarit, vere liberi eritis. 2Cor. 3, 17. Dominus vero Spiritus ille est: tibi autem Spiritus ille Domini, illic libertas. Confer Rom. 14. 9. 1 Joh. 2.27. Joh. 14. 26. xvj. 13. Rom. 8. 13, 14.
units.tr: Sin is therefore absolutely reigning when the sinner serves it entirely, while he remains outside communion with Christ and the grace of the sanctifying Spirit, and has not been set free from it through that grace. John 8. 36. If the Son sets you free, you will be truly free. 2 Cor. 3. 17. Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. Compare Rom. 14. 9; 1 John 2. 27; John 14. 26; 16. 13; Rom. 8. 13, 14.

units.la: Fieri tamen potest, & contingit saepe, ut regeniti ac sanctificati tentationibus aliquando & aliquamdiu succumbant; atque ita praelio inferiores sint, peccatum vero praevaleat, Spiritu se tunc non exerente; quamvis tandem bello plus quam victores futuri, per virtutem Christi. Huc pertinet deprecatio Psal. 19. 14. A contumaciis subtrahe servum Tuum, ne dominentur in me: tunc integer & insons ero a defectione magna. Confer Matth. 6. 13. xxv). 41. Spiritus enim in ipsis manens, eos erigit rursum & stabilitshoftem vero aeternit. 1 Joh. 3. 9. Quisquis natus est ex Deo, peccato non dat operam; quoniam semen Ipsius in eo manet: nec potest peccare, eo quod ex Deo natus est. Adde v,18. Rom. 16,20.
units.tr: Yet it can happen, and often does, that the regenerate and sanctified sometimes and for some time yield to temptations, and so are inferior in the battle, while sin prevails because the Spirit is not then exerting Himself; though in the end, by the power of Christ, they will be more than conquerors in the war. To this belongs the prayer of Ps. 19. 14. Keep back Your servant from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me; then shall I be blameless and innocent of great transgression. Compare Matt. 6. 13; 25. 41. For the Spirit, remaining in them, raises them up again and establishes them, but the enemy eternally. 1 John 3. 9. Whoever is born of God does not practise sin, for His seed remains in him; nor can he sin, because he is born of God. Add 1 John 5. 18; Rom. 16. 20.

units.la: Aliter se habet peccatum tentans quidem, sed non praevalens; ubi tentatus per gratiam actualem superior evadit, etiam in isto conflictu: quod in regenitis & sanctificatis passim est obvium.
units.tr: It is otherwise with sin that tempts but does not prevail, where the tempted person, through actual grace, comes out the victor even in this conflict; this is found everywhere among the regenerate and sanctified.

units.la: Peccato regnanti affine est, quod vocatur peccatum in deliciis; ad quod peccator per corruptionem suam, aut reliquias ejus validiores, praeceteris inclinatur, ita ut aegre ab eo divellatur, illud passim excusare conetur, nec facile admittat ejus reprehensionem. Prov. 9. 17. Aquae furtivae suaves sunt, &c. xx. 17. Suavis est cibus falsitatis. Confer exemplum Herodis, Marc. 6. 17.
units.tr: Akin to reigning sin is what is called sin in delights, to which the sinner, through his corruption or its remaining strength, is more inclined than to others, so that he is hardly torn away from it; he tries to excuse it everywhere and does not easily admit reproof of it. Prov. 9. 17. Stolen waters are sweet, etc. 20. 17. Food gained by falsehood is sweet. Compare the example of Herod, Mark 6. 17.

units.la: Contrarium est peccatum odio habitum. Am. 5.15. Odio habete malum. Psal. 119. 104, 128. Odi omnem semitam falsitatis. L. Se-
units.tr: The opposite is sin hated. Amos 5. 15. Hate evil. Ps. 119. 104, 128. I hate every path of falsehood.

units.la: L. Sequuntur Fructus peccatorum actualium. Primò autem Mors spiritualis per ea continuatur, & incrementum capit. In genere damni huc pertinet ulterior deformatio Imaginis Divinæ; dum ejus reliquiæ amplius corrumpuntur, & conscientia vastatur. Eph. iv, 18, 19. „Abalienati à vita Dei, propter ignorantiam quæ est in ipsis, per obdurationem cordis ipsorum: qui postquam dedolucrunt, sese dediderunt lasciviæ, ad certatim patrandam impuritatem omnem. 22. De seductricibus cupiditatibus sese corrumpit. Adde Judæ, 12. Jerem. 13, 23.
units.tr: Next follow the fruits of actual sins. First, spiritual death is continued and grows through them. In the kind of loss belongs the further deformation of the Divine Image, as its remnants are more and more corrupted and the conscience is laid waste. Eph. 4. 18, 19. "Alienated from the life of God, because of the ignorance that is in them, through the hardening of their hearts; who, having become callous, have given themselves up to lasciviousness, to practise every kind of impurity eagerly." Eph. 4. 22: he corrupts himself through deceitful lusts. Add Jude 12; Jer. 13. 23.

units.la: In genere sensus est continuatio & aggravatio Servitutis spiritualis, sive subjectionis ad potestatem hostium spiritualium: 1. Diaboli, qui efficaciter operatur in peccatoribus sibi relictis. 2 Petr. 2. 19. A quo quis superatus est, huic etiam in servitutem est addictus.
units.tr: In the kind of sense, there is a continuation and aggravation of spiritual servitude, or subjection to the power of spiritual enemies: (1) of the devil, who works effectively in sinners left to themselves. 2 Pet. 2. 19. By whom a man is overcome, to him he is also enslaved.

units.la: 2 Cor. iv, 4. In quibus Deus hujus sæculi excæcavit mentes, &c. Eph. 2, 2. „Ut est vita mundi hujus, secundum principem cui est potestas aëris, & spiritus nunc agentis in hominibus contumacibus. Confer Ioh. 12, 31. xvj. 11. Act. 26, 18. 2 Tim. 2, 26. Hebr. 2, 14.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 4. 4. In whom the god of this age has blinded the minds, etc. Eph. 2. 2. According to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now works in the disobedient. Compare John 12. 31; 16. 11; Acts 26. 18; 2 Tim. 2. 26; Heb. 2. 14.

units.la: 2. Similiter se habet Servitus mundi; subjectio ad quælibet irritamenta malorum, quibus mundus abundat. 1 Ioh. 5. 19. Mundum totum in illo improbo jacere. iv, 5. E mundo sunt; ideo mundana loquuntur. Adde ij. 15, 16. Phil. 3. 19.
units.tr: (2) Likewise there is the servitude of the world, subjection to whatever allurements of evil the world abounds in. 1 John 5. 19. The whole world lies in the wicked one. 4. 5. They are of the world; therefore they speak worldly things. Add James 4. 15, 16; Phil. 3. 19.

units.la: Itemque 3. Servitus peccati habitualis multum adaucti & confirmati per exempla, irritamenta; & consuetudinem vitiosam. Rom. 6, 16. Jerem. 13, 23.
units.tr: And likewise (3) the servitude of habitual sin, greatly increased and confirmed by examples, allurements, and evil custom. Rom. 6. 16; Jer. 13. 23.

units.la: Accedit Terror conscientiæ, cum Desperatione conjunctus; ex incremento reatus, & poenarum gravissimarum certò imminentium in æternum, si peccatores sibi relinquantur. Heb. 2. 15. Metu mortis per omnem vitam damnates servitutis. Adde x. 31. Prov. 28. 1. Isf. 33. 14.
units.tr: To this is added the terror of conscience, joined with despair, arising from the increase of guilt and of the most grievous punishments certainly impending for eternity, if sinners are left to themselves. Heb. 2. 15. Through fear of death they were all their lifetime subject to bondage. Add Heb. 10. 31; Prov. 28. 1; Isa. 33. 14.

units.la: Occurrit interim admiranda Dei benignitas ac φιλανθρωπία erga electos; in Christo : Eph.1,7 Col.1·14. 1 Joh. 1,7. Rom. 8. 1. Joh. 3.16. v. 24. Quin & circa alios adhibetur quædam Moderatio; primò interna, in nonnullis Imaginis Divinæ reliquiis, quamvis non salutaribus: quò pertinent Principia quædam tum theoretica, tum practica; Synterefis & Conscientia naturalis; Inclinatio ad quædam civiliter bona, & Aversatio atrociorum quorundam criminum: Rom. 1.19,20,32: ij.14,15. 1 Cor. 5.1, &c. Accedit in quibusdam Gratia cohibens, refrenans, illuminans, &c. Deinde etiam externa, in mediis Politicis, Ecclesiasticis, Scholasticis, OEconomicis; quibus multi a variis peccatis retrahuntur, &c.
units.tr: Meanwhile the admirable kindness and philanthropy (φιλανθρωπία) of God toward the elect in Christ comes to meet us: Eph. 1. 7; Col. 1. 14; 1 John 1. 7; Rom. 8. 1; John 3. 16; 5. 24. Indeed, toward others too a certain moderation is applied: first internal, in some remnants of the Divine Image, though not saving ones; to this belong certain principles, both theoretical and practical: synderesis and natural conscience; an inclination toward certain things that are civilly good, and an aversion to certain atrocious crimes. Rom. 1. 19, 20, 32; 2. 14, 15; 1 Cor. 5. 1, etc. In some there is added a restraining, curbing, enlightening grace, etc. Then also external moderation, in political, ecclesiastical, scholastic, and domestic means, by which many are withdrawn from various sins, etc.

units.la: LI. Mortem spiritualem comitatur corporalis. Ad hujus inchoationem internam, in genere damni, pertinet ulterior sanitatis, roboris, ac vivacitatis amissio: Job. 14.1,2. Homo natus muliere, brevis ætate, satur commotione, &c. Psal. 90.5,6,8,10. lv.24. 1 Cor. xi.30.
units.tr: LI. Bodily death accompanies spiritual death. To its internal beginning, in the kind of loss, belongs a further loss of health, strength, and vigour: Job 14. 1, 2. Man, born of a woman, short of days and full of turmoil, etc. Ps. 90. 5, 6, 8, 10; 55. 24; 1 Cor. 11. 30.

units.la: In genere sensûs, accedunt fatigationes, dolores, cruciatûs, morborum molestiæ, & species quandoque novæ: Job. 16. 1. Deut. 28. 21, 22, 27, 28,35.
units.tr: In the kind of sense there are added fatigues, pains, torments, the troubles of diseases, and sometimes new forms of them: Job 16. 1; Deut. 28. 21, 22, 27, 28, 35.

units.la: Ad inchoationem externam, in genere damni, Amissio bonorum externorum, quæ tum sustentandæ, tum cohonestandæ vitæ serviebant: utpote 1. Paupertas, sive inopia victûs, vestitûs, possessionum: Prov. 6. 11. Deut. 28.16,17,18,48.
units.tr: To the external beginning, in the kind of loss: the loss of external goods, which served both to sustain and to adorn life. These are: (1) poverty, or want of food, clothing and possessions: Prov. 6. 11. Deut. 28. 16, 17, 18, 48.

units.la: 2. Amissio dominii in creaturas inferiores; unde nunc sæpe damna inferuntur, quin & vulnera; cædes, &c.
units.tr: (2) The loss of dominion over the lower creatures, whence now injuries are often inflicted, even wounds, slaughter, etc.

units.la: 3. Privatio gloriæ, & miseræ vilitas: 1 Sam. 2. 30. Rom. 3.23.
units.tr: (3) Privation of glory and wretched worthlessness: 1 Sam. 2. 30. Rom. 3. 23.

units.la: In genere sensûs, occurrunt calamitates & adversa innumera, cruciatûs ac dolores inducentia, opprobria, &c. Deut. 28.25,26,37,38. Levit. 26.21,22. Joel. 1,4,-. Psal. 29.5,7,10. Confer 1 Reg. 13.24. 2,ij.23,24. xvij.24. Verum etiam hic intervenit Moderatio: intus enim conceditur aliquod vitæ spatium; & multiplex demonstratio benignitatis ac longanimitatis Divinæ, hominem ad officia suæ revocantis: Gen. 6. 3. Rom. 2. 4. Et simul externe conceduntur quæ ad vitam tantisper confervandam necessaria sunt; alimenta, medicamenta, &c. Act. 14. 17. xvij. 25, 26. Nec non reliquiæ quædam veteris dominii: Gen. 9. 2.
units.tr: In the sphere of sense, countless calamities and adversities occur, bringing torments and pains, reproaches, etc.: Deut. 28. 25, 26, 37, 38. Lev. 26. 21, 22. Joel 1, 4. Ps. 29. 5, 7, 10. Compare 1 Kings 13. 24; 2 Kings 23. 24; 17. 24. Yet even here moderation intervenes: inwardly a certain span of life is granted, and there is a manifold demonstration of the divine kindness and long-suffering, calling man back to his duty: Gen. 6. 3; Rom. 2. 4. And at the same time outwardly are granted those things which are necessary for sustaining life for the time being: food, medicines, etc.: Acts 14. 17; 17. 25, 26. Also certain remnants of the old dominion: Gen. 9. 2.

units.la: Sed ista omnia illustriora sunt, & salutaria, in fidelibus: Tit 1. 15. Rom. 14. 14. Act. 15. 9. Rom. 8. 17. 1 Cor. 3. 21, 22, 23. Hos. 2. 17.
units.tr: But all these things are more illustrious and salutary in believers: Titus 1. 15; Rom. 14. 14; Acts 15. 9; Rom. 8. 17; 1 Cor. 3. 21, 22, 23; Hos. 2. 17.

units.la: LII. Sic fuerunt Initia dolorum, & Mors inchoata. Mors corporalis consummatur actuali separatione Animæ a Corpore. Eccl. 12. 7. Redeunte ipso pulvere in terram, &c. Hebr. 9. 27. Sicut illud Statutum est hominibus, ut semel Moriantur, postea vero Iudicium. Hinc tamen prorsus eximendi sunt fideles, qui novissimo die erunt superstites: 1 Cor. 11. 51. 1 Thess. 4. 16, 17.
units.tr: LII. Thus were the beginnings of pains and the beginning of death. Bodily death is completed by the actual separation of the soul from the body, Eccl. 12. 7, the dust itself returning to the earth, etc. Heb. 9. 27: As it is appointed to men once to die, but after this the judgment. Yet believers who are alive on the last day are wholly exempted from this: 1 Cor. 15. 51; 1 Thess. 4. 16, 17.

units.la: Corpus porro resolvitur in suas partes, & elementa; intercedente fere in istum finem humatione; alibi etiam combustione. Abjici sine sepultura, ut cadaver canibus, avibus, & feris laniandum relinquatur; vel etiam publico ludibrio, nauseæ, & aversationi objiciatur, specialem habet ignominiam: Deut. 28. 26. Psal. 79. 2, 3. Jerem. 22. 19. xxxvj. 30.
units.tr: Further, the body is dissolved into its parts and elements, burial almost always intervening to this end, and elsewhere burning. To be cast out unburied, so that the corpse is left to be torn by dogs, birds and beasts, or even to be exposed to public mockery, disgust and loathing, carries a special infamy: Deut. 28. 26; Ps. 79. 2, 3; Jer. 22. 19; 36. 30.

units.la: Anima vero statim a separatione sistitur coram Deo judice: Eccl. 12. 7. eique sua mansio, suus status assignatur: qui est condemnationis & cruciatuum in omnibus infidelibus: Act. 1. 25. 1 Petr. 3, 19, 20. Judæ, 7. Luc. 16. 23,-26, 28. Fidelium enim propter redemtionem Christi alia omnino est conditio: Joh. 5. 24. x, 27, 28. 2 Cor. 5. 1, 2, 6, 8. Phil. 1. 21, 23. Luc. 16. 22, 25. xxiij. 43.
units.tr: The soul, however, immediately after separation is brought before God the judge (Eccl. 12. 7), and is assigned its dwelling and its state, which for all unbelievers is one of condemnation and torments: Acts 1. 25; 1 Pet. 3. 19, 20; Jude 7; Luke 16. 23–26, 28. For believers, on account of Christ's redemption, the condition is altogether different: John 5. 24; 10. 27, 28; 2 Cor. 5. 1, 2, 6, 8; Phil. 1. 21, 23; Luke 16. 22, 25; 23. 43.

units.la: LIII. Mortis spiritualis, atque universæ maledictionis ex-
units.tr: LIII. The complete consummation of spiritual death and of the whole curse

units.la: extrema confummatio fiet die noviffimo, in univerfali illo judicio: ubi infideles & improbi fufcitabuntur ad opprobria & contemtum æternum: mox condemnati conjicientur in gehennam, ad fupplicia & cruciatus æternos, abfque ullo fine, aut remiffione: Dan. 12.2. Job. 5.28, 29. Matth. 10. 28. XXV.31,32,33,41,46. Jude 14, 15. Apoc. 14. 11. XX, 10,-13. XXj, 8. Marc. 9. 44, 46, 48.
units.tr: will take place on the last day, in that universal judgment, where unbelievers and the wicked will be raised to reproach and everlasting contempt. Soon the condemned will be cast into gehenna, to everlasting punishments and torments, without any end or remission: Dan. 12. 2; John 5. 28, 29; Matt. 10. 28; 25. 31, 32, 33, 41, 46; Jude 14, 15; Rev. 14. 11; 20. 10–13; 21. 8; Mark 9. 44, 46, 48.

units.la: Fidelium vero & piorum, juxta Euangelium, ftatus æternus erit beatiffimus ac gloriofiffimus. Vide hæc paucis indicata fup. cap. 1. th. 41. pluribus σὺν Θεῷ explicanda & confirmanda cap. 19.
units.tr: The eternal state of believers and of the pious, according to the Gospel, will be most blessed and most glorious. These things are indicated briefly here above in ch. 1, th. 41, and are to be explained and confirmed at length, with God's help [σὺν Θεῷ], in ch. 19.

units.la: LIV. Quod ad Praxin, 1. Hoc agamus fedulo, ut fint nobis fenfus exercitati ad difcretionem boni & mali: Hebr. 5.14. 1 Cor. 14.20. Matth. 10.16.
units.tr: LIV. As to practice: (1) Let us diligently take care that our senses are exercised in discerning good and evil: Heb. 5. 14; 1 Cor. 14. 20; Matt. 10. 16.

units.la: 2. Legi Divinæ in eum finem ferio ac perpetuo ftudeamus: Pfal. 1.2. cxix. 99,-105. Deut. 4.6.
units.tr: (2) Let us earnestly and constantly study the divine law to this end: Ps. 1. 2; 119. 99–105; Deut. 4. 6.

units.la: 3. Super peccatis noftris, & vilitate, quam ea inducunt, humiliemur: de turpitudine erubefcamus: ex reatu nos ipfos judicemus: Pfal. 51. 5,6, 7. Jef. 64.6. 1 Cor. xi. 31. Jerem. 2. 19.
units.tr: (3) Let us be humbled over our sins and the vileness they bring; let us blush at the baseness; let us judge ourselves by our guilt: Ps. 51. 5, 6, 7; Isa. 64. 6; 1 Cor. 11. 31; Jer. 2. 19.

units.la: 4. Juftitiam Dei in omnibus fuis judiciis agnofcamus, & prædicemus: Pfal. 51. 6. Rom. 3. 4.
units.tr: (4) Let us acknowledge and proclaim the justice of God in all his judgments: Ps. 51. 6; Rom. 3. 4.

units.la: 5. Ad Chriftum Servatorem omni defiderio anhelemus; fumma ope contendamus; ejufque communionem per fidem quæramus: Matth. 1. 21. v. 6. xi. 28. Rom. 7. 24. Phil. 3. 8, 9.
units.tr: (5) Let us pant after Christ the Saviour with every desire, strive with the greatest effort, and seek communion with him through faith: Matt. 1. 21; 5. 6; 11. 28; Rom. 7. 24; Phil. 3. 8, 9.

units.la: 6. Caftigationes patienter feramus, & ad emendationem noftri applicemus: Mich. 7. 9. Pfal. 119. 71. 1 Cor. xi. 32. Hebr. 12. 11. Rom. 8. 28.
units.tr: (6) Let us bear chastisements patiently and apply them to our amendment: Mic. 7. 9; Ps. 119. 71; 1 Cor. 11. 32; Heb. 12. 11; Rom. 8. 28.

units.la: 7. Confcientiam fæpiffime & accuratiffime exploremus; fenfus & inclinationes obfervemus, &c. Thren. 3. 40. Zephan. 2.1. 1 Cor. xi. 28. 2, xiij, 5. Matth. 15. 19, 20. Pfal. 131: 1. Job. 31.1.
units.tr: (7) Let us examine our conscience very often and most accurately; let us observe our feelings and inclinations, etc.: Lam. 3. 40; Zeph. 2. 1; 1 Cor. 11. 28; 2 Cor. 13. 5; Matt. 15. 19, 20; Ps. 131. 1; Job 31. 1.

units.la: 8. Vigilemus fpeciatim adverfus peccata, quæ folebant esse familiaria, vel in deliciis; caveamus à peccato regnante, contra conscientiam, recidivâ spirituali, &c. Prov. 4. 23. Jerem. 17, 9. 1 Petr. 5. 8.
units.tr: (8) Let us watch especially against those sins which used to be familiar or among our delights; let us beware of the reigning sin, of sinning against conscience, of spiritual relapse, etc.: Prov. 4. 23; Jer. 17. 9; 1 Pet. 5. 8.

units.la: 9. Imbecillitatem nostram spectemus; viribus propriis ne confidamus; prudentiam sanctorum & robur spirituale in Christo per fidem quæramus, ab Eo expectemus: Matth. 26. 41. Jac. 3, 1, 2. iv. 6. 2 Cor. 3, 5. Thren. 5. 21. 1 Thess. 5. 23. 24.
units.tr: (9) Let us regard our weakness; let us not trust in our own strength; let us seek prudence from the saints and spiritual strength in Christ through faith, and expect it from him: Matt. 26. 41; Jas. 3. 1, 2; 4. 6; 2 Cor. 3. 5; Lam. 5. 21; 1 Thess. 5. 23, 24.

units.la: 10. Ex gravitate ac multitudine peccatorum & poenarum, à quibus per Christum liberamur, recte æstimemus beneficium redemtionis; eoque magis ad amorem Dei & Christi, & animum gratum perpetuo præstandum, nos devinctos agnoscamus: Luc. 1, 74, 75. vij, 47, 50. Rom. 6. 1,-. 2 Cor. 5. 14, 15.
units.tr: (10) From the gravity and multitude of the sins and punishments from which we are freed through Christ, let us rightly estimate the benefit of redemption, and so acknowledge ourselves more bound to show love to God and Christ perpetually and a grateful mind: Luke 1. 74, 75; 7. 47, 50; Rom. 6. 1; 2 Cor. 5. 14, 15.

units.la: 11. Magis etiam aliorum peccantium commiseratione tangamur, &c. Luc. 22, 32. 2 Cor. 5. 11. Jac. 5. 19, 20. cum Hebr. 2, 18. iv. 15.
units.tr: (11) Let us also be moved even more by compassion for other sinners, etc.: Luke 22. 32; 2 Cor. 5. 11; Jas. 5. 19, 20; compare Heb. 2. 18; 4. 15.

units.la: CAPUT XI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XI.

units.la: De Fœdere Euangelico.
units.tr: On the Gospel Covenant.

units.la: Fœdus Euangelicum definitur. Partium inæqualitas. Fœdus reconciliationis. 1. Quid Deus in hoc negotio egerit. 2. Quid Christus Mediator. 3. Quid Populus fœderatus agat. 4. Partes hujus conventionis. Finis supremus. Subordinatus. Medium proximum. 5. Communio ejus interna, electorum propria; c. Pontif. Socin. &c. Externa reprobis quibusdam obtingit. 6. Participes istius Fœderis varie. 7. Quomodo Fœdus æternum. Ejus initium. 8. Euangelium. 9. Promissionis. Impletionis. Realiter idem. 10. Acceptiones variæ Euangelii.
units.tr: The Gospel covenant is defined. The inequality of the parties. The covenant of reconciliation. 1. What God does in this business. 2. What Christ the Mediator does. 3. What the covenanted people do. 4. The parts of this agreement. The supreme end. The subordinate end. The proximate means. 5. Its inward communion, proper to the elect; against the Papists, the Socinians, etc. Its outward communion falls to certain reprobates. 6. The various participants in this covenant. 7. How the covenant is eternal. Its beginning. 8. The Gospel. 9. Of promise and of fulfilment; really the same. 10. The various senses of the Gospel.

units.la: gelii. 11. Fœderis Euangelici comparatio cum Le-gali. 12. Male Pontif. statuunt Consilia Euange-lica. &c. Usus Legis circa Fœdus Euangelicum, 13. Testamentum. Unum reipsa: prout una Hæreditas. 14. Ex morte ejusdem Testatoris. 15. Eadem doctrina Testamentaria sub V. T. quæ sub N. 16. Eadem fides justificans. 17. Sententiæ Socin. &c. Nec non Pontif. Obj. solv. 18. OEco-nomiæ V. T. duæ periodi illustriores. 19. Prima Euangelii prædicatio. Vocatio, Justificatio, &c. 20. Instituta cerimonialia. Sacrificia. Sacramenta. 21. Quæ tempore Abrahami accesserint. 22. Altera periodus. Ejus Signa extraordinaria. Ordinaria, 23. Ministri extraord. Ordin. 24. Sacerdotes. Eorum consecratio. 25. Summus. Ejus ornatus. Unctio. 26. Summus Israelitarum Senatus. Nazirai. Mundi. 27. Sacrificium. Expiatorium. Eucharisticum. Eorum consecratio. 28. Suffitus sacer. Oleum sacrum. Aqua expiationis. 29. Lucerna sacra. Tuba argentea. Cibi sacri. 30. Novalia. Primitiæ. Decimæ. Vota. 31. Tabernaculum. Ejus partes continentes. 32. Velum. Sanctum Sanctorum. Arca fœderis. Cherubim. Thuribulum aureum. Sanctum Altare suffitus. Lychnuchus. 33. Atrium. Altare holocaustorum. Labrum æneum. 34. Templum profanatum. Combustum. restauratum. iterum profanatum. repurgatum. renovatum. penitus evertsum. 35. Tempora sacra. Dies. Sabbathum. Neomenia. 36. Festum Paschatis. Pentecostes. Tabernaculorum. 37. Festum Tubarum. Dies expiationis. 38. Annus Sabbathicus. Jubilæus. Status Israelitarum Politicus. 39. OEco-nomia nomia N. T. ab illa distinguitur differentia temporis. 40. Claritate. Libertate. 41. Quantitate intensiva; & extensiva. 42. Adventus Messiæ jam dudum præteriit; c. Judæos. 43. Objectiones solv. 44. Vocatio Gentium. 45. Permutatio in Œconomiam magis spiritualem & gloriosam, abrogato veteri cultu typico. 46. Objectiones solv. 47. Praxis. 48.
units.tr: ...gospel. 11. Comparison of the Gospel covenant with the Legal. 12. The Papists wrongly posit "evangelical counsels", etc. The use of the Law with respect to the Gospel covenant. 13. The testament: one in reality, as one inheritance. 14. From the death of the same Testator. 15. The same testamentary doctrine under the Old Testament as under the New. 16. The same justifying faith. 17. The opinions of the Socinians, etc., and likewise the objections of the Papists, answered. 18. Two more illustrious periods of the economy of the Old Testament. 19. The first preaching of the Gospel. Calling, justification, etc. 20. The ceremonial institutions. Sacrifices. Sacraments. 21. What was added in the time of Abraham. 22. The second period. Its extraordinary signs; its ordinary ones. 23. Extraordinary and ordinary ministers. 24. The priests and their consecration. 25. The high priest; his vestments; anointing. 26. The supreme senate of the Israelites. Nazirites. Clean persons. 27. Sacrifice: expiatory, eucharistic; their consecration. 28. Sacred incense. Holy oil. Water of expiation. 29. The sacred lampstand. The silver trumpet. Sacred foods. 30. Fallow land. First fruits. Tithes. Vows. 31. The tabernacle and its containing parts. 32. The veil. The Holy of Holies. The ark of the covenant. The cherubim. The golden censer. The holy altar of incense. The lampstand. 33. The court. The altar of burnt offerings. The bronze laver. 34. The temple profaned, burnt, restored, profaned again, cleansed, renewed, utterly overthrown. 35. Sacred times: days, the Sabbath, the new moon. 36. The feasts of Passover, Pentecost, and Tabernacles. 37. The Feast of Trumpets. The Day of Atonement. 38. The sabbatical year. The jubilee. The political state of the Israelites. 39. The economy of the New Testament is distinguished from that one by difference of time. 40. By clarity. By liberty. 41. By intensive and extensive quantity. 42. The coming of the Messiah has long since passed; against the Jews. 43. Objections answered. 44. The calling of the Gentiles. 45. The change into a more spiritual and glorious economy, with the old typical worship abrogated. 46. Objections answered. 47. Practice. 48.

units.la: I. [Decorated initial S] Uccedit Restitutio Generis electi, juxta Fœdus Euangelicum, seu Gratiæ, & Fidei: quod est Gratiosa dispositio Dei erga homines electos, per peccatum in miseria constitutos; ut isti ex Satisfactione & Merito Mediatoris Christi, remissionem peccatorum, justitiam, salutem, atque omnia ad hanc necessaria, gratis consequantur per fidem: ipsi autem Euangelio credant, resipiscant, & gratitudinem ac novam obedientiam Deo consequenter præstent, ad laudem gloriosæ ejus misericordiæ.
units.tr: I. Next comes the restoration of the elect race, according to the gospel covenant, or of grace and faith. This is God's gracious disposition toward elect men, who through sin have been placed in misery, so that these men, from the satisfaction and merit of Christ the Mediator, may freely obtain through faith the forgiveness of sins, righteousness, salvation, and all things necessary to these; while they themselves believe the gospel, repent, and consequently render gratitude and new obedience to God, to the praise of his glorious mercy.

units.la: Maxime hic conspicua est Partium contrahentium Inæqualitas, Deinque ad Homines συγκατάθεσις; & quod hoc sit Fœdus Reconciliationis: 2 Cor. 5. 19. Deus erat in Christo mundum reconcilians Sibi. Col. 1. 20. Ut per Eum reconciliaret omnia Sibi, &c.
units.tr: Here the inequality of the contracting parties is most conspicuous, and in men a consent [συγκατάθεσις]; and this is a covenant of reconciliation: 2 Cor. 5. 19. God was in Christ reconciling the world to Himself. Col. 1. 20. That through Him He might reconcile all things to Himself, etc.

units.la: II. Deus in hoc negotio 1. Mediatorem ipse proposuit: Joh. 3. 16. Ita enim Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum illum unigenitum dederit, &c. Rom. 3. 25. Gal. iv. 4.
units.tr: II. God in this matter 1. Himself proposed the Mediator: John 3. 16. For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, etc. Rom. 3. 25. Gal. 4. 4.

units.la: 2. Iustitiam, salutem, atque omnia ad hanc necessaria, ipsius satisfactione, & merito fundata, offert & confert gratis per fidem: 1 Cor. 1. 30.-Estis in Christo Jesu, qui factus est nobis sapientia a Deo, justitia & sanctificatio, & redemtio. Joh. 1. 16. Eph. 2. 8. 2 Petr. 1. 3, 4.
units.tr: 2. He offers and freely confers, through faith, righteousness, salvation, and all things necessary to these, founded on his satisfaction and merit: 1 Cor. 1. 30. You are in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God, righteousness and sanctification and redemption. John 1. 16. Eph. 2. 8. 2 Pet. 1. 3, 4.

units.la: 3. Stipulatur autem ab electis praxin fidei & resipiscentiæ: Marc. 1. 15. Resipiscite, & credite Euangelio. Itemque gratitudinis: Col. 3. 17. Quicquid feceritis certis-id facitegratias agentes Deo. Ac novæ obedientiæ: Gen. 17. 1. - Indesinenter ambula coram Me, & esto integer. Rom. 6. 13. Sistite vos Deo ut ex mortuis vivos, &c.
units.tr: 3. He requires, however, from the elect the practice of faith and repentance: Mark 1. 15. Repent, and believe the gospel. Likewise gratitude: Col. 3. 17. Whatever you do in word or deed, do it giving thanks to God. And new obedience: Gen. 17. 1. Walk before Me without ceasing, and be blameless. Rom. 6. 13. Present yourselves to God as living from the dead, etc.

units.la: III. Christus Mediator & Sponsor hujus Fœderis.
units.tr: III. Christ as Mediator and Surety of this Covenant.

units.la: 1. Vadimonium suscepit: Isef. 53. 10. Exposuit seipsum sacrificium pro reatu. Ipse de se, Hebr. x. 7. (ex Psal. 40. 8, 9.) Ecce adsum, ut faciam Deus voluntatem Tuam.
units.tr: 1. He undertook the surety: Isai. 53. 10. He offered Himself as a sacrifice for guilt. He says of Himself, Heb. 10. 7 (from Ps. 40. 8, 9): Behold, I come to do Your will, O God.

units.la: 2. Agendo & patiendo, omnia ad justitiam & salutem necessaria plenissime consummavit: Hebr. x. 10. Qua voluntate sanctificati sumus, per oblationem corporis Iesu Christi semel factam.
units.tr: 2. By acting and suffering, He most fully accomplished all things necessary for righteousness and salvation: Heb. 10. 10. By that will we have been sanctified, through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once made.

units.la: 3. Eademque, tum revelat & offert moraliter: Isef. 61. 1, 2. cum Luc. 4. 18. Ut evangelizem pauperibus misit Me ... ut prædicem captivis dimissionem: tum applicat & confert efficaciter; Joh. x. 27, 28. Oves illæ Meæ vocem Meam audiunt, & sequuntur Me. Et Ego vitam æternam do eis: neque rapiet eas quisquam e manu Mea.
units.tr: 3. And He both reveals and offers them morally: Isai. 61. 1, 2, with Luke 4. 18. He has sent Me to preach the gospel to the poor ... to proclaim liberty to the captives; and He both applies and effectually confers them: John 10. 27, 28. My sheep hear My voice, and they follow Me. And I give them eternal life; and no one shall snatch them out of My hand.

units.la: IV. Populus vero fœderatus
units.tr: IV. The people in covenant

units.la: 1. Promissiones illas Divinas certo credit: Act. 13. 48. Crediderunt quotquot erant ordinati ad vitam æternam. Rom. 1. 17, iv, 23, 24.
units.tr: 1. They firmly believe those divine promises: Acts 13:48, "As many as were ordained to eternal life believed." Rom. 1:17; 4:23, 24.

units.la: 2. Constanter sperat: Rom. 8. 23. Apud nos ipsos suspiramus, adoptionem exspectantes, -. 25. Per tolerantiam expectamus.
units.tr: 2. They constantly hope: Rom. 8:23, "We ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption"; v. 25, "We wait for it with patience."

units.la: 3. Et novæ obedientiæ, ac gratitudini, serio dat operam: Psal. 110. 3. Populi tui oblationes voluntariæ futuræ sunt. Unde Paulus, in sui conversione: Act. 9, 6. Domine, quid me vis facere? & Rom. 7. 22. Delector lege Dei, quod ad interiorem hominem, &c. Adde Act. 2. 37. Phil. 3. 14. 2 Cor. 13. 13.
units.tr: 3. And they earnestly apply themselves to new obedience and gratitude: Ps. 110:3, "Your people will be willing offerings." Hence Paul, at his conversion: Acts 9:6, "Lord, what will you have me do?" and Rom. 7:22, "I delight in the law of God according to the inner man," etc. Add Acts 2:37; Phil. 3:14; 2 Cor. 13:13.

units.la: V. Partes igitur hujus Conventionis sunt, hinc Deus reconciliari volens hominibus electis, imo eos sibi reconcilians in Christo; inde Homines electi, qui reconciliationem accipiunt: Mediator autem intercedit Christus: 2 Cor. 5. 19. Rom. 5. 11. 1 Tim. 2. 5, 6.
units.tr: V. The parties to this covenant are therefore these: on one side God, who wishes to be reconciled to elect men, indeed reconciles them to himself in Christ; on the other side the elect men, who receive the reconciliation; and Christ intervenes as Mediator: 2 Cor. 5:19; Rom. 5:11; 1 Tim. 2:5, 6.

units.la: Finis supremus est Dei gloria: Prov. 16, 4. Subordinati dinatus, Hominum pax, & salus: Eph. 1. 13, 14, 15. Medium proximum, Unio & communio cum Christo per fidem. Eph. 3. 17. cui inservit Vocatio: 1 Joh. 1. 3. Rom. 8. 30. quæ Christi redemtionem præsupponit: Eph. 1. 7. &c.
units.tr: The ultimate end is the glory of God: Prov. 16:4. Subordinate to it are the peace and salvation of men: Eph. 1:13, 14, 15. The proximate means is union and communion with Christ through faith: Eph. 3:17, to which calling serves: 1 John 1:3; Rom. 8:30, which presupposes the redemption of Christ: Eph. 1:7, etc.

units.la: VI. Cæterum hujus Fœderis communio vel interne spectatur & mystice; vel externe tantum. Prior consideratio ad electos restringitur, contra quàm existimant Pontif. Socin. Anabapt. Remonstr. & alii. Posterior quibusdam reprobis etiam obtingit.
units.tr: VI. Moreover, the communion of this covenant is viewed either internally and mystically, or externally only. The former consideration is restricted to the elect, contrary to what the Papists, Socinians, Anabaptists, Remonstrants and others think. The latter also falls to certain reprobates.

units.la: Prius assertionis nostræ membrum probamus:
units.tr: We prove the first member of our assertion:

units.la: 1. Ex conditione beneficiorum ad internam communionem istius Fœderis pertinentium; quæ individuum cum salute nexum habent, & electorum salvandorum propria sunt. Nam quos præscivit, etiam prædestinavit, conformandos imagini Filii sui; quos vero prædistinavit, eos etiam vocavit: & quos vocavit, eos etiam justificavit: quos autem justificavit, eos etiam glorificavit. Rom. 8. 29, 30. Sic fides est electorum Dei Tit. 1. 1. non vero omnium; 2 Thess. 3. 2. Et credidisse dicuntur, quotquot ad vitam æternam erant ordinati; Act. 13. 48.
units.tr: 1. From the condition of the benefits pertaining to the internal communion of this covenant, which have an inseparable bond with salvation and belong to the elect who are to be saved. "For whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son; and whom he predestined, them he also called; and whom he called, them he also justified; and whom he justified, them he also glorified." Rom. 8:29, 30. Thus faith is "of the elect of God," Titus 1:1, and not of all; 2 Thess. 3:2. And they are said to have believed, "as many as were ordained to eternal life," Acts 13:48.

units.la: 2. Ex consideratione Christi Mediatoris; qui suos efficaciter salvaturus, iisque vitam æternam certo daturus est: Joh. 6. 39. X. 27, 30. Rom. 5. 9, 10, 11. 1 Petr. 1, 5.
units.tr: 2. From the consideration of Christ the Mediator, who is going to save his own effectually and certainly give them eternal life: John 6:39; 10:27, 30; Rom. 5:9, 10, 11; 1 Pet. 1:5.

units.la: 3. Ex æterna & immutabili electione certarum definitè personarum ad communionem beneficiorum vere salutarium, atque ipsam beatitudinem consequendam. Vide sup. cap. 6. th. 15. Deus autem singula exequitur juxta consilium voluntatis suæ, Eph. 1, 11.
units.tr: 3. From the eternal and unchangeable election of certain definite persons to the communion of benefits truly saving, and to the attainment of blessedness itself. See above, ch. 6, th. 15. God, moreover, carries out each thing "according to the counsel of his will," Eph. 1:11.

units.la: 4. Ex eventu: Nam qui non salvantur etiam non pertinuerunt ad internam communionem Fœderis Euangelici, de quibus tenendum illud, 1 Joh. 2. 19. Si fuissent ex nobis, mansissent utique nobiscum. Posterius patet, Ex conditione Ecclesiæ externæ institutæ; multitudinis videl. coeuntis ad communes aliquos actus externos, Prædicationem Euangelii, Administrationem Sacramentorum, &c. Huc pertinet similitudo Areæ, cujus triticum à paleis repurgandum dicitur, Matth. 3. 12. Agri variis partibus varie consiti; xiij, 3. &c. Speciatim hic notandi τρέσκαιροι; ibid. verf. 21. Filii regni foras ejiciendi; viij. 12. Palmites in Christo fructum non ferentes: Joh. xv. 2. quales fuere Judas Iscariotes; Matth. x. 1,4. Simon Magus; Act. x. 13. & similes, de quibus vide 2 Petr. 2. 22. atque hoc sensu, Multivocati, pauci vero electi dicuntur, Matth. 20. 16. xxij. 14.
units.tr: 4. From the outcome: for those who are not saved also did not belong to the internal communion of the Gospel covenant, concerning whom that saying holds, 1 John 2:19: "If they had been of us, they would surely have remained with us." The latter is evident from the condition of the external Church instituted, namely of the multitude gathering for certain common external acts: the preaching of the Gospel, the administration of the sacraments, etc. To this pertains the likeness of the threshing floor, from which the wheat is said to be purged of the chaff, Matt. 3:12; of the field variously sown in various parts, 13:3, etc. Here especially are to be noted the temporary believers (τρέσκαιροι), ibid. verse 21; the sons of the kingdom to be cast out, 8:12; the branches in Christ not bearing fruit, John 15:2, of which kind were Judas Iscariot, Matt. 10:1, 4; Simon Magus, Acts 8:13; and similar persons, concerning whom see 2 Pet. 2:22. And in this sense "many are called, but few are chosen," Matt. 20:16; 22:14.

units.la: VII. Secundum distinctionem datam, sunt qui utroque modo habent communionem Fœderis Euangelici; scil. qui in Ecclesia institura viventes, fide salvifica præditi sunt: alii neutro modo, ut infideles in Gentilismo, Muhammedismo, aut Judaismo: alii interne, non externe; ut Catechumeni vere fideles, à Gentilismo, &c. conversi, sed in communionem Ecclesiæ alicujus institutæ nondum recepti: alii externe, non interne; de quibus th. præced.
units.tr: VII. According to the distinction given, there are those who have communion in the Gospel covenant in both ways, namely those who, living in the instituted Church, are endowed with saving faith; others in neither way, such as unbelievers among the Gentiles, the Muhammadans or the Jews; others internally but not externally, such as the catechumens, truly faithful who have been converted from Gentilism, etc., but not yet received into the communion of any instituted Church; others externally but not internally, concerning whom in the preceding thesis.

units.la: VIII. Quia Fœdus Euangelicum ab æterno in salutem electorum est præordinatum; ut patet, tum ex generali consideratione Decreti; Isf. 46. 10. Eph. 1.
units.tr: VIII. Because the Gospel covenant was predestined from eternity for the salvation of the elect, this is clear both from the general consideration of the decree: Isa. 46:10; Eph. 1:2; (1)

units.la: 2. Act. 15. 18. tum ex ipsa speciali prædestinatione Christi, & Christianorum; Eph. 1. 4. quæ salus in æternum quoque duratura est; Psal. 16. 11. xlviij. 15. Joh. 3. 16, 36. v. 24. xvij, 3. recte dicitur Fœdus æternum; Gen. 17. 7. Jerem. 32. 40. sed cum inter Deum & homines electos in miseria sua constitutos hoc Fœdus formaliter intercedat &, initium ejus collocandum est post lapsum, in prima Euangelii promulgatione. Gen. 3. 15.
units.tr: 2. Acts 15:18; and from the special predestination itself of Christ and Christians: Eph. 1:4; which salvation is also to endure for ever: Ps. 16:11; 48:15; John 3:16, 36; 5:24; 17:3. It is rightly called an "everlasting covenant," Gen. 17:7; Jer. 32:40. But since this covenant formally intervenes between God and the elect men placed in their misery, its beginning is to be located after the fall, in the first promulgation of the Gospel, Gen. 3:15.

units.la: IX. Dispensationi ejus fervit Euangelium; quasi dicas. Bonum nuncium; ab εὐ bene, & ἀγγέλλω nuncio; sic Luc. 2. 10. Ecce, evangelizo vobis gaudium magnum, --. Ief. 52. 7. Ixj. 1, 2, 3. Marc. 16. 15, 16. & alibi. Est autem Euangelium, Doctrina a Deo profecta, & per Christum, ejusque Ministros, multifariam promulgata, de remissione peccatorum, justitia, & vita æterna per fidem ipsius consequenda, ad salutem electorum, & gloriosæ Dei misericordiæ demonstrationem.
units.tr: IX. The Gospel serves its dispensation; as one might say, "good news," from εὐ, "well," and ἀγγέλλω, "I announce"; thus Luke 2:10, "Behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy"; Isa. 52:7; 61:1, 2, 3; Mark 16:15, 16, and elsewhere. The Gospel, moreover, is the doctrine proceeding from God and promulgated in many ways through Christ and his ministers, concerning the remission of sins, righteousness and eternal life to be obtained through faith in him, to the salvation of the elect and the glorious demonstration of the mercy of God.

units.la: X. Estque tum Euangelium promissionis; de Christo in carne exhibendo; quale obtinuit sub œconomia V. T. vel Impletionis; de Christo in carne exhibito; quale spectandum est sub œconomia N. Hinc 1 Petr. 1. 10. Prophetæ de ventura in vos gratia prophetarunt. 12. Quibus revelatum est, eos non sibi, sed nobis ea administrare, quæ nunc annunciata sunt vobis, &c. Similiter Paulus prædicavit Euangelium Dei, quod ante promiserat per Prophetas, - De Filio Suo : Rom. 1. 1, 2, 3.
units.tr: X. The Gospel is both the "Gospel of promise," concerning Christ to be exhibited in the flesh, which it held under the economy of the Old Testament, and the "Gospel of fulfilment," concerning Christ exhibited in the flesh, which is to be regarded under the economy of the New Testament. Hence 1 Pet. 1:10, "The prophets prophesied of the grace that would come to you"; v. 12, "To whom it was revealed that they did not minister these things to themselves but to us, which are now announced to you," etc. Similarly Paul "preached" the Gospel of God, "which he had promised beforehand through the prophets" concerning his Son: Rom. 1:1, 2, 3.

units.la: Et hactenus quidem, in modo dispensationis Euangelicæ, accidentalis aliqua distinctio agnoscenda est; sed ipsum tamen Euangelium essentialiter unum idemque est: nam Iesus Christus heri & hodie idem est, & in sæcula: Hebr. 13. 8. unde & æternum appellatur, Apoc. 15. 6. Quod non est aliud; Gal. 1. 7, 8, 9. Adde Ioh. 14. 6. Act. 4. 12. x. 43. 1 Cor. 3. 11. x. 1, - 4.
units.tr: And so far, in the mode of the Gospel dispensation, some accidental distinction is to be acknowledged; but the Gospel itself is essentially one and the same: for "Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever," Heb. 13:8; whence it is also called eternal, Rev. 14:6. There is no other, Gal. 1:7, 8, 9. Add John 14:6; Acts 4:12; 10:43; 1 Cor. 3:11; 10:1–4.

units.la: XI. Sic Euangelium, ubi proprie & stricte sumitur, salutaria in Christo annunciat: unde Euangelium pacis; Eph. 6. 15. & salutis, dicitur; I. 13. Aliquando latius accipitur; prout fideles in praxi sua dirigit, adhibita etiam lege per modum indicis & normæ: 1 Cor. 11. 28, 31. Phil. 1. 27. Jac. 1. 25. ij. 12. Aliquando denique latissime, prout ipsa sanctio Fœderis Legalis nonnunquam repetitur, suisque objectis ex voluntate Dei applicatur: Rom. 2. 16.
units.tr: XI. Thus the Gospel, when taken properly and strictly, announces the saving things in Christ; whence it is called the "Gospel of peace," Eph. 6:15, and of salvation, 1:13. Sometimes it is taken more broadly, as it directs the faithful in their practice, the law also being employed by way of a sign and rule: 1 Cor. 11:28, 31; Phil. 1:27; Jas. 1:25; 2:12. Finally, sometimes most broadly, as the very sanction of the Legal covenant is sometimes repeated and applied, with its objects, from the will of God: Rom. 2:16.

units.la: XII. Fœdus Euangelicum cum Legali convenit in quibusdam generalibus: utpote, 1. respectu Auctoris Dei, Et quidem 2. Contrahentis cum Hominibus. 3.
units.tr: XII. The Gospel covenant agrees with the Legal in certain general respects: namely, 1. with respect to God as Author; and indeed 2. with respect to the contracting of God with men. 3.

units.la: Cap. XI.
units.tr: Chapter XI.

units.la: Ita ut horum Obedientia utrobique sit necessaria. 4. Vita æterna Promissa; & 5. Finis, Dei gloria.
units.tr: So the obedience of these is necessary on both sides. 4. Eternal life is promised; and 5. the end is the glory of God.

units.la: Sed in specialibus plurimum ab eo discrepat: & quidem potissimum ipsa Summa & Conditione; quæ in Fœdere Legali erat istas Fac hoc, & vives: sin minus, maledictus esto. Levit. 18. 5. Ezech. 20. 11. Rom. x. 5. Deut 27. 26. Gal. 3. 10. Sed in Fœdere Euangelico hæc: Qui credit in Filium, accipit remissionem peccatorum, & vitam æternam: Act. x. 43. Joh. 3. 36. Magis istud apparet, considerato
units.tr: But in particulars it differs greatly from that, and chiefly in its summary and condition. In the Legal Covenant this was: Do this, and you shall live; if not, you shall be cursed. Lev. 18. 5. Ezek. 20. 11. Rom. 10. 5. Deut. 27. 26. Gal. 3. 10. But in the Gospel Covenant it is this: Whoever believes in the Son receives forgiveness of sins and eternal life. Acts 10. 43. John 3. 36. This appears more clearly when we consider the following.

units.la: 1. Genere & Modo communionis: Illud enim est quasi Fœdus amicitiæ; quod Deus immediatè iniit cum Adamo, ejusque posteris. Hoc vero est Fœdus reconciliationis; quod pepigit Deus cum electis in Christo ipsorum Mediatore & Sponsore: 2 Cor. 5. 18, 19. 1 Tim. 2. 5. Hebr. 7. 22.
units.tr: 1. The kind and manner of communion. The former is as it were a covenant of friendship, which God entered into immediately with Adam and his posterity. The latter is a covenant of reconciliation, which God made with the elect in Christ, their Mediator and Surety. 2 Cor. 5. 18, 19. 1 Tim. 2. 5. Heb. 7. 22.

units.la: 2. Respectu utriusque partis, & principii: Illud enim pro imperio suo, & sapienti consilio, Deus iniit cum Homine integro: Hoc vero ex mera Dei misericordia processit erga Hominem perditum, & in peccatis suis plane morruum: Rom. 5. 6, 8, 10. viij. 3.
units.tr: 2. With respect to each party and the principle. The former God entered into, by his sovereign will and wise counsel, with man in his integrity. The latter proceeded from the pure mercy of God toward lost man, who was utterly dead in his sins. Rom. 5. 6, 8, 10. 8. 3.

units.la: 3. Obiectorum latitudine: Illud ad omnes extenditur: Rom. 3. 19. Hoc proprie & interne ad electos restringitur. Vide sup. th. 6.
units.tr: 3. The breadth of its objects. The former extends to all. Rom. 3. 19. The latter is properly and inwardly restricted to the elect. See above, th. 6.

units.la: 4. Promissorum amplitudine: Illud Vitam tantum pollicetur: Hoc ipsam Justitiam, atque omnia ad Salutem necessaria: Rom. 1. 16, 17. 2 Petr. 1. 3.
units.tr: 4. The range of its promises. The former promises only life; the latter promises righteousness itself and everything necessary for salvation. Rom. 1. 16, 17. 2 Pet. 1. 3.

units.la: 5. Fundamento: quod illic fuit propria hominis facultas; hic Jesus Christus, ejusque satisfactio, & meritum, morte consummata: quapropter & hoc Testamentum dicitur; illud non item: Hebr. 9. 15,-18.
units.tr: 5. Foundation. The former had as its foundation man's own ability; the latter has Jesus Christ, his satisfaction and merit, consummated by death. For this reason the latter is also called a Testament, while the former is not. Heb. 9. 15-18.

units.la: 6. Effectis: Illud docet quid justum sit; Hoc ipsam justitiam in Christo monstrat, & confert per fidem. 1 Cor. 3. 6,-9. Jerem. 31. 33, 34. Rom. 8. 3, 4.
units.tr: 6. Effects. The former teaches what is just; the latter shows righteousness itself in Christ and confers it through faith. 1 Cor. 3. 6-9. Jer. 31. 33, 34. Rom. 8. 3, 4.

units.la: 7. Tempore: Illud ante lapsum est initum: Hoc post cum. Gen. 2. 17. iij. 15.
units.tr: 7. Time. The former was entered into before the fall; the latter after it. Gen. 2. 17. 3. 15.

units.la: 8. Cognitione : Illud per naturam innotescit; Rom. 1. 19, 20, 31. ij. 14, 15. Hoc non supernaturali revelatione : 1 Cor. 2. 7, -10. Eph. 3. 9, 10.
units.tr: 8. Knowledge. The former becomes known through nature. Rom. 1. 19, 20, 31. 2. 14, 15. The latter is known not through supernatural revelation. 1 Cor. 2. 7-10. Eph. 3. 9, 10.

units.la: 9. Duratione : Illud antiquatum est in electis efficaciter vocatis & justificatis; Hebr. 8, 8. 13. Hoc vero perpetuum est; Gen. 16. 7. Rom. xi. 29.
units.tr: 9. Duration. The former has been abolished in the elect who are effectually called and justified. Heb. 8. 8, 13. The latter, however, is perpetual. Gen. 16. 7. Rom. 11. 29.

units.la: XIII. Male Pontificii Euangelium cum Lege confundunt, statuentes Consilia quaedam Euangelica; atque item Socinian i, cum sequacibus, contendentes, Legem Moralem per Christum sub N. T. auctam esse & perfectiorem redditam. Vide sup. cap. 8. th. 32. & cap. 9. th. 18. Interim tenendum, quod Legi post lapsum, circa Foedus Euangelicum, usus sui ministeriales etiam conveniant: docet enim,
units.tr: XIII. The Papists wrongly confuse the Gospel with the Law, holding that there are certain evangelical counsels; likewise the Socinians and their followers contend that the moral law was enlarged and made more perfect through Christ under the New Testament. See above, chap. 8, th. 32, and chap. 9, th. 18. Meanwhile it must be held that the Law, after the fall, also agrees with the Gospel covenant in its ministerial uses. For it teaches:

units.la: 1. Quam perfecta, atque omnibus numeris absoluta requiratur justitia; hanc autem Euangelium in Christo monstrat. Rom. 3, 25, 28, 31. viij. 4, x. 4.
units.tr: 1. How perfect and in every respect complete the righteousness required is; and this righteousness the Gospel shows in Christ. Rom. 3. 25, 28, 31. 8. 4. 10. 4.

units.la: 2. Hominem facultatibus istis destitutum inopiae & injustitiae suae convincit: Euangelium vero Christum revelat, & hominem miseriae suae sibi conscium ad ipsum invitat; & sic illa quasi Paedagogus est ad Christum: Gal. 3. 24. Joh. 16. 9, 10.
units.tr: 2. It convinces man, who is destitute of those powers, of his poverty and unrighteousness. The Gospel, however, reveals Christ and invites to him the man who is conscious of his misery. In this way the Law is, as it were, a schoolmaster to Christ. Gal. 3. 24. John 16. 9, 10.

units.la: 3. Explicat modum gratitudinis ac novae obedientiae Deo praestandae; ad quam invitamur beneficiis Euangelio revelatis, sic in nos collatis; sublato tamen rigore foederali, & maledictionis aculeo, per gratiam Domini Jesu: Rom. 6. 11. vij. 22. xij. 1. xiij. 8. Jac. 1. 25. ij. 8, 12.
units.tr: 3. It sets out the manner of gratitude and of new obedience to be rendered to God, to which we are invited by the benefits revealed in the Gospel and so conferred upon us; the federal rigour and the sting of the curse, however, being removed through the grace of the Lord Jesus. Rom. 6. 11. 7. 22. 12. 1. 13. 8. James 1. 25. 2. 8, 12.

units.la: XIV. Testamenti appellatio de Foedere Euangelico recte etiam usurpatur; juxta locum Hebr. 9. 15, -22. quin & voces בְּרִית & διαθήκη isto significatu etiam occurrunt. Confer Exod. 24. 8. cum Hebr. 9. 20.
units.tr: XIV. The term Testament is also rightly applied to the Gospel covenant, according to the passage in Heb. 9. 15-22. Indeed the words [בְּרִית] and [διαθήκη] also occur in this sense. Compare Exod. 24. 8 with Heb. 9. 20.

units.la: Gal. 3.15. Consequenter Christus etiam Testator dicitur, quod Fœdus istud morte ipsius confirmatum fit: quemadmodum autem unus est Testator, & una ipsius Mors: sic unum re ipsa Testamentum: quod tamen ratione duplicis dispensationis in V. & N. T. dispesci solet.
units.tr: Gal. 3. 15. Consequently Christ too is called the Testator, because this covenant was confirmed by his death. But just as there is one Testator and one death of his, so there is in fact one Testament; which nevertheless is usually divided into Old and New Testament on account of the twofold dispensation.

units.la: Unum duntaxat re ipsa Testamentum esse, probamus primo: Quia una eademque Salus est fiue Hæreditas; cujus fideles tum V. tum N. T. facti sunt, & fiunt participes: quod paret, 1. ex promissione Divina Abrahamo proposita, Gen. 15.1. Ego clypeus sum tibi, merces tua ampla valde. xvij. 7. Ut fit Fœdus perpetuum. Me esse tibi Deum, & femini tuo post te. Consequenter ad Mosen, Exod. 3.6. Ego sum Deus patris tui, Deus Abrahami, Deus Ifaaci, Deus Jacobi. quod conserendum cum Pfal. 33.12. Beata gens illa, cujus Jehovah Deus est, --. Inde autem vitam æternam, & beatam resurrectionem, collegit Servator, Matth. 22.31,32. qui ipse iterum Matth. 8.11. Dico vobis, multos ab oriente & occidente venturos: & accubituros cum Abrahamo, Ifaaco, & Iacobo, in Regno cœlorum. Sic ad ejusdem Regni cœlestis hæreditatem, cum Patriarchis & fidelibus V. T. perveniunt; qui ex Gentilismo convertuntur sub N. juxta idem illud Fœdus perpetuum.
units.tr: We prove that there is in fact only one Testament, first, because there is one and the same salvation or inheritance, of which the faithful under both the Old and the New Testament have been and are made partakers. This appears, 1. from the divine promise made to Abraham, Gen. 15. 1: I am your shield, your reward exceedingly great. Chapter 17. 7, so that the covenant may be perpetual: I will be God to you and to your seed after you. Consequently to Moses, Exod. 3. 6: I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob. This is to be compared with Ps. 33. 12: Blessed is that nation whose God is Jehovah. From this the Saviour gathered eternal life and the blessed resurrection, Matt. 22. 31, 32. He himself says again, Matt. 8. 11: I say to you that many will come from east and west, and will recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven. Thus they attain, together with the patriarchs and the faithful of the Old Testament, the inheritance of that same heavenly kingdom; those who are converted from Gentilism under the New Testament do so according to that same perpetual covenant.

units.la: 2. Hebr. xi. 5. Per fidem Enoch fuit translatus: -testimonium obtinuerat, quod fuerit gratus Deo: & 6. --Nam qui accedit ad Deum, hunc credere oportet esse Deum, & præmia largiri iis, qui ipsum requirunt. Sic illo etiam tempore credebant fideles gratiosam Dei communionem, & præmii largitionem juxta Fœdus gratiæ. Similiter de Abrahamo, verf. 9. 10. ac porro de reliquis. verf. 13,-16. Secundum fidem mortui sunt isti omnes, &c. Adde verf. 26. & 35. & xij. 22, 23. Hierusalem cœlestis, spiritus justorum consummatorum.
units.tr: 2. Heb. 11. 5: By faith Enoch was translated; he had obtained the testimony that he was pleasing to God. And verse 6: For whoever comes to God must believe that he exists, and that he rewards those who seek him. Thus in that time too the faithful believed in gracious communion with God and in the bestowal of reward according to the covenant of grace. Similarly of Abraham, verses 9, 10, and then of the rest, verses 13-16: These all died according to faith, etc. Add verses 26 and 35, and 12. 22, 23: the heavenly Jerusalem, the spirits of the perfected righteous.

units.la: 3. Illustris est prophetia, Dan. 12. 2. Tandem multi ex dormientibus in pulverulenta terra, expergiscentur; hi ad vitam æternam, &c. Atque adeo Paulus, Act. 26. 6, 7. Ob spem promissionis factæ patribus nostris à Deo, ad quam promissionem duodecim tribus nostræ--sperant se deventuras, &c.
units.tr: 3. The prophecy in Dan. 12. 2 is clear: Many of those sleeping in the dusty earth shall awake; these to eternal life, etc. So too Paul, Acts 26. 6, 7: Because of the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers, to which promise our twelve tribes hope to attain, etc.

units.la: 4. Et eximia moribundi Patriarchæ confessio. Gen. 49. 18. Salutem tuam expecto, Jehovah. Atque item Jobi, 19. 25, 27. Equidem ego novi, Redemtorem meum vivere, &c. Adde Psal. 16. 5, 8, 9-11. xxxvj, 9, 10. lxxiij. 23, 26. Quin & Num. 23. 10.
units.tr: 4. And there is the remarkable confession of the dying patriarch, Gen. 49. 18: I wait for your salvation, Jehovah. Likewise that of Job, 19. 25, 27: For I know that my Redeemer lives, etc. Add Ps. 16. 5, 8, 9-11; 36. 9, 10; 73. 23, 26. Indeed also Num. 23. 10.

units.la: XV. Secundo, Quia Salus etiam fidelium V. T. pendebat à Morte ejusdem Testatoris, sive Satisfa- ctione & Merito Christi.
units.tr: XV. Secondly, because the salvation of the faithful of the Old Testament also depended on the death of the same Testator, that is, on the satisfaction and merit of Christ.

units.la: Unde 1. Hebr. 9. 15. quod ejus mors quoque intercessit ad redemtionem earum transgressionum; quæ fuerant sub priore pacto. Vide etiam 22, 23. Et 25, 26. Neque ut sæpe offerat seipsum, alioquin oportuisset Ipsum sæpe passum fuisse à jacto mundi fundamento, &c. Statim igitur à jacto mundi fundamento exeruit se virtus mortis Christi; qui unica sui oblatione consummavit in perpetuum eos, qui sanctificantur, x. 14.
units.tr: Hence, first, Heb. 9. 15: his death also intervened for the redemption of those transgressions which were under the first covenant. See also vv. 22, 23, and 25, 26. Nor was it that he should offer himself often; otherwise he would have had to suffer often since the foundation of the world, etc. Therefore, from the foundation of the world the power of Christ's death showed itself forth, he who by the one offering of himself has perfected for ever those who are sanctified, x. 14.

units.la: 2. Rom. 3. 25, 26. Quem præstituit Deus, ut esset placamentum per fidem in sanguine Ipsius; propter dissimulationem peccatorum quæ antecesserunt, Deo illa tolerante. Ad demonstrationem justitiæ suæ præsenti tempore: ut sit ipse justus, & justificans eum qui est ex fide Jesu. Scil. ante Christi adventum fuit dissimulatio & tolerantia quædam peccatorum, quasi per inducias: sic illis temporibus Deus pœnas pro peccatis fidelium V. T. justitiæ suæ satisfactorias, non exegit: sed earum exactionem distulit usque in tempus N. T. ubi Christus sanguine suo intercessit, & placationem sic peregit, ut justitia Dei sufficienter demonstrata sit, atque ita Deus justus declaratus; quod non remittat peccata, nisi virtute satisfactionis, à Christo suo temtempore præstitæ. Lex enim cassa non est reddita; sed stabilita; verf. 31.
units.tr: Second, Rom. 3. 25, 26: whom God set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, for the passing over of the sins that had been committed beforehand, God bearing with them, for the demonstration of his righteousness at the present time, that he might be just and the justifier of him who is of the faith of Jesus. That is, before Christ's coming there was a kind of passing over and forbearance of sins, as though by a truce. Thus in those times God did not exact penalties satisfying his justice for the sins of the faithful of the Old Testament, but deferred their exaction until the time of the New Testament, when Christ intervened with his blood and accomplished the propitiation in such a way that the justice of God was sufficiently demonstrated, and God was thus declared just, because he does not remit sins except by the power of the satisfaction rendered by Christ in his own time. For the law is not made void but established; v. 31.

units.la: 3. Act. 15. 11. Per gratiam Domini Jesu Christi, credimus NOS servatum iri, quemadmodum & ILLOS. Ubi per NOS, intelligendos esse non tantum Apostolos, sed etiam fideles N.T. per ILLOS autem, Patres & fideles V. T. ex versu præcedenti satis manifestum est. Quæstio enim instituta erat de Discipulis ex Gentilismo conversis: & palam asseritur, jugum Legis portari non potuisse, neque sic salutem acquiri. Idem ergo est modus salutis consequendæ per gratiam Domini Jesu Christi, tum sub V. tum sub N. T.
units.tr: Third, Acts 15. 11: through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we believe that we shall be saved, just as they. Here by "we" are to be understood not only the Apostles but also the faithful of the New Testament; by "they," the Fathers and the faithful of the Old Testament, as is sufficiently clear from the preceding verse. For the question had been raised about disciples converted from the Gentiles, and it is plainly asserted that the yoke of the Law could not be borne, nor salvation so obtained. The way of obtaining salvation through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ is therefore the same both under the Old and under the New Testament.

units.la: 4. Huc denique referri debet universalitas illa mortis Christi: quod pro omnibus mortem gustarit; Hebr. 2. 9. ubi tota electorum & salvandorum universitas intelligi debet. Omnes dicuntur peccasse, & justificari per redemtionem Christi; Rom. 3. 23, 24. ut hoc fit necessarium medium justificationis à peccatis. Per unum Christum, & ipsius obedientiam, justitia venit in omnes, (qui nempe justificantur, & ad Fœdus gratiæ pertinent:) quemadmodum per unum Adamum, ejusque transgressionem, condemnatio venit in omnes, (qui rei constituuntur, & ad Fœdus operum pertinebant): Rom. 5. 11, 12, 15, 17, 18, 19. 1 Cor. 15. 22, quin imo Joh. 14. 6. Nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per Christum. Act. 4. 12. Neque aliud nomen sub cælo datum est inter homines, per quod quis possit salvari. Similiter Apoc. 5. 8, 9. dicitur Christus redemisse nos Deo per sanguinem suum, ex omni tribu, & lingua, & populo, & natione. Adde Apoc. 13. 8. 1 Petr. 1. 19, 20. Quæ quidem omnia talia sunt, ut fideles V. T. omnino complectantur.
units.tr: Fourth, to this must finally be referred that universality of Christ's death, that he tasted death for all, Heb. 2. 9, where the whole multitude of the elect and those to be saved must be understood. All are said to have sinned and to be justified through the redemption of Christ, Rom. 3. 23, 24, so that this becomes the necessary means of justification from sins. Through the one Christ and his obedience, righteousness came upon all (namely those who are justified and belong to the covenant of grace), just as through the one Adam and his transgression condemnation came upon all (who are made guilty and belonged to the covenant of works): Rom. 5. 11, 12, 15, 17, 18, 19; 1 Cor. 15. 22. Indeed, John 14. 6: No one comes to the Father except through Christ. Acts 4. 12: Nor is there any other name under heaven given among men by which one may be saved. Similarly Apoc. 5. 8, 9 says that Christ redeemed us to God by his blood, out of every tribe, and tongue, and people, and nation. Add Apoc. 13. 8; 1 Pet. 1. 19, 20. All these things are such that they wholly embrace the faithful of the Old Testament.

units.la: XVI. Tertio, Quia eadem doctrina Testamentaria de Christo, ejusque justitia, etiam sub V. T. fuit propositæ: ejusque adventus in carnem, & reliqua istuc pertinentia, plurimis prophetiis fuerunt prædicta. dicta, variisque typis praefigurata: ut patet.
units.tr: XVI. Third, because the same testamentary doctrine concerning Christ and his righteousness was also proposed under the Old Testament; and his coming in the flesh and the other matters pertaining to it were foretold by very many prophecies and prefigured by various types, as is evident.

units.la: 1. In ipsa historia Euangelica: sic enim Servator noster, Luc. 24. 27. Exorsus a Mose et Prophetis, interpretabatur - in omnibus Scripturis, quae de Se scripta erant. Atque iterum verf. 44, 45, 46. unde frequens loquendi formula, Hoc autem factum est, ut implerentur Scripturae Prophetarum. Matth. 26. 56. & alibi passim. Confer Ioh. 1. 46. v. 39, 46.
units.tr: 1. In the Gospel history itself. For thus our Saviour, Luke 24. 27: "Beginning from Moses and the Prophets, he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures what was written concerning himself." And again vv. 44, 45, 46. Hence the frequent formula: "But this came to pass that the Scriptures of the Prophets might be fulfilled," Matt. 26. 56, and elsewhere passim. Compare John 1. 46; v. 39, 46.

units.la: 2. In Actis Apostolorum: utpote de Passionibus Christi; Act. 3. 18. Deus autem, quae pronunciaverat per os omnium Prophetarum suorum, Christum suum perpessurum, ita implevit. Atque amplius, verf. 21, 22-25. cum Deut. 18. 15, 18, 19. Moses etenim ad Patres dixit; Prophetam suscitabit vobis Dominus Deus vester ex fratribus vestris, sicut me, &c. Sed et omnes Prophetae a Samuele, et deinceps praenunciarunt dies istos. Adde Act. x. 43. xiij. 32, 33.
units.tr: 2. In the Acts of the Apostles, for example concerning the sufferings of Christ: Acts 3. 18, "But God, what he had foretold by the mouth of all his Prophets, that his Christ would suffer, thus fulfilled." And further vv. 21, 22-25, with Deut. 18. 15, 18, 19: "Moses indeed said to the fathers, The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet from your brothers, as he raised me up, etc. Yes, and all the Prophets from Samuel onwards have foretold these days." Add Acts 10. 43; 13. 32, 33.

units.la: 3. In Epistolis: sic Rom. 1. 1, 2, 3. Euangelium Dei, (quod ante promiserat, per Prophetas suos, in Scripturis sanctis.) De Filio suo, &c. Similiter iij. 21, 22. Iustitia Dei manifesta facta est, comprobata testimonio Legis, ac Prophetarum: justitia inquam Dei per fidem Iesu Christi in omnes, et super omnes, qui credunt. Nempe eadem doctrina de justificatione, idem justificandi modus, tum sub V.T. per Prophetas, tum sub N. per Apostolos & Euangelistas exhibitus est. His adde Gal. 3. 8, 9. cum Gen. 12, 3. xviij. 18. xxij, 18. ac porro Gal. 4. 21. et seqq. ubi explicatur, quomodo Foedus Euangelicum adumbratum fuerit in Isaaco, filio Abrahami, ex Sara ad libertatem & hereditatem natro. Ita Col. 2. 16, 17. cerimoniale discrimen cibi & potus, itemque respectus Novilunii, Festorum, & Sabbathorum, dicitur fuisse. Umbra rerum futurarum; Corpus vero Christi. Per Umbram igitur ad Corporis agnitionem, & fidem adduci debuerunt Foederati istius temporis. Illustria etiam hujus veritatis testimonia extant in Epist. ad Hebr. ubi cap. 1. 1. Multis modis, multisque vicibus, olim Deus locutus dicitur Patribus in Prophetis. Et iij, 5. Moses fidus in tota domo Dei, ut famulus, ad testificanda quae post erant dicenda. Adhaec viij, 5. de Sacerdotibus V. T. differte asseritur, quod exemplari et umbrae deservierint rerum coelestium. Conferx, 5,-10. cum Psal. 40. 7, 8, 9. & rursus 15, 16, 17. cum Ierem. 31, 31,-34. Adde 1 Petr. 1. 9,-12, 20. ij. 6; 22, 24. cum Isj. 28. 16. liij. 4, 9. &c.
units.tr: 3. In the Epistles: thus Rom. 1. 1, 2, 3, "the Gospel of God (which he had promised beforehand through his Prophets in the holy Scriptures) concerning his Son," etc. Similarly iii. 21, 22: "The righteousness of God has been made manifest, witnessed to by the Law and the Prophets: the righteousness, I say, of God through faith in Jesus Christ unto all, and upon all who believe." Namely, the same doctrine of justification and the same mode of justifying were set forth both under the Old Testament through the Prophets, and under the New through the Apostles and Evangelists. To these add Gal. 3. 8, 9 with Gen. 12. 3; 18. 18; 22. 18; and further Gal. 4. 21 ff., where it is explained how the Gospel covenant was foreshadowed in Isaac, son of Abraham, born of Sarah to liberty and inheritance. So Col. 2. 16, 17: the ceremonial distinction of food and drink, and likewise the regard for new moons, feasts and sabbaths, is said to be "a shadow of things to come, but the body is Christ." Through the shadow, therefore, the covenanted people of that time ought to have been led to the knowledge and faith of the body. Illustrious testimonies to this truth also exist in the Epistle to the Hebrews: at ch. 1. 1, God is said to have spoken "in many ways and in many portions of old to the fathers by the Prophets"; and at iii. 5, Moses was "faithful in all God's house, as a servant, to testify those things which were to be spoken afterwards." Further, at viii. 5, the priests of the Old Testament are said to have served "the copy and shadow of heavenly things." Compare x. 5-10 with Psalm 40. 7, 8, 9; and again 15, 16, 17 with Jer. 31. 31-34. Add 1 Pet. 1. 9-12, 20; ii. 6, 22, 24 with Isa. 28. 16; liii. 4, 9, etc.
