units.la: 4. Adjungi possunt insigniora quaedam loca V.T. utpote Gen. 3. 15. de Semine mulieris contrituro caput serpentis. XLIX. 10. de adventu ipsius Schilo. Num. 24. 17. de Stella ex Jacobo oritura, Sceptro ex Israële prodituro. & Dan. 9. 24. De adventu Messiae, de iniquitatibus expiandis, & aeterna justitia afferenda; & similia passim obvia. Item Hag. 2. 8, 9. Mal. 3. 1. iv, 2.
units.tr: 4. There can be added certain more notable passages of the Old Testament: for example Gen. 3. 15, concerning the Seed of the woman who shall bruise the serpent's head; xlix. 10, concerning the coming of Shiloh; Num. 24. 17, concerning the Star to rise out of Jacob and the Sceptre to arise out of Israel; and Dan. 9. 24, concerning the coming of the Messiah, to expiate iniquities and bring in everlasting righteousness; and similar passages met with everywhere. Likewise Hag. 2. 8, 9; Mal. 3. 1; iv. 2.

units.la: XVII. Quarto, Quia eadem fides justificans obtinuit sub V.T. quae nunc obtinet sub N. Hoc autem 1. ex superioribus facile deducitur: si enim eadem salus per eundem Servatorem, juxta idem Euangelium; consequenter eadem fides: unde & ista una dicitur, Eph. 4. 5. Confer Rom. x. 10,-.
units.tr: XVII. Fourth, because the same justifying faith obtained under the Old Testament that now obtains under the New. This follows, first, easily from what has been said above: for if the salvation is the same, through the same Saviour, according to the same Gospel, then consequently the faith is the same; whence it is also called one, Eph. 4. 5. Compare Rom. 10. 10 ff.

units.la: 2. Accedunt exempla fidelium V. T. iis qui sub N. vivunt, ad imitationem proposita: nominatim Abrahami, & Davidis. De Abrahamo quidem Rom. 4.
units.tr: 2. To these are added the examples of the faithful of the Old Testament, set forth for imitation to those who live under the New; namely those of Abraham and David. Of Abraham indeed, Rom. 4.

units.la: 3. Credidit Abraham Deo, et imputatum est ei ad justitiam. Ac deinde verf. 23, 24. Non scriptum est autem propter eum solum, quod, hoc imputatum fuerit ei. Sed etiam propter nos, quibus futurum est ut imputetur; iis nimirum qui credunt, &c. Similiter Gal. 3. 7. Noftis eos, qui ex fide sunt, esse filios Abrahami. & 9. Itaque qui ex fide sunt, benedicuntur cum fideli illo Abrahame: sic passim ejusdem fidei ad justitiam imputatio, atque eadem ex fide benedictio, & Abrahamo, & reliquis fidelibus N. T. differte assignatur.
units.tr: 3. "Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness." And then vv. 23, 24: "Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was reckoned to him; but also for us, to whom it shall be reckoned, namely those who believe," etc. Similarly Gal. 3. 7: "Know that those who are of faith are the sons of Abraham," and v. 9: "So then those who are of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham." Thus everywhere the imputation of the same faith unto righteousness, and the same blessing from faith, is assigned both to Abraham and to the other faithful of the New Testament.

units.la: De Davide autem Act. 2. 30. 31. Cum sciret-fore, ut ex fructu lumbi ipsius, quod ad carnem attinet, Christum illum suscitaret, quem collocaret super ejus thr ono, Praescius locutus est de resurrectione Christi--. Atque item Matth. 22. 43, 44. --Quomodo ergo David per Spiritum vocat eum Dominum, dicens (Psal. cx. 1.) Dixit Dominus Domino meo, &c. Sic ille per Spiritum praescivit, & credidit, futuram Christi ex familia sua nativitatem; mortem, resurrectionem, & dominium: imo Dominum suum dixit per Spiritum; a quo consequenter salutem & gloriam expectavit. Vide amplius Rom. 4. 6, 7, 8. cum Psal. 32. 2. & 2 Cor. 4. 13, 14. cum Psal. 116. 10.
units.tr: Of David, Acts 2:30–31 says: since he knew that God had sworn to him that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit upon his throne, he, foreseeing this, spoke of the resurrection of Christ. Likewise Matt. 22:43–44: How then does David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying (Ps. 110:1), The Lord said to my Lord, and so on. Thus he, by the Spirit, foresaw and believed that Christ would be born of his family, and that he would die, rise again and reign. Indeed, he called his Lord by the Spirit, and from him he consequently looked for salvation and glory. See further Rom. 4:6–8 with Ps. 32:2, and 2 Cor. 4:13–14 with Ps. 116:10.

units.la: 3. Item exempla aliorum, non tantum Prophetarum: 1 Petr. 1. 11. 12. sed fidelium quorumcunque: Matth. 13. 17. ut Abelis, Enochi, Noachi, & similium; de quibus fuse admodum, Hebr. xi. Pari ratione de Israelitis in deserto, testatur Apostolus 1 Cor. x. 3, 4. Omnes eandem escam spiritualem edisse, & omnes eundem potum spiritualem bibisse: bibebant enim ex sequente spirituali petra; petra vero illa erat Christus. Sic igitur, qui inter eos vere fideles fuerunt, eandem nobiscum spiritualem gratiam sacramentaliter obsignatam, fide perceperunt; & Messiam suo tempore venturum certo crediderunt: quod in reliquiis ipsorum circa adventum Christi, saeculo tam corrupto, manifestum est; nominatim in Simeone, qui expectabat consolationem Israel; Luc. 2. 25. In Anna Prophetissa; quae palam agnoscebat Dominum: & loquebatur de eo omnibus, qui redemptionem expectabant Hierosolymis, verf. 38. In Joseph o Arimathaeo; qui & ipse expectabat regnum Dei; Luc. 23. 51. In Samaritana; Joh. 4. 25. ejusque popularibus; verf. 29. &c.
units.tr: 3. Likewise, there are the examples of others, not only of the prophets (1 Pet. 1:11–12), but of all the faithful (Matt. 13:17), such as Abel, Enoch, Noah and others like them, of whom Hebrews 11 speaks at length. In the same way the Apostle, in 1 Cor. 10:3–4, testifies concerning the Israelites in the wilderness: They all ate the same spiritual food, and they all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and that rock was Christ. So, those who were truly faithful among them, by faith received the same spiritual grace, sealed to them sacramentally, as we do, and firmly believed that the Messiah would come in his time. This is evident in their remnant around the coming of Christ, in an age so corrupt: namely in Simeon, who was waiting for the consolation of Israel (Luke 2:25); in Anna the prophetess, who openly acknowledged the Lord and spoke of him to all who were looking for redemption in Jerusalem (v. 38); in Joseph of Arimathea, who himself was waiting for the kingdom of God (Luke 23:51); in the Samaritan woman (John 4:25), and in her fellow townspeople (v. 29), and so on.

units.la: 4. Consequenter Gentiles, qui olim fuerant absque Christo, abalienati a civili statu Israelis, & extranei quod ad pactorum promissiones attinet; - Eph. 2. 12. nunc in ejusdem Ecclesiæ Catholicæ communionem adoptati, atque unum facti sunt, soluto intergerini parictis septo; verf. 14. Vide etiam 16,19,-. Rom. xi. 17,-. Gal. 6. 16. iv,26. Hebr. 12.22,23.
units.tr: 4. Consequently, the Gentiles, who once were without Christ, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers to the covenants of promise (Eph. 2:12), are now adopted into the communion of the same Catholic Church, and have been made one, the dividing wall of partition having been broken down (v. 14). See also vv. 16, 19; Rom. 11:17; Gal. 6:16; 4:26; Heb. 12:22–23.

units.la: XVIII. Socinian, quibus hac in parte valde assines sunt Anabapt. & Remonstr. promissiones spirituales ac salutares, earumque agnitionem & fidem à V.T. prorsus removent; & non nisi bona corporalia & temporalia fidelibus istius œconomiæ proposita fuisse, existimant. Sed & Pontif. triplicem quandoque salutis viam recensent; 1. Legem naturæ, 2. Legem Mosis. & 3. Euangelium, five Gratiam. Idem viam Cœli sub V.T. clausam fuisse volunt; nec quenquam ingressum, ante mortem Christi. Sed perperam; ut probatum.
units.tr: XVIII. The Socinians, with whom the Anabaptists and Remonstrants are closely allied on this point, altogether remove from the Old Testament the spiritual and saving promises and the knowledge and faith of them, and they think that only good bodily and temporal things were set before the faithful of that dispensation. But the Papists also sometimes list three ways of salvation: (1) the law of nature; (2) the law of Moses; and (3) the Gospel, or grace. The same people want the way to heaven to have been closed under the Old Testament, and that no one entered it before the death of Christ. But this is wrong, as has been proved.

units.la: Obj. 1. Lex per Mosen data est: non gratia, quæ per Christum demum facta. Ergo. Joh. 1.17. Resp. Lex quidem sub V.T. rigide fuit inculcata: sed cum Morali obtinuit etiam Cerimonialis, quæ Christum adumbravit, & docuit convenienter isti œconomiæ. Sic per istam dispensationem, parcius quidem & obscurius promissiones Euangelicæ fuerunt propositæ: cum in N.T. Gratia & Veritas per Christum præstita sit: Gratia, oppositæ ad Fœdus Legale; Veritas, ad umbras futurorum bonorum. Sed idem tamen re ipsa fuit Fœdus Euangelicum; atque eadem beneficia salutaria jam tum secundum rem obtinuerunt.
units.tr: Objection 1. The law was given through Moses, not grace, which came through Christ at last. Therefore... (John 1:17). Answer. Indeed, under the Old Testament the law was rigorously inculcated, but along with the moral law there also held sway the ceremonial law, which foreshadowed Christ and taught what suited that dispensation. Thus, under that dispensation the evangelical promises were set forth more sparingly and obscurely, whereas in the New Testament grace and truth have come through Christ: grace as opposed to the legal covenant, truth as opposed to the shadows of good things to come. Yet it was in reality the same evangelical covenant, and the same saving benefits were already obtained in substance.

units.la: Obj. 2. Lex & Prophetæ usque ad Johannem: postea Regnum cœlorum annunciari cœpit: Matth. 11.12, 13. Resp. Tantisper obtinuit prædagogia Legis, cum typis & prophetiis de Christo venturo: sed Johannes eum præsentem demonstravit. Ac deinceps obtinuit Euangelium implerionis.
units.tr: Objection 2. The law and the prophets were until John; after that the kingdom of heaven began to be preached (Matt. 11:12–13). Answer. The pedagogy of the law held sway for a time, together with the types and prophecies of the Christ who was to come; but John pointed to him as already present. From then on the Gospel of fulfilment held sway.

units.la: Obj. 3. Nobis primum annunciata est ista salus, &c. Euangelium prius non prædicatum: Hebr. ij. 3. Eph. 3. 8,9. 2 Tim. 1. 10. 1 Petr. 1.11,12. Resp. Ista etiam accipienda sunt de Euangelio impletionis, oppositæ ad Euangelium promissionis; & de uberiori illius gratiâ.
units.tr: Objection 3. This salvation was first announced to us, etc.; the Gospel was not preached before (Heb. 2:3; Eph. 3:8–9; 2 Tim. 1:10; 1 Pet. 1:11–12). Answer. These passages too are to be understood of the Gospel of fulfilment, as opposed to the Gospel of promise, and of its fuller grace.

units.la: Obj. 4. Sub V. T. priore tabernaculo adhuc consistente, via ad ipsum cœleste Sacrarium nondum facta fuit manifesta; eo quod sacrificium ipsius Christi nondum fuerit peractum Hebr. 9. 8. Ergo. Resp. Ingressi tamen sunt fideles in Cœlum, per anticipationem, virtute ipsius Christi: cujus satisfactio & meritum per immutabilem decreti Divini certitudinem, valorem suum jam tum habuit in esse cognito; licet actu non præcesserit ipsum esse reale: quemadmodum in pactis bonæ fidei, similia passim obvia sunt.
units.tr: Objection 4. Under the Old Testament, while the earlier tabernacle still stood, the way into the heavenly sanctuary itself had not yet been made manifest, because the sacrifice of Christ himself had not yet been offered (Heb. 9:8). Therefore... Answer. Nevertheless, the faithful did enter heaven by anticipation, by the power of Christ himself. His satisfaction and merit already had their value in known being, on account of the unchangeable certainty of the divine decree, although the real being had not yet actually preceded; just as in contracts made in good faith, similar things are found everywhere.

units.la: XIX. In œconomia V. T. duæ potissimum illustriores periodi spectandæ veniunt: quarum prior est ab Adamo ad Mosen, posterior à Mose ad Christum. In universum œconomia ista fuit quasi infantilis, ac proinde quodammodo servilis; licet revera fideles etiam tunc liberi fuerint & hæredes: Gal. 4. 1, 2, 3. paulatim tamen adolevit, quasi infante ad annos pubertatis & sui juris accedente propius.
units.tr: XIX. In the economy of the Old Testament two principal and more notable periods are to be considered: the first is from Adam to Moses, the second from Moses to Christ. On the whole, that economy was, as it were, infantile, and therefore in some measure servile, although in truth the faithful even then were free and heirs (Gal. 4:1–3); yet it gradually matured, as an infant draws nearer to the years of puberty and to being of age.

units.la: Initio quidem obtinuit Ministerium extraordinarium, per Patriarchas; quos Sp. Sanctus extraordinariè afflavit, ac de fide & cultu Divino πολυμερῶς καὶ πολυτρόπως instruxit: Hebr. 1. 1. cum Num. 12. 6.
units.tr: At first, indeed, there held sway an extraordinary ministry through the patriarchs, whom the Holy Spirit inspired extraordinarily and instructed in faith and divine worship in many portions and in many ways [πολυμερῶς καὶ πολυτρόπως] (Heb. 1:1; compare Num. 12:6).

units.la: Ordinarium vero, ex illorum directione per ipsos Patres familias, & Primogenitos; qui sacra potissimum administrabant, dum fere erant Ecclesiolæ domesticæ.
units.tr: But the ordinary ministry came from their direction, through the heads of families themselves and the firstborn, who chiefly administered the sacred things, while the households were almost little domestic churches.

units.la: XX. Prima interim Euangelii prædicatio facta est ab ipso Deo, statim post lapsum in Paradiso; Gen. 3. 15, Semen mulieris conteret caput serpentis. Confer Apoc. 12. 7. Rom. 16. 20. Matth. 3. 7. 1 Joh. 3. 8. Hebr. 2. 14. Gal. 4. 4. Consequenter cœptum est invocari nomen Domini, fidelibus ad istiusmodi exercitia frequentius collectis Gen. 4. 26. atque distinctio facta inter filios Dei, & filios hominum, vj; 2. Sic exercita tunc fuit Vocatio, atque obtenta Justificatio, Adoptio, Sanctificatio; & expectata Glorificatio: quam insigniter confirmavit Enochi post exemplarem fidei, ac pietatis demonstrationem, in cœlum translatio: Gen. 5. 22,24. Hebr. xi. 5. Ac deinde etiam Arcæ structura, & Noachi cum familia per eam conservatio à diluvio; Hebr. xi, 7. 1 Petr. 3. 20, 21.
units.tr: XX. Meanwhile the first preaching of the Gospel was made by God himself, immediately after the fall in Paradise: Gen. 3:15, The seed of the woman shall crush the head of the serpent. Compare Rev. 12:7; Rom. 16:20; Matt. 3:7; 1 John 3:8; Heb. 2:14; Gal. 4:4. Consequently, men began to call upon the name of the Lord, as the faithful gathered more often for such exercises (Gen. 4:26), and a distinction was made between the sons of God and the sons of men (6:2). Thus there were then exercised calling, and justification, adoption, sanctification were obtained, and glorification was expected. This was remarkably confirmed by the translation of Enoch into heaven, after his exemplary demonstration of faith and piety (Gen. 5:22, 24; Heb. 11:5). And then also by the building of the ark and the preservation of Noah with his family through it from the flood (Heb. 11:7; 1 Pet. 3:20–21).

units.la: XXI. Quædam etiam instituta Cerimonialia jam tunc obtinuerunt: scil. Distinctio animalium mundorum & immundorum; Gen. 7. 1. quæ tum Sacrificiis inserviit, tum etiam Sanctificationem adumbravit.
units.tr: XXI. Certain ceremonial institutions also held sway even at that time, namely the distinction between clean and unclean animals (Gen. 7:1), which both served for sacrifices and also foreshadowed sanctification.

units.la: Jus primogenituræ, cui annexa Sacrorum cura; Gen. 4.7. xxv. 31,-34. xxvij, 36. cum Exod. 4. 22. 23.
units.tr: The right of the firstborn, to which the care of sacred things was attached (Gen. 4:7; 25:31–34; 27:36; compare Exod. 4:22–23).

units.la: Item Decimæ Deo dicatæ; Gen. 14. 20. cum Hebr. 7. 4, 5.
units.tr: Likewise tithes dedicated to God (Gen. 14:20; compare Heb. 7:4–5).

units.la: Atque ipsum quoque Sacerdotium, aliquamdiu ante Leviticum. Sic Gen. 14. 18. commemoratur Melchizedek. Rex Schalemi, sacerdos Deo fortí excelso: unde ordo Melchizedeki. Psal. 110. 4.
units.tr: And the priesthood itself, for some time before the Levitical priesthood. Thus Gen. 14:18 mentions Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, whence the order of Melchizedek (Ps. 110:4).

units.la: Sacrificia etiam recensentur: utpote Caini de frugibus terræ, & Abelis, de primogenitis, & eximiis pecudum suarum: Gen. 4. 3, 4, 5. Hebr. xi. 4. Atque item Noachi statim post diluvium; qui Gen. 8. 20. exstructo Jehovæ altari, ex omnibus pecudibus & volucribus mundis holocausta obtulit; & odoratus est Jehovah odorem illum gratum. Quod conferendum cum Eph. 5. 2. Christus dilexit nos, & tradidit semet ipsum pro nobis, oblationem ac victimam Deo, in odorem bonæ fragrantiæ. Similiter Abrahamus in peregrinationibus suis Altaria passim exstruxit; Gen. 12. 7, 8; xiij, 14, 18. Memorabile autem præ cæteris fuit Sacrificium filii ejus unici Isaaci, Divinitus mandatum ab ipso inchoatum, sed ariete vicario consummatum, xxij 1,-14. Deinde Isaacus quoque Altare legitur exstruxisse; xxvj, 25. quemadmodum & Jac, 32,20. Atque item J.
units.tr: Sacrifices are also recorded: such as that of Cain from the fruits of the earth, and that of Abel from the firstborn and choicest of his flocks (Gen. 4:3–5; Heb. 11:4). Likewise that of Noah immediately after the flood, who, having built an altar to the LORD, offered burnt offerings from every clean animal and bird; and the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma (Gen. 8:20–21). This should be compared with Eph. 5:2: Christ loved us and gave himself up for us, an offering and sacrifice to God, a fragrant aroma. Similarly, Abraham in his wanderings built altars everywhere (Gen. 12:7–8; 13:4, 18). Most memorable of all was the sacrifice of his only son Isaac, commanded by God and begun by him, but completed with a substitute ram (Gen. 22:1–14). Then Isaac too is read to have built an altar (Gen. 26:25), as also Jacob (Gen. 33:20). Likewise...

units.la: F f Job in terra Hutzi, qui filios suos post eorum convivia sanctificavit, ac pro numero eorum Holocausta obtulit; Job. 1. 5. Et postea ipse Deus ad Eliphazum Themaniten. cap. 42. 7, 8. Accensa est ira mea in te, & in duos amicos tuos. Quamobrem nunc sumite vobis septem juvencos, septemque arietes, & adite servum meum Iobum; ut offerendum curetis holocaustum pro vobis; & servus meus Job oret pro vobis, ut non afficiam vos poena flagitii, &c. Sic Deus offensus, sed idem placabilis, placari voluit sacrificio precibus comitato; atque hoc medium satisfactionis & reconciliationis typicæ, intercedere ad eorum liberationem à poenâ.
units.tr: Job in the land of Uz, who sanctified his sons after their feasts and offered burnt offerings according to their number; Job 1:5. Afterwards God himself spoke to Eliphaz the Temanite: My anger is kindled against you and against your two friends. Therefore now take for yourselves seven young bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and have a burnt offering offered for yourselves; and my servant Job shall pray for you, so that I do not visit you with punishment for your folly, etc. Thus God was offended, yet the same God was willing to be appeased by a sacrifice accompanied by prayers; and this means of satisfaction and typical reconciliation was intercession for their deliverance from punishment.

units.la: Sacramenta hujus Fœderis ordinaria ab initio non comparent. De Arca Noachi, & conservatione per eam à diluvio, dictum th. 20. Ipsa interim Sacrificia, quatenus communionem cum Altari inferebant, ipsique offerentes pariter coram Domino convivium sacrum celebrabant, aliquid sacramentale involvebant:
units.tr: The ordinary sacraments of this covenant do not appear from the beginning. The ark of Noah, and preservation through it from the flood, were spoken of in thesis 20. Meanwhile the sacrifices themselves, insofar as they brought communion with the altar, and the offerers likewise celebrated a holy meal before the Lord, involved something sacramental:

units.la: 1 Cor. x. 18. Exod. 18. 12. Sic enim communionem gratiosi istius Fœderis obsignabant.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 10:18. Exod. 18:12. For in this way they sealed the communion of this gracious covenant.

units.la: XXII. Tempore autem Abrahami insigniora quædam accesserunt: specialis scil. ipsius Abrahami Vocatio; Gen. 12. 1, 2, 3, 7. Fœderis Evangelici renovatio; xv. 1, 5, &c. Promissio terræ Canaan; quæ cœlestis patriæ typus fuit; xvij, 8. atque item Seminis benedicti; verf. 16. 19, 21. addito insuper Sacramento Circumcisionis: verf. 10, 14.
units.tr: XXII. In the time of Abraham, however, some more notable things were added: namely, Abraham's own special calling; Gen. 12:1, 2, 3, 7. The renewal of the Gospel covenant; ch. 15:1, 5, etc. The promise of the land of Canaan, which was a type of the heavenly fatherland; 17:8. And likewise of the blessed Seed; vv. 16, 19, 21. With the sacrament of circumcision added besides: vv. 10, 14.

units.la: Deinde Electio in personis Isaaci & Jacobi, dilectis præ Ismaële & Esavo, fuit repræsentata: Rom. 9. 11, 12, 13. Salutis impetratio & applicatio, in Benedictione Abrahami per Melchizedekum Sacerdotem & Regem; Gen. 14. 18, 19, 20. Hebr. 7. 1, 10. & promissione Seminis benedicti, atque item terræ Canaan, aliquoties iterata. Justificatio per expressum Dei testimonium; Gen. 15. 6. Rom. 4. 3, 10. 11, 12. Adoptio per distinctionem Filiorum promissionis ex matre libera: & Hæreditatis assignationem ad eos; Gal. 4. 22, 26, 28, 30, 31. Sanctificatio etiam per Circumcisionem; Deut. 30. 6. Col. 2, 11. Ac denique Glorificatio per Benedictiones ac Promissiones terræ Canaan; Hebr. xi. 9, 10, 13. -22.
units.tr: Then election was represented in the persons of Isaac and Jacob, loved above Ishmael and Esau: Rom. 9:11, 12, 13. The obtaining and application of salvation, in the blessing of Abraham through Melchizedek, priest and king; Gen. 14:18, 19, 20. Heb. 7:1, 10. And in the promise of the blessed Seed, and likewise of the land of Canaan, repeated several times. Justification through the express testimony of God; Gen. 15:6. Rom. 4:3, 10, 11, 12. Adoption through the distinction of the children of promise from the free mother, and the assignment of the inheritance to them; Gal. 4:22, 26, 28, 30, 31. Sanctification also through circumcision; Deut. 30:6. Col. 2:11. And finally glorification through the blessings and promises of the land of Canaan; Heb. 11:9, 10, 13–22.

units.la: XXIII. Altera periodus, à Mose ad Christum, conditionibus hujus Fœderis scripto consignatis, cultu magis ordinato, novisque tum extraordinariis, tum ordinariis additamentis, multo fuit illustrior.
units.tr: XXIII. The second period, from Moses to Christ, when the conditions of this covenant were committed to writing, worship was more ordered, and new additions, both extraordinary and ordinary, were made, was much more illustrious.

units.la: Extraordinarie quidem Salutis impetratio & applicatio adumbrata fuit per Liberationem Israelitarum ex Ægypto, factam ministerio Mosis, qui hac potissimum in parte typus Christi fuit: Act. 7. 35, 36. Hebr. 3. 2, -6, xi, 28. ac porro per Introductionem in terram Canaan, duce Josua, altero Christi typo: Hebr. 4. 8. xj, 16. tum etiam per Transitum maris rubri, quo salvi iter ingressi sunt Canaan versus, hostibus ipsorum extinctis: 1 Cor. 10, 2. iremque per Nubem, qua adversus externas injurias tegebantur, lucemque & refectionem ac directionem habebant, tum interdiu, tum noctu: 1 Cor. x, 1. Exod. 13, 21. Psal. 105, 39. nec non per Manna cœlitus datum, & Aquam e rupe, quæ sacramentaliter fuit Christus, in perpetuum nutrimentum: 1 Cor. x. 3, 4. Joh. 6. 32, 33. ac denique per æneum Serpentem, cujus aspectu, à serpentibus ignitis letharliter vulnerati & infecti, curabantur; Joh. 3. 14. viij. , 18. xij, 32, 33.
units.tr: Extraordinarily, indeed, the obtaining and application of salvation was foreshadowed through the liberation of the Israelites from Egypt, effected by the ministry of Moses, who in this part especially was a type of Christ: Acts 7:35, 36. Heb. 3:2–6; 11:28. Further, through the introduction into the land of Canaan under Joshua, another type of Christ: Heb. 4:8; 11:16. Also through the passage of the Red Sea, by which they went safely on their way toward Canaan, their enemies being destroyed: 1 Cor. 10:2. And through the cloud, by which they were covered against external injuries and had light, refreshment and direction, both by day and by night: 1 Cor. 10:1. Exod. 13:21. Ps. 105:39. Nor less through the manna given from heaven, and the water from the rock, which sacramentally was Christ, as perpetual nourishment: 1 Cor. 10:3, 4. John 6:32, 33. And finally through the bronze serpent, by whose sight those wounded and infected by fiery serpents were healed unto death; John 3:14; 8:28; 12:32, 33.

units.la: Ordinarie per Sacerdotes, & eminentiore quodam modo per Pontificem maximum, Sacrificia expiatoria, & Altaria, aliaque instrumenta, in istum usum destinata: Hebr. 5. 1. x. -1, -xiij, 8, 9, 10; Justificatio specialius per Sacrificia ad remissionem peccatorum ordinata, variaque ablutiones, & sacramentum Paschatis: Hebr. 9, 13, 14, 22, 23. 1 Cor. 5. 7. Adoptio per Primogenitos Deo sacros: Exod. 13. 11, -16. Rom. xj; 16Sanctificatio per instituta illa, quæ munditiem spestabant: Hebr. 9.13, 14. Glorificatio denique, per Hæreditatem terræ Canaan; & specialia quædam Symbola gratiosæ præsentiæ Divinæ, Tabernaculum videl. (cui postea Templum successit, atque inprimis Sanctum sanctorum: Hebr. xi. 13, 14, 16. ix, 2, 3, 9, 11, 12. 1 Reg. 8. 21, 29, 30, 42, 43.
units.tr: Ordinarily, through the priests, and in a more eminent manner through the high priest, expiatory sacrifices, altars, and other instruments destined for this use: Heb. 5:1; 10:1; 13:8, 9, 10. Justification more specifically through the sacrifices ordained for the remission of sins, and various ablutions and the sacrament of the Passover: Heb. 9:13, 14, 22, 23. 1 Cor. 5:7. Adoption through the firstborn consecrated to God: Exod. 13:11–16. Rom. 11:16. Sanctification through those institutions which pertained to cleansing: Heb. 9:13, 14. Finally glorification, through the inheritance of the land of Canaan; and certain special symbols of the gracious presence of God, namely the Tabernacle (to which the Temple later succeeded, and especially the Holy of Holies): Heb. 11:13, 14, 16; 9:2, 3, 9, 11, 12. 1 Kings 8:21, 29, 30, 42, 43.

units.la: XXIV. Sed propius in ista periodo spectemus, 1. Personas, 2. Res & agenda, 3. Loca, 4. Tempora.
units.tr: XXIV. But let us look more closely at this period, 1. at the persons, 2. at the matters and duties, 3. at the places, 4. at the times.

units.la: Personæ occurrunt, tum Sacrorum administræ, tum aliter Sacræ & Mundæ.
units.tr: The persons appear both as ministers of the sacred rites and as otherwise holy and clean.

units.la: Ministri extraordinarii erant Prophetæ, viri ex quacunque tribu promiscuè à Deo excitati, ad cultum ipsius instituendum, eundemve collapsum restaurandum, ad explicanda arcana, prædicenda futura, & nominatim de Messia, ejusque adventu, officiis, beneficiis, &c. ac proinde Christum summum illum Prophetam quodammodo præfigurantes: Deut. 18. 15, -19. Act. 3. 22, 23, 24. x. 43. 1 Petr. 1. 10, 11, 12: 2. I. 19, 20, 21.
units.tr: The extraordinary ministers were the prophets, men raised up by God indiscriminately from any tribe, to establish his worship or to restore it when it had fallen, to explain hidden things, to foretell the future, and especially concerning the Messiah, his coming, offices, benefits, etc.; and thus in some measure foreshadowing Christ, the supreme Prophet: Deut. 18:15–19. Acts 3:22, 23, 24; 10:43. 1 Pet. 1:10, 11, 12. 2 Pet. 1:19, 20, 21.

units.la: Munus autem Propheticum, cum extraordinarium esset, ipsum quoque Sacerdotium eminenter in se comprehendebat: Levit. 7. 15, -. 1 Reg. 18. 31, -.
units.tr: The prophetic office, since it was extraordinary, also eminently comprehended the priesthood itself: Lev. 7:15. 1 Kings 18:31.

units.la: Ordinarii erant Sacerdotes, ac suo etiam modo reliqui Levitæ; quorum illi perpetua successionis linea ex Aharonis familia defumti, ad Sacerdotium in Tabernaculo, ac deinde in Templo obeundum applicati: Exod. 28. 1. xxix. 44. Num. 18. 1, 7. xxv. 13. populo docendo, sacrificiis offerendis, benedictioni, alijsque agendis sacris, ordinarie operam dabant. Mal. 2. 7. Num. 6. 22, -. Et sic Christum Sacerdotem verè consummatissimum, omnis benedictionis auctorem, eundemque Doctorem summum, præfigurabant: Hebr. 7. 11, -; 23, 24, 25. iij. 1. Eph. 1. 3.
units.tr: The ordinary ministers were the priests, and in their own way the rest of the Levites. The priests, taken from the family of Aaron in a perpetual line of succession and assigned to serve the priesthood in the Tabernacle and then in the Temple, ordinarily labored at teaching the people, offering sacrifices, blessing, and performing other sacred duties: Exod. 28:1; 29:44. Num. 18:1, 7; 25:13. Mal. 2:7. Num. 6:22. And so they foreshadowed Christ, the truly most complete Priest, the author of every blessing, and likewise the supreme Teacher: Heb. 7:11; 7:23, 24, 25; 3:1. Eph. 1:3.

units.la: Hi, primogenitorum loco adhibiti, Sacerdotibus præsto erant: Num. 3. 9, 12, 13. vij. 13, -19. xviij. 6. Tabernaculumque cum ejus instrumentis custodiebant ac deportabant: iv. 3, 5, -15. &c.
units.tr: These, employed in place of the firstborn, stood ready to serve the priests: Num. 3:9, 12, 13; 7:13–19; 18:6. They also guarded and carried the Tabernacle with its instruments: 4:3, 5–15, etc.

units.la: XXV. Sacerdotes autem esse debuerunt personæ ab omni corporis vitio prorsus immunes, & ad functionem istiusmodi habiles. Levit. 21. 17,-24.
units.tr: XXV. The priests, however, had to be persons entirely free from every bodily defect and fit for such a function: Lev. 21:17–24.

units.la: Consecratio eorum fiebat coram tota Ecclesia: Levit. 8. 3. adhibita Lotione: Exod. 29, 4. Amictu sacro Tunica sc. cum Baltheo, Tiara, & Femoralibus: Exod. 28. 4, 40, 42, 43. xxix. 8, 9. Sacrificiis specialibus, cum applicatione sanguinis ex ariete ad auriculam infimam, & pollices dextros: Exod. 29. 15; 20, 24, 25, Accedebat conspersio ex oleo sacro, & sanguine de altari, in ipsos, & vestes ipsorum: 21. Levit. 8. 30. Iisdem assignati erant Cibi sancti: Levit. 22, 2, 3, 10, 11, atque insuper mandata specialis abstinentia, mundities & gravitas: xxi, 1,-9. Ut videl. absolutissima Christi perfectio & sanctitas, nec non salutis per eum impetratio & applicatio, adumbraretur: Hebr. 7. 26, 27, &c.
units.tr: Their consecration took place before the whole Church: Lev. 8:3, with washing: Exod. 29:4; with sacred vestments, namely the tunic with girdle, the turban, and the linen breeches: Exod. 28:4, 40, 42, 43; 29:8, 9; with special sacrifices, and the application of blood from the ram to the lower part of the ear and the right thumbs: Exod. 29:15, 20, 24, 25. To this was added a sprinkling of holy oil and blood from the altar upon them and their garments: 21. Lev. 8:30. To the same were assigned holy foods: Lev. 22:2, 3, 10, 11; and besides, a command of special abstinence, cleanness and gravity: 21:1–9. So that the most complete perfection and holiness of Christ, and the obtaining and application of salvation through him, might be foreshadowed: Heb. 7:26, 27, etc.

units.la: XXVI. In Sacerdotibus unus erat Summus, ab Aharone successionis vicissitudine descendens, cui peculiaris cultus, & observatio anniversaria in Sancto Sanctorum competebat; unde & illustrior Christi typus fuit. Levit. 16, 2. &c. xxi. 12. Hebr. 7.23, ix. 6. 7. &c.
units.tr: XXVI. Among the priests there was one high priest, descending from Aaron by the order of succession, to whom belonged the special worship and the annual observance in the Holy of Holies; whence he was also a more illustrious type of Christ: Lev. 16:2, etc.; 21:12. Heb. 7:23; 9:6, 7, etc.

units.la: Notandus etiam peculiaris ejus Ornatus: quo dignitatem Christi eminentissimam præfigurabat. Primarium ejus ornamentum fuit Amiculum, & Pectorale, cum nominibus duodecim tribuum in gemmis; Exod. 28. 2,-. Ita Christus coram Patre Ecclesiam repræsentat. In hoc latebant Urim & Thummim. verf. 39. ex quibus responsa dabantur; & quæ Christum designabant, Verbum & Interpretem Patris.
units.tr: His distinctive adornment is also to be noted, by which he foreshadowed the most eminent dignity of Christ. Its chief ornament was the ephod and the breastplate, with the names of the twelve tribes set in gems: Exod. 28:2, etc. Thus Christ represents the Church before the Father. Within this were hidden the Urim and Thummim, v. 39, by which answers were given; and which designated Christ, the Word and Interpreter of the Father.

units.la: Caput illius exornabat Cidaris, cum Lamina aurea: verf. 36. 37. 38. Summam Christi dignitatem designans.
units.tr: The head was adorned with a cidaris (turban) with a golden plate: Exod. 28, 36, 37, 38, signifying the supreme dignity of Christ.

units.la: Unctio ejus peculiaris quoque fuit; oleum scil. tum in Tabernaculum, & quæ in eo erant, tum in caput summi Sacerdotis, effundebatur: Levit. 8. 10, 11, 12. Sic plenitudo Spiritus, sanctitatis, omniumque donorum in Christo, Ecclesiam perfundit, & perficit: Psal. 2. 6. xlv, 8. cxxxiij, 2, 3. Joh. 1. 16. Col. 2. 3, 9, 10.
units.tr: Its anointing was also special: oil was poured out both upon the Tabernacle and the things in it, and upon the head of the high priest: Lev. 8, 10, 11, 12. So the fullness of the Spirit, of holiness, and of all gifts in Christ floods and perfects the Church: Ps. 2, 6; 45, 8; 133, 2, 3; John 1, 16; Col. 2, 3, 9, 10.

units.la: Specialis etiam in illo requirebatur mundities & gravitas: Levit. 21. 10, 11, 12. &c.
units.tr: A special purity and dignity was also required in him: Lev. 21, 10, 11, 12, etc.

units.la: XXVII.
units.tr: XXVII.

units.la: Affinis erat Summus Israelitarum Senatus, ex Sacerdotibus Leviticis, constituto etiam supremo Judice in ista Θεοκρατία, ad arduas lites & controversias dirimendas: Deut. 17. 8, 9, 12. Confer
units.tr: Akin to this was the supreme senate of the Israelites, made up of Levitical priests. In that theocracy a supreme judge was also appointed to settle difficult lawsuits and controversies: Deut. 17, 8, 9, 12. Compare

units.la: 2 Chron. 19. 8, 9. Sic Christus Regale habet Sacerdotium: Zach. 6. 11, &c. xij, 7, 10.
units.tr: 2 Chron. 19, 8, 9. So Christ has a royal priesthood: Zech. 6, 11, etc.; 12, 7, 10.

units.la: Personae aliter Sacrae erant Nazirei, qui se peculiari voto ad tempus segregabant, & sanctificabant Deo, juxta ipsius institutum: Num. 6. 2, &seqq. Consequenter typi erant singularis sanctimoniae Christi. Extraordinarium exemplum nativi Nazirei occurrit in Simsone; Jud. 13. 5. cui non absimile videtur, quod exstat de Johanne Baptista: Luc. 1, 15.
units.tr: Other persons were consecrated in a different way: the Nazirites, who by a special vow set themselves apart for a time and sanctified themselves to God, according to his own institution: Num. 6, 2 ff. Consequently they were types of the singular holiness of Christ. An extraordinary example of a Nazirite from birth occurs in Samson: Judg. 13, 5. Not unlike this is what is related of John the Baptist: Luke 1, 15.

units.la: Occurrunt denique Mundi; immunes a qualicunque cerimoniali immunditia: eaque vel communi; qua quis immundus erat usque ad vesperam; tunc autem lotis vestibus purgabatur: Levit xj. 24, 25. &c. vel speciali; quae quidem gravior inducebatur ex contactu cadaveris humani, ossium, aut sepulchrorum: Num. 19. 16. itemque ex gonorrhaea: Levit. 15. & partu recens edito: cap. 12. Sed gravissima, oriebatur ex Lepra: cap. xiij, xiv. De modis purgationum vide ibid. Hac interim ratione omnis nostra spiritualis immundities, in Christo unice expianda, & remedium nativae nostrae corruptionis in ipso solo quaerendum, significabatur: Tit. 2. 12, 14. Psal. 51, 7.
units.tr: Finally there were the unclean, those immune from any ceremonial impurity. This was either the common uncleanness, by which a person was unclean until evening and was then cleansed by washing his clothes: Lev. 11, 24, 25, etc.; or a special uncleanness, which was incurred more gravely by contact with a human corpse, bones or graves: Num. 19, 16; likewise by gonorrhoea: Lev. 15; and by childbirth: ch. 12. But the most grievous arose from leprosy: chs. 13, 14. On the modes of purification see ibid. In this way was signified that all our spiritual impurity is to be expiated uniquely in Christ, and that the remedy for our native corruption is to be sought in him alone: Titus 2, 12, 14; Ps. 51, 7.

units.la: XXVIII.
units.tr: XXVIII.

units.la: Sequuntur Res & agenda sacra: in quibus spectandum primo Sacrificium, quod erat Res sacra ab offerente adducta, & a Sacerdote, ritu sacro supra altari Deo oblata. Eratque vel Expiatorium, vel Eucharisticum.
units.tr: There follow the sacred things and sacred acts, in which we should consider first the sacrifice. This was a sacred thing brought by the offerer and offered upon the altar to God by the priest with sacred rite. It was either expiatory or eucharistic.

units.la: Expiatorium ad carnalem peccatorum expiationem in foro illo civili erat ordinatum: Hebr. 9. 13. Levit. v. 5, 13. Atque interim remissionem peccatorum in foro poli adumbrabat: Hebr. 9. 14, 15, 23. Eratque vel pro omnibus peccatis; ut Holocaustum, quod totius victimæ combustione peragebatur: Levit. 1, 3, 13. vj, 9, 10, 11. vel pro certis tantum: iisque rursum vel ex errore, vel ex infirmitate commissis: iv, v, vj. Sic Christus pro omnibus & singulis electorum peccatis, tum maximis, tum minoribus, se obtulit: Hebr. 9. 14. x, 5, 10, 14. Jef. 53. 11, 12.
units.tr: The expiatory sacrifice was ordained for the carnal expiation of sins in that civil court: Heb. 9, 13; Lev. 5, 5, 13. Meanwhile it foreshadowed the remission of sins in the heavenly court: Heb. 9, 14, 15, 23. It was offered either for all sins, as the burnt offering, which was accomplished by the burning of the whole victim: Lev. 1, 3, 13; 6, 9, 10, 11; or only for certain sins, and these again committed either through error or through weakness: chs. 4, 5, 6. So Christ offered himself for all and each of the sins of the elect, both the greatest and the least: Heb. 9, 14; 10, 5, 10, 14; Isa. 53, 11, 12.

units.la: Eucharisticum, ad gratitudinem coram Deo in Christo testificandam, ordinatum erat: ubi Christus, ejusque satisfactio & meritum eâdem operâ præfigurari debuit: Exod. 24. 5. Levit. 3. 1, &c. Sic interim nos ipsos, & omnia nostra, grato animo ipsi Deo debemus offerre: Hos. 14. 3. Hebr. 13. 15.
units.tr: The eucharistic sacrifice was ordained to bear witness to gratitude before God in Christ. Here Christ, and his satisfaction and merit, ought to have been foreshadowed at the same time: Exod. 24, 5; Lev. 3, 1, etc. Thus we ourselves, and all that is ours, ought to offer ourselves to God with a grateful heart: Hos. 14, 3; Heb. 13, 15.

units.la: Illud autem peragebatur, aut solis Muneribus; aut adhibitis etiam Animalibus: quorum prius Libatio dicebatur; ubi cibus, potus, sal, thus, oleum, &c. offerebantur: posterius iterum aut Pinguedinis tantum victimarum incensione; & Hostia pacificorum appellabatur: aut Animalium quoque mactatione, cum Libatione, expediebatur; & Sacrificium laudis dicebatur.
units.tr: This was done either with the offerings alone, or with animals also added. The former was called a libation, when food, drink, salt, incense, oil, etc. were offered. The latter was again performed either by burning only the fat of the victims, and was called a peace offering; or with the slaughter of animals as well as the libation, and was called a sacrifice of praise.

units.la: Consecrationi Sacrificiorum in universum, præter ipsum Altare, de quo Exod. 29. 37. Matth. 23. 19. serviebant quoque Ignis, & Sal: Marc. 9. 49. Levit. 11. 13. Ignis Spiritum Sanctum adumbravit: Matth. 3. 11. Act. 2. 3. per quem Christus se ipsum obtulit inculpatum Deo: Hebr. 9. 14. ac simul passiones iræ Divinæ, quas Mediator pro nobis tulit: Marc. 9. 43, 44. Jef. 53. 4, 5, 10. Omnis etiam oblatio Sale Fœderis debuit saliri, ad significandum Fœdus Dei salutare & perpetuum: in quo fideles confirmati & corroboratæ roborati, pacem Dei omnibus aliis rebus anteponunt, certoque conservantur ex omnibus periculis & difficultatibus: Marc. 9. 47, 49, 50.
units.tr: In general, besides the altar itself (of which Exod. 29, 37; Matt. 23, 19), fire and salt also served the consecration of the sacrifices: Mark 9, 49; Lev. 11, 13. Fire foreshadowed the Holy Spirit: Matt. 3, 11; Acts 2, 3, through whom Christ offered himself without blemish to God: Heb. 9, 14; and at the same time the sufferings of the divine wrath which the Mediator bore for us: Mark 9, 43, 44; Isa. 53, 4, 5, 10. Every offering also had to be salted with the salt of the covenant, to signify God's saving and perpetual covenant. In it the faithful, confirmed and strengthened, place the peace of God above all other things and are surely preserved from all dangers and difficulties: Mark 9, 47, 49, 50.

units.la: XXIX. Secundo, Suffitus Sacer de cujus confectione vide Exod. 30. 34, 35. Ejus erat, ut Sacerdos ex eo contunderet minutatim, poneret super Thymiaterium, & adoleret suffitum unoquoque mane ac vespere coram Iehova: verf. 46: Addita lege, ne quis similem suffitum in usum privatum sibi pararet, è populo caeteroquin exscindendus: verf. 37, 38. Sic Intercessio Christi; & fervidae fidelium preces in ipsius nomine, adumbrabantur: Pfal. 141. 2. Apoc. 5. 8. a quibus procul abesse debet profanitas: Eccles. 5. 1. Pfal. 50. 15, 16.
units.tr: XXIX. Second, there was the holy incense, concerning whose preparation see Exod. 30, 34, 35. The priest was to pound it finely, place it upon the censer, and burn it every morning and evening before Jehovah: verse 46. A law was added that no one should prepare a similar incense for private use, on pain of being cut off from the people: verses 37, 38. So the intercession of Christ and the fervent prayers of the faithful in his name were foreshadowed: Ps. 141, 2; Rev. 5, 8. Profanity must be kept far from these: Eccles. 5, 1; Ps. 50, 15, 16.

units.la: Tertio Oleum Sacrum, cujus usus erat ad Tabernaculum integrum, cum vasis, & instrumentis suis omnibus, ipsoque ejus atrio, omnes item personas in illo ministrantes, earumque vestes, ungendas & consecrandas, Exod. 30. 25, 30: addita simili lege ut in Suffitu, & pari sanctione comminatoria: verf. 31, 32, 33. Hoc pacto figurabantur praestantissima Sp. Sancti dona, quibus Christus in humana sua natura, & singuli fideles, atque omnia ad ipsos pertinentia, Deo sanctificantur in honorem: Hebr. 1, 9. 1 Joh. 2. 20, 27. simulque docebatur, Sanctum canibus non dandum: Matth. 7. 6.
units.tr: Third, the holy oil, whose use was to anoint and consecrate the whole Tabernacle with its vessels and all its instruments, its very court, likewise all the persons ministering in it and their garments: Exod. 30, 25, 30. A similar law was added as with the incense, with an equal threat of punishment: verses 31, 32, 33. In this way were foreshadowed the most excellent gifts of the Holy Spirit, by which Christ in his human nature, and each of the faithful, and all things pertaining to them, are sanctified to God for his honour: Heb. 1, 9; 1 John 2, 20, 27. At the same time it was taught that what is holy is not to be given to dogs: Matt. 7, 6.

units.la: Quarto, Aqua expiationis erat, qua separati ex immunditia purgabantur carnaliter. Num. 19. 9. Ita sanguis Christi nos purgat ab omni peccato:
units.tr: Fourth, there was the water of expiation, by which those separated from uncleanness were cleansed in the flesh: Num. 19, 9. So the blood of Christ cleanses us from all sin:

units.la: 1 Joh. 1, 7. atque omni immunditia spirituali, Zach. 13. 1.
units.tr: 1 John 1, 7; and from all spiritual uncleanness: Zech. 13, 1.

units.la: XXX. Quinto, Lucernae Sacrae septem erant in Candelabro aureo, instruendae quovis mane oleo olivarum extuso puro; & accendendae singulis vesperis, ut per noctem essent luminaria in atrio conventus Exod. 25. 31, 37. xxvij, 20, 21. Levit. 24. 2, 3, 4.
units.tr: XXX. Fifth, there were seven holy lamps on the golden candlestick, to be furnished every morning with pure beaten olive oil and lit every evening, so that there might be lights through the night in the court of the congregation: Exod. 25, 31, 37; 27, 20, 21; Lev. 24, 2, 3, 4.

units.la: Sic illuminatio per Verbum & Spiritum figurabatur:
units.tr: So illumination through the Word and the Spirit was foreshadowed:

units.la: Sexto, Tubæ erant duæ argenteæ, opere continente factæ, ut Sacerdotes earum clangore cœtum convocarent, lætitiam celebrarent, vel etiam profectionem castrorum imperarent. Num. 10. 2. Sic clangor Verbi Spiritu comitati, ejusque virtus in colligenda Ecclesia, lætis annunciandis, peccatis arguendis, & fidelibus ad spiritualem pugnam incitandis, adumbrabatur: Jes. 58. 1. Eph. 6. 11, -18. Psal. 89. 16.
units.tr: Sixth, there were two silver trumpets, made of beaten work, so that the priests might call the assembly with their clangour, celebrate joy, or even command the departure of the camp: Num. 10, 2. So the clangour of the Word, accompanied by the Spirit and its power, was foreshadowed in gathering the Church, in announcing joyful tidings, in convicting of sins, and in stirring the faithful to spiritual battle: Isa. 58, 1; Eph. 6, 11–18; Ps. 89, 16.

units.la: Septimo, Cibifacri ex præscripto ipsius Dei Sacerdotibus fuere destinati; sanctissimi quidem maribus eorum solis comedendi permittebantur in atrio conventus; alii etiam familiis eorum. Sanctissimæ erant reliquiæ ex Sacrificiis pro peccato, quorum sanguis non portabatur in Sanctuarium; atque ex muneribus eorum. Levit. 7. 6, 7, 9, 10, vj. 16,-18, 25, 26; viij. 31, 32. similiter illis dati erant Panes propositionis. xxiiij. 5, 9. Hac ratione figurabatur virtus Christi conservatrix & nutrix vitæ spiritualis in electis. Prov. 9. 2, 5. Psal. 23. 1, 5. Iob. 6. 33, 35, 48, 50, 51.
units.tr: Seventh, holy food was assigned to the priests by the prescription of God himself. The most holy portions could be eaten by their males alone, in the court of the congregation; others also by their families. The most holy were the remains of the sin offerings, whose blood was not carried into the sanctuary, and of their gifts: Lev. 7, 6, 7, 9, 10; 6, 16–18, 25, 26; 8, 31, 32. Likewise the bread of the Presence was given to them: Lev. 24, 5, 9. In this way was foreshadowed the power of Christ, which preserves and nourishes spiritual life in the elect: Prov. 9, 2, 5; Ps. 23, 1, 5; John 6, 33, 35, 48, 50, 51.

units.la: XXXI. Succedunt quædam secundario in rebus sacris spectanda; ut pote primo Novalia:
units.tr: XXXI. Certain things are to be regarded as subsidiary in sacred matters; first, the first-fruits of new plantings:

units.la: nam cujusque arboris ab Israelitis plantatæ in Canaan, fructus esculenti, postquam tribus annis habiti essent præputiati, in cibum non assumendi, quarto anno separabantur, ut essent res sanctæ laudationum Jehovæ; & quinto demum anno ab Israelitis percipiebantur: Levit 19. 23,-25. Hoc pacto significatum fuit, omnia alimenta nobis quidem per peccatum immunda; sed per fidem in Christum, precibus & gratiarum actionibus, sanctificari: Tit. 1, 15. 1 Tim 4. 4, 5. Rom. 14. 6. 1 Cor. 10. 31.
units.tr: For the fruit of every tree that the Israelites planted in Canaan was, for three years, regarded as uncircumcised and not to be taken as food; in the fourth year it was set apart as holy, for the praises of Jehovah; and only in the fifth year was it taken into use by the Israelites: Levit. 19. 23–25. By this arrangement it was signified that all foods are indeed unclean for us through sin, but are sanctified through faith in Christ, by prayers and thanksgivings: Tit. 1. 15. 1 Tim. 4. 4, 5. Rom. 14. 6. 1 Cor. 10. 31.

units.la: Secundo Primitiæ, quæ erant primi proventus, tum rerum, tum personarum, Deo sacri: Exod. 13. 2, 13. xxij. 29, 30. Num. 15. 20, 21. Sic optima quæque Deo, ejusque cultui, sunt consecranda: Isf. 66. 20, 21. 1 Cor. 6. 19, 20. Interim Christus omnium creaturarum primogenitus, in quo nos etiam sanctificamur, fuit adumbratus: Col. 1. 15. Hebr. 1. 2, ij. 10, 11.
units.tr: Second, the first-fruits, which were the first yield both of things and of persons, were holy to God: Exod. 13. 2, 13. xxij. 29, 30. Num. 15. 20, 21. So too, all the best things are to be dedicated to God and to his worship: Isa. 66. 20, 21. 1 Cor. 6. 19, 20. Meanwhile Christ, the firstborn of all creatures, in whom we too are sanctified, was foreshadowed: Col. 1. 15. Heb. 1. 2, 2. 10, 11.

units.la: Tertio, Decimæ quoque possessionum ac proventuum Deo, ejusque cultui, offerebantur, in sustentationem Levitarum, pauperum, &c. Gen. 14. 20. Levit 27. 30. Deut. 26. 12, &c. Sic ex omnibus, quæ nobis suppetunt, in similes usus pios erogandum pro re nata, quantum necessitas postulat, & facultates nostræ ferunt: Gal. 6. 6, 9. Jac. 2. 13, 15. 16. Hebr. 13. 16.
units.tr: Third, tithes of possessions and produce were also offered to God and to his worship, for the support of the Levites, the poor, and so on: Gen. 14. 20. Lev. 27. 30. Deut. 26. 12, etc. So too, from all that is at our disposal, we ought to spend as much as necessity requires and our means allow, for similar pious uses as occasion arises: Gal. 6. 6, 9. Jas. 2. 13, 15, 16. Heb. 13. 16.

units.la: Quarto denique Vota, quibus Deo liberi ad cultum suum promittebantur & dicabantur personæ, vel res: Levit 27. 2, &c. seqq. Exemplum personæ Deo dicatæ, vide 1 Sam. 1. 11, 22. &c. Sed frequenter in votis redemptio habebat locum, suspensa tamen æstimatione Sacerdotis: Levit. 27. 25. Sed חרם, quod speciali modo ex personis, aut rebus quibuscunque, Deo devotum erat, usibus humanis sic eximebatur, ut vendi aut redimi non posset: Num. 21, 2,
units.tr: Fourth and last, there were vows, by which persons or things were promised and dedicated freely to God for his worship: Lev. 27. 2, etc., following. For an example of a person dedicated to God, see 1 Sam. 1. 11, 22, etc. But in vows redemption frequently had a place, though the valuation was reserved to the priest: Lev. 27. 25. But the herem [חרם], which was devoted to God in a special way, whether persons or things of any kind, was exempted from human use in such a way that it could be neither sold nor redeemed: Num. 21. 2, 3. Josh. 6. 17, 18. 1 Sam. 15. 3.

units.la: 3. Ios. 6. 17, 18. 1 Sam. 15. 3. Sic in usus Ecclesiasticos, aliosque pios, liberaliter conferendum est ex iis, quæ largitus est Deus: 1 Cor 9. 7, 11, 13, 14. xvj. 2. Gal. 6. 6, 10. Hebr. 13. 16. Nec quæ sic donata sunt, injuste vel fraudulenter aliorsum interverti debent: Matth. 22. 21. Rom. 2. 22. Act. 5. 1-11.
units.tr: So too, from what God has bestowed, we ought to give liberally to ecclesiastical uses and other pious purposes: 1 Cor. 9. 7, 11, 13, 14. 16. 2. Gal. 6. 6, 10. Heb. 13. 16. Nor should things so given be diverted to other purposes unjustly or fraudulently: Matt. 22. 21. Rom. 2. 22. Acts 5. 1-11.

units.la: XXXII. Agendum porro de Locis sacris. De his generatim vide Exod. 20. 24. Levit. 17. 2, 9. Deut. 12. 5.xiv. 23. Speciatim vero jussu Dei, ad peragendum cultum sacrum, destinatum fuit primo Tabernaculum, ac deinde Templum. Tabernaculum, pro ratione peregrinantium in deserto, mobile quidem & terrestre Sanctuarium fuit; sed tum conditionem peregrinantis in hisce terris Ecclesiæ; tum immobile, & cœleste illud Sanctuarium præfiguravit: Exod. 25. 8, . Hebr. 9. 1, &c.
units.tr: XXXII. Next we must treat of the sacred places. On these in general see Exod. 20. 24. Lev. 17. 2, 9. Deut. 12. 5, 14. 23. In particular, by God's command, the tabernacle and then the temple were appointed for the performance of sacred worship. The tabernacle, suited to the condition of a people wandering in the desert, was indeed a movable and earthly sanctuary; but it foreshadowed both the condition of the Church as a pilgrim in this world and that immovable and heavenly sanctuary: Exod. 25. 8, Heb. 9. 1, etc.

units.la: Duæ vero partes continentes in eo potissimum spectandæ: Tegumentum videl. & Tabulatum. Tegumentum externum erat, & quidem triplex; sed ordinatum ad interna tegenda & protegenda: Exod. 26. 14. xxvij. 9. Sic Deus Ecclesiam suam, & singula ejus membra, protegit perpetuo: Isa 4. 5, 6. Psal. 27. 5.
units.tr: Two parts that contain are to be noted in it especially: namely the covering and the boarding. The external covering was threefold, and it was arranged to cover and protect the inner parts: Exod. 26. 14; 27. 9. So God continually protects his Church and each of its members: Isa. 4. 5, 6. Ps. 27. 5.

units.la: Tabulatum constabat Asseribus & Transtillis, cum suis Stylobatis & Annulis: Exod. 26. 15, . Artificiosa Tabernaculi coagmentatio Ecclesiam figurabat, per commissuras & compages suas congruenter unitam cum Christo capite suo per Spiritum intus agente: Eph. 4. 12, 13, 15. 16. iij. 16.
units.tr: The boarding consisted of boards and bars, with their sockets and rings: Exod. 26. 15, etc. The skilful joining of the tabernacle foreshadowed the Church, fittingly united through its joints and fastenings with Christ its head, who works within it through the Spirit: Eph. 4. 12, 13, 15, 16; 3. 16.

units.la: XXXIII. Tabernaculum bipertitum erat, in Sanctum Sanctorum, & Sanctum, intercedente Velo: Exod. 26. 33. Hebr. 9. 2, 3.
units.tr: XXXIII. The tabernacle was divided into two parts, the Holy of Holies and the Holy Place, with the veil lying between them: Exod. 26. 33. Heb. 9. 2, 3.

units.la: Velum opere artificiosissimo confectum, & Cherubinis erat refertum, atque ex quatuor columnis ligneis, sed auro obductis, suspensum: Exod 26. 31,-33. Sic Christus, cui inserviunt exercitus Angelici, majestatem suam vere Divinam humana carne quasi operiens, ad Deum & Cœlum viam nobis paravit: Hebr. 10. 19,-22. cum Isa. 6. 2, 3. Joh. 1. 52. Hebr. 1, 6, 14.
units.tr: The veil, made with the most skilful work and embroidered with cherubim, was hung from four wooden pillars, though overlaid with gold: Exod. 26. 31-33. So Christ, whom the armies of angels serve, veiling his truly divine majesty as it were in human flesh, prepared for us a way to God and heaven: Heb. 10. 19-22, with Isa. 6. 2, 3. John 1. 51. Heb. 1. 6, 14.

units.la: Sanctum Sanctorum erat intra Velum, quo summus Sacerdos semel quotannis ingrediebatur Exod. 26. 33, 34. Hebr. 9. 3, 7. Hoc ipsum Cœlum figurabat, in quod Christus nostro bono semel ingressus est: verf. 11, 12 ; 24, 25. Erat autem in eo Arca fœderis, cui intus impositæ erant Tabulæ legis: Exod. 25. 16. Hebr. 9. 4. immisso superne Operculo propitiatorio: Exod. 25. 17. Sic Christus maledictionem Legis à fidelibus avertit, & jus Legis pro iis ipse adimplevit: Rom. 3. 25. viij, 3, 4.
units.tr: The Holy of Holies lay within the veil, into which the high priest entered once a year: Exod. 26. 33, 34. Heb. 9. 3, 7. This itself foreshadowed heaven, into which Christ entered once for our good: vers. 11, 12, 24, 25. In it was the Ark of the covenant, in which the tables of the law were placed: Exod. 25. 16. Heb. 9. 4; with the mercy seat put on top: Exod. 25. 17. So Christ turns away the curse of the Law from the faithful, and fulfilled the right of the Law on their behalf: Rom. 3. 25; 8. 3, 4.

units.la: 4. In extremitatibus Operculi erant duo Cherubim: Exod. 25 18, 20. e quorum medio Deus Mosen alloquebatur: verf. 22. Num. 7. 89. Sic Deus in Christo, & per ipsum, suos docet ac regit: Pfal 80. 2. xcix, 1.
units.tr: 4. At the ends of the mercy seat were two cherubim: Exod. 25. 18, 20, from between whom God spoke to Moses: vers. 22. Num. 7. 89. So God, in Christ and through him, teaches and rules his people: Ps. 80. 2; 99. 1.

units.la: Eodem pertinebat Thuribulum aureum, inserviens suffitui istic faciendo ad Propitiatorium: Hebr. 9. 4. Levit. 16. 12, 13. Sic intercessio Christi in coelis, & nostrae preces in ejus nomine, figurabantur: Apoc. 8. 3,-5. Ad Arcam porro collocata fuit Urna aurea, mannam in se occultam habens; atque insuper virga Aaronis, quae germinaverat: Hebr. 9. 4. Exod 16. 33, 34. Sic Christus suos spiritualiter & efficaciter alit ac regit: Apoc 2. 17. Col. 3. 1, 2, 3. 1 Cor. 10. 3.
units.tr: To the same place belonged the golden censer, serving to make the incense there before the mercy seat: Heb. 9. 4. Lev. 16. 12, 13. So the intercession of Christ in heaven, and our prayers in his name, were foreshadowed: Rev. 8. 3-5. Moreover, beside the ark was placed the golden urn, holding the manna hidden within it; and besides, Aaron's rod, which had budded: Heb. 9. 4. Exod. 16. 33, 34. So Christ spiritually and effectively nourishes and rules his people: Rev. 2. 17. Col. 3. 1, 2, 3. 1 Cor. 10. 3.

units.la: Sanctum erat ante Velum; ubi Sacerdotes ordinarie sacra peragebant: Hebr. 9. 2. Hoc Christi humanitatem adumbrabat; ac porro Ecclesiam mysticam; verf. 11,-. Erat in eo Altare suffitus, e lignis Sittim, ex cujus angulis prominebant cornua auro puro obducta; Exod 30. 1, 2, 3. in quibus semel quotannis facienda erat expiatio, per sanguinem sacrificii pro peccato in die solennis expiationis: verf. 10. Sic Christus gloriosissime pro nobis comparet coram Patre, atque intercedit, virtutem sanguinis atque oblationis suae repraesentans: Hebr. 9. 24, &c. x, 14. Atque item Mensa e lignis Sittim, auro etiam obducta; cum vasis aureis, & duodecim scutulis, &c. quibus imponebantur Panes propositionis. Exod. 25. 23, 29, 30. Actandem Lychnuchus aureus: verf. 31, 37. Sic docebatur, Christum, suis cibum & lucem esse, ad vitam aeternam: Pfal. 23. 1, &c.
units.tr: The Holy Place lay before the veil, where the priests ordinarily performed the sacred rites: Heb. 9. 2. This foreshadowed the humanity of Christ, and further the mystical Church: vers. 11, etc. In it was the altar of incense, made of acacia wood, from whose corners horns projected, overlaid with pure gold: Exod. 30. 1, 2, 3. On these, once a year, atonement was to be made, by the blood of the sin offering on the day of the solemn atonement: vers. 10. So Christ most gloriously appears before the Father for us, and intercedes, representing the power of his blood and his offering: Heb. 9. 24, etc.; 10. 14. Likewise there was the table of acacia wood, also overlaid with gold, with the golden vessels and twelve dishes, etc., on which the bread of the Presence was placed: Exod. 25. 23, 29, 30. Finally, the golden lampstand: vers. 31, 37. So it was taught that Christ is food and light for his people, unto eternal life: Ps. 23. 1, etc.

units.la: XXXIV. Erat insuper Atrium, ipsum Tabernaculum ambiens; atque omnibus patens: Exod. 27. 9, &c. Sic notabatur externae & visibilis Ecclesiae conditio: Pfal. 55. 15. Apoc. 11. 1, 2. In eo stabat ante portam Tabernaculi Altare holocaustorum, e lignis Sittim consectum, sed aere circumquaque obductum: Exod. 27. 1. 2. 27. 1, 2. Sic Christi humanitas per Deitatem sustentata est, & digna effecta ad peragendam nostri cum Deo reconciliationem: Hebr. 5. 8, 9. & sic ipse praedicatur in Ecclesia visibili: Tit. 2. 11, 12. Ac porro Labrum æneum; purgandis Sacerdotibus, Tabernaculum administrandum ingressuris, destinatum: Exod. 30. 18, 21. Sic non nisi sanguine & Spiritu Christi a peccatis abluti, ad Deum recte appropinquare possumus: Hebr. 10. 22. 1 Joh. 1. 6, 7.
units.tr: XXXIV. There was moreover the court, surrounding the tabernacle itself and open to all: Exod. 27. 9, etc. So the condition of the external and visible Church was marked: Ps. 55. 15. Rev. 11. 1, 2. In it, standing before the door of the tabernacle, was the altar of burnt offerings, made of acacia wood but covered with bronze all round: Exod. 27. 1, 2; 27. 1, 2. So the humanity of Christ, sustained by the Deity, was made worthy to accomplish our reconciliation with God: Heb. 5. 8, 9; and so he is proclaimed in the visible Church: Tit. 2. 11, 12. Further, the bronze laver, appointed for cleansing the priests who were to enter to minister in the tabernacle: Exod. 30. 18, 21. So we can draw near to God rightly only when cleansed from sins by the blood and Spirit of Christ: Heb. 10. 22. 1 John 1. 6, 7.

units.la: XXXV. Succedit Templum; in quod ipsum Ta- bernaculum, post varias de loco in locum transporta- tionis, cum Arca, tandem fuit illatum: 1 Reg. 8. 4. 2 Chron. 5. 5.
units.tr: XXXV. Next comes the Temple. After various transfers of the Tabernacle from place to place, it was at last brought into it together with the Ark: 1 Kings 8:4; 2 Chronicles 5:5.

units.la: Templum illud a Salomone Rege pacifico, Hierosolymis in monte Moria, ubi fuerat area Ornanis Jebusæi, fuit exstructum: 2 Chron. 36. 14. 1, xxj, 22, 26, 28. xxij, 1. De hujus figura & fabrica, atque instrumentis, vide 1 Reg. vi. & vij. 2 Chron. iij. & iv. Hoc interim tenendum, quod Templum illud, & loci stabilitate, & ornatuum amplitudine, longe magnificentius fuerit Tabernaculo. Sic spirituale Ecclesiæ incrementum, plenitudo item & stabilitas, ac denque præstantia bonorum spiritualium in Christo, propius fuit adumbrata.
units.tr: That Temple was built in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite had been, by Solomon the peaceable king: 2 Chronicles 36:14; 1 Chronicles 21:22, 26, 28; 22:1. For its form, construction and furnishings, see 1 Kings 6 and 7, and 2 Chronicles 3 and 4. We should hold this in mind: that Temple, both in the stability of its site and in the grandeur of its adornments, was far more magnificent than the Tabernacle. In this way the spiritual growth of the Church, its fullness and stability, and finally the excellence of the spiritual goods in Christ, were more closely foreshadowed.

units.la: Veruntamen ad imperfectionem istius œconomiæ demonstrandam, Templum illud aliquoties expilatum; 1 Reg. 14. 25. 2 Chron. 24. 7. & profanatum; 2 Chron 33. 4, 5, 7. tandem a Chaldæis eversum; Esr. 5. 12. & igne combustum est; 2 Reg. 25. 9. Post reditu tamen è captivitate Babylonica, Templum ex mandato Cyri denuo ædificatum; 2 Chron. 36. 22, 23. Esr. 1. 2, 3. iij. 2, 3. Sed structura ejus per malevolos primum impedita; iv. sub Dario & Artaxerxe deinceps continuata; vj. 1, 6, 15. tandem fuit consummata; ibid. Sic nimirum Ecclesia per Euangelium erat restauranda: Zach. 6. 12, 13.
units.tr: Yet, to show the imperfection of that economy, that Temple was several times plundered (1 Kings 14:25; 2 Chronicles 12:9; 2 Chronicles 24:7) and defiled (2 Chronicles 33:4, 5, 7), and at last was overthrown by the Chaldeans (Ezra 5:12) and burned with fire (2 Kings 25:9). After the return from the Babylonian captivity, however, the Temple was rebuilt by the command of Cyrus (2 Chronicles 36:22, 23; Ezra 1:2, 3; 3:2, 3). But its construction was first hindered by malicious men (Ezra 4), and afterwards, under Darius and Artaxerxes, it was carried on (Ezra 6:1, 6, 15), and at last it was completed (ibid.). Thus, of course, the Church was to be restored through the Gospel: Zechariah 6:12, 13.

units.la: Stante Templo secundo Christus opus redemtionis nis nostræ peragere debuit:Hag. 2. 8,-10. Sed posteaquam illud ab Antiocho Epiphane profanatum: Dan. 8, 11, &c. xj, 31. a Juda Maccabæo repurgatum; 1 Macc. 4. 43,- ab Herode Magno splendide restauratum fuit; tandem, juxta prophetiam Dan. 9. 26. & ipsius Christi prædictionen, Matth. 23. 38. xxIv, 2. à Tito Vespasiano penitus eversum est absque ulla spe restaurationis. Sic umbra cessavit, exhibito corpore: Iob. 1. 17. Col 2. 17. Hebr. 10. 1, 2.
units.tr: While the second Temple stood, Christ was to accomplish the work of our redemption (Haggai 2:8–10). But after it had been defiled by Antiochus Epiphanes (Daniel 8:11, etc.; 11:31), and cleansed again by Judas Maccabeus (1 Maccabees 4:43), and magnificently restored by Herod the Great, at last, according to the prophecy of Daniel 9:26 and the prediction of Christ himself (Matthew 23:38; 24:2), it was utterly overthrown by Titus Vespasian, with no hope of restoration. Thus the shadow ceased when the body was presented: John 1:17; Colossians 2:17; Hebrews 10:1, 2.

units.la: XXXVI. Supersunt Tempora sacra, cultui œconomico V. T. specialiter dicata: horum quædam recurrebant quotannis, five aliquoties, five semel: quædam non nisi plurium annorum lapsu.
units.tr: XXXVI. There remain the sacred times, specially dedicated to the economic worship of the Old Testament. Some of these recurred every year, or several times, or once; others only after the passing of several years.

units.la: Aliquoties quotannis recurrebant primo Dies: Singulis enim diebus sua stata erant sacra: Juge scil. sacrificium agni anniculi in holocaustum, cum munere suo, tum mane tum iterum vesperi offerendum; iisdemque temporibus suffitus in Thymiaterio faciendus erat: Num. 28. 2,-8. xxIx, 38,-42. xxx, 7, 8, 26. Sic jugis noster cultus Deo præstandus & acceptus est in Christo: Rom. 12. 1.
units.tr: Some recurred several times each year. First, the days: for each day had its own stated sacred rites, namely the continual sacrifice of a yearling lamb as a burnt offering, with its meal offering, to be offered both in the morning and again in the evening; and at the same times incense was to be burned on the altar of incense (Numbers 28:2–8; 29:38–42; 30:7, 8, 26). In this way our continual worship is rendered to God and accepted in Christ: Romans 12:1.

units.la: Secundo Sabbathum sub V. T. hebdomadatim sanƈta quiete erat transigendum, & quidem ipso die a creatione septimo, duplicato tunc jugi sacrificio: Num. 28. 9, 10. Ita quò magis cultui Divino vacamus, eo debemus reconciliationem Christi meditari ardentius.
units.tr: Second, the Sabbath, which under the Old Testament was to be spent in holy rest each week, on the seventh day itself from the creation, the continual sacrifice being then doubled (Numbers 28:9, 10). So the more we give ourselves to the worship of God, the more earnestly we ought to meditate on the reconciliation effected by Christ.

units.la: Tertio Kalendæ, seu Neomeniæ; quæ erant principia Mensium, cum denuo conspiceretur Luna post sui cum Sole conjunctionem. De speciali cultu tunc præscripto, vide Num. 28. 11,-15. Sic omnes menses & tempestates, per Christum nobis sanctificantur.
units.tr: Third, the Kalends, or New Moons, which were the beginnings of the months, when the moon was again seen after its conjunction with the sun. For the special worship prescribed at that time, see Numbers 28:11–15. In this way all months and seasons are sanctified to us through Christ.

units.la: XXXVII. Semel quotannis recurrebant Festa: eaque vel magis, vel minus solennia; atque item so- lennis dies expiationis. Festa magisolennia erant, primo
units.tr: XXXVII. Festivals recurred once a year, some more solemn and some less so; likewise the solemn Day of Atonement. The more solemn festivals were, first,

units.la: Festum Paschatis; quod celebrandum erat mense pri-mo moanni sacri, qui nostro Martio potissimum respondet: atque huc pertinuit esus Agni paschalis, & Panum azymorum, atque item Dies Convocationis. Agnus paschalis die decimo quarto, qui erat plenilunii, inter duas vespȩras debuit jugulari; integer ad ignem assari;à personis mundis cum azymis & amaris herbis comedi; reliquiis, si quæ superessent in matutinum sequens, igne combustis: Exod. 12. 2,-6, 8, 9. 10, 46. Num. 9. 1,-5. Sic commemorabatur egressus ex Ægypto; & fides eadem opera dirigebatur in Christum, Agnum inculpatum: 1 Petr. 1, 19. tollentem peccata mundi: Iob. 1. 29. cujus morte redemti è servitute spirituali in cœlestem hæreditatem traducimur. Panes azymi, quibus per septem dies vescendum fuit, remoto ipso primo die omni è domibus fermento, Exod. 12. 15. indicabant, ab omni perversæ doctrinæ & iniquitatis fermento abstinendum accurate: 1 Cor. 5. 6, 8. Per dies autem Convocationis, qui erant primus, & septimus, sive ultimus Paschatis, quibus nullum opus, præter ciborum præparationem, permissum fuit: Exod. 12. 16. indigitabatur omnimoda, per initium & finem, totius vitæ nostræ Deo consecratio: 1 Cor. 5. 7.
units.tr: the Feast of the Passover, which was to be celebrated in the first month of the sacred year, which corresponds chiefly to our March. To this belonged the eating of the paschal lamb and of the unleavened bread, as well as the Day of Assembly. The paschal lamb, on the fourteenth day, which was the day of the full moon, was to be slain between the two evenings; it was to be roasted whole over the fire; it was to be eaten by clean persons with unleavened bread and bitter herbs; and whatever remained until the next morning was to be burned with fire (Exodus 12:2–6, 8, 9, 10, 46; Numbers 9:1–5). In this way the departure from Egypt was commemorated, and faith was at the same time directed to Christ, the spotless Lamb (1 Peter 1:19), who takes away the sin of the world (John 1:29), by whose death we, redeemed from spiritual bondage, are brought into the heavenly inheritance. The unleavened bread, which had to be eaten for seven days, all leaven having been removed from the houses on the first day (Exodus 12:15), showed that we must carefully abstain from every leaven of perverse doctrine and wickedness (1 Corinthians 5:6, 8). Moreover, the days of assembly, which were the first and the seventh, or last, of the Passover, on which no work was permitted except the preparation of food (Exodus 12:16), pointed to a complete consecration of our whole life to God, at its beginning and its end (1 Corinthians 5:7).

units.la: Secundo Festum septimanarum; de quo Levit. 23. 10, -14. Scilicet die decimo sexto mensis primi afferendus erat ad Sacerdotem manipulus primitiarum, agitandus coram Jehovâ. Sic messis cerimonialiter sanctificata, nostri spiritualem sanctificationem per Christum figurabat. Exinde septem numerandæ erant septimanæ; postridie vero erat Pentecoste: tunc novum munus adferri debuit Iehovæ in agitationem; de quo copiose ibid. vers. 15,-21. Sic videl. cum lætitiâ spirituali celebrare debuerunt memoriam liberationis ex Ægypto; simulque spiritualem liberationem per Christum fide contemplari. Deut. 16. 10, 11, 12. Hebr. xi. 28, 29. 1 Cor. x. 1,-4.
units.tr: Second, the Feast of Weeks, concerning which see Leviticus 23:10–14. That is, on the sixteenth day of the first month a sheaf of the firstfruits was to be brought to the priest and waved before Jehovah. In this way the harvest, ceremonially sanctified, prefigured our spiritual sanctification through Christ. After that seven weeks were to be counted, and on the day after them came Pentecost; then a new offering was to be brought to Jehovah for waving, concerning which see more fully in the same chapter, verses 15–21. Thus, namely, they were to celebrate with spiritual joy the memory of their deliverance from Egypt, and at the same time to contemplate by faith the spiritual deliverance through Christ: Deuteronomy 16:10, 11, 12; Hebrews 11:28, 29; 1 Corinthians 10:1–4.

units.la: Tertio ; Festum Tabernaculorum celebrandum erat die decimo quinto mensis septimi : ac deinceps : agitanda tunc erat lætitia coram Iehova , per septem dies continuos ; & commemorandum, quomodo Israelitæ Ægyptum egressi habitassent in tabernaculis: Levit. 23. 34,-36;40,-43. Nehem 8.15,-19. De sacrificiis & muneribus hujus Festi vide Num. 29.12, &seqq. Sic Christus, ejusque vita humilis, σκηνωσις ἐν ἡμῖν, mors & redemtio, cum gaudio spirituali indefinenter commemoranda : Zach. 14. 16, &c. Ioh. 1. 14.
units.tr: Third, the Feast of Tabernacles was to be celebrated on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, and for the following days: joy was then to be expressed before Jehovah for seven continuous days, and it was to be remembered how the Israelites, having come out of Egypt, had dwelt in tabernacles (Leviticus 23:34–36, 40–43; Nehemiah 8:15–19). For the sacrifices and offerings of this feast, see Numbers 29:12 and following. Thus Christ, and his humble life, [tabernacling among us] (σκηνωσις ἐν ἡμῖν), his death and redemption, are to be commemorated without ceasing, with spiritual joy: Zechariah 14:16, etc.; John 1:14.

units.la: XXXVIII. Minus solenne erat Festum Tubarum ;
units.tr: XXXVIII. The Feast of Trumpets was less solemn;

units.la: primo die mensis septimi, tubarum clangore, quiete, & sanćta convocatione transigendum: Levit. 23. 24, 25. De sacrificiis hujus Festi vide Num. 29. 1,-6. Sic autem continua spiritualis lætitia, & gratiarum actio, sub Euangelio resonare debent : Ies. 35. 1, 2, 10, Phil. 4. 4 1 Thessal. 5. 16.
units.tr: it was to be kept on the first day of the seventh month, with the clangour of trumpets, rest, and a holy assembly: Lev. 23. 24, 25. For the sacrifices of this feast see Num. 29. 1-6. So too, under the Gospel, continual spiritual joy and thanksgiving ought to resound: Ies. 35. 1, 2, 10; Phil. 4. 4; 1 Thess. 5. 16.

units.la: Superest Solennis dies expiationis. Decimo scil. die mensis septimi, animæ stato & quieto jejunio eranť affligendæ: Levit. 16, 29. 31. Num. 29. 7. oblatis sacrificiis, ut in octavo Festi tabernaculorum; & ordinato peculiari cultu ad sanćtuarium , tentorium conventus , altare , Sacerdotes , totumque populum, per Pontificem expiandos : Levit 16. 32,- 34. Sic omnes fideles per Christum expiati sunt , omnisque eorum sanctificatio ex ipso proficiscitur : Hebr. 9. 14. 1 Ioh. 2. 2. Tit. 1. 15
units.tr: There remains the solemn Day of Atonement. On the tenth day of the seventh month, namely, souls were to be afflicted by a fixed and quiet fast: Lev. 16. 29, 31; Num. 29. 7. Sacrifices were offered, as on the eighth day of the Feast of Tabernacles, and a special worship was ordained, by which the sanctuary, the tent of meeting, the altar, the priests and the whole people were to be atoned for through the High Priest: Lev. 16. 32-34. So all the faithful have been atoned for through Christ, and all their sanctification proceeds from him: Heb. 9. 14; 1 John 2. 2; Tit. 1. 15.

units.la: XXXIX. Plurium annorum lapsu recurrebant AnnusSabbathicus,& Jubilæus.Ille erat septimus quisqʒ inde ab introitu in terram Canaan , quo terra quievit, & omnis ejus cultus fuit intermissus : Levit 25. 4,7. Sic quies cœlestis per Christum adumbrabatur : Hebr. 4, 6, 11. Col. 3. 1, 2.
units.tr: XXXIX. After the passing of several years there recurred the Sabbatical Year and the Jubilee. The former was every seventh year from the entry into the land of Canaan, in which the land rested and all its cultivation was suspended: Lev. 25. 4, 7. So the heavenly rest was foreshadowed through Christ: Heb. 4. 6, 11; Col. 3. 1, 2.

units.la: Hic erat annus quisque quinquagesimus, quo omnibus Tubarum clangore libertas promulgari , singuli ad hæreditates & familias suas reverti, & servi populares manumitti consueverant: Levit. 25. 8, 16; 27, 28. &c. Sic plena libertas per Christum parta, hæreditas cœlestis per eundem vindicata, & Euangelio promulgata, figurabatur: Isai. 61. 1, 3-4. Luc. 4. 17, 18-21.
units.tr: This was every fiftieth year, in which liberty was proclaimed to all with the clangour of trumpets, each man returned to his inheritance and family, and native servants were accustomed to be set free: Lev. 25. 8, 16; 27. 28, etc. So full liberty won through Christ, the heavenly inheritance claimed by the same, and proclaimed in the Gospel, was prefigured: Isa. 61. 1, 3-4; Luke 4. 17, 18-21.

units.la: Sed neque prætereundum, quod ipse status Israelitarum politicus, à Deo peculiaribus quibusdam legibus speciatim ordinatus ac munitus, spiritualem & beatum Ecclesiæ statum, in communione Christi, figurarit: Eph. 2. 12, 13, 14; 19, 20-22. Hebr. 12, 22, 23-24. 1 Petr. 2. 9, 10.
units.tr: But it should not be passed over that the political state of the Israelites itself, ordained and fortified by God with certain peculiar laws, prefigured the spiritual and blessed state of the Church in communion with Christ: Eph. 2. 12, 13, 14; 19, 20-22; Heb. 12. 22, 23-24; 1 Pet. 2. 9, 10.

units.la: XL.
units.tr: XL.

units.la: Sic satis de œconomia V. T. Succedit œconomia N.T. quam ejusdem essentialiter Fœderis ac Testamenti esse cum Veteri, probavimus nuper. Notandum interim discrimen aliquod accidentale, tum ratione temporis, tum respectu qualitatis & quantitatis:
units.tr: So much for the economy of the Old Testament. There follows the economy of the New Testament, which we have lately proved to be essentially the same covenant and testament as the Old. Meanwhile it should be noted that there is some accidental difference, both with respect to time, and with respect to quality and quantity:

units.la: Ratione temporis: quia sub V. T. Messias credebatur exhibendus; unde vota fidelium, Utinam lacerans cœlos descenderes! Isai. 64. 1. O si quis daret te fratrem esse mihi, sugentem ubera matris meæ! Cant. 8. 1. & similia; virtute fidei & infallibili promissionum Divinarum certitudine interim sustentata: Isai. 9. 5. At sub N. T. prædicatur Messias exhibitus. Confer Historias Euangelicas.
units.tr: With respect to time: because under the Old Testament the Messiah was believed still to be exhibited; hence the prayers of the faithful, "Oh that you would tear the heavens and come down!" Isa. 64. 1. "Oh that you were my brother, nursing at my mother's breasts!" Song 8. 1. & similar things, sustained meanwhile by the strength of faith and the infallible certainty of the divine promises: Isa. 9. 5. But under the New Testament the Messiah is proclaimed as already exhibited. Compare the Gospel histories.

units.la: XLI.
units.tr: XLI.

units.la: Ratione qualitatis, Claritas sub N.T. longe major est, quam sub V. Tunc enim obtinuit umbra; nunc sub N. ipsum corpus: Col. 2. 17. & expressa forma rerum: Hebr. 10. 1. Illic fideles promissa eminus tantum fuere conspicati; hic adepti: Hebr. 11. 13. atque adeo in universum doctrina Euangelica sub N. T. & Verbo clarius explanatur, & signis expressius confirmatur in ordine ad intellectum nostrum; quàm olim sub V. 2 Cor. 3. 11-13.
units.tr: With respect to quality, the clarity under the New Testament is far greater than under the Old. For then the shadow prevailed; now under the New, the body itself: Col. 2. 17; and the express form of things: Heb. 10. 1. There the faithful only saw the promised things from afar; here they have obtained them: Heb. 11. 13. And so, in general, the evangelical doctrine under the New Testament is explained more clearly by the Word, and confirmed more expressly by signs, with respect to our understanding, than it once was under the Old: 2 Cor. 3. 11-13.

units.la: Libertas nunc etiam major est: primo enim sub V. T. Fœdus Legale rigide identidem fuit inculcatum, hæc consolationibus Euangelicis tam clare ac suaviter temperatum ; ac proinde populus quadam servitutis specie detinebatur. At sub N. T. ipsum Euangelium clarius, prædicatur ; gratia tum sanctificationis, tum adoptionis major est, atque adeo major liberras. Hebr. 8. 8,-10. &c. Ierem. 31. 31, &c. Gal. 3. 24, 26. Deinde sub V. T. obtinuit jugum istud Legis Cerimonialis, onerosum & grave. Sed totum hoc in N. T. omnino sublatum est. unde Paulus, Gal. 5.1,2,3. In libertate igitur, qua Christus nos liberavit, perstate; & ne regredientes implicamini servitutis jugo, &c. Vide etiam Act. 15 10.
units.tr: Liberty is now also greater.
