He teaches, namely, that for someone to be judged or acknowledged as righteous before God, a faith of whatever kind, or an oral profession, is not sufficient; rather a living faith is required, which shows itself by its vital acts, even those commanded. See verses 1:14, 17, 18, 19, 20, and compare Gen. 15. 6; 22. 1, 2, 3, 9, 10, 12, 16, 17, 18. Reply 2. Many in the age of the Apostles and afterwards were so foolish that from a merely historical faith they conceived a confidence of salvation, and wished to be reckoned righteous from external communion in the Church and profession of the Gospel. Indeed faith itself is in the heart, but since theirs was not saving faith, they deceived themselves and wished to lead others into a similar opinion of them by external oral profession. The Apostle refutes this rashness and deception. 3. Works are not truly and spiritually good unless they proceed from saving faith: Rom. 14. 23; Titus 1. 15; Heb. 2. 6. But the person who has this active principle is conscious of it to himself, and where his works correspond to his profession, they also provide others with a sufficient argument for a judgement of charity. 4. Calvin, in the place cited, says nothing of the kind that the Apologist objects; but in §10 and 11 he discusses historical and temporary faith, where, among other things: "Although there is great likeness and affinity between the elect of God and those who for a time are endowed with a transitory faith, yet that confidence which Paul celebrates, so that with full mouth they cry, Abba, Father, flourishes only in the elect. Therefore, that God regenerates the elect alone with incorruptible seed forever, so that the seed of their life never perishes, implanted in their hearts; so firmly does he seal in them the grace of his adoption that it is stable and sure. But this in no way prevents that lower operation of the Spirit from having its course also in the reprobate. Meanwhile the faithful are taught diligently..."

units.la: Pp „cordi,, cordibus insitum: ità solidè in illis obsignat adoptio-,, nis suæ gratiam, ut stabilis ac rata fit. Sed hoc ,, minimè obstat, quin illa inferior Spiritûs operatio ,, cursum suum habeat etiàm in reprobis. Interea ,, docentur fideles folicitè & humiliter seipsos excu-,, tere, ne pro fidei certitudine obrepat carnis fecu-,, ritas. Adde, quòd reprobi nunquàm sensum gra-,, tiæ, nisi confusum, percipiunt; ut umbram po-,, tiùs apprehendant, quàm solidum corpus.
units.tr: Yet it engraves the grace of his adoption so firmly on their hearts that it is stable and sure. But this in no way prevents that lesser operation of the Spirit from running its course in the reprobate as well. Meanwhile the faithful are taught to examine themselves carefully and humbly, lest carnal security creep in under the pretence of certainty of faith. Add that the reprobate never perceive the sense of grace except in a confused way, so that they grasp a shadow rather than the solid body.

units.la: XXII. Subjiciunt; Si quis ea, quæ à Socino dicun-
units.tr: XXII. They object: If anyone weighs what is said by Socinus

units.la: tur, in hàc materiâ, fine gratiâ, fine odio, expendat, eum velit nolit, cogi tandem confiteri, illum in substantiâ rei cum Reformatis consentire, manente folùm hoc discrimine (causam semper ἀπεγκαταρκτικῶ excipe, ut quæ ad hanc materiam non pertineat.) quòd obedientiam fidei formam vocet, cùm Reformatæ Ecclesiæ eam vocent effectum, fructum, fœtum, fine quo fides esse non possit. Quantulum (ait Apologista) hoc est? Quis vel cicum interduit? &c. Resp. 1. Cùm Socinus, abnegatâ Christi justitiâ, quæ ipsius pro nobis Satisfactionem ac Meritum complectitur, fidem quatenùs viva est, & obedientiam tanquàm istius formam, illi substituit, atque hominem coram Deo justificare contendit, toto cœlo distat ab Ecclesiis Reformatis. Quid autem fit de Remonstrantibus, vide ampliùs apud Curcellæum, in Differtatione 4. R. 2. Causa ἀπεγκαταρκτικὴ, Christi Satisfactio & Meritum, nobis imputata, & fide apprehenfa, non minùs pertinent ad hanc de Justificatione materiam, quam fundamentum ad ædificium. Apoftolus emphaticè, 1. Cor. 15. 17. Quod fi Christus non est suscitatus, inanis est fides vestra; adhùc estis in peccatis vestris. Similiter inanis est fides, & nulla juftificatio Euangelica, fi Christus pro peccatis nostris non satisfecit, necfuâ justitiâ vitam æternam nobis acqui-
units.tr: on this matter, without grace and without hatred, he will, willy-nilly, be forced at last to confess that Socinus agrees with the Reformed in substance, the only difference remaining being this (I set aside the principal cause, ἀπεγκαταρκτικῶ, as it does not pertain to this subject): that he calls obedience the form of faith, whereas the Reformed Churches call it the effect, fruit and offspring, without which faith cannot exist. How small is this (says the Apologist)? Who would so much as flinch? etc. Reply 1. Since Socinus, denying the justice of Christ, which embraces his satisfaction and merit on our behalf, sets obedience in its place as the form of faith, so far as faith is living, and contends that man is justified before God by this, he is worlds apart from the Reformed Churches. As for what the Remonstrants hold, see more fully in Curcellaeus, in Dissertation 4, R. 2. The principal cause, Christ's satisfaction and merit, imputed to us and apprehended by faith, pertains no less to this doctrine of justification than the foundation pertains to the building. The Apostle says emphatically, 1 Cor. 15. 17: "If Christ is not raised, your faith is vain; you are still in your sins." Likewise faith is vain, and there is no evangelical justification, if Christ did not satisfy for our sins and did not by his righteousness acquire eternal life for us.

units.la: . acquisivit. R. 3. Si obedientia statuatur forma fidei, & sic qualiscunque justitia propria subfituatur unicæ verissimæ ac perfectissimę justitiæ Christi, id maximum & gravissimum est à veritate Euangelicâ divortium. Quòd Remonstrantibus hoc tantulum non fit, ut vel ciccum interdùint, ea est calamitas fundi ipsorum. Rom. 10. 3. R. 4. Qui Euangelio rectè auscultant, facilè intelligunt, Christum perfectissimum Servatorem fide apprehendi, atque itâ unionem & communionem cum ipso obtineri : apprehendi autem prout nobis à Deo factus est justitia, ad nostri justificationem; ac porrò ut auctorem sanctificationis, ad præstandam sanctè gratitudinem ac novam obedientiam, quæ justificationem sequitur.
units.tr: Reply 3. If obedience is set up as the form of faith, and so some kind of proper righteousness is substituted for the one, most true and most perfect righteousness of Christ, this is the greatest and most grievous divorce from evangelical truth. That the Remonstrants do not so much as flinch at this is the calamity of their cause. Rom. 10. 3. Reply 4. Those who listen rightly to the Gospel readily understand that Christ, the most perfect Saviour, is apprehended by faith, and thus union and communion with him are obtained; he is apprehended as he has been made by God righteousness for us, for our justification, and further as the author of sanctification, to render holy gratitude and new obedience, which follows justification.

units.la: XXIII. Sunt & aliæ quædam Objectiones : utpotè, 1. Rom. 2. 13. Qui Legem præstant, justificabuntur, &c. Resp. Sic aliquoties repetitur Fœdus Legale, & conditio per ipsum ad Justificationem requisita : non quòd sic homines in hoc rerum statû justificari possint; sed ut impotentiam atque reatum suum inde agnoscant, & Euangelicæ doctrinæ de Christo ejusque justitiâ, auscultent.
units.tr: XXIII. There are also some other objections, namely: 1. Rom. 2. 13. "The doers of the Law shall be justified," etc. Reply: The covenant of Law, and the condition required by it for justification, is repeated in this way several times; not because men can be justified in this state of affairs by it, but so that they may recognise their impotence and guilt from it, and listen to the evangelical doctrine of Christ and his righteousness.

units.la: Obj. 2. Matth. 12. 37. Ex sermonibus tuis justificaberis. &c. Resp. Intelligenda ibi est justificationis declaratio; sive judicium consequens, quòd quis coram Deo justus sit. Per sermones enim aliis innotescere solet, quid intùs sit in animo. Confer verf. 35.
units.tr: Objection 2. Matt. 12. 37: "By your words you will be justified," etc. Reply: What is meant there is the declaration of justification, or the consequent judgment that someone is righteous before God. For what is in the mind is usually made known to others through words. Compare verse 35.

units.la: Obj. 3. Passim exigitur praxis respipiscentiæ, ac novæ obedientiæ, ad remissionem peccatorum: Ergò, &c. Resp. Tunc respicitur sensus istius gratiæ in conscientiâ nostrâ; vel etiàm actualis liberatio à malis pœnalibus, aut ipsa fruitio vitæ æternæ: atque indicatur conditio quædam ad sensum & fruitionem istam prærequisita; in quâ tamen ipsum jus impunitatis ac beatitudinis non fundatur.
units.tr: Objection 3. Repentance and the practice of new obedience are everywhere required for the forgiveness of sins; therefore, etc. Reply: Then the sense of this grace in our conscience is in view, or actual deliverance from penal evils, or the very enjoyment of eternal life; and a certain condition prerequisite for that sense and enjoyment is indicated; yet the right of impunity and blessedness is not founded on that condition itself.

units.la: XXIV. Rejiciendus nunc etiam est error Osiandri, Justitiam Dei essentialem in Justificatione nobis imputari. Hùc autem pertinent rationes; 1. Justitia Christi, ut Mediatoris ac Sponsoris nostri, quæ Satisfactionem ac Meritum ipsius complectitur, nobis imputatur; ut sup. probatum: ea verò non est justitia Dei essentialis, & sic tribus Personis communis.
units.tr: XXIV. Now the error of Osiander must also be rejected, which holds that God's essential righteousness is imputed to us in justification. The following reasons pertain to this. 1. The righteousness of Christ as our Mediator and Surety, which comprises his satisfaction and merit, is imputed to us, as has been proved above; but this is not the essential righteousness of God, and so it is common to the three Persons.

units.la: 2. Justitia Dei essentialis increata est & infinita; atque adeò homini absolutè impossibilis: consequenter eam Deus ab homine postulare non potest; nec homini imputare.
units.tr: 2. The essential righteousness of God is uncreated and infinite, and therefore absolutely impossible for a man; consequently God cannot require it from a man, nor impute it to a man.

units.la: 3. Justitia quæ nobis imputatur, æstimatur tanquàm satisfactoria & meritoria apud justitiam remunerativam Deo essentialem; ac proinde ab eâ diversa est.
units.tr: 3. The righteousness that is imputed to us is reckoned as satisfactory and meritorious before the remunerative justice essential to God, and therefore it is different from that justice.

units.la: 4. Lex ab hominibus requirebat obedientiam formaliter humanam, & pro peccatis hominum pœnas formaliter humanas: illam Christus præstitit, has pertulit, quâ homo; licet Deitate conferente dignitatem ac valorem infinitum. Ista ergò justitia Christi nobis imputatur, non Dei essentialis.
units.tr: 4. The Law required of men obedience that is formally human, and for the sins of men it required penalties that are formally human. Christ performed the former and bore the latter as man, although by the conferring of his Deity they have infinite dignity and value. Therefore it is the righteousness of Christ that is imputed to us, not the essential righteousness of God.

units.la: Obj. 1. Rom. 10. 3. vocatur Justitia Dei: & 2 Cor. 5. 21. nos dicimur effici Justitia Dei in Christo. Ergò. Resp. Non quòd subjectivè & formaliter Justitia ipsius Dei sit; sed efficienter; quatenùs illa Justitia nobis à Deo procurata est, per istum Mediatorem ac Sponsorem; & sic opus ac donum Dei est. Hinc dicitur Justitia ex Deo per fidem, Phil. 3. 9. & Christus nobis à Deo factus justitia; 1. Cor. 1. 30.
units.tr: Objection 1. Rom. 10. 3 is called the righteousness of God, and 2 Cor. 5. 21 says that we are made the righteousness of God in Christ. Therefore. Reply: Not because it is subjectively and formally the righteousness of God himself, but efficiently; in so far as that righteousness has been procured for us by God, through this Mediator and Surety, and so it is the work and gift of God. Hence it is called righteousness from God through faith, Phil. 3. 9, and Christ is made by God our righteousness, 1 Cor. 1. 30.

units.la: Obj. 2. 2 Petr. 1. 4. dicuntur nobis maxima ac pretiosa promissa donata, ut per hæc efficeremur Divinæ consortes naturæ. Ergò. Resp. Non quòd essentialis Dei justitia nobis formaliter imputetur, aut subjectivè nobis communicetur; sed secundùm similitudinem analogicam, per imaginem Dei in nobis restitutam, juxta gratiam Euangelicam.
units.tr: Objection 2. 2 Pet. 1. 4 says that the greatest and precious promises have been given to us, so that through these we might become partakers of the divine nature. Therefore. Reply: Not because the essential righteousness of God is formally imputed to us, or communicated to us subjectively; but according to an analogical likeness, through the image of God restored in us, according to evangelical grace.

units.la: Obj. 3. Deus ad justificationem creaturæ rationalis non acceptat justitiam aliam, nisi suam essentialem. Ergò. Resp. Imò hic tantùm acceptat, sive admittit, justitiam creatam, tùm habitualem, tùm actualem; quæ valeat apud Justitiam suam essentialem; & sic ab eâ diversa sit.
units.tr: Objection 3. God does not accept any other righteousness for the justification of a rational creature than his own essential righteousness. Therefore. Reply. Indeed, here he accepts, or admits, only created righteousness, both habitual and actual; which avails before his essential righteousness, and so is different from it.

units.la: XXV. Quò certius aliæ etiàm difficultates expediantur, distinguenda est actualis justificatio à decreto justificationis; similiter ut actualis creatio à decreto creationis, & actualis providentia à decreto providentię, &c. Vide Eph. I. 7,--11. Ac porrò justificatio actualis vel activè spectatur, seu efficienter; vel passivè, seu terminativè. Justificatio activa nihil aliud est, quàm Deus justificans: Rom. 8. 33. sive ipse Deus in relatione ad electos vocatos credentes, ut qui ab Ipso judicialiter transferantur in statum justitiæ. Sed justificatio passiva nihil aliud est, quàm status justitiæ in homine electo vocato credente, cum respectu ad Deum sic judicantem.
units.tr: XXV. In order that other difficulties may be settled more surely, actual justification must be distinguished from the decree of justification; just as actual creation is distinguished from the decree of creation, and actual providence from the decree of providence, etc. See Eph. I. 7–11. Furthermore, actual justification is viewed either actively, that is efficiently, or passively, that is terminatively. Active justification is nothing other than God justifying: Rom. 8. 33, that is God himself in relation to the elect, called and believing, who are judicially transferred by him into the state of righteousness. But passive justification is nothing other than the state of righteousness in the elect, called and believing man, with respect to God so judging.

units.la: Porrò etiàm justificatio distinguenda est ab ejus promissione, vel indicio qualicunque: Gal. I. 8. Prævidens Scriptura, Deum ex fide justificaturum Gentes, ante euangelizavit Abrahæ, Benedicentur (inquiens) in te omnes Gentes.
units.tr: Furthermore, justification must also be distinguished from its promise, or from any indication of it: Gal. I. 8. Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, preached the gospel beforehand to Abraham: "In you," it says, "all the Gentiles will be blessed."

units.la: Ac tandem spectatur justificatio vel formaliter, vel virtualiter, vel consequenter. Formaliter peragitur justificatio, cùm homo electus, efficaciter vocatus, & sic apprehensus à Christo, vicissim fide apprehendit Christum; atque itâ mutuam illam unionem & communionem Christi ac beneficiorum ipsius accipit. Rom. 8. 30. Quos vocavit, eos etiàm justificavit. III. 28. Colligimus igitur fide justificari hominem, &c. Virtualiter peracta est nostri justificatio potissimum, cùm Christus, consummata salutis nostræ impetratione, ipse fuit justificatus, & nos in Ipso tanquam Capite nostro; 1 Tim. 3. 16. 2 Cor. 5. 19. Col. I. 19, 20. Imò & quodammodò, sed remotius, cùm Filius Dei statim post lapsum factus est Mediator ac Sponsor electorum, & actualis ista relatio initium sumsit: Gen. 3. 15. XXII. 18. Isef. 53. 10, 11. Proximè autem in primo momento regenerationis & conversionis: nam in actû secundo, ubi producitur fides actualis, & sic homo credere incipit, justificatur formaliter.
units.tr: Finally, justification is viewed either formally, or virtually, or consequently. Justification is carried out formally when the elect man, effectually called and so apprehended by Christ, in turn apprehends Christ by faith, and so receives that mutual union and communion of Christ and his benefits. Rom. 8. 30: "Those whom he called, these he also justified." III. 28: We conclude therefore that a man is justified by faith, etc. Our justification was accomplished virtually chiefly when Christ, the securing of our salvation having been completed, was himself justified, and we in him as our Head: 1 Tim. 3. 16; 2 Cor. 5. 19; Col. I. 19, 20. Indeed also in a certain way, but more remotely, since the Son of God became Mediator and Surety of the elect immediately after the fall, and that actual relation began: Gen. 3. 15; XXII. 18; Isa. 53. 10, 11. Most nearly, however, at the first moment of regeneration and conversion: for in the second act, where actual faith is produced and man begins to believe, he is justified formally.

units.la: Consequenter denique justificari dicimur, cùm coram Deo justi esse deprehendimur ac declaramur, tùm in propriâ conscientiâ per actum fidei reflexum; tùm etiam apud alios, judicio charitatis ex fructibus fidei justificantis formato.
units.tr: Consequently, we are finally said to be justified when we are found and declared righteous before God, both in our own conscience through a reflexive act of faith, and also before others, by the judgment of charity formed from the fruits of justifying faith.

units.la: XXVII. Quaeritur ergò, 1. An Justificatio obtinuerit sub V. T.? Resp. Electi vocati credentes etiam formaliter fuerunt justificati, per fidem suam, promissioni Euangelicæ habitam, juxta illam œconomiam. Sic enim justitiam Christi, verbo promissionis in antecessum sibi propositam, atque in plenitudine temporis certissimè præstandam, receperunt. Atque ita fideles istius temporis etiam verè habuerunt plenam ἄφεσιν, remissionem omnium peccatorum suorum; ac jus vitæ æternæ: licet respectû Sponsoris, qui solutionem præstiturus erat statuto tempore, fuerit πάρεσις, transmissio & dilatio. Psal. 32. 1, 2. 11. 3, 4, 9, 11. CIII. 3, 10, 12. CXXX. 3, 4.
units.tr: XXVII. The question is, therefore: (1) Did justification obtain under the Old Testament? Answer. The elect who were called and believed were also formally justified, through their faith placed in the evangelical promise, according to that economy. For in this way they received the righteousness of Christ, which was set before them in advance by the word of promise and was most certainly to be furnished in the fullness of time. And so the faithful of that time truly had full remission [ἄφεσιν] of all their sins, and a right to eternal life, although with respect to the Surety, who was to make payment at the appointed time, it was a passing over [πάρεσις], that is, a deferral and postponement. Ps. 32:1, 2, 11; 3, 4, 9, 11; 103:3, 10, 12; 130:3, 4.

units.la: Obj. Hebr. 10. 18. Ubi est horum (peccatorum) remissio, non est amplius oblatio pro peccato: Atqui sub V. T. adhùc requirebatur oblatio pro peccato: Ergo tunc non erat remissio peccatorum. Resp. Ex collatione versuum 10, 12, 14, 19, 20. manifestissimum est, Apostolum illic speciatim loqui de remissione prorsus absolutâ, ubi Sponsor satisfactionem plenissimam ipso actû præstitit, & Sacerdos oblationem spiritualiter atque in æternum expiatoriam consummavit. Nos autem, juxta alia loca S. Scripturæ, diximus de remissione ipsorum fidelium V. T. ex virtute oblationis Christi tunc adhuc consummandæ: quæ non excludebat, sed requirebat, oblationem Christi futuram; & oblationes insuper Legales, tanquàm ejus typos.
units.tr: Objection. Heb. 10:18: Where remission of these sins is, there is no more offering for sin. But under the Old Testament an offering for sin was still required. Therefore there was then no remission of sins. Answer. From a comparison of verses 10, 12, 14, 19 and 20 it is most manifest that the Apostle is speaking there particularly of a remission that is wholly absolute, where the Surety has by that very act rendered the fullest satisfaction and the Priest has spiritually and for ever completed an atoning offering. We, however, following other passages of Holy Scripture, have spoken of the remission of the Old Testament believers themselves, by virtue of the offering of Christ which was still to be completed then. This did not exclude but required the future offering of Christ, and in addition the legal offerings as its types.

units.la: XXVIII. Quær. 2. An infantibus electis regenitis etiàm competat Justificatio? Resp. Illi etiàm habent Spiritum fidei, principium ac semen fidei actualis; & passivè apprehensi sunt à Christo, ad inchoatam unionem & communionem ipsius, ac beneficiorum ejus, atque hæc gratia illis obsignatur Baptismo; sicut olim factum est Circumcisione, sigillo justitiæ fidei; Rom. 4. 11. Act. 2. 38, 39. xx. 16.
units.tr: XXVIII. Question 2: Does justification also belong to regenerate elect infants? Answer. They too have the Spirit of faith, the principle and seed of actual faith; and they have been passively apprehended by Christ, for the inchoate union and communion with him and his benefits. This grace is sealed to them in Baptism, just as it once was in Circumcision, the seal of the righteousness of faith; Rom. 4:11; Acts 2:38, 39; 22:16.

units.la: Obj. Non sunt capaces fidei actualis: Ergò. Resp. Attamen habent principium: unde etiàm activè apprehensuri & recepturi sunt Christum, ejusque justitiam, si tantisper maneant superstites. Sin minùs, quòd jàm virtualiter habent in Christo, ad quod passivè apprehensi sunt, de facto illis applicabitur; & ipsi activè recipient in alterâ vitâ: Talium enim est Regnum Dei; Marc. 10. 14.
units.tr: Objection. They are not capable of actual faith; therefore... Answer. Nevertheless they have the principle, whence they will also actively apprehend and receive Christ and his righteousness, if they remain alive for a while. But if not, what they already have virtually in Christ, to which they have been passively apprehended, will in fact be applied to them; and they themselves will actively receive it in the other life: for of such is the Kingdom of God; Mark 10:14.

units.la: XXIX. Quær. 3. An peccata dici possint nobis remissa priùs, quàm sint commissa; & priùs, quàm actû resipiscamus, atque in Christum credamus? Resp. Imò virtualiter in Christo: sed non formaliter.
units.tr: XXIX. Question 3: Can sins be said to be remitted to us before they have been committed, and before we actually repent and believe in Christ? Answer. Yes, virtually in Christ, but not formally.

units.la: Obj. 1. Non enim non sunt affectiones. Nulla igitur remissio peccatorum nondùm commissorum. Resp. Neg. consequ. Erant enim omninò committenda, juxta decretum Dei permissivum; & præscita per scientiam visionis; & Christo imputata, &c.
units.tr: Objection 1. Sins are not yet not-committed, for they are not nothing. Therefore there is no remission of sins not yet committed. Answer. I deny the consequence. For they were certainly to be committed, according to God's permissive decree, and foreknown by the knowledge of vision, and imputed to Christ, etc.

units.la: Obj. 2. Non est quòd peccata tantoperè fugiamus, si ea jàm ante sint remissa, &c. Resp. Neg. consequ. Quia nihilò minor est eorum turpitudo, & repugnantia adversus Sanctitatem Dei, & Imaginem Dei in nobis, &c.
units.tr: Objection 2. There is no reason to flee sins so eagerly if they have already been remitted beforehand, etc. Answer. I deny the consequence. Because their wickedness is no less, nor their opposition to the holiness of God and to the image of God in us, etc.

units.la: XXX. Quær. 4. An unico actû, eoque immutabili, bili, justificemur ? Resp. Imo formaliter: Si enim 1. Christum spectemus; Ipse omninò consummavit, quæcunque ad Justitiam pertinent. Si 2. Vocationem salutarem; hàc totus Christus nobis proponitur, cum omnibus suis beneficiis salutaribus, qui nos ad totalem secùm unionem & communionem apprehendit. Si 3 Fidem; hàc Ipsum sic totaliter apprehendimus vicissim; & speciatim, quatenùs nobis factus est justitia perfecta; unde nobis pleno jure competit impunitas ac vita æterna. Si 4. ipsam Justificationem formaliter; hàc nobis adjudicatur tota isthæc salus. Undè patet, unico actu individuo formaliter peragi Justificationem cujusque credentis; non autem successivè.
units.tr: XXX. Question 4: Are we justified by one act, and that an unchangeable one? Answer. Yes, formally. For if (1) we look to Christ, he himself has wholly accomplished all that pertains to righteousness. If (2) we look to the saving calling, through it the whole Christ is set before us, with all his saving benefits, who apprehends us to a total union and communion with himself. If (3) we look to faith, by it we in turn apprehend him wholly; and particularly insofar as he has been made perfect righteousness for us, whence by full right impunity and eternal life belong to us. If (4) we look to justification itself formally, by it this whole salvation is adjudged to us. Hence it is evident that the justification of each believer is formally accomplished by one individual act, and not successively.

units.la: Eundem actum dicimus quoque immutabilem: quia 1. Decretum Electionis, 2. Fœdus gratiæ, 3. Vocatio efficax, & 4. reliqua beneficia Christi salutaria, immutabilia sunt χαρίσματα, Rom. xi.29. Adde speciatim insignem locum Rom.8.33,34. Quis intentabit crimina adversus electos Dei? Deus est qui justificat. Quis est qui condemnat? &c. Atque ista observanda contra Pontificios, Remonstrantes, aliosque.
units.tr: We also call this same act unchangeable, because (1) the decree of election, (2) the covenant of grace, (3) effectual calling, and (4) the other saving benefits of Christ are unchangeable gifts [χαρίσματα], Rom. 11:29. Add especially the notable passage Rom. 8:33, 34: Who shall bring any charge against God's elect? It is God who justifies. Who is it that condemns? etc. And these things are to be observed against the Papists, the Remonstrants, and others.

units.la: Pontificii non solùm negant, Justificationem unico actû perfici; sed eam quoque distinguunt in primam & secundam. Primam vocant, quâ quis ex injusto fit justus, per merita de congruo. Secundam, quâ quis ex justo fit justior, per merita de condigno. Quæ omnia in superioribus satis refutata sunt.
units.tr: The Papists not only deny that justification is completed by one act, but also divide it into a first and a second. They call the first that by which someone is made righteous from unrighteous, through merits of congruity. The second is that by which someone is made more righteous from righteous, through merits of condignity. All of which have been sufficiently refuted in the earlier sections.

units.la: Quomodò autem quotidiè adhùc petamus remissionem peccatorum, vide cap. 9. th. 45. §. 3.
units.tr: As to how we still daily ask for the remission of sins, see chap. 9, th. 45, §3.

units.la: XXXI. Quær. 5. An post hanc vitam obtineatur aliqua remissio peccatorum? Resp. Non formaliter, neque peccatorum hic non remissorum, quòd patet ex modò probatis. Interim sicut sententia justificatoria per renovatam praxin fidei ac resipiscentiæ denuò
units.tr: XXXI. Question 5: Is any remission of sins obtained after this life? Answer. Not formally, nor of sins not remitted here, as is evident from what has just been proved. Meanwhile, just as the sentence of justification is renewed through the renewed exercise of faith and repentance, again...

units.la: Cap.XV. De Justificatione, Reconcil. & Adopt.
units.tr: Chapter XV. On Justification, Reconciliation and Adoption

units.la: nuò applicatur & percipitur cum consolatione in hâc vitâ; itâ in die extremi judicii ejusdem sententiæ fiet solennis promulgatio, & simul plenissima executio. Hinc 2 Tim. I. 18. de Onesiphoro; Det ei Dominus, ut invceniat misericordiam apud Dominum in die illo! & Matth. 25. 34, —. Tunc dicet Rex his, qui à dextrâ sua erunt; Venite, benedicti Patris mei; possidete Regnum, paratum vobis à jactu fundamentis mundi: Esurivi enim, & dedistis mihi quo vescerer. &c.
units.tr: ...is applied and perceived with consolation in this life; so on the day of the last judgment this same sentence will be solemnly proclaimed and at the same time most fully executed. Hence 2 Tim. I. 18, of Onesiphorus: May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord in that day! And Matt. 25. 34: Then the King will say to those on his right hand: Come, you blessed of my Father, possess the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry, and you gave me something to eat, etc.

units.la: XXXII. Justificationi cohæret Reconciliatio; quæ nunc spectatur in applicatione. Estque Actus gratiosus relativus, quo peccator redemtus & credens, dùm justificatur, simul etiàm traducitur ex statû inimicitiæ & iræ, ad statum pacis & amicitiæ cum Deo. Isef. 32. 17. Opus justitiæ erit pax, & opus justitiæ tranquillitas & securitas usque in sæculum. Rom. 5. 1, 2. Justificati igitur ex fide, pacem habemus erga Deum per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum: Per quem etiam fide habuimus aditum in gratiam hanc, &c. 9. Justificati igitur Ejus sanguine, servabimur nunc multò magis per Eum ab irâ. II. —per quem nunc Reconciliationem affecti sumus. Jac. 2. 23. Credidit Abraham Deo, & imputatum est ei ad justitiam, & amicus Dei vocatus est.
units.tr: XXXII. Reconciliation is joined to justification, and is now viewed in its application. It is a gracious, relative act, by which the redeemed and believing sinner, while he is justified, is at the same time transferred from the state of enmity and wrath to the state of peace and friendship with God. Isa. 32. 17: The work of righteousness will be peace, and the effect of righteousness quietness and security for ever. Rom. 5. 1, 2: Being justified therefore by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ; through whom we have also had access by faith into this grace, etc. Rom. 5. 9: Being justified therefore by his blood, we shall be saved now much more through him from wrath. Rom. 5. 11: through whom we have now received reconciliation. Jas. 2. 23: Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness, and he was called the friend of God.

units.la: Actum gratiosum dicimus; quia ex speciali gratiâ ac misericordiâ Dei erga electos procedit. Relativum verò; quia statûs nostri mutationem relativam inferte formaliter.
units.tr: We call it a gracious act because it proceeds from the special grace and mercy of God toward the elect. We call it relative because it formally brings about a relative change in our state.

units.la: Terminus à quo, est statu inimicitiæ & iræ: Eph. 2. 3. Rom. 8. 7. Isef. 59. 2. lxiii. 10. Ad quem, est statûs pacis & amicitiæ cum Deo in Christo: Col. I. 21.
units.tr: The terminus from which is the state of enmity and wrath: Eph. 2. 3; Rom. 8. 7; Isa. 59. 2; Isa. 63. 10. The terminus to which is the state of peace and friendship with God in Christ: Col. 1. 21.

units.la: Christus, verè Mediator reconciliationis: [Hebrew]; Isef. 7. 14. Vir socius Dei; Zach. 13. 7. eam nobis impetravit. Vide sup. cap. 12. th. 24. Quatenus autem Ipse oblatione sui peccata nostra expiavit, in Ipso reconciliati sumus virtualiter. Sed in hunc statum formaliter traducimur, cum credentes istius etiam beneficii reddimur actu participes. Consequenter autem declaratur ista nostri in hunc statum translatio, atque exercetur amicitia, sancta voluntatis nostrae conformatione ad sanctissimam voluntatem Dei nostri. Joh. 15. 14, 15. Vos Amici mei critis, si feceritis quaecunque Ego praecipio vobis. &c. Psal. 85. 9.
units.tr: Christ, the true Mediator of reconciliation, is Immanuel (Isa. 7. 14), the man who is God's companion (Zech. 13. 7); He obtained it for us. See above, chap. 12, th. 24. In so far as He expiated our sins by offering Himself, we are reconciled virtually in Him. But we are formally transferred into this state when, as believers, we are actually made partakers of this benefit. Consequently, this our transfer into this state is declared, and friendship is exercised through the holy conformity of our will to the most holy will of our God. John 15. 14, 15: You are my friends, if you do whatever I command you, etc. Ps. 85. 9.

units.la: XXXIII. Pax describi solet, Ordinata animorum concordia.
units.tr: XXXIII. Peace is usually described as the orderly concord of souls.

units.la: Ejus vel nomen amabile est. Unde & Hebraei in salutationibus eam aliis precari solent. Hic autem agitur de Pace cum ipso Deo, potentissimo, beatissimo, beneficentissimo, fidelissimo: quae certe Pax optima rerum, Quas homini novisse datum est. Phil. 4. 7. Pax Dei, quae superat omnem intellectum, praesidio erit cordibus vestris, &c. Confer Joh. 14. 27.
units.tr: Its very name is lovely; hence the Hebrews are accustomed to wish it to others in their greetings. Here, however, we are dealing with peace with God himself, most powerful, most blessed, most beneficent, most faithful; which is surely the best of all things that it is given to man to know. Phil. 4. 7: The peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts, etc. Compare John 14. 27.

units.la: Ab ea dependet 1. Pax conscientiae: quia conscientia in homine locum Dei quodammodo tenet; Rom. 2. 14. Confer Rom. 5. 2. XIV. 17. Eph. 3. 12. 1 Joh. 5. 14.
units.tr: From this depends (1) peace of conscience, because conscience in man holds in some way the place of God; Rom. 2. 14. Compare Rom. 5. 2; Rom. 14. 17; Eph. 3. 12; 1 John 5. 14.

units.la: 2. Ex hac promanat Pax cum rationalibus creaturis Deo morigeris; ac speciatim cum Angelis : Hebr. 12. 22. I. 14.
units.tr: (2) From this flows peace with rational creatures who are obedient to God, and especially with the angels: Heb. 12. 22; Heb. 1. 14.

units.la: 3. Mala, quae aliunde inferri possent, vel avertuntur, vel mirabiliter in bonum convertuntur: Prov. 16. 7. Cum placuerint Jehovae viae viri, etiam inimicos ejus pacatos reddet. Psal 118. 6. 1 Cor. 10. 13. Rom. 8. 28. Novimus, quod eos qui diligunt Deum omnia simul adjuvant in bonum.
units.tr: (3) Evils which might otherwise be brought in from elsewhere are either averted or wonderfully turned into good. Prov. 16. 7: When a man's ways please the LORD, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him. Ps. 118. 6; 1 Cor. 10. 13; Rom. 8. 28: We know that for those who love God all things work together for good.

units.la: 4. Accedit omnium bonorum affluentia: Psal. 72. 7. Florebit in diebus Ejus justus; & multitudo pacis, donec non sit luna. IV. 7, 8, 9. XVI. 5. 6. XXXVI. 3, 6, 11. &c.
units.tr: (4) To this is added an abundance of all good things. Ps. 72. 7: In his days the righteous shall flourish, and abundance of peace, until the moon is no more. Ps. 4. 7, 8, 9; Ps. 16. 5, 6; Ps. 36. 3, 6, 11, etc.

units.la: XXXIV. Amicitia vero communiter est Mutua
units.tr: XXXIV. Friendship, however, is commonly a mutual

units.la: quorundam, efficax, & aperta benevolentia. Hæc autem Amicitia inter Deum optimum, maximum, beatissimum, ac beneficentissimum; & inter fideles, quos Ipse pro singulari sua φιλανθρωπία ad istum statum beatissimum evehit. Quò autem magis inæqualis est hæc amicitia, quò miserior antecedens nostra conditio, quò beatior status ad quem evehimur; eò magis admiranda est hæc Dei nostri misericordia.
units.tr: goodwill, effective and open, between certain people. This friendship exists between God, the best, greatest, most blessed and most beneficent, and the faithful, whom He, by His singular philanthropy [φιλανθρωπία], raises to this most blessed state. But the more unequal this friendship is, the more wretched our previous condition and the more blessed the state to which we are raised, the more admirable is this mercy of our God.

units.la: Abraham, pater fidelium, amicus Dei vocatus est; Iac. 2. 23. Deus autem illi promiserat, Gen. 17. 7. Ut sim tibi in Deum, & semini tuo post te. Quod vidêl. exerturus esset suam Deitatem, adeoque infinitam potentiam, sapientiam, beatitudinem, & gloriam, circa ipsum, & semen ipsius, in bonum eorum; ad cujus feminis societatem, ac felicitatis communionem, nos etiam adsciti sumus. Huc quadrat illud, Psal. 33. 12. Beata gens, cujus Jehovah est Deus, &c. Confer Gen. 15. 1. Psal. 23. 1,--. & similia. Nostrum igitur est, vicissim Deo nostro sanctissimâ dilectione adhærere, voluntati ipsius conformari, ac gloriæ ipsius promovendæ per omnia operam dare: Psal. 73. 23. Gen. 17. 1. Rom. 12. 1,2. 1 Cor. 10. 31.
units.tr: Abraham, the father of the faithful, was called the friend of God; Jas. 2. 23. God had promised him, Gen. 17. 7: That I may be a God to you and to your seed after you. Namely, He was going to display His Deity, and so His infinite power, wisdom, blessedness and glory, toward him and his seed, for their good; and we too have been admitted into the fellowship of that seed and the communion of its happiness. To this fits Ps. 33. 12: Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD, etc. Compare Gen. 15. 1; Ps. 23. 1,--; and similar passages. It is therefore our task, in turn, to cling to our God with most holy love, to be conformed to His will, and to labour in every way to promote His glory: Ps. 73. 23; Gen. 17. 1; Rom. 12. 1, 2; 1 Cor. 10. 31.

units.la: XXXV. Succedit Adoptio; Actus gratiosus relati- vus & œconomicus, quo fideles justificati ac recon- ciliati assumuntur & evehuntur in dignitatem filiorum Dei.
units.tr: XXXV. Adoption follows: a relative and economic gracious act, by which believers who have been justified and reconciled are taken up and raised to the dignity of the sons of God.

units.la: Gal. 4. 5. Ut eos, qui Legi erant obnoxii, redimeret; ut Adoptionem filiorum reciperemus. III. 26. Omnes enim Filii Dei estis, per fidem, in Christo Jesu. Joh. I. 12. Quotquot Eum acceperunt, dedit eis hanc dignitatem, ut Filii Dei fierent, nempe iis qui credunt in nomen Ejus.
units.tr: Gal. 4. 5. That He might redeem those who were under the Law, and that we might receive the adoption of sons. III. 26. For you are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus. John 1. 12. As many as received Him, to them He gave the right to become sons of God, namely to those who believe in His name.

units.la: Actum gratiosum dicimus, juxta 1 Joh. 3. 1. Videte, qualem charitatem dedit nobis Pater, nempe ut Filii Dei vocemur. Sed relativum; quia formaliter infert, relativam statùs nostri mutationem. OEconomicum verò; quia ad familiam Dei spectat, statumque filialem pro formali termino habet. Eph. 2. 19. Concives sanctorum, ac domestici Dei. III. 15. Ex quo tota familia in cœlis & in terrâ nominatur.
units.tr: We call it a gracious act, in line with 1 John 3. 1. Behold what manner of love the Father has given us, that we should be called the sons of God. But it is relative, because it formally brings about a relative change in our standing. It is economic, because it pertains to the family of God and has the filial state as its formal term. Eph. 2. 19. Fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God. III. 15. From whom the whole family in heaven and on earth is named.

units.la: Hæc autem Filiatio non est propria & naturalis, ex generatione; qualis competit unigenito & proprio Filio Dei Patris: Joh. I. 14. III. 16. Rom. 8. 32. Psal. 2. 7. Hebr. I. 3, 5. Nec impropria generalis, ex gratiâ creationis ad imaginem Dei; sicut Adam Filius Dei appellatur, Luc. 3. 38. ad quam in electis Angelis accedit specialis gratia conservationis & confirmationis: sic isti Filii Dei vocantur. Joh. I. 6, II. 1. Neque communis hominum reproborum cum electis, ex gratiâ eminentiȩ Politicæ: unde Magistratus Filii Dei nuncupantur, Psal. 82. 6. vel externæ communionis in Fœdere Evangelico: quales etiàm Filii Dei, & Filii Regni appellantur. Gen. 6. 2. Matth. 8. 12. Sed gratiæ specialis ac salutaris, qualem descripsimus.
units.tr: This sonship, however, is not proper and natural, arising from generation, which belongs to the only-begotten and proper Son of God the Father: John 1. 14. 3. 16. Rom. 8. 32. Ps. 2. 7. Heb. 1. 3, 5. Nor is it improper and general, arising from the grace of creation in the image of God; thus Adam is called a son of God, Luke 3. 38. To this, in the elect angels, there is added a special grace of preservation and confirmation; in this way they too are called sons of God. John 1. 6; 2. 1. Nor is it the common sonship of reprobate men with the elect, arising from the grace of political eminence; whence magistrates are named sons of God, Ps. 82. 6; nor the sonship of external communion in the Gospel covenant; in this sense also the children of God and the sons of the kingdom are so called. Gen. 6. 2. Matt. 8. 12. Rather, it is the sonship of special and saving grace, of the kind we have described.

units.la: XXXVI. Adoptio peragitur formaliter in tempore; sed juxta decretum, quòd de eâ fuit ab æterno. Eph. I. 5. Prædestinavit nos, quos adoptaret in filios, --. Unde etiàm electi nondùm vocati, Filii Dei denominantur ὑιοὶ θεοῦ, Joh. XI. 52.
units.tr: XXXVI. Adoption takes place formally in time, but in accordance with the decree concerning it which existed from eternity. Eph. 1. 5. He predestined us to adoption as sons, ... Hence even the elect who are not yet called are named sons of God, υἱοὶ θεοῦ [huioi theou], John 11. 52.

units.la: Causa ejus efficiens prima, est Deus; & secundùm specialem appropriationem, Pater; ex ineffabili gratiâ & misericordiâ: Eph. I. 5. I. Joh. 3. 1.
units.tr: Its first efficient cause is God, and, according to the special appropriation, the Father; from ineffable grace and mercy. Eph. 1. 5. 1 John 3. 1.

units.la: Causa media est Christus, quâ Mediator; qui interim est Filius ille proprius & primogenitus: Rom. 8. 32. Hebr. I. 6. atque ut Filius domui suæ præest: Hebr. 3. 6. Et juxta II. 10,--13. Princeps salutis, multos Filios in gloriam adducens, --non erubescit Fratres ipsos vocare, &c.
units.tr: The intermediate cause is Christ, as Mediator; who, moreover, is that proper and firstborn Son. Rom. 8. 32. Heb. 1. 6. And as Son He presides over His house. Heb. 3. 6. And according to Heb. 2. 10-13: The captain of salvation, bringing many sons to glory, ... is not ashamed to call them brethren, etc.

units.la: In Christo autem, cùm Ipse Mediator constitutus est, ac porrò cùm reconciliationem nostri actû impetravit, virtualiter facta est Adoptio: sed nos eam formaliter demum consequimur per fidem nostram, una cum Justificatione & Reconciliatione applicata: Gal. 4. 4, 5, 6. III. 26. Joh. I. 12.
units.tr: In Christ, however, when He was constituted Mediator, and further when He obtained our reconciliation by His act, adoption was made virtually; but we attain it formally only through our faith, applied together with justification and reconciliation. Gal. 4. 4, 5, 6. III. 26. John 1. 12.

units.la: Eam sequitur speciális testificatio Spiritus: Rom. 8. 15, 16. Accepistis Spiritum adoptionis; per quem clamamus, Abba, Pater: Qui ipse Spiritus testatur una cum spiritu nostro, quod sumus filii Dei. Gal. 4. 5, 6. Nec tamen propterea cum Socinianis; eorumque sequacibus, putandum est, quod fides praecedat omnem Spiritus Sancti in nobis operationem: ipsa enim prima regeneratio & conversio ab Eo etiam procedit.
units.tr: There follows a special testimony of the Spirit. Rom. 8. 15, 16. You have received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, Abba, Father. The same Spirit bears witness together with our spirit that we are children of God. Gal. 4. 5, 6. Yet for all that, we must not think, with the Socinians and their followers, that faith precedes every operation of the Holy Spirit in us; for even the first regeneration and conversion proceeds from Him.

units.la: Consummata vero applicatio bonorum ex hac gratia resultantium, seu plena filiorum adoptivorum in possessionem missio, fiet novissimo die, in beata resurrectione: unde etiam haec metonymice Adoptionis nomine venit: Rom. 8. 23, 24. Adoptionem expectantes, id est, redemptionem corporis nostri. Nam spe servati sumus.
units.tr: The complete application of the benefits that result from this grace, or the full sending of adopted sons into their inheritance, will take place on the last day, in the blessed resurrection; hence this too is metonymically called by the name of adoption. Rom. 8. 23, 24. Waiting for adoption, that is, the redemption of our body. For we were saved by hope.

units.la: Interim privilegia statim adsunt insignia: Libertas Christiana, Filialis animi fiducia apud Patrem nostrum coelestem, Conformatio specialis cum Christo, ac tandem Haereditas.
units.tr: Meanwhile the outstanding privileges are present at once: Christian liberty, the filial confidence of spirit before our heavenly Father, special conformity to Christ, and finally the inheritance.

units.la: XXXVII. Primo occurrit Libertas Christiana:
units.tr: XXXVII. First comes Christian liberty:

units.la: 2 Cor. 3. 17. Ubi Spiritus ille Domini, illic Libertas. Gal. 4. 26. Illa quae sursum est Hierusalem, libera est, quae est mater omnium nostrum. Estque tum primaria, tum secundaria.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 3. 17. Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. Gal. 4. 26. That Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all. It is both primary and secondary.

units.la: Primaria est immunitas a servitute spirituali, ac miserà subjectione ad peccatum, mortem, & potestatem Diaboli. Respectu peccati, patet ex Joh. 8. 34, 35, 36. Omnis, qui committit peccatum, servus est peccati. Si ergo vos Filius in libertatem vindicarit, vere liberi eritis. Rom. 6. 14, 17, 18. Respectu mortis; Joh. 5. 24. Qui sermonem meum audit, & credit Ei qui misit me, habet vitam aeternam; & in condemnationem non veniet; sed transfivit à morte in vitam. Rom. 5. 17. VIII. 1. 1 Cor. 15. 22, 23, 53, -57. Respectu Diaboli; Hebr. 2. 14, 15. Ut per mortem aboleret eum, qui mortis habebat imperium, hoc est Diabolum: Et liberos redderet quotquot metu mortis, per omnem vitam obnoxii erant servituti. Rom. 16. 20. Deus pacis conteret Satanam sub pedes vestros citò.
units.tr: The primary liberty is immunity from spiritual servitude and wretched subjection to sin, death, and the power of the devil. With respect to sin, it is clear from John 8. 34, 35, 36: Everyone who commits sin is the servant of sin. If therefore the Son shall make you free, you shall be free indeed. Rom. 6. 14, 17, 18. With respect to death: John 5. 24. He who hears my word and believes Him who sent me has eternal life; and shall not come into condemnation, but has passed from death to life. Rom. 5. 17; 8. 1. 1 Cor. 15. 22, 23, 53-57. With respect to the devil: Heb. 2. 14, 15. That through death He might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil; and deliver all those who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage. Rom. 16. 20. The God of peace will crush Satan under your feet shortly.

units.la: Atque ista, quod ad rem ipsam, sub V. T. quoque obtinuit: quoniam regeneratio, justificatio, sanctificatio, & glorificatio inchoata, tunc etiam locum habuerunt. Graduum tamen differentia admittenda est; cùm haeredes tunc quasi infantes essent: Gal. 4. 1.
units.tr: And this, as far as the thing itself is concerned, held good under the Old Testament also, since regeneration, justification, sanctification, and the beginnings of glorification were then present as well. Yet a difference of degrees must be allowed, since the heirs were then, as it were, infants. Gal. 4. 1.

units.la: XXXVIII. Secundaria est immunitas à paedagogiâ Legis: ubi insigne est discrimen Vet. ac N.T. Gal. 3. 23, 24, 25. Antequàm venisset fides (Euangelii impleti), sub Legis praesidio tenebamur conclusi,--. Itaque Lex paedagogus noster fuit in Christum respiciens,--. At postquàm venit fides, non amplius sub paedagogo sumus. IV. 1,--4. Interim à Lege morali, quantum ad usum normalem, non sumus immunes: sic enim ipsa est Lex libertatis; Jac. I. 25. II. 12. & perpetua regula obedientiae Patri nostro coelesti praestandae; Matth. 5: 16,--20. unde Paulus diserte, 1 Cor. 9. 21. Cùm non sim exlex Deo; sed in Lege in Christo.
units.tr: XXXVIII. Secondary liberty is immunity from the tutelage of the Law, in which there is a notable difference between the Old and New Testaments. Gal. 3. 23, 24, 25. Before faith came (the faith of the fulfilled Gospel), we were kept under the custody of the Law, shut up ... So the Law was our tutor, leading us to Christ ... But after faith has come, we are no longer under a tutor. 4. 1-4. Yet we are not free from the moral Law, as far as its normal use goes; for in this sense it is the law of liberty, James 1. 25; 2. 12, and the perpetual rule of obedience to be rendered to our heavenly Father; Matt. 5. 16-20. Whence Paul plainly says, 1 Cor. 9. 21. Not being without law to God, but under the law to Christ.

units.la: Verùm in consideratione Foederali occurrit Condemnatio, per ejus Sanctionem: unde fideles per Christum liberati sunt; quod ad Libertatem primariam pertinet. Occurrit etiàm rigida istius Foederis inculcatio, & frequens ejus repetitio, pro paedagogiâ V. T. Accessit Lex Cerimonialis; quae materialiter istud jugum fecit gravius: atque item Forensis Mosaica. At verò sub N. T. instructiones & consolationes Euangelicae admodùm clare & copiosè subministrantur: Lex Cerimonialis abrogata est; itemque Forensis Mosaica, quatenùs ad istam Politiam spectabat in specie. Vide sup. cap. XI. th. 41. & 46.
units.tr: But in the federal consideration there is condemnation through its sanction; from this the faithful have been freed through Christ, and this pertains to the primary liberty. There is also the rigid insistence of that covenant and its frequent repetition, befitting the tutelage of the Old Testament. The ceremonial Law was added, which made this yoke materially heavier, and likewise the Mosaic forensic law. But under the New Testament, evangelical instructions and consolations are supplied very clearly and abundantly; the ceremonial Law has been abrogated, and likewise the Mosaic forensic law, insofar as it pertained specifically to that polity. See above, chap. XI, th. 41 and 46.

units.la: Hæc autem Libertas nunc omninò agnosci atque observari debet ; postquàm Lex illa non solùm in morte Christi mortua, sed etiàm deinceps sepulta, ac mortifera facta est. Col. 2. 14. Delctum, quod adversùm nos erat, rituum chirographum, quod erat nobis subcontrarium, Ipse cruci affixum è medio sustulit. Gal. 5. 1, 2, 3. In Libertate igitur, quâ Christus nos liberavit, perstate ; & ne regredientes, implicamini Servitutis jugo. Ecce, ego Paulus dico vobis, si circumcidami, Christum nihil vobis profuturum. Testor enim rursùm omni homini qui circumciditur, eum esse debitorem totius Legis servandæ. Adde Gal. 4. 9, 10, 11. Col. 2. 16, 17.
units.tr: This liberty, moreover, must now be wholly acknowledged and observed, since that Law was not only dead in the death of Christ, but was afterwards buried and made deadly. Col. 2. 14. He blotted out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to His cross. Gal. 5. 1, 2, 3. Stand fast, therefore, in the liberty by which Christ has made us free, and do not be entangled again in the yoke of bondage. Behold, I Paul say to you, that if you are circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing. For I testify again to every man who is circumcised that he is a debtor to keep the whole Law. Add Gal. 4. 9, 10, 11. Col. 2. 16, 17.

units.la: Obj. 1. At Paulus ipse Timotheum circumcidit; Act. 16. 3. Resp. Id fecit, priusquàm Libertas ista satis esset promulgata & confirmata inter Judæos; & Lex cerimonialis honestè sepulta: non ex religione ac necessitate istius cultûs; sed ad evitandum scandalum, quod Judæi infirmi cæteroquin erant sumturi ex societate illius incircumcisi in ministerio Evangelii. Sic Apostolus se Judæis factum dicit, ut Judæum ; ut eos Christo lucrifaceret ; 1 Cor. 9. 20, 22. Vide etiàm Act. 21. 20. Sed cùm satis promulgata & confirmata esset illa Libertas ; Titum minimè circumcidit ; Gal. 2. 3, 4, 5.
units.tr: Obj. 1. But Paul himself circumcised Timothy; Acts 16:3. Resp. He did this before that liberty had been sufficiently promulgated and confirmed among the Jews, and before the ceremonial law had been honourably buried. He did it not from any religious conviction or necessity of that worship, but to avoid giving offence, which the Jews, being weak, would otherwise have taken from his fellowship in the ministry of the Gospel with an uncircumcised man. So the Apostle says that he became to the Jews as a Jew, that he might win them to Christ; 1 Cor. 9:20, 22. See also Acts 21:20. But once that liberty had been sufficiently promulgated and confirmed, he by no means circumcised Titus; Gal. 2:3-5.

units.la: XXXVIII. Cùm Deus libertatem nobis fecerit ab istis statutis suis propriis; multò minùs voluit conscientias nostras premi jugo statutorum humanorum, aut qualiumcunque superstitionum. Col. 2. 8.
units.tr: XXXVIII. Since God has freed us from his own ceremonial statutes, much less has he wished our consciences to be burdened with the yoke of human statutes or of any superstitions whatever. Col. 2:8.

units.la: Videte, ne quis sit, qui vos depredetur per Philosophiam & inanem seductionem, secundùm traditionem hominum, secundùm elementa mundi, & non secundùm Christum. 20,--23. „Itaque si mortui cum Christo, liberi estis „ab elementis mundi, quid ut viventes in mundo, „ritibus oneramini; Ne ederis, neque gustaris, neque „attigeris? Quæ omnia ipso usu corrumpuntur, præ„scripta ex præceptis & doctrinis hominum: Quæ ratio„nem quidem habent sapientiæ in cultu voluntario & submissione animi, & in eo quòd corpori non parcant; nec tamen ullius sunt pretii, cùm ad ea „spectent quibus farcitur caro. 1 Cor. 7. 23. Pretio emti estis; ne estote servi hominum.
units.tr: See to it that no one takes you captive through philosophy and empty deceit, according to the tradition of men, according to the elemental spirits of the world, and not according to Christ. Col. 2:8, 20-23. "If therefore you died with Christ and are free from the elemental spirits of the world, why, as though living in the world, do you submit to regulations: 'Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch'? All these things perish with the using, being precepts and doctrines of men. These have indeed an appearance of wisdom in self-chosen worship and humility of mind, and in not sparing the body; yet they are of no value whatever, since they serve only the gratification of the flesh." 1 Cor. 7:23. You were bought with a price; do not become slaves of men. Pretio emti estis; ne estote servi hominum.

units.la: Alia tamen est ratio Legum ac Statutorum Politicorum, quæ à Principe, vel Magistratu, deducuntur ex Lege Divina Morali, & æquitate naturali, ad commune bonum societatis civilis; contra Anabaptistas. Vide sup. cap. 9. th. 3. & 73.
units.tr: There is, however, a different principle for the laws and political statutes which the prince or magistrate enacts from the divine moral law and natural equity for the common good of civil society; this is against the Anabaptists. See above, chap. 9, th. 3 and 73.

units.la: Similiter in rebus adiaphoris & licitis tenendæ sunt Regulæ, ab ipso Deo circa eas præscriptæ. Vide sup. cap. 8. th. 27. Vitandum ergò est Scandalum, hoc est, ejusmodi factum, quo alius in via veritatis, quæ est secundùm pietatem, offenditur atque impeditur. Rom. 14. 13. Hic potius adhibete judicium, ut ne fratri proponatis quippiam ad quod impingat, vel offendat. Adde Matth. 18. 6,–9. Hic verò interdum utrimque peccatur; ubi scandalum datum & acceptum concurrunt. Scandalum datum, est peccatum dantis; quo ipse alteri præbet causam offensionis, sive facto aliquo absolutè & semper malo; sive aliàs licitò quidem, sed istis circumstantiis non conveniente, propter libertatis abusum. Acceptum, est peccatum accipientis; quo is offenditur ex facto alterius. Fieri tamen potest, ut quis alteri causam offensionis objiciat, nec tamen is offendatur: ubi solius dantis peccatum est. Aliquando etiàm per accidens propriæ malitiæ contingit, ut quis offendatur bono opere, & bene facto; vel etiàm passione alterius: quod, discriminis causa, scandalum sumtum aliqui vocant. Sic Christus 1 Petr. 2. 7. dicitur, Lapis ad quem impingitur, & petra offendiculi. & Luc. 2. 34. positus casui & resurrectioni multorum in Israël, & in signum cui contradicatur. Confer Matth. 13. 57. XV. 12. XXXVI. 31.
units.tr: Similarly, in matters indifferent and lawful the rules laid down by God himself concerning them must be observed. See above, chap. 8, th. 27. Therefore scandal is to be avoided, that is, a deed by which another is offended and hindered on the way of truth, which is according to godliness. Rom. 14:13. Judge rather this, that you put no stumbling block or occasion of falling before a brother. Add Matt. 18:6-9. Here, however, sometimes sin is committed on both sides, where scandal given and scandal taken coincide. Scandal given is the sin of the one who gives it, by which he himself provides another with an occasion of offence, either by a deed that is absolutely and always evil, or by one that is otherwise lawful but unsuited to these circumstances, on account of the abuse of liberty. Scandal taken is the sin of the one who receives it, by which he is offended at another's deed. It can happen, however, that someone holds out to another an occasion of offence, and yet that other is not offended; in that case the sin belongs to the giver alone. Sometimes too it happens, through the accident of one's own malice, that someone is offended by a good work and a well-done deed, or even by another's suffering; for the sake of distinction some call this scandal taken. Thus Christ is called, 1 Pet. 2:7, "a stone over which men stumble, and a rock of offence," and, Luke 2:34, "set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel, and for a sign that is spoken against." Compare Matt. 13:57; 15:12; 36:31.

units.la: Hic peccatum solummodò est insumente. Ei affine est scandalum proprium; ubi quis peccato habituali proprio, vel etiàm cupiditate, aut pravâ ratiocinatione actuali, sibi ipsi existit causa amplius peccandi. Matth. 18: 8, 9. Si verò manus tua, aut pes tuus, facit ut tu offendas, &c. cum Jac. 1, 14, 15.
units.tr: Here the sin lies only in the one who takes offence. Akin to this is one's own scandal, where someone, through his own habitual sin, or even through desire, or through a perverse actual reasoning, becomes to himself the cause of sinning further. Matt. 18:8, 9. If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, etc., compare Jas. 1:14, 15.

units.la: XXXVII. Sedulò autem cavendum, ne perpe- ràm arripiatur Libertas, ut data carni occasio, aut ma- litiæ velamen: Gal. 5. 13. 1 Petr. 2. 16.
units.tr: XXXVII. Great care, however, must be taken that liberty is not rashly seized upon as an occasion for the flesh or a cover for malice; Gal. 5:13; 1 Pet. 2:16.

units.la: ne profanitas, iniquitas, luxus, impuritas, stultiloquium, &c. accenseantur adiaphoris & licitis; aut culicum nomine, missis fcil. camelis, deglutiantur. Vide Matth. 5. 19. XII, 36. XXIII. 23, 24. Eph. 5. 2, 3, 4, 15, 16, 17. 1 Thess. 5. 22. Judæ, 23.
units.tr: Let profanity, iniquity, luxury, impurity, foolish talk and the like not be counted among things indifferent and lawful, nor be swallowed down under the pretext of straining out gnats while letting camels through. See Matt. 5:19; 12:36; 23:23, 24. Eph. 5:2, 3, 4, 15, 16, 17. 1 Thess. 5:22. Jude 23.

units.la: Similiter, circa confessionem fidei, attendendum est contra Libertinos, Socinianos, Remonstrantes, &c. ne prætextu libertatis prophetandi, hæreses & errores noxii spargantur; atque itâ puritas fidei vitietur, unitas Ecclesiæ scindatur, & tranquillitas publica turbetur: Tit. I, 7, - 11. III, 8, 9, 10. Gal. 1. 7, 8, 9.
units.tr: Similarly, with regard to the confession of faith, attention must be paid against the Libertines, the Socinians, the Remonstrants and others, lest under the pretext of liberty to prophesy, harmful heresies and errors be spread abroad; and thus the purity of the faith be corrupted, the unity of the Church be torn apart, and public tranquillity be disturbed. Titus 1:7-11; 3:8-10. Gal. 1:7, 8, 9.

units.la: XXXVIII. Accedit Filialis animi fiducia apud Patrem nostrum cœlestem: postquàm enim per Spiritum adoptionis cognovimus, nos verè in istam dignitatem affumtos & evectos esse à Patre cœlesti, animo humili quidem & reverenti coram Ipso comparemus jugiter; sic tamen ut solidam fiduciam interim habeamus in tantâ Ipsius gratiâ & salute per Christum, tùm in orationibus adIpsum, tùm etiàm in universâ vitâ nostra. Eph. 3. 12: In Quo habemus loquendi libertatem, & aditum cum fiducia, per fidem Ipsius. Hebr. 4. 16. 1 Joh. 5. 14. Matth. 7. 11. Rom. 8. 38, 39. Pfal. 2. 11. Phil. 2. 12. Quin & ipsæ castigationes, paternum Dei erga nos affectum declarant luculenter: Hebr. 12. 6, 7, 8. Rom. 5. 3. &c.
units.tr: XXXVIII. There is also the filial confidence of spirit before our heavenly Father. For once we have come to know through the Spirit of adoption that we have truly been taken up and raised to this dignity by the heavenly Father, we ought always to approach him with a humble and reverent mind, yet so as meanwhile to have a firm confidence in so great a grace and salvation of his through Christ, both in prayers addressed to him and in our whole life. Eph. 3:12: In whom we have boldness of speech and access with confidence through his faith. Heb. 4:16. 1 John 5:14. Matt. 7:11. Rom. 8:38, 39. Ps. 2:11. Phil. 2:12. Indeed, even chastisements clearly declare God's fatherly affection towards us; Heb. 12:6, 7, 8. Rom. 5:3, etc.

units.la: XXXIX. Specialis conformatio cum Christo ea est, ut trans-
units.tr: XXXIX. The special conformity with Christ is this: that we are trans-

units.la: transformemur ad proximam quandam fimilitudinem cum isto Fratre nostro primogenito, quemadmodum arctissime cum Ipso uniti sumus. Rom. 8.29. Nam quos praescivit, etiam praedestinavit conformandos imagini Filii sui; ut Is sit primogenitus inter multos fratres. Gal. 4.19. Filioli mei, quos iterum parturio, usquequo formetur Christus in vobis. Unde Ecclesia mystice etiam Christus appellatur, propter intimam & arctissimam unionem cum isto Capite suo; 1 Cor. 12. 12. Act. 9. 4, 5. Matt. xxv. 35, 36, 40. & Concio Primogenitorum qui conscripti sunt in caelis; Hebr. 12. 23. Quin imo propter unctionis participationem de qua sup. cap. 12. th. 1. & 34. Christiani suo modo etiam facti sunt Prophetae, Sacerdotes, & Reges.
units.tr: transformed into a certain close likeness to this our firstborn Brother, just as we are most closely united with Him. Rom. 8.29: For whom He foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He might be the firstborn among many brothers. Gal. 4.19: My little children, for whom I am again in labour until Christ is formed in you. Hence the Church is also mystically called Christ, on account of her intimate and most close union with this her Head: 1 Cor. 12.12; Acts 9.4, 5; Matt. 25.35, 36, 40; and the assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, Heb. 12.23. Indeed, through participation in the anointing, of which above, ch. 12, th. 1, and 34, Christians have in their own way also been made prophets, priests, and kings.

units.la: Prophetae quidem, respectu cognitionis mysteriorum Dei, quae aliis quoque charitativa instructione ad mutuam aedificationem proponere & explicare possunt ac debent. Act. 2. 17, 18. ex Joël. 2.28, 29. Erit ultimis diebus; (dicit Deus:) effundam ex Spiritu meo in quamvis carnem: & Prophetabunt filii vestri, & filiae vestrae, &c.
units.tr: As priests, inasmuch as they have been sanctified to God, they draw near to Him familiarly, and offer spiritual sacrifices of gratitude toward God and of beneficence toward their neighbour. Rev. 1:6: "He has made us kings and priests to God and His Father." 1 Pet. 2:5: "A holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God through Jesus Christ." Verse 9: "A royal priesthood," ... "that you may proclaim His virtues." Rom. 12:1: "That you present your bodies a living, holy sacrifice, pleasing to God, your reasonable worship." Heb. 13:16: "But do not forget beneficence and fellowship, for with such sacrifices God is pleased."

units.la: Sacerdotes, quatenus Deo sanctificati, ad Ipsum familiariter accedunt; & spiritualia sacrificia gratitudinis erga Deum, ac beneficentiae erga proximum suum, offerunt. Apoc. I. 6. Fecit nos Reges & Sacerdotes Deo & Patri suo. 1 Petr. 2. 5. Sacerdotium sanctum, ad offerendum spirituales hostias, acceptas Deo per Iesum Christum. 9. Regale sacerdotium, -. ut virtutes praedicetis Illius, -. Rom. 12. 1. Ut sistatis corpora vestra hostiam vivam, sanctam, placentem Deo, rationalem illum cultum vestrum. Hebr. 13. 16. Beneficentiae vero & communicationis ne oblivisciminí: talibus enim victimis delectatur Deus.
units.tr: Priests, inasmuch as they are sanctified to God, approach Him familiarly and offer spiritual sacrifices of gratitude toward God and of beneficence toward their neighbour. Rev. 1.6: He made us kings and priests to God and His Father. 1 Pet. 2.5: A holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. 2.9: A royal priesthood, ... that you may proclaim the virtues of Him, ... Rom. 12.1: That you present your bodies as a living, holy sacrifice, pleasing to God, which is your rational worship. Heb. 13.16: But do not forget beneficence and sharing, for God is pleased with such sacrifices.

units.la: Reges denique, quatenus Christi participes, & spiritualiter nobilitati, Ipsius virtute hostes spirituales facile subjiciunt, ac de iis triumphant; adhaec domini-um um spirituale in res alias obtinent, & cum Christo in thronum ipsius evehendi sunt. Apoc. I. 6. 1 Petr. II. 9. Item Act. 17. 11. Fuerunt isti generosiores, &c. Rom. 16. 20, Joh. 16. 33. Rom. 8. 37. In his omnibus amplius quàm victores sumus, per Eum qui dilexit nos. 1 Cor. III. 21, 22. 23. Omnia namque vestra sunt, -. Apoc. III. 21, 22. Qui vicerit, tribuam ci ut sedeat mecum in throno meo; ut & Ego vici, & sedeo cum Patre meo in throno Ejus.
units.tr: Kings, finally, inasmuch as they are partakers of Christ and spiritually ennobled, by His power easily subdue their spiritual enemies and triumph over them; moreover they obtain a spiritual dominion over other things, and are to be raised with Christ to His throne. Rev. 1.6; 1 Pet. 2.9. Likewise Acts 17.11: These were more noble, etc. Rom. 16.20; John 16.33; Rom. 8.37: In all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us. 1 Cor. 3.21, 22, 23: For all things are yours, ... Rev. 3.21, 22: To him who overcomes I will grant to sit with Me on My throne, as I also overcame and sit with My Father on His throne.

units.la: XL. Hæreditas tandem gloriosissima est ac beatissima.
units.tr: XL. Finally, the inheritance is most glorious and most blessed.

units.la: Rom. 8. 17. Quòdsi Filii, etiam Hæredes: Hæredes quidem Dei, Coheredes autem Christi. Gal. 4. 1. Hæres Dominus omnium. 1 Cor. 3. 21, 22, 23. Sic modò restitutum habemus dominium spirituale quarumvis rerum: unde etiam fluit, omnium ad hanc vitam sustentandam & pie condecorandam spectantium, usus purus coram Domino: Tit. I. 15. Omnia munda mundis. Rom. 14: 14. 1 Cor. 10. 25, 26. Quin & Angeli ministerio pro iis funguntur: Hebr. I. 14.
units.tr: Rom. 8.17: But if sons, then also heirs: heirs indeed of God, and co-heirs with Christ. Gal. 4.1: The Lord of all is heir. 1 Cor. 3.21, 22, 23. Thus we now have restored to us a spiritual dominion over all things; whence also flows the pure use, before the Lord, of all things that pertain to sustaining this life and adorning it piously: Titus 1.15: To the pure all things are pure. Rom. 14.14; 1 Cor. 10.25, 26. Indeed the angels also serve on their behalf in ministry: Heb. 1.14.

units.la: In altero autem sæculo, cœlesti beatitudine & gloria æterna fruemur, etiam hæreditaris titulo; qui quidem adjicitur titulo juris, ex justificatione: Rom. 8. 17. 1 Joh. 3. 2. Dilecti, nunc filii Dei sumus: scimus autem fore, ut cum Ipse factus fuerit manifestus, similes ei simus: quoniam videbimus Eum sicuti est.
units.tr: In the other age, however, we shall enjoy heavenly blessedness and eternal glory, also by the title of inheritance; which title is indeed added to the title of right that comes from justification: Rom. 8.17; 1 John 3.2: Beloved, now we are children of God; and it has not yet been revealed what we shall be, but we know that when He appears we shall be like Him, because we shall see Him as He is.

units.la: XLI. Ista igitur Adoptio est longè eminentissima ac saluberrima; captum mundi prorsùs exsuperans:
units.tr: XLI. This adoption, therefore, is by far the most eminent and most salutary, utterly surpassing the grasp of the world:

units.la: 1 Joh. 3. 1. Videte, qualem charitatem dedit nobis Pater: nempe ut Filii Dei vocemur: propterea mundus non novit nos, quia non novit Eum.
units.tr: 1 John 3.1: See what kind of love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God; for this reason the world does not know us, because it did not know Him.

units.la: Plurimùm verò differt ab Adoptione, quæ apud homines aliquando peragitur. Humana enim Adoptio I. fieri fere solet ob defectum, vel indigentiam, filii naturalis. Hic autem Filius naturalis ab æterno præexistebat: attamen Pater cœlestis ex abundapundantia bonitatis suæ fideles adoptat; Filiique naturalis similitudinem quandam, & conjunctionem cum eo mysticam, adoptivis communicat.
units.tr: It differs very much from the adoption that is sometimes carried out among men. For, first, human adoption usually takes place on account of the lack or need of a natural son. But this natural Son existed from eternity; nevertheless the heavenly Father, out of the abundance of His goodness, adopts the faithful, and communicates to the adopted a certain likeness to the natural Son and a mystical conjunction with Him.

units.la: 2. Illa in denominatione, & rerum externarum communicatione, consistit. Hæc non fit sine actione intrinsecâ, & novæ vitæ productione.
units.tr: 2. The former consists in a change of name and in the communication of external goods. The latter does not happen without an intrinsic action and the production of new life.

units.la: 3. Illa solet esse personæ extraneæ, non nisi ex adoptione jus habentis ad hæreditatem. Hi verò adoptivi jam ante per justificationem ex merito Christi jus sibi adjudicatum habent; ad quod sublimior iste titulus accedit.
units.tr: 3. The former is usually of a person outside the family, who has a right to the inheritance only through adoption. But these adopted children already have a right adjudged to them beforehand, through justification, from the merit of Christ; to which this more exalted title is added.

units.la: 4. Juxta illam filius patri in hæreditate succedit. Hic adoptivi participes fiunt hæreditatis assignatæ, ipsoPatre & Filio primogenito in æternum manentibus.
units.tr: 4. In the former, a son succeeds his father in the inheritance. In the latter, the adopted become sharers in the inheritance assigned to them, the Father Himself and the firstborn Son remaining in it for ever.

units.la: XLII. Pro Praxi;
units.tr: XLII. For Practice;

units.la: 1. Fidei nostræ veritatem per fructus suos sedulò exploremus, ut de Justificatione etiàm certi simus: 2 Cor. 13. 5. Jac. II. 18. Ac pro isto beneficio animum gratum præstemus jugiter: quò magis refellatur Adversariorum calumnia, doctrinam nostram esse pietati inimicam: Psal. 103. 1, 4, 10, 11, 12. cxvi. 12. cxxx. 4. Luc. 7. 47. 1 Petr. 3. 1, 2.
units.tr: 1. Let us diligently test the truth of our faith by its fruits, so that we may also be certain of justification: 2 Cor. 13:5. James 2:18. And let us constantly show a grateful mind for this benefit, so that the calumny of our adversaries, that our doctrine is hostile to piety, may be the more refuted: Ps. 103:1, 4, 10, 11, 12; 116:12; 130:4. Luke 7:47. 1 Pet. 3:1, 2.

units.la: 2. Pacem cum Deo nostro ficcolamus, ut ne iterum ad stultitiam convertamur: Psal. lxxxv. 9. ac propterea deseramus amicitiam hujus mundi: 1 Joh. II. 15. 16. cum 1 Reg. 15. 19.
units.tr: 2. Let us cherish peace with our God, so that we may not turn back again to folly: Ps. 85:9; and therefore let us forsake the friendship of this world: 1 John 2:15, 16, with 1 Kings 15:19.

units.la: 3. Patrem nostrum cœlestem filiali reverentia sancte colamus ac diligamus: Mal. I. 6. 1 Joh. 3. 2, 3. IV. 19. Deut. 32. 6. Et fiduciam in Ipso habeamus constanter; etiàm in mediis afflictionibus: Eph. 3. 12. Hebr. 3. 14. IV. 16. Matth. 7. 11. Heb. 12. 6, 7, 8.
units.tr: 3. Let us holily honour and love our heavenly Father with filial reverence: Mal. 1:6; 1 John 3:2, 3; 4:19; Deut. 32:6. And let us constantly have confidence in Him, even in the midst of afflictions: Eph. 3:12; Heb. 3:14; 4:16; Matt. 7:11; Heb. 12:6, 7, 8.

units.la: 4. Liberati per Redemtorem Jesum, ne revertamur ad turpissimam servitutem peccati, sub gravissimam tyrannidem Diaboli: in libertate istâ stemus; neque ulli creaturæ conscientias nostras subjiciamus:
units.tr: 4. Having been set free through the Redeemer Jesus, let us not return to the most shameful slavery of sin, under the most grievous tyranny of the Devil: let us stand in this liberty, and let us not subject our consciences to any creature.

units.la: Cap.XV. De Justificatione, Reconcil. & Adopt. 613
units.tr: Chapter XV. On Justification, Reconciliation and Adoption. 613

units.la: ciamus : Gal. 5. 1, 2. Joh. 8. 34, 35, 36. Rom. 2. 14, 17, 18. XVI. 20. 1 Petr. 5. 8, 9. Hebr. 12. 16. Imitagini Christi magis conformemur indies: Rom. 8. 29.
units.tr: ...let us not submit ourselves: Gal. 5. 1, 2. Joh. 8. 34, 35, 36. Rom. 2. 14, 17, 18. XVI. 20. 1 Petr. 5. 8, 9. Hebr. 12. 16. Let us be conformed more and more day by day to the image of Christ: Rom. 8. 29.

units.la: 1 Cor. XI. 1. Gal. 5. 19. Matth. 16. 24. XI. 29. Instructioni mutuae operam demus: 1 Thess. 5. 11. Col. 3. 16. Hebr. 3, 13. 1 Petr. 11. 9. Nos ipsos, & nostra, hostiam gratam Deo offeramus: Rom. 12. 1. 1 Petr. 2. 5. Hebr. 13. 16. Fortiter adversus hostes spirituales depugnemus, ad thronum Regni coelestis adspirantes: Eph. 6. 10, 18. 1 Petr. 5. 8, 9. Apoc. 3. 21, 22.
units.tr: 1 Cor. XI. 1. Gal. 5. 19. Matth. 16. 24. XI. 29. Let us apply ourselves diligently to mutual instruction: 1 Thess. 5. 11. Col. 3. 16. Hebr. 3, 13. 1 Petr. 11. 9. Let us offer ourselves and our possessions as a sacrifice acceptable to God: Rom. 12. 1. 1 Petr. 2. 5. Hebr. 13. 16. Let us fight bravely against spiritual enemies, aspiring to the throne of the heavenly kingdom: Eph. 6. 10, 18. 1 Petr. 5. 8, 9. Apoc. 3. 21, 22.

units.la: 5. Haereditatem illam beatissimam certò speremus; atque itâ omnes hujus vitae labores & calamitates solemur: Rom. 8. 17, 25, 28. 1 Joh. III. 1, 2.
units.tr: 5. Let us firmly hope for that most blessed inheritance, and so console ourselves in all the labours and calamities of this life: Rom. 8. 17, 25, 28. 1 Joh. III. 1, 2.

units.la: CAP. XVI.
units.tr: CAP. XVI.

units.la: De Sanctificatione.
units.tr: Concerning Sanctification.

units.la: S Anctificatio. Sanctitas varia. 1. Actio realis. Efficientia Dei: Christi: Spiritus S. Verbi; & Sa-cramentorum. 2. Subjecta. 3. Termini. Idea. 4. Non consistit in solâ actuum emendatione: c. Socin. &c. 5. Ex habitibus actûs secundi. Praxis fidei & resipiscentiæ. 6. Errores Pontif. de Pœnitentiâ, tan-quàm speciali actû justitiæ: & Sacramento. 7. De ejus materiâ & formâ. 8. Confessio. 9. Auricularis, Pontif. refut. 10. Objectiones solv. 11. Bona operâ. Ex fide. 12. In gloriam Dei. 13. Secundùm Legem ipsius. 14. Non sufficit opinio cultûs Divini. Nec εὐλαβείας, &c. 15. Illorum utilitas. Necessitas, 16. Perfectio varia. 17. Perfectio graduum non in hâc vitâ : c. Pontif. Socin. &c. 18. Objectiones solv. 19. Praxis. 20.
units.tr: Sanctification. Holiness is of various kinds. 1. The real act. The efficient causes: God, Christ, the Holy Spirit, the Word and the Sacraments. 2. The subjects. 3. The termini; the idea. 4. It does not consist in the mere amendment of acts, against the Socinians etc. 5. It arises from the habits of the second act. Practice of faith and repentance. 6. The errors of the Papists about repentance, as a special act of justice, and about the Sacrament. 7. Its matter and form. 8. Confession. 9. Auricular confession; the Papists refuted. 10. Objections answered. 11. Good works from faith. 12. To the glory of God. 13. According to his Law. 14. The opinion of divine worship is not enough, nor is piety (eulabeia) etc. 15. Their usefulness and necessity. 16. Various kinds of perfection. 17. The perfection of degrees is not in this life, against the Papists, Socinians etc. 18. Objections answered. 19. Practice. 20.

units.la: I. [S]Equitur ex ordine Sanctificatio; Actio realis, quâ redemti vocati & justificati deinceps à turpitudine peccati transformantur ad puritatem imaginis Dei, & ad gloriam ipsius.
units.tr: I. Sanctification follows in order. It is a real act by which those who have been redeemed, called and justified are thereafter transformed from the filthiness of sin into the purity of the image of God and into his glory.

units.la: Nomen Sanctus à verbo sancio deducitur; & in creaturis rationalibus vitiorum expertem notat. Affines sunt Justitia & Sanctitas: unde Luc. I. 74, 75. Serviamus Ipsi cum sanctitate & justitiâ. Justitia tamen proprie dici videtur respectu juris; aut legis, quæ juris est norma: Sanctitas verò respectu ipsius Dei, & similitudinis cum ipso. Levit. xi. 44, 45. Estote sancti, quia sanctus sum. Confer 19. 2. xx. 7, 8, 26. 1 Petr. I. 16.
units.tr: The name "holy" is derived from the verb "to sanctify" and, in rational creatures, denotes freedom from vices. Righteousness and holiness are related, whence Luke 1:74, 75: "that we might serve him in holiness and righteousness." Righteousness, however, seems properly to be spoken of with respect to law, or to right, of which the law is the rule; but holiness with respect to God himself and to likeness to him. Lev. 11:44, 45: "Be holy, for I am holy." Compare Lev. 19:2; 20:7, 8, 26; 1 Pet. 1:16.

units.la: Sanctitas in universum vel est essentialis & independens; Dei. 1 Sam. II. 2. Isf. 40. 25. Apoc. 15. 3, 4. vel accidentalis & dependens; creaturarum. Hæc rursus; vel in rebus inanimatis; relativa ad Deum, ejusque cultum, Exod. III. 5. xii. 16. xv. 13. xxviii. 2, 4. xxix. 6, 29, 31, 33. xxx. 25, 31, 32. xxxi. 10, 14, 15. &c. vel illustrior, in creaturis rationalibus, quæ tum personæ, tum actionis, notans conformitatem cum voluntate Dei.
