units.tr: Holiness in general is either essential and independent, belonging to God (1 Sam. 2:2; Isa. 40:25; Rev. 15:3, 4), or accidental and dependent, belonging to creatures. The latter is again either in inanimate things, relative to God and his worship (Exod. 3:5; 12:16; 15:13; 28:2, 4; 29:6, 29, 31, 33; 30:25, 31, 32; 31:10, 14, 15, etc.), or, more conspicuously, in rational creatures, which is spoken of both of persons and of actions, denoting conformity with the will of God.

units.la: Personæ sanctitas, respectu ortûs, vel est originalis; vel adventitia.
units.tr: The holiness of a person, with respect to origin, is either original or adventitious.

units.la: Originalis ex creatione in Angelis & Hominibus fuit; utpote ad imaginem Dei conditis: Matth. 25. 31. Dan. 4. 13. Ex conceptione, in Christo: Luc. I, 35.
units.tr: Original holiness from creation existed in angels and in men, as they were made in the image of God (Matt. 25:31; Dan. 4:13). From conception it existed in Christ (Luke 1:35).

units.la: Adventitia homini lapso accidit tum in hac tum in futurâ vitâ. In hâc vitâ irregenitis obtingit relativa quædam sanctitas externa, vel etiam interna non salutaris. Sed regenitorum sanctitas est tum externa per imputationem; tùm interna salutaris, ex mystica unione & communione cum Christo per Sp. S. 1 Cor.6. 11. Sanctificati estis in nomine Domini Iesu, & per Spiritum Dei nostri. Eph. 5,25,26. Sed post hanc vitam erit perfectissima sanctitas glorificatorum: Eph.5,27.
units.tr: Adventitious holiness comes to fallen man both in this life and in the life to come. In this life, the unregenerate obtain a certain relative external holiness, or even an internal holiness that is not saving. But the holiness of the regenerate is both external, through imputation, and internal and saving, arising from mystical union and communion with Christ through the Holy Spirit (1 Cor. 6:11: "You were sanctified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God"; Eph. 5:25, 26). But after this life there will be the most perfect holiness of the glorified (Eph. 5:27).

units.la: II. Sanctificationis genus constituimus actionem realem: quia terminus ad quem reali efficientia produci debet. Sic Deo tribuitur haec actio: 1 Thess. 5,23. Deus pacis sanctificet vos totos. Joh. 17, 17. Ezech. 36, 25, 26, 27.
units.tr: II. We set down the genus of sanctification as a real act, because the terminus to which it leads must be produced by real efficacy. Thus this act is ascribed to God (1 Thess. 5:23: "May the God of peace sanctify you wholly"; John 17:17; Ezek. 36:25, 26, 27).

units.la: Christo Mediatori hic sunt fuę partes, tùm impetratoriae, tùm applicatorię: 1 Cor. 1. 30. 2, v, 17. Eph. 5.25,26.
units.tr: Christ the Mediator has here his own offices, both of obtaining and of applying (1 Cor. 1:30; 2 Cor. 5:17; Eph. 5:25, 26).

units.la: Sed Sp. Sancto, juxta ordinem Divinarum Personarum, proximè haec actio tribuitur: 2 Thess. II, 13. Per sanctificationem Spiritus. Tit. 3.5. Renovationem Spiritus Sancti.
units.tr: But this act is ascribed most immediately to the Holy Spirit, according to the order of the divine Persons (2 Thess. 2:13: "through the sanctification of the Spirit"; Titus 3:5: "the renewal of the Holy Spirit").

units.la: Verbi autem & Sacramentorum efficacia hic moralis est: Joh. 17,17. Sanctifica eos Tua veritate: sermo ille Tuus veritas est. Rom. 6, 4. Consepulti Christo per baptismum. 1 Cor. 12, 13.
units.tr: The efficacy of the Word and of the Sacraments here is moral (John 17:17: "Sanctify them in your truth; your word is truth"; Rom. 6:4: "buried with Christ through baptism"; 1 Cor. 12:13).

units.la: III. Subjecta sunt redemti, vocati, & justificati. Praecedit enim Redemtio; quâ Christus eos acquisivit: Vocatio; quâ ipsi ad unionem cum Christo traducuntur: atque adeò Regeneratio; quâ vita spiritualis iis inditur: imò & Justificatio; quae posita vitâ spirituali, & fide salvifica, non potest non poni. Tales actionem hanc recipiunt. Ipsi interim, ut spiritualiter viventes, hic etiàm efficientiam quandam exferunt, qualis causis secundis convenit. Rom. 12, 1, 2. Adhortor igitur vos, fratres, per miserationes Dei, ut sistatis corpora vestra hostiam vivam, sanctam, placentem Deo. - Transformate vos per renovationem mentis, ut probetis quae sit voluntas Dei, &c. Eph. 4, 22,23,24. Phil. II, 12, 13.
units.tr: III. The subjects are the redeemed, the called and the justified. For redemption comes first, by which Christ acquired them; then calling, by which they are brought into union with Christ; and so regeneration, by which spiritual life is infused into them; indeed justification too, which, once spiritual life and saving faith are posited, cannot but be posited. Such persons receive this act. Meanwhile they, as living spiritually, also put forth here a certain efficacy of their own, such as belongs to secondary causes (Rom. 12:1, 2: "I urge you therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God ... be transformed by the renewal of your mind, that you may prove what the will of God is," etc.; Eph. 4:22, 23, 24; Phil. 2:12, 13).

units.la: Qq Totus autem homo beatam hanc tranfmutationem subit, mente, voluntate, affectibus: quin imò corpus, & singula ejus membra, usurpantur ad sanctimoniam: Rom. 6,12,13. xiv,7,8. 1 Theff. 4,3,4,5. 1Cor. 6,20.
units.tr: Moreover the whole man undergoes this blessed transformation, in mind, will and affections; indeed the body and each of its members are also employed for holiness (Rom. 6:12, 13; 14:7, 8; 1 Thess. 4:3, 4, 5; 1 Cor. 6:20).

units.la: 1 Theff. 5,23.
units.tr: 1 Thess. 5:23.

units.la: IV. Terminus à quo est turpitudo peccati: Terminus ad quem est puritas imaginis Dei, & conformatio ad gloriam ipsius: Ezech. 36,25,26,27. Eph. 4,22, 23,24. Rom. 12,1,2. Col. III, 9, 10. Cùm exuti illo vetere homine-sitis induti novo &c. Hebr. 9,14. 1 Cor. 10,31. Rom. 6,22.
units.tr: IV. The terminus from which is the filthiness of sin. The terminus to which is the purity of the image of God and conformity to his glory (Ezek. 36:25, 26, 27; Eph. 4:22, 23, 24; Rom. 12:1, 2; Col. 3:9, 10: "since you have put off the old man and put on the new," etc.; Heb. 9:14; 1 Cor. 10:31; Rom. 6:22).

units.la: Idea igitur in hoc negotio nobis imitanda est Sanctitas Jehovæ; Lev. xi, 44. xix, 2. xx, 7, 8, 26. Matt. 5, 48. Eph. 5, 1. Et Christi exemplum in vita sua humili; 1 Petr. 2, 21, 22. Matth. xi, 29. Phil. 2, 5, 6, 7, 8. Et suo modo exempla aliorum per ejus gratiam sanctificatorum: 1 Cor. xi, 1. Hebr. 12,1. 13,7.
units.tr: The idea, therefore, that we must imitate in this matter is the holiness of Jehovah (Lev. 11:44; 19:2; 20:7, 8, 26; Matt. 5:48; Eph. 5:1), and the example of Christ in his humble life (1 Pet. 2:21, 22; Matt. 11:29; Phil. 2:5, 6, 7, 8), and, in their own way, the examples of others sanctified by his grace (1 Cor. 11:1; Heb. 12:1; 13:7).

units.la: V. Sanctificatio non consistit in sola actuum emendatione; quod volunt Socdiniani, aliique Pelagianizantes: sed, quemadmodùm per Regenerationem inditæ fuerunt novæ facultates, ità per Sanctificationem conferuntur novi habitus spirituales, virtutes Theologicæ, quæ indies perficiuntur, & ad actus secundos excitantur.
units.tr: V. Sanctification does not consist in the mere amendment of acts, as the Socinians and other semi-Pelagians hold. Rather, just as new faculties were infused through regeneration, so through sanctification new spiritual habits, the theological virtues, are conferred, which are daily perfected and stirred up to second acts.

units.la: Probatur ista veritas, 1. ex promissionibus novi Fœderis: Jerem. 31, 33, 34. Dabo Legem meam in medio eorum: & in corde eorum describam eam, &c. Ezech. 36,27. Et Spiritum meum dabo in medio vestri; efficiamque; ut in præceptis meis ambuletis, &c.
units.tr: This truth is proved, first, from the promises of the New Covenant: Jer. 31:33, 34: "I will put my law in the midst of them, and write it on their hearts," etc.; Ezek. 36:27: "I will put my Spirit within you and cause you to walk in my statutes," etc.

units.la: 2. Illustria sunt exempla; 2 Tim. 1, 5, 6, 7. Memoria repetens eam, quæ in te est, minimè simulatam fidem; quæ habitavit prius in avia tua Loïde, & in matre tua Eunica: persuasus sum autem, quòd in te quoque. Quam ob causam in memoriam revoco tibi, ut exsuscites donum Dei, quod in te est, per impositionem tionem manuum mearum. Non enim dedit nobis Deus spiritum formidinis; sed roboris, et charitatis, et sanitatis animi. Similiter cum jam Petrus esset a Satana ventilandus, instar tritici, dixit Christus; Luc. 22, 32. Ego deprecatus sum pro te, ne deficiat fides tua, Mansit igitur in ipso, nec defecit iste habitus, etiam in gravissima tentatione & lapsu; ubi actuum secundorum satis notabilis fuit desectus.
units.tr: Second, there are notable examples. 2 Tim. 1:5, 6, 7: "Calling to mind the sincere faith that is in you, which first dwelt in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that it dwells in you also. For this reason I remind you to stir up the gift of God that is in you through the laying on of my hands. For God did not give us a spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind." Likewise, when Peter was about to be sifted by Satan like wheat, Christ said: Luke 22:32: "I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail." That habit therefore remained in him and did not fail, even in the most grievous temptation and fall, in which there was a rather notable lack of second acts.

units.la: 3. Habituales virtutes diserte recensentur, 2 Petr. 1, 4.-8. Gal. 5, 22. 1 Cor. 13, 8. 13.
units.tr: Third, the habitual virtues are expressly enumerated (2 Pet. 1:4–8; Gal. 5:22; 1 Cor. 13:8, 13).

units.la: 4. Hebr. 5, 14. appellantur expresse Adulti, qui propter habitum sensus habent exercitatos, ad discretionem boni et mali. Confer Phil. 1, 6, 9.
units.tr: Fourth, in Heb. 5:14 those are expressly called adults, who by reason of habit have their senses exercised to discern good and evil. Compare Phil. 1:6, 9.

units.la: VI. Ex istis habitibus educuntur actus secundi; omnis generis exercitia pietatis, & bona opera. Matth. 5, 16. Ita splendeat lux vestra coram hominibus, ut videant vestra bona opera. 1 Tim. 4, 7. Tit. 11, 14. Phil. 4, 8.
units.tr: VI. From these habits proceed second acts: every kind of exercise of piety and good works (Matt. 5:16: "Let your light so shine before men that they may see your good works"; 1 Tim. 4:7; Titus 2:14; Phil. 4:8).

units.la: In hoc genere valde illustris est quotidiana praxis Fidei & Resipiscentiae. 2 Thess. 1, 3. Fides vestra vehementer augescit; et abundat mutua Charitas. 2 Cor. 4, 16. Col. 1, 9, 10, 11. Quantum ad Fidem attinet, ea speciatim promissiones Evangelicas ad praesentem nostram conditionem applicamus, ut continuetur in nobis subjectiva certitudo nostrae Justificationis; & simul corroboremur in vita spirituali ac praxi pietatis: Gal. 2, 20. Confer sup. cap. 2. th. 21. Quod vero ad praxin Resipiscentiae, ad singulas actiones sedulo attendimus, ut per gratiam Dei perficiatur in nobis tum mortificatio veteris, tum vivificatio novi hominis: Rom. 6, 4. Phil. 4, 8, 9.
units.tr: In this area the daily practice of faith and repentance is especially conspicuous. 2 Thess. 1, 3. Your faith grows exceedingly, and the mutual love of you all abounds. 2 Cor. 4, 16. Col. 1, 9, 10, 11. As far as faith is concerned, we apply the evangelical promises to our present condition, so that the subjective certainty of our justification is maintained in us, and at the same time we are strengthened in the spiritual life and the practice of godliness: Gal. 2, 20. Compare above, chap. 2, th. 21. As for the practice of repentance, we attend carefully to each single action, so that by the grace of God both the mortification of the old man and the quickening of the new man may be brought to completion in us: Rom. 6, 4. Phil. 4, 8, 9.

units.la: VII. Pontificii Poenitentiam externam in foro Ecclesiae, cum interna in foro conscientiae confundentes, ex ea faciunt specialem virtutem; ex praeconcepto Satisfactionis errore, in ordine ad Justitiam Dei: sed ab interna ista plurimùm differt externa demonstratio pœnitentiæ coram Ecclesiâ; ut resipiscentibus ministerialiter denuncietur remissio peccatorum suorum, & abstenti ad communionem denuò admittantur.
units.tr: VII. The Papists, confusing outward repentance in the forum of the Church with inward repentance in the forum of conscience, make of it a special virtue, from the preconceived error of satisfaction in relation to the justice of God. But this outward demonstration of repentance before the Church differs greatly from that inward repentance, in that through the ministry the forgiveness of sins is announced to the penitent, and those who have been put away are readmitted to communion.

units.la: Nec specialis virtus esse potest; cùm ejus natura generalior sit, quàm ut certam virtutis speciem constituat: de singulis enim virtutibus omissis, & vitiis commissis, pœnitentia agi potest ac debet.
units.tr: Nor can it be a special virtue, since its nature is too general to constitute a particular species of virtue: for repentance can and ought to be exercised concerning each single virtue neglected and each vice committed.

units.la: Sed & Sacramentum reputant non minùs absurdè: 1. quia ei non insunt Sacramenti requisita.
units.tr: But they also regard it as a sacrament, no less absurdly: (1) because the requisites of a sacrament do not inhere in it.

units.la: 2. Quia Virtus & Sacramentum toto genere differunt.
units.tr: (2) Because virtue and sacrament differ in their whole genus.

units.la: 3. Ipse Baptismus est Sacramentum refipiscentiæ, sive pœnitentiæ: Act. 19, 4. Marc. 1, 4. Matth. 3, 11. Rom. 6, 4.
units.tr: (3) Baptism itself is the sacrament of repentance or penitence: Acts 19, 4. Mark 1, 4. Matt. 3, 11. Rom. 6, 4.

units.la: VIII. Neque minùs errant in definiendâ materiâ & formâ hujus imaginarii Sacramenti. Illam communiter constituunt in contritione cordis, confessione oris, & satisfactione operis.
units.tr: VIII. Nor do they err less in defining the matter and form of this imaginary sacrament. They commonly constitute the matter in contrition of heart, confession of mouth, and satisfaction of work.

units.la: Sed cùm materia Sacramenti debeat esse res externa sensibilis, ad eam saltem, ut pars, trahi non debet contritio cordis; utpote soli Deo nota. Et ipse Becanus: Omnes fatentur, contritionem non esse necessariam in Sacramento pœnitentiæ; quia ibi sufficit attritio. Confer etiam quod exstat de pœnitentia Judæ, Matth. 27, 3, 4, 5.
units.tr: But since the matter of a sacrament ought to be an external, sensible thing, contrition of heart ought not to be drawn into it, at least as a part, since it is known to God alone. Becanus himself says: All admit that contrition is not necessary in the sacrament of penance, because attrition suffices there. Compare also what is recorded of the repentance of Judas, Matt. 27, 3, 4, 5.

units.la: Satisfactio præstatur post Absolutionem; consequenter non potest esse pars materiæ: forma enim præsupponit materiam.
units.tr: Satisfaction is performed after absolution; consequently it cannot be part of the matter, for the form presupposes the matter.

units.la: IX. Confessio alia quidem est Divinæ laudis & veritatis; de quâ, Rom. 10, 10. Ore fit confessio ad salutem. Alia nostræ fraudis & iniquitatis; unde 1 Joh. 1, 9: Si confiteamur peccata nostra, fidelis est, & justus, ut remittat nobis peccata nostra. Psal. 32, 5. Prov. 28, 13.
units.tr: IX. Confession is of two kinds. One is the confession of divine praise and truth, of which: Rom. 10, 10. With the mouth confession is made unto salvation. The other is the confession of our own fault and iniquity, whence: 1 John 1, 9: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins. Ps. 32, 5. Prov. 28, 13.

units.la: Hæc
units.tr: This

units.la: Hęc necessariò fieri debet ipsi Deo; cui tanquàm Legislatori & Judici absolutè summo, soli in statum nostrum internum & æternum potestatem habenti, peccavimus: atque adeò sincerè, & particulatim, ex intimo turpitudinis & reatûs nostri sensû ea facienda est. Psal. 51, 5, 6. Prævaricationes meas ego agnosco; & peccatum meum coram me est semper. Tibi, Tibi soli peccavi. 32, 5. Dan. 9, 3.-7. Luc. 15, 21. 18, 13.
units.tr: This must necessarily be made to God himself, to whom, as the absolutely supreme Lawgiver and Judge, alone having power over our internal and eternal state, we have sinned; and so it must be made sincerely and particularly, out of a deep sense of our own filthiness and guilt. Ps. 51, 5, 6. I acknowledge my transgressions, and my sin is ever before me. Against thee, thee only, have I sinned. Ps. 32, 5. Dan. 9, 3-7. Luke 15, 21. 18, 13.

units.la: Sed & coram Ecclesiâ, vel ejus Antecessoribus, fieri debet confessio peccatorum (non tamen particularis) ab adultis, qui in Ecclesiæ communionem recipi cupiunt. Sic Matth. 3, 6. qui ad Johannem exibant, baptizabantur ab eo, confitentes peccata sua. Adde Act. 19, 17, 18.
units.tr: But confession of sins (not however particular) must also be made before the Church, or its elders, by adults who wish to be received into communion with the Church. Thus Matt. 3, 6. those who came out to John were baptized by him, confessing their sins. Add Acts 19, 17, 18.

units.la: Similiter etiàm publici & scandalosi peccatores, à sacrâ communione abstenti, ad publicam peccatorum suorum confessionem rectè adiguntur, priusquam à censuris Ecclesiasticis absolvantur; ut istâ ratione tollatur scandalum Ecclesiæ datum: 1 Tim. 5, 20. Eos, qui peccant, in conspectû omnium arguc; ut & reliqui metuant. Necessarium quoque est, ut qui injuriam aliis fecerunt privatim, hoc ipsum iis privatim confiteantur: Jac. 5, 16. Confitemini alii aliis offensas. Matt. 5, 23, 24. cum 6, 14. XVIII: 21, 22. Luc. 17, 3, 4. Imò etiam ad spiritualem instructionem & consolationem perutile est, ut, qui scrupulosam, vel dubitantem, vel aliter infirmam habet conscientiam, adeat aliquem spectatæ fidei ac pietatis, atque inprimis Ecclesiæ Pastorem, & ab eo solidam instructionem ex Verbo Dei petat: Mal. 2, 7. Labia enim Sacerdotis custodiunt scientiam; & Legem requirent ex ore ejus. &c. Gal. 6, 1. Rom. 14, 1.
units.tr: Likewise, public and scandalous sinners, who are kept away from the holy communion, are rightly brought to a public confession of their sins before they are absolved from ecclesiastical censures, so that by this means the scandal given to the Church may be removed: 1 Tim. 5, 20. Rebuke those who sin in the sight of all, so that the rest also may fear. It is also necessary that those who have wronged others privately should confess this very thing to them privately: James 5, 16. Confess your faults to one another. Matt. 5, 23, 24, with 6, 14; 18, 21, 22; Luke 17, 3, 4. Indeed it is also most useful for spiritual instruction and consolation that whoever has a scrupulous, doubting, or otherwise weak conscience should approach someone of proven faith and piety, and above all the minister of the Church, and seek from him solid instruction out of the Word of God: Mal. 2, 7. For the lips of the priest keep knowledge, and men shall seek the law at his mouth. etc. Gal. 6, 1. Rom. 14, 1.

units.la: X. Sed ab hac Confessione SS. Literis consentaneâ
units.tr: X. But from this confession, which agrees with Holy Scripture,

units.la: plurimùm recessit Pontificiorum Confessio auricularis, quæ fit in aurem Sacerdotis ab omnibus & singulis adultis
units.tr: the auricular confession of the Papists has departed very far. It is made into the ear of the priest by all and each of the adults

units.la: {y} Ecclesiæ ... Literis consentaneâ dultis baptizatis, saltem semel in anno, de omnibus peccatis mortalibus, cum omnibus eorum circumstantiis, ut ab ipso remissionem accipiant; addita gravi conditione, ut quæ quis peccata mortalia illum celaverit sciens, eorum remissionem consequi non possit.
units.tr: of the Church, baptized, at least once a year, concerning all mortal sins with all their circumstances, so that they may receive forgiveness from him. It carries the added grave condition that whoever knowingly conceals a mortal sin from him cannot obtain forgiveness for it.

units.la: Sed 1. Christus ministerium remissionis quidem mandavit Ministris Euangelii: sed ab auriculari illâ Confessione eam minimè suspendit; de quâ ne quidem in SS. Literis. Requiritur autem in Dispensatoribus, ut quisque fidus reperiatur: 1 Cor. 4, 2.
units.tr: But first, Christ indeed committed the ministry of forgiveness to the ministers of the Gospel, but he did not make it depend on that auricular confession, of which not even a word is found in Holy Scripture. Moreover, it is required of stewards that each one be found faithful: 1 Cor. 4, 2.

units.la: 2. Talis illa sperata remissionis consecutio impossibilis est: cum nemo omnium, & singulorum peccatorum suorum, cum suis circumstantiis, possit recordari, & sic ea confiteri, ut eorum remissionem accipiat. Psal. 19. 13. Delicta sua quis intelligit?
units.tr: Second, that hoped-for obtaining of forgiveness is impossible, since no one can recall all and each of his sins with their circumstances, and so confess them that he receives their forgiveness. Psal. 19. 13. Who understands his errors?

units.la: 3. Plurima & gravissima sunt ejus incommoda: necessario enim tenentur homines soliciti, an satis exactè conscientiam suam examinaverint, & apud Sacerdotem exoneraverint; an peccata mortalia à venialibus recte distinxerint, &c. Sæpè etiàm homines per examina Confessariorum docentur peccata prius ignota, & ad ea incitantur: tyrannis & avaritia Sacerdotum fovetur, &c.
units.tr: Third, its disadvantages are very many and very grave. People are necessarily kept anxious as to whether they have examined their conscience carefully enough and unburdened it before the priest, and whether they have rightly distinguished mortal sins from venial ones, and so on. Often too, through the questioning of confessors, people are taught sins previously unknown to them and are incited to commit them. The tyranny and avarice of priests are thereby fostered, and so on.

units.la: 4. Absurdè ea statuitur pars Pænitentiæ; cùm hæc ad animum pertineat; & illa hujus effectus sit, & signum consequens.
units.tr: Fourth, that part of penance is absurdly assigned to it, since penance pertains to the mind, while that confession is its effect and a consequent sign.

units.la: XI.
units.tr: XI.

units.la: Obj. 1. Christus Ministris Euangelii dedit potestatem ligandi & solvendi: Matt. 16, 19, XVIII:18. Joh. 20, 23. Resp. Non tamen solvendi, aut remittendi, pro ipsorum arbitrio; aut postulatâ priùs tali Consessione.
units.tr: Objection 1. Christ gave the ministers of the Gospel the power of binding and loosing: Matt. 16, 19; 18, 18. John 20, 23. Answer: not, however, of loosing or forgiving at their own discretion, or without such confession first being demanded.

units.la: Obj. 2. Occurrunt exempla, Matth. III, 6. Act. 19, 17, 18. Ergò. Resp. Non commemoratur istic 1. confessio particularis omnium & singulorum peccatorum cum suis circumstantiis. 2. Non auricularis. 3. Neque à baptizatis; (quibus Pœnitentia dicitur altera tabula post naufragium) sed à catechumenis baptizandis facta.
units.tr: Objection 2. Examples occur: Matt. 3, 6. Acts 19, 17, 18. Therefore, answer: there is mentioned there (1) no particular confession of all and each of the sins with their circumstances; (2) not an auricular one; (3) and not one made by the baptized (to whom repentance is called the second plank after shipwreck), but one made by catechumens about to be baptized.

units.la: Obj. 3. Christus hominem à lepra sanatum misit ad Sacerdotem, ut se ei ostenderet: Matth. 8, 4. Ergò spiritualis lepra est Sacerdotibus ostendenda; sive peccata per Confessionem exponenda. Resp. Misit hominem sanatum, ut pro eo fieret secundum Legem Cerimonialem; Levit. 14. quae tunc nondum erat abrogata: non autem misit ut à Sacerdote sanaretur; neque ut post auricularem confessionem absolveretur.
units.tr: Objection 3. Christ sent the man healed of leprosy to the priest, that he might show himself to him: Matt. 8, 4. Therefore spiritual leprosy must be shown to the priests, or sins must be laid open by confession. Answer: he sent the healed man so that an offering might be made for him according to the ceremonial law, Lev. 14, which at that time was not yet abrogated; but he did not send him to be cleansed by the priest, nor to be absolved after auricular confession.

units.la: Obj. 4. Mandatum exstat Iac. 5, 16. Confitemini alii aliis offensas, &c. Resp. Recte Cardinalis Cajetanus ad locum; Nec est Iermo de Confessione Sacramentali: ut patet ex eo, quod dicit; Confitemini invicem. Sacramentalis enim Confessio non fit invicem; sed Sacerdotibus tantùm: Sed de Confessione, quâ mutuò fatemur nos peccatores, ut oretur pro nobis; & de Confessione hinc & indè erratorum, pro mutuâ placatione & reconciliatione.
units.tr: Objection 4. There is a command at James 5, 16: Confess your faults to one another, and so on. Answer: Cardinal Cajetan rightly says on the passage that "the discourse here is not about sacramental confession," as is clear from what he says: "Confess to one another." For sacramental confession is not made to one another, but to priests only. Rather, the text speaks of the confession by which we mutually acknowledge ourselves to be sinners, so that prayer may be made for us, and of the confession of faults committed on both sides, for mutual appeasement and reconciliation.

units.la: XII. Pergimus ad considerationem bonorum ope- rum ab hominibus sanctificatis in hac vitâ praestando- rum.
units.tr: XII. We proceed to consider the good works to be performed in this life by men who have been sanctified.

units.la: Describuntur autem; Actus humani, ex fide procedentes, atque in Dei gloriam, juxta praescriptum Legis ipsius praestiti. Actus humani opponuntur naturalibus illis, qui rationi non subjacent; ut si quis suâ gravitate cadat deorsum; quòd cibi in ventriculo coquantur, &c. nam cultus nostep debet esse rationalis: Rom. 12, 1.
units.tr: Good works are described as human acts, proceeding from faith and performed in the glory of God according to the prescription of his law. Human acts are set against those natural ones which are not subject to reason, as when someone falls downward by his own weight, or food is digested in the stomach, and so on; for our worship ought to be rational: Rom. 12, 1.

units.la: Tres verò conditiones potissimùm requiruntur, ut opera nostra sint verè bona: una ex parte principii; altera ex parte finis; tertia ex parte normæ. Prima, ex parte principii, est, ut ex verâ fide salvificâ procedant: Rom. 14, 23. Quicquid ex fide non est, peccatum est. Hebr. xi, 6. Fieri non potest, ut absque fide quifquam Deo gratus sit. 1 Tim. 1, 5. Tit. 1, 15. Omnis enim aptitudo ad spiritualiter bene operandum, ex gratia Dei in Christo per fidem accipi debet: Eph. 3, 17. Hebr. 9, 14. Act. 15, 9. Gal. II, 20. Joh. 15, 3, 5. 1 Cor. I, 30. II, 16. Rom. 12, 2. Eph. 5, 15, 16. I, 6. Rom. 14, 17, 18, 22, 23.
units.tr: Three conditions are chiefly required so that our works may be truly good: one on the side of the principle, another on the side of the end, and a third on the side of the norm. The first, on the side of the principle, is that they proceed from true saving faith: Rom. 14, 23. Whatever is not of faith is sin. Heb. 11, 6. It is impossible for anyone to be pleasing to God without faith. 1 Tim. 1, 5. Tit. 1, 15. For every fitness to act spiritually well must be received through faith from the grace of God in Christ: Eph. 3, 17. Heb. 9, 14. Acts 15, 9. Gal. 2, 20. John 15, 3, 5. 1 Cor. 1, 30; 2, 16. Rom. 12, 2. Eph. 5, 15, 16; 1, 6. Rom. 14, 17, 18, 22, 23.

units.la: Propter defectum hujus conditionis opera infidelium, quamvis forte materialiter Legi Divinæ conformia, non sunt tamen opera verè & spiritualiter bona.
units.tr: Because this condition is lacking, the works of unbelievers, though perhaps materially conformed to the divine law, are nevertheless not truly and spiritually good works.

units.la: XIII. Altera conditio, quæ finem respicit, hæc est; ut opera fiant in gloriam Dei, ut in finem primarium atque ultimum: 1 Cor. 10, 31. Quicquid facitis, omnia in Dei gloriam facite. Phil. 1, 10, 11. Col. 3, 17. 1 Tim 4, 3, 4, 5. Item Matth. 5, 16. 1 Petr. 2, 12; 9.
units.tr: XIII. The second condition, which regards the end, is this: that works be done for the glory of God, as the primary and ultimate end: 1 Cor. 10, 31. Whatever you do, do all to the glory of God. Phil. 1, 10, 11. Col. 3, 17. 1 Tim. 4, 3, 4, 5. Likewise Matt. 5, 16. 1 Pet. 2, 12; 9.

units.la: Huic interim fini primario & ultimo subordinatur, tum salus nostra: Jef. 45, 19. Non dixi semini Jacobi; In vanum quaerite me. Psal. 19, 12. 1 Sam. 2, 30. 1 Tim. 4, 8. Rom. 2, 7. Hebr. XI, 26. XII, 2. Tum aliorum ædificatio: Col. 3, 16. Docendo & commonefacientes vos mutuo psalmis, hymnis, & cantionibus spiritualibus.
units.tr: Subordinate to this primary and ultimate end are both our own salvation: Isa. 45, 19. I did not say to the seed of Jacob, Seek me in vain. Psal. 19, 12. 1 Sam. 2, 30. 1 Tim. 4, 8. Rom. 2, 7. Heb. 11, 26; 12, 2; and the edification of others: Col. 3, 16. Teaching and admonishing one another in psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs.

units.la: XIV. Tertia denique conditio ad normam spectat; nimirum ut opera nostra fiant secundum Legem Dei.
units.tr: XIV. Third, finally, the condition concerns the rule: namely, that our works be done according to the Law of God.

units.la: Sic enim 1. diserte præcipitur, Deut. 4, 1, 2. Nunc ergo o, Israël, audi statuta & judicia, quæ Ego doceo vos, ut faciatis, ut vivatis: - Non addetis ad verbum, quod Ego præcipio vobis: neque diminuetis quicquam ex eo. V, 32, 33. XI, 32. XII, 32. Levit. 18, 5. Ezech. 18, 9. XX, 18, 19. Matth. 5, 19. Jac. II, 10.
units.tr: For first, this is expressly commanded: Deut. 4:1, 2. Now therefore, O Israel, hear the statutes and judgments which I teach you, that you may do them, that you may live: You shall not add to the word which I command you, nor take away anything from it. Cf. 5:32, 33; 11:32; 12:32. Lev. 18:5. Ezek. 18:9; 20:18, 19. Matt. 5:19. James 2:10.

units.la: 2. Suprema & independens Dei Opt. Max. ἐξουσία & gloria, ac nostra moralis dependentia ab ipso, & subjectio ad ejus cultum atque obsequium, omnia postulant, ut norma obedientiæ & cultus ab ipso nobis præscribatur.
units.tr: Second, the supreme and independent authority [ἐξουσία] and glory of God the best and greatest, and our moral dependence on him and subjection to his worship and obedience, all require that the rule of obedience and worship be prescribed to us by him.

units.la: 3. Formalis ratio peccati, seu mali moralis, consistit in difformitate à Lege Divina : 1 Joh. 3. 4. unde etiam per Legem cognoscitur ; Rom. 3, 20. VII, 7. Ergo bonitas moralis consistit in conformitate cum norma Divinitus praescriptâ in Lege.
units.tr: Third, the formal reason of sin, or of moral evil, consists in a departure from the Divine Law: 1 John 3:4. Whence also it is known through the Law: Rom. 3:20; 7:7. Therefore moral goodness consists in conformity to the rule prescribed by God in the Law.

units.la: 4. Secundum istam normam de operibus hominum, seu bonis, seu malis, judicat, & judicabit ipse Deus: Iac. 4. 12. II. 12. Rom. 2, 14, 15, 16.
units.tr: Fourth, God himself judges, and will judge, the works of men, whether good or evil, according to this rule: James 4:12. 2:12. Rom. 2:14, 15, 16.

units.la: Secundum istam igitur normam agenda sunt, quae istic praecepta; & fugienda, quae prohibita: circa ea vero quae Deus reliquit adiaphora in thesi, in hypothesi nihilominus observandae sunt regulae pro illa praxi praescriptae. Vide sup. cap. 8. th. 27.
units.tr: Therefore those things which are commanded are to be done according to this rule, and those which are forbidden are to be avoided. As for those things which God has left as indifferent in principle, nevertheless in their practice the rules prescribed for that practice are to be observed. See above, ch. 8, th. 27.

units.la: XV. Consequenter bonis operibus accenseri non debent, quae ista norma posthabita, fiunt ex qualicunque opinione cultus Divini, aut intentione gloriae Divinae: Joh. 16. 2. Veniet tempus, cùm quisquis trucidabit vos, putabit se cultum praestare Deo. Col. II. 23. vel ab aliis hominibus excogitata & mandata sunt: Matth. 15. 9. ex Isef. 29. 13. Dixit Deus, frustra Me colunt, docentes doctrinas, quae sunt mandata hominum. Col. II. 20, 21, 22.
units.tr: XV. Consequently, those things are not to be counted among good works which, with this rule set aside, are done out of some opinion of divine worship or with an intention of the glory of God: John 16:2. The time is coming when whoever kills you will think that he offers service to God. Col. 2:23. Or which have been devised and commanded by other men: Matt. 15:9, from Isa. 29:13. God said, In vain do they worship me, teaching doctrines which are the commandments of men. Col. 2:20, 21, 22.

units.la: Plurimum vero distat cultus ille voluntarius, ἐθελοθρησκία, à cultu spontaneo, qui libenti animo praestatur juxta praescriptum Dei: Psal. 110. 3. Populus tuus spontaneus, &c.
units.tr: But that voluntary worship [ἐθελοθρησκία] differs greatly from the spontaneous worship which is rendered with a willing mind according to the prescription of God: Ps. 110:3. Your people will be willing, etc.

units.la: Ubi vero mandata hominum Divinis adversantur; prorsus Deo obediendum est potius, quam hominibus: Act. 4, 19. v, 29.
units.tr: But where the commandments of men oppose the Divine ones, one must obey God rather than men: Acts 4:19; 5:29.

units.la: Neque in Adiaphoris à moribus & consuetudinibus arcessenda est bonitas moralis; sed à regulis Divinis: Rom. xII. 2. Ne vos configurate saeculo isti: - ut probetis quae sit voluntas Dei, bona illa, placens, ac perfecta.
units.tr: Nor is moral goodness in matters indifferent to be derived from customs and usages, but from the Divine rules: Rom. 12:2. Do not be conformed to this world, but that you may prove what is the will of God, that good, pleasing and perfect will.

units.la: XVI. In Adjunctis bonorum operum, videndum primo de eorum utilitate ac necessitate; & porro de perfectione, vel imperfectione.
units.tr: XVI. Concerning the accompaniments of good works, we must consider first their usefulness and necessity; and further, their perfection or imperfection.

units.la: Utilitas amplissima est: 1 Tim. 4. 8. Pietas ad omnia utilis est, ut quae promijfionem habeat vitae praesentis, ac futurae. Phil. II, 12. 1 Tim. II, 14.
units.tr: Their usefulness is very great: 1 Tim. 4:8. Godliness is profitable for all things, since it has the promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come. Phil. 2:12. 1 Tim. 2:14.

units.la: Imo etiam necessitas (in adultis) agnoscenda est, tum praecepti; unde infertur nostrum officium & obsequium debitum: tum quoque medii; ut fine hoc ad possessionem ac fruitionem coelestis beatitudinis perveniri non possit. Hebr. 12: 14. Pacem sectamini cum omnibus, & sanctimoniam, fine quanemo videbit Dominum. Matth. III. 10. Jam vero etiam securis ad radicem arborum posita est: omnis igitur arbor, non ferens fructum bonum, exciditur; & in ignem abjicitur.
units.tr: Indeed, a necessity (in adults) is also to be acknowledged, both of precept, whence our duty and due obedience follow; and also of means, since without this one cannot attain to the possession and enjoyment of heavenly blessedness. Heb. 12:14. Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no one will see the Lord. Matt. 3:10. Even now the axe is laid to the root of the trees; therefore every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and cast into the fire.

units.la: Magis hoc patet, 1. ex consideratione Christi: qui non minus Sanctificationem nobis impetravit, quam Justificationem, &c. 1 Cor. I. 30. VI. 11. Luc. I. 74, 75. Rom. 6: 2, -. Ephes. 5: 25, 26, 27. Tit. 2: 13, 14. Hebr. 9: 13, 14. Imo & Justificatio necessario secum trahit Sanctificationem. Vide sup. cap. 2. th. 23. §. 4.
units.tr: This is more evident, first, from the consideration of Christ, who obtained for us sanctification no less than justification, etc.: 1 Cor. 1:30; 6:11. Luke 1:74, 75. Rom. 6:2 ff. Eph. 5:25, 26, 27. Titus 2:13, 14. Heb. 9:13, 14. Indeed justification also necessarily brings sanctification along with it. See above, ch. 2, th. 23, §4.

units.la: 2. Respectu Dei; Patri nostro sanctissimo ac beneficentiffimo, tanquam filii genuini, obsequium & animum gratum probare debemus in omnibus; Eique conformari in Ipsius gloriam. Deut. 8: 10, 11. XXXII: 5, 6, 7. Ief. I: 2, 16, 17. Mal. I: 6. 1 Cor. 6: 19, 20.
units.tr: Second, with respect to God: as to our most holy and most beneficent Father, we ought to show obedience and a grateful mind in all things, as genuine children, and to be conformed to him for his glory. Deut. 8:10, 11. 32:5, 6, 7. Jer. 1:2, 16, 17. Mal. 1:6. 1 Cor. 6:19, 20.

units.la: 3. Respectu nostri ipsorum; Quod fidem vere salvificam habeamus, & sic in statum gratiae translati simus, ex istis fructibus colligimus: Matth. 12.33: Jac. II: 17. Eadem operâ de nostrâ vocatione, ipsaque adeo electione, certi reddimur: 2 Petr. I: 10. Atque in futurum sic damnationem effugimus: Matth. 3: 7, 8, 10. & aeternam beatitudinem ac gloriam consequimur: Phil. II: 12. III: 14. 1 Cor. 9: 24. Hebr. 12. 1, 2. 2 Tim. 1: 7, 8.
units.tr: Third, with respect to ourselves: that we have a truly saving faith, and so have been transferred into the state of grace, we gather from these fruits: Matt. 12:33. James 2:17. By the same work we are made certain of our vocation and even of our election: 2 Pet. 1:10. And thus in future we escape damnation: Matt. 3:7, 8, 10, and attain eternal blessedness and glory: Phil. 2:12; 3:14. 1 Cor. 9:24. Heb. 12:1, 2. 2 Tim. 1:7, 8.

units.la: 4. Respectu proximi nostri; ista ratione annitendum dum est, ut eum Christo lucrifaciamus; & nostro exemplo ad pietatem, ac sanctimoniam, studiumque Salutis æternæ, adducamus: Matth. 5. 16. 1 Petr. 3. 1, 2. 1 Thess. 5, 11.
units.tr: Fourth, with respect to our neighbour: in this way we must strive to win him for Christ, and by our example to lead him to godliness and holiness and zeal for eternal salvation: Matt. 5:16. 1 Pet. 3:1, 2. 1 Thess. 5:11.

units.la: XVII. Perfectio triplex hoc loco spectari potest:
units.tr: XVII. Perfection may be considered here in three ways:

units.la: 1. Perfectio sinceritatis; quâ idem pietatis studium, quod foris ostenditur verbis & gestibus, intùs existit in animo; absque partitione cordis: prout simulatores dicuntur loqui labio blanditiarum in corde & corde, Pfal. 12. 3. Hæc perfectio requiritur Deut. 6, 5. Diliges Jehovam Deum tuum toto corde tuo, & tota anima tua. Confer Job. I, 1. Pfal. 139, 23, 24. 1 Reg. 15, 8. Contraria est hypocrisis: Jef. 29, 13. Ezech. 33, 31.
units.tr: 1. The perfection of sincerity: by which the same zeal for godliness that is shown outwardly in words and gestures exists inwardly in the mind, without a divided heart; as hypocrites are said to speak with a lying lip, and with a double heart, Ps. 12:2. This perfection is required in Deut. 6:5. You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, and with all your soul. Compare Job 1:1. Ps. 139:23, 24. 1 Kings 15:8. Hypocrisy is contrary to it: Isa. 29:13. Ezek. 33:31.

units.la: 2. Perfectio partium; quâ omnia & singula officia, Divinitùs nobis præscripta, sine exceptione obseruantur; sicut Præcepta Legis certum nexum inter se habent: Jac. II, 10. De hâc pro more gentis suæ falsò gloriabatur juvenis Pharisæus. Matth. 19, 20. Omnia hæc observavi à juventute mea. Verius de Zachariâ & Elizabethâ, Luc. 1, 6. Incedentes in omnibus præceptis & constitutionibus Domini inculpatè. Vide similiter de Josiâ, expresså etiàm perfectione sinceritatis, 2 Reg. XXIII. 25. De Asâ verò indicatur quidem perfectio sinceritatis, sed cum quâdam exceptione circa perfectionem partium, 2 Chr. 15, 17.
units.tr: 2. The perfection of parts: by which all and each of the duties prescribed to us by God are observed without exception, just as the precepts of the Law have a certain connection among themselves: James 2:10. Of this the young Pharisee falsely boasted, according to the custom of his nation: Matt. 19:20. All these things I have observed from my youth. More truly of Zacharias and Elizabeth, Luke 1:6. Walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord. Similarly see of Josiah, in whom perfection of sincerity is also expressly stated: 2 Kings 23:25. But of Asa, indeed, perfection of sincerity is indicated, but with a certain exception as to perfection of parts: 2 Chron. 15:17.

units.la: 3. Perfectio graduum; ut obedientia Deo præstetur non tantùm sincerè; & secundùm omnes partes; verùm insuper ad extremum virium, prout omnes noftrę vires à morali providentiâ Dei omninò dependent moraliter, quemadmodùm à creatione & providentiâ reali realiter. Marc. XII, 30. Luc. X. 27. ex Deut. 6, 5: Diliges Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo & ex totâ animâ tuâ, & totis viribus tuis, & ex totâ cogitatione tuâ. Nihil igitur in corde & animâ esse debet isti obedientiæ ac dilectioni adversum.
units.tr: 3. The perfection of degrees: that obedience be rendered to God not only sincerely and in all parts, but moreover to the utmost of our strength, since all our powers depend entirely, morally, on the moral providence of God, just as they depend really on his creation and real providence. Mark 12:30. Luke 10:27, from Deut. 6:5: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength, and with all your mind. Therefore nothing in heart and soul ought to be opposed to this obedience and love.

units.la: XVIII. Istam
units.tr: XVIII. This

units.la: aquarum, quæ fructum suum dat in tempore: & folium ejus non decidit. Similis est locus Ierem. 17, 8. Ergò prosperitas spiritualis non interrupta, piis ubique & semper obtingit. Resp. Illud intelligendum est secundùm quid: ut spiritualis vigor, & fertilitas, ac prosperitas detur; & maneat vita spiritualis, nec deficiat totaliter, nedùm finaliter; sed perficiatur in diem Jesû Christi, Phil. 1, 6. dum verè fideles principium illud, quo sustentantur, non obstantibus eorum lapsibus, & decremento aliquo, tamen per hanc Dei & Christi gratiam, firmum retinent ad finem usque; Hebr. III, 14.
units.tr: of waters, which yields its fruit in season, and whose leaf does not wither. A similar passage is Jer. 17:8. Therefore spiritual prosperity, unbroken, is granted to the godly everywhere and always. Answer: This must be understood in a qualified sense: spiritual vigour, fertility and prosperity are given, and spiritual life remains and does not fail entirely, much less finally, but is brought to completion on the day of Jesus Christ, Phil. 1:6. For true believers, though their falls and some decline do not hinder it, nevertheless keep through the grace of God and Christ that principle by which they are sustained, firm to the end; Heb. 3:14.

units.la: IV. Causa efficiens ac perficiens est tùm Deus, tùm Christus Mediator.
units.tr: IV. The efficient and perfecting cause is both God and Christ the Mediator.

units.la: Deus non solùm potest, sed etiàm vult, vere fideles in isto statu ad æternam salutem conservare. Ipsum posse, manifestissimum est ex absolutâ omnipotentiâ. Sed & velle, constat, tùm ex electione; tùm ex specialibus promissionibus. De Electione illustria sunt testimonia. Joh. 6, 39, 40. „Hæc est voluntas ejus, qui misit Me, Patris: ut ex eo omni, quod Mihi dederit, non perdam quicquam; sed suscitem illud in ultimo isto die, &c. Eph. 1, 4, 5. „Elegit nos in Ipso ante jactum mundi fundamentum, ut simus Sancti & inculpati, &c. Matth. 24, 24. „Excitabuntur pseudo-Christi ac pseudo-prophetæ: adeò ut seducant (si fieri possit) etiàm electos: Ista παραλόγισις, ει δυνατόν, si fieri possit, indicat immunitatem electorum à seductione. Confer. Apoc. 13, 8. Adde Rom. 8, 28-31. 2 Thess. 2, 13, 14.
units.tr: God not only can, but also wills, to preserve truly believing people in this state unto eternal salvation. That he can is most evident from his absolute omnipotence. That he wills it is established both by election and by special promises. There are clear testimonies concerning election: John 6:39, 40: "This is the will of the Father who sent me, that of all that he has given me I should lose nothing, but raise it up on the last day, etc." Eph. 1:4, 5: "He chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and blameless, etc." Matt. 24:24: "False christs and false prophets will arise, so as to deceive (if it were possible) even the elect." This paralogism, ei dunaton [εἰ δυνατόν], "if it were possible", indicates the elect's immunity from deception. Compare Rev. 13:8. Add Rom. 8:28-31; 2 Thess. 2:13, 14.

units.la: V. Certitudinem eandem Deus promissionibus variis revelavit, tùm in V. tùm in N. T.
units.tr: V. God revealed the same certainty by various promises, both in the Old and in the New Testament.

units.la: In V. T. illustres promissiones extant in Psalmis: 37, 24. Cum ceciderit (justus) non prosternetur; quia Jehovah sustentat manum ejus. CXII, 6, 9. CXXV. 1, 2, 3. Qui confidunt in Jehova, sunt ut mons Tsijon, qui tis adversis, & variis casibus hujus vitæ, dixerat priùs Apostolus: istis autem verbis docet, quo robore interim substiterit, deque victoriâ obtinendâ certus fuerit : non verò, quòd perfectionem graduum modò consecutus esset.
units.tr: In the Old Testament, illustrious promises are found in the Psalms: Ps. 37:24: "Though he (the righteous) fall, he shall not be cast down, for Jehovah upholds his hand." Ps. 112:6, 9; Ps. 125:1, 2, 3: "Those who trust in Jehovah are like Mount Zion, which..." [the text here is garbled in the scan; it runs on to speak of adverse circumstances and the various chances of this life, which the Apostle had mentioned before. By these words he teaches with what strength he stood firm in the meantime, and was certain of obtaining the victory; not that he had already attained the perfection of the degrees.]

units.la: XX. Pro Praxi; 1. Exploremus seriò, nos ipsos, an realem animi mutationem, virtutes illas spirituales, in nobis experiamur: 2Cor. 13, 5. 1, xi, 28. Zeph. II, 1. Psal. 139, 23, 24.
units.tr: XX. For Practice: 1. Let us seriously examine ourselves, whether we experience in ourselves a real change of mind and those spiritual virtues: 2 Cor. 13:5; 1 Cor. 11:28; Zeph. 2:1; Ps. 139:23, 24.

units.la: 2. Ex istis habitibus exercitia virtutum producamus; contraria verò vitia aversemur & fugiamus:
units.tr: 2. From these habits let us bring forth the exercises of the virtues, and let us turn away from and flee the contrary vices:

units.la: 3. Ex fide salvificâ rectè operari assuescamus: Act. 15, 9. Gal. II, 20. 1 Tim. I, 5. Tit. I, 15. Rom. 14, 23. Hebr. xi, 6. Gloriam DEI semper intendamus:
units.tr: 3. Let us accustom ourselves to work rightly from saving faith: Acts 15:9; Gal. 2:20; 1 Tim. 1:5; Titus 1:15; Rom. 14:23; Heb. 11:6. Let us always aim at the glory of God:

units.la: 1 Cor. 10, 31. Col. 3, 17. Phil. I, 10, 11. Matth. 5, 16. Et normam Legis Divinæ sedulò ac libenter in omnibus sequamur: Deut. 4, 1, 2. v. 32, 33. xi, 32. xii, 32. Rom. 7, 22.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 10:31; Col. 3:17; Phil. 1:10, 11; Matt. 5:16. And let us diligently and gladly follow the rule of the divine Law in all things: Deut. 4:1, 2; 5:32, 33; 11:32; 12:32; Rom. 7:22.

units.la: 4. Insignem utilitatem ac necessitatem bonorum operum rite expendamus: 1 Tim. 4, 8. Phil. 2, 12. Hebr. xii, 14.
units.tr: 4. Let us weigh properly the remarkable usefulness and necessity of good works: 1 Tim. 4:8; Phil. 2:12; Heb. 12:14.

units.la: 5. In universâ sanctitatis & obedientiæ praxi sinceritatem præstemus coram Deo sanctissimo atque omniscio: Gen. 17, 1. Psal. 26, 11. cxxxix, 23, 24.
units.tr: 5. In the whole practice of holiness and obedience, let us show sincerity before the most holy and omniscient God: Gen. 17:1; Ps. 26:11; Ps. 139:23, 24.

units.la: 6. Imperfectionis ac tenuitatis nostræ nobis confeii, eò magis defectus supplere, & quotidie prosicere, annitamur sedulò: 2 Cor. 4, 16. Phil. 3, 12. - 15.
units.tr: 6. Having become aware of our imperfection and weakness, let us earnestly strive all the more to make up for our defects and to advance daily: 2 Cor. 4:16; Phil. 3:12-15.

units.la: CAP. XVII.
units.tr: CAP. XVII.

units.la: De Conservatione, & Corroboratione.
units.tr: On Preservation and Strengthening.

units.la: COnservatio. 1. Qualis actio. Ejus effectus. 2. Perseverantia quæ. 3. Causa efficiens, & perficiens. Decretum. 4. Promissiones de eâ. 5. Impetratio. 6. Applicatio realis. 7. Institutio per Verbum, & Sacramenta. 8. Castigatio. 9. Studium ipsorum sanctificatorum, 10. Fines. 11. Vera sententia asseritur, c. Pontif. Socin. Remonstr. &c. 12. Objectiones solv. 13. Ac porrò aliæ. 14. Corroboratio. Qualis actio. Termini. 15. Infirmitates variæ. Robur, & incrementa. 16. Causa efficiens principalis. Media. 17. Fines. 18. Praxis. 19.
units.tr: Preservation. 1. What kind of action it is. Its effect. 2. What the perseverance is. 3. The efficient and perfecting cause; the decree. 4. The promises concerning it. 5. Impetration. 6. Real application. 7. Its institution through the Word and the sacraments. 8. Chastisement. 9. The study of the sanctified themselves. 10. The ends. 11. The true view is asserted against the Papists, Socinians, Remonstrants, etc. 12. Objections answered. 13. Other points besides. 14. Strengthening: what kind of action it is; its terms. 15. Various weaknesses; strength and growth. 16. The principal efficient cause; the means. 17. The ends. 18. Practice.

units.la: I. SEquitur Conservatio, ad Fœdus gratiæ, & salutis per Christum impetratæ applicationem, speciatim pertinens. Hæc describitur; Actus Dei & Christi gratiosus atque efficax, quo omnes & singuli verè fideles, justificati, ac sanctificati, quantumvis in se debiles, in isto suo statu potenter continuantur; adeò quidem ut jam ex eo totaliter & finaliter deficere non possint, sed per certam perseverantiam ad æternam gloriam sint traducendi. Rom. 5, 10. ,,Nam si, cùm inimici essemus, reconciliati fuimus Deo per mortem Filii ,,ejus; multo magis reconciliati Servabimur per vitam Ipsius. 1 Petr. 1, 5. Qui potentiæ Dei præsidio ,,Custodimini per fidem, ad salutem paratam revelari ,,tempore ultimo. 1 Thess. 5,23,24. 2: 111,3.
units.tr: I. Preservation follows, belonging specifically to the application of the covenant of grace and of the salvation obtained through Christ. It is described thus: it is the gracious and efficacious act of God and Christ by which all and each of the truly faithful, justified and sanctified, however weak in themselves, are powerfully kept in this their state, so that from it they can by no means fail entirely and finally, but are brought through a sure perseverance to eternal glory. Rom. 5:10: "For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life." 1 Pet. 1:5: "who by the power of God are kept through faith unto a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time." 1 Thess. 5:23, 24.

units.la: XVIII. Istam perfectionem graduum in hac vita non obtineri, probamus contra Pontificios, Socinianos, aliosque Perfectiftas; 1. ex disertis quibusdam testimoniis: 1 Cor. 13, 9, 10, 11. Ex parte cognoscimus, & ex parte prophetamus. Postquam autem advenerit quod perfectum est, &c. Cùm essem infans, &c. Cognitioni multum adhuc deest; atque adeò etiàm praxi, quæ cognitionem sequitur pro rata. Rom. 8, 23. Primitias Spiritus habemus: plenam messem expectamus, postea percipiendam. Phil. 3, 12, 13. Non quod jàm metam apprehenderim, aut jàm jam consummatus: sed persequor, experiens an ipse quoque apprehendam, cujus etiam rei causa apprehensus fui à Christo Jesù. Fratres, ego me ipsum non reor metam apprehendisse. Nondum ergo consecutus erat perfectionem sanctitatis pariter ac gloriæ. Adde Prov. 20, 9. Eccl. 7, 20. 1 Reg. 8, 46. Ief. 64. 6. Iac. 3, 2. 1 Joh. 1. 8, 9, 10.
units.tr: XVIII. That this perfection of degrees is not attained in this life we prove against the Papists, the Socinians, and other Perfectionists: 1. from certain plain testimonies. 1 Cor. 13:9, 10, 11: "We know in part, and we prophesy in part. But when that which is perfect has come," etc.; "When I was a child," etc. Much is still lacking to our knowledge, and therefore also to our practice, which follows knowledge in proportion. Rom. 8:23: "We have the firstfruits of the Spirit; we wait for the full harvest, to be received afterwards." Phil. 3:12, 13: "Not that I have already attained the goal, or am already made perfect; but I press on, to see whether I may also lay hold of that for which I was laid hold of by Christ Jesus. Brethren, I do not reckon myself to have laid hold of it." He had not yet attained perfection, of holiness or of glory alike. Add Prov. 20:9; Eccl. 7:20; 1 Kings 8:46; Isa. 64:6; James 3:2; 1 John 1:8, 9, 10.

units.la: 2. Ex causa istius imperfectionis; Carne corruptâ, in regenitis & sanctificatis adhuc reliquâ, & Spiritui repugnante: Gal. V, 17. Nam Caro concupiscit adversus Spiritum; Spiritus autem adversus Carnem: hæc autem inter se opposita sunt, ut non quæcunque voluerit, eadem faciatis. In iisdem subjectis sunt duo ista principia contraria. Hinc etiàm Paulus de se ipso graviter conqueritur, Rom. 7, 14. Vide fup. cap. 10. th. 37.
units.tr: 2. From the cause of this imperfection: the corrupt flesh, still remaining in the regenerate and sanctified, and opposing the Spirit. Gal. 5:17: "For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; for these are opposed to one another, so that you do not do the things that you would." In the same subjects these two contrary principles are present. Hence Paul himself also complains bitterly of himself, Rom. 7:14. See above, chap. 10, th. 37.

units.la: 3. Ex perpetuo studio proficiendi; quod in persectis fruftraneum foret; 2 Cor. 4, 16. Propterea non segnescimus: sed etiamsi externus homo noster corrumpitur, internus tamen renovatur indies. Phil. 3, 14. Unum autem ago; ea quidem, quæ à tergo sunt obliviscens, ad ea verò quæ à fronte sunt contendens, scopum versus feror, ad palmam supernæ vocationis Dei, in Christo Jesu. Psal. 84, 8.
units.tr: 3. From the constant zeal for progress, which would be pointless in the perfect. 2 Cor. 4:16: "Therefore we do not lose heart; but though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day." Phil. 3:14: "But this one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind, and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal, for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus." Ps. 84:8.

units.la: 4. Ex quotidiano studio remissionis peccatorum, ut eam in cordibus nostris sentiamus, etiàm super peccatis & lapsibus nostris quotidianis: Matth. 6, 12. Et remitte nobis debita nostra! Psal. 19, 13. Errores quis intelligat? ab occultis munda me! cxxx, 3. 4, cxliii, 2. Et usus Cœnæ Dominicæ identidem repeti debet, ad percipiendam in conscientiis nostris remissionis istius certitudinem: Matth. 26, 28. Hæc est sanguis meus novi Testi, qui pro vobis effundetur in remissionem peccatorum, cum 1 Cor. xi, 26. Quotiescunque ederitis panem hunc, & poculum hoc biberitis, mortem Domini annunciatis, usquequo venerit.
units.tr: 4. From the daily zeal for the forgiveness of sins, so that we feel it in our hearts, even for our daily sins and lapses. Matt. 6:12: "And forgive us our debts." Ps. 19:13: "Who can understand his errors? Cleanse me from hidden faults." Ps. 130:3, 4; Ps. 143:2. And the use of the Lord's Supper ought to be repeated from time to time, to receive in our consciences the certainty of this forgiveness. Matt. 26:28: "This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins"; with 1 Cor. 11:26: "As often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes."

units.la: XIX. Obj. 1. Alicubi in SS. Literis perfecti & adulti celebrantur: Ergo. Resp. Tales comparatè dicuntur, qui sincerè omnes officiorum suorum partes complent, & gradibus insigniter profecerunt; licet non illam graduum perfectionem obtinuerint, quam Lex Dei postulat, & quam posteà in cœlis habebimus. Imò eorum, qui sic laudantur, vitia & defectus etiam annotantur passim; aut aliundè colliguntur.
units.tr: XIX. Objection 1. In the Holy Scriptures some are celebrated as perfect and mature; therefore... Answer: such are called perfect in a comparative sense, who sincerely fulfil all the parts of their duties and have advanced remarkably in their stages, although they have not attained that perfection of degrees which the law of God requires, and which we shall have afterwards in heaven. Indeed, the faults and defects of those who are so praised are also noted here and there, or gathered from elsewhere.

units.la: Obj. 2. Christus Matth. xi. 30. jugum suum dicit esse facile, & onus leve. Similiter 1 Joh. 5, 3. Mandata Ejus non sunt gravia. Resp. 1. Christus de doctrinâ suâ isthic loquitur, qualis ea nunc potissimùm obtinet sub N. T. & distinguitur à rigido & condemnante Ministerio Legis, durisque ejus repetitionibus sub V. T. Nunc solùm credendum est in Christum Servatorem unicum & perfectissimum, clarissimè propositum, ad beatam Ipsius communionem: & præstanda est vicissim dilectio, gratitudo, ac nova obedientia, dùm per Divinam gratiam tutò ac suaviter ducimur ad cœlestem gloriam. 2. Propter majorem hanc amplitudinem & claritatem gratiæ, præcepta Dei magis etiàm diligimus, iisque delectamur ex animo; ut nobis non sint gravia, sed suavia.
units.tr: Objection 2. Christ, at Matt. 11:30, says that his yoke is easy and his burden light. Likewise 1 John 5:3: "His commandments are not grievous." Answer 1. Christ is speaking there of his doctrine, as it now chiefly stands under the New Testament, and as it is distinguished from the rigid and condemning ministry of the law and its harsh demands under the Old Testament. Now it is only necessary to believe in Christ, the sole and most perfect Saviour, set forth most clearly, for blessed fellowship with him; and in turn love, gratitude and new obedience are to be rendered, while by divine grace we are led safely and sweetly to heavenly glory. 2. Because of this greater breadth and clarity of grace, we love the commandments of God even more and take delight in them from the heart, so that they are not grievous to us but sweet.

units.la: Obj. 3. Phil. 4, 13. Omnia valeo per Eum, qui me corroborat, nempè Christum. Ergo. Resp. De mulpræclarum σωτήριον, de victis hostibus, & superatis omnibus periculis, per gratiam Dei in Christo. Adde Eph. 4, 30. 1 Joh. 3, 9. 1 Petr. 1, 23.
units.tr: Objection 3. Phil. 4:13: "I can do all things through him who strengthens me," namely Christ. Therefore... Answer: this refers to a most glorious salvation, to enemies conquered and all dangers overcome, by the grace of God in Christ. Add Eph. 4:30; 1 John 3:9; 1 Pet. 1:23.

units.la: VI. Quod sic Decreto constitutum est, & promissionibus revelatum, hoc ipsum Deus constanter ac potenter exequitur. Christus nimirum hoc fine datus est nobis Salvator & Conservator. Unde, quisquis in Ipsum credit, dicitur non periturus, sed habiturus vitam æternam; Joh. 3, 16. Rom. 8, 31, 32. Christus autem sanctissima oblatione sua, æternam salutem certò impetravit, quibus ea destinata ac promissa erat: Rom. 5, 9, 10, 11. Justificati Ejus sanguine, servabimur multo magis per Eum ab ira, &c. Ecce fidam illam Conservationem, post Justificationem in Christi sanguine. Nam non solum remissionem peccatorum nobis impetravit, verum etiam purificationem à maculâ, & liberationem à servitute spirituali. Vide Rom. 6, 6, -11. Hebr. 9, 13, 14.
units.tr: VI. What has been so established by decree and revealed in promises, God himself carries out constantly and powerfully. Christ, indeed, was given to us for this very end, as Saviour and Preserver. Hence whoever believes in him is said "not to perish, but to have eternal life." John 3:16; Rom. 8:31, 32. Christ, moreover, by his most holy offering, certainly obtained eternal salvation for those for whom it was destined and promised. Rom. 5:9, 10, 11: "Justified by his blood, we shall be saved much more through him from wrath," etc. Behold that faithful preservation, after justification in the blood of Christ. For he has obtained for us not only the remission of sins, but also purification from stain and deliverance from spiritual bondage. See Rom. 6:6-11; Heb. 9:13, 14.

units.la: Accedit insuper jugis Christi pro nobis intercessio: Rom. 8, 35. Quis est qui condemnet? Christus is est qui mortuus est: -qui etiam intercedit pro nobis. Quis nos separabit à charitate Christi? Hebr. 7, 24, 25. Luc. 22, 31, 32. Joh. 17, 9, 11, 15, 17, 20. Hoc est validissimum remedium adversus totalem ac finalem apostasiam: Joh. xi. 41, 42. Pater, gratias ago Tibi, quòd Me audieris. Ego verò sciebam Me semper à Te audiri.
units.tr: In addition there is the unceasing intercession of Christ for us. Rom. 8:34, 35: "Who is it that condemns? Christ is the one who died, and who also intercedes for us. Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?" Heb. 7:24, 25; Luke 22:31, 32; John 17:9, 11, 15, 17, 20. This is the most powerful remedy against total and final apostasy. John 11:41, 42: "Father, I thank you that you have heard me. I knew indeed that you always hear me."

units.la: VII. Impetrationem illam excipit efficax applicatio, per Ipsius virtutem omnipotentem; quâ omnia obstacula facilè superat, & obtinet quod intendit. Sic inchoatam in fidelibus sanctitatem confervat ab interitû, per Sp. Sancti efficaciam. Hæc efficacia admodùm emphaticè describitur Eph. 1, 17, - 20. Ubi eadem Divina virtus, & efficax Potentia, per quam Christus ex mortuis est suscitatus, in electis regenerandis, sanctificandis, & & conscientiam quodammodo honestè bonam, illuminatam & refrænatam; eam postea repellere potuerunt, & naufragium facere circa fidem; atque adeo amittere quod habuerunt: cùm fidem verè salvificam, & conscientiam spiritualiter bonam, nunquàm habuerint. 4. Hebr. 6, 6. conditio illa, si prolabantur, nihil ponit in esse. Et quæ Apostolus istic expressit, accipi possunt de fide solùm temporaria, & gratiâ Spiritus Sancti illuminante non salutari; qualis est eorum, qui peccant in Spiritum Sanctum. 5. Juxta locum Petri, nonnulli institutionis Christianæ, & illuminationis cujusdam non salutaris participes facti, veritatem illam amplexi sunt, & secundùm eam facere quædam cœperunt; postea verò ad priores suas corruptiones relapsi sunt. Verum ab istis Canibus & Suibus non valet consequentia ad veras Oves Christi; de quibus instituta erat quæstio. 6. Arbores istæ apud Judam nunquàm fuerunt verè radicatæ in Christo; nec vixerunt in ejus communione mysticâ: solùm speciem aliquam præbuerant, & spem aliis fecerant, in externam communionem Ecclesiæ institutæ adsciti: deindè relapsi, speciem illam amiserunt; & bis, sive omninò mortui, δὶς ἀποθανόντες, deprehensi sunt.
units.tr: VII. An effective application follows that impetration, through his almighty power, by which he easily overcomes all obstacles and attains what he intends. Thus he preserves from perishing the holiness begun in believers, through the efficacy of the Holy Spirit. This efficacy is described most emphatically at Eph. 1:17-20, where the same divine power and effective might by which Christ was raised from the dead is shown to work in the elect, regenerating, sanctifying, and... [the Latin here is garbled] ...a conscience in some measure honestly good, enlightened and restrained. Such persons could afterwards cast these away and make shipwreck concerning the faith, and so lose what they had; since they never had a truly saving faith and a spiritually good conscience. 4. At Heb. 6:6, the condition "if they fall away" posits nothing as actual. What the Apostle there expressed can be understood of a merely temporary faith, and of an illumination by the Holy Spirit that is not saving, such as belongs to those who sin against the Holy Spirit. 5. According to Peter's passage, some who have become partakers of Christian instruction and of a certain non-saving enlightenment embraced the truth, and began to do some things in accordance with it; but afterwards they relapsed into their former corruptions. But the inference from these dogs and swine does not hold for the true sheep of Christ, which was the question at issue. 6. Those trees in Jude were never truly rooted in Christ, nor did they live in his mystical communion; they had only presented some appearance and given hope to others, being received into the external communion of the Church. Then, having relapsed, they lost that appearance; and they were found "twice dead" [δὶς ἀποθανόντες], Jude 12.

units.la: XV. Corroboratio est actus efficacis gratiæ, quo sanctificati adhuc debiles, spirituali robore confirmantur; itaquidem ut crescat interior homo, fortis evadat, & ad perfectionem proficiat; in ipsorum salutem, ac Dei & Christi gloriam. 2 Cor. I, 21. Qui nos confirmat (βεβαιῶν) in Christum, Deus est. Col. 1. 10. Crescentes in agnitione Dei. Omnipotentiâ potentes facti, secundùm gloriosum robur ipsius, &c. 2 Thess. III, 3. Fidelis est Dominus, qui stabilit vos.
units.tr: XV. Corroboration is an act of efficacious grace by which the sanctified, still weak, are strengthened with spiritual vigour, so that the inner man may grow, become strong, and advance towards perfection, for their own salvation and for the glory of God and Christ. 2 Cor. 1:21: "He who establishes (confirms) us in Christ is God." Col. 1:10: "Growing in the knowledge of God." "Made strong with all power, according to the glorious might of him," etc. 2 Thess. 3:3: "The Lord is faithful, who will establish you."

units.la: Etiàm hæc actio realis est; ut patet ex termino reali, incremento novi hominis. Et quidem efficax hyperphysica: Divina enim hæc efficientia superat omnia obstacula. mus, est Gloria DEI; quæ in Ejus φιλανθρωπία, multiformi sapientia, constanti fidelitate, iupereminenti potentia, mirabiliter elucescit. Hæc sanctificatos agnoscere & celebrare oportet: Rom. V, 9. 9. 10. Eph. 3, 10, 11, I, 19. 1 Thess. 5, 24. 1 Petr, II, 19.
units.tr: This action is also real, as is clear from its real term, the growth of the new man. It is indeed efficacious and hyperphysical, for this divine efficiency overcomes all obstacles. The end of it is the glory of God, which shines wondrously in his love of mankind, his manifold wisdom, his constant faithfulness, and his surpassing power. The sanctified ought to acknowledge and celebrate this: Rom. 5:9, 10; Eph. 3:10, 11; Eph. 1:19; 1 Thess. 5:24; 1 Pet. 1:19.

units.la: Isti summo fini subordinatur alter, ipsorum conservatorum Beatitudo æterna. Hinc diserte Apostolus, 2 Thess. I, 9, 10. Oramus semper pro vobis, ut Deus - complcat - opus fidei potenter. Hebr. 10, 35, -39.
units.tr: Subordinate to this highest end is another, the eternal blessedness of those who are preserved. Hence the Apostle says expressly, 2 Thess. 1:9, 10: "We always pray for you, that God may fulfil the work of faith powerfully." Heb. 10:35–39.

units.la: XII. Ex superioribus abunde patet, vere fideles perseverare in isto statu; nec fieri posse, ut totaliter ac finaliter deficiant. Quod tenendum contra Pontificios, Socinianos, Anabaptistas, & Remonstrantes. Lutherani vero statuunt, eos quidem totaliter, non tamen finaliter, posse deficere. Nec difficile est Classes argumentorum ex præmissis construere: utpote 1. Ex decreto Electionis; ex cujus immutabili certitudine sequitur, quod electi totaliter deficere non possint, nedum finaliter. Vide sup. th. 4. & cap. 6. th. 7.
units.tr: XII. From what has been said above it is abundantly clear that true believers persevere in this state, and that it is not possible for them to fall away totally and finally. This must be held against the Papists, the Socinians, the Anabaptists, and the Remonstrants. The Lutherans, however, maintain that they can indeed fall away totally, but not finally. Nor is it difficult to construct classes of arguments from the premises, namely: 1. From the decree of election. From its unchangeable certainty it follows that the elect cannot fall away totally, much less finally. See above, th. 4, and ch. 6, th. 7.

units.la: 2. Ex certissimis Promissionibus, de perseverantia in nobis efficienda. Vide th. 5.
units.tr: 2. From the most certain promises concerning the perseverance to be effected in us. See th. 5.

units.la: 3. Ex validissima salutis æternæ, & mediorum istuc necessariorum, pro nobis impetratione per Christum; ejusdemque intercessione, quæ semper exauditur. Vide th. 6.
units.tr: 3. From the most valid impetration, through Christ, of eternal salvation and of the means necessary to it for us, and from his intercession, which is always heard. See th. 6.

units.la: 4. Ex efficaci applicatione salutis impetratæ, ac mediorum necessariorum, in ipsis redemtis. Vide th. 7. & seqq.
units.tr: 4. From the efficacious application of the salvation procured, and of the necessary means, to the redeemed themselves. See th. 7 and following. ## XIII. Objection 1.

units.la: XIII. Obj. 1.

Aliqui homines fidei professionem, & communionem Ecclesiæ, deserunt totaliter. Ergo. Resp. Isti à posteriori deprehenduntur nunquam habuisse vivam ac salvificam fidem, aut communionem internam Ecclesiæ mysticæ; sed tantum fidem historicam, ac temporalem, vel simulatam. latam; & gratiam non regenerantem ad salutem, sed quadantenùs illuminantem & refrœnantem; 1ob. 2, 19.
units.tr: Some men wholly abandon the profession of faith and the communion of the Church. Therefore (the perseverance of believers fails). Answer: These men are discovered, from the outcome, never to have had a living and saving faith or internal communion with the mystical Church, but only a historical and temporal faith, or a feigned one, and a grace that does not regenerate unto salvation but only somewhat enlightens and restrains. 1 John 2:19.

units.la: Obj. 2. Occurrunt exempla varia; ut Adami, Angelorum lapsorum, Davidis, Salomonis, Petri, Judæ Ifcariotæ, Hymenæi, Demæ. &c. Ergò. Resp. 1. Adamus, cùm laberetur primùm, non fuit sub Fœdere Euangelico; sed Legali. 2. Angeli lapfi similiter sub aliquo Fœdere operum fuerunt; quod non habuit easdem promissiones cum Euangelico. 3. David nec totaliter defecit; quod patet ex precatione, Pfal. LI. 13. nec finaliter; quia resipuit. 4. Salomonis Apostasiam totalem & finalem Adversarii probare non possunt. 5. Cum in Petri ore confessio deficeret, non defecit tamen fides in corde; juxta promissionem. Luc. 22, 32. 6. Judas Apostolarum quidem deferuit; non autem veram fidem sàlvificam, quam nunquàm habuit. 7. Hymenæus, aliique similes, duntaxat temporarii fuerunt; non verè fideles. 8. Demas quidem dicitur præfens fæculum dilexisse, ut vitam suam periculo exponere noluerit, & Paulum deseruerit: sed hinc nihil conficitur pro totali ac finali defectione à fide salvificâ. Si verò prorsùs defecisset, iterùm à posteriori liqueret, ipsum nunquàm fuisse verè fidelem.
units.tr: Objection 2. Various examples occur: Adam, the fallen angels, David, Solomon, Peter, Judas Iscariot, Hymenaeus, Demas, etc. Therefore (the saints can fall totally and finally). Answer 1. Adam, when he first fell, was not under the covenant of the Gospel but under the covenant of the Law. 2. The fallen angels likewise were under some covenant of works, which did not have the same promises as the Gospel. 3. David did not fall totally, as is clear from his prayer, Ps. 51:13, nor finally, because he repented. 4. The adversaries cannot prove that Solomon's apostasy was total and final. 5. When confession failed in Peter's mouth, faith did not nevertheless fail in his heart, according to the promise, Luke 22:32. 6. Judas indeed fell away from the apostles, but not from true saving faith, which he never had. 7. Hymenaeus and others like him were only temporary, not truly believers. 8. Demas is said to have loved the present age, so that he was unwilling to expose his life to danger and deserted Paul; but nothing follows from this for a total and final defection from saving faith. If he had indeed wholly fallen away, it would again be clear a posteriori that he had never been truly a believer.

units.la: Obj. 3. Peccata, qualia David, aliique, commiferunt, digna sunt, ob quæ tales Dei gratiâ penitùs destituantur: nec possunt simul consistere cum verâ fide & sanctimoniâ. Resp. 1. Alia est ratio Fœderis gratiæ, per quod verè fœderatis omnia & singula sua peccata non solùm remittuntur; sed & vitæ spiritualis principium in iis potenter confervatur, unde ex lapsû denuò resurgunt. 2. Tam contraria, ut sunt hinc vera fides, ac vita spiritualis & sanctimonia; indè peccata, inprimis gravia; simul in eodem subjecto singulari esse nequeunt secundùm idem, & & confervandis, etiàm exeri ac demonstrari dicitur. Sic Pater etiàm in hoc negotio operatur per Spiritum Sanctum. Vide insuper Eph. II, 1,-5, 20, 21, 22. 1 Cor. I, 8, 9. 10, 13. Phil. 1, 6. 2 Theff. 2, 15, 16, 17. Rom. 8, 17. 1 Petr. I, 3, 4, 5. Eandem gratiam petebat David Psal. 51, 13, 4. cxliii, 10.
units.tr: Objection 3. Sins such as those David and others committed are worthy of this, that such men should be utterly deprived of God's grace, and they cannot consist together with true faith and holiness. Answer 1. The covenant of grace is of a different kind, by which for those truly within it not only are all and each of their sins remitted, but also the principle of spiritual life is powerfully preserved in them, whence they rise again after a fall. 2. True faith, spiritual life and holiness are so contrary to grave sins, especially, that they cannot be together in the same singular subject in the same respect; and the Father also works in this matter through the Holy Spirit, both in preserving and in bringing forth and displaying these graces. See further Eph. 2:1–5, 20–22; 1 Cor. 1:8, 9, 10, 13; Phil. 1:6; 2 Thess. 2:15–17; Rom. 8:17; 1 Pet. 1:3, 4, 5. David asked for the same grace: Psal. 51:13, 14; Psal. 143:10.

units.la: VIII. Potenti illi ac reali operationi Divinæ, subservit moralis, per institutionem, & castigationem.
units.tr: VIII. Moral means, through instruction and chastisement, serve that powerful and real operation of God.

units.la: Institutio fit per Verbum Dei: quod ipsum, sub potenti illâ reali hyperphysicâ operatione Spiritûs, est semen incorruptibile regenerationis nostræ, vitam illam producens, quæ manet in æternum. Unde 1 Petr. I, 23. Regeniti ex femine incorruptibili; id est, per sermonem Dei vivum, & manentem in æternum. Eph. 4, 12, -16.
units.tr: Instruction is effected through the Word of God, which itself, under that powerful, real, and supernatural operation of the Spirit, is the incorruptible seed of our regeneration, producing that life which abides forever. Hence 1 Pet. 1:23: "Born again of incorruptible seed"; that is, "through the living word of God, which abides forever." Eph. 4:12-16.

units.la: Institutio sæpè dogmatica adhibetur, quæ officium perseverantiæ præscribit: additis etiàm promissionibus: Matth. 24, 13. Qui subsisterit ad finem usque, is servabitur. Apoc. II, 10, 11. Esto fidelis, usque ad mortem, & dabo tibi coronam vitæ. - Qui vicerit, nequaquam lædetur à morte secundâ. Hebr. 3, 14. Atque item comminationibus; Rom. 8, 13. Si secundum carnem vixeritis, futurum est ut moriamini. Ezech. 33, 13, 14, 15. Gal. 5, 19, 20, 21. Hujusmodi comminationes ostendunt, quid inspectâ fidelium infirmitate, fieri posset; ut majori studio ad gratiam Dei confugiant. Insignis adhortatio commemoratur Act. 14, 22. ubi de Paulo & Barnabâ; Confirmantes animos discipulorum: hortantes, ut permanerent in fide. Similis dehortatio à contrariâ defectione est, Hebr. 10, 25, 35. Accedit reprehensio; quâ aberrare incipientibus, peccati sui fœditas exponitur, ut ad veram resipiscentiam adducantur: Tit. I, 13. Gal. 3, 1, 3. 2 Cor. 7, 9, 10, 11.
units.tr: Instruction is often given in the form of doctrine, which prescribes the duty of perseverance and adds promises: Matt. 24:13, "He who endures to the end shall be saved"; Rev. 2:10-11, "Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life," and "He who overcomes shall not be hurt by the second death"; Heb. 3:14. It likewise adds warnings: Rom. 8:13, "If you live according to the flesh, you are going to die"; Ezek. 33:13-15; Gal. 5:19-21. Warnings of this kind show what could happen, given the weakness of the faithful, so that they may flee with greater zeal to the grace of God. A notable exhortation is recorded in Acts 14:22, concerning Paul and Barnabas, "confirming the souls of the disciples and exhorting them to continue in the faith." A similar dissuasion from the opposite defection is Heb. 10:25, 35. Reproof is also added, by which the foulness of sin is exposed to those who begin to go astray, so that they may be brought to true repentance: Tit. 1:13; Gal. 3:1, 3; 2 Cor. 7:9-11.

units.la: Verbo Deus Sacramenta voluit esse annexa; sigillorum instar; quibus gratia Dei, & communio Fœderis æterni, obsignatur fidelibus; atque ipsorum gratitudo erga Deum, ac sanctimonia, vicissim confirmatur. Ut patet de Circumcisione; Gen. 17,7. De Baptismo; Rom. 6,4,22. Gal. 3,27,29. Tit. 3, 5. De S. Cœnâ; 1 Cor. XI, 24, 25, 28,29. 10, 21. Quæ autem beneficia sic ex instituto ipsius Dei & Christi fidelibus obsignantur, eadem deinceps certissimè ab iis percipiuntur.
units.tr: God willed that the sacraments be joined to the Word, like seals, by which the grace of God and the fellowship of the eternal covenant are sealed to believers, and their gratitude toward God and their holiness are in turn confirmed. This is clear for circumcision, Gen. 17:7; for baptism, Rom. 6:4, 22; Gal. 3:27, 29; Tit. 3:5; and for the Lord's Supper, 1 Cor. 11:24, 25, 28, 29; 10:21. The benefits which are thus sealed to believers by the institution of God and of Christ are afterwards most certainly received by them.

units.la: IX. Institutioni illi adjungitur castigatio: Variæ enim afflictiones Divinitus immitti solent, ad carnem suppriměndam. Ità sc. qui Verbo non reguntur, verberibus corriguntur. Hinc David de se ipso: Psalm. 119, 71. Bonum mihi est, quòd afflictus fuerim; ut discam statuta Tua. 67. Ief. 26, 16. Hos. 2,6. VI, I. 1 Cor. XI, 32. Hebr. 12, 10, 11. Speciatim huc pertinet disciplina Ecclesiastica; quâ membra Ecclesiæ institutæ, de scandalis reprehenduntur; & si forte contumacius in illis pergant, à communione tandem segregantur; ut ipsi resipiscant; & alii, illorum exemplo moniti, in officiis perseverent: 1 Cor. V, 5, 6, 7.
units.tr: IX. Castigation is joined to this instruction. For various afflictions are usually sent by God to subdue the flesh; thus those who are not ruled by the Word are corrected with stripes. Hence David says of himself: Ps. 119:71, "It is good for me that I was afflicted, that I might learn your statutes"; ibid. 67; Isa. 26:16; Hos. 2:6; 6:1; 1 Cor. 11:32; Heb. 12:10, 11. Church discipline belongs especially here, by which the members of the instituted church are rebuked for scandals; and if they persist more stubbornly in them, they are at last cut off from communion, so that they may repent, and others, warned by their example, may persevere in their duties: 1 Cor. 5:5, 6, 7.
