For in the institution of this sacrament its administration is expressly joined to the preaching of the Word. "What God has joined together, let not man separate" (Matt. 19:6).

units.la: Hinc 2. de iisdem Ministris, 1 Cor. 4, 1. Sic de nobis reputet homo, ut de Ministris Christi, & Dispensatoribus Mysteriorum Dei. Istis autem Mysteriis Sacramenta quoque sunt accensenda. Confer Rom. 10, 15.
units.tr: Hence, second, concerning the same ministers: "Let a man so regard us, as ministers of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God" (1 Cor. 4:1). Sacraments too must be counted among these mysteries. Compare Rom. 10:15.

units.la: 3. Sigillo Principis nemo uti debet, ad aliquid ipsius auctoritate obsignandum, & confirmandum, nisi hoc ei mandatum fuerit. At hic nullis aliis istiusmodi mandatum datum est.
units.tr: Third, no one ought to use a prince's seal to seal or confirm anything by his authority unless it has been committed to him; but no such commission has been given to anyone in this matter.

units.la: 4. Accedunt exempla in SS. Literis commemorata. De Johanne Baptistâ dictum est satis. Similiter de Apostolis & Discipulis Christi; Joh. 3, 26. IV, 1, 2. Act. II, 38, 41. VIII, 26, 29, 38. IX, 10, 11, 17, 18. XXII, 16, XVI, 14, 15, 32, 33. 1 Cor. I, 14, 16.
units.tr: Fourth, there are examples recorded in Holy Scripture. Enough has been said of John the Baptist. Likewise of the apostles and disciples of Christ: John 3:26; 4:1, 2; Acts 2:38, 41; 8:26, 29, 38; 9:10, 11, 17, 18; 22:16; 16:14, 15, 32, 33; 1 Cor. 1:14, 16.

units.la: XXIV. Jus istud nimis coarctant, qui in baptizaturo requirunt, 1. vocationem legitimam; 2. doctrinam rectam; & 3. vitam puram.
units.tr: XXIV. Those who require of the one who baptizes, first, a lawful calling; second, sound doctrine; and third, a pure life, restrict this right too narrowly.

units.la: Quod enim ad primam conditionem attinet; Ministrum quidem legitimè vocatum esse oportet, respectû conscientiæ ipsius: si tamen quid secus initio fuerit factum, atque interim ille Ecclesiâ acquiescente Ministerio fungatur, & aliquos baptizet, hi pro legitimè baptizatis haberi etiàm debent. Quod ad secundam; ubi essentialia fidei Christianæ, atque ipsius Baptismi, servantur, non est Baptismus pro nullo habendus.
units.tr: As to the first condition: the minister must indeed be lawfully called, with respect to his own conscience. If, however, something was done otherwise at the start, and yet he discharges the ministry with the consent of the Church and baptizes some people, these also ought to be held as lawfully baptized. As to the second: where the essentials of the Christian faith and of Baptism itself are preserved, the Baptism is not to be regarded as null.

units.la: Quantum denique ad tertiam; Minister procul dubio pietati ac sanctimoniæ debet operam dare: 1 Tim. III. 2. Tit. I, 7. At si peccata ipsius clandestina sint, aut Minister disciplinâ Ecclesiasticâ necdum coercitus & prohibitus, tenendum est istud vulgatum;
units.tr: Finally, as to the third: the minister undoubtedly ought to devote effort to piety and holiness (1 Tim. 3:2; Titus 1:7). But if his sins are secret, or if the minister has not yet been restrained and prohibited by church discipline, that common saying must be held:

units.la: Vim Sacramenti non mutat vita Ministri. Sic rebaptizari non oportuit eos, qui à Judâ proditore, unâ cum aliis Discipulis Christi functionem sacram obeunte, fuissent baptizati. Quid tum enim, si infidi fuerunt quidam; nam ipsorum infidelitas fidem Dei cassam reddet? Rom. 3, 3. Confer Matth. 23, 2, 3. Phil. I, 16, 18.
units.tr: The life of the minister does not change the power of the sacrament. Thus those who were baptized by Judas the traitor, while he performed the sacred function along with the other disciples of Christ, ought not to have been rebaptized. For what then, if some were unfaithful? Will their unfaithfulness make the faith of God void? (Rom. 3:3). Compare Matt. 23:2, 3; Phil. 1:16, 18.

units.la: XXV. Alii nimis extendunt jus baptizandi, dum illud Laicis, etiam fœminis, vel pueris lu dentibus, aut infidelibus, & non baptizatis, quoque tribuunt,
units.tr: XXV. Others extend the right to baptize too far, when they grant it also to laymen, even to women, to boys at play, or to unbelievers and the unbaptized.

units.la: Contra istos afferimus primò, nullum laicis, nedum mulieribus, jus esse baptizandi: cum ejus rei nullum mandatum, nullum exemplum, extet in Sacris Literis. Hûc accedit, quòd etiam fœminis interdictum sit palàm in Ecclesiâ loqui; 1 Cor. 14, 34, 35. 1 Tim. II, 11, 12. Et quòd Pontificii, hîc à nobis dissentientes, Sacramentum Eucharistiæ nequaquàm concedant Laicis administrandum: atqui idem est utriusque Sacramenti Auctor, & iidem utriusque Ministri instituti.
units.tr: Against these men we maintain, first, that laymen have no right to baptize, still less women, since there is no command or example of this in the Sacred Writings. In addition, women are plainly forbidden to speak in the Church (1 Cor. 14:34, 35; 1 Tim. 2:11, 12). Moreover, the Papists, who differ from us here, by no means allow the Lord's Supper to be administered by laymen, yet the Author of both sacraments is the same, and the same ministers were appointed for both.

units.la: Obj. 1. Zippora, Mosis uxor, filium suum circumcidisse legitur, Exod. 4, 25. Resp. 1. Factum istud aliis etiam adjunctis, utpote convitiis & obmurmuratione, vitiatum, non probat jus. Quid, quòd præsente marito, primario Dei Prophetâ, id agere fuerit ausa? Certè, per Adversarios nulla mulier præsumeret baptizare sub Episcopi oculis. 2. Circumcisio instituta fuit tempore Abrahami, antequàm ordinaria rerum sacrarum administratio itâ esset circumscripta & limitata, ut fa-ctum ětum posteà sub V. T. atque etiàm sub N.
units.tr: Objection 1. We read that Zipporah, the wife of Moses, circumcised her son (Exod. 4:25). Answer 1. That deed, being tainted by other circumstances, namely reproaches and grumbling, does not prove a right. Moreover, did she dare to do it in the presence of her husband, the chief prophet of God? Certainly, among our opponents no woman would presume to baptize under the eyes of a bishop. 2. Circumcision was instituted in the time of Abraham, before the ordinary administration of sacred things was so circumscribed and limited that the deed could later be done under the Old Testament, or even under the New.

units.la: Obj. 2. Petrus Actor. 10, 48. jussit eos, qui in domo Cornelii Spiritum Sanctum acceperant, baptizari. Ergò. Resp. Non dicitur, id factum per fideles Laïcos. Nos potiùs factum intelligimus, si non per ipsum Petrum, saltem per Euangelistam, aut alium aliquem Verbi Ministrum.
units.tr: Objection 2. Peter (Acts 10:48) ordered those who had received the Holy Spirit in the house of Cornelius to be baptized. Therefore... Answer. It is not said that this was done by lay believers. We understand that it was done, if not by Peter himself, at least by an evangelist or some other minister of the Word.

units.la: Asserimus secundò, sacra ludum nequaquàm fieri oportere; & Baptismum sic datum differre à vero, quantum histrio à rege quem repræsentat.
units.tr: We maintain, secondly, that sacred things must by no means be made into a game, and that baptism so given differs from true baptism as much as an actor differs from the king he represents.

units.la: Atque item tertiò, neutiquàm pro vero Baptismo habendum esse, qui à Muhammedano aliquo, similive infideli, esset collatus: cùm talis homo hactenùs non fit idoneus Baptismum accipere, nedùm aliis eum conferre.
units.tr: Likewise, thirdly, that baptism conferred by some Mohammedan, or similar unbeliever, must in no way be regarded as true baptism, since such a man is so far not fit to receive baptism, much less to confer it on others.

units.la: XXVI. Nunc de obječto videamus! Requiritur, ut saltem sit homo, & quidem vivens, cui conferetur Ba- ptismus. Hoc exigit,
units.tr: XXVI. Now let us consider the subject. It is required that the one to whom baptism is conferred be at least a human being, and indeed a living one. This is demanded by:

units.la: 1. Institutio Christi; Matth. 18, 19.
units.tr: 1. The institution of Christ (Matt. 28:19).

units.la: 2. Praxis Johannis Baptistæ, & Discipulorum Christi.
units.tr: 2. The practice of John the Baptist and of the disciples of Christ.

units.la: 3. Finis Baptismi; obsignatio gratiæ regenerantis & justificantis.
units.tr: 3. The purpose of baptism, which is the seal of regenerating and justifying grace.

units.la: 4. Analogia aliorum Sacramentorum, tùm V. tùm N. Test.
units.tr: 4. The analogy of the other sacraments, both of the Old and of the New Testament.

units.la: Rejicimus igitur primò Baptismum campanarum; quem Pontificii solent adhibere, nomina hominum iis indentes, adscitis etiàm testibus.
units.tr: We therefore reject, first, the baptism of bells, which the Papists are accustomed to employ, inscribing the names of men on them, with witnesses also added.

units.la: Rejicimus deinde Baptismum mortuorum; ad quem referimus Baptismum viventium loco ac vice mortuorum: cùm Sacramentum istud mortuis prodesse non possit. Eccl. xi, 3.
units.tr: We reject next the baptism of the dead, which we refer to the baptism of the living in place and stead of the dead, since that sacrament cannot benefit the dead (Eccl. 11:3).

units.la: Id tamen fecisse leguntur antiqui nonnulli hæretici. Nec desunt qui existiment, Apostolum spestàsse istum morem. 1 Cor. 15, 29. Quid facient βαπτιζόμενοι ὑπὲρ τῶν νεκρῶν, &c. Loci istius variæ quidem adferuntur explicationes. Mihi vero præ cæteris placent istæ, quarum una Baptismum sanguinis & persecutionum, super statû mortuorum, eorumque resurrectione, intelligit. Vide seqq. verss. 30, 31, 32. cum Act. 23, 6. XXIV, 21. XXVIII, 20. Altera accipit ipsum Baptismum fluminis, sive aquæ: quatenus, tanquàm mortui cum Christo, aquam subimus. Rom. 6, 3. Consepulti igitur Ei sumus per Baptismum in mortem.
units.tr: Yet some ancient heretics are read to have done this, and there are not lacking those who think the Apostle alluded to this custom (1 Cor. 15:29): "What will they do [βαπτιζόμενοι ὑπὲρ τῶν νεκρῶν], etc.?" Various explanations of that passage are offered. But to me the following please most of all: one of them understands the baptism of blood and persecutions, concerning the state of the dead and their resurrection. See the following verses 30, 31, 32, together with Acts 23:6; 24:21; 28:20. Another takes it as the baptism of water itself, insofar as we, as dead with Christ, undergo the water: "Therefore we were buried with Him through baptism into death" (Rom. 6:3, 4).

units.la: XXVII. Baptizandi autem tùm adulti, tùm infantes fœderati.
units.tr: XXVII. Those to be baptized are both adults and the infants of the covenant.

units.la: Sed adultos priùs in Religione Christianâ institui, & fidem ac resipiscentiam profiteri oportet. Hoc patet, 1. ex solenni illâ institutione Baptismi, Matth. 28, 19. Marc. 16, 15.
units.tr: But adults must first be instructed in the Christian religion and profess faith and repentance. This is clear: 1. from that solemn institution of baptism (Matt. 28:19; Mark 16:15).

units.la: 2. Ex adjunctâ promissione, & oppositâ comminatione, Marc. 16, 16.
units.tr: 2. From the promise attached to it and the threat set against it (Mark 16:16).

units.la: 3. Ex praxi Johannis Baptistæ, & Apostolorum; Matth. III. 1, 2. &c. Act. II. 38, 41. &c.
units.tr: 3. From the practice of John the Baptist and of the Apostles (Matt. 3:1, 2, etc.; Acts 2:38, 41, etc.).

units.la: Propterea 4. Hebr. 6, 2. fundamento Resipiscentiæ ab operibus mortuis, & Fidei in Deum, adjicitur Baptismatum doctrina.
units.tr: Therefore, 4. Heb. 6:2 adds the doctrine of baptisms to the foundation of repentance from dead works and faith in God.

units.la: Nullum interim discrimen faciendum est gentis, nationis, sexûs, aut qualiscunque conditionis externæ: Gal. III. 27, 28.
units.tr: Meanwhile no distinction is to be made of nation, race, sex, or any external condition whatever (Gal. 3:27, 28).

units.la: XXVIII. Ad infantes quod attinet; eos qui parentibus fidelibus, aut saltem alterutro fideli, nati sunt, etiàm baptizandos esse, asserimus contra A- nabaptistas.
units.tr: XXVIII. As for infants, we maintain, against the Anabaptists, that those born to believing parents, or at least to one believing parent, are also to be baptized.

units.la: Argumentamur autem 1. à Fœdere gratiæ, ejusque promissis. Sic enim Actor. II. 38, 39. Petrus ad Judæos corde compunctos, & salutare consilium rogantes: Resipiscite, & baptizetur unusquisque vestrûm in nomen Iesu Christi, in remissionem peccatorum: & accipietis donum Spiritus Sancti. Vobis enim facta est promissio, & liberis vestris, & omnibus longè post futuris, quoscunque videlicet advocaverit Dominus Deus noster. Quibus facta est promissio Foederis gratiæ, illi sub N. T. debent baptizari in remissionem peccatorum. Hæc enim est illatio Apostoli.' Porrò autem subsumit; Istis Judæis corde compunctis, unà cum liberis ipsorum, factam esse promissionem, &c. Unde pro conclusione sequitur; illos baptizandos fuisse, unà cum liberis ipsorum. Quod autem infantes debeant intelligi eodem Fœdere comprehensi, patet ex verbis Fœderis, Gen. XVII, 7, 11, 12. ubi institutum, ut infantes mascu li octavo die propterea circumciderentur.
units.tr: We argue, first, from the covenant of grace and its promises. For thus Peter speaks to the Jews, pricked in heart and asking for the saving counsel (Acts 2:38, 39): "Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins; and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is made to you, and to your children, and to all who are afar off, whomever the Lord our God shall call." To those to whom the promise of the covenant of grace is made, they ought to be baptized under the New Testament for the remission of sins. This is the Apostle's inference. Next he assumes: the promise was made to these Jews pricked in heart, together with their children, etc. Hence the conclusion follows: they were to be baptized, together with their children. That infants must be understood as included in the same covenant is clear from the words of the covenant (Gen. 17:7, 11, 12), where it was instituted that male infants should be circumcised on the eighth day.

units.la: 2. Ex solenni institutione Baptismi pro Sacramento initiationis, in locum Circumcisionis. Sic enim extat Matth. XXVIII, 19, 20. Profecti ergo discipulos facite (μαθητεύσατε) omnes gentes; baptizantes eos in nomen Patris, & Filii, & Spiritus Sancti: Docentes eos observare omnia quæcunque præcepi vobis. Christus tria mandavit; ex universis gentibus sibi discipulos quasi in scholam colligi; hos baptismo initiari; & doceri observationem omnium quæ ipse præcepit. Ab ista initiatione per Baptismum infantes Fœderati minimè excluduntur; imò verò in eâ includuntur; ut patet ex constitutione illâ Genes. XVII. 7, 11, 12. ubi de Circumcisione, Sacramento initiationis. Quod verò Baptismus Circumcisioni successerit; & res eadem, quæ olim Circumcisione significata fuit, nunc nobis Baptismo significetur, clarius etiam patet, ex Col. II. 2, 12, 13. ubi Apostolus Legis cerimonialis, & speciatim Circumcisionis pro N. T. abrogationem eo probat; quòd fideles N. T. rem Circumcisione olim significatam, haberent sibi modò significatam Baptismo. Gratia enim sub N. T. non est coarctata; sed latius extensa, quàm fuit sub V. T. Gal. III. 28.
units.tr: 2. From the solemn institution of baptism as the sacrament of initiation in place of circumcision. For thus it stands (Matt. 28:19, 20): "Go, therefore, and make disciples [μαθητεύσατε] of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you." Christ commanded three things: that disciples be gathered for Himself from all nations as into a school; that these be initiated by baptism; and that they be taught to observe all that He has commanded. From this initiation through baptism the covenanted infants are by no means excluded; rather they are included in it, as is clear from that ordinance (Gen. 17:7, 11, 12), where circumcision, the sacrament of initiation, is spoken of. That baptism succeeded circumcision, and that the same thing which was once signified by circumcision is now signified to us by baptism, is also clearer from Col. 2:11, 12, where the Apostle proves the abrogation of the ceremonial law, and specifically of circumcision, under the New Testament by this: that believers under the New Testament have now signified to them by baptism the thing once signified by circumcision. For grace under the New Testament is not confined, but extended more widely than it was under the Old Testament (Gal. 3:28).

units.la: 3. A gratiâ Spiritûs Sancti. Qui enim Spiritûs Sancti sunt participes, hos quoque baptizari oportet; docente Petro, Act. 10, 47. Num quis aquam prohibere potest, quo minus baptizentur isti, qui Spiritum Sanctum acceperunt, sic ut & nos? At vero Infantes Fidelium sunt quoque participes Spiritus Sancti: sic enim Sancti dicuntur, 1 Cor. VII.14. Quòd autem haec sanctimonia etiam salutaris sit, liquet sententia ipsius Christi, Matth. XIX. 14. Marc. X. 14. Luc. XVIII. 16. Sinite puerulos venire ad me; & ne prohibete eos: talium enim est regnum Dei. Qui jus coelestis beatitudinis habent, iidem ex naturali miseria liberati sunt; Spiritum Christi habent, & per eum regeniti sunt: Rom. VIII. 8, 9. Joh. III. 3, 5.
units.tr: 3. From the grace of the Holy Spirit. For those who are partakers of the Holy Spirit ought also to be baptized, as Peter teaches (Acts 10:47): "Can anyone forbid water, that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit just as we have?" But the infants of believers are also partakers of the Holy Spirit; for thus they are called "holy" (1 Cor. 7:14). That this holiness is also saving is clear from the very words of Christ (Matt. 19:14; Mark 10:14; Luke 18:16): "Suffer the little children to come to me, and do not forbid them; for of such is the kingdom of God." Those who have a right to heavenly blessedness are also delivered from natural misery; they have the Spirit of Christ and have been born again through Him (Rom. 8:8, 9; John 3:3, 5).

units.la: 4. A communione cum Christo, & Ecclesia ipsius; in quâ etiam includitur spiritualis ablutio, res Baptismo significata: cùm autem illa infantibus fidelium quoque conveniat, jam signum ipsum, & per illud insitio in communionem Christi atque Ecclesiae, non debet iis negari. Antecedens de infantibus fidelium patet, Joël. II. 16. Congregate populum, sanctificate congregationem, coadunate senes, congregate parvulos & sugentes ubera. Ezech. XVI. 20. Tulisti insuper filios tuos, & filias tuas, quos generasti Mihi, &c. Adde Deut. XXIX. 10, 11. Gal. II. 15. 1 Cor. VII. 14. Ita palàm infantes Ecclesiae, & communioni gratiae in eâ, accensentur. Hanc verò communionem, & in eâ purificationem, obsignat nunc Baptismus: unde Actor. II. 41. Qui libenter receperunt sermonem ejus, baptizati sunt; & additae sunt Ecclesiae die illo animae quasi ter mille. Confer Rom. VI. 3, 4.
units.tr: 4. From communion with Christ and His Church, which also includes spiritual washing, the thing signified by baptism. Since this belongs also to the infants of believers, the sign itself, and through it the engrafting into the communion of Christ and the Church, ought not to be denied them. The antecedent, concerning the infants of believers, is plain from Joel 2:16: "Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the little ones and those who nurse at the breast." Ezek. 16:20: "You have moreover taken your sons and your daughters, whom you bore to Me," etc. Add Deut. 29:10, 11; Gal. 2:15; 1 Cor. 7:14. Thus infants are plainly reckoned to the Church and to the communion of grace in it. This communion, and the purification in it, is now sealed by baptism; whence Acts 2:41: "Those who gladly received his word were baptized; and there were added to the Church that day about three thousand souls." Compare Rom. 6:3, 4.

units.la: 1 Cor. XII. 13. Gal. III. 27. Eph. V. 25, 26. Ad Ecclesiam igitur, omnesque communionis istius veré participes, pertinet etiam Baptismus, lavacrum aquae, quo Verbum promissionis obsignando singulis applicatur. Confer etiam exemplum extraordinarii illius Baptismi sub V. T. 1 Cor. 10. 1, 2.
units.tr: 1 Cor. XII. 13. Gal. III. 27. Eph. V. 25, 26. Baptism, the washing of water by which the Word of promise is applied to each person in its sealing, therefore belongs to the Church and to all who truly partake of this communion. Compare also the example of that extraordinary Baptism under the Old Testament, 1 Cor. 10. 1, 2.

units.la: XXIX. Obj. 1. Nusquam extat in SS. Literis quòd
units.tr: XXIX. Objection 1. Nowhere does it stand written in Holy Scripture

units.la: quòd Apostoli Infantes baptizârint. Ergò Resp. Καλὰ λέξιν id quidem non extat; ut neque extat, eos fœminas ad Sacram Cœnam admisisse. Quemadmodùm tamen de posteriori non dubitant Adversarii, sic neque de priori nos dubitare oportet. Vide interim exempla familiarum baptizatarum, sine restrictione ad adultos; Act. 16, 15, 33. 1 Cor. 1, 16.
units.tr: that the apostles baptized infants. Therefore. Answer: Well said [Καλὰ λέξιν]. Indeed, that does not stand written, any more than that they admitted women to the Holy Supper. Yet as the Adversaries do not doubt the latter, neither ought we to doubt the former. Meanwhile, see the examples of baptized households, without any restriction to adults: Acts 16. 15, 33. 1 Cor. 1. 16.

units.la: Obj. 2. In hominibus ad Ecclesiam institutam adscifcendis, eique per Baptismum initiandis, præcedit institutio, & ipsorum fides: Matth. 28. 19. Marc. 16, 16. Resp. Istud de adultis intelligendum est: sed eâdem operâ quoque μαθητεύοντες, discipuli fiunt, atque in familiam & scholam Christi introducuntur, & adsciscuntur, eorum infantes.
units.tr: Obj. 2. In the admission of men to the Church as instituted, and their initiation into it by Baptism, instruction and their own faith come first: Matt. 28:19; Mark 16:16. Answer. That must be understood of adults. But by the same action, as they are made disciples [μαθητεύοντες] and introduced and admitted into the household and school of Christ, so are their infants.

units.la: Obj. 3. Eâdem ratione forent infantes etiâm admittendi ad Cœnam Dominicam: quod absurdum. Ergò. Resp. Cum res Baptismo significata ad infantes quoque pertineat, atque hi Baptismi capaces sint, ab eo prohiberi non debent: aliter res habet in sacrâ Cœnâ, Sacramento nutritionis; ad cujus participationem prærequiritur etiâm debita sui exploratio; 1 Cor. xi, 28. cujus infantes non sunt capaces.
units.tr: Obj. 3. By the same reasoning infants would also have to be admitted to the Lord's Supper, which is absurd. Therefore. Answer. Since the thing signified by Baptism pertains also to infants, and since they are capable of Baptism, they ought not to be barred from it. It is otherwise in the holy Supper, the sacrament of nourishment, for participation in which a due self-examination is also required beforehand, 1 Cor. 11:28, and infants are not capable of this.

units.la: Obj. 4. Si Baptismus successisset in locum Circumcisionis, nihil opus fuisset circumcisos adhuc baptizari. Absurdum verò est consequens. Ergò. Resp. Quamvis Baptismus Circumcisioni successerit in N. Test.; tamen qui fuerant in infantiâ circumcisi, deindè etiam ineunte N. Testamento baptizati suat, ut ipsorum transitus in istam œconomiam, isto Sacramento obsignaretur.
units.tr: Obj. 4. If Baptism had succeeded into the place of circumcision, there would have been no need for those already circumcised to be baptized. But the consequence is absurd. Therefore. Answer. Although Baptism succeeded circumcision in the New Testament, nevertheless those who had been circumcised in infancy were also baptized at the beginning of the New Testament, so that their passage into this economy might be sealed by this sacrament.

units.la: Obj. 5. Infantes nondum intelligunt usum & efficaciam Baptismi; sic Pædobaptismusferè similis est Baptismo campanarum, apud Pontificios. Resp. Longè dispar est ratio: nam res significata ad infantes fœderatos etiâm verè pertinet; minimè verò ad campanas. Et Infantes, ubi adoleverint, gratiam Baptismo sibi significatam & obsignatam ipsi intelligent. Confer Iob. 13, 7. cum Psal. 22, 10, 11. Neque omittendum, quòd parentes eò magis admoneantur atque incitentur ad liberos istos piè educandos: Deut. 6, 7, 20. Eph. 6, 4. 2 Tim. 3, 15. Quid, quòd istud argumentum æquè olim contra Circumcisionem infantium urgeri potuisset, ut nunc contra eorum Baptismum?
units.tr: Obj. 5. Infants do not yet understand the use and efficacy of Baptism; thus infant baptism is almost like the baptism of bells among the Papists. Answer. The case is far different: for the thing signified pertains truly to covenanted infants, but in no way to bells. And infants, when they have grown up, will themselves understand the grace signified and sealed to them in Baptism. Compare Job 13:7 with Ps. 22:10, 11. Nor should it be omitted that parents are all the more admonished and stirred to bring up these children in godliness: Deut. 6:7, 20; Eph. 6:4; 2 Tim. 3:15. Moreover, could this argument not have been pressed just as well against the circumcision of infants in former times as it is now against their baptism?

units.la: XXX. Quæ sic asserta atque defensa sunt; non statim referri debent ad fœtus nondum natos, aut ex parte tantùm natos: cum tales separatim per se ad Ecclesiam institutam referri nondum possint.
units.tr: XXX. What has been asserted and defended in this way ought not straightway to be referred to unborn fetuses, or to those only partly born, since such cannot yet be separately referred to the instituted Church on their own.

units.la: Partus autem monstrosi, superioribus saltem partibus, ac potissimùm capite, rationis domicilio, humanam naturam retinentes, non debent à Baptismo prohiberi.
units.tr: Monstrous births, however, at least in their upper parts, and above all in the head, the seat of reason, retaining human nature, ought not to be barred from Baptism.

units.la: Quemadmodum neque spurii, parentibus, fide ac resipiscentiâ non omninò destitutis, nati. Locus Deut. XXIII. 2. restringendus est ad Politiam Israëliticam: neque sic accipiendus, quasi spurii, aliique ibi commemorati, ab omni gratiâ salutari, ejusque obsignatione per Sacramenta, fuissent exclusi.
units.tr: Likewise neither are illegitimate children, born of parents who have not wholly lacked faith and repentance, to be barred. Deut. 23:2 must be restricted to the Israelite polity, and it is not to be taken as if bastards and others mentioned there had been excluded from all saving grace and from its sealing through the sacraments.

units.la: Ad Infidelium libros quod attinet; cùm Baptismus sit signum Fœderis inter Deum, & inter nos ac semen nostrum, unde infideles alieni sunt; sequitur, tales liberos non esse ad Baptismum admittendos, nisi parentum alteruter saltem ad fidem convertatur; 1 Cor. 7. 14.
units.tr: As for the children of unbelievers: since Baptism is the sign of the covenant between God and us and our seed, from which unbelievers are aliens, it follows that such children are not to be admitted to Baptism unless at least one of the parents is converted to the faith; 1 Cor. 7:14.

units.la: Similiter neque baptizandi sunt liberi hæreticorum apertorum, à fundamento fidei Christianę verè aberrantium: aliter tamen statuendum de illis, qui fundamentum servant, licet erroribus aliis implicentur.
units.tr: Likewise children of open heretics, who have truly strayed from the foundation of the Christian faith, are not to be baptized. Otherwise, however, must we decide about those who keep the foundation, though they are entangled in other errors.

units.la: Quantum verò ad excommunicatos, si saltem alteruter parentum resipiscat, & Ecclesiæ reconciliari seriò studeat, liberi à Baptismo excludendi non sunt.
units.tr: As for excommunicated persons: if at least one of the parents repents and earnestly seeks reconciliation with the Church, the children are not to be excluded from Baptism.

units.la: Si quis infantes expositos sustulerit, & non subsit probabilis metus, ne sint parentibus Judæis, vel Muhammedanis, aut aliter prorsus infidelibus nati, parentum ἀςφρϊα videbitur compensanda pietate & ςφγή communis matris Ecclesiæ, atque eorum qui infantes expositos ex commiseratione tollunt.
units.tr: If anyone has taken up exposed infants, and there is no probable fear that they were born of Jewish or Muslim parents, or of parents altogether unbelieving in some other way, the lack of natural affection [ἀστοργία] of the parents will seem to be made good by the piety and affection [στοργή] of the common mother, the Church, and by those who take up exposed infants out of compassion.

units.la: Qui verò parentibus quidem non Christianis nati sunt, sed jure belli, emtionis, donationis, simili vel aliquâ ratione, in potestatem Christianorum venerunt: tutius videtur, si prius doceantur Religionem Christianam, deinde autem edita ejus confessione baptizentur.
units.tr: But those who were indeed born of non-Christian parents, yet came into the power of Christians by right of war, purchase, gift, or some similar means, it seems safer that they first be taught the Christian religion and then be baptized after they have made confession of it.

units.la: XXXI. Nunc de Baptismi necessitate videamus!
units.tr: XXXI. Let us now consider the necessity of Baptism.

units.la: Nos non solum necessitatem expedientiæ asserimus; respectu insignium ejus utilitatum atque effectuum: sed & necessitatem præcepti Divini; ut sine gravi culpa negligi non possit. Rejicimus igitur contrarium errorem Socinianorum, contendentium, aquæ Baptismum non habere præceptum Christi, aut saltem non perpetuum & universale.
units.tr: We do not assert only a necessity of expedience, with respect to its notable benefits and effects, but also a necessity of divine precept, so that it cannot be neglected without grave guilt. We therefore reject the contrary error of the Socinians, who contend that water baptism has no precept of Christ, or at least not a perpetual and universal one.

units.la: Argumentamur autem 1. Ex ipsâ Baptismi institutione; Joh.I, 33. Matth.28, 18, 19, 20. Marc.16, 15, 16.
units.tr: We argue, first, from the institution of Baptism itself: John 1:33. Matt. 28:18, 19, 20. Mark 16:15, 16.

units.la: 2. Ex praxi Johannis Baptistæ, & Discipulorum Christi secundum istud mandatum: Matth.III, 11, 13, 15, 16. Joh.III, 26. IV, 1, 2. Act.II, 38, 39, 41. VIII, 38. X. 47, 48. XVI, 15, 33. 1 Cor.I, 14, 16. Eph. 4, 5, 6. Hebr. 6, 1, 2.
units.tr: Second, from the practice of John the Baptist and of Christ's disciples in keeping with this command: Matt. 3:11, 13, 15, 16. John 3:26; 4:1, 2. Acts 2:38, 39, 41; 8:38; 10:47, 48; 16:15, 33. 1 Cor. 1:14, 16. Eph. 4:5, 6. Heb. 6:1, 2.

units.la: 3. Ex utilitate, non solum pro Ecclesia Christiana subinitiis N. T. primùm instituendâ; sed etiàm deinceps: Rom.VI, 3, 4. 1 Cor.XII, 13. Gal.III, 27. Col. II, 11, 12. Eph. 5, 25, 26. Item Marc.I, 4. Act.II, 38. XXII, 16. Tit.III, 5.
units.tr: Third, from its usefulness, not only for the Christian Church of the New Testament, which was first to be instituted in its beginnings, but also thereafter: Rom. 6:3, 4. 1 Cor. 12:13. Gal. 3:27. Col. 2:11, 12. Eph. 5:25, 26. Likewise Mark 1:4. Acts 2:38; 22:16. Titus 3:5.

units.la: 4. Propterea qui Baptismum Johannis olim rejecerunt in primis istis initiis dicuntur consilium Dei adversus seipsos rejecisse, Luc.VII, 30. Quanto magis istud dicendum, post folennem præcepti istius iterationem, & ampliorem extensionem, additis etiàm promissionibus præstantissimis ?
units.tr: Fourth, therefore those who in those first beginnings rejected the baptism of John are said to have rejected God's counsel against themselves, Luke 7:30. How much more must this be said after the solemn repetition of this precept and its wider extension, with the most excellent promises added!

units.la: Exc. Matt. 28, 19. Marc. 16, 16. agitur de doctrinâ & initiatione, sine ablutione, per aquam. Resp. 1. Imò propria vocabulorum significatio non est temerè deferenda. 2. Praxis Apostolorum eam confirmat. 3. Vox Baptismi doctrinam & institutionem sine ablutione in SS. Literis non significat. 4. Etiàm istìc doctrina satis diserte adjungitur Baptismo, tanquam res aliqua distincta.
units.tr: Objection: Matt. 28:19 and Mark 16:16 speak of teaching and initiation without washing with water. Answer. 1. Indeed, the proper meaning of words should not be lightly set aside. 2. The practice of the Apostles confirms this. 3. The word Baptism does not signify teaching and instruction without washing in the Holy Scriptures. 4. Even there, teaching is clearly enough joined to baptism as something distinct.

units.la: Obj. 1. Verus Christianismus, ac vita spiritualis, in homine interiori proprie consistit. Ergò nihil opus est Baptismo aquæ. Resp. Neg. confequ. cùm vita spiritualis actibus externis se quoque exerat ac demonstret; & adminiculis externis etiàm producatur, foveatur, promoveatur, Verbo sc. & Sacramentis: undè ipsi Sociniani usum Cœnæ Dominicæ aliquo modo agnoscunt & retinent.
units.tr: Objection 1. True Christianity and spiritual life consist properly in the inner man. Therefore there is no need of water baptism. Answer. I deny the consequence, since spiritual life also shows and manifests itself by external acts, and is also brought forth, nourished and promoted by external aids, namely the Word and the sacraments. Hence the Socinians themselves in some way acknowledge and retain the use of the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Obj. 2. Johannes dixit Matth. III, 11. Christum baptizaturum Spiritu & igne. Ergò Resp. Hoc dixit de Baptismo interno, quem Christus confert: sed non dixit, quòd Christus esset abrogaturus Baptismum aquæ.
units.tr: Objection 2. John said (Matt. 3:11) that Christ would baptize with the Spirit and with fire. Therefore... Answer. He said this of the internal baptism which Christ confers, but he did not say that Christ would abolish the baptism of water.

units.la: Obj. 3. Paulus negat, se missum fuisse ad baptizandum: 1 Cor. 1, 17. Ergò. Resp. Apostolus non loquitur absolutè, sed comparatè: quòd esset potiùs & principaliùs missus ad euangelizandum, quàm ad baptizandum: Confer Hos. 6, 6. Joh. 6, 27. Nam etiàm ipse aliquos baptizavit; verf. 16.
units.tr: Objection 3. Paul denies that he was sent to baptize, 1 Cor. 1:17. Therefore... Answer. The Apostle does not speak absolutely but comparatively: that he was sent chiefly and principally to preach the gospel rather than to baptize. Compare Hos. 6:6, John 6:27. For he himself also baptized some, v. 16.

units.la: XXXII. Non tamen agnoscimus absolutam necessitatem medii in Baptismo, acsi qualiscunque ejus privatio hominem necessariò damnaret. Nam 1. Gratia salutaris per Baptismum non confertur; sed ad eum præsupponitur, & per eum obsignatur. In quibus vera fides est cum resipiscentiâ, si adulti fuerint; aut Spiritus fidei ac resipiscentiæ, si sunt infantes; atque adeò Baptismus interior, & spiritualis ablutio peccatorum, per Christi sanguinem ac Spiritum; illi, secundùm Euangelium, non possunt ab æternâ salute excludi. Sed in quibusdam, citra Baptismum morientibus, ista bona insunt. Ergò, &c.
units.tr: XXXII. Nevertheless we do not acknowledge an absolute necessity of Baptism as a means, as though any lack of it whatever necessarily condemned a person. For, first, saving grace is not conferred through Baptism; rather it is presupposed to it and sealed by it. In those who have true faith with repentance, if they are adults, or the Spirit of faith and repentance, if they are infants, and so an inner baptism and spiritual washing away of sins through the blood and Spirit of Christ, these, according to the Gospel, cannot be excluded from eternal salvation. But some who die without Baptism have these good things within them. Therefore, etc.

units.la: 2. Deus etiàm est Deus feminis nostri: Gen. 17, 7. ad liberos quoque pertinet ista promissio: Act. 2, 39. Confer 1 Cor. 7, 14. Matth. 19, 14. Ergò gratia salutaris confertur etiàm citra Baptismum.
units.tr: Second, God is also the God of our offspring: Gen. 17:7. This promise pertains also to children: Acts 2:39. Compare 1 Cor. 7:14, Matt. 19:14. Therefore saving grace is conferred even without Baptism.

units.la: 3. Mares ante octavum diem, & sic citra Circumcisionem, morientes sub V. T. aliique in quibus gravi de causâ aliquandiu omissum fuit istud Sacramentum; Joseph. 5, 5. atque item feminæ; non tamen idcirco excludebantur à salute æternâ. Ac porrò latro pœnitens sine Baptismo salvatus est. Alii contrà nonnulli, quamvis baptizati, gratiæ tamen salutaris fuerunt expertes. Ergò, &c.
units.tr: Third, males who died before the eighth day, and so without circumcision, and others in whom this sacrament was for some time omitted for a grave reason under the Old Testament, Josh. 5:5, and likewise women, were not on that account excluded from eternal salvation. Moreover, the penitent thief was saved without Baptism. On the other hand, some who were baptized nevertheless lacked saving grace. Therefore, etc.

units.la: 4. Pro confirmatione Baptismi dixit Christus, Marc. 16, 16. Qui crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit, salvabitur: subjungit etiàm; Qui verò non crediderit, condemnabitur: minimè verò; Qui non fuerit baptizatus, quamvis crediderit, aut Fœdere gratiæ fuerit comprehensus, tamen condemnabitur.
units.tr: Fourth, in confirmation of Baptism Christ said, Mark 16:16: He who believes and is baptized shall be saved. He also adds: But he who does not believe shall be condemned. He did not, however, say: He who has not been baptized, though he believes, or who has been comprised in the covenant of grace, shall nevertheless be condemned.

units.la: Pontificii potissimum objiciunt locum Joh. III. 5. Amen amen dico tibi, nisi quis fuerit regenitus ex aquâ & spiritu, non poterit introire in regnum Dei. Ubi Aquam de Baptismo externo intelligunt, regenerationem per hunc produci contendunt, & sic salutem æternam ab eo suspendunt. Resp. Regeneratio per Baptismum externum non producitur; sed obsignatur. Spiritui Sancto ista efficacia competit: qui vivificat; Joh. 6, 63. 2 Cor. 3, 6. Atque idem Spiritus per Aquam etiàm recte intelligi potest. Vide Jef. 44, 3. Ezech. 36, 25, 26, 27. Joël. II, 28, 29. Joh. 4, 14. VII, 38, 39. & confer Matth. 3, 11. Verùm amplius, quemadmodùm Spiritus Sanctus & aqua exterioris Baptismi, ubi conjunguntur, non sunt tamen causæ partiales, neque ejusdem ordinis & efficaciæ; sic neque sunt ejusdem necessitatis.
units.tr: The Papists chiefly object the passage John 3:5: Truly, truly I say to you, unless anyone is born again of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. They understand the water to be external Baptism, contend that regeneration is produced through it, and so make eternal salvation depend on it. Answer. Regeneration is not produced through external Baptism but is sealed by it. This efficacy belongs to the Holy Spirit, who gives life: John 6:63; 2 Cor. 3:6. And that same Spirit can rightly be understood also through the water. See Isa. 44:3, Ezek. 36:25, 26, 27, Joel 2:28, 29, John 4:14; 7:38, 39, and compare Matt. 3:11. Moreover, just as the Holy Spirit and the water of external Baptism, where they are joined, are not partial causes of the same order and efficacy, so they are not of the same necessity.

units.la: Obj. 2. In posteris Abrahami, qui non erant circumcisi, exterminari debuerunt ex populo suo. Ergò. Resp. Istud ad contemtum proprie pertinet: ideò; nec ante octavum diem mascùli circumcidebantur, & prorsùs eximebantur feminæ: & propter morbos, aliave incommoda, differri potuit Circumcisio.
units.tr: Objection 2. Among the descendants of Abraham who were not circumcised, they had to be cut off from their people. Therefore... Answer. That applies properly to contempt. Therefore males were not circumcised before the eighth day either, and females were entirely exempt, and on account of illness or other inconveniences circumcision could be deferred.

units.la: Nunc casus occurrit, utrùm potiùs carendum sit Baptismo; an ille petendus & accipiendus à Ministro hæretico? Resp. Si accipi posset à Ministro orthodoxo, iste Baptismus procul dubio præferendus est: si verò non sit spes ejus obtinendi; & Minister præcipua essentialia fidei Christianæ, ac Baptismi, adhùc fervet integra, neque sit periculum scandali, aut necessitas participationis in illâ hæresi; accipiendus videtur.
units.tr: Now a case arises: whether one should rather go without Baptism, or whether it should be sought and received from a heretical minister. Answer. If it could be received from an orthodox minister, that Baptism is undoubtedly to be preferred. But if there is no hope of obtaining it, and the minister still keeps the chief essentials of the Christian faith and of Baptism intact, and there is no danger of scandal or necessity of participating in that heresy, it seems it should be received.

units.la: XXXIII. Locus Baptismi administrandi ordinarie debet esse, ubi pro coetù fidelium Euangelium præ- dicatur: quoniàm
units.tr: XXXIII. Baptism should ordinarily be administered where the Gospel is preached to the assembly of the faithful, for the following reasons:

units.la: 1. Sacramenta sunt Verbi prædicati sigilla.
units.tr: 1. Sacraments are seals of the preached Word.

units.la: 2. Ibi magis reverenter, & minùs perfunctorie, fiet administratio.
units.tr: 2. Administration will then be carried out more reverently and with less perfunctoriness.

units.la: 3. Sic plures erunt testes Baptismi, quibus etiàm memoria sui Baptismi refricabitur; & quorum interest; quinàm adsciscantur in eandem secùm communionem.
units.tr: 3. There will be more witnesses to the baptism, which will also refresh the memory of each person's own baptism, and it matters that others be admitted into the same communion with them.

units.la: 4. Et plurium preces pro quolibet baptizando sociabuntur. Aliter tamen fieri potest propter persecutiones, aliave incommoda.
units.tr: 4. The prayers of many will be joined for each person baptized. It may nevertheless be done otherwise because of persecutions or other hardships.

units.la: Quod ad tempus attinet; tùm adulti, tùm etiàm infantes fœderati, baptizandi sunt quam primùm id fieri commodè poterit; Act. II, 41, VIII, 38. XVI, 14, 15; 33, XXII, 16. Certum tempus, quod necessariò expectandum esset, non determinavit Deus, aut Christus.
units.tr: As to time, both adults and covenanted infants are to be baptized as soon as this can conveniently be done (Acts 2:41, 8:38, 16:14, 15, 33, 22:16). God and Christ have not fixed a certain time that would have to be awaited.

units.la: XXXIV. Ad temporis considerationem referri etiam potest quæstio, quoties aliquis fit baptizandus?
units.tr: XXXIV. Under the consideration of time falls also the question of how often a person is to be baptized.

units.la: Nos, unumquemque fœderatum semel baptizandum, afferimus; non verò iterandum esse Baptismum, contra Anabaptistas; qui indè nomen acceperunt. Sic enim 1. Apostolus diserte, Eph.4,4,5,6. Unum est corpus, & unus Spiritus: sicut & vocati estis in unam spem vocationis vestræ: unus Dominus, una fides, unum baptisma, unus Deus & Pater omnium, qui est super omnes, & in omnibus vobis. Unicum est corpus Ecclesiæ Catholicæ, unicus Dominus & Salvator Christus, unicus Deus & Pater omnium fidelium, unica in singulis fides salvifica, unica spes salutis; ac similiter unicus Baptismus singulorum. Aliter de Cœnâ Dominicâ: licet enim unus Panis appelletur, 1 Cor. 10, 17. minimè tamen unica cujusque fidelis communicatio indicatur: sed clarissimè, 1 Cor. XI, 25, 26. Hoc facite, quotiescunque biberitis, ad mei commemorationem. Quotiescunque enim ederitis panem hunc, &c.
units.tr: We affirm that each covenanted person is to be baptized once only, and that baptism is not to be repeated, against the Anabaptists, from whom they took their name. For, first, the Apostle says plainly (Eph. 4:4-6): There is one body and one Spirit, as you were called in one hope of your calling; one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, who is above all and through all and in you all. There is one body of the Catholic Church, one Lord and Saviour Christ, one God and Father of all believers, one saving faith in each, one hope of salvation; and likewise one baptism for each. It is otherwise with the Lord's Supper. Although one bread is called one (1 Cor. 10:17), the repeated communion of each believer is not thereby excluded; rather, it is shown most clearly in 1 Cor. 11:25, 26: Do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me. For as often as you eat this bread, etc.

units.la: 2. Unica est principalis res significata, nostri regeneratio, insitio in Christum atque Ecclesiam mysticam, justificatio: beneficia illa semel accepta, eadem perpetuò durant. 1 Joh. 3,19. Quisquis natus est ex Deo, peccato non dat operam; quoniam semen ipsius in eo manet. Adde II, 19. 1 Petr. I, 3, 4, 5. Rom. 8, 1, 33, 34. Aliter iterum res habet in Cœnâ Dominicâ: successivè enim, & sæpius iteratis vicibus, peragitur nutritio & corroboratio spiritualis; cujus ista est Sacramentum.
units.tr: 2. The principal thing signified is single: our regeneration, engrafting into Christ and the mystical Church, justification. Those benefits, once received, continue for ever (1 John 3:9): Whoever is born of God does not commit sin, for his seed remains in him. Add 2:19; 1 Pet. 1:3, 4, 5; Rom. 8:1, 33, 34. Again it is otherwise with the Lord's Supper, in which spiritual nourishment and strengthening are carried on successively and by repeated occasions; of this the Supper is the sacrament.

units.la: 3. Baptismus nobis dicta beneficia non solùm obsignat pro præsenti & præterito tempore, sed etiàm pro futuro: unde idem Baptismus quidem sæpius in memoriam revocandus est; non verò iterandus: Act. 2, 38, 39. Resipiscite, & baptizetur unusquisque vestrûm in nomine Jesu Christi, in remissionem peccatorum: & accipietis donum Spiritus Sancti. Vobis enim facta facta est promissio, & liberis vestris, Ad remissionem peccatorum in universum, & expectationem donorum Sp. Sancti, pertinuit unicus Baptismus. Gal. III, 27. Nam quicunque in Christum baptizati fuistis, Christo fuistis induti. Ad unicum praeteritum Baptismum provocat Apostolus, ejusque memoriam illis renovat ad vitam deinceps recte instituendam. Similiter Rom. 6, 3, 4, 10, 11. Confer Joh. 13, 10.
units.tr: 3. Baptism seals to us the said benefits not only for the present and the past, but also for the future. Hence the same baptism is indeed to be recalled to memory often, but not repeated: Acts 2:38, 39: Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is to you and to your children. A single baptism pertains to the forgiveness of sins in general and to the expectation of the gifts of the Holy Spirit. Gal. 3:27: For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ. The Apostle appeals to the single past baptism and renews its memory among them, so that they may afterwards live rightly. Similarly Rom. 6:3, 4, 10, 11. Compare John 13:10.

units.la: 4. Circumcisio cuique sub V. T. non nisi semel administrabatur, & sic participatio Foederis obsignabatur; Gen. 17, 7, 10, 11. In eundem usum pro N.T. successit Baptismus; Col. II, 11, 12. Ac proinde nec iste iterari debet.
units.tr: 4. Under the Old Testament circumcision was administered to each person only once, and thus participation in the covenant was sealed (Gen. 17:7, 10, 11). Baptism succeeded to the same use under the New Testament (Col. 2:11, 12). Accordingly, neither is it to be repeated.

units.la: XXXV. Pontificii commentiscuntur Characterem indelebilem; signum quoddam spirituale perpetuum, imprimi animae per Baptismum; itemque per Confirmationem, & per Ordinem; cujus ergo ista iterari non debeant. Sed talem Characterem S. Scriptura nescit.
units.tr: XXXV. The Papists invent an indelible character, a certain perpetual spiritual mark imprinted on the soul through baptism, likewise through confirmation and through ordination; for which reason these are not to be repeated. But Holy Scripture knows no such character.

units.la: Neque etiam solide probatur superior assertio ex Hebr. 6, 4. quasi Illuminatio istic esset Baptismus.
units.tr: Nor is the above assertion soundly proved from Heb. 6:4, as if "enlightenment" there meant baptism.

units.la: Obj. 1. Evidens Anabaptismi exemplum occurrit, Act. 19, 1. &c. Ergo. Resp. Istic verf. 1, 2, 3. agitur de duodecim Discipulis Ephesiis, qui se Johannis Baptismo baptizatos esse confitebantur; sed Spiritum Sanctum non accepisse, nec de Spiritu Sancto quicquam audivisse. Sequitur de illis, verf. 4,
units.tr: Obj. 1. A clear example of Anabaptism occurs in Acts 19:1 etc. Therefore (the argument is that baptism must be repeated). Resp. There, in verses 1-3, the subject is the twelve Ephesian disciples, who confessed that they had been baptized with John's baptism, but had not received the Holy Spirit, nor had they heard anything about the Holy Spirit. It follows about them, in verse 4:

units.la: 5. Dixit autem Paulus; Johannes quidem baptizavit Baptismo respipiscentiae, dicens populo, ut in eum qui venturus erat post ipsum crederent, hoc est, in Christum Jesum. Quivero illum, nempe Johannem, audiverunt; baptizati sunt in nomen Domini Jesu. Negamus Anabaptismum ex illo loco recte colligi: ista enim verba, Qui vero illum audiverunt, &c. sunt Pauli verba de Johanne: non vero Lucae historiographi de Paulo. Postea Lucas distincte; Et cum imposuisset eis manus Paulus, venit Spiritus Sanctus in eos: & loquebantur linguis, & prophetabant.
units.tr: 5. But Paul said: John indeed baptized with the baptism of repentance, telling the people that they should believe in him who was to come after him, that is, in Christ Jesus. When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. We deny that Anabaptism is rightly inferred from this passage. For these words, When they heard, etc., are Paul's words about John, not the words of the historian Luke about Paul. Afterwards Luke states distinctly: And when Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke with tongues and prophesied.

units.la: Obj. 2. Fieri potest, ut baptizati prolabantur in hæresies, aut alia peccata gravissima; & postea denuò convertantur: illi igitur rebaptizandi sunt. Resp. Serió quidem monendi, reprehendendi, & ad renovatam praxin resipiscentiæ excitandi; non tamen iterùm baptizandi: sicut hominem gravissimo morbo correptum, non opus est denuò nasci; sed curari per medicamenta idonea, ut sanitati, restituatur.
units.tr: Obj. 2. It may happen that baptized persons fall into heresies or other most grave sins and afterwards are converted again; therefore they are to be rebaptized. Resp. They are indeed to be admonished earnestly, rebuked, and roused to a renewed practice of repentance; but they are not to be baptized again. Just as a man seized by a most grave disease does not need to be born again, but is to be cured by suitable remedies so that he is restored to health.

units.la: XXXVI. Alterum Novi Testamenti Sacramentum est Cœna Dominica: 1 Cor. xi, 20, 23,-26. Ea discribitur: Sacramentum spiritualis nutritionis & corroborationis, à Christo institutum; fidelibus adultis usu Panis & Poculi identidem significans & obsignans communionem Corporis & Sanguinis Christi, tanquàm cibi & potûs pro interiori homine, ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: XXXVI. The other sacrament of the New Testament is the Lord's Supper (1 Cor. 11:20, 23-26). It is described as a sacrament of spiritual nourishment and strengthening, instituted by Christ, which from time to time signifies and seals, to adult believers, by the use of bread and cup, the communion of the body and blood of Christ, as food and drink for the inner man, unto eternal life.

units.la: Institutio extat Matth. xxvi, 26, -29. Marc. 14, 22,-25. Luc. 22, 19, 20. unde ea repetitur, 1 Cor. xi, 23,-26. Ego enim accepi à Domino, quod & tradidi vobis, &c.
units.tr: The institution is found in Matt. 26:26-29; Mark 14:22-25; Luke 22:19, 20, whence it is repeated in 1 Cor. 11:23-26: For I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you, etc.

units.la: Causa igitur efficiens primaria istius Sacramenti est Christus Θεάνθρωπος, Novi Fœderis Mediator, Dominus ac Salvator noster. Hinc Cœna Dominica nuncupatur, 1 Cor. 10, 21 cum 16, 17. xi, 20, 23.
units.tr: The primary efficient cause of this sacrament is Christ, the God-man [Θεάνθρωπος], Mediator of the New Covenant, our Lord and Saviour. Hence it is called the Lord's Supper (1 Cor. 10:21 with 16:17; 11:20, 23).

units.la: Secundaria, sive ministra, est Minister Euangelii, Ecclesiæ Antecessor; cui ista administratio pro conditione Sacramentorum, & ordine Ecclesiastico N. T., Divinitùs mandata est: 1 Cor. 4, 1.
units.tr: The secondary, or ministerial, cause is the minister of the Gospel, the leader of the Church, to whom this administration has been divinely committed, in keeping with the nature of the sacraments and the ecclesiastical order of the New Testament (1 Cor. 4:1).

units.la: XXXVII. Subjectam & quasi materiam consti- tuit Substantia gemina cum adjunctis Ritibus. Sub- stantia illa est tùm Panis, tùm Vinum.
units.tr: XXXVII. The subject, and as it were the matter, is constituted by a twofold substance together with the accompanying rites. That substance is both bread and wine.

units.la: Prius ergò symbolum est Panis; & quidem vulgaris cibarius; quali Christus procul dubio usus est: quique ἀναλογίαν habet cum re significatâ, corpore Christi, animæ noftræcibo ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: Therefore the first symbol is bread, and indeed common food, such as Christ without doubt used. It has an analogy with the thing signified, the body of Christ, the food of our soul unto eternal life.

units.la: Non recte igitur à Pontificiis adhibentur Minutiæ farinaceæ, quæ plurimùm differunt à Pane usuali.
units.tr: Therefore the Papists rightly do not use floury wafers, which differ greatly from ordinary bread.

units.la: Christum Pane azymo usum esse, fatemur; ob Legem cerimonialem de Pafchate; quæ abrogata est.
units.tr: We grant that Christ used unleavened bread, because of the ceremonial law concerning the Passover, which has been abrogated.

units.la: Obj. 1 Cor. 5, 7, 8. prohibetur fermentum, & præcipiuntur panes infermentati. Resp. Fermentum malitiæ & nequitiæ prohibetur; præcipiuntur autem panes infermentati sinceritatis & veritatis: ut est in textu. Sed nihil de Pane azymo in S. Cœnâ.
units.tr: Objection. 1 Cor. 5:7, 8 forbids leaven and prescribes unleavened bread. Answer. Leaven of malice and wickedness is forbidden, but unleavened bread of sincerity and truth is prescribed, as is said in the text. But nothing is said about unleavened bread at the Holy Supper.

units.la: Alterum Symbolum est Poculum vini: Christus enim diserte γέννημα τῆς ἀμπέλου appellavit, Matth. 26,29. Luc. 22,18. Neque Vinum aquâ dilui debet; quod censent Pontificii necessarium esse, saltem necessitate præcepti Ecclesiastici. Verùm non certò constat, Christum istud vinum aquâ temperasse; nedùm præceperit talem mixtionem, ut partem hujus Sacramenti, vel aliter necessariam.
units.tr: The second symbol is the cup of wine, for Christ expressly called it the fruit of the vine, Matt. 26:29; Luke 22:18 [γέννημα τῆς ἀμπέλου]. Wine ought not to be diluted with water, which the Papists think necessary, at least by necessity of ecclesiastical precept. But it is not certainly established that Christ mixed that wine with water, much less that he commanded such a mixing as a part of this sacrament, or as otherwise necessary.

units.la: XXXVIII. Usum Poculi in S. Cœnâ necessarium statuimus, tanquàm partem integralem & principalem: nam 1. quos, Christus manducare jusserat, eosdem omnes jussit bibere; dicens, Bibite ex eo omnes; Matth. 26, 27. Marc. 14, 23. De Apostolis ibi sermonem esse, fatemur: sic tamen, ut Christus Sacramentum administraverit; illi Ecclesiam communicantem repræsentaverint.
units.tr: XXXVIII. We hold that the use of the cup in the Lord's Supper is necessary, as an integral and principal part. First, those whom Christ had bidden to eat, he bade all to drink, saying, Drink ye all of it; Matt. 26:27; Mark 14:23. We grant that the discourse there is about the apostles, but in such a way that Christ administered the sacrament, and they represented the communicating Church.

units.la: 2. Paulus integram Ecclesiam Corinthiacam, cujus partem longè maximam constituebant Laïci, quos vocant, ab Idololatriâ dehortatur; ratione desumtâ ab usû istius Poculi; 1 Cor. 10. 14, 15, 16, 21. & Sacramenti istius institutionem & usum legitimum accuratè iisdem describens, Poculum non minùs commemorat, nec minùs latè extendit, quàm Panem; XI, 23, -29.
units.tr: Second, Paul dissuades the whole Corinthian church, of which by far the greater part were the so-called laity, from idolatry, on grounds drawn from the use of this cup (1 Cor. 10:14, 15, 16, 21). In describing the institution and lawful use of this sacrament accurately in the same passages (11:23-29), he mentions the cup no less, and extends it no less widely, than the bread.

units.la: 3. Accedit ratio à communione Sanctorum desumta; quæ postulat, ut omnes fideles, eorundem beneficiorum salutarium, atque adeò etiàm Sacramentorum, sint participes. De hac communione, Eph. 4, 4, 5, 6. Galat. 3, 26, 27, 28. Quin respectu Coenæ Dominicæ. 1 Cor. 10, 17. & specialiùs respectu Poculi, xii, 13. Per unum Spiritum nos omnes in unum corpus baptizati sumus: - & omnes poti sumus in unum Spiritum.
units.tr: Third, there is the argument drawn from the communion of saints, which requires that all the faithful be partakers of its saving benefits, and so of the sacraments also. On this communion see Eph. 4:4, 5, 6; Gal. 3:26, 27, 28. Indeed, with respect to the Lord's Supper, see 1 Cor. 10:17, and more specifically with respect to the cup, 12:13: By one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, and all have been made to drink into one Spirit.

units.la: 4. Accedit & hoc, quòd cùm Domino aliquram nostram spiritualem specie Convivii significare placuerit, ejus quoque plenitudinem cibo & potù distinctè exhibitis figurare visum fuerit: Pane scil. & Vino. Vide Psal. civ, 14, 15.
units.tr: Fourth, the Lord was pleased to signify our spiritual life under the image of a banquet, and so it has seemed fitting to portray its fullness distinctly by the food and drink set before us, namely bread and wine. See Ps. 104:14, 15.

units.la: Atque istam plenitudinem agnovit & observavit dudùm ipsa etiàm Ecclesia Romana. P. Gelasius apud Gratianum de Consecrat. Dist. 2. „Comperimus, „quòd quidam, sumta tantummodò corporis sacri por„tione, à calice sacrati cruoris abstineant: quod pro„cul dubio, quoniàm nescio quâ superstitione docen„tur adstringi, aut integra Sacramenta percipiant, „aut ab integris arceantur. Quia divisio unius ejuf„demque mysterii sine grandi sacrilegio non potest provenì„re. Tandem verò A. D. cıɔ cccc xv. in Concilio Constantiensi Sess. 13. contrarium audacissimâ temeritate decretum est.
units.tr: This fullness was acknowledged and observed long ago by the Roman Church itself. Pope Gelasius, in Gratian's Decretum, De Consecratione, dist. 2: "We have learned that certain persons, when they have taken only a portion of the sacred body, abstain from the chalice of the consecrated blood; which without doubt, since they are taught to be bound by some superstition I know not what, either receive the sacraments entire or are kept away from the entire ones. For the division of one and the same mystery cannot take place without great sacrilege." Finally, in the year 1415, in the Council of Constance, session 13, the contrary was decreed with most audacious rashness.

units.la: Obj. 1. Aliquoties Panis, ejusque fractio, solùm commemoratur; ut Luc. 24, 30. & alibi. Ergò. Resp. Ubi hoc Sacramentum locutione illà intelligi debet, synecdochicè Poculum comprehenditur, secundùm ejus institutionem, & praxin Apostolorum ac primitivæ Ecclesiæ, alibi satis clarè ac plenè expressam. Alias, ut potissimùm Luc. 24, 30. convivium humanæ familiaritatis intelligendum est. Interim confer Genef. 43, 16, 25, 31, 32, 34.
units.tr: Objection 1. Sometimes bread and its breaking alone are mentioned, as in Luke 24:30 and elsewhere. Therefore... Answer. Where this sacrament must be understood by that expression, the cup is included synecdochically, according to its institution and the practice of the apostles and the primitive Church, which is expressed quite clearly and fully elsewhere. Otherwise, as especially in Luke 24:30, a meal of human familiarity is to be understood. Meanwhile compare Gen. 43:16, 25, 31, 32, 34.

units.la: Obj. 2. Accedunt varia incommoda: periculum enim est, ne calix sanguinis Dominici interim effundatur, &c. nonnulli sunt abstemii, &c. Resp. Præter-quàm quàm quòd prius illud falsâ transsubstantiationis hypothesi nitatur; non solùm perperàm vetus Ecclesia, quæ hoc Sacramentum sub utráque specie dispensavit, imprudentiæ accusatur; sed etiàm ipsi Christo, qui itâ instituit, ignorantia objicitur, perblasphemiam. Et facilè aliter istis difficultatibus obviàm iri potest.
units.tr: Objection 2. Various inconveniences attend it: there is a danger that the cup of the Lord's blood may meanwhile be spilled, etc.; some are abstainers, etc. Answer. Apart from the fact that the former rests on the false hypothesis of transubstantiation, not only is the ancient Church, which dispensed this sacrament under both kinds, wrongly accused of imprudence, but Christ himself, who so instituted it, is charged with ignorance, which is a great blasphemy. These difficulties can easily be met in another way.

units.la: Obj. 3. Nihil opus est usû Calicis: unâ enim cum Corpore Christi accipitur ipsius Sanguis, per concomitantiam. Resp. 1. Sic falsò supponitur μετάβασις, 2. Christus Calicem distinctè instituit, 3. Eoque Sanguinem suum, non ut in vasis conclusum, sed ut effusum pro nobis, significavit. 4. Idem urgeri posset de Sacerdotibus conficientibus, ut vocant.
units.tr: Objection 3. There is no need of the use of the cup, for his blood is received together with the body of Christ, by concomitance. Answer. First, a transition [μετάβασις] is thus falsely presupposed. Second, Christ instituted the cup distinctly. Third, by it he signified his blood, not as enclosed in vessels but as poured out for us. Fourth, the same could be urged about the priests who consecrate, as they are called.

units.la: Distinctè verò in hoc Sacramento adhibendum est Poculum, ut & Panis. Itâ requirit institutio, & exemplum Christi; doctrina, & praxis Apostolorum; atque usus Ecclesiæ primitivæ. Idem suadet analogia alituræ naturalis, quæ cibo & potû distinctis peragitur. Non rectè igitur darentur buccæ intinctæ, aut panis vino intritus.
units.tr: But in this sacrament the cup, as well as the bread, must be used distinctly. So the institution and example of Christ require; so the teaching and practice of the apostles, and the usage of the primitive Church, demand. The analogy of natural nourishment, which is carried on by distinct food and drink, suggests the same. Therefore morsels dipped or bread steeped in wine would not rightly be given.

units.la: XXXIX. Inter Ritus adjunctos Pani & Poculo, communis est eorum acceptorum Sanctificatio; quæ εὐλογία, benedictio, appellatur, Matth. 26, 26. Marc. 14, 22. 1 Cor. 10, 16. & εὐχαριστία, gratiarum actio, Luc. 22, 19. 1 Cor. xi, 24. Sicut in aliis alimentis etiàm commemoratur εὐλογία; Matth. 14, 19. & εὐχαριστία; 1 Tim. 4, 3, 4. Hoc autem loco specialis Sanctificatio intelligenda est, ad usum Sacramentalem.
units.tr: XXXIX. Among the rites accompanying the bread and the cup, the sanctification of what is received is common to both. It is called blessing [εὐλογία], Matt. 26:26; Mark 14:22; 1 Cor. 10:16, and thanksgiving [εὐχαριστία], Luke 22:19; 1 Cor. 11:24. As in other foods too blessing is mentioned, Matt. 14:19, and thanksgiving, 1 Tim. 4:3, 4. In this place, however, a special sanctification is to be understood, namely for sacramental use.

units.la: Pontificii Consecrationem appellare solent: intelliguntque arcanorum verborum super Pane & Vino recitationem, à Sacerdote faciendam, quâ natura eorum realiter & substantialiter transmutetur in verum ac proprie dictum Corpus & Sanguinem Christi.
units.tr: The Papists are wont to call this consecration, and they understand by it the recitation of secret words over the bread and wine, to be made by the priest, by which their nature is really and substantially changed into the true and properly so-called body and blood of Christ.

units.la: Sed 1. male Confecrationem illam peragi exiftimant, non aliis quàm iftis verbis, Hoc eft Corpus meum; & Hic eft Sanguis meus: cum potius antecedentem Dei invocationem, ipfamque Chrifti inftitutionem, quam repetunt & fequuntur fideles ipfius Miniftri, ifta Sanctificatio fiat. Sic Matth. 26, 26, 27, 28. praeceffit ἀλογία & ἀχαρίστια, pro quâ illi Confecrationem appellare geftiunt: poftea dixit Chriftus; Hoc eft Corpus meum, & Hic eft Sanguis meus, &c.
units.tr: But first, they wrongly think that this consecration is performed by no other words than these: This is my body, and This is my blood. Rather, this sanctification takes place by the preceding invocation of God and by Christ's own institution, which the faithful ministers themselves repeat and follow. Thus in Matt. 26:26-28 the blessing [εὐλογία] and thanksgiving [εὐχαριστία] came first, for which they are eager to call it consecration; afterwards Christ said, This is my body, and This is my blood, etc.

units.la: 2. Male confequenter ifta verba admurmurant Panni & Vino: cùm Chriftus palàm Difcipulos compellaverit; iifque explicuerit, quid daret, & quo fine.
units.tr: Second, they wrongly mutter these words over the bread and wine, since Christ openly addressed the disciples and explained to them what he was giving and for what purpose.

units.la: 3. Gravifsimo item errore fic ftatuunt fieri veram tranfubftantiationem: quae poft quaedam ex profeffo refutabitur.
units.tr: Third, they also hold, with the gravest error, that true transubstantiation takes place in this way. This will be refuted expressly after some matters.

units.la: Communis etiam eft altera fubsequens Benedictio; Hymnus fc. quo celebratur Dei benignitas, & gratiae pro tali illâ communione aguntur: Matth. 26, 30. Marc. 16, 26.
units.tr: Also common is the other, subsequent blessing: a hymn by which the goodness of God is celebrated and thanks are rendered for such communion. Matt. 26:30; Mark 16:26.

units.la: XL. Ad Panem fpeciatim pertinent duae Administrantis actiones; Fractio, & Diftributio ad manducandum. Sic enim praeivit Chriftus Convivator, & primus S. Coenae Minifter; Matth. xxvi, 26. Marc. xiv, 22. Luc. xxii, 19. 1 Cor. xi, 24. Hinc à priori, Coena fynecdochicè Fractio panis appellatur, Actor. 2, 42. Sic autem figuratur laceratio corporis Chrifti, ac dolores paffionis ipfius, ipfaque adeò feparatio animae à corpore; & mutua fidelium in Chrifto communio: 1 Cor. x, 16. Interim ifte ritus non eft cenfendus primarius aut effentiae Sacramenti conftitutivus: fed fecundarius, ad modum adminiftrationis, juftamque ejus integritatem, pertinens.
units.tr: XL. Two actions of the administrant belong specifically to the bread: the breaking and the distribution for eating. For so Christ, the host and first minister of the Lord's Supper, went before: Matt. 26:26; Mark 14:22; Luke 22:19; 1 Cor. 11:24. Hence, from the prior, the Supper is synecdochically called the breaking of bread, Acts 2:42. In this way is figured the laceration of Christ's body, the pains of his passion, and even the separation of the soul from the body, and the mutual communion of the faithful in Christ: 1 Cor. 10:16. Meanwhile this rite is not to be judged primary or constitutive of the essence of the sacrament, but secondary, pertaining to the mode of administration and to its due integrity.

units.la: XLI. Quod ad Diftributionem: Euangeliftae, & Paulus, fatis diferte commemorant, Chriftum Difcipulis fuis dediffe fractum panem, iifque dixiffe: Accipite, comedite: &c. Matth. 26, 26. Marc. 14, 22. Luc. xxii, 19. I Cor. xi, 23, 24, 26. Isti institutioni consentanea fuit praxis Ecclesiæ Apostolicæ, I Cor. 10, 17.
units.tr: XLI. As to the distribution: the evangelists and Paul mention quite plainly that Christ gave his disciples the broken bread and said to them, Take, eat, etc.; Matt. 26:26; Mark 14:22; Luke 22:19; 1 Cor. 11:23, 24, 26. The practice of the apostolic Church was consistent with this institution, 1 Cor. 10:17.

units.la: Graviter verò peccant Pontificii; qui in privatis suis Missis, ut vocant, non distribuunt Panem; sed Sacerdos eum manducat solus.
units.tr: Yet the Papists sin grievously, who in their private Masses, as they call them, do not distribute the bread, but the priest eats it alone.

units.la: Ad Modum distributionis quod attinet; in historiâ Euangelicâ, & commemoratione Paulinâ, nulla est ratio dubitandi, quin Christus Discipulis Panem in manus præbuerit, non autem ori ingesserit: nihil enim extat, unde oriri possit suspicio, Christum hîc à communi & usitatâ cibum adultis porrigendi ratione discessisse: nec aliter commode fieri potuit, per veterum discumbendi morem. Atque ita diutissime obtinuit in Ecclesiâ, ut panis manibus accipereturr. Glíscente tamen superstitione aliter factum apud Pontificios: Eucharistia enim Laïcis à Sacerdote in os ingeritur.
units.tr: As for the manner of distribution: in the Gospel history and Paul's account there is no reason to doubt that Christ offered the bread to the disciples into their hands, and did not put it into their mouths. Nothing exists from which any suspicion could arise that Christ here departed from the common and customary way of offering food to adults, nor could it conveniently have been done otherwise, given the ancient manner of reclining at table. And so for a very long time it prevailed in the Church that the bread was received in the hands. As superstition grew, however, the Papists did otherwise, for the Eucharist is placed by the priest into the mouths of the laity.

units.la: Distributioni isti ad manducandum, plane etiam adversatur honorifica bostiæ adservatio in pyxide; ut deinde circumgestetur, & ostentetur ad ἀρτολα-τρείαν.
units.tr: The honourable reservation of the host in a pyx, to be carried about and displayed for worship as bread-worship [ἀρτολατρεία], also plainly opposes this distribution for eating.

units.la: XLII. Ad Vinum pertinet ritus Administrantis, ut is ipsum Poculo infusum singulis Communicantibus bibendum præbeat. Sic enim Christus Matth. 26, 27, 28. Accepto poculo, ac gratis astis, dedit iis, dicens; Bibite ex eo omnes, &c. Atque inde hoc Sacramentum synecdochice Potatio appellatur, I Cor. 12, 13. Omnes poti sumus in unum Spiritum.
units.tr: XLII. The rite of the administrant pertains to the wine: that he offer it, poured into the cup, to each of the communicants to drink. For so Christ says (Matth. 26, 27, 28): Taking the cup and giving thanks, he gave it to them, saying: Drink of it, all of you, etc. And from this the sacrament is called, by synecdoche, a drinking (I Cor. 12, 13): We have all been made to drink into one Spirit.

units.la: Sequuntur Actiones Communicantium; ut nimirum Discipulorum exemplo, acceptum illum Panem edant, & de Poculo omnes bibant; Matth. 26, 26, -29. Marc. 14, 22, -25. I Cor. xi, 24, -26.
units.tr: There follow the actions of the communicants: namely, that, following the example of the disciples, they eat that bread received, and all drink from the cup (Matth. 26, 26-29; Marc. 14, 22-25; I Cor. xi, 24-26).

units.la: De Genuflexione, similive aliquo gestû adorantium, quo sacra symbola excipienda forent, nihil habet institutio Dominica; nec Apostolorum, aut Ecclesiæ primitivæ, praxis.
units.tr: The Lord's institution has nothing about kneeling, or any similar gesture of worshippers, with which the sacred symbols were to be received; nor does the practice of the Apostles or of the early Church.

units.la: XLIII. Res significata hujus Sacramenti, est communionis Christi, & gratiæ N. T. continuatio, atque incrementum, ad perficiendam vitam spiritualem. Panis & Vinum significant & obsignant Christi carnem ac sanguinem, verum spiritualem animarum nostrarum alimentum; cibum & potum, ad vitam æternam in nobis perficiendam. Hinc de ipso Pane, Matth. 26, 26. Hoc est corpus meum. & de Vino, verf. 28. Hoc est sanguis meus, &c. Confer de re significata, Joh. 6, 48. 55, -58.
units.tr: XLIII. The thing signified by this sacrament is the continuation and increase of communion with Christ and of the grace of the New Testament, for perfecting spiritual life. Bread and wine signify and seal the flesh and blood of Christ, the true spiritual nourishment of our souls; food and drink for bringing eternal life to perfection in us. Hence, concerning the bread itself, (Matth. 26, 26) This is my body; and concerning the wine (v. 28) This is my blood, etc. Compare, for the thing signified, Joh. 6, 48, 55-58.

units.la: Porro autem Panis accepti & sanctificati fractio significat corporis Christi pro nobis contritionem, clavis ac lancea factam: Isef. 53, 5. Joh. 19, 34. xx, 25, 27. ipsamque adeo mortem: 1 Cor. xi, 26. Ejusdem distributio designat illius communicationem necessariam ad vitam æternam, quæ per Sp. Sanctum peragitur efficaciter: Luc. xxii, 19, 1 Cor. xi, 24. cum xii, 13.
units.tr: Furthermore, the breaking of the bread taken and sanctified signifies the contrition of Christ's body for us, made by the nails and the spear (Isa. 53, 5; Joh. 19, 34; xx, 25, 27), and indeed death itself (1 Cor. xi, 26). Its distribution designates the communication of it, necessary for eternal life, which is effectively accomplished through the Holy Spirit (Luc. xxii, 19; 1 Cor. xi, 24; compare xii, 13).

units.la: In Communicantibus vero corporalis ejus panis significat eum mysticum unius ejusdemque veri corporis Christi, ad æternam vitam justitiæ ac gloriæ, atque adeo veram sanctorum cum Christo & inter se communionem: 1 Cor. x, 16, 17. Panis, quem frangimus nonne communio corporis Christi est? quoniam unus est panis, unum corpus nos illi multi sumus: nam omnes ex uno illo pane participamus. Confer de re significata, Joh. 6, 35, 47, 48.
units.tr: In the communicants, moreover, that corporeal bread signifies the mystical union with the one and the same true body of Christ, unto eternal life of righteousness and glory, and so the true communion of the saints with Christ and with one another (1 Cor. x, 16, 17): The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? Since there is one bread, we, though many, are one body, for we all partake of that one bread. Compare, for the thing signified, Joh. 6, 35, 47, 48.

units.la: Similiter Vini in Poculum effusi communicatio significat spiritualem communionem sanguinis Christi, ad remissionem peccatorum impetrandam, ac Novum Testamentum sanciendum, pro nobis effusi; Matth. xxvi, 28. Luc. xxii, 20.
units.tr: Likewise, the communion of wine poured into the cup signifies the spiritual communion of Christ's blood, to obtain the remission of sins and to ratify the New Testament, which was poured out for us (Matth. xxvi, 28; Luc. xxii, 20).

units.la: Potus vero & communio vini, ore corporis assumti, proprius denotat & obsignat internam spiritualem tualem sanguinis Christi perceptionem & communionem, quæ à Spiritû Sancto perficitur; & fide verâ, tanquàm ore animæ, accipitur: ac porrò veram & mutuam istiusmodi sanctorum communionem : 1Cor. 10, 16, XII, 13.
units.tr: But the drinking and communion of wine, received by the mouth of the body, properly denotes and seals the inner spiritual perception and communion of Christ's blood, which is brought about by the Holy Spirit; and it is received by true faith, as by the mouth of the soul; and further, the true and mutual communion of such saints (1Cor. 10, 16; XII, 13).

units.la: XLIV. Forma igitur Cœnæ Dominicæ, pro natura Sacramentorum, consistit in Divinâ, per Verbum Christi, ordinatione Panis & Vini, usûsque eorum, ad visibilem significationem & obfignationem communionis invisibilis mysticæ cum Christo, in gratiâ Fœderis Euangelici, continuandæ ac perficiendæ.
units.tr: XLIV. The form of the Lord's Supper, therefore, according to the nature of sacraments, consists in the divine ordination, through the Word of Christ, of bread and wine, and of their use, for the visible signification and sealing of the invisible mystical communion with Christ, to be continued and perfected in the grace of the Gospel covenant.

units.la: Atque inde emergunt Prædicationes Sacramentales: utpote 1. 1 Cor. XI, 24. Hoc meum est corpus, quod pro vobis frangitur. Id est, Hæc res, Panis iste acceptus, sanctificatus, & fractus, est signum ac monumentum Corporis Christi similiter frangendi; vel nunc fracti.
units.tr: From this emerge the sacramental predications, namely: (1) 1 Cor. XI, 24: This is my body, which is broken for you. That is: this thing, the bread taken, sanctified and broken, is a sign and memorial of the body of Christ similarly broken, or now broken.

units.la: 2. Ibidem verf. 25. Hoc Poculum est Novum illud pactum, per meum Sanguinem. Id est, hoc Vinum, Poculo isto contentum, est signum ac monumentum Novi Fœderis gratiæ, per Sanguinem Christi obsignati. Confer porrò verf. 25, & 26.
units.tr: (2) Ibid. v. 25: This cup is the new covenant in my blood. That is: this wine, contained in this cup, is a sign and memorial of the new covenant of grace, sealed through the blood of Christ. Compare further vv. 25 and 26.

units.la: 3. Matth. 26, 28. Hoc est Sanguis meus, Novi pacti, qui pro multis effunditur in remissionem peccatorum. Id est, Hujus Poculi contentum, fructus vitis, est signum commemorativum Sanguinis mei, quo novum illud Fœdus sancitur, &c. Confer 1 Cor. XI. 25, 26.
units.tr: (3) Matth. 26, 28: This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the remission of sins. That is: the contents of this cup, the fruit of the vine, is a commemorative sign of my blood, by which that new covenant is ratified, etc. Compare 1 Cor. XI, 25, 26.

units.la: 4. 1 Cor. 10, 16. Poculum benedictionis, cui benedicimus, nonne communio Sanguinis Christi est? &c. Hoc est, signum ac sigillum mysticæ istius communionis. Similis prædicatio est ibid. verf. 3, 4.
units.tr: (4) 1 Cor. 10, 16: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? etc. That is: a sign and seal of that mystical communion. A similar predication is at ibid. vv. 3, 4.

units.la: In istis autem prædicationibus Sacramentalibus, tropus non proprie existit in copulâ verbali est; sed potiùs in attributo: per copulam enim termini connectuntur, & temporis circumstantia simul exprimitur. tur. Verùm in attributo ipsa res significata ponitur pro signo illius rei.
units.tr: In these sacramental predications, however, the trope does not properly lie in the verbal copula is, but rather in the predicate in attributo: for the copula connects the terms, and at the same time expresses the circumstance of time. But in the predicate the thing signified itself is put for the sign of that thing.
