units.la: XLV. Finis cuius est, I. ut inter cœnandum Christi solenniter recordemur; & fides in Ipsum, pro nobis mortuum, & ad justitiam ac salutem nobis communicatum, suscitetur & confirmetur, Luc. 22, 19. 1 Cor. xi, 24, 25.
units.tr: XLV. The end for which is: first, that during the supper we solemnly remember Christ, and that faith in him, who died for us and was communicated to us for righteousness and salvation, may be stirred up and confirmed (Luc. 22, 19; 1 Cor. xi, 24, 25).

units.la: 2. Ut beneficia N. Test. continuentur, & promoveantur: talis enim promissio appósita est usui Panis; Luc. 22, 19. 1 Cor. xi, 24. x, 16. & Vini; Matth. 26, 28. 1 Cor. x, 16. xii, 13.
units.tr: Second, that the benefits of the New Testament may be continued and advanced; for such a promise is attached to the use of the bread (Luc. 22, 19; 1 Cor. xi, 24; x, 16), and of the wine (Matth. 26, 28; 1 Cor. x, 16; xii, 13).

units.la: 3. Ut excitemur ad Servatorem nostrum debitâ gratitudine colendum & celebrandum: 1 Cor. xi. 26.
units.tr: Third, that we may be stirred to honour and celebrate our Saviour with due gratitude (1 Cor. xi, 26).

units.la: 4. Ut extimulemur ad mutuæ dilectionis & communionis studium: 1 Cor. 10, 17. Serió autem fugimus dissidia, & contemtum fratrum: xi, 18, 20, 22, Finis vero cui est Cœtus baptizatorum adultorum, fidem ac resipiscentiam ore & opere profitentium.
units.tr: Fourth, that we may be spurred on to the zeal of mutual love and communion (1 Cor. 10, 17). Yet we seriously flee from dissensions and the contempt of the brethren (xi, 18, 20, 22). The end for whom is the assembly of baptized adults, professing faith and repentance by word and deed.

units.la: 1. Cœtus requiritur; exemplo primæ S. Cœnæ: 1 Cor. xi, 20. x, 16, 17.
units.tr: (1) An assembly is required, following the example of the first Holy Supper (1 Cor. xi, 20; x, 16, 17).

units.la: 2. Et quidem baptizatorum; prius enim est nasci, quàm pasci; adeòque & Sacramentum regenerationis, quàm spiritualis nutritionis: Matth. 28, 19. Tit. 3, 5. Hebr. 6, 2, cum Exod. 12, 48.
units.tr: (2) And indeed of the baptized; for it is first to be born, before being fed, and so the sacrament of regeneration precedes that of spiritual nourishment (Matth. 28, 19; Tit. 3, 5; Hebr. 6, 2, with Exod. 12, 48).

units.la: 3. Eorumque adultorum: isti enim soli sunt habiles ad officia in hoc Sacramento necessaria: 1 Cor. xi, 24-29.
units.tr: (3) And of adults; for only they are fit for the duties required in this sacrament (1 Cor. xi, 24-29).

units.la: 4. Denique talium, qui fidem ac resipiscentiam ore & opere profiteantur. Hoc Pastores videre debent sedulò: 1 Cor. 10, 21, xi, 20, 27, 28. Sed & sincera debet esse illa professio: Joh. 6, 27, 29. Rom. 10, 10, Gal. 5, 6. Alias incurritur crimen Corporis ac Sanguinis Christi violati: 1 Cor. xi, 29. Fideles castigationibus fiunt obnoxii; 30, 31, 32. Hypocritæ autem æternæ damnationi; Matth. 24, 51. Marc. 16, 16. Rom. 8, 13.
units.tr: (4) Finally, of such as profess faith and repentance by word and deed. Pastors must watch over this carefully (1 Cor. 10, 21; xi, 20, 27, 28). But that profession must also be sincere (Joh. 6, 27, 29; Rom. 10, 10; Gal. 5, 6). Otherwise one incurs the guilt of violating the body and blood of Christ (1 Cor. xi, 29). The faithful become liable to chastisement (30, 31, 32); hypocrites, however, to eternal damnation (Matth. 24, 51; Marc. 16, 16; Rom. 8, 13).

units.la: XLVI. Coenæ Dominicæ omninò adversatur Missa Papistica. Illius appellatio & significatio sacra est. Vide sup. th. 36. Hanc Bellarminus, à Missione, seu Dimissione populi, dictam existimat. Alii originem Hebraicam quaerunt in voce ᵺᵺᵺ, quos ipse Bellarminus rationibus non contemnendis refutat.
units.tr: XLVI. The Papistical Mass is wholly opposed to the Lord's Supper. Its name and meaning are sacred; see above, th. 36. Bellarmine thinks that it was named from Missione, that is, the dismissal of the people. Others seek a Hebrew origin in the word (Hebrew), which Bellarmine himself refutes with not contemptible arguments.

units.la: Ad rem ipsam quod; Auctor Coenæ Dominicæ est Dominus Christus. Missæ vero Pontificiæ non est unus auctor; sed plurimi, ac diversorum temporum, servi infidi, collatis superstitionum symbolis, centonem illum tandem confecerunt. Dudum enim agitatum fuit mysterium iniquitatis.
units.tr: As to the thing itself: the author of the Lord's Supper is the Lord Christ. The Papistical Mass has no single author, but many faithless servants of different times, bringing together the symbols of superstition, at last put together that patchwork. For the mystery of iniquity had long been at work.

units.la: Administri autem Coenæ Dominicæ, sunt Ministri Euangelii. Sed Missæ Mysteq jactantur Sacerdotes proprie ad sacrificandum oleo specialiter consecrato inuncti. At nemo sibi ipsi sumit honorem Sacerdotii: sed qui vocatur à Deo, sicut & Aharon. Ubi verò agitur de Sacerdotio N. T. diserte docetur, abrogatum esse Sacerdotium Aharonicum, tanquam imperfectum, umbraticum, typicum; cùm Christus sit Sacerdos secundum ordinem Melchizedeki: ac proindè, 1. sine Patre, sine Matre, sine genere, nec initium dierum habens, nec vitæ finem; atque in æternum manens, ex vi indissolubilis vitæ, ut Sacerdotium ipsius ad alios non transeat; Hebr. 7, 3, 15, 16, 24.
units.tr: The ministers of the Lord's Supper are the ministers of the Gospel. But in the Mass priests, anointed with specially consecrated oil in order to offer sacrifice, are properly boasted of. Yet no one takes the honour of the priesthood to himself, but he who is called by God, as Aaron was. Where the New Testament speaks of the priesthood, it plainly teaches that the Aaronic priesthood has been abrogated as imperfect, shadowy and typical, since Christ is a priest after the order of Melchizedek: and therefore (1) without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but abiding for ever by the power of an indissoluble life, so that his priesthood does not pass to others; Heb. 7.3, 15, 16, 24.

units.la: 2. Sanctus, innocens, impollutus, segregatus à peccatoribus: verf. 26.
units.tr: 2. Holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners: v. 26.

units.la: 3. Sponsor melioris Fœderis: verf. 22. sive Mediator N. T. cujus mors intercederet ad redemtionem transgressionum: ix, 15. Et Testator suâ morte ratum faciens istud Testamentum: 16, 17.
units.tr: 3. Surety of a better covenant: v. 22; or Mediator of the New Testament, whose death came between for the redemption of transgressions: ix. 15. And Testator, ratifying that testament by his death: vv. 16, 17.

units.la: 4. Major iis, quibus Ipse benedicit; & quos, vel quæ, sanctificat; atque adeò victima humanitatis suæ: vii, 7. ii, 11. x, 10. Job. 17, 19
units.tr: 4. Greater than those whom he blesses, and whom or which he sanctifies; and so the victim of his own humanity: vii. 7; ii. 11; x. 10; Job. 17, 19.

units.la: 5. Ipse Sacerdos & Sacrificium: qui seipsum obtulit per Spiritum S. semel sufficientissimè : Hebr. 7, 27, 28. IX, 14. X, 10, 12, 14. Quæ omnia soli Christo omnino propria sunt. Alios Sacerdotes N. T. prorsus ignorat S. Scriptura. Cùm enim quilibet fideles dicuntur Sacerdotes; ut 1 Petr. II, 9. Apoc. I, 6. V, 10. id metaphoricè accipiendum; & quidem sic, respectu Sacrificiorum eucharisticorum; Rom. 12, 1. Hebr. 13, 16.
units.tr: 5. He is himself both Priest and Sacrifice, who offered himself through the Holy Spirit once, most sufficiently: Heb. 7.27, 28; ix. 14; x. 10, 12, 14. All these things belong wholly and solely to Christ. Holy Scripture entirely knows no other priests of the New Testament. For although all the faithful are called priests, as in 1 Pet. ii. 9; Rev. i. 6; v. 10, this must be understood metaphorically, and indeed in that way with respect to the eucharistic sacrifices: Rom. 12.1; Heb. 13.16.

units.la: XLVII. Materiam S. Cœnæ constituunt verus Pa- nis & Vinum, cum Ritibus à Domino institutis.
units.tr: XLVII. The matter of the Lord's Supper consists of true bread and wine, with the rites instituted by the Lord.

units.la: In Missa verò sunt Nebulæ nummulariæ, mera veri & ordinarii Panis simulachra; & Vinum aquâ superstitiosè dilutum. Sed hoc nequidem in Missa publica distribuitur Communicantibus: in privata nulla prorsus Communicantibus fit distributio: in sicca ipse etiam Sacerdos siccus est. Sic manifestum infert sacrilegium. In vestibus porrò, gestibus, actionibus aliis, multiplex relucet superstitio: Matth. 15, 9, 13.
units.tr: In the Mass, however, there are coin-like wafers, mere likenesses of true and ordinary bread, and wine diluted superstitiously with water. But this is not even distributed to the communicants in the public Mass; in the private Mass there is no distribution to the communicants at all; in the dry Mass the priest himself is dry. Thus it plainly brings in sacrilege. Moreover, in vestments, gestures and other actions, manifold superstition shines forth: Matt. 15.9, 13.

units.la: Forma S. Cœnæ consistit in communionis sacrificii corporis & sanguinis Christi Divinâ significatione & obsignatione; per Panem sanctificatum, fractum, distributum, & à Communicantibus comesum; Vinumque effusum, sanctificatum, distributum, & à Communicantibus bibitum. Sic Panis & Vini vera substantia conservatur; sed in spiritualem usum convertitur: verum ac proprie dictum corpus & sanguis Christi ex illis non conficitur; sed pro communi Sacramentorum naturâ & conditione significatur atque obsignatur. In Missa verò statuitur primò transubstantiatio Panis ac Vini in verum ac proprie dictum corpus ac sanguinem Christi; ita ut substantia Panis ac vini omnino intereat, & accidentia eorum sola sine ullo subjecto supersint: Christi autem verum & proprie dictum corpus ac sanguis ex Pane & Vino fiant; ex Pane sc. corpus, & sanguis per concomitantiam, &c.; at-
units.tr: The form of the Lord's Supper consists in the Divine signification and sealing of the communion of the sacrifice of the body and blood of Christ, through bread that is consecrated, broken and distributed, and eaten by the communicants; and wine that is poured out, consecrated, distributed and drunk by the communicants. Thus the true substance of bread and wine is preserved, but is turned to a spiritual use: the true and properly so-called body and blood of Christ are not made from them, but are signified and sealed according to the common nature and condition of the sacraments. In the Mass, however, it is laid down first that the bread and wine are transubstantiated into the true and properly so-called body and blood of Christ, so that the substance of bread and wine wholly perishes, and only their accidents remain without any subject; while the true and properly so-called body and blood of Christ are made from the bread and wine: from the bread, namely the body, and the blood by concomitance, etc.; but

units.la: Cap. XVIII. De Obsignatione.
units.tr: Cap. XVIII. On Sealing.

units.la: &c. atque ista corporis & sanguinis Christi substantia istic sola extet, sine suis accidentibus & proprietatibus; quamvis eas nihilominus retineat. Deinde etiam statuitur vera Corporis Christi oblatio per Sacerdotem Missificum, super altari, ad impetrandam remissionem peccatorum pro vivis & pro mortuis; sive verum ac proprie dictum Sacrificium expiatorium.
units.tr: etc. And this substance of the body and blood of Christ remains there alone, without its accidents and properties, though it nevertheless retains them. Next, it is also asserted that there is a true offering of the body of Christ by the Missa-sacrificing priest upon the altar, to obtain the remission of sins for the living and the dead; that is, a true and properly so-called expiatory sacrifice.

units.la: XLVIII. Transsubstantiatio ista refutatur primo, ex institutione Coenae Dominicae:
units.tr: XLVIII. This transubstantiation is refuted first, from the institution of the Lord's Supper:

units.la: nam 1. Christus istic verum Panem accepit, sanctificavit, fregit, distribuit, & edi jussit; Vinum similiter fusum sanctificavit, distribuit, & bibi jussit. Verum Panem ac Vinum non solum in initio, sed etiam in progressu & in consummatione istius administrationis, appellat S. Textus: & diserte Fructum vitis dixit Christus, cum biberetur; & Paulus, Panem & Vinum, etiam cum a Communicantibus ille editur, hoc bibitur; Matth. 26, 26, 27, 29. Marc. 14, 22, 23, 25. 1 Cor. xi, 23,-28. Talis ergo substantia Panis ac Vini debet agnosci; non prorsus alia sub iis accidentibus
units.tr: For (1) Christ took true bread, blessed it, broke it, distributed it, and bade it be eaten; likewise he blessed the poured-out wine, distributed it, and bade it be drunk. Holy Scripture calls the bread and wine by these names not only at the beginning but also in the course and at the close of this administration. Christ expressly called it the fruit of the vine when it was drunk, and Paul calls it the bread and the wine even when it is eaten by the communicants and drunk by them. Matt. 26:26, 27, 29; Mark 14:22, 23, 25; 1 Cor. 11:23-28. Therefore the substance of bread and wine must be recognised as such, not some altogether different substance under those accidents.

units.la: 2. Christus integer, corpore hactenus illaeso, sanguine suis vasis contento, una cum Discipulis suis accubuit, Sacramentum hoc instituit, atque ipse administravit. Substantia igitur Corporis & Sanguinis Christi vera ac proprie dicta, realiter distingui debet ab externis visibilibus symbolis, quae ipse Discipulis suis administravit.
units.tr: (2) Christ, whole and with his body as yet unhurt and his blood contained in its vessels, reclined together with his disciples, instituted this sacrament, and administered it himself. Therefore the substance of the body and blood of Christ, true and properly so called, must be really distinguished from the outward visible signs that he himself administered to his disciples.

units.la: 3. Sic Panem sanctificatum & fractum praebens, dixit; Hoc Meum est Corpus, quod pro vobis frangitur:
units.tr: (3) Offering the bread sanctified and broken, he said: This is my body, which is broken for you:

units.la: 1 Cor. xi. 24. Metonymice. Illaesus enim accumbebat. Neque nunc Corpus gloriosum vere frangitur. Similiter de Poculo: Hoc est Sanguis meus Novi Testamenti, qui pro multis effunditur in remissionem peccatorum; Matth. 26, 28. Sed Paulus hoc modo refert, 1 Cor. xi, 25. Hoc Poculum est Novum illud pactum per Meum Sanguinem. nem. & 1Cor. 10,16. Poculum benedictionis, cui benedicimus, nonne communio Sanguinis Christi est? Panis, quem frangimus, nonne communio Corporis Christi est? Neque Christus istis verbis indicavit, quid per ea fieret de Pane & Poculo; sed quid jam tum effet: cum veritas rei prior sit veritate enunciationis.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 11:24. Metonymically; for he was reclining unhurt. Nor is the glorified body truly broken now. Similarly of the cup: This is my blood of the New Testament, which is poured out for many for the remission of sins; Matt. 26:28. But Paul reports it thus, 1 Cor. 11:25: This cup is the New Covenant in my blood. Also 1 Cor. 10:16: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? Nor did Christ indicate by these words what would happen to the bread and cup, but what they already were; for the truth of the thing comes before the truth of the statement.

units.la: 4. Paulus de usu Panis; Hoc facite ad Mei commemorationem. Atque iterum de Poculo; Hoc facite, quotiescunque biberitis, ad Mei commemorationem. Quotiescunque enim ederitis Panem hunc, & Poculum hoc biberitis, mortem Domini annunciate, usque quo venerit: 1Cor. xi, 24, 25, 26. Quibus verbis aperte indicatur, in hoc Sacramento esse commemorationem Christi, & annunciationem mortis ipsius, usquedum ipse veniat ad extremum & universale judicium; sed Christum istic non adesse praesentem corporaliter.
units.tr: (4) Paul speaks of the use of the bread: Do this in remembrance of me. And again of the cup: Do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me. For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes: 1 Cor. 11:24, 25, 26. By these words it is plainly indicated that in this sacrament there is a remembrance of Christ and a proclamation of his death until he himself comes to the final and universal judgment; but that Christ is not present there bodily.

units.la: Secundo, ex natura Sacramentorum; in quibus 1. Signa oportet esse distincta a rebus significatis.
units.tr: Secondly, from the nature of the sacraments, in which (1) the signs must be distinct from the things signified.

units.la: 2. Debet servari analogia cum altero N. T. Sacramento; in quo utique non fit transsubstantiatio. Interim vide Tit. 3, 5. Act. II, 38. xxii, 16. cum 1 Joh. 1, 7. 1 Cor. 6, 11.
units.tr: (2) The analogy with the other sacrament of the New Testament must be preserved, in which certainly no transubstantiation takes place. Meanwhile see Titus 3:5; Acts 2:38; 22:16, compared with 1 John 1:7; 1 Cor. 6:11.

units.la: Quin 3. etiam cum Sacramentis V. T. Gen. 17, 10. 11. Exod. 12, 11, 12, 13. Rom. 4, 11.
units.tr: Moreover (3) also with the sacraments of the Old Testament: Gen. 17:10, 11; Exod. 12:11, 12, 13; Rom. 4:11.

units.la: Imo 4. cum ejusdem Sacramentis extraordinariis, quorum respectu Israelitae dicuntur eandem nobiscum esca spiritualem edisse, & eundem potum spiritualem bibisse; 1 Cor. 10, 3, 4. Cum tamen Christus tunc necdum fuerit incarnatus.
units.tr: Indeed (4) with the extraordinary sacraments of the same people, in regard to which the Israelites are said to have eaten the same spiritual food as we, and drunk the same spiritual drink: 1 Cor. 10:3, 4. Yet Christ had not then been incarnate.

units.la: Tertio, ex aliis Articulis fidei; & quidem 1. ex veritate & unitate humanae Christi naturae: unde sequitur ejus extensio, visibilitas, palpabilitas, & praesentia in uno tantum loco simul. Vide Marc. 16, 6. Luc. 24. 5, 6; 38. 39, 40.
units.tr: Thirdly, from the other articles of faith; and indeed (1) from the reality and unity of Christ's human nature, whence it follows that it is extended, visible, palpable, and present in only one place at a time. See Mark 16:6; Luke 24:5, 6, 38, 39, 40.

units.la: 2. Ex ortu humanae istius naturae; quae non est ex Pane & Vino, vi verborum a Sacerdote pronunciatorum; sed ex patribus, & Israëlitis, ex Judâ, ex lumbis & semine Davidis, atque ex B. Virgine Mariâ, persupernaturalem Spiritús Sanƈti operationem in eâ: Rom. 9, 5. Hebr. 7, 14. Act. 2, 30. Rom. 1, 3. Luc. I, 42; 45. Matth. I, 18. 20. Confer Matth. III, 9. Ioh. II, 9. Exod. 7, 10.
units.tr: (2) From the origin of this human nature, which is not from bread and wine by the power of the words pronounced by the priest, but from the fathers and Israelites, from Judah, from the loins and seed of David, and from the Blessed Virgin Mary, by the supernatural operation of the Holy Spirit in her: Rom. 9:5; Heb. 7:14; Acts 2:30; Rom. 1:3; Luke 1:42, 45; Matt. 1:18, 20. Compare Matt. 3:9; John 2:9; Exod. 7:10.

units.la: 3. Ex exaltatione, ascensione, & sessione Christi ad dextram Patris in cœlo; unde demùm novissimo die, corporaliter, localiter, & visibiliter, reversurus est ad universale iudicium: Ioh. 16. 28. XIV, 2, 3. Matth. 26, 11. XXIV, 23, 26, 27. Act. I, 11. III, 21. Col. 3, 1, 2, Hebr. 8, 4. Quod ergò nunc in terrâ existit, id non est verum ac proprie dictum corpus Christi.
units.tr: (3) From the exaltation, ascension, and sitting of Christ at the right hand of the Father in heaven; whence he is to return at last, on the final day, bodily, locally, and visibly, to the universal judgment: John 16:28; 14:2, 3; Matt. 26:11; 24:23, 26, 27; Acts 1:11; 3:21; Col. 3:1, 2; Heb. 8:4. What now exists on earth, therefore, is not the true and properly so-called body of Christ.

units.la: 4. Ex communione nostrâ cum Christo, quæ mystica est & spiritualis; non proprie corporolis Eph. III, 17. Inhabitet Christus per fidem in cordibus vestris, IV, 15, 16. 1 Cor. 12, 12, 13. Gal. II, 20. Col. III, 3. Unde etiàm vocatur esca spiritualis, & potus spiritualis; 1 Cor. 10, 3, 4. Adde Apoc. 2, 17, Ioh. 6, 35.
units.tr: (4) From our communion with Christ, which is mystical and spiritual, not properly corporeal: Eph. 3:17, "that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith"; 4:15, 16; 1 Cor. 12:12, 13; Gal. 2:20; Col. 3:3. Hence it is also called spiritual food and spiritual drink: 1 Cor. 10:3, 4. Add Rev. 2:17; John 6:35.

units.la: Quartò, ex absurdis quibusdam consequentibus, omni rationi adversis: nam 1. Accidentia Panis & Vini post transsubstantiationem sic existerent sine subjecto.
units.tr: Fourthly, from certain absurd consequences, opposed to all reason: for (1) after transubstantiation the accidents of bread and wine would thus exist without a subject.

units.la: 2. Corpus humanum verum ac proprie dictum existeret sine proprietatibus suis.
units.tr: (2) A true and properly so-called human body would exist without its properties.

units.la: 3. Fieret mutatio in præexistens; atque sic idem simul esset & non esset: nam corpus Christi statuitur per transsubstantiationem confici; & tamen idem numero existere ante transsubstantiationem.
units.tr: (3) A change would be made into something pre-existing, and so the same thing would at once be and not be; for the body of Christ is held to be made by transubstantiation, and yet to exist, numerically the same, before transubstantiation.

units.la: 4. Corpus gloriosum, quamvis sub alienis accidentibus, posse non solùm ab hominibus peccatoribus comedi: sed etiàm à muribus; atque in secessum ejici.
units.tr: (4) A glorified body, although under alien accidents, could be eaten not only by sinful men but also by mice, and be cast out into the privy.

units.la: Addi possent multa ex antiquitate Ecclesiasticâ.
units.tr: Many things could be added from ecclesiastical antiquity.

units.la: XLIX. Obj. 1 Agnoscenda est Transsubstantia- tio
units.tr: XLIX. Obj. 1: Transubstantiation must be acknowledged

units.la: tio, propter absolutam Dei omnipotentiam. Resp. 1. Frustrà provocatur ad Dei omnipotentiam, ubi non constat de ejus voluntate. 2. Deus mentiri, aut seipsum abnegare, non potest; neque consequenter facere contradictoria simul vera.
units.tr: because of God's absolute omnipotence. Reply 1: It is in vain to appeal to God's omnipotence where it is not established what his will is. 2: God cannot lie or deny himself, and consequently cannot make contradictories both true at once.

units.la: Obj.2. Christus Panem dixit corpus, & calicem sanguinem suum. Ergò. Resp. Dixit per usitatissimam metonymiam sacramentalem.
units.tr: Obj. 2: Christ called the bread his body, and the cup his blood. Therefore, etc. Reply: He spoke by a most common sacramental metonymy.

units.la: Obj.3. Christus dixit, Hoc est corpus meum: atque ita asseruit, id quod digitis tenetur, jàm esse verum ac proprie dictum corpus suum; atque adeò factam transsubstantiationem. Resp. Christus illud dicens, manifeste de pane locutus est: hinc Paulus; Panis, quem frangimus, &c. 1 Cor. 10, 16. Et Quisquis ederit panem hunc, &c. xi.27. neque obstat particula neutrius generis: sic enim saepius absolute indicatur res illa, cujus proxime facta est mentio. Vide Zach. 1, 9. IV, 4, 5.
units.tr: Obj. 3: Christ said, This is my body; and so he asserted that what is held in the fingers is now truly and properly his body, and that transubstantiation has therefore taken place. Reply: In saying this, Christ plainly spoke of the bread. Hence Paul: "The bread which we break," etc., 1 Cor. 10:16; and "Whoever shall eat this bread," etc., 11:27. Nor does the neuter particle stand in the way, for a thing is often indicated absolutely in this way, by the thing most recently mentioned. See Zech. 1:9; 4:4, 5.

units.la: Obj. 4. In verbis Christi, Luc. 22, 20. de Poculo, τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον, ἡ καινὴ Διαθήκη ἐν τῷ αἵματί μου, τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐκχυννόμενον, participium illud ἐκχυννόμενον casû non convenit cum nomine αἷμα; sed cum remotiore ποτήριον. Effusio ergò pertinet ad calicem; quia in eo per transsubstantiationem est verus ac proprie dictus sanguis Christi: quasi Servator dixisset; Hic sanguis meus, pro vobis effusus, est novum foedus, &c. Resp. Absurdissime illud dicitur: 1. Christus enim diserte affirmavit, contentum calicis esse fructum vitis. 2. Nec ipsi Pontificii audent asserere, Sanguinem Christi in Eucharistiâ effundi. Et 3. quomodò Christi sanguis proprie dici poterit Novum Testamentum in sanguine ipsius? 4. Participium τὸ ἐκχυννόμενον referri potest ad nomen αἷμα, per enallagen casûs satis obviam. Vide inter alia Apoc. I, 4, 5.
units.tr: Obj. 4: In Christ's words about the cup, Luke 22:20, the participle ἐκχυννόμενον [being poured out] does not agree in case with the noun αἷμα [blood] but with the more distant ποτήριον [cup]. The pouring out therefore belongs to the cup, because in it, through transubstantiation, there is the true and properly so-called blood of Christ, as if the Saviour had said: "This blood of mine, poured out for you, is the new covenant," etc. Reply: This is said most absurdly. 1: Christ plainly affirmed that the contents of the cup are the fruit of the vine. 2: Not even the Papists themselves dare to assert that the blood of Christ is poured out in the Eucharist. 3: And how could the blood of Christ properly be called the New Testament in his blood? 4: The participle τὸ ἐκχυννόμενον [the thing being poured out] can be referred to the noun αἷμα [blood], by an enallage of case, which is quite common. See among other places Rev. 1:4, 5.

units.la: Obj.. 5. Qui Sacramentum illud accipiunt indigne, rei sunt corporis & sanguinis Domini : ergò ipsum proprie dictum Corpus & Sanguinem Domini accipiunt, & contumelia afficiunt. Resp. Imò ipsum Corpus & Sanguinem Domini contemnunt, & contumelia afficiunt, in symbolis ab Ipso institutis, & sancte usurpari jussis.
units.tr: Obj. 5: Those who receive that sacrament unworthily are guilty of the body and blood of the Lord; therefore they receive the properly so-called body and blood of the Lord itself, and do it dishonour. Reply: Nay, they despise and do dishonour to the body and blood of the Lord itself, in the symbols instituted by him and commanded to be used holily.

units.la: Obj. 6. Christus Joh. 6, 50,-56. Se & Carnem suam dixit esse vere cibum ac panem ; Sanguinem verò potum, ad vitam æternam. Ergò Panis eucharisticus transsubstantiatur in verum ac proprie dictum Corpus Christi, &c. Resp. 1. Majori specie dicerent, Corpus Christi transsubstantiari in verum ac proprie dictum Panem, &c. 2, Isto tempore Cœna Dominica nondum erat instituta : ac proinde Christus non potuit tunc loqui de transsubstantiatione, quæ jam tunc fieret. 3. Manifeste loquitur de spirituali alimento, per fidem sumendo, & vitam spiritualem in æternum producturo ; verf. 33, 35. quod semper idem fuit ; 1 Cor. 10, 3, 4. Hebr. 13, 8. & significatur atque obsignatur Cœnâ Dominicâ postmodùm institutâ.
units.tr: Obj. 6. Christ, John 6:50-56, said that he himself and his flesh are truly food and bread, and his blood drink, for eternal life. Therefore the eucharistic bread is transubstantiated into the true and properly so-called body of Christ, etc. Reply. 1: They would more plausibly say that the body of Christ is transubstantiated into the true and properly so-called bread, etc. 2: At that time the Lord's Supper had not yet been instituted, and so Christ could not then speak of a transubstantiation which would only take place later. 3: He plainly speaks of spiritual food, taken by faith, which will produce spiritual life for ever; vv. 33, 35. This has always been the same; 1 Cor. 10:3, 4; Heb. 13:8. And it is signified and sealed by the Lord's Supper instituted afterwards.

units.la: Obj. 7. Paulus vidit Christum, Act. 9,5 .XVIII, 11.
units.tr: Obj. 7. Paul saw Christ, Acts 9:5; 18:11.

units.la: 1 Cor. 15, 5. Ergo poterit etiam simul existere in Cœlo, & in hoc Sacramento. &c. Resp. 1. In istis locis nequaquàm dicitur, Christum tunc corporaliter extitisse in Cœlo, & simul in terrâ apud Paulum. 2. Intelligenda est visio per ecstasin, aut aliam aliquam mentis elevationem supernaturalem ; aut in symbolo aliquo extraordinario, Christum secundùm humanam naturam repræsentante. Confer 2 Cor. 12, 2, 3, 4. Act. 7, 55,56.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 15:5. Therefore he could also exist at the same time in heaven and in this sacrament, etc. Reply: 1: In those passages it is by no means said that Christ then existed bodily in heaven and at the same time on earth with Paul. 2: The seeing must be understood as a vision through ecstasy, or some other supernatural elevation of the mind; or else as occurring in some extraordinary symbol representing Christ according to his human nature. Compare 2 Cor. 12:2-4; Acts 7:55, 56.

units.la: I. Ubiquitistæ pro Transsubstantiatione (μεταβολή) statuunt Consubstantiationem (συνουσίων) ut Christi Corpus sit in, cum, & sub Pane Cœnæ Dominicæ, &c.
units.tr: I. The Ubiquitists, in place of transubstantiation (μεταβολή), posit consubstantiation (συνουσίωσις), so that the body of Christ is in, with, and under the bread of the Lord's Supper, etc.

units.la: Hanc confutamus iisdem ferè argumentis, quibus Transsubstantiationem : primo, ex institutione Cœnæ Dominicæ: Quoniam 1. Christus suo Corpore mensæ accubuit, non illud proprie Discipulis in manum dedit, in, cum, & sub Pane.
units.tr: We refute this with almost the same arguments as we used against transubstantiation. First, from the institution of the Lord's Supper: because 1: Christ reclined at table with his body, and did not properly give that body into the disciples' hands, in, with, and under the bread.

units.la: 2. Dixit Corpus suum frangi, & Sanguinem effundi; sed utrumque demum futurum erat: ergo Corpus fractum, & Sanguis effusus proprie Discipulis tunc non dabatur, &c.
units.tr: 2: He said that his body would be broken and his blood poured out; but both were yet to happen. Therefore the broken body and the poured-out blood were not then properly given to the disciples, etc.

units.la: Secundo, ex natura & analogia aliorum Sacramentorum, tum V. tum N. Test. in quibus non est istiusmodi Confubstantiatio; sed rei spiritualis obsignatio in recto usu: ut patet in Circumcisione, & Agno Paschali. Atque item in extraordinario illo Sacramento, de quo Paulus, 1 Cor. 10, 4. Petra illa erat Christus: non certe per συμβολον Corporis aut Sanguinis Christi, in, cum & sub illa Petra, vel Aqua: Corpus enim Christi ὑπόστατον, verum ac proprie dictum, & Sanguis ipsius, tunc nondum existebant. Similiter in Baptismo non est talis συμβολα, &c.
units.tr: Second, from the nature and analogy of the other sacraments, both of the Old and of the New Testament, in which there is no such consubstantiation, but only the sealing of a spiritual thing in right use. This is plain in circumcision and the Passover lamb. Likewise in that extraordinary sacrament of which Paul speaks, 1 Cor. 10:4: "That rock was Christ." Certainly not by a symbol [συμβολον] of the body or blood of Christ in, with, and under that rock or the water; for the body of Christ, a true and properly so-called substance [ὑπόστατον], and his blood, did not yet exist then. Similarly, in baptism there is no such symbol, etc.

units.la: Tertio, ex Articulis fidei: 1. ex veritate & finitudine Corporis Christi.
units.tr: Third, from the articles of faith: 1: from the truth and finitude of the body of Christ.

units.la: 2. Ex locali ascensione ejus in Coelum, & remansione illic ad extremum usque judicium.
units.tr: 2: from his local ascension into heaven, and his remaining there until the last judgment.

units.la: 3. Ex communione nostra mystica cum Christo.
units.tr: 3: from our mystical communion with Christ.

units.la: Quarto, ex absurdis quibusdam consequentibus. Quod sic aliquod humanum Corpus esset penetrabile aliis; non haberet essentiam finitam ac circumscriptam; esset invisibile, impalpabile, &c. quibus proprietatibus Spiritus a Corpore distinguitur.
units.tr: Fourth, from certain absurd consequences. For if some human body were thus penetrable by others, it would not have a finite and circumscribed essence; it would be invisible, impalpable, etc., and by these properties the Spirit is distinguished from the body.

units.la: Obj. 1. Christus dixit; Hoc est corpus meum, &c. loquens de Corpore suo vero ac proprie dicto; quod consequenter dedit, in, cum, & sub pane. Resp. Christus procul dubio habuit humanam naturam veram ac proprie dictam; & Corpus tale in praedicato dicitur de Pane: sed per metonymiam sacramentalem: unde non sequitur συμβολα.
units.tr: Obj. 1. Christ said, This is my body, etc., speaking of his body in the true and properly so-called sense, which he consequently gave, in, with, and under the bread. Reply. Christ undoubtedly had a true and properly so-called human nature; and such a body is predicated of the bread, but by sacramental metonymy; hence it does not follow that there is a symbol.

units.la: Obj. 2. Fideles vere percipiunt ipsum Christum, &c. Resp. Accipiunt per fidem: eaque est res significata hujus Sacramenti.
units.tr: Obj. 2. The faithful truly receive Christ himself, etc. Reply. They receive him by faith, and this is the thing signified by this sacrament.

units.la: LI. In Missa insuper fingitur verum Sacrificium propitiatorium, ità ut proprie dictum Corpus & Sanguis Christi sub speciebus Panis ac Vini offeratur Deo, ad impetrandam remissionem peccatorum pro viventibus & mortuis. Plenius autem refutabitur istud commentum, si consideremus Altare, Sacrificium, Sacrificationem, & eos pro quibus Sacrificatio dicitur peragi.
units.tr: LI. Moreover, in the Mass a true propitiatory sacrifice is invented, so that the properly so-called body and blood of Christ are offered to God under the appearances of bread and wine, to obtain forgiveness of sins for the living and the dead. This fiction will be refuted more fully if we consider the altar, the sacrifice, the sacrificing, and those for whom the sacrifice is said to be performed.

units.la: 1. Ad Altare quod attinet; nullum externum existit, quod Christum sanctificare potuit, vel poterit: Sed ipse idem Sacerdos, & Sacrificium, se per Spiritum suum Deo obtulit inculpatum: Hebr. 9, 14. Joh. 17, 19. Confer Exod. 27, 1,-. xxix, 37. xxxviii. 1,-. xl, 10, 29. Levit. 8, 11. cum Matth. 23, 19. Quare Apostolus Hebr. 13, 10. Habemus altare, ex quo edendi non habent jus qui tabernaculo cultum praestant. Quibus verbis aperte indicat, nunc sub N. T. non quaerendum Altare aliquod terrestre; sed ipsum Christum solum. Quoniam igitur nunc non datur externum aliquod Altare, secundum tabulas Novi Foederis; absurde fingitur adhuc verum Sacrificium propitiatorium, quotidie Deo offerendum.
units.tr: 1. As for the altar: there is no external altar which could sanctify Christ, or ever will. But he himself, both priest and sacrifice, offered himself without blemish to God through his own Spirit: Heb. 9:14; John 17:19. Compare Exod. 27:1 ff.; 29:37; 38:1 ff.; 40:10, 29; Lev. 8:11, with Matt. 23:19. Wherefore the Apostle, Heb. 13:10: "We have an altar, from which those who serve the tabernacle have no right to eat." By these words he plainly indicates that under the New Testament no earthly altar is to be sought, but Christ alone. Since, therefore, no external altar now exists according to the tables of the New Covenant, it is absurdly imagined that there is still a true propitiatory sacrifice to be offered to God daily.

units.la: 2. Quod ad Sacrificium; hoc unicum est pro N. T. Corporis sc. Christi ad mortem transfixi, & Sanguinis effusi. Hebr. 9, 25, 26. Neque ut saepe offerat Semet ipsum: -- (Alioquin oportuisset Eum saepè passum fuisse à jacto mundi fundamento:) sed nunc semel in consummatione saeculorum, & ad peccatum per immolationem Sui ipsius è medio tollendum, factus est conspicuus. x. 14. Unica oblatione consummavit in perpetuum eos qui sanctificantur. Atqui verum Corpus Christi nunc non amplius obnoxium est morti, &c.
units.tr: 2. As for the sacrifice: for the New Testament there is only one, namely the body of Christ pierced to death, and his blood poured out. Heb. 9:25, 26: nor is it that he should often offer himself (otherwise he would have had to suffer often from the foundation of the world), but now once, at the consummation of the ages, he has been made manifest to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself. 10:14: By one offering he has perfected for ever those who are sanctified. But the true body of Christ is now no longer subject to death, etc.

units.la: 3. Quod ad Sacrificationem; haec vere unica est, in exexterna visibili Corporis Christi super ligno crucis transfixione, & Sanguinis effusione, ac morte ipsius, semel peracta. Hebr. 7, 27. Hoc fecit semel, cum semetipsum obtulit. ix, 12, 14. Per proprium sanguinem ingressus est semel Sacrarium, aeternam redemtionem nactus, &c. x, 10. Sanctificati sumus per oblationem corporis Jesu Christi semel factam: Adde, 12, 14. Rom. 6, 9, 10. 1 Petr. 3, 18. Item Hebr. x, 1, -5, 18.
units.tr: 3. As for the sacrifice, this is truly unique: it was accomplished once for all in the outward, visible piercing of Christ's body on the wood of the cross, the effusion of his blood, and his death. Heb. 7:27. He did this once, when he offered himself. 9:12, 14. Through his own blood he entered the sanctuary once, having obtained eternal redemption, etc. 10:10. We have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ made once for all. Add 12, 14. Rom. 6:9, 10. 1 Pet. 3:18. Likewise Heb. 10:1, 5, 18.

units.la: 4. Quantum vero ad eos, Pro quibusperacta est, vel perageretur, Sacrificatio; Christus unica oblatione omnia singulorum electorum peccata expiavit; Hebr. 10, 14. 1 Tim. 2, 6. Atque hoc singulis fidelibus in recto usu Coenae Dominicae obsignative applicatur: Luc. 22, 19, 20. 1 Cor. xi, 23, -29, x, 16, 17.
units.tr: 4. As for those for whom the sacrifice has been accomplished, or is to be accomplished: by his single offering Christ expiated the sins of each of the elect. Heb. 10:14. 1 Tim. 2:6. And this is applied to each of the faithful, as a seal, in the right use of the Lord's Supper: Luke 22:19, 20. 1 Cor. 11:23, 29; 10:16, 17.

units.la: Contra vero Missa per quam absurde dicitur offerri in remissionem peccatorum pro vivis & mortuis. Mortuos autem illi intelligunt in Purgatorio laborantes. Atqui remissio jam pridem perfectissime fuit impetrata; adeo ut nova adhuc impetratio, nihil aliud sit, quam impia perfectissimi Sacrificii Christi abnegatio. Simili absurditate statuunt, Missam spectatoribus & absentibus quoque prodesse; alienis ab Ecclesia, convertendis servire; imo etiam rebus aliis ad hominem pertinentibus.
units.tr: On the contrary, the Mass is absurdly said to be offered for the remission of sins, for the living and the dead. By the dead they mean those suffering in Purgatory. But remission was long ago obtained most perfectly, so that a new obtaining of it is nothing other than an impious denial of the most perfect sacrifice of Christ. With similar absurdity they maintain that the Mass benefits spectators and absent persons too, serves those outside the Church who are to be converted, and even benefits other things that pertain to man.

units.la: LII.
units.tr: LII.

units.la: Obj. 1. Gen. 14, 18, 19. Melchizedekus, Sacerdos Dei altissimi, obtulit Panem & Vinum. Ita praefiguratum fuit Sacrificium Missae. Resp. Imo protulit, ﬠ; atque iis ferculis Abrahamum cum suis copiis refecit.
units.tr: Obj. 1. Gen. 14:18, 19. Melchizedek, priest of God Most High, offered bread and wine. Thus the sacrifice of the Mass was prefigured. Resp. Nay, he brought out the bread and wine, and with those provisions refreshed Abraham and his company.

units.la: Obj. 2. Quaedam in S. Scriptura occurrunt de Altari, Suffitu, & Sacrificiis sub N. T. futuris, praeter unicum Sacrificium Christi. Ergo, &c. Resp. Ista metaphorice & spiritualiter sunt intelligenda de cultu Divino, precibus, gratiarum actionibus, eleemosynis, omnibusque bonis operibus: Isf. 19, 19, 20, 21. 20; 21. Mal. 1, 11. Confer Rom. 12, 1. Phil. 4, 18, Hebr. 13, 16.
units.tr: Obj. 2. Some things occur in Holy Scripture about an altar, incense, and sacrifices to be under the New Testament, besides the one sacrifice of Christ. Therefore, etc. Resp. These are to be understood metaphorically and spiritually, of divine worship, prayers, thanksgivings, almsgiving, and all good works: Isa. 19:19, 20, 21. 20; 21. Mal. 1:11. Compare Rom. 12:1, Phil. 4:18, Heb. 13:16.

units.la: Obj. 3. Christus dixit; Facite hoc ad Mei commemorationem; 1 Cor. xi, 24, 25. Facere autem ad Sacrificia pertinet. Resp. Imo verbum istud latissime patet; & pro subjecta materia debet exponi: sed a genere ad speciem non valet illatio affirmativa.
units.tr: Obj. 3. Christ said, Do this in remembrance of me, 1 Cor. 11:24, 25. But to do pertains to sacrifices. Resp. Nay, the word is very broad, and must be explained according to its subject matter; but an affirmative inference from genus to species does not hold.

units.la: Obj. 4. Act. 13, 1, 2. Doctores aliqui Antiocheni dicuntur fuisse λειτουργοῦντες, hoc est sacrificantes, sive officium Missæ celebrantes. Ergo. Resp. Verbum λειτουργεῖν generatim significat Ministrare. Ita Angeli Hebr. 1, 14. appellantur λειτουργικὰ πνεύματα, ministratorii spiritus. Et Rom. 13, 6. de Principibus & Magistratibus Politicis, λειτουργοὶ Θεοῦ εἰσί, Ministri Dei sunt. Atque ita dicitur, quòd Doctores Antiocheni fuerint λειτουργοῦντες, ministrantes Deo cum jejunio, sed nihil in specie de Sacrificio Missæ.
units.tr: Obj. 4. Acts 13:1, 2. Some teachers of Antioch are said to have been λειτουργοῦντες [leitourgountes], that is, sacrificing, or celebrating the office of the Mass. Therefore, etc. Resp. The verb λειτουργεῖν [leitourgein] generally means to minister. So angels are called λειτουργικὰ πνεύματα [leitourgika pneumata], ministering spirits, in Heb. 1:14. And in Rom. 13:6, of princes and civil magistrates, they are λειτουργοὶ Θεοῦ εἰσί [leitourgoi Theou eisin], ministers of God. And so it is said that the teachers of Antioch were λειτουργοῦντες, ministering to God with fasting; but nothing in particular about the sacrifice of the Mass.

units.la: LIII. Cœnæ Dominicæ finis est, fidelis ac grata recordatio Christi pro nobis crucifixi atque oblati, ad spiritualem Ipsius ac beneficiorum ex Ipso promanantium communionem; 1 Cor. xi, 24, 25. dum corda habemus sursum elevata ad Dominum, in cœlesti gloria viventem, ibique mansurum donec novissimo die revertatur ad extremum judicium, & plenam nostri glorificationem: 1 Cor. xi, 26. Aliter se habet Missa; ubi Christus secundum humanam naturam deorsum quaeritur; sub speciebus Panis ac Vini: & ore manducari fingitur, ad percipiendam remissionem peccatorum, aliaque tum spiritualia, tum corporalia beneficia.
units.tr: LIII. The end of the Lord's Supper is the faithful and grateful remembrance of Christ, who was crucified and offered for us, leading to spiritual communion with him and with the benefits that flow from him: 1 Cor. 11:24, 25; while we keep our hearts lifted up to the Lord, who lives in heavenly glory, and there remains until the last day, when he will return to the final judgment and to our full glorification: 1 Cor. 11:26. The Mass is otherwise: there Christ according to his human nature is sought below, under the species of bread and wine; and he is feigned to be eaten by the mouth, to receive the remission of sins and other benefits both spiritual and bodily.

units.la: Sed Adjuncta quoque lustremus! Cœna Dominica universam peccatorum remissionem, atque integram salutem, nobis obsignat in Christo solo, ejusque oblatione unica positam: Luc. 22, 19, 20. Sed Missæ farrago, Sanctorum merita, atque invocationem Idololatricam, includit. Et Panem consecratum, pro ipso Christo, in Missa, & extra eam, adorandum proponit.
units.tr: But let us also examine the accessories! The Lord's Supper seals to us the entire remission of sins and full salvation, in Christ alone and in his single offering: Luke 22:19, 20. But the Mass is a medley, including the merits of the saints and idolatrous invocation. And it sets forth the consecrated bread, to be adored in the Mass and outside it, as Christ himself.

units.la: Illa administratur lingua populo nota: hæc verò ignota.
units.tr: The former is administered in a language known to the people; the latter, however, in an unknown one.

units.la: Illa administratur ritibus à Christo institutis, hæc instrumentis, vestibus, gestibus, ritibus, &c. ab hominibus confictis.
units.tr: The former is administered with rites instituted by Christ; the latter with instruments, vestments, gestures, rites, etc., devised by men.

units.la: XIV. Nunc videamus de falsis Sacramentis! Sunt autem ea, quinque Pontificiorum; Confirmatio, Pœnitentia, Unctio extrema, Ordinatio, & Matrimonium: quæ hoc versiculo continentur; Ordino, Conjungo, Confirmo, Pœnitet, Ungo.
units.tr: XIV. Now let us see the false sacraments! There are five of the Papists: Confirmation, Penance, Extreme Unction, Ordination, and Matrimony; these are contained in the little verse Ordino, Conjungo, Confirmo, Poenitet, Ungo (I ordain, I join, I confirm, I repent, I anoint).

units.la: Sic illi in universum septem Sacramenta statuunt, hoc versiculo comprehensa; Abluo, Firmo, Cibo, Piget, Ungit, & Ordinat, Uxor.
units.tr: Thus they establish seven sacraments in all, comprised in the verse Abluo, Firmo, Cibo, Piget, Ungit, & Ordinat, Uxor (I wash, I strengthen, I feed, it grieves, he anoints, and he ordains, a wife).

units.la: Confirmatio illis est Sacramentum, quod baptizatis adolescentibus, vel adultis, confertur ab Episcopo (aut saltem ejus Suffraganeo) in fronte, per sacrum chrisma, additis solennibus verbis (Signo te signo crucis, & confirmo te oleo salutis, in nomine Patris, Filii, & Spiritus Sancti) & inflicta maxillæ alapa, ac data deinde Pace, adhibito etiam Compatre, potissimum circa tempus Pentecostes: ut sic fides corroboretur; & homini Christiano ad nomen Domini, quandocunque opus est, intrepide profitendum, animus addatur.
units.tr: Confirmation is for them a sacrament, conferred by the bishop (or at least his suffragan) on baptized adolescents or adults, on the forehead, with holy chrism, with the solemn words I sign you with the sign of the cross, and I confirm you with the oil of salvation, in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and with a blow to the cheek, and then the Peace is given; a godparent is also present, especially around the time of Pentecost, so that faith may be strengthened, and courage added to the Christian man to profess the name of the Lord fearlessly whenever necessary.

units.la: Sed opponimus huic commento, 1. Sacramentum confirmationis & corroborationis spiritualis, est nobis ipsa Cœna Dominica, secundum SS. Literas. Aliud ignoramus
units.tr: But we object to this invention: 1. For us the sacrament of confirmation and of spiritual strengthening is the Lord's Supper itself, according to the Sacred Letters. We know of no other.

units.la: 2. Istius Confirmationis, neque materia, neque forma, neque adjuncta, neque finis talis, comparent in S. Literis: unde concludimus, non esse verum N. T. Sacramentum.
units.tr: 2. Neither the matter, nor the form, nor the accessories, nor such an end of this confirmation appear in the Sacred Letters; whence we conclude that it is not a true sacrament of the New Testament.

units.la: 3. Absurde Episcopus, alapam interim infligens, persopersónam Diaboli, hominem suis colaphis exercentis, sustinet. Confer 2 Cor. 12, 7.
units.tr: 3. It is absurd that the bishop, while giving the blow, takes the part of the Devil, and the man who inflicts blows on others with his fists is the one who bears them. Compare 2 Cor. 12:7.

units.la: 4. Perperam ritus iste ab hominibus institutus dicitur characterem indelebilem animæ imprimere, gratiam baptismalem perficere, &c. atque eatenus ipsi Baptismo præstare.
units.tr: 4. It is wrongly said that this rite, instituted by men, imprints an indelible character on the soul, perfects baptismal grace, etc., and so provides something for Baptism itself.

units.la: Obj. 1. 2 Cor. I, 21, 22. memoratur confirmatio ibid. & 1 Joh. II, 27. unctio. Ergò. Resp. Istic manifestè agitur de confirmatione & unctione spirituali, per Spiritum Sanctum.
units.tr: Obj. 1. 2 Cor. 1:21, 22. Confirmation is mentioned there, and 1 John 2:27 mentions anointing. Therefore, etc. Resp. There it is clearly a matter of spiritual confirmation and anointing, through the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Obj. 2. Apostoli, Act. 8, 15. leguntur baptizatis imposuisse manus, &c. Resp. Hæc manuum impositio tunc iis significabat superventura in ipsos extraordinaria Spiritus Sancti dona, adeoque nunc non amplius obtinet, postquam hæc dona cessârunt. Confer Actor. 19, 6. x. 44, 48. itemque Matth. 7, 12.
units.tr: Obj. 2. The apostles, Acts 8:15, are read to have laid hands on the baptized, etc. Resp. This laying on of hands then signified to them the extraordinary gifts of the Holy Spirit about to come upon them, and so it no longer holds now, since those gifts have ceased. Compare Acts 19:6; 10:44, 48, and likewise Matt. 7:12.

units.la: LV. Pœnitentia hoc loco non consideratur, ut est conversio hominis à vana conversatione ad Deum verum, quâ primùm vita in melius mutatur: ea enim in adultis Baptismum antecedit; neque vim Sacramenti habet, juxta ipsos Adversarios. Illi enim statuunt, hanc esse Sacramentum novæ Legis, à Christo post resurrectionem suam institutum, iis qui post Baptismum laberentur, & peccata sua confiterentur, &c. tanquam alteram tabulam post naufragium, administrandum à Sacerdotibus, per ista verba; Ego te absolvo in nomine Patris, &c. Licet non desint casus reservati. Sed cum in tota illa actione, prout à Pontificiis describitur, nullum externum visibile elementum detur, ad quod Verbum institutionis & promissionis, accederet, ut fieret Sacramentum; neque signum audibile ex instituto Divino efficax ad effectum spiritualem, (quod tamen ipsi Adversarii in omni Sacramento requirunt) hanc pro Sacramento non esse habendam, extra dubium est. Accedit, quod non conveniat inter illos de forma hujus Sacramenti; aliis absolutionem statuentibus & formam & materiam simul; aliis formam duntaxat. Sed nihil istorum auctoritate SS. Literarum nititur.
units.tr: LV. Penance is not considered here as the conversion of a man from vain conduct to the true God, by which life is first changed for the better; for in adults this precedes Baptism, and it does not have the force of a sacrament, according to the Adversaries themselves. For they maintain that this is a sacrament of the New Law, instituted by Christ after his resurrection, for those who fall after Baptism and confess their sins, etc., as a second plank after shipwreck, to be administered by priests, with these words: I absolve you in the name of the Father, etc. Although cases reserved to higher authority are not lacking. But since in that whole action, as the Papists describe it, no external visible element is given, to which the word of institution and promise might be joined so as to make a sacrament, nor an audible sign efficacious by divine institution toward a spiritual effect (which the Adversaries themselves nevertheless require in every sacrament), it is beyond doubt that this should not be held a sacrament. Moreover, they do not agree among themselves about the form of this sacrament: some state that absolution is both form and matter at once, others the form alone. But none of these rests on the authority of the Sacred Letters.

units.la: LVI. Sacramentum extremæ unctionis vocant; cùm homo infirmus, qui jam videtur moriturus, sed pœnitentiam agit de peccatis suis, per Sacerdotem in certis corporis membris ungitur oleo, quod Episcopus consecravit, efficaciter (ex eorum opinione) conferente remissionem reliquiarum peccati; ad mentis relevationem; atque corporis sanitatem, siquidem ita expediat, recuperandam.
units.tr: LVI. They call it the sacrament of extreme unction: when a sick man, who now seems about to die but repents of his sins, is anointed by the priest with oil consecrated by the bishop, on certain parts of the body; this is held (in their opinion) to effectively confer the remission of the remnants of sin, for the relief of the mind and, if it is so expedient, for the recovery of bodily health.

units.la: Ex hâc descriptione satis apparet, 1. nullam esse talem Divinam institutionem.
units.tr: From this description it sufficiently appears: (1) that there is no such divine institution.

units.la: 2. Non esse Divinam promissionem gratiæ spiritualis justificantis & sanctificantis istis cerimoniis annexam.
units.tr: (2) That there is no divine promise of spiritual grace, justifying and sanctifying, annexed to these ceremonies.

units.la: 3. Neque analogiam, ad spiritualem istiusmodi effectum, Divinitus propositam.
units.tr: (3) Nor is there any analogy divinely proposed to such a spiritual effect.

units.la: 4. Neque statam & perpetuam cerimoniam, Ecclesiæ catholicæ præscriptam. Atque adeò non esse Sacramentum.
units.tr: (4) Nor is there a fixed and perpetual ceremony prescribed by the catholic Church. And so it is not a sacrament.

units.la: Obj. 1. Marc. 6, 13. Apostoli dicuntur multos ægros oleo unxisse, eosque sanasse, &c. Resp. Istud ad donum & opus miraculosæ sanationis manifeste pertinet. Gratis autem dicunt, istam unctionem præfigurasse suam sacramentalem.
units.tr: Objection 1: Mark 6:13 says that the apostles anointed many sick people with oil and healed them, etc. Answer: That pertains plainly to the gift and work of miraculous healing. They say, without reason, that this anointing foreshadowed their sacramental anointing.

units.la: Obj. 2. Jac. V, 14, 15. jubentur fideles ægrotantes, Presbyteros Ecclesiæ ad se vocare; qui eos oleo ungerent in nomine Domini, addita oratione; cum spe obtinendæ sanationis, & remissionis peccatorum; &c. Resp. Etiam ibi locus manifeste agit de miraculosâ sanatione, cujus symbolum erat talis unctio. Verùm cessante istoeffectu temere adhibetur symbolum. De remissione peccatorum conditionaliter loquitur Apostolus, &c. fatente etiam Card. Cajetano ad locum.
units.tr: Objection 2: James 5:14, 15 bids the faithful when they are sick to call the elders of the Church to them, who are to anoint them with oil in the name of the Lord, with prayer added, in hope of obtaining healing and forgiveness of sins, etc. Answer: There too the passage plainly deals with miraculous healing, of which such anointing was the sign. But when that effect has ceased, the sign is used rashly. The Apostle speaks of forgiveness of sins only conditionally, etc., as even Cardinal Cajetan admits on the passage.

units.la: LVII. Succedit Sacramentum Ordinis, quod vocant. In Ecclesiâ Dei omnia decenter & ordine fieri debere, juxta 1 Cor. 14, 40. in confesso est. Atque adeo neminem nisi legitime vocatum, Ministerium in ea exercere posse: quod cap. 20. probabitur.
units.tr: LVII. Next comes what they call the Sacrament of Orders. That in the Church of God "all things should be done decently and in order," according to 1 Cor. 14:40, is granted by all. And so no one may exercise the ministry in it unless lawfully called; this will be proved in chapter 20.

units.la: Pontificii communiter septem statuunt Ordines: quatuor minores; Ostiariorum, Lectorum (quibus Cantores fere accensentur,) Exorcistarum, & Acoluthorum: tres autem majores; Subdiaconorum, Diaconorum, & Presbyterorum, (quibus fere Episcopos accensent.) Vulgò unumquemque Ordinem dicunt esse Sacramentum, materiâ, forma, & essectu proprio distinctum; nec tamen esse plura Sacramenta. Alii tamen solum Presbyteratum Sacramentum esse contendunt, &c.
units.tr: The Papists commonly set down seven orders: four minor, those of doorkeepers, readers (to whom singers are generally added), exorcists, and acolytes; and three major, those of subdeacons, deacons, and presbyters (to whom they generally add bishops). Commonly they say that each order is a sacrament, distinct in matter, form and proper effect; yet they do not hold that there are several sacraments. Others, however, contend that only the presbyterate is a sacrament, etc.

units.la: Quantum ad materiam; in Ordinibus majoribus Signa adhibent duplicia; impositionem manuum scil. & traditionem instrumentorum; utpote Calicis & Patinæ in Presbyteratu, &c. Formam constituunt in verbis, quibus Episcopus tunc utitur: ex. gr. in ordinatione Presbyteri; Accipe potestatem offerre sacrificium Deo, missasque consecrare, tam pro vivis quam pro defunctis in nomine Domini. In ordinatione Diaconi; Accipe potestatem legendi Euangelium in Ecclesia Dei, &c. In ordinatione Acoluthi; Accipe ceroferarium cum cereo; & scias, te ad accendenda Ecclesiæ luminaria mancipatum. &c.
units.tr: As to the matter: in the major orders they use a double sign, namely the imposition of hands and the delivery of instruments, such as the chalice and paten in the presbyterate, etc. They locate the form in the words which the bishop then uses; for example, in the ordination of a presbyter: "Receive the power to offer sacrifice to God and to consecrate masses, for the living as well as the dead, in the name of the Lord." In the ordination of a deacon: "Receive the power to read the Gospel in the Church of God," etc. In the ordination of an acolyte: "Receive the candlestick with the candle, and know that you are dedicated to lighting the lamps of the Church," etc.

units.la: Effectum vulgò geminum faciunt; quòd istud Sacramentum gratiam conferat, & characterem in anima ordinati imprimat, in majoribus saltem Ordinibus. Verum ista omnia humanæ constitutionis sunt, & errorum plena,
units.tr: As to the effect, they commonly make it twofold: that this sacrament confers grace, and imprints a character on the soul of the one ordained, at least in the major orders. But all these things are of human constitution and full of errors.

units.la: Obj. 1 Tim. 4, 14. & 2, 1, 6. commemoratur gratia à Timotheo accepta, per manuum impositionem. Ergo. Resp. 1. Istic non agitur de gratiâ justificante & sanctificante, quæ Sacramentis proprie obsignatur. 2. Idem ritus olim etiam adhibitus fuit in qualicunque collatione extraordinariorum donorum Spiritûs Sancti. Sic nullo modo inde probatur Sacramentum.
units.tr: Objection: 1 Tim. 4:14 and 2 Tim. 1:6 mention the grace received by Timothy through the imposition of hands. Therefore, etc. Answer: (1) There is no question here of justifying and sanctifying grace, which is properly sealed by the sacraments. (2) The same rite was formerly also used in whatever conferral of extraordinary gifts of the Holy Spirit there was. So nothing is proved from this for a sacrament.

units.la: LVIII. De Matrimonio Pontificii recentiores sta- tuunt, illud esse Sacramentum verè ac proprie dictum
units.tr: LVIII. Concerning Matrimony: more recent Papists maintain that it is a sacrament truly and properly so called.

units.la: Nos breviter opponimus; 1. non esse à Deo, aut Christo, institutum, ut Sacramentale signum; aut sigillum gratiæ justificantis ac sanctificantis.
units.tr: We briefly oppose this: (1) that it was not instituted by God or Christ as a sacramental sign, or as a seal of justifying and sanctifying grace.

units.la: 2. Nec promissione de gratiâ illâ, in ejus usû exhibendâ, munitum.
units.tr: (2) Nor is it furnished with a promise of that grace to be exhibited in its use.

units.la: 3. Nihil esse in Christianorum matrimoniis, quo fidelium matrimonia sub V. T. caruerint; cum tamen Pontificii fere contendant, illud Novi T. duntaxat Sacramentum esse.
units.tr: (3) There is nothing in Christian marriages by which the marriages of the faithful were lacking under the Old Testament; yet the Papists mostly contend that it is a sacrament of the New Testament alone.

units.la: 4. Neque certam aliquam formam pro ejus administratione Divinitus esse præscriptam. Unde ipsi Adversarii multum differentiunt de assignandâ materiâ & formâ istius Sacramenti: alii enim materiam constituunt in verbis consensum exprimentibus: alii in ipso consensû; alii in personis, aut corporibus contrahentium; alii in ritibus quibusdam visibilibus, qui Ecclesiastica benedictione adhibentur: formam vero, vel in verbis contrahentium, quibus consensum declarant; vel in verbis à Sacerdote prolatis, &c.
units.tr: (4) Nor has any fixed form been prescribed by God for its administration. Hence the adversaries themselves differ widely in assigning the matter and form of this sacrament: some locate the matter in the words expressing consent, others in the consent itself, others in the persons or bodies of the contracting parties, others in certain visible rites used with ecclesiastical blessing; and the form they place either in the words of the contracting parties by which they declare their consent, or in the words spoken by the priest, etc.

units.la: Obj. 1. Ephes. 5, 32. dicitur vocatur Sacramentum. Ergo. Resp. Ibi Mysterium, pro quo Vulgata Versio habet Sacramentum, non ad Matrimonium ipsum; sed ad Spiritualem Christi cum Ecclesiâ unionem, refertur: quod etiam Cajetanus agnovit.
units.tr: Objection: Eph. 5:32 calls it a sacrament. Therefore, etc. Answer: There the word "mystery," for which the Vulgate has "sacrament," refers not to marriage itself but to the spiritual union of Christ with the Church; Cajetan also acknowledged this.

units.la: Obj. 2. 1 Tim. 2, 14. Servabitur tamen liberos gignendo, si manserint in fide, & charitate, ac sanctimoniâ, cum moderatione. Ex ista promissione salutis sequitur, Matrimonium esse Sacramentum. Resp. Apostolus ibi consolatur feminas adversûs molestias in liberorum procreatione: ita salutem iis promittit, si virtutibus ibi assignatis serio & constanter operam dederint: sed nullo modo dixit, ipsum Matrimonium istius salutis signum & sigillum esse; atque adeò Sacramentum.
units.tr: Objection: 1 Tim. 2:14, 15: "Yet she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness, with moderation." From this promise of salvation it follows that marriage is a sacrament. Answer: The Apostle there comforts women against the troubles of bearing children; he promises them salvation if they earnestly and constantly apply themselves to the virtues assigned there; but he by no means said that marriage itself is the sign and seal of that salvation, and so a sacrament.

units.la: LIX. Sed & Anabaptistæ quidam duobus veris Sacramentis accensent Lotionem pedum: quam etiàm inter Remonstrantes adoptavit Adolphus Venator. Hanc autem potissimùm probare conantur, ex Joh. 13, 4,16. Verum Christus ibi Sacramentum non instituit: sed lavando pedes Discipulorum suorum, isto exemplo ad quælibet officia charitatis sibi invicem humiliter præstanda, eos extimulare voluit; atque istâ occasione de spirituali ablutione ac puritate etiàm disseruit.
units.tr: LIX. Some Anabaptists also count among the two true sacraments the washing of feet, which Adolphus Venator also adopted among the Remonstrants. They try to prove this chiefly from John 13:4-16. But Christ did not institute a sacrament there; by washing his disciples' feet he wished to stir them, by this example, to perform humbly every office of charity towards one another, and on this occasion he also discoursed on spiritual cleansing and purity.

units.la: LX. Pro Praxi; 1. Exploremus nos ipsos, an Spiritum obsignantem verè habeamus: 2 Cor. 13, 5. cum 1, 21, 22. Eum ne extinguamus, quantum in nobis est: neque dolore afficiamus: 1 Thess. 5, 19. Eph. 4, 30.
units.tr: LX. For practice: (1) Let us examine ourselves, whether we truly have the sealing Spirit: 2 Cor. 13:5, compared with 1:21, 22. Let us not quench him, as far as in us lies, nor grieve him: 1 Thess. 5:19; Eph. 4:30.

units.la: 2. Qui baptizati sumus, speciatim verò in infantiâ, admirandam istam gratiam fœderalem, sic nobis applicatam & obsignatam, piâ animi oblectatione agnoscamus, & meditemur identidem: Act. 8, 39. II. 39. Psal. 20, 10, 11. Jugiter expendamus insitionem nostri in Christo, ad justificationis certitudinem subjectivam, & sanctificationis incrementum quotidianum: Rom. 6, 3,-6. atque item insitionem in corpore Ecclesiæ, ad mutuam parilem communionem bonorum salutarium, & praxin charitis non simulatæ: Gal. 3, 26,-29. Rom. 12, 3,-10. 1 Cor. 12, 12,-27. Eph. 4, 1,7, 13,-16.
units.tr: (2) Let us who have been baptized, especially in infancy, acknowledge and often meditate with pious delight on that wonderful covenant grace, so applied and sealed to us: Acts 8:39; 2:39; Ps. 20:10, 11. Let us constantly weigh our engrafting into Christ, for the subjective certainty of justification and the daily increase of sanctification: Rom. 6:3-6; and likewise our engrafting into the body of the Church, for mutual and equal communion of saving goods and the practice of unfeigned love: Gal. 3:26-29; Rom. 12:3-10; 1 Cor. 12:12-27; Eph. 4:1-7, 13-16.

units.la: 3. Ad usum Cœnæ Dominicæ, quoties occasio datur, debitè nos exploremus, præparemus, accedamus, cum pio desiderio: 1 Cor. xi, 28, 29. Luc. 22, 15. cum fame ac siti justitiæ Christi, & reliqui alimenti spiritualis: Matth. 5, 6. Apoc. 22, 17. cum Joh. 6, 27, 33, 35, 48, 50, 51, 53,-58.
units.tr: (3) Whenever an occasion is given for the use of the Lord's Supper, let us duly examine ourselves, prepare ourselves, and approach with a pious desire: 1 Cor. 11:28, 29; Luke 22:15; with hunger and thirst for the righteousness of Christ and for the rest of spiritual food: Matt. 5:6; Rev. 22:17; with John 6:27, 33, 35, 48, 50, 51, 53-58.

units.la: 4. Istam Corporis & Sanguinis Christi communionem rite æstimemus ac meditemur : 1 Cor. 10, 16. xi, 24, 25, 26. In eâ agnoscamus peccatorum remissionem, & totius N. T. ratificationem : Matth. 26: 26, 27, 28. 1 Cor. xi, 24, 25, 26. Hebr. 9, 15, -28. Sic in praxi vitæ spiritualis, ac verâ sanctimoniâ, corroboremur : Joh. 6, 33, -. 1 Cor. 10, 3, -12, xi, 20, -34. Hebr. 9, 13, 14. & ad mutuam charitatem excitemur : 1 Cor. 10, 17, xii, 13, -27.
units.tr: (4) Let us rightly esteem and meditate upon this communion in the body and blood of Christ: 1 Cor. 10:16; 11:24, 25, 26. In it let us acknowledge the remission of sins and the ratification of the whole New Testament: Matt. 26:26, 27, 28; 1 Cor. 11:24, 25, 26; Heb. 9:15-28. Thus let us be strengthened in the practice of spiritual life and true holiness: John 6:33 ff.; 1 Cor. 10:3-12; 11:20-34; Heb. 9:13, 14; and let us be stirred up to mutual love: 1 Cor. 10:17; 12:13-27.

units.la: 5. Quæ veris Sacramentis falsò & superstitiosè adjecta sunt, tanquàm characterem Bestiæ, refugiamus: Deut. 4, 2. v, 32. xii, 32. Gal. 1, 8, 9. iii, 15. Apoc. 13, 16, 17.
units.tr: (5) Let us shun whatever has been falsely and superstitiously added to the true sacraments, as the mark of the Beast: Deut. 4:2; 5:32; 12:32; Gal. 1:8, 9; 3:15; Rev. 13:16, 17.

units.la: CAP. XIX.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIX.

units.la: De Glorificatione.
units.tr: On Glorification.

units.la: Glorificatio, Actio realis. Termini. 1. Christi in eâ efficientia: & nexus cum aliis beneficiis, 2. Inchoatio ejus in hac vitâ. 3. Bona ejus. 4. Alii fructus. 5. Expectatio. Contrarium. 6. Consummatio. Mors fidelium. 7. Probatur beata existentia cum Christo. 8. De animabus impiorum. 9. Purgatorium Pontif. refut. 10. Objectiones solv. 11. Limbus Patrum refut. c. eosd. 12. Atque item Limbus infantium. 13. Glorificatio integrarum personarum. Gloriosa resuscitatio. Subjecta. Causa efficiens. 14. Duo actus. Prob. 15. Eorundem numero corporum: c. Socin. 16. Objectiones solv. 17. Transmutatio fidelium superstitum. 18. Resuscitatio improborum, etiam in iisdem corporibus. 19. Judicium extremum, Actus Christi Regis. Patres fidelium, 20. Judicandi Angeli; &
units.tr: Glorification: a real action. Terms. 1. Christ's efficiency in it, and its connection with the other benefits; 2. its inception in this life; 3. its good things; 4. other fruits; 5. Expectation. The contrary. 6. Consummation. The death of believers. 7. The blessed existence with Christ is proved. 8. Concerning the souls of the wicked. 9. The Papists' purgatory refuted. 10. Objections answered. 11. The Limbo of the Fathers refuted, with the same. 12. And likewise the Limbo of infants. 13. Glorification of whole persons. Glorious resurrection. Subjects. Efficient cause. 14. Two acts. Proved. 15. The numerical identity of the same bodies: with the Socinians. 16. Objections answered. 17. Transformation of believers still living. 18. Resurrection of the wicked, also in the same bodies. 19. The last judgment, the act of Christ the King. The Fathers of believers, 20. Angels to be judged; &

units.la: & Homines. 21. Sententia justificatoria. 22. Condemnatoria. 23. Tempus. Prædictiones. Locus. 24. Executio æterna in improbis. 25. Gradus pœnarum. Causa efficiens. Societas. Locus. 26. Objectiones solv. 27. Executio in fidelibus. Beatitudo qualis. 28. Societas. Locus. Duratio. 29. Quæ abfutura. Quæ adfutura. Gradus gloriæ. 30. Mundus non annihilandus. Obj. solv. 31. Praxis. 32.
units.tr: and men. 21. Sentence of justification. 22. Of condemnation. 23. Time. Predictions. Place. 24. Eternal execution upon the wicked. 25. Degrees of punishments. Efficient cause. Fellowship. Place. 26. Objections answered. 27. Execution upon believers. The blessedness of what kind. 28. Fellowship. Place. Duration. 29. What will pass away. What will remain. Degrees of glory. 30. The world not to be annihilated. Obj. answered. 31. Practice. 32.

units.la: I. Glorificatio
units.tr: I. Glorification

units.la: Uccedit, Glorificatio; actio realis, quâ homines redemti & justificati ex conditione miserâ & vili reipsâ transferuntur in statum gloriosum ac verè felicem. Rom. VIII, 30. Quos justificavit, eos etiam glorificavit.
units.tr: Next comes Glorification: a real action by which men redeemed and justified are transferred from a wretched and base condition in actual fact into a glorious and truly happy state. Rom. 8:30: Whom he justified, them he also glorified.

units.la: Actionem realem dicimus; quia realem transmutationem in iis hominibus efficit.
units.tr: We call it a real action, because it effects a real transformation in these men.

units.la: Terminus à quo, est conditio misera, vilis, & ignominiosa; per turpitudinem peccatorum. Rom. 3, 23, Omnes peccaverunt, ac deficiuntur gloriâ Dei. Hos. 4, 7. Gloriam eorum ignominiâ commutabo. Psal. 14, 3. Isef. 64, 6. Jerem. 3, 24, 25.
units.tr: The terminus a quo is a wretched, base, and shameful condition, arising from the foulness of sins. Rom. 3:23: All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God. Hos. 4:7: I will change their glory into shame. Ps. 14:3. Isa. 64:6. Jer. 3:24, 25.

units.la: Terminus ad quem, est status felix, bonorum (præcipuè spiritualium ac cœlestium) copiâ affluens, & maxime gloriosus: Psal. 33, 12. Beata gens, cujus Jehovah est Deus; populus, quem elegit hæreditatem sibi. XXXVI, 8, 9, 10. Eph. 1, 3. 2 Cor. 3, 18. 1 Petr. 1, 8.
units.tr: The terminus ad quem is a happy state, abounding in good things (chiefly spiritual and heavenly) and most glorious: Ps. 33:12: Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people whom he chose as his inheritance. Ps. 36:8, 9, 10. Eph. 1:3. 2 Cor. 3:18. 1 Pet. 1:8.

units.la: II. Hanc salutem nobis impetravit, atque etiam nunc in humanâ quoque naturâ exaltatus καθ' οἰκονομίαν efficaciter applicat, Christus: Matth. 20, 28, Filius hominis - dedit animam suam redemtionis pretium pro multis. 1 Tim. 2, 5, 6. Eph. 1, 5,-8, 12. 1 Petr. 1, 18, 19. Ista autem gloria, licet in Justificatione nobis adjudicetur ; tamen per hanc actionem in nos confertur realiter : unde hæc metonymice quoque Redemtio appellatur, Rom. 8, 21, 23. Eph. 4, 30. Ad hanc etiam vocati sumus: 2 Petr. 1, 3. Vocavit nos ad gloriam ac virtutem. Quodque per Regenerationem primum in nobis productum est; per Sanctificationem vero, Conservationem, & Corroborationem continuatur & perficitur; & per Obsignationem ad subjectivam certitudinem magis applicatur; idem, quatenus decorem, felicitatem, & gloriam in se continet, ad præsentem hanc actionem quoque pertinet.
units.tr: II. Christ has obtained this salvation for us, and even now, exalted in human nature [according to the economy, καθ' οἰκονομίαν], he effectively applies it. Matt. 20:28: The Son of man ... gave his life as a ransom for many. 1 Tim. 2:5, 6. Eph. 1:5–8, 12. 1 Pet. 1:18, 19. Now this glory, although it is adjudged to us in justification, is nevertheless conferred on us in reality through this action; hence it is also called by metonymy redemption: Rom. 8:21, 23. Eph. 4:30. We are also called to it: 2 Pet. 1:3: He called us to glory and virtue. And what is first produced in us through regeneration, and is continued and perfected through sanctification, preservation, and strengthening, and is more fully applied to our subjective certainty through sealing, that same thing, insofar as it contains in itself beauty, happiness, and glory, belongs also to the present action.

units.la: III. Spectanda est Glorificatio, tum ut inchoata in hac vita; tum ut perfecta post hanc vitam..
units.tr: III. Glorification is to be considered both as begun in this life and as perfected after this life.

units.la: In hac vita consistit in restaurata imagine Dei, & inchoata conformitate Christi; quæ utique gloriosa est. Hinc 1 Cor.xi,7. conjunguntur Imago & Gloria. Confer Rom. 3, 23. Hæc est præsens quædam beatitudo, & vita æternum duratura. Vide Rom. 4, 5. Matth. 5, 3,-11. Joh. 3, 36. xvii, 3. Confer Eph. 4, 18.
units.tr: In this life it consists in the restored image of God and the begun conformity to Christ, which is certainly glorious. Hence in 1 Cor. 11:7 image and glory are joined. Compare Rom. 3:23. This is a present kind of blessedness, and eternal life that will endure. See Rom. 4:5; Matt. 5:3–11; John 3:36; 17:3. Compare Eph. 4:18.
1 John 3:15.

units.la: In hac vita gloriosa inest viva apprehensio & certus sensus, amoris Dei; ex unione & communione, quam cum Ipso habemus per Christum: 1 Joh. 1, 1, 3, 4.-Communio nostra fuit cum Patre; & cum Filio ejus Jesu Christo.
units.tr: In this life there is a glorious living apprehension and a certain sense of the love of God, arising from the union and communion which we have with him through Christ: 1 John 1:1, 3, 4: Our communion is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.

units.la: IV. In ista unione & communione inest 1. maxime sublimis ac beatissima Amicitia, & Familiaritas: Joh. 15, 15. Vos dixi amicos. Jac. 2, 23. Amicus Dei vocatus est. Eph. 2, 19. III, 15.
units.tr: IV. In this union and communion there is, first, a most sublime and most blessed friendship and familiarity: John 15:15: I have called you friends. James 2:23: He was called the friend of God. Eph. 2:19; 3:15.

units.la: 2. Participatio locupletissima spiritualium donorum gratiæ: Col. 2, 2, 7, 10. Ipsis charitate compactis, & omni opulentia certioratæ intelligentia, &c. atque ita amplus introitus in Regnum Dei: 2 Petr. 1. 8, 11.
units.tr: Second, a most abundant participation in the spiritual gifts of grace: Col. 2:2, 7, 10: knit together in love, and enriched with all the riches of full assurance of understanding, etc. And thus an abundant entrance into the kingdom of God: 2 Pet. 1:8, 11.

units.la: 3. Beatissima experientia benevolentiæ ac beneficentiæ Divinæ: Psal. 31. 20. Quam multum est Bonum Tuum, quod seposuisti timentibus Te! &c. lxv, 5. Nehem. 2. 8. Rom. 8, 28.
units.tr: Third, a most blessed experience of the goodwill and beneficence of God: Ps. 31:20: How great is your goodness, which you have laid up for those who fear you! etc. Ps. 65:5. Neh. 2:8. Rom. 8:28.

units.la: 4. Subjectiva certitudo perseverantiæ ac salutis æternæ : Rom. 8, 38, 39. Cui adjungitur indubitata spes gloriæ cœlestis: Rom. 5, 2. & libertas in omni necessitate adeundi ad Deum cum fiducia : Eph. 2, 18. III, 12. Hebr. 4, 16. X, 22.
units.tr: Fourth, subjective certainty of perseverance and of eternal salvation: Rom. 8:38, 39. To this is added the undoubting hope of heavenly glory: Rom. 5:2, and freedom in every need to approach God with confidence: Eph. 2:18; 3:12; Heb. 4:16; 10:22.

units.la: V. Ex superioribus sequuntur alii fructus præclari: utpote Consolatio adversus mala tristia : estque doloris aut metûs opprimentis relevatio, per auxilia in Christo, tum suppeditata, tum promissa: 2 Cor. 1, 3, 4, 5.Per Christum redundat consolatio nostra. Joh. 16, 33, 1 Joh. 5, 4. Rom. 8, 37. Col. 2, 2 Isaí. 40, 1.
units.tr: V. From what has been said there follow other splendid fruits: namely, consolation against sad evils; and it is a relief from grief or fear that weighs us down, through the helps in Christ, both those already supplied and those promised: 2 Cor. 1:3–5: Through Christ our consolation abounds. John 16:33; 1 John 5:4; Rom. 8:37; Col. 2:2; Isa. 40:1.

units.la: Per universam vitam hominis fideles se porrò diffundunt solida Pax & Gaudium. Rom. 14, 17. Regnum Dei est Pax & Gaudium.
units.tr: Through the whole life of a man, solid peace and joy spread further among believers. Rom. 14:17: The kingdom of God is peace and joy.

units.la: Pax ista est animi tranquillitas in Deo & Christo, ratione salutis jam inchoatæ, & postmodum consummandæ: Phil 4, 7. Pax illa Dei, quæ superat omnem mentem, præsidio custodiet corda vestra, & cogitationes vestras, in Christo Iesu. Ephef. 2, 14 Confer Ief. 9, 6. Joh. 14, 27.
units.tr: This peace is tranquillity of mind in God and Christ, on account of the salvation already begun and afterwards to be completed: Phil. 4:7: The peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus. Eph. 2:14. Compare Isa. 9:6; John 14:27.

units.la: Gaudium verò est animi delectatio in unione & communione summi boni : 1 Joh. 1, 3, 4. Communio nostra sit cum Patre, & cum Filio ejus Iesû Christo. Et hæc scribimus vobis, ut Gaudium vestrum sit plenum. Phil. 4, 4. Gaudete in Domino semper. 1 Petr. 1, 7, 8, Psal. 4, 7. 8. Luc. 10, 20. cum Matth. 25, 21, 23. Joh. 16, 11.
units.tr: Joy, however, is delight of the mind in the union and communion of the highest good: 1 John 1:3, 4: Our communion is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ. And we write these things to you, so that your joy may be full. Phil. 4:4: Rejoice in the Lord always. 1 Pet. 1:7, 8. Ps. 4:7, 8. Luke 10:20, compared with Matt. 25:21, 23. John 16:11.

units.la: VI. Ista igitur est Glorificatio inchoata; Primitiæ Spiritus; Rom. 8, 23. messem plenam certissimè promittentes, atque in adversis nos subsistere & victoriam obtinere facientes : 1 Petr. 4, 14.
units.tr: VI. This, then, is the glorification begun: the first-fruits of the Spirit, Rom. 8:23, most certainly promising the full harvest, and making us stand firm in adversities and obtain the victory: 1 Pet. 4:14.

units.la: Contraria est conditio impiorum; vere turpis, impura, vilis, ignominiosa. Deo omnibusque sanctis abominabilis. Hinc adjuncta & effecta tristissima, inquietudo, terror, desperatio, exitium denique omnium eorum qui in eo statu perseverant. Isf. 48,21. Non est pax (dicit Iehovah) impiis. lvii,20,21. Prov. 28, 1. Fugiunt, tametsi nemo persequatur. Psal. 73, 18, 19, 20. Iudæ, 13. Rom. 1,28. II, 15. Eph. 4,18,19. Ioh. 8, 14. Prov, 1, 26, 27; 31, 32.
units.tr: The contrary is the condition of the wicked: truly foul, impure, base, and shameful, and abominable to God and to all the saints. Hence the very sad accompaniments and effects: restlessness, terror, despair, and finally the ruin of all who persist in that state. Isa. 48:21: There is no peace, says the Lord, for the wicked.
