Isa. 57:20, 21. Prov. 28:1: They flee, though no one pursues. Ps. 73:18, 19, 20. Jude 13. Rom. 1:28; 2:15. Eph. 4:18, 19. John 8:14. Prov. 1:26, 27; 31:32.

units.la: VII. Post hanc vitam consummabitur Glorificatio: Fiberabimur enim ab omni imperfectione in anima & in corpore, atque omnis perfectio nobis communicabitur: 1 Cor. 13,9,10,12. Ex parte cognoscimus: --Postquam autem advenerit quod perfectum est; tunc quod est aliquatenus, abolebitur. &c. 2: 5,1,-8.
units.tr: VII. After this life the glorification will be completed: for we shall be freed from every imperfection in soul and body, and all perfection will be communicated to us: 1 Cor. 13:9, 10, 12: We know in part ... but when what is perfect has come, then what is partial will be done away with, etc. 2 Cor. 5:1–8.

units.la: Hæc autem Glorificatio spectanda est tum in anima separata, tum in persona integra.
units.tr: This glorification is to be considered both in the separated soul and in the whole person.

units.la: Mors temporaria & corporalis adhuc evenit fidelibus; non tamen ut poena stricte dicta; sed ut transitus in vitam æternam, & depositio reliquiarum peccati. Atque ita gradatim salus applicatur. Plenissima autem applicatio fiet novissimo die: Rom. 8, 10, 11. 1 Cor. 15, 20, 22, 23; 26. Infidelium alia est ratio, super quos ira Dei permanet: Ioh. 3, 36. & quos ea occupavit ad extremum usque; 1 Thess. II, 16.
units.tr: Temporal and bodily death still comes to believers; yet not as punishment strictly so called, but as a passage into eternal life and a laying aside of the remnants of sin. And thus salvation is applied by degrees. The fullest application, however, will take place on the last day: Rom. 8:10, 11. 1 Cor. 15:20, 22, 23, 26. The case of unbelievers is different, on whom the wrath of God remains: John 3:36. and whom it has seized to the very end: 1 Thess. 2:16.

units.la: VIII. Sic igitur animæ fidelium, a corporibus suis separatæ, a reliquiis peccatorum, aliarumque miserarum, pro sua parte liberantur, & ad perfectionem sanctitatis ac gloriæ, cum Christo apud Deum in cœlo percipiendam, statim transeunt. Hinc 1. Eccl. 12, 7. Revertitur pulvis in terram; & spiritus ad Deum, qui dedit illum. Quod de singulis quidem morientibus accipiendum; de fidelibus autem, ut vero statui gloriæ convenit. De his speciales, Isf. 57, 2. Ingredietur in pace, requiescent in cubilibus suis, &c. Hebr. 12, 23. Spiritus justorum consummatorum. Apoc. 14, 13. Beati ab hoc tempore mortui, ii qui in Domino moriuntur. Etiam dicit Spiritus: ut requiescant a laboribus suis, &c. Ioh. 5, 24. Qui credit-, habet vitam æternam; & in condemnationem non veniet : sed transijt à morte in vitam.
units.tr: VIII. Thus the souls of the faithful, separated from their bodies, are freed from the remnants of sin and from other miseries, each in its own measure, and at once pass on to receive perfection of holiness and glory, to be enjoyed with Christ before God in heaven. Hence: 1. Eccl. 12, 7. The dust returns to the earth, and the spirit returns to God who gave it. This is to be understood of dying men in general, but of the faithful it holds true in the way that befits their state of glory. Special texts concerning them are: Isa. 57, 2. They shall enter into peace; they shall rest in their beds, etc. Heb. 12, 23. The spirits of just men made perfect. Rev. 14, 13. Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on. Yes, says the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours, etc. John 5, 24. Whoever believes in me has eternal life, and shall not come into condemnation, but has passed from death to life.

units.la: 2. Huc pertinent exempla, Latronis post mortem statim in Paradisum migrantis, Luc. 23,43. cum verf. 46. & 2 Cor. 12, 3, 4, Animarum eorum, qui mactati fuerant propter Verbum Dei, -. Clamabant autem voce magna ; dicentes ; Usque quo, &c. Tum datæ sunt singulis stolæ albæ ; & dictum est, ut requiescerent adhuc paululum temporis, &c. Apoc. 6, 9, 10, 11. Confer vii, 9, 16, 14. Item Luc. 16, 22, 25, 27;-31. de animâ Lazari ab Angelis in sinum Abrahæ transportati, &c.
units.tr: 2. To this belong the examples of the thief who went straight into Paradise after death, Luke 23, 43, and of 2 Cor. 12, 3, 4; the souls of those who had been slain for the Word of God: They cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, etc. Then white robes were given to each of them, and it was said that they should rest a little while longer, etc. Rev. 6, 9, 10, 11. Compare Rev. 7, 9, 16, 14. Likewise Luke 16, 22, 25, 27-31, concerning the soul of Lazarus, carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom, etc.

units.la: 3. Accedit fides solida, & certa spes, filiorum Dei. Hanc exprimit Apostolus, Phil. I, 21,-24. - Constrictus utrimque teneor, desiderio tendens ad dimissionem, & ut cum Christo sim. & 2 Cor. 5, 1,-8.
units.tr: 3. Add the firm faith and certain hope of the sons of God. The Apostle expresses this in Phil. 1, 21-24. I am hard pressed on both sides, desiring to depart and be with Christ. and 2 Cor. 5, 1-8.

units.la: IX. De animabus vero impiorum, secundum SS. Literas dicendum,
units.tr: IX. Concerning the souls of the wicked, however, we must speak according to the Holy Scriptures,

units.la: quod post separationem à corporibus justo Dei judicio ablegentur in infernum : atque illic cruciatus & poenas peccatorum suorum perserant, Hinc 1. ratione loci, Judas proditor dicitur abiisse in suum locum, Act. 1,25. Ac similiter damnatus epulo, in locum tormenti venisse; Luc. 16. 28. Itemque 1 Petr. 3, 19, 20. memorantur spiritus existentes in carcere, - qui olim non paruerunt sermoni. Confer 2 Petr. II, 4.
units.tr: that after their separation from their bodies, by the just judgment of God, they are cast into hell, and there they endure the torments and punishments of their sins. Hence, 1. as to place: Judas the traitor is said to have gone to his own place, Acts 1, 25. Likewise the rich man who feasted came into the place of torment; Luke 16, 28. Also 1 Pet. 3, 19, 20 speaks of spirits in prison, who formerly did not obey the word. Compare 2 Pet. 2, 4.

units.la: 2. Ratione vero cruciatuum & poenarum, quales videl. naturæ spirituali conveniunt; Sodoma & Gomorra, iisque finitimæ civitates, h. e. animæ illorum hominum, dicuntur sustinere poenam ignis æterni. Et Epulo, gravissime cruciatus in flamma: Luc. 16, 23, 24, 25.
units.tr: 2. As to the torments and punishments, which are such as befit a spiritual nature: Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities near them, that is, the souls of those men, are said to suffer the punishment of eternal fire. And the rich man, in anguish in the flame: Luke 16, 23, 24, 25.

units.la: 3. Neque omittenda gravis præmonitio Christi, de metuendo Illo, qui postquam interemit corpus, potestatem habet conjiciendi in gehennam; Luc. 12, 4, 5.
units.tr: 3. Nor should we omit Christ's grave warning about fearing him who, after he has killed the body, has power to cast into hell; Luke 12, 4, 5.

units.la: Obi. Eccl. III, 19,20,21. dicuntur filii hominum mori, sicuti animal, &c. Resp. Id intelligendum est de accidentibus externis & visibilibus, in morte hominum & bestiarum. Quod vero conditio hominum coram Deo, plurimum differat à conditione bestiarum, satis patet ex verf. 17. Iustum & impium judicabit Deus. ac porro, XI, 9. XII, 7, 12, 13.
units.tr: Objection. Eccl. 3, 19, 20, 21 says that the sons of men die as the beasts do, etc. Answer: this must be understood of the outward and visible circumstances in the death of men and beasts. That the condition of men before God differs very greatly from that of beasts is clear enough from verse 17: God shall judge the just and the wicked. And further, Eccl. 11, 9; 12, 7, 12, 13.

units.la: X. Pontifici pro fidelibus, qui in peccatis venialibus moriuntur, statuunt locum aliquem intermedium, ubi pro culpa sua justitiae Divinae satisfaciant, & per poenas purgentur; donec postea ad coelestem beatitudinem admittantur. Purgatorium appellant; & carcerem aliquem subterraneum, inferno proximum, aut contiguum, existimant. Sed 1. Scriptura tantum duo loca animarum separatarum agnoscit, unum gloriae, alterum damnationis, atque indicat, unumquemque permanere in eo loco, in quem statim à morte transfit. Eccl. XI, 3. Si ceciderit arbor ad Austrum, sive ad Aquilonem; in quem locum ceciderit ipsa arbor, ibi erit.
units.tr: X. For the faithful who die in venial sins, the Papists posit some intermediate place where, for their guilt, they satisfy the divine justice and are cleansed through punishments, until they are afterwards admitted to heavenly blessedness. They call it Purgatory, and think it is some subterranean prison, close to or adjoining hell. But, first, Scripture recognises only two places for separated souls, one of glory and the other of damnation, and indicates that each remains in the place to which it passes immediately at death. Eccl. 11, 3. If a tree falls toward the south or toward the north, wherever the tree falls, there it will lie.

units.la: 2. Christus plenissime pro peccatis electorum justitiae Divinae satisfecit; adeo quidem ut nulla satisfactio ab iis exigi possit. Hebr. 10, 14-18. Unica oblatione Christus in perpetuum Consummavit eos qui sanctificantur. Et quia per Christi satisfactionem exstinctus est omnium peccatorum nostrorum reatus, sanguis ejus dicitur nos Purificare ab Omni peccato; 1 Joh. 1, 7. Nullum ergo peccatum reliquum est, à quo purgari deberemus tali Igne purgatorio.
units.tr: 2. Christ fully satisfied the divine justice for the sins of the elect, so completely that no satisfaction can be required of them. Heb. 10, 14-18. By one offering Christ has perfected for ever those who are sanctified. And since the guilt of all our sins has been removed by Christ's satisfaction, his blood is said to cleanse us from all sin; 1 John 1, 7. There is therefore no remaining sin from which we would need to be cleansed by such purgatorial fire.

units.la: 3. Idem patet ex natura Justificationis, quae plenam remissionem omnium peccatorum complectitur; adeo ut nulla amplius pro iis satisfactio exigenda sit. Rom. IV, 6, 7, 8. Sicut etiam David (Psal. 32, 1, 2.) Declarat beatum eum hominem, cui Deus imputat justitiam absque operibus: dicens; Beati, quibus remissae sunt Legis transgressiones; & quorum tecta sunt peccata, -. V, 1, 2. Iustificati igitur ex fide, pacem habemus apud Deum, -. 9. Iustificati nunc Ejus sanguine, ne, servabimur multò magis per Eum ab ira, VIII, 1. Nulla nunc est condemnatio iis qui sunt in Christo Iesu. Ergò nec temporalis illa condemnatio in Purgatorio. 33, 34. Quis intentabit crimina, &c.
units.tr: 3. The same is clear from the nature of justification, which embraces the full remission of all sins, so that no further satisfaction for them is to be required. Rom. 4, 6, 7, 8. As David also (Ps. 32, 1, 2) declares that man blessed to whom God imputes righteousness without works, saying: Blessed are those whose transgressions of the law are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Rom. 5, 1, 2. Therefore, being justified by faith, we have peace with God. 9. Since we are now justified by his blood, we shall be saved much more through him from wrath. Rom. 8, 1. There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. Therefore neither is that temporal condemnation in Purgatory. 33, 34. Who shall bring charges, etc.

units.la: 4. Distinctio peccatorum in mortalia & venialia, quæ Purgatorio substernitur, caret fundamento; & confutata est sup. cap. 10. th. 43.
units.tr: 4. The distinction of sins into mortal and venial, on which Purgatory is founded, lacks foundation, and it has been refuted above, chap. 10, th. 43.

units.la: XI. Obj. Matth. 5, 25, 26. Christus loquitur de carcere; unde qui in eum essent conjecti, non forent liberandi ante persolutum ultimum quadrantem: iste autem est Purgatorium: ex inferno enim nulla unquàm fit liberatio. Resp. Sed minimè dicit, homines post hanc vitam posse ultimum istum quadrantem persolvere; & sic liberari: ad ipsum igitur infernum istud pertinet.
units.tr: XI. Objection. Matt. 5, 25, 26. Christ is speaking of a prison; hence those who were cast into it would not be freed before the last farthing was paid. But this is Purgatory, for no one is ever released from hell. Answer: He does not at all say that men can pay that last farthing after this life and so be released; therefore that passage pertains to hell itself.

units.la: Obj. 2. 1 Cor. 3, 15. Ipse verò servabitur, itâ tamen ut per ignem. Scil. Purgatorium. Resp. Apostolus allegoricè loquitur de Doctoribus, solido ac salutari fundamento Christo superstruentibus vel doctrinas veras & utiles, vel incertas & inutiles - futurum autem, ut cujusque opus manifestum fiat, ut dies ipsum declaret, & ignis probet ac retegat. Verum iste non est ignis purgatorius & poenalis post hanc vitam; sed probatorius etiam in hoc sæculo; dum opus Ministerii probabitur deinceps, per ipsum Verbum Dei, Spiritu efficaciter cooperante. Confer Jerem. 23. 29. Mal. III, 2, 3. Matth. III, 11. Interim salvandi sunt, quamvis ægrè, qui fundamentum retinuerint. Confer Am. 4, 11. Zach. III, 2. 1 Petr. 4, 18.
units.tr: Objection 2. 1 Cor. 3, 15. Yet he himself shall be saved, but so as through fire. That is, Purgatory. Answer: the Apostle speaks allegorically of teachers who build upon the solid and saving foundation, Christ, either true and useful doctrines or uncertain and useless ones; the work of each will become manifest, for the day will declare it, and the fire will test and reveal it. But this is not a purgatorial and penal fire after this life; it is a testing fire even in this age, since the work of the ministry will be tested henceforth by the Word of God itself, with the Spirit effectively cooperating. Compare Jer. 23, 29; Mal. 3, 2, 3; Matt. 3, 11. Meanwhile, those who have held fast to the foundation are to be saved, though with difficulty. Compare Amos 4, 11; Zech. 3, 2; 1 Pet. 4, 18.

units.la: Obj. 3. Phil. II, 10. In nomine Iesu flectentur etiam genua subterraneorum. Hoc est, in Purgatorio laborantium. Resp. Indicatur ibi subjectio omnium creaturarum, etiam hostium, & damnatorum, ad Christum. Confer Gen. 41, 43. Esth. 3, 2. Item Psal. 72, 9, 11. 1 Cor. 15, 25, 26, 27. Job. 5, 27, 28, 29.
units.tr: Objection 3. Phil. 2, 10. At the name of Jesus every knee shall bow, even of those under the earth. That is, of those who suffer in Purgatory. Answer: what is indicated there is the subjection of all creatures, even enemies and the damned, to Christ. Compare Gen. 41, 43; Esth. 3, 2. Likewise Ps. 72, 9, 11; 1 Cor. 15, 25, 26, 27; Job 5, 27, 28, 29.

units.la: XII. Præter istud Purgatorium, duos insuper Limbos bos infernales falsò statuunt Pontificii; unum Patrum appellant, alterum Infantium. Limbum Patrum reliquis Inferni partibus, aut receptaculis, superiorem reputant; in quo patres, five fideles V. T. fuerint detenti, donec per Christi ad inferos descensum ex eo liberarentur.
units.tr: XII. Besides this Purgatory, the Papists falsely posit two further infernal Limbos: one they call the Limbo of the Fathers, the other the Limbo of Infants. They consider the Limbo of the Fathers to be higher than the other parts or receptacles of hell, and to be the place where the fathers, or the faithful of the Old Testament, were held until they were freed from it through Christ's descent into the underworld.

units.la: Verum 1. S. Scriptura talem locum non agnoscit.
units.tr: But, first, Holy Scripture does not recognise any such place.

units.la: 2. Satisfactio & Meritum Christi ἐφ' ἅπαξ etiam in istius temporis fidelibus efficax fuit: Ipsius Christus heri, & hodie idem est, & in saecula; Hebr. 13, 8. Confer Act. 15, 10, 11.
units.tr: 2. The satisfaction and merit of Christ, once for all [ἐφ' ἅπαξ], was effective also for the faithful of that time: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and for ever; Heb. 13, 8. Compare Acts 15, 10, 11.

units.la: 3. Quia fideles illi etiam justificati sunt per fidem: atque adeo non solum ab omni damnatione immunes fuerunt; sed etiam jus habuerunt ad ipsam coelestem beatitudinem. Sic de Abrahamo, Iac. II, 23. Credidit Abraham Deo; & imputatum est ei ad justitiam, & amicus Dei vocatus est. Confer Rom. IV, 1, - 5, 6, - 9. VIII, 30.
units.tr: 3. Those faithful men were also justified through faith, and so they were not only free from all condemnation but also had a right to the heavenly blessedness itself. So of Abraham: Jas. 2, 23. Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness, and he was called the friend of God. Compare Rom. 4, 1, 5, 6, 9; 8, 30.

units.la: 4. Christus localiter ad Limbum illum infernalem non descendit. Vide sup. cap. 12. th. 57.
units.tr: 4. Christ did not descend locally into that infernal Limbo. See above, chap. 12, th. 57.

units.la: Obj. 1. Zach. 9, 11. Emisi vinctos tuos de cisterna, in quā non est aqua. Hoc autem pertinet ad istum Limbum. Resp. Proximè pertinet ad liberationem ex captivitate Babylonicā; ac porrò ex omni miseriā spirituali, juxta Euangelium.
units.tr: Obj. 1. Zech. 9, 11: I have sent forth your prisoners out of the pit in which there is no water. This, however, refers to that Limbo. Resp. It refers rather to deliverance from the Babylonian captivity, and further, according to the Gospel, from every spiritual misery.

units.la: Obj. 2. 1 Sam. 28, 11, -. Pythonissa produxit Samuelem; non ex Coelo, sed ex Limbo. Ergò. Resp. Non Samuelem, aut ejus animam; sed Satanam, qui Prophetae personam mentiebatur: neque enim talis vir, ut Samuel, in potestate Diaboli & hominum nefariorum fuit post mortem suam. Vide Isf. 57, 2. Nec Deus Sauli respondere voluit per media ordinaria: 1 Sam. 28, 11, 15. nedum per Prophetam mortuum. Vide Isf. 8, 19, 20. Luc. 16, 30, 31. cum 2 Cor. XI, 14. Metaphoricè autem vocatur Samuel: propter imaginem, aut similitudinem.
units.tr: Obj. 2. 1 Sam. 28, 11: the witch of Endor brought up Samuel, not from heaven but from Limbo. Therefore... Resp. It was not Samuel, or his soul, but Satan, who pretended to be the person of the prophet. For a man such as Samuel was not, after his death, in the power of the Devil and of wicked men. See Isa. 57, 2. Nor did God wish to answer Saul through ordinary means, 1 Sam. 28, 11, 15, much less through a dead prophet. See Isa. 8, 19, 20; Luke 16, 30, 31, compared with 2 Cor. 11, 14. He is called Samuel only metaphorically, on account of the image or likeness.

units.la: XIII. Lim-
units.tr: XIII. Lim-

units.la: XIII. Limbum Infantium fingunt receptaculum infernale, in quo infantes sine Baptismo mortui, poenam damni tantum, vel exigui saltem sensus, ferant.
units.tr: XIII. They imagine a Limbo of Infants, an infernal receptacle in which infants who die without Baptism bear only the penalty of loss, or at least of a slight sense of pain.

units.la: Verùm 1. Scriptura nihil de isto loco tradit.
units.tr: But, first, Scripture says nothing about this place.

units.la: 2. Si infantes verè foederati fuerint, salutem iis promisit Deus: quae gratia ad Baptismum jam praesupponitur; non demùm per illum confertur.
units.tr: Second, if infants have truly been within the covenant, God has promised them salvation. This grace is already presupposed before Baptism; it is not conferred for the first time through it.

units.la: XIV. Succedit Glorificatio integrarum personarum, ad quam pertinent Gloriosa fidelium defunctorum Resuscitatio, publica eorundem in extremo judicio Justificatio, & Sententiae istius Executio aeterna ac beata.
units.tr: XIV. There follows the Glorification of whole persons, to which belong the glorious resurrection of the dead faithful, their public justification at the last judgment, and the eternal and blessed execution of that sentence.

units.la: Resuscitatio illa erit actio potens & gloriosa Christi, quâ Ipse cadavera omnium & singulorum fidelium suorum, quantumvis in pulverem redacta & dispersa, in consummatione saeculi restituet, gloriâ condecorabit, & animabus suis corpora singula reduniet, ad perfectam beatitudinem.
units.tr: That resurrection will be a powerful and glorious act of Christ, by which He himself, at the consummation of the age, will restore the corpses of all and each of his faithful, however much they have been reduced to dust and scattered, will adorn them with glory, and will reunite each body with its own soul, for perfect blessedness.

units.la: Subjecta recipientia Resuscitationis hujus gloriosae erunt cadavera Hominum fidelium; eaque omnia & singula. Matth. 10, 28. Trucidant corpus; animam autem non possunt trucidare. Joh. 5, 28, 29. Quia in monumentis sunt, audient vocem Ejus. Et prodibunt, qui bona fecerint, in resurrectionem vitae. Item Luc. xx. 36. Filii sunt Dei, cùm sint filii resurrectionis. Rom. 8, 29, 30. Nam quos praescivit, etiam praedestinavit conformandos imagini Filii sui; quos autem justificavit, eos etiam glorificavit.
units.tr: The subjects receiving this glorious resurrection will be the corpses of the faithful men, all and each of them. Matt. 10, 28: They kill the body, but cannot kill the soul. John 5, 28, 29: Because they are in the tombs, they shall hear his voice. And those who have done good shall come forth to the resurrection of life. Likewise Luke 20, 36: They are sons of God, since they are sons of the resurrection. Rom. 8, 29, 30: For whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son; and whom he justified, them he also glorified.

units.la: Causa efficiens primò est Deus: 1 Sam. 11, 6. Jehovah vivificat: Rom. 4, 17. 2 Cor. 1, 9. 1 Tim. 4, 18. Atque ita competit hoc opus Patri, Filio, & Spiritui Sancto: Joh. 5, 21. Rom. VIII, 11. per Divinam omnipotentiam: Ephes. 1, 19, 20. Phil. III, 21. κατ' ἐνέργειαν vero istud opus tribuitur Christo Mediatori, qui istam gloriam impetravit; sic ipse à mortuis resurrexit; & membra sua etiam suscitabit: Ioh. xi, 26. Dixit ei Icfus; Ego sum resurrectio & vita; qui credit in Me, etiamsi mortuus fuerit, vivet. Vide etiam Ioh. 5,26,-29. Ephes. II, 5, 6. 1 Cor. 15, 20,-23. Hanc suam virtutem demonstravit Christus in miraculosa resuscitatione Lazari; Ioh. xi, 23,27, 40,-44. adolescentis filii matris viduae; Luc. 7, 11,15. adolescentulae filiae Jairi; viii, 49,-54. & multorum sanctorum praedefunctorum circa mortem Christi; Matth. 28, 52, 53. Confer Actor. 9, 37,-41. xx,-9,-12. Item 1 Reg. 17, 17,-23: 2, iv, 20, 32,-37. xiii, 20, 21.
units.tr: The efficient cause is first God: 1 Sam. 11, 6: Jehovah gives life; Rom. 4, 17; 2 Cor. 1, 9; 1 Tim. 4, 18. Thus this work belongs to the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit: John 5, 21; Rom. 8, 11, through divine omnipotence: Eph. 1, 19, 20; Phil. 3, 21. But this work is ascribed, according to the working [κατ' ἐνέργειαν], to Christ the Mediator, who obtained this glory; so he himself rose from the dead, and he will also raise up his members: John 11, 26: Jesus said to her, I am the resurrection and the life; he who believes in me, even if he has died, shall live. See also John 5, 26-29; Eph. 2, 5, 6; 1 Cor. 15, 20-23. Christ showed this power of his in the miraculous raising of Lazarus, John 11, 23, 27, 40-44; of the son of the widowed mother, Luke 7, 11-15; of the daughter of Jairus, when she was a young girl, 8, 49-54; and of many saints who had died before, around the death of Christ, Matt. 27, 52, 53. Compare Acts 9, 37-41; 20, 9-12. Likewise 1 Kings 17, 17-23; 2 Kings 4, 20, 32-37; 13, 20, 21.

units.la: XV. Ad modum resuscitationis pertinent duo actus. Prior est ipsa revivificatio: & completitur cadaverum recollectionem; animarum propriarum iteratam cum illis unionem; atque ita veram illorum per has informationem; & quidem talem, ut ipsae personae integrae deinceps futurae sint, etiam ratione ipsorum corporum, immortales, incorruptibiles, gloriosae. Posterior est vivificatorum egressus in occursus Domini. Illustris est illa visio quae Ezechieli exhibita fuit, xxxvii, 1,-10. Officium siccorum, quae colligebantur, vivificabantur, &c. Confer Apoc. xx. 12, 13. Atque ipse Christus, Ioh. 5, 28, 29. Veniet hora, qua omnes, qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem Ejus. Et prodibunt, qui bona fecerint, in resurrectionem vitae. Adde 1 Cor. 15, 37,-44. 1 Thess. iv. 14, 16.
units.tr: XV. Two acts belong to the manner of resurrection. The first is the revivification itself, which is completed by the gathering of the corpses, the renewed union of each with its own soul, and thus the true informing of them by these souls; and indeed in such a way that the persons themselves, whole, will afterwards be immortal, incorruptible, and glorious, even as regards their bodies. The second is the going forth of the revived to meet the Lord. That vision shown to Ezekiel is illustrious, Ezek. 37, 1-10: the dry bones which were gathered together and made alive, etc. Compare Rev. 20, 12, 13. And Christ himself, John 5, 28, 29: The hour is coming, in which all who are in the tombs shall hear his voice. And those who have done good shall come forth to the resurrection of life. Add 1 Cor. 15, 37-44; 1 Thess. 4, 14, 16.

units.la: Ista autem resuscitatio fiet in consummatione saeculi, in adventu Domini, &c. Magnum hoc fidei mysterium ut contra Infideles afferimus; sic aliquot Argumentorum classibus probandum est. Huc pertinent 1. evidentissima quaedam effata V. T. utpote Dan. 12, 1, 2, 3. Multi dormientium in pulvere terrae expergiscentur; hi ad vitam aeternam, &c. Adde Job. 19, 25, 26, 27. Et Psal. 16, 9, 10. quae prophetia sic ad Christum pertinet, ut ad membra Ipsius deinceps applicari debeat suo modo. Item Hof. vi, 2.
units.tr: This resurrection will take place at the consummation of the age, at the coming of the Lord, etc. As we set forth this great mystery of faith against unbelievers, so it must be proved by several classes of arguments. To this belong, first, certain most evident sayings of the Old Testament, such as Dan. 12, 1, 2, 3: Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake; these to eternal life, etc. Add Job 19, 25, 26, 27; and Ps. 16, 9, 10, a prophecy which so pertains to Christ that it ought to be applied in its own way to his members afterwards. Likewise Hos. 6, 2.

units.la: 2. Ex effatis quibusdam ipsius Christi in N. T. qualia extant Iob. 5, 28, 29. Adde Matth. xxii, 29, 31, 33. 34. ubi Salvator mortuorum resurrectionem adversus Sadducaeos valide asserit.
units.tr: Second, from certain sayings of Christ himself in the New Testament, such as John 5, 28, 29. Add Matt. 22, 29, 31, 33, 34, where the Saviour strongly asserts the resurrection of the dead against the Sadducees.

units.la: 3. Ex confessionibus & doctrinis Apostolorum: Act. xxiv, 14, 15. Paulus de se ipso. Ut qui credam omnibus, quae in Lege & in Prophetis scripta sunt; ac spem habeam in Deo, fore, quam etiam ii ipsi (Pharisaei) expectant, resurrectionem mortuorum. 1 Cor. 15, 12, -. 1 Thess. 3, 14, 16. Apoc. 20, 12, 13.
units.tr: Third, from the confessions and teachings of the Apostles: Acts 24, 14, 15, Paul of himself: so that I believe all things which are written in the Law and in the Prophets, and have hope in God that there will be a resurrection of the dead, which these very men (the Pharisees) also expect. 1 Cor. 15, 12ff.; 1 Thess. 3, 14, 16; Rev. 20, 12, 13.

units.la: 4. Ex redargutione haereticorum, contrariam opinionem foveнтium & spargentium: 2 Tim. 2, 16, 17, 18. Qui circa fidem aberrarunt a scopo, dicentes, resurrectionem jam esse factam, &c.
units.tr: Fourth, from the refutation of heretics who cherish and spread the contrary opinion: 2 Tim. 2, 16, 17, 18: who have gone astray from the mark concerning the faith, saying that the resurrection has already taken place, etc.

units.la: XVI.
units.tr: XVI.

units.la: Quod autem ista resuscitatio futura sit eorundem numero corporum, quantum ad ipsam substantiam attinet; qualitatibus ad incorruptionem & gloriam solum mutatis, probatur specialius contra Socinianos: 1. quia erit vera resuscitatio corporum ex pulvere terrae, ex monumentis, ex mari; secundum loca Dan. xii, 2. Iob. 19, 25, 26, 27. Iob. 5, 28. 29. Apoc. xx, 12, 13. atqui haec de ipsis corporibus intelligenda sunt necessario.
units.tr: That this resurrection will be of the same bodies as to their very substance, with only their qualities changed to incorruption and glory, is proved more specifically against the Socinians: 1. because there will be a true raising of bodies from the dust of the earth, from tombs, and from the sea. This is shown by Dan. 12:2; Job 19:25, 26, 27; John 5:28, 29; Rev. 20:12, 13. But these passages must necessarily be understood of the bodies themselves.

units.la: 2. Accedunt alia testimonia, de ipsis corporibus nunc humilibus, & mortalibus, aut mortuis, loquentia: Rom. 8, 11. 1 Cor. 15, 53, 54. Oportet enim corruptibile istud induere incorruptibilitatem, &c. Phil. 3, 20, 21.
units.tr: 2. Other testimonies also speak of the bodies themselves, now lowly and mortal, or dead: Rom. 8:11; 1 Cor. 15:53, 54: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, etc.; Phil. 3:20, 21.

units.la: 3. Huc etiam pertinent exempla: primo quidem & potissimum ipsius Christi, qui eodem substantia corpore e sepulchro prodiit. Atqui Christus est nostrum caput; & primitiae resurgentium a mortuis, in gloriosam vitam, factus est. Hinc Angeli ad mulieres, Luc. 24, 5, 6. Quid inter mortuos quaeritis eum qui vivit? Non est hic: sed suscitatus est. Quapropter etiam Act. XXIV. 15. Resurrectionem mortuorum, tum justorum, tum injustorum.
units.tr: 3. Examples also belong here, first and above all that of Christ himself, who came forth from the sepulchre in the same substantial body. But Christ is our head, and he has been made the firstfruits of those who rise from the dead into glorious life. Hence the angels say to the women, Luke 24:5, 6: Why do you seek the living among the dead? He is not here, but is risen. Therefore also Acts 24:15: The resurrection of the dead, both of the just and of the unjust.

units.la: 2. Differte docetur quoque resuscitatio ad ignominiam, damnationem, & horrorem: Dan. XII, 2. Joh. 5, 29.
units.tr: 2. The resurrection to shame, condemnation and horror is also taught separately: Dan. 12:2; John 5:29.

units.la: 3. Judicium extremum, quod personarum resuscitationem praerequirit, erit universale; atque adeo infideles & improbos quoque complectetur: Rom. II, 5, 6. Thesaurizas tibi ipsi iram, in diem irae, & patefactionis justi judicii Dei; qui reddet unicuique secundum opera ipsius. 2 Cor. 5, 10. 2 Thess. 1, 6, 7, 8.
units.tr: 3. The final judgment, which presupposes the raising of persons, will be universal, and so will embrace also the unbelieving and the wicked: Rom. 2:5, 6: You are storing up for yourself wrath, on the day of wrath and of the revelation of the righteous judgment of God, who will render to each one according to his works. 2 Cor. 5:10; 2 Thess. 1:6, 7, 8.

units.la: 4. Consequenter improbi damnati, aeternas poenas perferent, anima & corpore pariter: quod mox probabitur. Ubi iterum supponitur eorum resuscitatio.
units.tr: 4. Consequently the wicked, when condemned, will undergo eternal punishments, in soul and body alike, as will shortly be proved, where again their resurrection is presupposed.

units.la: Obj. Resuscitatio peragetur a Christo; cum quo infideles non habent communionem: ergo illi non resuscitabuntur. Resp. Resuscitatio fidelium a Christo quidem peragetur, ut ipsorum Capite & Salvatore: Phil. 3, 21. Infidelium vero ab eodem, tanquam judice, ad judicandum ordinato: Act. 17, 31.
units.tr: Objection. The resurrection will be effected by Christ, with whom unbelievers have no communion; therefore they will not be raised. Answer. The resurrection of believers will indeed be effected by Christ as their Head and Saviour (Phil. 3:21), but that of unbelievers by the same Christ as judge, appointed to judge (Acts 17:31).

units.la: XX. Judicium extremum est Actus Regni Christi quo ille novissimo die de creaturis rationalibus, visibiliter in nubibus Coeli justam sententiam pronunciabit; atque mox executioni mandabit; justos quidem palam justificando, & vitam aeternam gloriosam judicialiter iis decernendo; injustos autem condemnando, & aeternis cruciatibus adjudicando.
units.tr: XX. The final judgment is that act of the kingdom of Christ by which, on the last day, he will visibly pronounce, in the clouds of heaven, a just sentence upon the rational creatures, and will then at once commit it to execution: openly justifying the righteous, and judicially awarding them eternal glorious life, but condemning the wicked and adjudging them to eternal torments.

units.la: Quod fit actus Christi, patet ex locis, Joh. 5, 22. Act. 17, 31. Quod ad Regnum Ipsius pertineat; Matth. 25, 31. Cum venerit Filius hominis cum gloria sua, & omnes sancti Angeli cum Eo, tunc sedebit in Throno gloriae suae. Et congregabuntur coram Eo omnes gentes: & separabit eos, &c. Tunc dicet Rex iis, qui ad dexteram Ipsius erunt, &c.
units.tr: That this is an act of Christ is clear from the passages John 5:22 and Acts 17:31. That it pertains to his kingdom is shown by Matt. 25:31: When the Son of man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory. And all the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them, etc. Then the King will say to those who are at his right hand, etc.

units.la: Ex postremo illo loco etiam liquet, Christum adfuturum cum magna demonstratione Majestatis, in propria sua humana natura; per aspectabilem quendam confessum in Throno glorioso, & cum sanctis Angelis, qui ipsi adsistent. Confer Matth. 24, 29, 30, 31. 1 Thess. 4, 16. 2, 1, 7, 8. 2 Petr. 3, 10, 12. Judæ, 14, 15. Apoc. 20, 11, 12. Psal. L, 1,-6. Item Exod 19. 16, 18, 19. Gal. 3, 10. Hebr. 12, 18,-21.
units.tr: From this last passage it is also plain that Christ will come with great display of majesty, in his own human nature, with a visible assembly on a glorious throne and with the holy angels attending him. Compare Matt. 24:29, 30, 31; 1 Thess. 4:16; 2 Thess. 1:7, 8; 2 Pet. 3:10, 12; Jude 14, 15; Rev. 20:11, 12; Ps. 50:1-6. Likewise Exod. 19:16, 18, 19; Gal. 3:10; Heb. 12:18-21.

units.la: Ipsi autem fideles etiam judicabunt cum & sub Christo; ejus justum judicium agnoscentes, & approbantes: quod quidem ad arctissimam illorum cum Christo unionem, Regni Ejus participationem, adeoque ipsorum gloriam pertinebit; simulque ad majorem damnatorum convictionem. Hinc Matth. 19, 28. Sedebitis vos etiam in thronis duodecim, judicium serentes. &c. 1. 1 Cor. 6. 2. 3. An ignoratis, Sanctos mundum judicaturos? 2. an ignoratis fore, ut Angelorum judices simus?
units.tr: The believers themselves will also judge, together with and under Christ, acknowledging and approving his just judgment. This will pertain to their most intimate union with Christ, their participation in his kingdom, and so to their own glory, and at the same time to the fuller conviction of the condemned. Hence Matt. 19:28: You also will sit on twelve thrones, judging, etc.; 1 Cor. 6:2, 3: Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? and do you not know that we shall judge angels?

units.la: XXI.
units.tr: XXI.

units.la: Judicandi autem venient, tum Angeli, tum Homines. De Angelis patet ex loco proxime allegato. Specialius vero ad malos Angelos refertur judicium condemnatorium; 2 Petr. 2, 4. Deus Angelis, qui peccaverunt, non pepercit; sed in tartarum detrusos catenis caliginis tradidit, damnationi asservatos. Judæ, 6. Angelos, qui non servarunt suam originem, sed reliquerunt suum domicilium, judicio magni illius diei vinculis æternis sub caligine servasse. Matth. 25, 4. Dicet iis, qui ad sinistram erunt; Execrandi, abite à Me in ignem illum æternum, paratum Diabolo & Angelis ejus.
units.tr: Those who come to judge will be both angels and men. For the angels this is clear from the passage just cited. More specifically, the condemnatory judgment refers to the evil angels: 2 Pet. 2:4: God did not spare the angels who sinned, but cast them down into hell, delivering them into chains of darkness, reserved for damnation. Jude 6: The angels who did not keep their own origin but left their own dwelling, he has kept in eternal chains under darkness for the judgment of the great day. Matt. 25:41: He will say to those on the left, "Depart from me, you accursed, into that eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels."

units.la: Sed Judicium de Hominibus magis est nostrę considerationis: quod communiter proponitur Eccl. III, 17. Justum & impium judicabit Deus. XII, 14. Matth. 25, 32,-. Et congregabuntur coram Eo (Christo) omnes gentes; & separabit eos ab aliis, ut pastor oves ab hædis, &c. Act. 17, 31. Rom. 2, 6, 16. XIV, 10, 12. 2 Cor. 5, 10. Apoc. 20, 12, 13.
units.tr: But the judgment of men is more our concern, and it is commonly set forth at Eccl. 3:17: God will judge the righteous and the wicked. Eccl. 12:14; Matt. 25:32: And all the nations will be gathered before him (Christ), and he will separate them from one another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats, etc.; Acts 17:31; Rom. 2:6, 16; 14:10, 12; 2 Cor. 5:10; Rev. 20:12, 13.

units.la: Obj. 1. Joh. 5, 24. Qui credit,- non venit in judicium. tudo, terror, desperatio, exitium denique omnium eorum qui in eo statu perseverant. Isf. 48, 21. Non est pax (dicit Iehovah) impiis. lvii, 20, 21. Prov. 28, 1. Fugiunt, tametsi nemo persequatur. Psal. 73, 18, 19, 20. Iudæ, 13. Rom. 1, 28. II, 15. Eph. 4, 18, 19. Ioh. 8, 14. Prov. 1, 26, 27; 31, 32.
units.tr: Objection 1. John 5:24: He who believes does not come into judgment. Dread, terror, despair, and finally the destruction of all who persist in that state. Isa. 48:21: There is no peace, says the LORD, for the wicked. Isa. 57:20, 21; Prov. 28:1: The wicked flee when no one pursues. Ps. 73:18, 19, 20; Jude 13; Rom. 1:28; 2:15; Eph. 4:18, 19; John 8:14; Prov. 1:26, 27; 31:32.

units.la: VII. Post hanc vitam consummabitur Glorificatio: Liberabimur enim ab omni imperfectione in anima & in corpore, atque omnis perfectio nobis communicabitur: 1 Cor. 13, 9, 10, 12. Ex parte cognoscimus: — Postquam autem advenerit quod perfectum est; tunc quod est aliquatenus, abolebitur. &c. 2: 5, 1, -8.
units.tr: VII. After this life glorification will be completed. For we shall be freed from every imperfection in soul and body, and all perfection will be communicated to us: 1 Cor. 13:9, 10, 12: We know in part; but when what is perfect has come, what is in part will be done away, etc.; 2 Cor. 5:1-8.

units.la: Hæc autem Glorificatio spectanda est tum in anima separata, tum in persona integra.
units.tr: This glorification is to be considered both in the separated soul and in the whole person.

units.la: Mors temporaria & corporalis adhuc evenit fidelibus; non tamen ut poena stricte dicta; sed ut transitus in vitam æternam, & depositio reliquiarum peccati. Atque ita gradatim salus applicatur. Plenissima autem applicatio fiet novissimo die: Rom. 8, 10, 11. 1 Cor. 15, 20, 22, 23; 26. Infidelium alia est ratio, super quos ira Dei permanet: Ioh. 3, 36. & quos ea occupavit ad extremum usque; 1 Thess. II, 16.
units.tr: Temporal and bodily death still comes upon believers, yet not as punishment in the strict sense, but as a passage into eternal life and a laying aside of the remnants of sin. Thus salvation is applied gradually. The fullest application, however, will take place on the last day: Rom. 8:10, 11; 1 Cor. 15:20, 22, 23, 26. The case of unbelievers is different, for the wrath of God remains upon them (John 3:36), and it has overtaken them to the end (1 Thess. 2:16).

units.la: VIII. Sic igitur animæ fidelium, a corporibus suis separatæ, a reliquiis peccatorum, aliarumque miserarum, pro sua parte liberantur, & ad perfectionem sanctitatis ac gloriæ, cum Christo apud Deum in cœlo percipiendam, statim transeunt. Hinc 1. Eccl. 12, 7. Revertitur pulvis in terram; & spiritus ad Deum, qui dedit illum. Quod de singulis quidem morientibus accipiendum; de fidelibus autem, ut vero statui gloriæ convenit. De his specialius, Isf. 57, 2. Ingredietur in pace, requiescent in cubilibus suis, &c. Hebr. 12, 23. Spiritus justorum consummatorum. Apoc. 14, 13. Beati ab hoc tempore mortui, ii qui in Domino moriuntur. Etiam dicit Spiritus: ut requiescant a laboribus suis, &c. Ioh. 5, 24. Qui credit, habet vitam æternam; & in condemnationem non veniet : sed transfivit à morte in vitam.
units.tr: VIII. So then the souls of believers, separated from their bodies, are freed in their own part from the remnants of sin and from other miseries, and at once pass on to receive perfection of holiness and glory with Christ before God in heaven. Hence: (1) Eccl. 12:7: The dust returns to the earth, and the spirit to God who gave it. This is to be understood of dying people in general, but of believers in the sense that suits the state of glory. More specifically, Isa. 57:2: They shall enter into peace, they shall rest in their beds, etc.; Heb. 12:23: the spirits of the just made perfect. Rev. 14:13: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on. Yes, says the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours, etc.; John 5:24: He who believes has eternal life, and will not come into condemnation, but has passed from death into life.

units.la: 2. Hùc pertinent exempla, Latronis post mortem statim in Paradisum migrantis, Luc. 23,43. cum verf. 46. & 2 Cor. 12, 3, 4, Animarum eorum, qui maftati fuerant propter Verbum Dei,-. Clamabant autem voce magna, dicentes ; Usque quo, &c. Tum date sunt singulis stolæ albæ ; & dictum est, ut requiescerent adhuc paululum temporis, &c. Apoc. 6, 9, 10, 11. Confer vii, 9, 10, 14. Item Luc. 16, 22, 25, 27,-31. de animâ Lazari ab Angelis in sinum Abrahæ transportati, &c.
units.tr: (2) Examples belong here as well: the thief who went straight into Paradise after death (Luke 23:43), and with him verse 46; and 2 Cor. 12:3, 4. The souls of those who were slain for the Word of God... They cried out with a loud voice, saying, "How long?" etc.; Then white robes were given to each of them, and they were told that they should rest a little while longer, etc. Rev. 6:9, 10, 11; compare 7:9, 10, 14. Likewise Luke 16:22, 25, 27-31, concerning the soul of Lazarus carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom, etc.

units.la: 3. Accedit fides solida, & certa spes, filiorum Dei. Hanc exprimit Apostolus, Phil. 1, 21,-24. - Constrictus utrimque teneor, desiderio tendens ad dimissionem, & ut cum Christo sim. & 2 Cor. 5, 1,-8.
units.tr: 3. Add to this the solid faith and certain hope of the sons of God. The Apostle expresses this in Phil. 1:21-24: I am hard pressed between the two, having a desire to depart and be with Christ; and in 2 Cor. 5:1-8.

units.la: IX. De animabus verò impiorum, secundum SS. Literas dicendum, quod post separationem à corporibus justo Dei judicio ablegentur in infernum : atque illic cruciatus & poenas peccatorum suorum perserant, Hinc 1. ratione loci, Judas proditor dicitur abiisse in suum locum, Act. 1, 25. Ac similiter damnatus epulo, in locum tormenti venisse; Luc. 16. 28. Itemque 1 Petr. 3, 19, 20. memorantur spiritus existentes in carcere,-qui olim non paruerunt sermoni. Confer 2 Petr. II, 4.
units.tr: IX. Concerning the souls of the wicked, we must speak according to the Holy Scriptures: after their separation from the body, by the just judgment of God they are consigned to hell, and there they endure the torments and punishments of their sins. Here, first, with respect to place: Judas the traitor is said to have gone to his own place (Acts 1:25), and likewise the rich man in the parable is said to have come into the place of torment (Luke 16:28). Also in 1 Pet. 3:19, 20 mention is made of spirits in prison, who formerly did not obey the word. Compare 2 Pet. 2:4.

units.la: 2. Ratione verò cruciatuum & poenarum, quales videl. naturæ spirituali conveniunt ; Sodoma & Gomorra, iisque finitimæ civitates, h. e. animæ illorum hominum, dicuntur sustinere poenam ignis æterni. Et Epulo, gravissimè cruciatus in flamma : Luc. 16, 23, 24, 25.
units.tr: 2. With respect to the torments and punishments, which are such as befit a spiritual nature: Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities neighbouring them, that is, the souls of those men, are said to suffer the punishment of eternal fire (Jude 7). And the rich man is greatly tormented in the flame (Luke 16:23, 24, 25).

units.la: 3. Neque omittenda gravis præmonitio Christi, de metuendo Illo, qui postquam interemit corpus, potestatem habet conjiciendi in gehennam ; Luc. 12, 4, 5.
units.tr: 3. Nor should we pass over the grave warning of Christ concerning him to be feared, who, after he has killed the body, has power to cast into hell (Luke 12:4, 5).

units.la: Obj. Eccl. III, 19, 20, 21. dicuntur filii hominum mori, sicut sicuti animal, &c. Resp. Id quod intelligendum est de accidentibus externis & visibilibus, in morte hominum & bestiarum. Quod vero conditio hominum coram Deo, plurimum differat à conditione bestiarum, satis patet ex vers. 17. Iustum & impium judicabit Deus. ac porrò, XI, 9. XII, 7, 12, 13.
units.tr: Objection. Eccles. 3:19, 20, 21 says that the sons of men die as the beast does, and so on. Answer. This must be understood of the external and visible circumstances in the death of men and beasts. That the condition of men before God differs greatly from that of beasts is clear enough from v. 17: God will judge the righteous and the wicked; and further Eccles. 11:9; 12:7, 12, 13.

units.la: X. Pontificii pro fidelibus, qui in peccatis venialibus moriuntur, statuunt locum aliquem intermedium, ubi pro culpa sua justitiæ Divinæ satisfaciant, & per pœnas purgentur; donec postea ad cœlestem beatitudinem admittantur. Purgatorium appellant; & carcerem aliquem subterraneum, inferno proximum, aut contiguum, existimant. Sed 1. Scriptura tantum duo loca animarum separatarum agnoscit, unum gloriæ, alterum damnationis, atque indicat, unumquemque permanere in eo loco, in quem statim à morte transfit. Eccl. XI, 3. Si ceciderit arbor ad Austrum, sive ad Aquilonem; in quem locum ceciderit ipsa arbor, ibi erit.
units.tr: X. The Papists, for the faithful who die in venial sins, hold that there is some intermediate place where they make satisfaction to the divine justice for their guilt and are purged by punishments, until afterwards they are admitted to heavenly blessedness. They call it Purgatory, and they think it is some subterranean prison, close to or adjoining hell. But, first, Scripture acknowledges only two places for separated souls, one of glory and the other of damnation, and it indicates that each one remains in the place into which he passes immediately at death: Eccles. 11:3, If the tree falls to the south or to the north, in whatever place the tree falls, there it shall be.

units.la: 2. Christus plenissime pro peccatis electorum justitiæ Divinæ satisfecit; adeo quidem ut nulla satisfactio ab iis exigi possit. Hebr. 10, 14-18. Unica oblatione Christus in perpetuum consummavit eos qui sanctificantur. Et quia per Christi satisfactionem exstinctus est omnium peccatorum nostrorum reatus, sanguis ejus dicitur nos Purificare ab Omni peccato; 1 Joh. 1, 7. Nullum ergo peccatum reliquum est, à quo purgari deberemus tali Igne purgatorio.
units.tr: 2. Christ has made full satisfaction to the divine justice for the sins of the elect, so fully that no satisfaction can be demanded of them. Heb. 10:14-18: By one offering Christ has perfected for ever those who are sanctified. And because the guilt of all our sins has been extinguished through Christ's satisfaction, his blood is said to cleanse us from all sin (1 John 1:7). Therefore no sin remains from which we would need to be cleansed by such a purging fire.

units.la: 3. Idem patet ex naturâ Justificationis, quæ plenam remissionem omnium peccatorum complectitur; adeò ut nulla amplius pro iis satisfactio exigenda sit. Rom. IV, 6, 7, 8. Sicut etiam David (Psal. 32, 1, 2.) Declarat beatum eum hominem, cui Deus imputat justitiam absque operibus: dicens; Beati, quibus remissæ sunt Legis transgressiones; & quorum tecta sunt peccata. v. 1, 2. Iustificati igitur ex fide, pacem habemus apud Deum, 9. Iustificati nunc Ejus sanguine ne, servabimur multo magis per Eum ab ira, VIII, 1. Nulla nunc est condemnatio iis qui sunt in Christo Iesu. Ergo nec temporalis illa condemnatio in Purgatorio. 33, 34. Quis intentabit crimina, &c.
units.tr: 3. The same is evident from the nature of justification, which embraces the full remission of all sins, so that no further satisfaction for them is to be required. Rom. 4:6, 7, 8. Just as David too (Ps. 32:1, 2) declares blessed the man to whom God imputes righteousness without works, saying: Blessed are those whose transgressions of the law are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Vv. 1, 2. Therefore, being justified by faith, we have peace with God (5:1, 9). Being now justified by his blood, we shall be saved much more by him from wrath (8:1). There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. Therefore neither is that temporal condemnation in Purgatory. 8:33, 34: Who shall bring a charge, and so on.

units.la: 4. Distinctio peccatorum in mortalia & venialia, quæ Purgatorio substernitur, caret fundamento; & confutata est sup. cap. 10. th. 43.
units.tr: 4. The distinction of sins into mortal and venial, on which Purgatory is based, lacks foundation, and it has been refuted above, chap. 10, th. 43.

units.la: XI. Obj. Matth. 5, 25, 26. Christus loquitur de carcere; unde qui in eum essent conjecti, non forent liberandi ante persolutum ultimum quadrantem: iste autem est Purgatorium: ex inferno enim nulla unquam fit liberatio. Resp. Sed minime dicit, homines post hanc vitam posse ultimum istum quadrantem persolvere; & sic liberari: ad ipsum igitur infernum istud pertinet.
units.tr: XI. Objection. Matt. 5:25, 26. Christ speaks of a prison, from which those who were cast into it were not to be released before the last farthing was paid; but this is Purgatory, for there is never any release from hell. Answer. He by no means says that men after this life can pay that last farthing and so be released; therefore that prison pertains to hell itself.

units.la: Obj. 2. 1 Cor. 3, 15. Ipse vero servabitur, itatamen ut per ignem. Scil. Purgatorium. Resp. Apostolus allegorice loquitur de Doctoribus, solido ac salutari fundamento Christo superstruentibus vel doctrinas veras & utiles, vel incertas & inutiles - futurum autem, ut cujusque opus manifestum fiat, ut dies ipsum declaret, & ignis probet ac retegat. Verum iste non est ignis purgatorius & poenalis post hanc vitam; sed probatorius etiam in hoc sæculo; dum opus Ministerii probabitur deinceps, per ipsum Verbum Dei, Spiritu efficaciter cooperante. Confer Jerem. 23. 29. Mal. III, 2, 3. Matth. III, 11. Interim salvandi sunt, quamvis ægrè, qui fundamentum retinuerint. Confer Am. 4, 11. Zach. III, 2. 1 Petr. 4, 18.
units.tr: Objection 2. 1 Cor. 3:15: He himself will be saved, yet so as through fire. That is, Purgatory. Answer. The Apostle speaks allegorically of teachers who build upon the solid and saving foundation, Christ, either true and useful doctrines or uncertain and useless ones; but the work of each will be made manifest, for the day will declare it, and the fire will test and reveal it. But this is not a purgatorial and penal fire after this life, but a testing fire even in this age, since the work of the ministry will then be tested by the Word of God itself, with the Spirit effectively co-operating. Compare Jer. 23:29; Mal. 3:2, 3; Matt. 3:11. Meanwhile, those who have held to the foundation are to be saved, though with difficulty. Compare Amos 4:11; Zech. 3:2; 1 Pet. 4:18.

units.la: Obj. 3. Phil. II, 10. In nomine Iesu flectentur etiam genua subterraneorum. Hoc est, in Purgatorio laborantium. Resp. Indicatur ibi subjectio omnium creaturarum, etiam hostium, & damnatorum, ad Christum. Confer Gen. 41, 43. Esth. 3, 2. Item Psal. 72, 9, 11. 1 Cor. 15, 25, 26, 27. Iob. 5, 27, 28, 29.
units.tr: Objection 3. Phil. 2:10: at the name of Jesus every knee shall bow, even of those under the earth. That is, of those who suffer in Purgatory. Answer. There is indicated there the subjection of all creatures, even enemies and the damned, to Christ. Compare Gen. 41:43; Esth. 3:2; likewise Ps. 72:9, 11; 1 Cor. 15:25, 26, 27; John 5:27, 28, 29.

units.la: XII. Præter istud Purgatorium, duos insuper Limbos bos infernales falsò statuunt Pontificii; unum Patrum appellant, alterum Infantium. Limbum Patrum reliquis Inferni partibus, aut receptaculis, superiorem reputant; in quo patres, sive fideles V. T. fuerint detenti, donec per Christi ad inferos descensum ex eo liberarentur.
units.tr: XII. Besides that Purgatory, the Papists falsely posit two further infernal limbos: one they call the limbo of the Fathers, the other that of infants. They judge the limbo of the Fathers to be higher than the other parts or receptacles of hell, a place in which the fathers, or the faithful of the Old Testament, were detained until they were released from it through Christ's descent into the underworld.

units.la: Verùm 1. S. Scriptura talem locum non agnoscit.
units.tr: But, first, Holy Scripture does not acknowledge any such place.

units.la: 2. Satisfactio & Meritum Christi ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν etiam in istius temporis fidelibus efficax fuit: Iesus Christus heri, & hodie idem est, & in sæcula; Hebr. 13, 8. Confer Act. 15, 10, 11.
units.tr: 2. The satisfaction and merit of Christ on our behalf [ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν] was effective also for the faithful of that time: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and for ever (Heb. 13:8). Compare Acts 15:10, 11.

units.la: 3. Quia fideles illi etiam justificati sunt per fidem: atque adeo non solum ab omni damnatione immunes fuerunt; sed etiam jus habuerunt ad ipsam cœlestem beatitudinem. Sic de Abrahamo, Iac. II, 23. Credidit Abraham Deo; & imputatum est ei ad justitiam, & amicus Dei vocatus est. Confer Rom. IV, 1, - 5, 6, - 9. VIII, 30.
units.tr: 3. Because those faithful men too were justified by faith, and so they were not only free from all condemnation, but also had a right to heavenly blessedness itself. So of Abraham, James 2:23: Abraham believed God, and it was imputed to him for righteousness, and he was called the friend of God. Compare Rom. 4:1-5, 6-9; 8:30.

units.la: 4. Christus localiter ad Limbum illum infernalem non descendit. Vide sup. cap. 12. th. 57.
units.tr: 4. Christ did not descend locally into that infernal limbo. See above, chap. 12, th. 57.

units.la: Obj. 1. Zach. 9, 11. Emisi vinctos tuos de cisterna, in quà non est aqua. Hoc autem pertinet ad istum Limbum. Resp. Proximè pertinet ad liberationem ex captivitate Babylonicà; ac porrò ex omni miseriâ spirituali, juxta Euangelium.
units.tr: Objection 1. Zech. 9:11: I have sent forth your prisoners out of the pit in which there is no water. This, however, pertains to that limbo. Answer. It pertains most immediately to the liberation from the Babylonian captivity, and further to liberation from all spiritual misery, according to the Gospel.

units.la: Obj. 2. 1 Sam. 28, 11, -. Pythonissa produxit Samuelem; non ex Cœlo, sed ex Limbo. Ergò. Resp. Non Samuelem, aut ejus animam; sed Satanam, qui Prophetæ personam mentiebatur: neque enim talis vir, ut Samuel, in potestate Diaboli & hominum nefariorum fuit post mortem suam. Vide Ies. 57, 2. Nec Deus Sauli respondere voluit per media ordinaria: 1 Sam. 28, 11, 15. nedùm per Prophetam mortuum. Vide Ies. 8, 19, 20. Luc. 16, 30, 31. cum 2 Cor. XI, 14. Metaphoricè autem vocatur Samuel: propter imaginem, aut similitudinem.
units.tr: Objection 2. 1 Sam. 28:11ff. The medium brought up Samuel, not from heaven but from the limbo. Therefore. Answer. It was not Samuel, or his soul, but Satan, who falsely played the part of the prophet. For such a man as Samuel was not, after his death, in the power of the devil and of wicked men; see Isa. 57:2. Nor did God wish to answer Saul through ordinary means (1 Sam. 28:11, 15), much less through a dead prophet. See Isa. 8:19, 20; Luke 16:30, 31, compared with 2 Cor. 11:14. But he is metaphorically called Samuel on account of the image or likeness.

units.la: XIII. Lim-
units.tr: XIII. The Limbo of Infants

units.la: XIII. Limbum Infantium fingunt receptaculum infernale, in quo infantes sine Baptismo mortui, poenam damni tantum, vel exigui saltem sensus, ferant.
units.tr: XIII. The Limbo of Infants they imagine to be an infernal receptacle, in which infants who have died without Baptism bear only the punishment of loss, or at least of some slight sense of pain.

units.la: Verùm 1. Scriptura nihil de isto loco tradit.
units.tr: But, first, Scripture says nothing about this place.

units.la: 2. Si infantes verè foederati fuerint, salutem iis promisit Deus: quae gratia ad Baptismum jam praesupponitur; non demùm per illum confertur.
units.tr: Second, if infants have truly been within the covenant, God has promised them salvation; this grace is already presupposed before Baptism and is not conferred only through it.

units.la: XIV. Succedit Glorificatio integrarum personarum, ad quam pertinent Gloriosa fidelium defunctorum Resuscitatio, publica eorundem in extremo judicio Justificatio, & Sententiae istius Executio aeterna ac beata.
units.tr: XIV. There follows the Glorification of whole persons, to which belong the glorious resurrection of the dead faithful, the public justification of the same at the last judgment, and the eternal and blessed execution of that sentence.

units.la: Resuscitatio illa erit actio potens & gloriosa Christi, quâ Ipse cadavera omnium & singulorum fidelium suorum, quantumvis in pulverem redacta & dispersa, in consummatione saeculi restituet, gloriâ condecorabit, & animabus suis corpora singula reduniet, ad perfectam beatitudinem.
units.tr: That resurrection will be a powerful and glorious act of Christ, by which He will restore, in the consummation of the age, the corpses of all and each of His faithful, however much they have been reduced to dust and scattered; He will adorn them with glory and rejoin each body to its own soul, for perfect blessedness.

units.la: Subjecta recipientia Resuscitationis hujus gloriosae erunt cadavera Hominum fidelium; eaque omnia & singula. Matth. 10, 28. Trucidant corpus; animam autem non possunt trucidare. Iob. 5, 28, 29. Quia in monumentis sunt, audient vocem Ejus. Et prodibunt, qui bona fecerint, in resurrectionem vitae. Item Luc. xx. 36. Filii sunt Dei, cum sint filii resurrectionis. Rom. 8, 29, 30. Nam quos praescivit, etiam praedestinavit conformandos imagini Filii sui; - quos autem justificavit, eos etiam glorificavit.
units.tr: The recipient subjects of this glorious resurrection will be the corpses of the faithful, all and each of them. Matth. 10, 28. They kill the body, but they cannot kill the soul. Iob. 5, 28, 29. Because they are in the tombs, they will hear His voice. And those who have done good will come forth to the resurrection of life. Likewise Luc. 20, 36. They are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection. Rom. 8, 29, 30. For whom He foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son; and whom He justified, these He also glorified.

units.la: Causa efficiens primò est Deus: 1 Sam. II, 6. Iehovah - vivificat: Rom. 4, 17. 2 Cor. 1, 9. 1 Tim. 4, 18. Atque ita competit hoc opus Patri, Filio, & Spiritui Sancto: Iob. 5, 21. Rom. VIII, 11. per Divinam omnipotentiam: Ephes. 1, 19, 20. Phil. III, 21. κατ' ἐνέργειαν vero istud opus tribuitur Christo Mediatori, qui istam gloriam impetravit; sic ipse à mortuis resurrexit; & membra sua etiam suscitabit: Ioh. XI, 26. Dixit ei Icsus; Ego sum resurrectio & vita; qui credit in Me, etiamsi mortuus fuerit, vivet. Vide etiam Ioh. 5, 26, -29. Ephes. II, 5, 6. I Cor. 15, 20, -23. Hanc suam virtutem demonstravit Christus in miraculosa resuscitatione Lazari; Ioh. XI, 23, 27, 40, -44. adolescentis filii matris viduae; Luc. 7, 11, -15. adolescentulae filiae Jairi; VIII, 49, -54. & multorum sanctorum praedefunctorum circa mortem Christi; Matth. 28, 52, 53. Confer Actor. 9, 37, -41. XX, -9, -12. Item I Reg. 17, 17, -23: 2, IV, 20, 32, 37. XIII, 20, 21.
units.tr: The efficient cause is first of all God: 1 Sam. 2, 6. Jehovah makes alive; Rom. 4, 17. 2 Cor. 1, 9. 1 Tim. 4, 18. And so this work belongs to the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit: Iob. 5, 21. Rom. 8, 11, through divine omnipotence: Ephes. 1, 19, 20. Phil. 3, 21. But this work is ascribed to Christ the Mediator as its active agent [κατ' ἐνέργειαν], since He obtained this glory; so He Himself rose from the dead, and He will also raise up His members: Ioh. 11, 26. Jesus said to her, I am the resurrection and the life; he who believes in Me, even if he has died, will live. See also Ioh. 5, 26–29. Ephes. 2, 5, 6. 1 Cor. 15, 20–23. Christ demonstrated this His power in the miraculous raising of Lazarus, Ioh. 11, 23, 27, 40–44; of the son of the widowed mother, Luc. 7, 11–15; of the young daughter of Jairus, 8, 49–54; and of many saints who had died, around the death of Christ, Matth. 27, 52, 53. Compare Act. 9, 37–41; 20, 9–12. Likewise 1 Reg. 17, 17–23; 2 Reg. 4, 20, 32, 37; 13, 20, 21.

units.la: XV. Ad modum resuscitationis pertinent duo actus.
units.tr: XV. Two acts belong to the manner of the resurrection.

units.la: Prior est ipsa revificatio: & complectitur cadaverum recollectionem; animarum propriarum iteratam cum illis unionem; atque ita veram illorum per has informationem; & quidem talem, ut ipsae personae integrae deinceps futurae sint, etiam ratione ipsorum corporum, immortales, incorruptibiles, gloriosae. Posterior est vivificatorum egressus in occursus Domini. Illustris est illa visio quae Ezechieli exhibita fuit, XXXVII, 1, -10. Officium siccorum, quae colligebantur, vivificabantur, &c. Confer Apoc. XX. 12, 13. Atque ipse Christus, Ioh. 5, 28, 29. Venit hora, qua omnes, qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem Eius. Et prodibunt, qui bona fecerint, in resurrectionem vitae. Adde I Cor. 15, 37, -44. I Thess. IV. 14, 16.
units.tr: The first is the revivification itself, which comprises the gathering together of the corpses, their renewed union with their own souls, and thus the true informing of them by these souls; and indeed in such a way that the persons themselves, whole, will thereafter be immortal, incorruptible and glorious, including in respect of their bodies. The second is the going forth of the made-alive to meet the Lord. That vision which was shown to Ezekiel, 37, 1–10, is illustrious: the work upon the dry bones, which were gathered together, made alive, and so on. Compare Apoc. 20, 12, 13. And Christ Himself, Ioh. 5, 28, 29: The hour is coming, in which all who are in the tombs will hear His voice. And those who have done good will come forth to the resurrection of life. Add 1 Cor. 15, 37–44; 1 Thess. 4, 14, 16.

units.la: Ista autem resuscitatio fiet in consummatione saeculi, in adventu Domini, &c. Magnum hoc fidei mysterium ut contra Infideles afferimus; sic aliquot Argumentorum classibus probandum est. Huc pertinent 1. evidentissima quaedam effata V. T. utpote Dan. 12, 1, 2, 3. Multi dormientium in pulvere terrae exergisecentur; hi ad vitam aeternam, &c. Adde Iob. 19, 25, 26, 27. Et Psal. 16, 9, 10: quae prophetia sic ad Christum pertinet, ut ad membra Ipsius deinceps applicari debeat suo modo. Item Hof. vi, 2.
units.tr: This resurrection, however, will take place at the consummation of the age, at the coming of the Lord, and so on. As we set forth this great mystery of faith against unbelievers, so it must be proved by several classes of arguments. To this belong, first, certain most evident sayings of the Old Testament, such as Dan. 12, 1, 2, 3: Many of those sleeping in the dust of the earth will awake; these to eternal life, and so on. Add Iob. 19, 25, 26, 27; and Psal. 16, 9, 10, a prophecy which so pertains to Christ that it ought thereafter to be applied in its own way to His members. Likewise Hos. 6, 2.

units.la: 2. Ex effatis quibusdam ipsius Christi in N. T. qualia extant Joh. 5, 28, 29. Adde Matth. xxii, 29, 31, 33. 34. ubi Salvator mortuorum resurrectionem adversus Sadducæos validè asserit.
units.tr: Second, from certain sayings of Christ Himself in the New Testament, such as are found at Joh. 5, 28, 29. Add Matth. 22, 29, 31, 33, 34, where the Saviour strongly asserts the resurrection of the dead against the Sadducees.

units.la: 3. Ex confessionibus & doctrinis Apostolorum: Act. xxiv, 14, 15. Paulus de se ipso. Ut qui credam omnibus, quæ in Lege & in Prophetis scripta sunt; ac spem habeam in Deo, fore, quam etiam ii ipsi (Pharisæi) expectant, resurrectionem mortuorum. 1 Cor. 15, 12, -.
units.tr: Third, from the confessions and teachings of the Apostles: Act. 24, 14, 15, Paul of himself: That I believe all things which are written in the Law and in the Prophets; and I have hope in God that there will be a resurrection of the dead, which they themselves (the Pharisees) also expect. 1 Cor. 15, 12.

units.la: 4. Ex redargutione hæreticorum, contrariam opinionem foventium & spargentium: 2 Tim. 2, 16, 17, 18. - Qui circa fidem aberrarunt à scopo, dicentes, resurrectionem jam esse factam, &c.
units.tr: Fourth, from the refutation of heretics who hold and spread the contrary opinion: 2 Tim. 2, 16, 17, 18: Those who concerning the faith have wandered from the mark, saying that the resurrection has already taken place, and so on.

units.la: XVI.
units.tr: XVI.

units.la: Quòd autem ista resuscitatio futura sit eorundem numero corporum, quantum ad ipsam substantiam attinet; qualitatibus ad incorruptionem & gloriam solum mutatis, probatur specialius contra Socinianos: 1. quia erit vera resuscitatio corporum ex pulvere terræ, ex monumentis, ex mari; secundùm loca Dan. xii, 2. Job. 19, 25, 26, 27. Joh. 5, 28. 29. Apoc. xx, 12, 13. atqui hæc de ipsis corporibus intelligenda sunt necessariò.
units.tr: That this resurrection will be of the same bodies, as to their very substance, with only their qualities changed to incorruption and glory, is proved more specifically against the Socinians: (1) because there will be a true raising of bodies from the dust of the earth, from tombs, and from the sea, according to the passages Dan. 12:2; Job 19:25, 26, 27; John 5:28, 29; Rev. 20:12, 13. But these passages must necessarily be understood of the bodies themselves.

units.la: 2. Accedunt alia testimonia, de ipsis corporibus nunc humilibus, & mortalibus, aut mortuis, loquentia: Rom. 8, 11. 1 Cor. 15, 53, 54. Oportet enim corruptibile istud induere incorruptibilitatem, &c. Phil. 3, 20, 21.
units.tr: (2) There are other testimonies that speak of the very bodies, now lowly and mortal, or dead: Rom. 8:11; 1 Cor. 15:53, 54, For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and so on; Phil. 3:20, 21.

units.la: 3. Huc etiam pertinent exempla: primò quidem & potissimùm ipsius Christi, qui eodem substantiâ corpore è sepulchro prodiit. Atqui Christus est nostrum caput; & primitiæ resurgentium à mortuis, in gloriosam vitam, factus est. Hinc Angeli ad mulieres, Luc. 24, 5, 6. Quid inter mortuos quæritis cum qui vivit? Non est hic: sed suscitatus est. Quapropter etiam Christus suum corpus Discipulis palpandum dedit, ut certi essent de ejus identitate. Verf. 39, 40. Videte manus meas, & pedes meos: nam Ego ipse sum. Contrectate Me, & videte, &c. Joh. xx. 27. Conferendus est locus Apostoli, 1 Cor. 15, 20, -23, 47, 48, 49. ubi nostram resurrectionem ex resurrectione Christi, atque utriusque similem esse modum, tum in corporis identitate, tum in qualitatibus, docemur.
units.tr: (3) Examples also belong here, first and above all that of Christ himself, who came forth from the sepulchre in the same substantial body. Christ is our head, and he has been made the firstfruits of those who rise from the dead into glorious life. Hence the angels said to the women, Luke 24:5, 6: Why do you seek the living among the dead? He is not here, but is risen. For this reason Christ also gave his body to the disciples to be touched, so that they might be certain of its identity: vv. 39, 40, See my hands and my feet, for it is I myself. Handle me and see, etc.; John 20:27. The passage of the Apostle, 1 Cor. 15:20-23, 47-49, should be compared, where we are taught that our resurrection is like Christ's resurrection, and that the mode of each is alike, both in the identity of the body and in its qualities.

units.la: Nec omittenda exempla eorum, qui jam antea fuerunt ex mortuis suscitati; & sic quodammodo typum gesserunt istius resurrectionis: Matth. 27, 52, 53. Luc. 7, 12, 15. VIII. 54, 55. Joh. xi, 43, 44, &c. Ergo & hanc resuscitationem eorundem numero corporum esse oportet.
units.tr: Nor should we omit the examples of those who were raised from the dead earlier, and who in a certain way bore the type of this resurrection: Matt. 27:52, 53; Luke 7:12-15; 8:54, 55; John 11:43, 44, etc. Therefore this resurrection too must be of the same bodies.

units.la: 4. Per infinitam Dei sapientiam ac potentiam talis resuscitatio non solum est possibilis; sed per Ipsius justitiam quoque necessarium est, ut eadem personae, quarum partes essentiales quoque sunt corpora, retributionem accipiant pro operibus, per corpora, tanquam instrumenta consubstantialia, factis; atque adeo in iisdem etiam corporibus. Ita 2 Thess. 1, 6, 7. Justum est apud Deum, vicissim reddere iis, qui vos affligunt afflictionem: Vobis vero, qui affligimini, &c. 2 Cor. 5, 10. Omnes enim nos comparere oportet coram tribunali Christi, ut unusquisque reportet quae in corpore fecerit, congruenter ad id quod fecerit, sive bonum, sive malum.
units.tr: (4) By the infinite wisdom and power of God such a resurrection is not only possible, but by his justice it is also necessary that the same persons, whose essential parts are bodies, should receive a recompense for their works done through their bodies, as consubstantial instruments; and so in the same bodies. So 2 Thess. 1:6, 7: It is just with God to repay affliction to those who afflict you, and to you who are afflicted, etc.; 2 Cor. 5:10: For we must all appear before the judgement seat of Christ, that each may receive what he has done in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or evil.

units.la: XVII. Obj. 1.
units.tr: XVII. Objection 1.

units.la: Resuscitatio ista impossibilis videtur ob cadaverum tam diu mortuorum adeo multas mutationes; ob ἀνθρωποφάγως, &c. Resp. Imo infinitae Dei sapientiae & potentiae ea facilis est: Matth. xxii, 29. Rom. iv, 17. Phil. iii, 21. Hebr. xi, 18. Ipse enim non minus separanda separare, conjungenda conjungere, & mutanda mutare potest: quam ex nihilo creaturas producere potuit.
units.tr: This resurrection seems impossible because of the many changes in bodies so long dead, and because of anthropophagy [ἀνθρωποφάγως], and so on. Answer: on the contrary, it is easy for the infinite wisdom and power of God: Matt. 22:29; Rom. 4:17; Phil. 3:21; Heb. 11:18. For he can no less separate what must be separated, join what must be joined, and change what must be changed, than he was able to produce creatures out of nothing.

units.la: Obj. 2. Dan. 12, 2. dicitur; Multi dormientium in pulvere terræ, expergiscentur, &c. Si autem Multi; ergò non omnes. Resp. Neg. Consequ. Per Multos commodè intelligimus suscitandorum ad vitam æternam; dùm alii suscitandi sunt ad damnationem & opprobrium.
units.tr: Objection 2. It is said in Dan. 12:2: Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, etc. But if many, then not all. Answer: I deny the consequence. By many we fitly understand those who are to be raised to eternal life, while others are to be raised to condemnation and shame.

units.la: Obj. 3. 1 Cor. 15, 44. dicit Apostolus, suscitandum esse corpus spirituale: ergò non idem numero. Resp. Spirituale appellat, non respectû ipsius substantiæ; sed qualitatum.
units.tr: Objection 3. The Apostle says in 1 Cor. 15:44 that a spiritual body is to be raised; therefore not the same in number. Answer: he calls it spiritual not with respect to its substance, but to its qualities.

units.la: Obj. 4. Ibidem verf. 50. negat Apostolus, carnem & sanguinem consequi posse hæreditatem regni Dei. Ergò. Resp. Istic non loquitur de substantiâ; sed de imperfectionibus, tùm damnabilibus, tùm miserabilibus Confer Iob. I, 13. Iob. III, 6. Matth. 16, 17. Eph. 6, 12.
units.tr: Objection 4. In the same place, v. 50, the Apostle denies that flesh and blood can inherit the kingdom of God. Therefore... Answer: there he is not speaking of the substance, but of the imperfections, both damnable and miserable. Compare Job 1:13; Job 3:6; Matt. 16:17; Eph. 6:12.

units.la: XVIII. Refuscitationi isti analoga erit Mutatio gloriosa, quæ fidelibus tunc superstitibus continget; ut sine morte ad eandem illam gloriam, cum fidelibus à morte resuscitatis, transmutentur. Hinc 1 Cor. 15, 51, 52, 53. Ecce, Mysterium vobis dico: Non omnes quidem obdormiemus; sed omnes mutabimur: momento, &c. 1 Theff. IV, 15, 16, 17. Cujus Transmutationis specimen quoddam datum est in Enocho & Eliâ, sine morte translatis. Vide sup. cap. 12. th. 62.
units.tr: XVIII. The glorious change that will come to the faithful who are still alive at that time will be analogous to this resurrection, so that without death they are transformed into the same glory as the faithful raised from death. Hence 1 Cor. 15:51-53: Behold, I tell you a mystery: we shall not all indeed sleep, but we shall all be changed, in a moment, etc.; 1 Thess. 4:15-17. A certain specimen of this transformation was given in Enoch and Elijah, who were translated without death. See above, chap. 12, th. 62.

units.la: Obj. Hebr. 9, 27. Statutum est hominibus, ut semel moriantur, postea vero judicium. Nulli igitur à morte erunt immunes. Resp. Statuti istius pœnalis abolitio à Christo fidelibus impetrata, novissimo die plenè applicabitur: non igitur mirum, superstites tunc fideles sine morte ad gloriam transituros.
units.tr: Objection. Heb. 9:27: It is appointed to men once to die, and after that the judgement. Therefore none will be exempt from death. Answer: the abolition of that penal statute, obtained for the faithful by Christ, will be fully applied on the last day; so it is no wonder that the faithful who are alive at that time will pass to glory without death.

units.la: XIX. Improbi & infideles Refuscitationis gloriosæ non erunt participes: sed Refuscitationem ex morte temporali, integrarum personarum, iisdem quoque corporibus; verùm cum horrore ac ignominiâ, & ad cruciatûs æternos, experientur. Sic 1. Refuscitatio mortuorum ad injustos quoque extenditur:
units.tr: XIX. The wicked and unbelieving will not share in the glorious resurrection; but they will experience a resurrection from temporal death, of whole persons, in the same bodies, yet with horror and shame, and to eternal torments. Thus (1) the resurrection of the dead extends to the unjust also:

units.la: Act. XXIV. 15. Resurrectionem mortuorum, tum justorum, tum injustorum.
units.tr: Acts 24:15: the resurrection of the dead, both of the just and of the unjust.

units.la: 2. Diserte docetur quoque resuscitatio ad ignominiam, damnationem, & horrorem: Dan. XII, 2. Joh. 5, 29.
units.tr: (2) The resurrection to shame, condemnation and horror is also taught expressly: Dan. 12:2; John 5:29.

units.la: 3. Judicium extremum, quod personarum resuscitationem praerequirit, erit universale; atque adeo infideles & improbos quoque complectetur: Rom. II, 5, 6. Thesaurizas tibi ipsi iram, in diem irae, & patefactionis justi judicii Dei; qui reddet unicuique secundum opera ipsius. 2 Cor. 5, 10. 2 Thess. 1, 6, 7, 8.
units.tr: (3) The last judgement, which presupposes the raising of persons, will be universal, and so will embrace unbelievers and the wicked also: Rom. 2:5, 6: You store up for yourself wrath on the day of wrath, and of the revelation of the righteous judgement of God, who will render to each according to his works. 2 Cor. 5:10; 2 Thess. 1:6-8.

units.la: 4. Consequenter improbi damnati, aeternas poenas perferent, anima & corpore pariter: quod mox probabitur. Ubi iterum supponitur eorum resuscitatio.
units.tr: (4) Consequently the wicked, when condemned, will suffer eternal punishments, in soul and body alike; which will be proved shortly. There too their resurrection is again presupposed.

units.la: Obj. Resuscitatio peragetur a Christo; cum quo infideles non habent communionem: ergo illi non resuscitabuntur. Resp. Resuscitatio fidelium a Christo quidem peragetur, ut ipsorum Capite & Salvatore: Phil. 3, 21. Infidelium vero ab eodem, tanquam judice, ad judicandum ordinato: Act. 17, 31.
units.tr: Objection. The resurrection will be effected by Christ, with whom unbelievers have no communion; therefore they will not be raised. Answer. The resurrection of the faithful will indeed be effected by Christ as their Head and Saviour: Phil. 3:21. But that of unbelievers by the same Christ as judge appointed to judge: Acts 17:31.

units.la: XX. Judicium extremum est Actus Regni Christi quo ille novissimo die de creaturis rationalibus, visibiliter in nubibus Coeli justam sententiam pronunciabit; atque mox executioni mandabit; justos quidem palam justificando, & vitam aeternam gloriosam judicialiter iis decernendo; injustos autem condemnando, & aeternis cruciatibus adjudicando.
units.tr: XX. The last judgement is an act of the kingdom of Christ, by which on the last day he will pronounce a just sentence on rational creatures, visibly in the clouds of heaven, and will at once commit it to execution: justifying the righteous openly, and judicially decreeing to them glorious eternal life; but condemning the unjust, and adjudging them to eternal torments.

units.la: Quod fit actus Christi, patet ex locis, Joh. 5, 22. Act. 17, 31. Quod ad Regnum Ipsius pertineat; Matth. 25, 31. — Cum venerit Filius hominis cum gloria sua, & omnes sancti Angeli cum Eo, tunc sedebit in Throno gloriae suae. Et congregabuntur coram Eo omnes gentes: & separabit eos, &c. Tunc dicet Rex iis, qui ad dextram Ipsius erunt, &c.
units.tr: That this is an act of Christ is clear from the passages John 5:22 and Acts 17:31. That it pertains to his kingdom, Matt. 25:31: When the Son of man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory. And all nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them, etc. Then the King will say to those who are at his right hand, etc.

units.la: Ex postremo illo loco etiam liquet, Christum adfuturum cum magna demonstratione Majestatis, in propria sua humana natura; per aspectabilem quendam confessum in Throno glorioso, & cum sanctis Angelis, qui ipsi adstitent. Confer Matth. 24, 29, 30, 31. 1 Thess. 4, 16. 2, 1, 7, 8. 2 Petr. 3, 10, 12. Judae, 14, 15. Apoc. 20, 11, 12. Psal. L, 1,-6. Item Exod 19. 16, 18, 19. Gal. 3, 10. Hebr. 12, 18,-21.
units.tr: From this last passage it is also clear that Christ will come with great display of majesty, in his own human nature, with a visible assembly on a glorious throne, and with the holy angels standing by him. Compare Matt. 24:29-31; 1 Thess. 4:16; 2:1, 7, 8; 2 Pet. 3:10, 12; Jude 14, 15; Rev. 20:11, 12; Ps. 50:1-6. Likewise Exod. 19:16, 18, 19; Gal. 3:10; Heb. 12:18-21.

units.la: Ipsi autem fideles etiam judicabunt cum & sub Christo; ejus justum judicium agnoscentes, & approbantes: quod quidem ad arctissimam illorum cum Christo unionem, Regni Ejus participationem, adeoque ipsorum gloriam pertinebit; simulque ad majorem damnatorum convictionem. Hinc Matth. 19, 28. Sedebitis vos etiam in thronis duodecim, judicium serentes. &c. 1. 1 Cor. 6. 2. 3. An ignoratis, Sanctos mundum judicaturos? 2. an ignoratis fore, ut Angelorum judices simus?
