Neque vixit in Monasterio; nec in deserto pluribus incolis destituto. Vide Luc. 1, 39, 40. Ios. 15, 61, 62.
units.tr: Obj. 6. John the Baptist, by his clothing, his food, and his place of dwelling, displayed monastic or anchoretic life. Therefore. Resp. That extraordinary minister of God and forerunner of Christ lived very frugally. But nothing is read of a vow of celibacy in him, nor of voluntary poverty, nor of blind obedience to any man. Nor did he live in a monastery, or in a desert without inhabitants. See Luke 1, 39, 40; Josh. 15, 61, 62.

units.la: XXXIV. Sic de Partibus Ecclesiæ institutæ: suc- cedunt Functiones obeundæ; tùm domatim; tùm publicè.
units.tr: XXXIV. Thus concerning the parts of the instituted Church. There follow the functions to be discharged: partly in the household (domatim), partly in public.

units.la: Vide Act. 20, 20. Nam non solùm ipsis Fidelibus conveniunt varia Exercitia domi suæ peragenda, ut Fidei, Spei, Charitatis; Precum, Lectionis Verbi Divini, Psalmodiæ, Instructionis juniorum & imperitorum, &c. Sed & Antecessoribus domatim obeundæ sunt quædam functiones. Sic enim Pastorum & Seniorum est familiariter fideles admonere & excitare ad officia, quà publicè, quà privatim observanda; reprehendere inordinatos; corroborare infirmos; reconciliare dissidentes; visitare ægros, &c. Luc. 14, 23.
units.tr: See Acts 20:20. For various exercises to be carried out at home belong not only to the faithful themselves, such as those of faith, hope and charity; of prayer, reading of the Divine Word, psalm-singing, and instruction of the young and ignorant, etc. Certain functions are also to be discharged house by house by the office-bearers. For it is the task of pastors and elders to visit the faithful familiarly and to stir them up to duties to be observed partly in public and partly in private; to rebuke the disorderly; to strengthen the weak; to reconcile those at variance; to visit the sick, etc. Luke 14:23.

units.la: 2 Tim. 4, 2. Diaconorum similiter est visitare eos potissimùm qui eleemosynis sustentantur, aut iis indigent; ut necessitatem iltorum sublevent, non solùm rebus corporalibus; verùm etiàm adhortationibus spiritualibus.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 4:2. Likewise it is the task of deacons to visit especially those who are sustained by alms or are in need of them, so that they may relieve their necessity, not only with bodily things but also with spiritual encouragement.

units.la: XXXV. Sequuntur functiones quæ pertinent tùm ad Cœtum publicum, tùm ad alios Conventus Ec- clesiasticos.
units.tr: XXXV. There follow the functions which pertain both to the public assembly and to other ecclesiastical gatherings.

units.la: In Publico Cœtû ordinaria & perpetua sunt Publica S. Scripturæ prælectio, Psalmodia Ecclesiastica, Preces, Concio, Catechizatio, Benedictio, & Eleemosynarum collectio; alia non sunt perpetua.
units.tr: The ordinary and perpetual parts of the public assembly are the public reading of Holy Scripture, ecclesiastical psalmody, prayers, sermon, catechizing, blessing, and the collection of alms. Other things are not perpetual.

units.la: Publica S. Scripturæ prælectio ab Anagnostis, seu Prælectoribus, peragi solet; ità quidem ut Textus Biblicus verè Canonicus clarè & distinctè prælegatur ex ordine, atque omnes pariter audiant, ad spiritualem ædificationem: vel etiam selecti Textus prælegantur, in quibus potissimùm continentur præcipua capita fidei Christianæ, & praxios spiritualis. Atque istâ ratione hoc quoque agitur, ut sermo Christi inhabitet in nobis copiosè, cum omni sapientiâ: Col. 3, 16. Hùc pertinet insignis locus, Deut. 31, 11, 12, 13. Cùm venerit universus Israël, ut appareat coram Jehovâ Deo tuo,- leges Legem istam coram universo Israël. - Et filii eorum, qui non noverunt, audiant, & discant timere Deum vestrum, &c. Insigne exemplum publicæ Lectionis est Nehem. 8, 2, - 5, 8, 18. Vide etiam Act. 13, 27. xv, 21. 2 Cor. 3, 14, 15. Item Luc. 4, 16, - 19. Col. 4, 16.
units.tr: The public reading of Holy Scripture is usually performed by readers (Anagnostae, or lecturers), in such a way that a biblical text, truly canonical, is read clearly and distinctly in order, so that all alike hear it, for spiritual edification. Or selected texts are read, in which the chief heads of the Christian faith and of spiritual practice are principally contained. In this way also it is brought about that the word of Christ dwells richly in us, with all wisdom: Col. 3:16. Here belongs the notable passage Deut. 31:11–13: "When all Israel comes to appear before Jehovah your God, you shall read this law before all Israel ... and their children, who have not known it, shall hear and learn to fear your God," etc. A notable example of public reading is Neh. 8:2–5, 8, 18. See also Acts 13:27; 15:21; 2 Cor. 3:14, 15; likewise Luke 4:16–19; Col. 4:16.

units.la: XXXVI. Psalmodia Ecclesiastica est Cantus Psalmorum, qui in cœtû Ecclesiastico à Fidelibus pari- ter peragitur, ad communem eorum ædificationem, & Dei gloriam.
units.tr: XXXVI. Ecclesiastical psalmody is the singing of psalms, which the faithful perform together in the ecclesiastical assembly, for their common edification and the glory of God.

units.la: Sic diserte 1 Cor. 14, 26. Quid igitur est fratres? quoties convenitis, quisque vestrûm canticum habet: - omnia ad ædificationem fiant. Col. 3, 16. Docendo vos mutuo Psalmis, & hymnis, & cantionibus spiritualibus, cum gratia canentes in vestro corde Domino. Eph. v, 19. Confer 1 Chron. 6, 31, 32. Obtinuit istud exercitium antiquitus in Ecclesia Christiana. Consequenter etiam in Reformatione Psalmodia repurgata fuit a superstitionibus Papisticis, &c.
units.tr: Thus expressly 1 Cor. 14:26: "What is it then, brethren? Whenever you come together, each of you has a psalm; let all things be done for edification." Col. 3:16: "Teaching and admonishing one another in psalms, hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord." Eph. 5:19. Compare 1 Chron. 6:31, 32. This exercise has been in use in the Christian Church from antiquity. Consequently, also in the Reformation, psalmody was purged of Papistical superstitions, etc.

units.la: Plurimum autem facit ad communem ædificationem, ut præeunte idoneo aliquo Præcentore, tota multitudo Ecclesiastica simul canat. Vide Exod. 15, 1. Ista enim ratione singuli fideles in communi quasi schola exercentur, & excitantur ad canendum quoque privatim. Jac. 5, 13. Propterea etiam Psalmodia Ecclesiastica peragenda est lingua communiter nota; ut singuli fideles ita spiritualiter ædificentur; 1 Cor. 14, 15.
units.tr: Moreover, it contributes greatly to common edification that, with some suitable precentor leading, the whole ecclesiastical multitude sing together. See Exod. 15:1. For in this way the individual faithful are, as it were, trained in a common school and stirred to sing privately as well. James 5:13. For this reason ecclesiastical psalmody is also to be performed in a commonly known language, so that the individual faithful may be spiritually edified; 1 Cor. 14:15.

units.la: XXXVII. Quod ad Preces Ecclesiasticas; Act. 6, 4.
units.tr: XXXVII. Concerning ecclesiastical prayers. Acts 6:4.

units.la: cum Apostoli proposuissent de Diaconis administrationi mensarum præficiendis, subjecerunt; Nos vero in Oratione, & administratione Sermonis perdurabimus. Et 1 Cor. 14, 15, 16. ubi de dono Linguarum; Quid est igitur? orabo spiritu, sed orabo etiam intelligentia: -- quandoquidem si benedixeris spiritu, is qui implet locum Idiota, quomodo dicturus est Amen ad tuam gratiarum actionem? nam quid dicas nescit. Nam tu quidem bene gratias agis; sed alius non ædificatur. Vide etiam Nehem. 9, 15. Act. 21, 5.
units.tr: When the apostles had proposed that deacons be appointed over the administration of tables, they added: "But we will continue in prayer and in the ministry of the word." And 1 Cor. 14:15, 16, where concerning the gift of tongues: "What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, but I will pray also with the understanding ... for if you bless with the spirit, how will he who fills the place of the unlearned say Amen to your thanksgiving? For he does not know what you say. For you indeed give thanks well, but the other is not edified." See also Nehem. 9, 15; Acts 21:5.

units.la: Hinc deducimus primo contra Anabaptistas, Ministrum in Precibus Ecclesiasticis clara voce præire debere reliquæ multitudini; quæ animo & cogitationibus, vel etiam submissa voce, eum sequatur: cæteroquin 1. non est una communis omnium oratio.
units.tr: From this we deduce, first, against the Anabaptists, that the minister must lead the ecclesiastical prayers with a clear voice before the rest of the multitude, which follows him in mind and thought, or even in a lowered voice. Otherwise: (1) there is not one common prayer of all.

units.la: 2. Reliqui non possunt ædificari per orationem Ministri.
units.tr: (2) The rest cannot be edified by the minister's prayer.

units.la: 3. Non possunt ad eam dicere Amen.
units.tr: (3) They cannot say Amen to it.

units.la: 4. Nou 4. Non possunt aliàs commodè singulorum preces pariter finiri.
units.tr: (4) Otherwise the prayers of individuals cannot conveniently be brought to an end together.

units.la: Colligimus secundo contra Pontifícios, Preces illas peragendas esse linguâ vernaculâ, & communiter notâ in coetu: sic enim 1. Apostolus diserte docet, etiàm intelligentiâ orandum esse.
units.tr: We gather, second, against the Papists, that those prayers are to be performed in the vernacular, commonly understood in the assembly. For thus: (1) the Apostle expressly teaches that one must pray also with understanding.

units.la: 2. Docet, reliquos alioqui non ædificari.
units.tr: (2) He teaches that otherwise the others are not edified.

units.la: 3. Nec posse dicere Amen ad precationem linguâ peregrinâ habitam.
units.tr: (3) Nor can they say Amen to a prayer uttered in a foreign tongue.

units.la: 4. Nec potest esse communis cultus rationalis, qui non intelligitur ab omnibus communiter. Vide 1 Cor. 14, 23.
units.tr: (4) Nor can there be a common rational worship that is not commonly understood by all. See 1 Cor. 14:23.

units.la: XXXVIII. Quoniàm Preces in spiritû & veritate peragi debent, ex sincerâ & continuâ animi intentione ac devotione, quâ Ministrum præire oportet, & reliquos subsequi; inde etiam sequitur, minus recte in Precibus Ecclesiasticis adhiberi Antiphonas, & Responsoria; uti fieri solet in Officio Romano: ista enim magis affinia sunt Hominum inter se Dialogis, quam communibus omnium Precibus ad Deum.
units.tr: XXXVIII. Since prayers ought to be performed in spirit and in truth, from a sincere and continuous intention and devotion of mind, in which the minister ought to lead and the rest to follow, it follows also that antiphons and responsories are used less rightly in ecclesiastical prayers, as is customary in the Roman Office. For these are more akin to dialogues between men than to the common prayers of all to God.

units.la: Et quoniàm in Precibus illis consistit magna pars Ministerii Ecclesiastici; sequitur, isti Ministerio nequaquàm satisfieri, si solummodò certæ quædam Formulæ precum publicè prælegantur, aut memoriter recitentur: hoc enim à quolibet fieri facilè poterit. Et spiritualis intentio ac devotio plus requirit, respectû præsentis cujusque occasionis. Formulæ interim quædam rectè habentur, in usum incipientium & imperitorum; atque ut constet, quæ soleant ac debeant esse præcipua ingredientia Precum Ecclesiasticarum.
units.tr: And since a great part of the ecclesiastical ministry consists in those prayers, it follows that this ministry is by no means discharged if only certain set formulas of prayer are read publicly or recited from memory; for anyone can easily do this. Spiritual intention and devotion require more, with regard to the present occasion of each case. Meanwhile certain formulas are rightly kept for the use of beginners and the unskilled, and so that it is clear what ought to be, and usually are, the principal ingredients of ecclesiastical prayers.

units.la: Perpetuæ autem sunt Preces, quæ à Ministro tum Concioni præmittuntur, tum eâ finitâ peraguntur. Minister etiam Catechizationes, & Sacramentorum administrationes, à Precibus inchoat; & Precibus, ubi peractæ sunt, terminat.
units.tr: Prayers are perpetual, however, which the minister says both before the sermon and after it is finished. The minister also begins catechizings and administrations of the sacraments with prayer, and when they are done, ends them with prayer.

units.la: * XXXIX. Concio est Textus alicujus Biblici plenior explicatio & applicatio, à Ministro coram Auditoribus facta, ad spiritualem ædificationem. Huc 1. pertinent exempla, tum V. tum N. T. utpote Nehem. 8, 7, 8, 9. Et Levitæ intelligere faciebant populum Legem: populus autem erat in loco suo. Et legerunt in libro ipso, in Lege Dei explanatè, & appositerunt intellectum, & intellexerunt Scripturam ipsam. Ipse Servator in Novo Testamento, Luc. 4, 20, 21, 22. in Synagoga Nazarenâ Scripturam explicuit & applicuit. Vide etiam xxiv, 27. Itemque de Philippo, Act. 8, 35. & de Paulo, xx, 7.
units.tr: XXXIX. A sermon is a fuller explanation and application of some biblical text, made by the minister before the hearers, for spiritual edification. To this belong, first, examples from both the Old and the New Testament, such as Neh. 8:7–9: "And the Levites caused the people to understand the law, and the people stood in their place. And they read in the book, in the law of God, distinctly, and gave the sense, and they understood the Scripture itself." The Saviour himself, in the New Testament, explained and applied Scripture in the synagogue at Nazareth: Luke 4:20–22. See also Luke 24:27. Likewise of Philip, Acts 8:35, and of Paul, Acts 20:7.

units.la: 2. Speciale opus Ministerii in Verbo: Unde Act. 4, 4. Nos in Oratione & administratione Sermonis perduravimus. Rom. 10, 14, 15. Quomodo credent ei, de quo non audierint? quomodo autem audient absque Prædicante? quomodo autem prædicabunt, nisi missi fuerint? sicut scriptum est &c. 12, 7, 8. 1 Thess. 5, 12, 13. 1 Tim. 5, 17. 2, II. 2. IV. 2.
units.tr: Second, the special work of the ministry is in the Word, whence Acts 4:4: "We have continued in prayer and in the administration of the word." Rom. 10:14, 15: "How shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? And how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach unless they are sent? As it is written," etc. Rom. 12:7, 8; 1 Thess. 5:12, 13; 1 Tim. 5:17; 2 Tim. 2:2; 4:2.

units.la: 3. In ipsum quoque finem conscripti sunt Libri sacri:
units.tr: Third, the holy books were also written for this very end:

units.la: 2 Tim. 3, 16, 17. Tota Scriptura Divinitus est inspirata; & utilis ad doctrinam, ad redargutionem, ad correctionem, ad disciplinam quæ est in justitia: ut persectus sit homo Dei, ad omne opus bonum perfecte instructus. Rom. 15, 4, IV, 23, 24. 1 Cor. 10, 11. 1 Tim. 4, 13, -16.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 3:16, 17: "All Scripture is divinely inspired and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for training in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work." Rom. 15:4; 4:23, 24; 1 Cor. 10:11; 1 Tim. 4:13–16.

units.la: 4. His consentanea est praxis Ecclesiæ antiquæ.
units.tr: Fourth, the practice of the ancient Church is consonant with these.

units.la: Concludimus ergo contra Libertinos quosdam, non sufficere, si ipse contextus Biblicus per Anagnosten aliquem nude prælegatur; sed Concliones insuper habendas esse.
units.tr: We conclude, therefore, against certain Libertines, that it is not enough for the Biblical text merely to be read aloud bare by some reader; sermons must in addition be delivered.

units.la: Obj. Atqui S. Scriptura perfecta est & perspicua. Ergo. Resp. Ipsa in se objective talis est: attamen Deus hominum ignorantiæ, tarditati, & inadvertentiæ subveniri etiam voluit, per istiusmodi explicationes, & applicationes. XL. Initio autem Textus aliquis Biblicus prælegi debet: exemplo ipsius Christi, Luc. 4, 16-22.
units.tr: Objection: Holy Scripture is perfect and perspicuous. Therefore (no sermon is needed). Reply: It is so in itself, objectively; yet God has also willed that the ignorance, slowness and inattentiveness of men be remedied by such explanations and applications. XL. At the beginning, some Biblical text ought to be read, following the example of Christ himself, Luke 4, 16-22.

units.la: Prælegendus autem est Textus lingua communiter nota : quod Auditorum ædificatio prorsus requirit.
units.tr: The text to be read should be in a language commonly known, which the edification of the hearers absolutely requires.

units.la: Aliquando seliguntur Textus, qui conditioni Auditorum, ac præsenti tempori, magis convenire videntur; aliàs libri quidam sacri, aut capita, ex ordine tractantur, tum V. tum N. T.
units.tr: Sometimes texts are selected which seem better suited to the condition of the hearers and to the present time; at other times certain books or chapters of Scripture, both Old and New Testament, are treated in order.

units.la: Minus recte eædem duntaxat sectiones quotannis perpetuo repetuntur; Euangelia scil. & Epistolæ Dominicales: sic enim Concionatorum ignaviæ, & Auditorum ignorantiæ, litatur.
units.tr: It is less right that the same sections alone be repeated every year in perpetuity, namely the Gospels and the Epistles for the Sundays; for in this way the idleness of preachers and the ignorance of hearers are gratified.

units.la: Imo & Textus prolixiores præferendi sunt ordinariè brevioribus: hinc enim facilius multa & varia, ad communem ædificationem utilissima, elici possunt; quibus Auditores solidius instruentur.
units.tr: Indeed, longer texts are generally to be preferred to shorter ones, for from them many and varied things, most useful for common edification, can more easily be drawn out, by which the hearers are more solidly instructed.

units.la: Rectè etiam ob maximam necessitatem, & amplissimam utilitatem, quotannis repetuntur capita Doctrinæ Catecheticæ: ut in Ecclesiis nostris per singulas Dominicas concionibus pomeridianis fieri solet. Sic enim Apostolus, Phil. 3, 1. Eadem scribere vobis, mihi quidem haud piget; vobis autem tutum est. Et 2 Tim. 1. 13. Expressam formam teneto sanorum sermonum, quos à me audisti, cum fide & charitate, quæ est in Christo Iesu.
units.tr: It is also rightly done, because of the very great need and the very wide usefulness, that the heads of catechetical doctrine are repeated every year, as is customary in our churches in the afternoon sermons on each Sunday. For so the Apostle says, Phil. 3, 1: "To write the same things to you is indeed no trouble to me, but it is safe for you." And 2 Tim. 1, 13: "Hold fast the pattern of sound words which you have heard from me, in faith and love which are in Christ Jesus."

units.la: XLI. Sed nunc paucis dicamus de Inventione, Dispositione, Exornatione, & Actione Concionatoria!
units.tr: XLI. But now let us say a few words about the invention, arrangement, ornamentation and delivery of the sermon.

units.la: Inventio versatur circa materiam Concionis. Ea vero, quantum ad εὕρεσιν attinet, petenda est primo ac potissimum ex libro S. Scripturæ; ut sit tractatio vere Scripturaria: juxta 1 Petr. 4, 11. Si quis loquitur, loquatur ut eloquia Dei. 1 Cor. 11, 13. Confer Act. 18, 14.
units.tr: Invention concerns the matter of the sermon. As far as discovery [εὕρεσιν] is concerned, it is to be sought first and above all from the book of Holy Scripture, so that the treatment is truly scriptural, according to 1 Pet. 4, 11: "If anyone speaks, let him speak as the oracles of God." 1 Cor. 11, 13. Compare Acts 18, 14.

units.la: 2 Tim. 3, 16, 17. Sed & secundario ex libro naturæ; nam & Cœli enarrant gloriam Dei, &c. Psal. 19, 2, 3; Act. 14, 17. Accedit tertio liber conscientiæ, & experientiæ spiritualis; sed juxta librum Scripturæ: sic enim Concionator plurimum juvabitur ac dirigetur in applicationibus feliciter faciendis: Hebr.5,2,3. Rom.7, 13.--. Atque item quarto liber Ecclesiæ; cujus conditionem sibi Concionator habere debet quam exploratissimam, ut norit quid maxime dici conveniat. Vide Hebr. 5, 11,--. 1 Cor. 3, 1, 2, 3. Phil. 3, 15, 16. Subsidiariam quoque operam præstabunt Conciones aliorum recte observatæ, & Scripta insignium Theologorum.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 3, 16, 17. But secondarily also from the book of nature, for "the heavens declare the glory of God," etc., Ps. 19, 2, 3; Acts 14, 17. Thirdly, there is added the book of conscience and of spiritual experience, but read according to the book of Scripture; for thus the preacher will be greatly helped and directed in making the applications successfully: Heb. 5, 2, 3; Rom. 7, 13. And likewise, fourthly, the book of the Church, whose condition the preacher ought to know as thoroughly as possible, so that he knows what is most fitting to say. See Heb. 5, 11; 1 Cor. 3, 1, 2, 3; Phil. 3, 15, 16. Sermons of others rightly observed, and the writings of distinguished theologians, will also furnish subsidiary help.

units.la: Observandum vero, quod Inventio debeat esse varia & rara: non semper, aut sæpe eadem; ne fastidium creetur Auditoribus: Matth. 13, 52 Omnis Scriba edoctus Regno cælorum, similis est cuipiam patrifamilias, qui profert e thesauro suo nova & vetera.
units.tr: It must be observed, however, that the invention ought to be varied and uncommon, not always or often the same, lest weariness be created in the hearers: Matt. 13, 52: "Every scribe instructed for the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who brings out of his treasure new things and old."

units.la: XLII. Partes constituentes potissimum sunt Expli- catio Textus, & Applicatio.
units.tr: XLII. The constituent parts are chiefly the explanation of the text and the application.

units.la: In Explicatione, genuinus sensus ex dictionibus ac phrasibus, antecedentibus & consequentibus, nec non collatione similium, & quandoque dissimilium, clare & accommodate ad captum Auditorum proponendus est. Cavendum autem ne ea sit nimis prolixa, nec operosa; neque tamen obscura.
units.tr: In the explanation, the genuine sense is to be set forth clearly and suitably to the grasp of the hearers, from the words and phrases, from what precedes and follows, and also from the comparison of similar and sometimes dissimilar passages. Care must be taken that it is not too long or laborious, nor, on the other hand, obscure.

units.la: Applicatio fit per Documenta, & eorum Usus.
units.tr: Application is made through doctrines and their uses.

units.la: Documentum hoc loco est thesis Theologica, quæ ex Textu jam explicato vel immediate conficitur, vel per proximam & evidentem consequentiam deducitur.
units.tr: Here a doctrine is a theological proposition which is either drawn immediately from the text already explained, or deduced by a near and evident consequence.

units.la: Usus documenti est ejus propior & efficacior applicatio ad animos Auditorum; tum ratione veritatis: quo pertinet instructio, & oppositi erroris refutatio: Rom. 15, 4. 2 Tim. 3, 16 Tit. 1, 7, 9, 10, 11. Tum ratione boni honesti: quo pertinent querelæ, reprehensiones, admonitiones, methodica explicatio probæ praxios, media & adminicula virtutum, remedia vitiorum, signa sincerae praxios: 2 Tim. 3. 16, 17. IV, 1, 2. I, I, 5. 1, 1, 5. Tit. 1, 13. II, 11, 12, 13. 2 Cor. 13, 5. Tum etiam ratione boni jucundi: quo pertinent corroborationes in fide ac spe, & consolationes adversus quævis mala tristia; nec non signa status illius, cui ista bona sunt propria: Isef. 40, 1, 2. 1 Thess. 4, 18. Rom. 5, 1,-5. VIII, I, 10, II, 14,-18, 24,-. 2 Cor. 1, 5, 6, 7. 2 Thess. 3, 3. Jac. I, 1, 3, 4. 1 Petr. I, 3,-9.
units.tr: The use of a doctrine is its closer and more effective application to the minds of the hearers; this is done with respect to truth, to which belongs instruction and the refutation of the opposite error: Rom. 15, 4; 2 Tim. 3, 16; Titus 1, 7, 9, 10, 11. And with respect to the good and honourable, to which belong complaints, rebukes, admonitions, the methodical explanation of sound practice, the means and aids of virtues, the remedies for vices, and the signs of sincere practice: 2 Tim. 3, 16, 17; 4, 1, 2; 1, 1, 5; Titus 1, 13; 2, 11, 12, 13; 2 Cor. 13, 5. Also with respect to the good and pleasant, to which belong strengthening in faith and hope, and consolations against any sad evils, as well as the signs of that state to which these good things belong: Isa. 40, 1, 2; 1 Thess. 4, 18; Rom. 5, 1-5; 8, 1, 10; 11, 14-18, 24; 2 Cor. 1, 5, 6, 7; 2 Thess. 3, 3; James 1, 1, 3, 4; 1 Pet. 1, 3-9.

units.la: XLIII. Quantum ad Dispositionem attinet; ubi quis recte præmeditatus fuerit Textus sui Scopum, cum Explicatione & Applicationibus, non multum laborandum erit de Exordio. Hoc enim non absolute, nec semper necessarium est. Ubi autem adhibebitur, sumatur à materiâ Scopo proximâ; & ad Textum perspicuè accommodetur.
units.tr: XLIII. As regards the arrangement: when someone has rightly pondered the scope of his text, together with the explanation and applications, he will not need to labour much over the exordium. For this is not absolutely or always necessary. Where it is used, it should be taken from the matter, from a scope near at hand, and fitted clearly to the text.

units.la: Pro Narratione, Textus summatim proponatur, ejusque Scopus perspicuè indicetur.
units.tr: For the narration, the text is to be set out briefly and its scope clearly indicated.

units.la: Succedit Distributio; quæ non verbis, sed sensu niti debet: ac porro instituì in partes quam paucissimas; neque enim facile superandus est numerus ternarius, aut quaternarius. Cavendum porro, ne Subdivisionum numerus nimium crescat.
units.tr: Next comes the division, which ought to rest not on words but on sense; and it should be made into as few parts as possible, for the number three or four is not easily exceeded. Care must further be taken that the number of subdivisions does not grow too large.

units.la: Sequitur Explicatio: ubi genuinus sensus perspicuè proponatur; ex antecedentibus & consequentibus demonstretur; atque item per loca parallela illustretur & confirmetur; vel etiam per exempla, tum similia, tum dissimilia.
units.tr: Then follows the explanation, in which the genuine sense is clearly set forth, demonstrated from what precedes and follows, and likewise illustrated and confirmed through parallel passages, or even through examples, both similar and dissimilar.

units.la: Deinde instituitur Applicatio per Documenta, eorumque Usus. Potissimum vero unumquodque Documentum cum suis Usibus, subjiciendum est illi parti, aut particulæ, unde ipsum adæquate fluit.
units.tr: Then the application is set up through doctrines and their uses. Indeed, each doctrine together with its uses should be placed under that part or particle from which it flows fully.

units.la: Restat Epilogus; qui non debet esse operosus, vel admodum artificiosus: Concionem interim finiat adhortatione potius, aut consolatione; quam elencho, aut reprehensione.
units.tr: There remains the epilogue, which ought not to be laborious or too artful; let the preacher end the sermon rather with exhortation or consolation than with refutation or rebuke.

units.la: XLIV. Quod ad Exornationem; cavendum Con- cionatori, ne Stylus hinc fit rusticus, aut nimis plebeius
units.tr: XLIV. Concerning embellishment: the preacher must take care that his style does not become rustic or too plebeian,

units.la: jus; nec inde nimis sublimis, aut affectatus: sed gravis, & Scripturarius; attamen perspicuus.
units.tr: nor on the other hand too lofty or affected, but grave and scriptural, yet still clear.

units.la: Ad Actionem pertinent Vox & Gestus. Illa fit clara; & distincta, rebusque accommodata.
units.tr: To delivery belong voice and gesture. The voice should be clear and distinct, and suited to the matter.

units.la: In his; totius Corporis status fit erectus. Vultus inserviat exprimendis affectibus. Brachium, praecipue dextrum, moveatur decore. Manus complicatae precibus conveniunt: Digiti complicati reprehensionibus; explicati demonstrationi & numerationi inserviunt.
units.tr: As for the body, the whole posture should be upright. The face should serve to express the feelings. The arm, especially the right, should move with grace. Hands joined together suit prayers; fingers folded serve for rebukes, while fingers extended serve for pointing out and counting.

units.la: XLV. Catechizatio est familiarior quaedam institutio Religionis, per explicationes ad captum Catechumenorum accommodatas, itemque per interrogationes & responsiones. Prov. 22, 6. Imbue puerum juxta viam suam: etiam cum senuerit, non recedet ab ea. Gal. 6, 6. Hebr. 6, 1, 2, 3.
units.tr: XLV. Catechizing is a more familiar instruction in religion, given through explanations adapted to the understanding of the catechumens, and likewise through questions and answers. Prov. 22:6. Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it. Gal. 6:6. Heb. 6:1, 2, 3.

units.la: Ratione loci dispescitur Catechizatio in Domesticam; quae in familiis peragitur a Parentibus, aliisve personis idoneis: Scholasticam; quae in scholis a Praeceptoribus: & Ecclesiasticam; quae in Ecclesiis peragitur a Pastoribus, aliisve Catechistis. Haec autem vel publica est, vel quasi-publica.
units.tr: With regard to place, catechizing is divided into domestic, which is carried on in households by parents or other suitable persons; scholastic, which is carried on in schools by teachers; and ecclesiastical, which is carried on in churches by ministers or other catechists. This last is either public or quasi-public.

units.la: Ratione eorum qui exercentur Catechizatio vel est rudiorum, vel provectiorum. Atque ita Dogmaticae Catechizationes ad singulorum captum fiunt. Accedunt Catechizationes elenticae, de Controversiis; Practicae, in quibus Praxis doctrinae Catecheticae pertractatur; atque item Scripturariae, ad librum aliquem S. Scripturae.
units.tr: With regard to those who are instructed, catechizing is either for beginners or for the more advanced. Thus dogmatic catechizings are adapted to the capacity of each individual. To these are added elenctic catechizings, concerning controversies; practical ones, in which the practice of catechetical doctrine is treated; and likewise scriptural ones, on some book of Holy Scripture.

units.la: XLVI. Benedictio nunc intelligitur, qua Concionator, peractis sacris, coetum Ecclesiasticum dimittit. Vide Num. 6, 23, & confer Clausulas in Epistolis Paulinis. Istiusmodi autem Benedictio non solum est apprecatoria; sed etiam denunciatoria, secundum gratiosam Dei promissionem.
units.tr: XLVI. The blessing is understood as that by which the preacher, when the sacred acts are finished, dismisses the ecclesiastical assembly. See Num. 6:23, and compare the closing formulas in the Pauline epistles. Such a blessing is not only a prayer, but also a declaration, according to God's gracious promise.

units.la: Superest Eleemosynarum collectio per Diaconos in coetu tû Ecclesiastico facienda; ut possint illas deinceps pauperibus distribuere, atque ita necessitatem eorum sublevare. Vide Joh. 12, 6. Actor. 4, 34, 35, 37. v, 2. Sed postea ab Apostolis, consentiente fidelium multitudine, hæc provincia Diaconis demandata fuit; Act. 6, 2,
units.tr: There remains the collection of alms, to be made by the deacons in the ecclesiastical assembly, so that they may afterwards distribute these to the poor and so relieve their need. See John 12:6; Acts 4:34, 35, 37; 5:2. But afterwards this duty was entrusted to the deacons by the apostles, with the consent of the multitude of believers; Acts 6:2,

units.la: 3. Confer 1 Cor. 16, 1, 2.
units.tr: 3. Compare 1 Cor. 16:1, 2.

units.la: XLVII. Sequuntur Agenda in publico cœtu Ecclesi- astico, non perpetua; attamen suis occasionibus recur- rentia.
units.tr: XLVII. There follow the acts performed in the public ecclesiastical assembly, which are not perpetual, yet recur on their own occasions.

units.la: Atque hæc potissimum sunt Administratio S. Baptismi, & Cœnæ Dominicæ; Excommunicatio, & Excommunicatorum reconciliatio; publica Ministrorum confirmatio; Jejunium publicum, & dies Eucharisticus; ac tandem Matrimonii confirmatio.
units.tr: These are chiefly the administration of holy Baptism and of the Lord's Supper; excommunication and the reconciliation of the excommunicated; the public confirmation of ministers; the public fast and the thanksgiving day; and finally the public confirmation of marriage.

units.la: De Sacramentis Baptismi, & Sacræ Cœnæ, eorumque Administratione, actum est sup. cap. 18.
units.tr: Concerning the sacraments of Baptism and the Holy Supper, and their administration, it was treated above in chapter 18.

units.la: Excommunicatio publicè etiam peragitur, secundum formulam in Liturgiâ nostrâ expressam, quoties necessitas postulat. Ubi scil. membrum aliquod Ecclesiæ, nobiscum prius etiam Cœnæ Dominicæ particeps, à veritate fidei Christianæ defecit ad errores fundamentales, aut à sanctimoniâ vitæ ad peccata insigniter scandalosa; nec præviasadmonitiones multas ac varias audivit. Non tamen ad plenam & publicam Excommunicationem proceditur, nisi explorata & compertâ satis ejus pertinaciâ. Vide Matth. 18, 17. 1 Cor. 5, 2, 5, 13. Tit. 3, 10.
units.tr: Excommunication is also carried out publicly, according to the form expressed in our liturgy, whenever necessity demands it. This is so when some member of the Church, who had previously shared with us in the Lord's Supper, has fallen away from the truth of the Christian faith into fundamental errors, or from holiness of life into sins that are notoriously scandalous, and has not heeded many and various earlier admonitions. Yet full and public excommunication is not proceeded to unless his obstinacy has been sufficiently examined and established. See Matt. 18:17; 1 Cor. 5:2, 5, 13; Titus 3:10.

units.la: Si verò contingat, excommunicatum postea resipiscere, veramque emendationem promittere ac reipsâ præstare, Ecclesia pœnitentem illum denuo admittit; juxta 2 Cor. II, 7. Atque adeo publica ejus Reconciliatio etiam celebratur.
units.tr: But if it happens that the excommunicated person afterwards repents, promises true amendment and actually makes it good, the Church receives him again as a penitent, according to 2 Cor. II, 7. And so his public reconciliation is also celebrated.

units.la: XLVIII. Publica Ministrorum confirmatio est tum Pastorum, tùm Seniorum gubernantium, ac Diaconorum, prius electorum: peragitur quælibet coram facie Ecclesiæ, post trinam denunciationem; ut sic exploretur & obtineatur publicus omnium confensus.
units.tr: XLVIII. The public confirmation of ministers applies both to the ministers and to the elders who govern, and to the deacons, who have first been elected. Each is carried out in the presence of the Church after a threefold announcement, so that the general consent of all may be tested and obtained.

units.la: Jejunium publicum, urgente publica aliqua calamitate, aut insigni periculo, indicitur; & celebrari solet hac ratione, ut ab Anagnostis prælegantur capita Biblica huic occasioni convenientia, similesque Psalmi cantentur: Et à Pastore Conciones Precesque hùc quoque accommodentur; Auditores ad considerationem peccatorum, & resipiscentiam adhortando.
units.tr: A public fast is proclaimed when some public calamity or extraordinary danger presses. It is usually observed in this way: the readers read aloud biblical chapters suited to the occasion, and similar psalms are sung; and the minister also adapts sermons and prayers to it, urging the hearers to consider their sins and to repent.

units.la: Dies Eucharisticus instituitur, cum insignia quædam beneficia Dei percepimus, ad publicam gratitudinem ipsi præstandam. Hoc fine præleguntur Capita Biblica praxin gratitudinis continentia, & tales Psalmi cantantur. Pastores autem eandem gratitudinis praxin tum in Concionibus serio urgent; tum in Orationibus præstant, ac porro promittunt Ecclesiæ nomine.
units.tr: A day of thanksgiving is appointed when we have received some notable blessings from God, to be offered to him in public gratitude. For this purpose biblical chapters setting forth the practice of gratitude are read, and such psalms are sung. The ministers, moreover, both earnestly press this same practice of gratitude in their sermons, and exhibit it in their prayers, and further promise it in the name of the Church.

units.la: Publica Matrimonii Confirmatio, ubi occasio eam postulat, peragitur quoque juxta formulam in Liturgia Ecclesiarum nostrarum expressam.
units.tr: The public confirmation of marriage, when the occasion requires it, is likewise carried out according to the form expressed in the liturgy of our churches.

units.la: Sunt & Exercitia, quæ sub ductû Doctorum Academicorum, in ordine ad Ecclesiam, ejusque ædificationem, haberi solent. Eaque sunt Publica, vel Privata.
units.tr: There are also exercises, which are usually held under the direction of the academic teachers, with a view to the Church and its edification. These are either public or private.

units.la: Publica, sunt tum Lectiones, tum Disputationes Privata autem sunt Collegia Dogmatica, vel Polemica, vel Practica, &c.
units.tr: The public ones are both lectures and disputations. The private ones are dogmatic, polemical or practical colleges, etc.

units.la: XLIX. Succedunt alii Conventus Ecclesiastici: qui vel sunt Antecessorum cujusque Ecclesiæ particularis institutæ; vel Delegatorum à pluribus Ecclesiis particularibus. In singulis Ecclesiis particularibus institutis occurrit Synedrium, sive Presbyterium. Paulus diserte Πρεσβυτέριον appellat, 1 Tim. 4,14. Collegium scil. Presbyterorum, tum simul docentium, tum solummodo gubernantium. Ad hoc, ubi Presby-teri teri sunt pauciores, etiam Diaconi admittuntur. In isto autem Collegio, quia Deus non est incompositi status auctor; sed pacis; 1 Cor. 14, 33. ut omnia decenter & ordine fiant, Præses requiritur, qui negotia tractanda proponat; suffragia singulorum roget & colligat; atque ex votis, seu communibus, seu pluribus ac potioribus, conclusionem formet. Quæ autem sic tractata & conclusa sunt, in libro peculiari consignantur: in eum finem, ubi Pastores plures sunt; Præsidi adjungitur Scriba.
units.tr: XLIX. There follow other ecclesiastical assemblies, which are either those of the elders of each particular established church, or those of delegates from several particular churches. In each established particular church there is a synedrium, or presbytery. Paul expressly calls it presbyterium [Πρεσβυτέριον], 1 Tim. 4:14: the college, that is, of elders, both those who teach together and those who only govern. To this, where the elders are fewer, deacons are also admitted. Now in this college, because God is the author not of disorder but of peace (1 Cor. 14:33), and so that all things may be done decently and in order, a president is required, who lays out the matters to be treated, asks for and collects the votes of each, and forms the conclusion from the votes, whether common or of the majority and the more weighty. What has been so treated and concluded is recorded in a special book. For this purpose, where there are several ministers, a clerk is added to the president.

units.la: L. Negotia ad Presbyterium pertinentia, potissimum sunt; primò curare ut recte peragantur ea, quæ ad Cœtum publicum, communemque ædificationem, spectant; atque adeò ut suis etiam libris identidem inscribantur nomina Baptizatorum, ad Cœnæ Dominicæ communionem admissorum, & Matrimonio in Ecclesiâ junctorum.
units.tr: L. The matters pertaining to the presbytery are chiefly these: first, to take care that those things which concern the public assembly and common edification are carried out correctly, and therefore that the names of those baptized, of those admitted to communion in the Lord's Supper, and of those joined in marriage in the Church are written in its books from time to time.

units.la: Secundò, quæ in domesticis singulorum membrorum Ecclesiæ visitationibus vitiosa observata sunt, & per Pastores Senioresve corrigi non potuerunt, ad Presbyterium referri debent; ut decernatur, quid facto opus sit.
units.tr: Second, the faults observed in the domestic visitations of the individual members of the Church, which could not be corrected by the ministers or elders, must be referred to the presbytery, so that it may decide what needs to be done.

units.la: Tertiò, Attendendum, ut in Antecessoribus Ecclesiasticis, tùm in reliquis Membris, conservetur puritas fidei, & sanctimonia vitæ.
units.tr: Third, care must be taken that the purity of faith and holiness of life are preserved both among the ecclesiastical teachers and among the other members.

units.la: Quartò, Ubi postulat necessitas, progrediendum est ulterius in Disciplina Ecclesiastica. Hanc 1. pro N. T. instituit Christus, dicens Petro, Matth. 16, 19 Et tibi dabo claves Regni cœlorum: & quicquid ligaveris in terrâ, erit ligatum in cœlis; & quicquid solveris in terrâ, erit solutum in cœlis. Ac similia reliquis Discipulis; xviii; 15,-18. Joh. 20, 23. Quæ cùm semper necessaria sint ad Ecclesiæ ædificationem, certè ad Ministros ordinarios etiam extendi debent.
units.tr: Fourth, where necessity requires, the church discipline must be pressed further. Christ instituted this for the New Testament, saying to Peter: Matt. 16:19. And I will give to you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven; and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven. Likewise to the other disciples, Matt. 18:15-18; John 20:23. Since these things are always necessary for the edification of the Church, they must certainly be extended also to the ordinary ministers.

units.la: 2. Apostoli consequenter Ecclesiis eam tradiderunt: 1 Cor. 5, 2, 7. de homine quodam incestuoso; Cum potestate Domini nostri Jesu Christi tradatur iste homo Satanæ, ad interitum carnis, ut spiritus salvus sit. Ac porro 9, 11, 12, 13. - Tollite hunc sceleratum e vobis. 2 Thess. 3, 14, 15. Tit. 3, 10, 11.
units.tr: 2. The apostles consequently handed this over to the churches: 1 Cor. 5:2, 7, concerning a certain incestuous man: With the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, let this man be delivered to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved. And further 5:9, 11, 12, 13: Put away that wicked person from among you. 2 Thess. 3:14, 15; Titus 3:10, 11.

units.la: 3. Indicantur fines, quorum gratia necessaria est ista Disciplina; tum ratione Fœderis Divini, ac Sigillorum ejus, ne scil. ista profanentur; tum ratione Dei, iræque ipsius, ne hæc adversus totam Ecclesiam concitetur: Matth. 7, 6. Ne date quod sanctum est canibus. cum Psal. L. 16, 17. Impio dixit Deus; quid assumis pactum meum in os tuum? tu vero odisti disciplinam. Ac 1 Cor. 5, 6. An nescitis, paulo fermenti totam massam fermentari. xi, 30, 31. Propterea inter vos multi sunt ægroti & valetudinarii; & dormiunt multi. Hæc Corinthiis propter Disciplinæ neglectum evenerunt.
units.tr: 3. The ends are indicated for the sake of which this discipline is necessary: both with regard to the divine covenant and its seals, lest these be profaned, and with regard to God and his anger, lest it be stirred up against the whole Church: Matt. 7:6, Do not give what is holy to dogs; compare Psalm L. 16, 17: But to the wicked God said, What have you to do with declaring my statutes, or taking my covenant in your mouth? Yet you hate discipline. And 1 Cor. 5:6, Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump? 11:30, 31: For this reason many among you are weak and sickly, and many sleep. These things happened to the Corinthians on account of their neglect of discipline.

units.la: 4. Idem analogice colligi potest ex cerimonialibus quibusdam constitutionibus V. T. Exod. 12, 48. Num. 9, 6, 7, 10. &c.
units.tr: 4. The same can be inferred by analogy from certain ceremonial regulations of the Old Testament: Exod. 12, 48; Num. 9, 6, 7, 10, etc.

units.la: Exc. Excommunicatio ab Apostolis perata, fuit extraordinaria: ut videre est in Ananiâ & Sapphirâ subito & miraculose necatis; Act. 5, 1, - 11. Resp. In Apostolica Ecclesia fatemur circa Disciplinam aliquando fuisse extraordinaria quædam adjuncta: verum res ipsa est usus perpetui; atque sic Ecclesiis mandata.
units.tr: Exc. Excommunication pronounced by the Apostles was extraordinary, as is seen in Ananias and Sapphira, who were struck dead suddenly and miraculously: Acts 5, 1–11. Resp. We grant that in the Apostolic Church there were sometimes certain extraordinary additions concerning discipline. But the thing itself is of perpetual use, and so it has been committed to the Churches.

units.la: Obj. Coercitio peccantium pertinet ad Magistratum Politicum. Ergo. Resp. Magistratui Politico tarta tecta conservari debet sua potestas Politica, ratione status exterioris ac temporalis. Verum nunc de mero ministerio agimus, ordinato per institutionem Christi ad hominem interiorem, & statum ejus æternum.
units.tr: Obj. The punishment of sinners belongs to the civil magistrate; therefore... Resp. The civil magistrate's political power must remain entire, by reason of the outward and temporal state. But now we are speaking of the pure ministry, which by Christ's institution is ordained for the inner man and his eternal state.

units.la: LI. Ecclesiam appellavit Christus in negotio hujus Disciplinæ, Matth. 18, 17. non tamen eo sensu, quasi omnia istuc spectantia per omnia & singula ejus Membra necessario agi deberent; quod volunt Brownista. Nam cùm Ecclesia sit consideranda ut corpus organicum, quod distincta habet membra, quibus distinctæ etiam sunt proprietates & operationes; ideo scandala ad Ecclesiam referuntur in Presbyterio, quæ ibi per Antecessores ea audit, reprehendit, &c.
units.tr: LI. In the matter of this discipline Christ called the Church, Matt. 18, 17, yet not in the sense that everything pertaining to it must necessarily be carried out through every single member, as the Brownists want. For since the Church is to be considered as an organic body, which has distinct members, and therefore distinct properties and operations, offences are referred to the Church in the eldership, which hears and rebukes them through its officers, and so on.

units.la: Atque hùc spectant speciales istæ rationes: 1. Ecclesia, juxta ordinationem Christi & Apostolorum, suos habet Antecessores; quos consequenter in exercitio Disciplinæ tales etiam sese præstare oportet. Act. 20, 28. 1 Cor. 12, 28. 1 Thess. 5, 12. 1 Tim. 5, 17. Hebr. 13, 17.
units.tr: To this relate the following special reasons. 1. The Church, according to the ordinance of Christ and the Apostles, has its officers, and these ought consequently to show themselves such in the exercise of discipline: Acts 20, 28; 1 Cor. 12, 28; 1 Thess. 5, 12; 1 Tim. 5, 17; Heb. 13, 17.

units.la: 2. Christus Apostolis, tanquàm istiusmodi Antecessoribus, Claves Regni cœlorum mandavit; ac ministerialem potestatem peccata remittendi, vel retinendi, dedit: Matth. 16, 19. xviii, 18. Joh. 20, 23. 1 Cor. 5, 3, 4, 5. 2, 11, 10.
units.tr: 2. Christ gave the keys of the kingdom of heaven to the Apostles as officers of this kind, and gave them a ministerial power of remitting or retaining sins: Matt. 16, 19; 18, 18; John 20, 23; 1 Cor. 5, 3, 4, 5; 2, 11, 10.

units.la: 3. Isto etiam modo Apostolus reprehensionem, quæ est hujus Disciplinæ, diserte ad multos refert; 2 Cor. 2, 6.
units.tr: 3. In the same way the Apostle expressly refers the rebuke, which belongs to this discipline, to many: 2 Cor. 2, 6.

units.la: 4. Omnia in Ecclesiâ ordine ac decenter fieri debent: 1 Cor. 14, 40. Non omnes eandem habent facultatem, vel functionem. Antecessorum igitur est etiam hac parte sese Antecessores præstare, &c.
units.tr: 4. All things in the Church ought to be done in order and decently: 1 Cor. 14, 40. Not all have the same faculty or function. It is therefore the duty of the officers to show themselves such in this respect also, etc.

units.la: LII. Excommunicatio adhibetur demùm, ubi quis à fidei salutaris veritate, aut à fideli observantia deficiens, scandalum dedit; & monitionibus ac reprehensionibus præviis corrigi non potuit.
units.tr: LII. Excommunication is applied only when someone, having fallen from the truth of saving faith or from faithful observance, has given offence, and could not be corrected by prior admonitions and rebukes.

units.la: Ea autem vel major est vel minor. Per Majorem fit peccatoris, cujus pertinacia & impœnitentia satis diù explorata est, separatio & exclusio à communione Ecclesiæ institutæ, & à symbolis gratiæ in eâ. Hæc simul ministerialiter est declaratoria, illum hominem, quamdiù & quatenus talis manet, à Deo & Christo exclusum esse à communione gratiæ salutaris, atque ipso Regno cœlorum. Itâ Ministri non architectotectonicè realiter efficienter, nec absolutè, quamquam excludunt Regno cœlorum; sed solum minis-terialiter, declarativè, & hypotheticè.
units.tr: This excommunication is either major or minor. By the greater excommunication the sinner, whose obstinacy and impenitence have been sufficiently tested over a long time, is separated and excluded from communion in the instituted Church and from the signs of grace in it. This at the same time is ministerially declaratory: that this man, as long as and in so far as he remains such, is excluded by God and Christ from communion in saving grace and from the kingdom of heaven itself. Thus the ministers do not act architectonically, really, efficiently, or absolutely, although they exclude from the kingdom of heaven; but only ministerially, declaratively, and hypothetically.

units.la: Minor Excommunicatio est, qua illi, qui scandalum jam publicè dederunt; sed resipiscentiam hactenus non egerunt; aut de quorum resipiscentia nondum ita constat, ut per eam scandalum posse videri extinctum, ab actuali communione Cœnæ Dominicæ tantisper suspenduntur; donec vel post exploratam resipiscentiam denuò admittantur; vel etiam post compertam impœnitentiam, major excommunicatio in eos stringatur.
units.tr: The minor excommunication is that by which those who have already given public offence, but have not yet repented, or whose repentance is not yet so clearly established that the offence can be seen to be extinguished by it, are suspended from actual communion in the Lord's Supper for the time being, until either, after repentance has been tested, they are readmitted, or, after impenitence has been established, the greater excommunication is brought upon them.

units.la: Isti quodammodo affinis est simplex abstentio, qua illi de quibus scandalum aliquod publicè notum est, si prope instet administratio S. Cœnæ, à communione interim abstinentur, dum cognoscatur de ipsorum pœnitentia; vel etiam forte de circumstantiis quibusdam ipsius scandali: ne, dum scandalum publicè notum est, pœnitentia vero hactenus ignota, alii per eorum admissionem ad S. Synaxin offendantur.
units.tr: Akin to this is simple abstention, by which those whose publicly known offence is at issue are, if the administration of the Lord's Supper is near, kept from communion meanwhile, until their repentance, or perhaps certain circumstances of the offence itself, have been investigated; so that, while the offence is publicly known but the repentance is hitherto unknown, others may not be scandalised by their admission to the holy Supper.

units.la: LIII. Ex dictis sequitur, primò; etiam ob grave & publicum scandalum, neminem esse excommunicandum, sine praevia admonitione. Quod contra rigidos quosdam Anabaptistas probatur; 1. Ex institutione ipsius Christi; qui in redargutione fratris scandalosi aliquot gradus observari voluit ante Excommunicationem: Matth. 18, 15, 16, 17.
units.tr: LIII. From what has been said it follows, first, that no one is to be excommunicated, even for a grave and public offence, without prior admonition. This is proved against certain rigid Anabaptists: 1. from the institution of Christ himself, who wished several steps to be observed before excommunication in rebuking an offending brother: Matt. 18, 15, 16, 17.

units.la: 2. Similiter Paulus hominem haereticum semel atque iterum monendum constituit, priusquam deviteur; Tit. 3, 10.
units.tr: 2. Likewise Paul lays down that a heretical man is to be admonished once and again before he is shunned: Titus 3, 10.

units.la: 3. Ipsius Excommunicationis finis est, ut ad pudorem ac resipiscentiam adducantur peccatores:
units.tr: 3. The very purpose of excommunication is that sinners may be brought to shame and repentance:

units.la: 1 Cor. 5, 5. 2 Thess. 3, 14. Si igitur iste finis facilius modo obtineri possit, satis patet, ad Excommunicationem non esse veniendum.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 5, 5; 2 Thess. 3, 14. If therefore this purpose can more easily be obtained now, it is plain enough that one should not come to excommunication.

units.la: Attamen scandalo publico statim convenit Reprehensio publica; juxta doctrinam Pauli, 1 Tim. 5, 20, & praxin; Gal. 2, 14.
units.tr: Yet public reproof is at once fitting for public offence, according to Paul's teaching, 1 Tim. 5, 20, and his practice, Gal. 2, 14.

units.la: Secundò, Minimè etiam excommunicandi sunt peccatores, post scandalum quantumvis grave, jam resipiscentiam demonstrantes: nam 1, tunc obtinetur Excommunicationis finis.
units.tr: Second, sinners are by no means to be excommunicated, however grave the offence, once they show repentance: for, first, the purpose of excommunication is then attained.

units.la: 2. Ipse Deus tales non excludit Regno cœlorum: Ergò nec Ecclesia verè potest declarare, eos esse à Deo exclusos,
units.tr: 2. God himself does not exclude such people from the kingdom of heaven; therefore neither can the Church truly declare that they are excluded by God.

units.la: LIV. Neque verò putandum, per Excommunicationem extingui omnem fidelium obligationem ad excommunicatos, sive naturalem, sive œconomicam, sive civilem. Consequenter, eam non esse justam causam Divortii. Vide sup. cap. 9. th. 94.
units.tr: LIV. Nor is it to be thought that by excommunication every obligation of the faithful towards the excommunicated is extinguished, whether natural, domestic, or civil. Consequently, excommunication is not a just cause of divorce. See above, chapter 9, thesis 94.

units.la: Gravior autem istius judicii expressio fit per Anathema; Galat. 1. 8, 9. & per Anathema Maran atha: 1 Cor. 16, 22. ubi peccator, omni spe hactenus adjecta, judicio Divino relinquitur.
units.tr: A more severe expression of this judgment is made by anathema, Gal. 1, 8, 9, and by Anathema Maranatha, 1 Cor. 16, 22, where the sinner, all hope having been cut off, is left to divine judgment.

units.la: Illegitimæ verò Excommunicationes nullam habent efficaciam: quales sunt Papales in Orthodoxos, &c.
units.tr: Illegitimate excommunications, however, have no efficacy: such are the Papal ones against the Orthodox, etc.

units.la: LV. Olim Novatiani lapsos, quantumvis pœnitentes, non recipiebant. Rectius Orthodoxi excommunicatos, post declaratam resipiscentiam, atque hactenus extinctum scandalum, ad communionem Ecclesiæ ac symbolorum gratiæ denuò admittunt: ita enim 1, æquum est, ut cessante causâ Excommunicationis, cessaret etiam ipsa Excommunicatio. 1 Cor. 5, 5. 2 Thess. 3, 14.
units.tr: LV. Formerly the Novatians did not receive the lapsed, however penitent. The Orthodox more rightly, after declared repentance and when the offence has been extinguished, readmit the excommunicated to communion in the Church and in the signs of grace. For, first, it is fitting that when the cause of excommunication ceases, excommunication itself should cease: 1 Cor. 5, 5; 2 Thess. 3, 14.

units.la: 2. Diserte etiam Apostolus de eodem illo incestuoso, quem excommunicandum judicaverat, 1 Cor. 5, 3. postquam de ejus resipiscentiâ cognovisset; 2: 11, 6, 7, 8, Consolemini illum; ne quo modo redundante tristitiâ absorbeatur vir hujusmodi. Quapropter rata m facite in illum charitatem. 3. Ipse Deus quosvis peccatores serio resipiscentes admittit: Ezech. 18, 21. Ergo.
units.tr: 2. The Apostle also speaks expressly of that same incestuous man, whom he had judged to be excommunicated, 2 Cor. 2, 3, after he had learned of his repentance: 2, 6, 7, 8, Comfort him, lest by any means he be swallowed up with excessive sorrow. Wherefore confirm your love towards him. 3. God himself admits any sinners who seriously repent: Ezek. 18, 21. Therefore...

units.la: 4. Singuli fideles semper debent parati esse ad remittendas injurias; & sic imitari ipsum Deum nobis remittentem: Matth. vi, 14, 15. xviii, 21. --. Ergo & Ecclesia non minus debet remittere, ubi Deus remittit.
units.tr: 4. Individual believers ought always to be ready to remit injuries, and so to imitate God himself, who forgives us: Matt. 6, 14, 15; 18, 21. Therefore the Church too ought to forgive no less, when God forgives.

units.la: Apud ipsos Catholicos olim Excommunicatorum poenitentium Reconciliatio tardis ac difficilibus gradibus peragebatur: interdum tamen fiebat quædam Remissio; unde sequioribus saeculis Papales Indulgentiæ natæ sunt.
units.tr: Among the Catholics themselves in former times the reconciliation of excommunicated penitents was carried out through slow and difficult stages; sometimes, however, a certain remission was granted, whence in later centuries the Papal indulgences arose.

units.la: Observandum autem, lapsos & excommunicatos Poenitentes, sua Poenitentia, ejusque demonstratione, non satisfacere justitiæ Divinæ: nullus enim merus homo ei satisfacere potest pro peccatis suis: Matth. 16, 26. Hoc Christus præstitit solus: ut probatum est suo loco. Sed Ecclesiæ quodammodo satisfacere, quam offenderunt; ut videl. scandalum resipiscendo extinguant.
units.tr: It is to be observed, however, that lapsed and excommunicated penitents do not satisfy divine justice by their penitence and its demonstration; for no mere man can satisfy him for his sins: Matt. 16, 26. Christ alone accomplished this, as has been proved in its place. But they do in some measure satisfy the Church, which they have offended, namely by extinguishing the offence through repentance.

units.la: LVI. Ad Presbyterium quoque pertinet Vocatio Ministrorum, si qui desiderentur; nec non Dimissio Pastoris ad aliam Ecclesiam magis laborantem vocati, cum Vitæ Ministeriique testimonio. Imo etiam quorumcunque Membrorum, alio migrantium, Dimissio cum testimonio convenienti.
units.tr: LVI. It also belongs to the eldership to call ministers, if any are needed; and likewise to dismiss a minister who has been called to another Church that is in greater need, together with a testimony of his life and ministry. Indeed, a dismissal with a suitable testimony belongs to any members who move elsewhere.

units.la: Quoties autem habenda est Classis, ad eam quoque deputandi sunt, qui nomine hujus Ecclesiæ ibi comparent.
units.tr: Whenever a classis is to be held, those are also to be deputed to it who appear there in the name of this Church.

units.la: Diaconi in Ecclesiis majoribus distinctos suos habent conventus, ubi de negotiis Diaconiæ suæ agunt; eleemosynis scil. collectis, aut colligendis, deque earum distributione. Ubi vero distinctos conventus non habent, eadem in communi conventu Presbyterii etiam aguntur.
units.tr: Deacons in the larger Churches have their own separate meetings, where they deal with the business of their diaconate, namely the alms collected or to be collected, and their distribution. Where they do not have separate meetings, these matters are also dealt with in the common meeting of the eldership.

units.la: LVII. Sequuntur Conventus plurium Ecclesiarum parti-
units.tr: LVII. Next come the assemblies of several particular churches, which are established, by union or confederation, for mutual help and for common edification.

units.la: particularium, juxta unionem aut confœderationem, mutui auxilii causâ institutam, ad communem ædificationem. Hujus rei insigne exemplum habemus in Ecclesiâ Apostolicâ, Act. 15, 1,-29. ubi à delegatis Ecclesiæ Antiochenæ, Presbyteris Ecclesiæ Hierosolymitanæ, ipsíque Apostolis ibi præsentibus, gravis controversia determinata est; cui sola Antiochena, propter turbas ibi excitatas non sufficiebat.
units.tr: We have a notable example of this in the apostolic Church, Acts 15:1–29, where a grave controversy was settled by delegates of the Antiochene church, by the elders of the Jerusalem church, and by the apostles themselves, who were present there. The Antiochene church alone was not sufficient for this, because of the disturbances that had been stirred up there.

units.la: Alibi etiam notamus vicinarum aliquot Ecclesiarum conjunctionem; & communionem sanctorum sic etiam cum remotioribus observatam: ita Rom. 15, 26. Libuit Ecclesiis Macedoniæ & Achajæ pariter conferre aliquid in pauperes sanctos, qui erant Hierosolymis. Vide etiam 2 Cor. 8, 1, 4, 19, itemque 1 Cor. XI, 16.
units.tr: Elsewhere too we note the joining together of several neighbouring churches, and the fellowship of the saints, which was observed in this way even with more distant churches: so Rom. 15:26, "It pleased the churches of Macedonia and Achaia to make a contribution for the poor saints who were at Jerusalem." See also 2 Cor. 8:1, 4; 9:1–2, and likewise 1 Cor. 11:16.

units.la: Sic ergò istiusmodi unio & communicatio plurium Ecclesiarum particularium necessaria est, non quidem simpliciter ad esse; sed ad bene esse omnium & singularum. Atque ita cumulative, bonum bono additum facit majus bonum: non autem se habet privative; quasi per eam quælibet particularis desineret esse Ecclesia, suamque potestatem ipsa exercere non posset, aut deberet.
units.tr: Such a union and communion of several particular churches is therefore necessary, not indeed simply for their being, but for the well-being of all and of each one. In this way it adds good to good, a greater good cumulatively; it does not stand in a privative relation, as if by it any particular church would cease to be a church, or could not, or ought not, to exercise its own power itself.

units.la: LVIII. Ecclesiarum aliquot vicinarum in medio- cri tractu ejusdem ferè Provinciæ confœderatio, & communicatio, consistit in Classe; ut nunc appella- tur.
units.tr: LVIII. The confederation and communion of several neighbouring churches in a moderately sized district of the same province is called, as it is now named, the Classis.

units.la: In hac comparere solent omnes Pastores istius districtûs; atque insuper Seniores singuli ab Ecclesiis istis singulis, aut saltem ab Ecclesiis majoribus, literis fidei à suis delegantibus instructi. Eidem Conventui interesse etiam solent singuli Correspondentes, à singulis Classibus ejusdem Synodi Provincialis.
units.tr: In this assembly all the ministers of that district usually appear; and in addition, one elder from each of these churches, or at least from the larger churches, furnished with letters of faith from those who sent them. The individual correspondents from each Classis of the same Provincial Synod also usually take part in the same assembly.

units.la: In Classe Pastor aliquis Præses constituitur electione, vel etiam ex ordine. Cujus est curare, ut omnia ordine ac decenter in isto Conventû fiant; negotia tractanda proponere: suffragia colligere, & indè conclusionem formare. Praesidi adjungitur Assessor; cujus est Praesidem in dirigendo Conventu juvare: atque item Scriba; cujus est acta ipsius Conventus fideliter consignare.
units.tr: In the Classis a minister is appointed as president, either by election or in turn. It is his task to see that everything is done in good order and decently in this assembly, to propose the business to be dealt with, to collect the votes, and from these to form a conclusion. An assessor is attached to the president, whose task is to help the president in directing the assembly; and likewise a clerk, whose task is to record faithfully the proceedings of the assembly itself.

units.la: Ad Classem pertinent, tum negotia communia Ecclesiarum istius distinctus: tum negotia graviora, super quibus Presbyteria auxilium Classis requirunt: nec non Provocationes & querelae eorum, qui se Presbyterii sui judicio gravatos exi stimant.
units.tr: To the Classis belong: the common business of the churches of that district; the weightier matters, on which presbyteries ask the help of the Classis; and also the appeals and complaints of those who think they have been aggrieved by the judgment of their presbytery.

units.la: LIX. Ex aliquot Delegatis omnium Classium ejusdem Provinciae, constituitur Synodus Provincialis. Accedunt Correspondentes ex Synodis vicinarum Provinciarum.
units.tr: LIX. From several delegates of all the Classes of the same province a Provincial Synod is constituted. Correspondents from the synods of neighbouring provinces join it.

units.la: In ea constituuntur Directores, ut supra.
units.tr: In it directors are appointed, as above.

units.la: Tractantur vero negotia omnium Ecclesiarum istius Provinciae communia; atque etiam graviora, in quibus Classis aliqua auxilium Synodi petit; nec non Provocationes & Querelae eorum, qui se judicio suae Classis gravatos putant.
units.tr: The business common to all the churches of that province is dealt with, and also the weightier matters, in which some Classis seeks the help of the Synod; and likewise the appeals and complaints of those who think they have been aggrieved by the judgment of their own Classis.

units.la: Similiter ex Delegatis Synodorum Provincialium ejusdem Nationis, constituitur Synodus Nationalis. Accedunt Correspondentes aliarum Nationum eandem fidem profitentium.
units.tr: Similarly, from delegates of the provincial synods of the same nation a National Synod is constituted. Correspondents from other nations professing the same faith join it.

units.la: Constituuntur Directores, &c.
units.tr: Directors are appointed, etc.

units.la: Tractantur autem hic Negotia omnibus ut plurimum ejusdem Nationis Ecclesiis communia; tum fidei puritatem, tum graviores casus conscientiae, tum etiam ordinem Ecclesiasticum spectantia.
units.tr: Here the business that is for the most part common to all the churches of the same nation is dealt with: both the purity of the faith, and the more serious cases of conscience, and also matters concerning ecclesiastical order.

units.la: Nuncupantur etiam Concilia œcumenica; quasi convocata & collecta ex Ecclesiis totius orbis, πάσης τῆς οἰκουμένης. Sed nulla vere & proprie talia unquam fuerunt: nisi quod Synodus Hierosolymitana quodammodo haberi potuit œcumenica, propter Apostolos Doctores œcumenicos.
units.tr: These are also called ecumenical councils, as if convoked and gathered from the churches of the whole world [πάσης τῆς οἰκουμένης]. But truly and properly speaking, no such council has ever existed, except that the Jerusalem synod could in some measure be regarded as ecumenical, on account of the apostles, who were ecumenical teachers.

units.la: LX. Non autem putandum est cum Remonstrantibus, eos, qui ad Synodum mittuntur, debere, durante litis examine, nulli vel personæ, vel Ecclesiæ, vel Confessioni esse adstrictos: nam 1. nunquam iis licet, fidem suam Verbo Dei fundatam, & juxta illud Confessione aliquâ expressam, abnegare, vel deponere.
units.tr: LX. It must not, however, be supposed with the Remonstrants that those who are sent to a synod ought, while the examination of the dispute lasts, to be bound to no person, church or confession; for, first, it is never lawful for them to deny or lay aside their faith, which is founded on the Word of God and expressed in some confession according to it.

units.la: 2. Semper oportet eos Deo, Christo, & SS. Literis, quibus orthodoxæ Confessiones consentaneæ sunt, adstrictos manere.
units.tr: Second, they must always remain bound to God, to Christ, and to the Holy Scriptures, with which the orthodox confessions agree.

units.la: 3. Neque de Apostolis existimandum, eos in Synodo Hierosolymitanâ, priorem suam fidem ac notitiam de iis rebus depositisse: Act. 15, 6, -.
units.tr: Third, nor is it to be thought that the apostles, in the Synod of Jerusalem, laid aside their earlier faith and knowledge of those matters: Acts 15:6.

units.la: 4. Neque alii Judices suam scientiam Juris, Legum, Statutorum, Consuetudinum, & Sententiarum in similibus casibus latarum, tenentur deponere.
units.tr: Fourth, nor are other judges bound to lay aside their knowledge of law, of statutes, of customs, and of judgments pronounced in similar cases.

units.la: Neque similiter putandum, in iis quæ controversi juris sunt, nimium sibi arrogare Synodos, si dicant; Hoc credendum est constanter & firmiter: cum enim suam sententiam ex Verbo Dei confirmant, hæc confirmatio omninò admitti debet propter auctoritatem Verbi Divini, quâ eâ nititur. Si aliter fiat, contra Deum peccatur, quòd ipsius testimonium in dubium vocetur: 1 Joh. 5, 10. Confer Hebr. 13, 17. 1 Thess. II, 13.
units.tr: Nor, likewise, should it be thought that synods arrogate too much to themselves in matters of disputed law if they say, This must be believed constantly and firmly; for when they confirm their opinion from the Word of God, this confirmation ought wholly to be admitted, on account of the authority of the divine Word on which it rests. If it is done otherwise, sin is committed against God, in that his testimony is called into doubt: 1 John 5:10. Compare Heb. 13:17; 1 Thess. 2:13.

units.la: Quin & Adversarii aliter sentientes, quotquot SS. Literas acceperunt, eâdem quoque auctoritate devinciuntur.
units.tr: Indeed, even the opposing adversaries, as many as have received the Holy Scriptures, are bound by this same authority.

units.la: Obj. 1 Cor. 5, 12, 13. Extranei ab Ecclesiâ non sunt judicandi. Ergò. Resp. Apostolus ibi de Disciplinâ Ecclesiasticâ loquitur, quæ proprie versatur circa Membra Ecclesiæ alicujus institutæ. Verùm inde nequaquam sequitur, quod Adversarii intendunt.
units.tr: Objection: 1 Cor. 5:12–13, "Those outside the Church are not to be judged." Therefore... Answer: The apostle there speaks of ecclesiastical discipline, which properly concerns the members of a church that has been established. But it by no means follows from this what the adversaries intend.

units.la: LXI. Transeo ad Adjuncta; quæ nunc potissimùm occurrunt, Potestas, Visibilitas, Defectibilitas, & Notæ.
units.tr: LXI. I pass on to the Adjuncts, which now chiefly present themselves: Power, Visibility, Defectibility, and the Marks.

units.la: Potestas hoc loco Ministerialis intelligitur: autocratorica enim Christo Regi nostro spirituali propria est. Interim Christus Potestatem hujusmodi ministerialem in Ecclesiâ ordinavit; sic tamen, ut in exercitio Antecessoribus essent suæ partes Antecessoriæ. Est autem hæc Potestas, tum clavium, tum ordinationis. Ad Potestatem clavium pertinet tum Prædicatio Evangelii, tum Disciplina Ecclesiastica. Potestas Ordinationis est jus Ministros eligendi, vocandi, & confirmandi, Ecclesiæ ejusque Antecessoribus competens. De quibus sic satis in superioribus.
units.tr: Power is understood here as ministerial power, for autocratic power belongs to Christ our spiritual King alone. Christ has nonetheless ordained such ministerial power in the Church, yet in such a way that in its exercise the elders have their own elder-like parts. This power is both of the keys and of ordination. The power of the keys includes both the preaching of the Gospel and church discipline. The power of ordination is the right, belonging to the Church and to its elders, to choose, call and confirm ministers. Of these things enough has been said above.

units.la: LXII. Ecclesia in ratione mystica invisibilis est.
units.tr: LXII. The Church is invisible in its mystical aspect.

units.la: Sicut & instituta, universaliter spectata. Verum particularis quæque Ecclesia, in singularibus suis membris, conventibus, & functionibus externis, quando ex procedunt, est visibilis: Matth. 5, 14, 15. Fieri tamen potest, ut Ecclesiæ particulares, ob persecutiones hostium suorum, latere cogantur: vel etiam dispergantur; atque ità hostibus suis non sint conspicuæ; imo neque fidelibus quibusdam, dum hi cum illis congregari non possunt. Quod accidit tempore Eliæ, Rom. xi, 2, 3, 4, 18. Confer Joh. 20, 19, & Act. 12, 12, 13, 14. Quid autem longè post, & satis diu futurum esset de Ecclesiâ N. T. clarissimè ostensum est typo Mulieris illius, amictæ Sole, &c. de quâ, Apoc. 12, 6. Fugit in solitudinem, ubi habet locum paratum à Deo, ut illic alerent eam diebus mille ducentis sexaginta.
units.tr: So also is the Church as instituted, when viewed universally. But each particular church, in its individual members, assemblies and external functions, when these come forth, is visible: Matt. 5:14, 15. It may nevertheless happen that particular churches, because of the persecutions of their enemies, are forced to hide, or are even scattered, and so are not conspicuous to their enemies; indeed, not even to some of the faithful, since these cannot be gathered together with them. This happened in the time of Elijah: Rom. 11:2, 3, 4, 18. Compare John 20:19 and Acts 12:12, 13, 14. But what would happen long afterwards, and for a considerable time, concerning the Church of the New Testament, was most clearly shown by the type of that woman clothed with the sun, etc., of whom Rev. 12:6: she fled into the wilderness, where she had a place prepared by God, that they might nourish her there for 1,260 days.

units.la: Propterea qui puriorem Christianismum profitebantur, (qualem Deus propitius per Reformationem restituit,) prævalente Antichristianismo, latebras quærere coacti sunt in variis partibus ipsius Babylonis: qui Waldenses appellabantur, ac deinde etiam Bohemi, sæpius fuerunt oppressi, ac dispersi, &c. Magnum interim fuisse eorum numerum, satis manifestum est ex Catalogis Testium veritatis, ac Martyrologiis. Sic occurrendum Pontificiis; perpetuam Ecclesiæ visibilitatem jactantibus; & sæpe quærentibus. Ubi fuerit Ecclesia nostra ante Lutherum?
units.tr: Therefore those who professed a purer Christianity (such as God graciously restored through the Reformation), while Antichristianity prevailed, were forced to seek hiding places in various parts of Babylon itself. They were called Waldenses, and afterwards the Bohemians too; they were often oppressed and scattered, etc. Meanwhile, that their number was great is sufficiently clear from the catalogues of the Witnesses of the truth and from the martyrologies. So must the Papists be met, who boast of the perpetual visibility of the Church and who often ask: Where was our Church before Luther?

units.la: LXIII. Christus Rex æternus non potest omnino distitui subditis; Luc. I, 33. sed necessario impleri debet, quod promisit ipsa veritas, Matth. 16, 18. Portæ Inferorum non superabunt Ecclesiam. & xxviii, 20. Ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem saeculi. Verum Ecclesia quoque particularis est defectibilis: fieri enim potest, ut electi fideles & sanctificati tum moriantur tum alio migrent; temporarii autem deficiant ad hæreses, vel infidelitatem, & profanitatem. Ita Ecclesiæ plurimæ, quæ olim fuerunt in Asia, Muhammedismo succubuerunt; juxta comminationem olim factam Apoc. II, 5. Multæ etiam aliæ Antichristum secutæ sunt, & concesserunt Bestiæ ac Meretrici Babylonicæ; sicut prædictum, xiii, 3, 4, 8.
units.tr: LXIII. Christ the eternal King cannot altogether be deprived of subjects: Luke 1:33. But what Truth itself has promised must necessarily be fulfilled: Matt. 16:18, "The gates of hell shall not prevail" against the Church; and 28:20, "I am with you all days, even to the end of the age." Yet the particular Church is also defectible: for it may happen that elect and sanctified believers either die or migrate elsewhere, while temporary members fall away into heresy, or unbelief and profanity. Thus many churches which once existed in Asia succumbed to Muhammadanism, in accordance with the threat once made, Rev. 2:5. Many others also followed the Antichrist and yielded to the Beast and the Babylonian Harlot, as was foretold, Rev. 13:3, 4, 8.

units.la: Neque Indefectibilitatis privilegium datum est Ecclesiæ Romanæ; nec ulla talis promissio ei speciatim facta sed comminatio superioribus similis, Rom. xi, 17, -21. Ne efferter animo; sed metue. Nam si Deus naturalibus ramis non pepercit, vide ne tibi quoque non parcat. Confer 2 Thess. II, 3, -7. Apoc. 17, 3, 4, 5, 9; 18.
units.tr: Nor has the privilege of indefectibility been given to the Roman Church, nor was any such promise made to it specifically; rather, a threat similar to the above: Rom. 11:17-21, "Do not be proud, but fear. For if God did not spare the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare you not." Compare 2 Thess. 2:3-7; Rev. 17:3, 4, 5, 9; 18.

units.la: Obj. 1. Atqui occurrunt tam multæ & præclaræ promissiones de perpetuitate Ecclesiæ. Ergo. Resp. Quæ promissa sunt Ecclesiæ electorum, vel in universum dicta de Ecclesiâ instituta, non recte restringuntur ad Ecclesiam aliquam particularem, aut specialius ad Romanam. Orbis major est Urbe.
units.tr: Objection 1. But there are many and excellent promises concerning the perpetuity of the Church. Therefore... Answer: Those things which are promised to the Church of the elect, or said in general of the instituted Church, are not rightly restricted to some particular church, or more specially to the Roman one. The greater world is larger than the city.

units.la: Obj. 2. Paulus ad Romanos scripsit, I, 18. Gratias ago Deo meo per Iesum Christum, super omnibus vobis, quod fides vestra annunciatur in toto mundo. Ergo gloria & perpetuitas ista pertinet ad Ecclesiam Romanam. Resp. Neg. Consequ. Talis quidem tunc fuit fides Romanorum; verum inde nequaquam sequitur, eam semper per omnia saecula talem fuisse manifestam. Similia vide 2 Thess. I, 3, 4.
units.tr: Objection 2. Paul wrote to the Romans, 1:8: "I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world." Therefore this glory and perpetuity pertains to the Roman Church. Answer: I deny the consequence. Such indeed was the faith of the Romans at that time; but it does not at all follow that it was always, in every age, manifestly such. Compare similar things at 2 Thess. 1:3, 4.

units.la: Obj. 3. Ecclesia est columna & stabilimentum veritatis: 1 Tim. 3, 15. Ergò Resp. Ecclesia Catholica in universum, & quælibet particularis quatenus verum ac sanum membrum catholicæ est, veritati superstructa est, & per eam stabilita; eandemque aliis cognoscendam exhibet ministerialiter. Verum inde non sequitur cujusq; Ecclesiæ particularis indefectibilitas; nedum Romanæ: quæ iste spectatim non consideratur; sed Ephesina in quâ Timotheus erat. De hujus autem futurâ defectione vide Act. 20, 29, 30. Apoc. II, 4, 5.
units.tr: Objection 3. The Church is the pillar and ground of the truth: 1 Tim. 3:15. Therefore... Answer: The Catholic Church in general, and any particular church insofar as it is a true and sound member of the Catholic Church, is built upon the truth and established by it, and it ministerially presents that same truth to others to be known. But it does not follow from this that any particular church is indefectible, much less the Roman one, which is not considered here in this respect at all; rather, the Ephesian church, in which Timothy was, is meant. Concerning its future defection, see Acts 20:29, 30; Rev. 2:4, 5.

units.la: LXIV Sed Notas lustremus! Eæ sunt certa quædam signa, quæ per se facilius cognoscuntur, & ex quibus certò cognosci potest de Ecclesiæ cujusque veritate ac puritate.
