Necesse autem est, Notas illas esse proprias veræ Ecclesiæ, & perpetuas, & cogniti faciliores; atque itâ idoneas, per quas cognoscatur Ecclesia. Spectandum ergo Verbum Dei, SS. Literis expressum & comprehensum, pro uno & certo canone fidei ac morum: hinc Christus Joh. 8, 31. Si vos manseritis in Sermone meo; vere discipuli mei eritis. 47. Qui ex Deo est, verba Dei audit. x, 4, 5. Oves eum sequuntur (Pastorem verum); quia norunt vocem ejus. 26, 27. xvii, 17. Eph. 2, 20. Phil. 3, 16. Gal. 6, 16. Est autem hæc conveniențtia in Ecclesiâ quaque institutâ particulari spectanda, in iis quæ istic illustriora occurrunt; scil. 1. in Doctrinâ quæ ab Antecessoribus proponitur, & à multitudine reliquâ recipitur; vel etiam Confessione aliquâ edita comprehenditur. Hinc Tef. 8, 20. Ad Legem & ad testimonium: Si non dixerint secundum verbum hoc, non erit eis aurora. Matth. 18, 20. 1 Cor. 4, 1, 2, 6. 1 Petr. 4, 11. Act. 26, 22; xvii, 11.
units.tr: LXIV. But let us examine the Marks! These are certain signs which are more easily recognised in themselves, and from which the truth and purity of any Church can be known with certainty. It is necessary, however, that these marks be proper to the true Church, perpetual, and more easily known; and thus suitable for recognising the Church. Therefore we must look to the Word of God, expressed and contained in the Holy Scriptures, as the one and certain rule of faith and morals. Hence Christ says, John 8:31, "If you abide in my word, you will truly be my disciples"; v. 47, "He who is of God hears the words of God"; 10:4, 5, "The sheep follow him (the true Shepherd), for they know his voice"; 26, 27; 17:17; Eph. 2:20; Phil. 3:16; Gal. 6:16. This agreement is to be sought in every particular instituted Church, in those matters which appear more prominently there, namely: (1) in the doctrine which is set forth by the elders and received by the rest of the multitude, or is also comprehended in some published Confession. Hence Isa. 8:20, "To the law and to the testimony: if they do not speak according to this word, there is no dawn for them." Matt. 18:20; 1 Cor. 4:1, 2, 6; 1 Pet. 4:11; Acts 26:22; 17:11.

units.la: 2. In administratione Sacramentorum; utrum ea peragatur secundum institutionem Christi: hæc enim in recto usu singulis fidelibus sunt sigilla communionis suæ salutaris in Christo ac beneficiis ejus; eâdemque operâ Ecclesiæ cujusque particularis signa sunt, unde etiam innotescit vera ejus conditio, prout ea externè cognosci potest. Hùc pertinent accurate descriptiones, Matth. 28, 19, 20. 1 Cor. XI, 24, 25, 26.
units.tr: (2) In the administration of the Sacraments, whether it is carried out according to Christ's institution; for these, when rightly used, are seals to each of the faithful of their saving communion in Christ and his benefits; and by the same work they are signs of each particular Church, by which its true condition is also made known, insofar as it can be recognised externally. To this belong the exact descriptions at Matt. 28:19, 20 and 1 Cor. 11:24, 25, 26.

units.la: 3. In Exercitio Disciplinæ Ecclesiasticæ, quæ ordinata est ad veritatem ac puritatem in Ecclesiâ conservandam: Matth. 16, 19. XVIII, 15,-18. 1 Cor. 5, 6, 7, 11, 13, Tit. 3, 10.
units.tr: (3) In the exercise of Church discipline, which is ordained to preserve truth and purity in the Church: Matt. 16:19; 18:15-18; 1 Cor. 5:6, 7, 11, 13; Titus 3:10.

units.la: LXV. Minimè autem inutilis, aut supervacanea, cum Socinianis & Libertinis, censeri debet Notarum istarum investigatio; atque ex illis Ecclesiæ cognitio: nam 1. Unusquisque salutis suæ studiosus hoc agere debet, ut se fe adjungat veræ Ecclesiæ; atque in ejus communione particeps sit mediorum à Deo & Christo ordinatorum ad salutarem ædificationem; juxta exemplum in Ecclesiâ primitivâ, Act. II, 41, 42. post concionem & instructionem Petri; Qui libenter receperunt sermonem ejus, baptizati sunt; & additæ sunt Ecclesiæ die illo animæ quasi ter mille. Perdurabant autem in doctrinâ Apostolorum, & communicatione, & fractione panis, & orationibus. Vide etiam 1 Cor. XI, XII, XIV. Eph. 4, 11, 12, 13. Hebr. 10, 25.
units.tr: LXV. Yet the investigation of these Marks, and from them the knowledge of the Church, must by no means be judged useless or superfluous, as the Socinians and Libertines hold. For (1) everyone who is concerned for his salvation ought to see to it that he joins himself to the true Church, and that he shares in its communion of the means ordained by God and Christ for saving edification; following the example in the primitive Church, Acts 2:41, 42, after the sermon and instruction of Peter: "Those who gladly received his word were baptised; and there were added to the Church on that day about three thousand souls. And they continued in the doctrine of the apostles, and in fellowship, and in the breaking of bread, and in prayers." See also 1 Cor. 11, 12, 14; Eph. 4:11, 12, 13; Heb. 10:25.

units.la: 2. Qui aliam doctrinam adferunt, non sunt audiendi; neque ulla communio cum illis habenda: unde 2 Joh. 10, 11. Si quis venit ad vos, & hanc doctrinam non adfert, ne recipite eum in domum; nec Ave ei dicite. Joh. 10, 5, 16. Gal. I, 8, 9. Phil. 3, 2. Tit. 3, 10. 1 Joh. 4, 1.
units.tr: (2) Those who bring another doctrine are not to be heard, nor is any communion to be had with them. Hence 2 John 10, 11: "If anyone comes to you and does not bring this doctrine, do not receive him into the house, nor say to him, Hail." John 10:5, 16; Gal. 1:8, 9; Phil. 3:2; Titus 3:10; 1 John 4:1.

units.la: 3. Singulorum est ædificationem & prosperitatem veræ Ecclesiæ suis precibus promovere, quantum possunt. Psal. LI, 20. Benefac in voluntate tua Sijoni; ædifices muros Ierusalem! CXXII, 6. Matth. 6, 10.
units.tr: 3. It is the duty of each person to promote, by their prayers, the building up and prosperity of the true Church as far as they can. Ps. 51, 20: Do good in your good pleasure to Zion; build the walls of Jerusalem! Ps. 122, 6. Matt. 6, 10.

units.la: 4. Gaudendum est de ejus incremento & rebus secundis; atque isto nomine Deo agendæ sunt gratiæ: ac proinde distincte agnoscenda est vera Ecclesia per suas Notas. 1 Thess. 1, 2, 3. 2 Tob. 3, 3. Tob. 3, 4. Luc. 15, 4.-
units.tr: 4. We ought to rejoice at its increase and prosperity, and for this we must give thanks to God; and therefore the true Church must be recognised distinctly by its marks. 1 Thess. 1, 2, 3. 2 Tob. 3, 3. Tob. 3, 4. Luke 15, 4.-

units.la: LXVI. Pontificii alias & plures Notas Ecclesiæ constituunt; atque inter illos Bellarminus quidem ad quindenarium numerum procedit.
units.tr: LXVI. The Papists set up other and more numerous marks of the Church; and among them Bellarmine indeed goes on to fifteen.

units.la: Prima autem nota illi est Nomen Ecclesiæ, Christianorum, & Catholicismi. Sed nomen tum alibi, tum in hoc negotio, non præbet certum indicium. Apoc. 3, 1. ad Angelum Ecclesiæ, quæ Sardibus erat: Novi opera tua: nempe quod dicaris vivere; sed mortuus fis.
units.tr: The first mark for them is the name of the Church: Christian, and Catholic. But the name, both elsewhere and in this matter, does not provide a certain indication. Apoc. 3, 1. to the angel of the church that was at Sardis: "I know your works, that you are said to live, but you are dead."

units.la: Secunda est Antiquitas. Verum 1. ea non est Ecclesiæ propria; sed ipsi Diabolo communis: Joh. 8, 44. Neque 2. Ecclesiæ inseparabiliter convenit: initio enim non fuit antiqua. Et ipsa 3. difficillime cognoscitur; plurimisque adminiculis opus habet.
units.tr: The second is antiquity. But (1) it is not proper to the Church, but common to the devil himself: John 8, 44. Nor (2) does it belong to the Church inseparably, for at the beginning it was not ancient. And (3) it is very hard to recognize, and needs many supports.

units.la: Tertia est Duratio diuturna non interrupta; cui eadem opponimus.
units.tr: The third is continuous and uninterrupted long duration; to which we oppose the same.

units.la: Quarta est Amplitudo, & multitudo credentium. Verum 1. nec ista est Ecclesiæ propria: maxima enim est multitudo Muhammedi credentium; aliorumque errantium; Matth. 7, 13. Quoniam lata est porta, &c. Apoc. 13, 3. Admirans universa terra secuta est Bestiam. 8. Neque 2. est perpetua: Luc. 12, 32. Ne metuë, parve Grex iste; - . Matth. 7, 14. Angusta est porta, & strieta via, quæ ducit ad vitam: & pauci sunt qui inveniant eam.
units.tr: The fourth is the breadth and multitude of believers. But (1) this too is not proper to the Church: for the multitude of Muhammad's believers is greatest, and that of other erring people; Matt. 7, 13: Because the gate is wide, etc. Rev. 13, 3: The whole earth wondered and followed the Beast. (2) Nor is it perpetual. Luke 12, 32: Do not fear, little flock. Matt. 7, 14: The gate is narrow and the way is strait that leads to life, and few are those who find it.

units.la: Quinta est Successio Episcoporum. Verum. 1. Successio ejusdem Doctrinæ, & quidem veræ, difficulter cognoscitur. 2. Quid si foret Successio errorum; 3. Successio Sedis sola parum ad rem facit: Matth. 23, 2. In cathedra Mosis sedent Scribæ & Pharisæi. Adde, 13. & xvi, 6.
units.tr: The fifth is the succession of bishops. But (1) succession in the same doctrine, and indeed in true doctrine, is recognized with difficulty. (2) What if it were a succession of errors? (3) Succession of the seat alone counts for little: Matt. 23, 2: The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses' seat. Add 13, and 16, 6.

units.la: Sexta, Consensus Ecclesiæ antiquæ. Sed quam antiquæ? Annon etiam veræ? At quomodo cognoscetur Ecclesia antiqua vera? Septima, Unio Membrorum cum Capite Papâ, & inter se. At 1. vera Ecclesia non agnoscit Caput, nisi Christum. 2. Ista unio potius est Nota Ecclesiæ malignantium, & Antichristianæ: post pauca enim probabimus Papam esse Antichristum. 3. Unio inter se non est etiam veræ Ecclesiæ propria; sed & Regno Satanæ convenit; Matth. 12, 25, 26.
units.tr: The sixth is the consent of the ancient Church. But which ancient Church? Is it not also the true one? And how will the ancient true Church be known? The seventh is the union of the members with the head, the Pope, and with one another. But (1) the true Church acknowledges no head but Christ. (2) This union is rather a mark of a malignant and Antichristian church, for after a few things we will prove that the Pope is Antichrist. (3) Union among themselves is not proper to the true Church either, but also belongs to the kingdom of Satan: Matt. 12, 25, 26.

units.la: Octava, Sanctitas Doctrinæ. Verùm ista dignosci non potest, nisi cognitâ priùs Veritate; sine quâ omnis jactata Sanctitas mera superstitio est.
units.tr: The eighth is the holiness of the doctrine. But this cannot be discerned unless the truth has first been known, and without that every boasted holiness is mere superstition.

units.la: Nona, Efficacia doctrinæ. Sed nec illa verè Ecclesiæ propria est; quippè Antichristianæ etiàm conveniens:
units.tr: The ninth is the efficacy of the doctrine. But this too is not truly proper to the Church, since it also suits the Antichristian church:

units.la: 2 Thess. II, 9, 11. de Antichristo; Cujus adventus est ex efficacia Satanæ, cum omni potentiâ, --.
units.tr: 2 Thess. II, 9, 11, of Antichrist: whose coming is by the working of Satan, with all power, ...

units.la: Decima, Sanctimonia auctorum Religionis. Sed 1. Quomodò iterùm dignoscetur ista Sanctimonia? 2. Difficillima etiàm est investigatio, utrùm Religio ista hodierna sit eadem illi, quam Auctores docuisse perhibentur.
units.tr: The tenth is the sanctity of the authors of the religion. But (1) how again will this sanctity be recognized? (2) The investigation is also very difficult, whether this present religion is the same as that which its authors are said to have taught.

units.la: Undecima, Gloria Miraculorum. Verùm 1. Miracula etiàm fieri possunt ab iis, qui fide salvificâ destituuntur. Matth. 7, 22, 23. Multi dicent Mihi illo die; Domine, Domine, Nonne - in nomine Tuo Dæmonia ejecimus, & per nomen Tuum multas virtutes edidimus? Tunc autem profitebor eis? Certe nunquàm novi vos: abscedite à Me, qui operam datis iniquitati. 2. Opera valdè miranda, veris Miraculis effectu proximo & externâ specie simillima, fieri etiàm possunt à seductoribus, & salutaris Veritatis adversariis: 2 Thess. 2, 9. - Cum omni potentiâ, & signis, ac prodigiis mendacibus. Matth. 24, 24. Excitabuntur enim Pseudo-christi, & Pseudo-prophetæ: & edent signa magna, & miracula; adeò ut seducant, si fieri possit, etiàm electos. Apoc. 13, 13, 14. iterùm de Antichristo; Editque signa magna, -. Ista scil. à Deo permittuntur, & fiunt suo modo, atque ordinantur ad explorationem hominum: Deut 13, 1, 2, 3. Confer
units.tr: The eleventh is the glory of miracles. But (1) miracles can also be done by those who lack saving faith. Matt. 7, 22, 23: Many will say to me on that day, "Lord, Lord, did we not cast out demons in your name, and do many mighty works in your name?" Then I will declare to them, "I never knew you; depart from me, you who practise lawlessness." (2) Very wonderful works, most like true miracles in their immediate effect and outward appearance, can also be done by seducers and opponents of the saving truth: 2 Thess. 2, 9: with all power, and with lying signs and wonders. Matt. 24, 24: For false christs and false prophets will arise, and will show great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the elect. Rev. 13, 13, 14, again of Antichrist: and he performs great signs, ... Those, namely, are permitted by God and happen in their own way, and are ordained for the testing of men: Deut. 13, 1, 2, 3. Compare

units.la: exempla Magorum Ægyptiorum; Exod. 7, 11, 12, 22. viii, 7. & Simonis Magi; Act. 8, 9, 10. 3. Neque Miracula sunt penes veram Ecclesiam perpetua:
units.tr: the examples of the Egyptian magicians, Exod. 7, 11, 12, 22; 8, 7, and of Simon Magus, Acts 8, 9, 10. (3) Nor are miracles perpetually in the possession of the true Church.

units.la: 1 Cor. 12, 7. Unicuique datur declaratio Spiritus ad utilitatem. 11. - distribuens privatim illa singulis, sicut vult. cum. xiv, 22. Linguæ igitur sunt signum, non iis qui credunt; sed infidelibus. Augustinus de Civitate Dei lib. 22. cap. 8. de iisdem; Necessaria fuisse prius quam crederet Mundus, ad hoc ut crederet Mundus. Quisquis adhuc prodigia ut credat inquirit, magnum est ipse Prodigium; qui Mundo credente non credit.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 12, 7: To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good. 11: dividing them to each one individually as he wills. Compare 14, 22: Tongues, therefore, are a sign not for those who believe, but for unbelievers. Augustine, in The City of God, book 22, chapter 8, on the same point: they were necessary before the world believed, so that the world might believe. Whoever still seeks out prodigies in order to believe is himself a great prodigy, for he does not believe though the world believes.

units.la: Duodecima, Lumen Propheticum. Verum 1. etiam fide falsificā destituti, & seductores, prophetare possunt: Matth. 7, 22. - Nonne per nomen Tuum prophetavimus? - Deut. 13, 1, 2, 3. Cum surrexerit in medio tui Propheta, vel somnians somnium, &c. Confer exemplum Bilhami apud Moabitas prophetantis; Num. 23, 18, 24. xxiv, 3, 9, 15. - Apoc. 11, 14. & Cajaphæ in corruptissima Judæorum Ecclesia; Joh. xi, 49, 52. 2. Neque istud donum in vera Ecclesia perpetuum est; similiter ut de Miraculis modo oftensum.
units.tr: The twelfth is the prophetic light. But (1) even those destitute of saving faith, and seducers, can prophesy: Matt. 7, 22: Did we not prophesy in your name? Deut. 13, 1, 2, 3: When there arises in your midst a prophet, or one who dreams a dream, etc. Compare the example of Balaam prophesying among the Moabites, Num. 23, 18, 24; 24, 3, 9, 15; Rev. 11, 14; and of Caiaphas in the most corrupt Jewish church, John 11, 49–52. (2) Nor is this gift perpetual in the true Church, just as has been shown of miracles.

units.la: Decima tertia, Confessio Adversariorum. Sed testimonium humanum, idque inconstans, non potest huius rei certam notitiam præbere.
units.tr: The thirteenth is the confession of adversaries. But human testimony, and that an inconstant one, cannot provide certain knowledge of this matter.

units.la: Decima quarta Infelix exitus persecutorum Ecclesiæ. Sed 1. iste in hoc sæculo non semper est conspicuus. 2. Etiam pii & probi multa adversa hic patiuntur; & morte, quantum ad externam speciem, satis calamitosa afficiuntur. Eccl. 9, 1, 2. Etiam amorem, etiam odium; nescit homo ex omnibus, quæ ante eos sunt. Omnia eveniunt consimiliter omnibus: &c. Psal. 73. 2, - 5. Ego; pene declinaverunt pedes mei: - quia zelari in insanos, cum pacem impiorum viderem. - Joh. 21, 7, 15. Jerem 12, 1, 2. Luc. 16, 25. 1 Cor. 4, 9, - 13. xv, 19, 30, 31, 32. Hebr. xi, 35, - 38. Decima quinta denique illi est Felicitas temporaria defensorum Ecclesiæ. Verùm & ista 1. minimè propria est: quod satis patet ex modò allegatis. Nec 2. perpetua. Psal. 73, 14. Fui flagellatus omni die: & fuit increpatio mea singulis matutinis. Joh. 16, 33. In mundo oppressionem habebitis. Act. 14, 22. Oportere per multas afflictiones nos ingredi in Regnum Dei. Rom. 8, 17, 36. 2 Tim. 3, 12.
units.tr: The fourteenth is the unhappy end of the persecutors of the Church. But (1) in this age this is not always evident. (2) Even the pious and upright suffer many adversities here, and are afflicted by death, which, as far as outward appearance goes, is quite calamitous. Eccl. 9, 1, 2: Man knows neither love nor hatred from all that lies before him. All things happen alike to all: etc. Ps. 73, 2–5: As for me, my feet had almost stumbled, ... for I was envious of the arrogant, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked. John 21, 7, 15. Jer. 12, 1, 2. Luke 16, 25. 1 Cor. 4, 9–13; 15, 19, 30, 31, 32. Heb. 11, 35–38. The fifteenth and last is the temporal happiness of the defenders of the Church. But this too (1) is not proper to them, as is plain enough from what has just been cited. Nor (2) is it perpetual. Ps. 73, 14: I have been plagued all day long, and chastened every morning. John 16, 33: In the world you will have tribulation. Acts 14, 22: We must enter the kingdom of God through many tribulations. Rom. 8, 17, 36; 2 Tim. 3, 12.

units.la: Iståe igitur non rectè constituuntur Notæ, seu τεκμήρια veræ Ecclesiæ. Sed neque eas sic omnes competere Ecclesiæ Romanæ, neque semper competisse, accuratè animum advertenti facilè patet.
units.tr: These, therefore, are not rightly set up as the marks, or [τεκμήρια], of the true Church. But that they do not all belong to the Roman Church in this way, nor have always belonged to it, is easily clear to anyone who attends to the matter carefully.

units.la: LXVII. Superstunt Contraria; in quibus nunc potissimùm occurrunt Persecutiones & Seductiones.
units.tr: LXVII. What remains are the contraries; among these, persecutions and seductions now chiefly come to mind.

units.la: Persecutiones etiàm minimè defuerunt sub V. T. indè à primis Ecclesiæ incunabilis; juxta istud Gen. 3, 15. Inimicitias ponam, - i & tu conteres Ei calcaneum. Hinc Christus, Matth. 23, 35. Ut veniat super vos omnis sanguis justus, effusus super terram, à sanguine Abel justi, usque ad sanguinem Zachariæ filii Barachiæ, -. 37. Ierusalem, Ierusalem, interemtrix Prophetarum, & lapidatrix eorum qui ad te missi sunt! Adde 1 Joh. 3, 12. Gal. 4, 29. Hebr. xi, 35, -38.
units.tr: Persecutions were by no means lacking under the Old Testament from the earliest beginnings of the Church, according to Gen. 3, 15: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and you shall bruise his heel. Hence Christ says, Matth. 23, 35: That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah; 37: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you! Add 1 John 3, 12; Gal. 4, 29; Heb. 11, 35–38.

units.la: In N. autem T. initium factum est à Capite ac Domino nostro Jesu Christo; de cujus passionibus ac morte diximus suo loco. Vel jam ab ejus Prodromo Johanne Baptistâ, quem Herodes capite mulctavit; Matth. 14, 3,-12. Similem conditionem Christus Apostolis ac Discipulis suis proposuit & prædixit, v, 11. 12. xvi, 24. xx, 23. Adde alia paulo superius allegata. Consequenter occurrit statim exemplum Stephani Diaconi & Protomartyris, lapidati à Judæis; Act. 7, 59, 60. Magna persecutio adversus Ecclesiam Hierosolymitanam memoratur, viii, 1, 2. & tale studium Sauli etiàm adversùs alios fideles; ix, 1, 2. Iterùm Rex Herodes, injectis manibus, malè accepit nonnullos ex Ecclesiâ : interemit autem Jacobum, fratrem Johannis, gladio; & Petrum in carcerem conjecit, qui tamen per Angelum ex eo liberatus est; xii, 1,-. Similiter Apoc. 2, 13. - Antipas Martyr ille meus fidelis; qui trucidatus est apud vos, ubi Satanas habitat. Adde, 1o. III, 1o. VI, 9, 10, 11. 2 Cor. XI, 23, 24, 25.
units.tr: In the New Testament the beginning was made with the Head, our Lord Jesus Christ, whose sufferings and death we have discussed in their place. Or even earlier, with his forerunner John the Baptist, whom Herod beheaded; Matth. 14, 3–12. Christ set before his apostles and disciples a similar lot and foretold it: Matth. 10, 11, 12; 16, 24; 20, 23. Add the other passages cited a little above. Next comes the example of Stephen, the deacon and first martyr, stoned by the Jews; Acts 7, 59, 60. A great persecution against the Church at Jerusalem is recorded, Acts 8, 1, 2, and Saul showed the same zeal even against other believers; Acts 9, 1, 2. Again King Herod laid hands on some from the Church and treated them harshly. He killed James, the brother of John, with the sword, and threw Peter into prison, from which he was nevertheless freed by an angel; Acts 12, 1ff. Similarly Rev. 2, 13: Antipas, my faithful martyr, who was killed among you, where Satan dwells. Add Rev. 3, 10; Rev. 6, 9, 10, 11; 2 Cor. 11, 23, 24, 25.

units.la: Plurima istiusmodi etiam occurrunt in Historia Ecclesiastica: ubi potissimum commemorantur decem Persecutiones universales, sub Imperatoribus Gentilibus instituté. Cum vero Constantinus Magnus Religioni Christianæ nomen dedisset, non multo post Ariani persecuti sunt Orthodoxos; ac porro Julianus Apostata. Ubi autem deinde Antichristus Romanus fecit extulit, alii vero pro fidei puritate ei restiterunt, iterum factæ fuerunt persecutiones variæ; adversus Waldenses (ut appellabant) Bohemos, alios fideles in Germania, Gallia, Britannia, Belgio, &c. de quibus consulenda Martyrologia.
units.tr: Many such things also occur in Church history, where especially the ten universal persecutions under the Gentile emperors are recorded. But after Constantine the Great had given his name to the Christian religion, the Arians soon persecuted the Orthodox, and then Julian the Apostate did so. When later the Roman Antichrist rose up and others resisted him for the purity of the faith, various persecutions again took place: against the Waldenses (as they were called), the Bohemians, and other faithful in Germany, France, Britain, the Low Countries, and elsewhere. On these the Martyrologies should be consulted.

units.la: LXVIII. Seductiones
units.tr: LXVIII. Seductions

units.la: quibus alii à puritate fidei abducuntur fallaci persuasione Haereticorum & Apostatarum, sedulo etiam notandæ sunt. De his exstant Prophetiæ, Matth. 24, 24. Act. 20, 29, 30. 1 Tim. 4, 1, 2, 3: 2, III, 1, -9.
units.tr: By which others are drawn away from the purity of the faith through the deceptive persuasion of heretics and apostates, these too must be carefully noted. Prophecies about them exist: Matth. 24, 24; Acts 20, 29, 30; 1 Tim. 4, 1, 2, 3; 2 Tim. 3, 1–9.

units.la: Inter Haereticos sub N. T. primus recenseri solet Simon Magus; de quo Act. 8, 9, 10, 13, 18, -24. Sed
units.tr: Among the heretics under the New Testament, Simon Magus is usually listed first, concerning whom see Acts 8, 9, 10, 13, 18–24. But

units.la: 2 Tim. II, 16, 17. nominatim commemorantur Hymenæus, & Philetus; qui circa fidem aberrârunt à scopo, dicentes, Resurrectionem jàm esse factam, &c. Alii pro Observatione Legis Cerimonialis adhuc sub N. T. & pro Justificatione ex operibus contenderunt; Act. 15, 1, 2. Gal 1, 6, 7. III, 1. IV, 10, 11: V, 1, -4, 12. Phil. 3, 2, 3, 18, 19. Col. 2, 4, 8, 16, -. Diserte etiam Nicolaitæ appellantur, Apoc. II, 6, 15. In Historiâ Ecclesiastica porrò inter alios recitantur Ebion & Cerinthus, veram Christi Deitatem negantes; Marcionitæ, Montanistæ, Encratitæ, Sabelliani, Manichæi, Ariani & Photiniani, Pelagiani, Nestoriani, Eutychiani, Monotheletæ, &c.
units.tr: 2 Tim. 2, 16, 17 names Hymenaeus and Philetus by name, who strayed from the mark concerning the faith, saying that the resurrection had already taken place, etc. Others, even under the New Testament, contended for observance of the ceremonial law and for justification by works; Acts 15, 1, 2; Gal. 1, 6, 7; 3, 1; 4, 10, 11; 5, 1–4, 12; Phil. 3, 2, 3, 18, 19; Col. 2, 4, 8, 16ff. The Nicolaitans are also expressly named, Rev. 2, 6, 15. In Church history, moreover, among others are listed Ebion and Cerinthus, who denied the true deity of Christ; the Marcionites, Montanists, Encratites, Sabellians, Manichaeans, Arians and Photinians, Pelagians, Nestorians, Eutychians, Monothelites, and so on.

units.la: LXIX. Speciatim considerandus venit Antichristus: quæ appellatio diserte exstat, 1 Joh. 2, 18, 22. iv, 3.
units.tr: LXIX. The Antichrist must be considered in particular. This name expressly occurs in 1 John 2, 18, 22; 4, 3.

units.la: 2 Joh. 7. Ea autem, vi vocis inspectâ, notare potest vel. Christo contrarium: sicut dicitur ἀντίθεσις, oppositio; 1 Tim. 6, 20. ὁ ἀντικείμενος, ille opponens se; 2 Thess. II, 4. vel eum, qui locum Christi occupat, aut tenet: sicut dicitur Ἀνθύπατος, Proconsul; Actor. 13, 7. item ἀντίληψις, ἀντινομασία, &c. Sed Ἀντισέφτης utraque significatione reperitur; ut notet Ducem contrarium: & eum qui est loco Ducis. Sic etiam rectissimè accipitur ὁ Ἀνθίχεμος κατ' ἐξοχήν, qui se Christo substituit, tanquam Vicarium; atque interim Ipsi adversatur maximè: juxta Apoc. 13, 11. Vide aliam Bestiam, ascendentem è terrâ, habentem cornua duo similia Agni; sed loquebatur ut Draco. Verùm generatim vox illa quemvis Hæresiarcham notat.
units.tr: 2 John 7. This name, considered by the force of the word, can signify either what is contrary to Christ, as ἀντίθεσις [antithesis] is called opposition (1 Tim. 6, 20), or ὁ ἀντικείμενος [ho antikeimenos], one who sets himself against (2 Thess. 2, 4); or one who occupies or holds the place of Christ, as ἀνθύπατος [anthypatos] is called proconsul (Acts 13, 7); likewise ἀντίληψις [antilēpsis], ἀντονομασία [antonomasia], etc. But Antichristus is found in both senses, to signify a contrary leader and one who stands in the place of the leader. So too the Antichrist, ὁ Ἀντίχριστος κατ' ἐξοχήν [ho Antichristos kat' exochēn], is rightly understood as one who puts himself in Christ's place as a vicar, and yet is chiefly opposed to him, according to Rev. 13, 11: I saw another beast coming up out of the earth, having two horns like a lamb, but it spoke like a dragon. In general, however, that word denotes any heresiarch.

units.la: Magnus ille Antichristus secundùm SS. Literas describitur plenius, quod sit Papa Romanus, prout hic Satanæ efficaciâ per multiplicem à doctrinâ Christi defectionem paulatim exortus est, ac tandem Imperii Romani ruinâ patefactus; quî sub professionis Christi larvâ, Ipsius adversarius exiit, supra omnem Deum se efferens, sibique universalis Ecclesiæ & totius Orbis dominium arrogans; doctrinæ interim ac signorum mendaciis, vitæ impuræ exemplis, sævâque tyrannide, plurimos homines in errores, idololatriam, & exitium seducens; donec Christi Verbo, atque illustri adventû, tandem destruatur.
units.tr: The great Antichrist is described more fully according to the Holy Scriptures: he is the Roman Pope, who has gradually arisen through the efficacy of Satan by manifold defection from the doctrine of Christ, and at last has been revealed by the ruin of the Roman Empire. Under the mask of the profession of Christ he has come forth as Christ's adversary, exalting himself above every God and arrogating to himself dominion over the universal Church and the whole world. Meanwhile, by lying doctrines and signs, by examples of impure life and savage tyranny, he seduces very many men into errors, idolatry and ruin, until at last he is destroyed by the Word of Christ and by his illustrious coming.

units.la: LXX. Papam dicimus, sive Episcopum, aut Antistitem Ecclesiæ Dei: in quâ Antichristus non solùm est; sed etiam ei præest ac præsidet. 2 Thess. 2, 4. Ut in templo Dei - sedeat. h. e. in Ecclesia : Eph. 2, 21.
units.tr: LXX. We call the Pope, whether bishop or leader of the Church of God, the one in whom Antichrist not only is but also presides and sits in charge: 2 Thess. 2, 4, that he sits in the temple of God, that is, in the Church; Eph. 2, 21.

units.la: 2 Cor. 6, 16. Confer Apoc. 18, 4. perperam vero Pontificii illud exponunt de Templo Hierosolymitano. Addimus Romanum: propria enim ejus sedes debuit esse Roma; magna illa septem montium civitas; Apoc. xvii, 9. quae isto tempore regnum habebat super Reges terrae: verf. 18. Hic autem est ille Λατεινος, conficiens numerum 666. juxta Apoc. xiii, 18. quemadmodum olim observavit Irenaeus, discipulus Polycarpi, qui Apostolum Johannem audiverat. Unde etiam Vulgata Versio Latina ejus sectatoribus habetur authentica; & Officium publicum Latinum est. Atque isti Episcopo reliqua omnia conveniunt, quae de Antichristo praedicta sunt.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 6, 16. Compare Rev. 18, 4. The Papists wrongly explain this of the temple at Jerusalem. We add "Roman," for his proper seat ought to be Rome, that great city of seven hills (Rev. 17, 9), which at that time held kingdom over the kings of the earth (v. 18). Now this is the Λατεινος [Latinos] who makes up the number 666, according to Rev. 13, 18, as Irenaeus, the disciple of Polycarp who had heard the apostle John, once observed. Hence the Latin Vulgate version is also held authentic by his followers, and the Latin public office is based on it. And all the other things foretold of Antichrist agree with this bishop.

units.la: Efficaciam Satanae appellamus, juxta 2 Thess. 2, 9. Confer Gen. 3, 15. Joh. 8, 44. Eph. 2, 3. Hinc Causa formationis: Defectio, tum particularis, tum universalis. Particularis defectio jam Apostolorum aetate coepta fuit, partim per Haereticarchas: 1 Joh. 4, 1, partim per ambitiosos quosdam Ecclesiarum Ministros: 2 Joh. 9, 10. Sic enim multi Antichristi extitisse dicuntur; 1 Joh. 2, 18. quos Tertullianus Praecursores magni illius Antichristi recte appellavit; cum in iis effet spiritus illius: 1 Joh. 4, 3. Atque ita Mysterium iniquitatis jam tum operabatur: 2 Thess. 2, 7. Neque enim stipulae solum superstruebantur vero fundamento: 1 Cor. 3, 12. sed etiam errores valde graves; utpote contra Veritatem personae Christi: 1 Joh. 2, 22, 23. iv, 13. 2 Joh. 7. & officiorum ipsius: 1 Joh. 2, 22. De Justificatione hominis coram Deo ex operibus: Gal. 5, 4. cultu Angelorum: Col. II, 18. ciborum quorundam prohibitione: 21. ἐθελοθρησκεία, humilitatis ostentatione, corporisque immodica afflictione: 22, 23. Post excessum vero Apostolorum, Mysterium istud magis profecit; ut praedictum, Act. 20, 29, 30. Gnostici enim introduxerunt cultum imaginum Christi; Collyridiani, adorationem Virginis Mariae; Manichaei, necessitatem coelibatus Episcoporum; Encratitae, prohibitionem esus carnium; Cathari, gloriationem de bonorum operum meritis; Pelagiani, errores circa gratiam & liberum arbitrium; alii alios.
units.tr: We call it the efficacy of Satan, according to 2 Thess. 2, 9. Compare Gen. 3, 15; John 8, 44; Eph. 2, 3. Hence the cause of its formation is defection, both particular and universal. Particular defection began already in the age of the apostles, partly through heresiarchs (1 John 4, 1), and partly through certain ambitious ministers of the churches (2 John 9, 10). For thus many antichrists are said to have arisen (1 John 2, 18), whom Tertullian rightly called forerunners of that great Antichrist, since the same spirit was in them (1 John 4, 3). And so the mystery of iniquity was already at work (2 Thess. 2, 7). For not only was stubble built upon the true foundation (1 Cor. 3, 12), but also very grave errors arose: against the truth of the person of Christ (1 John 2, 22, 23; 4, 13; 2 John 7) and of his offices (1 John 2, 22); concerning the justification of man before God by works (Gal. 5, 4); the worship of angels (Col. 2, 18); the prohibition of certain foods (v. 21); self-chosen worship, ostentation of humility and immoderate affliction of the body (vv. 22, 23). After the departure of the apostles that mystery advanced further, as had been foretold (Acts 20, 29, 30). For the Gnostics introduced the worship of images of Christ; the Collyridians the adoration of the Virgin Mary; the Manichaeans the necessity of celibacy for bishops; the Encratites the prohibition of eating meat; the Cathari boasted of the merits of good works; the Pelagians fell into errors about grace and free will; and others into others.

units.la: Universalis defectio indicatur, 2 Thess. II, 3. Talis una fuit aperta; Arii, quem Athanasius Antichristi ἀντιχριστοῦ dixit. Isti autem involuta fuit Ecclesia Romana, cum Episcopo suo Liberio. Altera fuit latens, per incuriam studii Scripturarii, imperitiam, coecum Religionis zelum, nec non avaritiam & superbiam: quorum specimina satis multa sunt obvia. Hinc Victor Ecclesias Asiaticas a communione exclusit, ob diversum diem Paschatis servatum: &c. Accesserunt figmenta Miraculorum ad superstitiones committendas, & fabulae multarum Traditionum.
units.tr: A universal defection is indicated in 2 Thess. 2:3. One such defection was open, that of Arius, whom Athanasius called the Antichrist [antichristos]. Against that defection the Roman Church, with its bishop Liberius, was involved. The other was hidden, arising from neglect of the study of Scripture, from ignorance, from a blind zeal for religion, and also from avarice and pride, of which there are many plain examples. Hence Victor excluded the Asian churches from communion because they observed a different day for Easter, etc. Fictitious miracles were added to foster superstitions, and the fables of many traditions.

units.la: Opportuna interim occasio patefactionis supervenit: Imperii Romani ruina: 2 Thess. II, 6, 7, 8. cum Apoc. 13, 3, 11, 12. Imperator enim Byzantium migrans, Romam deseruit; & Roma vicissim Imperatoris jugum excussit. Sic autem revelatio facta est in Bonifacio III. anno 607. magis autem in Stephano II. anno 654.
units.tr: Meanwhile an opportune occasion for the revealing of the mystery arrived: the ruin of the Roman Empire (2 Thess. 2:6, 7, 8), together with Rev. 13:3, 11, 12. For the emperor moved to Byzantium and abandoned Rome, and Rome in turn threw off the yoke of the emperor. Thus the revelation was made in Boniface III, in the year 607, and more fully in Stephen II, in the year 654.

units.la: LXXI. Quod ad hypocrisin, & simulationem professionis Christi larvam; Antichristus fefellurus erat in templo Dei, atque ita hominēs seducturus: 2 Thess. 2, 4, 10. Dei Spiritum simulaturus: 1 Joh. 4, 13. & duo cornua habiturus, Agni similia: Apoc. 13, 11. Confer 1 Tim. 4, 1, 2. de spiritibus deceptoribus, per hypocrisin falsiloquis. Sic autem Pontifex Romanus inde a Bonifacio III. generatim quidem S. Scripturam, & summa capita Catechesios Christianae praetendit; sed subvertit simul: dum sese Christi vicarium appellat, &c.
units.tr: LXXI. As to hypocrisy and the mask of a pretended profession of Christ: the Antichrist was to deceive in the temple of God and so lead men astray (2 Thess. 2:4, 10); he was to counterfeit the Spirit of God (1 John 4:13), and he was to have two horns like a lamb (Rev. 13:11). Compare 1 Tim. 4:1, 2, concerning deceiving spirits who speak lies through hypocrisy. Thus the Roman Pontiff, from the time of Boniface III, puts forward in general the Holy Scripture and the chief heads of Christian catechesis, but at the same time subverts them, while he calls himself the vicar of Christ, etc.

units.la: Sed & sceleratus est: 2 Thess. II, 3, 8. actalis Christi adversarius; ἀντικείμενος: verf. 4. & sic Ἀντίχρι-
units.tr: But he is also wicked (2 Thess. 2:3, 8), the adversary of Christ [antikeimenos] (verse 4), and so Antichri-

units.la: Magis hoc patet per essecta: dum impie sese extollit supra Deum, aut quicquid Deus appellatur: 2 Thess. II, 4. Sic autem Papa Romanus Legibus Dei suas opponit, & praeponit; gravioremque redemtuuram Legum suarum constituit, quam Divinarum: quod videre est in Taxa poenitentiaria. Et sibi vendicat potestatem Sanctos canonizandi, cultumque religiosum iis decernendi; quod ipse Deus non potest: Isa. 42, 8. 2 Tim. II, 13. Quid jam mirum, si supra homines quoscunque sese extollat? Apoc. XI, 8. XVII, 1, 2, 7, 15. Sic autem Johannes XXII. dixit; "Summo Pontifici, in persona B. Petri, terreni simul & coelestis Imperii jura esse commissa. Hinc etiam Pontifex Tiaram cum triplici Corona aurea gestat, quae Regnum dicitur. Et Bonifacius VIII. pronunciavit, "Omnem humanam creaturam Pontifici Romano subesse; idque omnino esse de necessitate salutis.
units.tr: This is more clearly seen from his effects: he impiously exalts himself above God, or above whatever is called God (2 Thess. 2:4). Thus the Roman Pope sets his own laws against the laws of God and places them above them, and he establishes that the penalties of his own laws are more serious than the divine ones, as may be seen in the Penitential Taxation. He also claims for himself the power of canonizing saints and of decreeing religious worship to them, which God himself cannot do (Isa. 42:8; 2 Tim. 2:13). What wonder, then, if he exalts himself above all men whatsoever (Rev. 11:8; 17:1, 2, 7, 15)? Thus John XXII said: "To the supreme Pontiff, in the person of blessed Peter, the rights of both the earthly and the heavenly empire have been committed." Hence the Pontiff also wears a tiara with a triple golden crown, which is called a kingdom. And Boniface VIII declared that "every human creature is subject to the Roman Pontiff, and that this is altogether necessary for salvation."

units.la: Specialius praedictum fore, ut ostentaret se Deum esse:
units.tr: It was foretold more particularly that he would show himself to be God:

units.la: 2 Thess. II, 4. & ab incolis terrae adoraretur: Apoc. 13, 3. Sic autem, rogatu Bonifacii III. Imperator Phocas sedem Romanae & Apostolicae Ecclesiae pronunciavit Caput omnium Ecclesiarum. Unde porro immane jugum Legum anathemate sancitarum promanavit: sua autem judicia, imo & flagitia, omnium hominum; etiam Conciliorum, judiciis exemit a ἀνομ@: se Potestatis Christi Vicarium; Ecclesiam vero Sponsam suam appellavit; pro arbitrio item suo peccatorum remissionem, & varios coelestis gloriae gradus, dispensare praesumsit: quin & Dei, ac Divinae Majestatis, appellationem admisit. Consequenter etiam Clericos suos potestati Politicae subtraxit: Reges vero & Principes regnis ac dominationibus ipsorum aliquando exuit. Subditos a juramento fidelitatis & ab obedientia absolvit; ad Pedum suorum oscula illos admisit; imo etiam colla ipsorum suis pedibus aliquando compressit.
units.tr: (2 Thess. 2:4), and that he would be worshipped by the inhabitants of the earth (Rev. 13:3). Thus, at the request of Boniface III, the emperor Phocas declared the see of the Roman and Apostolic Church to be the head of all churches. From this there further flowed a monstrous yoke of laws sanctioned by anathema; he exempted his own judgments, and even his own shameful deeds, from the judgments of all men, even of Councils, a lawlessness [anomia]; he called himself the vicar of the power of Christ, and called the Church his spouse; he also presumed, at his own pleasure, to dispense the remission of sins and the various degrees of heavenly glory; nay, he admitted the title of God and of Divine Majesty. Consequently he also withdrew his clergy from political power, and sometimes stripped kings and princes of their kingdoms and dominions. He absolved subjects from the oath of allegiance and from obedience; he admitted them to kiss his feet, and indeed sometimes pressed their necks under his feet.

units.la: @ Ibid.
units.tr: Ibid.

units.la: LXXII. Seductionem ille peracturus erat illecebris Doctrinarum fallacium: idem Spiritus Antichristi opponitur Spiritui Dei; 1 Joh. 4, 3. ipse Pseudopropheta appellatur; Apoc. 16, 13. & Seductio iniquitatis ei tribuitur; 2 Thess. II, 10. Specialiús huc pertinent Leges iniquæ de Cœlibatu, & Delectu ciborum: 1 Tim. 4, 1, 2, 3. Sic Papa per universam passim Theologiam errores plurimos introduxit; atque etiam illos, de quibus prædictum erat diserte.
units.tr: LXXII. The Antichrist was to carry out seduction by the allurements of false doctrines: the same spirit of Antichrist is set against the Spirit of God (1 John 4:3); he is called a false prophet (Rev. 16:13), and the seduction of iniquity is attributed to him (2 Thess. 2:10). More especially to this belong the unjust laws concerning celibacy and the forbidding of foods (1 Tim. 4:1, 2, 3). Thus the Pope has introduced very many errors throughout almost all of theology, and even those of which it was expressly foretold.

units.la: Accedunt Signa mendacia, tum falsò conficta, tum ad mendaciorum confirmationem applicata: 2 Thess. II, 9. Apoc. 13, 13. Talia autem à Pontificiis passim jactantur & celebrantur.
units.tr: To these are added lying signs, both those falsely fabricated and those applied to confirm lies (2 Thess. 2:9; Rev. 13:13). Such things are everywhere boasted of and celebrated by the Papists.

units.la: Atque item Exempla vitæ impuræ: 2 Thess. II, 3, 8. Apoc. 17, 1, 5. XI, 8. Itâ in ipsorum Scriptis Pontifices Magi, Simoniaci, impuri, scelerati, recensentur plurimi.
units.tr: Likewise examples of an impure life (2 Thess. 2:3, 8; Rev. 17:1, 5; 11:8). Thus in their own writings very many popes are listed as magicians, simoniacs, impure men, and wicked men.

units.la: De Crudelitate & coactione tyrannicâ prædictum similiter Apoc. 17, 6. Complementum satis est evidens: attestatur enim frequens experientia; & sanguis fidelium, à Curiæ Romanæ satellitibus copiosissimè fusus, vindictam inclamavit diù; juxta Apoc. 6, 9. XVIII, 5. XIX, 2.
units.tr: Concerning cruelty and tyrannical coercion, a prophecy likewise appears in Rev. 17:6. The fulfilment is sufficiently evident: frequent experience bears witness to it, and the blood of the faithful, poured out most copiously by the satellites of the Roman Curia, has long cried out for vengeance, according to Rev. 6:9; 18:5; 19:2.

units.la: Effectus istius Seductionis est in hâc vitâ plurimorum hominum error multiplex: 2 Thess. II, 10, 11. Apoc. 8, 8. atque idololatria: XIII, 15. & post hanc vitam exitium, sive justa condemnatio omnium, qui ab illis non receperint: 2 Thess. II, 10, 11, 12.
units.tr: The effect of this seduction is, in this life, a manifold error among very many men (2 Thess. 2:10, 11; Rev. 8:8), and idolatry (Rev. 13:15); and after this life ruin, or the just condemnation of all who have not received the truth from them (2 Thess. 2:10, 11, 12).

units.la: Ipsius autem Antichristi eventus est ejus Destructio; quæ quidem inchoari debuit per Verbum Dei: 2 Thess. II, 8. ut retegerentur errores, idololatria, & tyrannis illius; multique homines, isto præconio moniti, Babylone exirent: Apoc. 18, 4. Reges autem & Principes excitati, eum deserrerent, spoliisque & injustis honoribus exuerent; XVII, 16. Quæ quidem cœpta sunt modò; rogandus autem est Dominus; ut Ipse propitius ac potens perficiat opus suum.
units.tr: The outcome of the Antichrist himself is his Destruction, which indeed ought to begin through the Word of God (2 Thess. 2:8), so that his errors, idolatry and tyranny might be uncovered, and many men, warned by this proclamation, might come out of Babylon (Rev. 18:4). Kings and princes, too, are to be stirred up to abandon him, to strip him of his spoils and unjust honours (Rev. 17:16). These things have indeed now begun, but the Lord must be asked that He Himself, propitious and powerful, may bring His work to completion.

units.la: Tandem vero consummabitur ejus abolitio in illustri adventu Domini: 2 Thess. II, 8. unde ille in infernum conjicietur: Apoc. 19, 2.
units.tr: Finally, however, his abolition will be consummated at the glorious coming of the Lord (2 Thess. 2:8), whereupon he will be cast into hell (Rev. 19:2).

units.la: LXXIII. Pontificii multa alia de Antichristo commiscuntur temere: futurum eum unum duntaxat hominem, religione Judaeum, ex tribu Dan; restauraturum Politiam, & cultum Judaicum, atque ipsum templum Hierosolymitanum; regnaturum solummodo tres annos cum dimidio; reversuros tunc Enochum & Eliam ex Paradiso, & cum illo congressuros, hinc interficiendos sed tertio die resurrecturos a morte, &c. Verum non ista; sed plane alia, & plurima, de eo traduntur in SS. Literis.
units.tr: LXXIII. The Papists rashly mix in many other things about the Antichrist: that he will be a single man only, a Jew by religion, of the tribe of Dan; that he will restore the Jewish polity and worship, and the temple of Jerusalem itself; that he will reign only three and a half years; that Enoch and Elijah will then return from paradise and will meet him, and that he will be killed by him but rise from the dead on the third day, etc. But these things are not what is handed down about him in the Holy Scriptures; rather, quite different and very many things are.

units.la: Nos autem merito colligimus contra eosdem, Ecclesiam Romanam esse Antichristianam, ac veram Babylonem Apocalypticam: atque adeo majores nostros calisas habuisse gravissimas ab ea exeundi: idem reliquis ista captivitate adhuc detentis, & salutis suae studiosis, agendum esse quantocyus; nemini vero ad ejus communionem, aut subjectionem, revertendum. Nam 1. disertum est mandatum & monitum Domini, Apoc. 18, 4. Exite ex ea, populc mi; ne participes fitis peccatorum ejus, & ex plagis ejus accipiatis. Confer Rom. 16, 17. 2 Cor. 6, 14.
units.tr: We, however, rightly conclude against the same men that the Roman Church is antichristian and the true Apocalyptic Babylon; and therefore our forefathers had very serious reasons for coming out of it. The same must be done as quickly as possible by the rest who are still held in that captivity and who care for their own salvation; but no one should return to its communion or subjection. For first, the command and warning of the Lord is clear: Rev. 18:4. Come out of her, my people, lest you be partakers of her sins and receive of her plagues. Compare Confer Rom. 16:17; 2 Cor. 6:14.

units.la: 2. Accedunt Canones satis graves & justae, respectu Credendorum; ubi multiplex haeresis & apostasia: quod passim annotatum est in superioribus.
units.tr: Second, there are the canons, quite grave and just, concerning the things to be believed, where there is manifold heresy and apostasy, as has been noted everywhere in the preceding sections.

units.la: 3. Similiter respectu Agendorum; ubi multiplex idololatria, superstitio, & prava dogmata morália eaque irreformabilia.
units.tr: Third, likewise concerning the things to be done, where there is manifold idolatry, superstition, and depraved moral doctrines, which cannot be reformed.

units.la: 4. Etiam respectu Regiminis; ubi immanissima tyrannis.
units.tr: Fourth, also concerning government, where there is most monstrous tyranny.

units.la: LXXIV. Sed & magna est, atque Ecclesiae valde contraria, & longe lateque diffusa, apostasia per Muhammedem instituta in Oriente, eodem fere tempore, quo Antichristus revelatus est in Occidente. Ille autem, sublatis SS. Bibliis, impurum suum Koranum substituit; fundamenta Religionis Christianæ subtulit; & paucas veritatis reliquias plurimis ac fœdissimis erroribus atque superstitionibus, partim ex Gentilismo, partim etiam ex Judaïsmo, mutuatis, corrupit penitus.
units.tr: LXXIV. But there is also a great apostasy, very contrary to the Church and spread far and wide, established in the East through Muhammad at about the same time that the Antichrist was revealed in the West. He, having removed the Holy Bibles, substituted his own impure Koran; he undermined the foundations of the Christian religion, and, corrupting the few remnants of truth with very many and most foul errors and superstitions, borrowed partly from Gentilism and partly also from Judaism, he thoroughly corrupted it.

units.la: Veræ Ecclesiæ vehementer etiam adversantur Sociniani; quique eorum sequaces, vel affines, sunt inter Remonstrantes, & Anabaptistas: ac porro Enthusiastæ, & Libertini: suo denique modo & gradu reliqui Anabaptistæ, Remonstrantes, & Ubiquitarii. Omnes denique homines carnales, mundani, ἄπιστοι.
units.tr: The Socinians also strongly oppose the true Church, and their followers or kin among the Remonstrants and the Anabaptists; further, the Enthusiasts and the Libertines; and finally, in their own way and degree, the remaining Anabaptists, Remonstrants and Ubiquitarians. In short, all carnal and worldly men, unbelievers [ἄπιστοι].

units.la: LXXV. Pro Praxi denique
units.tr: LXXV. Finally, for practice

units.la: 1. Probemus nos ipsos, an vere habeamus mysticam cum Christo & Ecclesiâ ipsius communionem: 2 Cor. 13, 5. atque in eâ studeamus proficere: Eph. 4, 15, 16.
units.tr: 1. Let us examine ourselves, whether we truly have mystical communion with Christ and his Church, 2 Cor. 13:5; and let us strive to grow in it, Eph. 4:15, 16.

units.la: 2. Sic vivamus in Ecclesiâ institutâ; omniaque spiritualis incrementi media observemus sedulò. Act. 11, 41, 42. Hebr. x, 25.
units.tr: 2. Let us live thus in the instituted Church, and diligently observe all the means of spiritual growth. Acts 2:41, 42; Heb. 10:25.

units.la: 3. Singuli, pro ratione vocationis, ordinis, ac donorum, conferamus quicquid in nobis est, ad communem Ecclesiæ ædificationem ac propagationem: Rom. 12, 4, - 11.
units.tr: 3. Each of us, according to his calling, office and gifts, should contribute whatever is in us to the common edification and propagation of the Church: Rom. 12:4–11.

units.la: 4. Adversus hostes nostros spirituales, omnesque seductiones & tentationes, corroboremur: atque in verâ fide, ac fideli sanctimoniâ, perseveremus: 1 Tim. 6, 12. Eph. 6, 10, - 17.
units.tr: 4. Let us be strengthened against our spiritual enemies and all seductions and temptations, and persevere in the true faith and faithful holiness: 1 Tim. 6:12; Eph. 6:10–17.

units.la: 5. Sic mente feramur, omnique studio contendamus, ad Ecclesiam triumphantem, & gloriam in cœlis æternam: Phil. 3, 10, - 14, 28. 2 Tim. 4, 7, 8.
units.tr: 5. Let our minds be carried, and let us strive with all eagerness, toward the triumphant Church and the eternal glory in heaven: Phil. 3:10–14, 28; 2 Tim. 4:7, 8.

units.la: Amen; veni Domine JESU!
units.tr: Amen; come, Lord Jesus!

units.la: Dominis Studiosis, Sacro Ministerio Dicatis, Salutem.
units.tr: To the Studious Gentlemen, Dedicated to the Sacred Ministry, Greetings.

units.la: OUm editio secunda Compendii Dogmatici D. ANDREÆ ESSENII, Collegæ Conjunctissimi, nescio quo fato, curæ meæ sit commissa, (quam curam ob pietatem in Collegam, libenter mihi imponi passus sum) incidit in mentem circa finem operis: Annon consultum esset huic Editioni addere illas disputationes, quas anno 1645. & 1646. Clariss. D. Johannes Hoornbeek, olim Præceptor venerandus, & postea Collega intimus in hac Academia conscripsit. Fuit intima amicitia inter utrumque Collegam; Fuit eadem intentio in gloria divina promovenda, & eundem modum eandemque Methodum observabant in tuenda causa Dei & Ecclesiæ; Eandem Theologiam profitebantur; Eandem etiam Methodum concionandi, quæ per Excellentiam diu ULTRAJECTINA vocata est, docebant, & juventuti Theologiæ dicatæ privatim & publice instillabant. Ut ergo Domini Studiosi horum duorum magnorum Virorum Theologiam Theoreticam & simul Methodum Ultrajectinam concionės formandi, utramque puram & immaculatam haberent, judicavi consultum hunc utrumque Theologum conjungere; præcipuè hoc tempore cum illa Methodus à nonnullis jam invertatur, permutetur, & pro genuina Ultrajectina plura verba quàm ipsius Textus retinere possint. Est etiam accommodata Academiæ : nam D. Studiosi exscribentes & repetentes DD. Pastorum conciones, vix possunt aliorum conciones exscribere & repetere, nisi hac Ultrajectina methodo habitas. Propterea nostri Studiosi à multis annis semper exscripserunt eorum Pastorum conciones, qui accuratiorem Methodum Ultrajectinam observabant ; etiam fatentur hodierni se aliorum conciones exscribere vix posse. Propter has & similes causas hanc Methodum secuti sunt Voetius, Schotanus, De Matius, Hoornbekius, Essenius aliique non sine honore nominandi, eamque etiam Juvenibus Academicis jugiter instillarunt; qui postea promoti, eâ clarâ & distinctâ Methodo, non sine magno fructu usi sunt in Ecclesiis suis. Mirati sæpe sunt multi, quomodo Academia nostra intra paucos annos ad tantum fastigium pervenerit, ut tam innumeri inde prodierint felices Pastores. Sed desinent mirari, si, præter diligentiam Professorum, etiam considerent hanc Ultrajectinam concionandi Methodum hic fuisse usitatam. Ad hanc discendam veniebant undique D. Studiosi. Si igitur hæc Methodus hinc turbaretur, & alia introduceretur, non utile esset Ecclesiæ & Academiæ nostræ, quę utraque assueta est illi Methodo;etiam alia Methodus Auditores perplexos redderet, qui parum inde retinere possent. Utinam Deo placeret ad bonum publicum hanc Methodum in hac Academia & Ecclesia confervare! Valete.
units.tr: When, by some fate I do not know, the second edition of the Compendium of Dogmatic Theology of Master Andreas Essenius, my most intimate colleague, was entrusted to my care (a care I gladly allowed to be laid upon me out of devotion to my colleague), there came to mind, near the end of the work, the question whether it would be advisable to add to this edition those disputations which the most distinguished Master Johannes Hoornbeek, once my venerable teacher and afterwards my closest colleague in this Academy, had written in the years 1645 and 1646. There was a close friendship between the two colleagues. They had the same aim of promoting the glory of God, and they observed the same manner and the same method in defending the cause of God and the Church. They professed the same theology, and they also taught the same method of preaching, which for its excellence has long been called the ULTRAJECTINE method, and they instilled it privately and publicly into the youth devoted to theology. Therefore, so that the studious gentlemen might have both the theoretical theology of these two great men and the Ultrajectine method of forming a sermon, each pure and unblemished, I judged it advisable to join these two theologians together. This is especially so at this time, when that method is already being inverted and altered by some, and in place of the genuine Ultrajectine method they retain more words than the text itself can bear. It is also suited to the Academy. For the studious gentlemen, in copying out and repeating the sermons of the reverend ministers, can hardly copy out and repeat the sermons of others unless these are delivered in this Ultrajectine method. For this reason our students for many years have always copied out the sermons of those ministers who observed the more exact Ultrajectine method; and even today they confess that they can scarcely copy out the sermons of others. For these and similar reasons Voetius, Schotanus, De Matius, Hoornbeek, Essenius, and others not to be named without honour followed this method, and they constantly instilled it into the young academics. These, afterwards promoted, used that clear and distinct method, not without great fruit, in their churches. Many have often wondered how our Academy in a few years rose to such a height that so many happy ministers came forth from it. But they will cease to wonder if, besides the diligence of the professors, they also consider that this Ultrajectine method of preaching was customary here. To learn it, studious gentlemen came from everywhere. If therefore this method were disturbed here and another introduced, it would not be useful to the Church and to our Academy, both of which are accustomed to that method; and another method would also render the hearers perplexed, who could retain little from it. Would that it might please God to preserve this method in this Academy and Church for the public good! Farewell.

units.la: JOHAN-
units.tr: JOHAN-

units.la: JOHANNIS HOORNBEEK, TRACTATUS DE RATIONE CONCIONANDI.
units.tr: JOHANNES HOORNBEEK, TRACTATUS DE RATIONE CONCIONANDI.

units.la: CAPUT PRIMUM.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: I. Concio est, actio sacra explicans Dei verbum, & applicans ad ædificationem Ecclesiæ, 1 Cor. 14, 3, 19, 26. Jesa. 21, 10. Jerem. 7, 2. Jezech. 3, 17. 1 Tim. 1, 5. & 6, 17.
units.tr: I. Concio is a sacred action that explains God's Word and applies it to the edification of the Church: 1 Cor. 14:3, 19, 26; Isa. 21:10; Jer. 7:2; Ezek. 3:17; 1 Tim. 1:5 and 6:17.

units.la: Concio aliquando pro cætu sumitur; at hic pro sermone ad cætum. Tertullianus utrumque egregiè, in apol. Coimus in cætum & congregationem, ut ad Deum quasi manu facta precationibus ambiamus orantes. Hæc vis Deo grata est. Oramus etiam pro Imperatoribus, pro ministris eorum, & potestatibus sæculi, pro rerum quiete, pro morâ finis: Coimus ad divinarum litterarum commemorationem, si quid præsentium temporum qualitas aut præmonere cogit, aut recognoscere &c.
units.tr: Concio is sometimes taken for the assembly, but here it means the sermon delivered to the assembly. Tertullian uses both senses admirably in the Apology: We meet together as an assembly and congregation, so that we may surround God with prayers as with a bundle of hands. This kind of violence is pleasing to God. We pray also for the emperors, for their ministers and the powers of the world, for the quiet of the times and the delay of the end. We meet to recall the divine letters, if the condition of the present times compels us either to forewarn or to recognise something, etc.

units.la: II. Actio sacra, quæ idcirco non nisi à sancto, & sanctè haberi potest. Qualis minister esse debeat, quam castigatæ, & piæ vitæ, docet compendio Apostolus in Epistolis ad Timotheum, & Titum.
units.tr: II. Sacred action, which for this reason can be undertaken only by a holy person and in a holy manner. What sort of minister he ought to be, and how chaste and pious his life, the Apostle teaches briefly in his Epistles to Timothy and Titus.

units.la: Quas tres Apostolicas epistolas ante oculos habere debet, cui est in Ecclesia Doctoris persona imposita, inquit Augustin. de Doctr. Christian. lib. 4. cap. 16. & cap. 27. Habet ut obedienter audiatur quantacunque granditate dictionis majus pondus vita dicentis. Et Gregor. M. praedicator quisque plus actibus, quam vocibus insonet, & bene vivendo vestigia sequacibus imprimat, ut potius agendo, quam loquendo, quo gradiatur, ostendat. Pastoral. part. 3. cap. 6. De vita eorum, qualis esse debeat, ex Veteris Ecclesiae instituto, & canonibus, alias agimus.
units.tr: One who has been placed in the office of teacher in the Church ought to keep these three apostolic epistles before his eyes, says Augustine, On Christian Doctrine, book 4, chapters 16 and 27. However great the eloquence of the speaker, he has the greater weight, so that he may be heard obediently, in the life he lives. And Gregory the Great: Let each preacher resound more by his deeds than by his voice, and by living well let him imprint footsteps for those who follow, so that by acting rather than speaking he shows the way they should walk. Pastoral Care, part 3, chapter 6. We treat elsewhere of the life such a man ought to lead, according to the practice and canons of the ancient Church.

units.la: Sanctus, & sanctè; I. e. 1. animo ad hoc. II. modo. III. fine, sanctis. Jerem. 3. 15. Jezech. 34. Phil. 1. 15, 16, 17, 18. Egregiè, & ut solet, ardenter Hieron. ep. ad Eustoch. de virginit. Sunt alii (de mei ordinis hominibus loquor) qui ideo presbyterium & diaconatum ambiunt, ut mulieres licentius videant. Omnis his cura de vestibus, si bene oleant: si pes, laxa pelle, non folleat. Crines calamistri vestigio rotantur, digiti de annulis radiant: & ne plantas humidior via spargat, vix imprimunt summa vestigia. Tales cum videris, sponsos magis existimato, quam clericos. Quidam in hoc omne studium vitamque posuerunt, ut matronarum nomina, domos morésque cognoscant. Ex quibus unum, qui hujus artis est princeps, breviter, strictimque, describam, quo facilius magistro cognito, discipulos recognoscas. Cum sole festinus exurgit, salutandi ei ordo disponitur, viarum compendia requiruntur, & pene usque ad cubilia dormientium Senex importunus ingreditur. Si pulvillum viderit, si mantile elegans, si aliquid domesticae supellectilis, laudat, miratur, attrectat, & se his indigere conquerens, non tam impetrat, quam extorquet, quia singulae metuunt veredarium urbis offendere.
units.tr: Holy, and holily: that is, (1) in mind, for this purpose; (2) in manner; (3) in aim, holy. Jer. 3:15; Ezek. 34; Phil. 1:15, 16, 17, 18. Jerome writes admirably, and as is his way, with fervour, in his letter to Eustochium on virginity: There are others (I am speaking of men of my own order) who seek the presbyterate and the diaconate only so that they may see women more freely. For such men all care is for their clothes, that they smell sweet; for their feet, that the soft leather does not wrinkle. Their hair is curled with tongs, their fingers flash with rings, and so that a damp road may not splash their soles, they scarcely set the tips of their feet down. When you see such men, think of them as bridegrooms rather than clergy. Some have put all their zeal and life into this, to know the names, houses and manners of the matrons. Of these, I will describe briefly and concisely the one who is chief of this art, so that, once the master is known, you may recognise the disciples. At sunrise he hurries out; the order of greetings is arranged, the shortcuts through the streets are sought, and the importunate old man goes in almost as far as the beds of those still sleeping. If he sees a cushion, if an elegant tablecloth, if any household furniture, he praises it, admires it, handles it, and complaining that he lacks such things, he does not so much obtain them as extort them, because each woman fears to offend the city's courier.

units.la: III. Ex S. Dei verbo.
units.tr: III. Of the Holy Word of God.

units.la: nim. solo Dei verbo, & omni Dei verbo, Luc. 16, 31. & 24, 27. Act. 20, 27. & 26, 22. Solo, quia solum. I. Authenticum. II. Canonicum.
units.tr: Only the Word of God, and the whole Word of God (Luke 16:31; 24:27; Acts 20:27; 26:22). "Only," because it alone is (I) authentic and (II) canonical.

units.la: 2 Tim. 3, 16. 2 Petr. 1, 10. Gal. 6, 16. Jef. 8, verf. 20. Reliqua scripta incerta, fallibilia, ad normam verbi divini examinanda, & nisi cum eo conveniant, in hoc genere non recipienda.
units.tr: (2 Tim. 3:16; 2 Pet. 1:10; Gal. 6:16; Isa. 8:20.) Other writings are uncertain and fallible; they are to be tested by the rule of the divine Word and, unless they agree with it, are not to be received in this matter.

units.la: Quaer. Annon item ex Catechismo? Resp. non ex Catechismo, ut scripto Canonico; verum ille laudabiliter etiam explicatur, probatur, pro concione tractatur; sed ex scriptura. Neque adeo discrepat sententia Cl. Amesii caf. conf. lib. 4. cap. 26. Scripturae enim locus catecheticae institutioni semper praemittitur; at parum refert, sive per explicationem textus, ad Catechesin deveniam, sive statim ad Catechesin (post lectum Scripturae locum, auditam) explicandam, ejusque nihil nisi ex scriptura probandum, ocyus accedam, cauta semper authoritate scripturae supra Catechesin, neque recepta Catechesi, nisi per Scripturam confirmata.
units.tr: Question: Is the Catechism to be included as well? Answer: Not as a canonical writing; rather, it is praiseworthily explained, proved and treated in sermons, but from Scripture. Nor does the opinion of the distinguished Amesius (Cas. Conscientiae, bk. 4, ch. 26) differ, for a passage of Scripture is always placed before catechetical instruction. It matters little whether I arrive at the Catechism by explaining a text, or go straight on to expound the Catechism after the passage of Scripture has been read and heard; and nothing in it is to be accepted unless it is proved from Scripture. I proceed to this more quickly, always holding Scripture's authority above the Catechism, and not accepting the Catechism unless it is confirmed by Scripture.

units.la: Omni, adeo nihil scriptum, quod non usum suum ad fidem & pietatem abunde etiam habeat.
units.tr: "Whole": so that nothing written is without its own use, abundantly serving faith and piety.

units.la: Quaer. I. An in Ecclesia ejusmodi interpretatio & concio verbi divini probanda sit? Aff. contra Libertinos, & Enthusiastas 1. ex institutione divina; istud enim medium Deus instituit, & sanctificavit, populum erudiendi. Matth. 28, 19. cum praxi Apostolica Rom. 1, 16. & 10, 14, 15. Ideo Deus in Ecclesia instituit ordinem docentium. Ephef. 4, 11, 12. Jesa. 30, 21. Jerem. 3, 15. III. Ab Exemplo, & usu Ecclesiae perpetuo, jam a Genef. 4, 26. hucusque, & in finem mundi. Matth. 28, 19. Ephef. 4, 12. IV. a fructu ejus certo, multiplici, & copioso. Jesa. 55, 10, 11.
units.tr: Question I: Should such interpretation and preaching of the divine Word be approved in the Church? Yes, against the Libertines and Enthusiasts: (1) from divine institution, for God instituted and sanctified this means of instructing the people (Matt. 28:19), with the apostolic practice (Rom. 1:16; 10:14, 15). Therefore God established in the Church an order of teachers (Eph. 4:11, 12; Isa. 30:21; Jer. 3:15); (III) from the example and the perpetual practice of the Church, from Gen. 4:26 until now, and to the end of the world (Matt. 28:19; Eph. 4:12); (IV) from its certain, manifold and abundant fruit (Isa. 55:10, 11).

units.la: Quaer. II. An etiam V. Testamentum hodie concionandum? Aff. contra veteres Cerdonianos, Marcionitas, Manichaeos, &c. Non enim soli Manichaei legem, Prophetasque condemnant, sed & Marcionitae, & alii Alii nonnulli, quorum sectae non ita innotuerunt populis Christianis, Augusti. lib. 1. contra adverf. legis & proph. cap. 1. Chryfoft. ferm. contra Anomaeos: & simul multos alios haereticos prosternere poterimus, videlicet, Marcionem, Manichaeum, Valentinum. Manichaei enim, & qui factionis illorum socii Prophetas, & Patriarchas contemnunt. Hodiernos Mennonitas. Vide Dooreslaer & Sylv. controv. 8. contra Mennon. aliosque Antinomos.
units.tr: Question II: Should the Old Testament also be preached today? Yes, against the ancient Cerdonians, Marcionites, Manichaeans, etc. "For not only the Manichaeans condemn the Law and the Prophets, but also the Marcionites and some others, whose sects have not become so well known to Christian peoples" (Augustine, bk. 1, Against the Adversaries of the Law and the Prophets, ch. 1). Chrysostom, sermon against the Anomoeans: "and at the same time we could overthrow many other heretics, namely Marcion, Manichaeus, Valentinus. For the Manichaeans, and those who are their companions in faction, despise the Prophets and Patriarchs." Likewise the present-day Mennonites. See Dooreslaer and Sylvius, Controversy 8, against the Mennonites and other Antinomians.

units.la: Quaer. III. An satis probari possit consuetudo illa (quae plurimis in locis obtinet) pro concione certas Dominicales, juxta Postillas (ut vocant) explicandi? Resp. Neg. vide Amef. loc cit. Primus, qui hunc ordinem introduxit, fuit Carolus M. A. Dccc. III. cujus jussu Alcuinus Levita homilias Patrum eum in finem collegit, postmodum locupletatas, atque ita porro desidiosi Clerici, ac Monachi nugaces illis solum populo exponendis inhaeserunt, quasi rotum Concionatorum officium, & verbum Dei illis jam contineretur, idque quidem juxta vanam festivitatum observantiam. Sixtinus Amama in orat. de Barbarie, hoc gradum fuisse recte judicat, ad barbariem illam, quae Ecclesiam tandem tam miserè defaedavit. Quare ubi fieri id commodè poterit, rectius mutatur, & aboletur, ut etiam ante aliquot annos Anno 1614. per ditionem Brandeburgicam illud factum.
units.tr: Question III: Can that custom (which holds in very many places) of explaining, for certain Sundays, according to the so-called Postils, be sufficiently justified? Answer: No. See Amesius, loc. cit. The first to introduce this order was Charles the Great, in the year 803, at whose command Alcuin the Levite gathered together homilies of the Fathers for that purpose, later enriched; and thereafter idle clergy and foolish monks clung to these alone, to be expounded to the people, as if the whole office of preachers and the Word of God were already contained in them, and that according to a vain observance of festivals. Sixtinus Amama, in his oration on Barbarism, rightly judges this to have been a step toward that barbarism which at last so wretchedly defiled the Church. Therefore, where this can conveniently be done, it is better to change and abolish it, as was done some years ago, in the year 1614, throughout the Brandenburg dominions.

units.la: IV. Ad aedificationem Ecclesiae: in doctrina veritatis, & in praxi pietatis, non in alterutro, sed utroque. Neque alius Concionatori scopus esse debet; non proprium bonum, sive lucri ex avaritia, Jezech. 34, 2, 3, 10. 1 Tim. 3, 3. Cod. de epifc. & Cler. l. omnem: purum habeant propositum, & pecunias contemnant, omnemque vitam suam ad clementissimum applicent Dominum. Ambrof. Offic. lib. 3. cap. 9. Synod. Nicen. 2. cap. 4. Bernard. ep. 24. Sive honoris, ex ambitione, Matth. 23, 6. Chrysosthom. de sacerd. lib. 5.
units.tr: IV. For the edification of the Church: in the doctrine of truth and the practice of piety, not in one alone but in both. Nor should a preacher have any other aim: not his own good, or gain from greed (Ezek. 34:2, 3, 10; 1 Tim. 3:3; Cod., de episcopis et clericis, law "omnem": let them have a pure purpose, despise money, and devote their whole life to the most merciful Lord). Ambrose, Duties, bk. 3, ch. 9; Second Council of Nicaea, can. 4; Bernard, letter 24. Nor for the sake of honour, from ambition (Matt. 23:6); Chrysostom, On the Priesthood, bk. 5.

units.la: V. Ita concionari nulli licet, nisi ab Ecclesia ad id vocato.
units.tr: V. No one may preach in this way unless he has been called to it by the Church.

units.la: In Ecclesia nimirum instituta & ordinata.
units.tr: That is, in the Church instituted and ordained.

units.la: Contra Socinianos, Catech. Racov. de Eccles. cap. 2. Smalc. c. Franz. part. 2. disp. 4. Theoph. Nicol. de Eccles. & missione. Volkel. de relig. lib. 6. cap. 12. Arg. I. ex ordinatione divina, Hebr. 5, 4. Rom. 10. 15. II. reprehensione, & peccato illorum, qui secus agunt. Jerem. 23, 21. III. ordine Ecclesiae, qui hoc possit. 1 Cor. 14. 40. & xxvii, 14. Joan. 5,
units.tr: Against the Socinians: Racovian Catechism, On the Church, ch. 2; Smalcius, against Francis, part 2, disp. 4; Theophilus Nicolai, On the Church and Mission; Volkelius, On Religion, bk. 6, ch. 12. Arguments: (I) from divine ordinance (Heb. 5:4; Rom. 10:15); (II) from the reproof and sin of those who act otherwise (Jer. 23:21); (III) from the order of the Church, which must allow this (1 Cor. 14:40; and 27:14; John 5:

units.la: 3. IV. Eadem est constans ratio omnium officiorum publicorum, ut nemo ea administret, citra peculiarem vocationem. V. Perpetuo Ecclesiae exemplo, & praxi, tam V. quam N. T. hucusque. Synod. VI. In Trullo ca. 64. ubi Schol. Balsam. Populum Domini docere, & divina decreta interpretari, solis antistitibus concessum est &c.
units.tr: 3). (IV) The same settled reasoning applies to all public offices, that no one administer them without a particular calling. (V) From the constant example and practice of the Church, both Old and New Testament, until now. Sixth Council in Trullo, can. 64, where the scholiast Balsamon says: "To teach the People of the Lord and to interpret the divine decrees has been granted to the bishops alone, etc."

units.la: Quaer. An S. Ministerii candidatis, Proponentibus, publicas liceat habere conciones, necdum ad ministerium vocatis? Resp. Non ita habent conciones, ut Concionatores; sed quasi specimina & exercitia concionum modo, se Praeparantes eo pacto ad ministerium, βαθμὸν ἑαυτοῖς καλὸν ἀφίαται, καὶ πολλὴν παρρησίαν ἐν πίστει τῇ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ 1 Timoth. 3, verf. 13. atque Ecclesiae se, suaque dona probant. Quare I. non ea authoritate loquuntur, ideoque nec libertate, & potestate, ac Pastores, licet etiam S. devotione audiendi, quia Dei verbum proponunt, cujus dignitas ab homine non pendet. II. Nec toties illis habendae conciones, ac si hoc eis de ordinario aliquo officio esset, quod ita non fit citra detrimentum Ecclesiae, praejudicium necessariae vocationis. III. Neque facile ubivis, ut qui specimina artis tis dant. IV. Neque omnia pastorum munia agunt, videlicet ad quæ singularis potestas requiritur, & vocatio ad ministerium istius Ecclesiæ, qualia, administratio Sacramentorum, & disciplina Ecclesiæ; quemadmodum in rep. tyronibus quidem, & Canditatis, conceditur, acta quædam, & instrumenta conscribere, non verò suâ authoritate ea signare, pronunciare, aut exequi.
units.tr: Question: May candidates for the holy ministry, who are being proposed, give public sermons before they have been called to the ministry? Answer: They do not preach as preachers do; rather they give sermons only as samples and exercises, preparing themselves in this way for the ministry, "for they acquire for themselves a good standing, and much boldness in the faith that is in Christ Jesus" (1 Tim. 3:13 [βαθμὸν ἑαυτοῖς καλὸν ἀφίαται, καὶ πολλὴν παρρησίαν ἐν πίστει τῇ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ]), and so prove themselves and their gifts to the Church. Therefore: (I) they do not speak with that authority, and so not with the freedom and power of ministers, although they too deserve the devout attention of hearers, since they propose the Word of God, whose dignity does not depend on man. (II) Nor should sermons be given so often as though this were some ordinary office, for that cannot be done without harm to the Church and prejudice to the necessary calling. (III) Nor readily everywhere, as those who give samples of skill. (IV) Nor do they perform all the duties of pastors, namely those which require a special power and the calling to the ministry of that particular Church, such as the administration of the sacraments and the discipline of the Church; just as in the case of trainees and candidates it is permitted to draw up certain acts and documents, but not to sign, pronounce or carry them out on their own authority.

units.la: CAPUT SECUNDUM.
units.tr: CHAPTER TWO.

units.la: I. Omnis concionandi ratio duobus absolvitur, formanda concione, & habenda. Utrumque ut recte fiat, artis sacræ est, & consistit in textu scripturæ explicando, & applicando; in quibus iterum duo proximè intendere debet Concionator, moveri, & movere, quo ipse sua concione moveatur, aliosque, qua doctrina, qua exemplo moveat: primum, rem dicit, alterum, modum; tertium, finem. Jam de priori parte, sc. concione formanda, quæ, vel communia concioni sint cum oratione in genere, vel in materia concionandi obvia cuivis, præteribimus, præcipuis modò inhæsuri.
units.tr: I. Every method of preaching consists of two parts: framing the sermon and delivering it. Doing both well belongs to the sacred art, and it consists in explaining and applying the text of Scripture. In these two parts the preacher ought chiefly to aim at two things: to be moved himself and to move others, so that he may be moved by his own sermon and may move others by doctrine and by example. The first concerns the matter, the second the manner, and the third the end. Now of the first part, namely framing the sermon, I shall pass over those points that are common to speech in general, or that lie open to anyone in the subject-matter of preaching, and I shall dwell only on the principal points.

units.la: II. In formanda concione videndum est, quid, & quomodo formes. 1 Cor. 2, 1. Ego ad vos veniens, non veni καθ' ὑπεροχὴν λόγῳ ἢ σοφίας, hoc de modo, annuncians vobis testimonium Dei, hoc rem spectat. Illud materiam dicit; hoc methodum, & stylum. Illud à Theologia habet; hoc à Logica, & Rhetorica quoque.
units.tr: II. In framing the sermon we must consider what we are to shape and how we are to shape it (1 Cor. 2:1): When I came to you, I came not with excellency of speech or of wisdom, declaring unto you the testimony of God. The first clause concerns this matter; the second concerns method and style. The first draws on theology; the second on logic, and on rhetoric as well.

units.la: III. Prima cura est textus, qui pro concione tractabitur, quem ex solo & omni Dei verbo legendum esse supra monuimus. Ille est, vel arbitrarius, vel status & certus, sive quem ordo Ecclesiæ, aut synedrium, aut ipsi Concionatores sibi fecerunt.
units.tr: III. The first care is the text that is to be treated in the sermon. As I have already observed, it must be read from God's word alone and from all of it. The text is either chosen freely or fixed and certain, that is, one that the order of the Church, or the synod, or the preachers themselves have appointed.

units.la: I V. In textu arbitrario, sive illum in Ecclesia, & loco proprio, vel alieno habeas (siquidem haud male à primis sæculis illud obtinuit, ut Baronius quoque notat tom. 1. Annal. ad A. 61. pag. 467. ut qui in alium locum venirent Episcopi, ab ejus loci Episcopo ad habendam ibi concionem invitarentur) hæc observanda. I. Ut primò & potissimum consideres, quid ibi loci concionari maximè conveniat. Contingit aliquandò, ut laboret Ecclesia notabili quo malo, sive circa veritatem, sive circa pietatem, in quo sæpe ab alio instrui mavult, & peregrini alicujus concio attentius audiri solet, sæpeque efficacior est ad permovendum, quam cujus quotidie, quantumlibet non inferior, habetur. Hoc ergò Concionatori præcipuè attendendum, sed & cum prudentia, ut pro statu loci magis concionem eligat, quam ut sui rationem duntaxat habens, vel eam conciohem promat, quam promptiorem habet, vel ex quâ plufculum honoris, applausus, aut commodi sibi speret. II. Ubi autem illud observari vel non potest, vel vix integrum, plerumque sumat textum magis practicum; quia passim defectus hic & in concionibus & in vita nostra observari solet, minus practicè illa institui: atque ita tutius, & majori cum fructu hic versabitur. Hæc communis querela; Abrenethij in Præf. ad Medic. animæ: plurimi libri, & conciones replentur speculativa, & contemplativa theologia: paucissimi Theologia practica. Vide & quæ doctè, ac pathetice hanc in rem disserit Telingius, nccess. demonstrat. lib. 3. cap. 4. & lib. 4. cap. 2. Præterea, quæ aliquando disp. de Theologia thes. 16. huc quoque attulimus. Jam olim Bernardus sermonem in Cant. octuagesimum ita exorsus est: Quidam vestrum (ut comperi) minus æquo animo ferunt, quod ecce jam per aliquot dies dum stupori & admirationi sacramentorum inhærere delectat, sermo quem ministramus, aut nullo fuerit, aut exiguo admodum moralium sale, conditus.
units.tr: IV. For a freely chosen text, whether you have it in your own church and place or in another's (for it has been customary since early ages, as Baronius also notes, tom. 1.
