units.tr: AUTHOR'S ADDITION.

units.la: UT maximum semper est Theologi studium, bene concionari: ita haud minimum studiosi negotium, artem ejus sacram probè addiscere. Nemo unquam est concionatus, qui non de ejus ratione sæpe cogitarit, & fideliter rem qui agit, attendit semper, quo pacto ad maximum Ecclesiæ fructum concio ejus possit institui. Eum in finem, ut cum studiosis nostris jam agamus, rectissimam ejus rationem nunc inquirere placet, & exponere. Quare commendamus non auctores modò, puta inter veteres, Chrysostomum lib. 5. de Sacerd. Augustt. de doctr. Christian. lib. 4. Gregor. M. in pastorali; inter recentes qui hac de re scripserunt, Erasmum, Hyperium, Keckermannum, Sohnium, (præter Pontificios, Granatensem, Augustt. Valerium, Stellam, Peresium, Iohannem à Iesu Maria. Polydorum Virgilium) Zepperum, Bucanum, Crocium, Hunnium, Ioh. Gerhardum, Scultetum, Perkinsum, Weemsum, Granogerum, Amesium, Rich. Bernardum, Telingium, Alstedium, Walæum, Strefonem, &c. Quodque præcipuè indicamus, Directorium cultus publici, in Anglia hoc anno authoritate Parlamenti editum, & erectum, cap. de prædicatione verbi: quo Theologi istius gentis, ob concionandi praxin præ omnibus celebres, observata sua simul centulerunt: sed & ipsarum concionum auditionem sedulam, atque lectionem; unde tum proprium judicium de optimâ methodo sibi colligant, ac formet studiosi; neque temere Rev. D. Strefo hoc technologiâ suâ Theol. fatetur se unice intendisse, ut istam Anglorum practicam feliciter deprehenderet, atque aliis communicaret; adeò præ omnibus merito se commendat.
units.tr: As the greatest concern of a theologian is always to preach well, so the no small task of a student is to learn thoroughly its sacred art. No one has ever preached who has not often thought about its method, and whoever faithfully performs this work always considers how his sermon may be arranged for the greatest benefit of the Church. To that end, since we are now dealing with our students, it pleases us to inquire into and set out its most correct method. Accordingly we commend not only authors, such as among the ancients Chrysostom (book 5 On the Priesthood), Augustine (On Christian Doctrine, book 4), Gregory the Great (in the Pastoral Care); and among the more recent writers who have written on this subject, Erasmus, Hyperius, Keckermann, Sohnius, (besides the Papists: Granatensis, Augustinus Valerius, Stella, Peresius, John of Jesus Mary, Polydorus Vergilius), Zepper, Bucanus, Crocius, Hunnius, John Gerhard, Scultetus, Perkins, Weemse, Granoger, Amesius, Richard Baxter, Telingius, Alsted, Walaeus, Strefon, etc.; and above all we point out the Directory of Public Worship, published and established this year in England by the authority of Parliament, chapter on the preaching of the Word, in which the theologians of that nation, most celebrated above all for the practice of preaching, have contributed their observations; and also the careful hearing of sermons themselves, and their reading, from which students may draw and form their own judgment about the best method. Nor without reason does Rev. Dr. Strefon confess in his Technologia that he aimed solely at discovering and communicating to others the happy practice of the English; so deservedly does he commend himself above all.

units.la: COROLLARIUM AUCTORIS,
units.tr: COROLLARY OF THE AUTHOR,

units.la: ANnon ex usu Ecclesiæ foret, Candidatos Ministerii etiam admittere ad Conventus Ecclesiasticos, ut Auditores? Sicut in senatu Romano, olim Senatorum filiis licuit, Sueton. in Augusto cap. 38. libris Senatorum, quò celerius R. P. assuescerent, curiæ interesse permisit. Et apud Judæos in summo Senatu Jerosolymitano, Sanhedrin etiam Candidati sedebant. Mischana Sanhedrin cap. 4. §. 4. וג שרות של תח Tres discipulorum, sive Candidatorum ordines coram illis sedebant. Quibus vel licuit aliquando interpellare, quod nos docet Moses Mikkotzi præc. aff. cvii. גם תלמיד etiam discipulus sedens coram judice, si videat innocentiam pauperis, & culpam divitis, tacere haud debet. Aff. prout Theologi Zelandi judicabant in Synodo Dordrac. Sess. xviii.
units.tr: Would it not be in keeping with the practice of the Church to admit candidates for the ministry also to ecclesiastical assemblies, as hearers? In the Roman senate it was once allowed for the sons of senators, as Suetonius says in Augustus ch. 38: he allowed the sons of senators to attend the Curia, so that they might more quickly become accustomed to the business of the Republic. And among the Jews, in the highest Senate at Jerusalem, the Sanhedrin, candidates also sat. Mishnah, Sanhedrin ch. 4 §4: three rows of disciples, or candidates, sat before them [שלש שורות של תלמידים]. They were sometimes even permitted to interrupt, as Moses Mikkotzi teaches us in affirmative precept 107: even a disciple sitting before the judge, if he sees the innocence of the poor man and the guilt of the rich man, ought not to keep silent [גם תלמיד]. This is affirmative, as the Zealand theologians judged in the Synod of Dort, session 18.
